intro.heading: Four different problems that all look like needing a maths tutor
paragraphs: IB mathematics generates more tutoring requests in Dubai than any other Diploma subject, and the requests arrive sounding identical. A parent says their child is struggling with maths and needs help before the May session. Underneath that sentence there are four quite different problems, and treating them as one is why families sometimes buy twenty sessions and see no grade movement.

The first problem is route. A student placed in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level who should be in Applications and Interpretation will work twice as hard for a lower grade, and the decision is usually made in Year 11 on the basis of an IGCSE or MYP result rather than on what the course actually demands. That is not fixed by tutoring; it is fixed by a conversation with the school, and the window for it is narrow.

The second is content pace. Higher Level in either route moves faster than any IGCSE or MYP course, and students who reached a grade 8 or a level 7 by memorising procedures hit the wall somewhere in the calculus. The third is the exploration, the internally assessed piece worth 20 per cent of the grade, which stalls on topic choice far more often than on mathematics. The fourth is technique: a student who understands the content and still loses method marks, misreads command terms, or runs out of time on Paper 1.

Those four need different interventions, and the first job of any tutor is to work out which one you have. A marked past paper and a look at the exploration draft settles it in ninety minutes. The rest of this page sets out what each problem looks like in detail: the route comparison, what each paper assesses and is worth, where marks leave the paper topic by topic, the exploration criteria letter by letter, and what the Dubai market charges.

On delivery, we are direct about it. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE — a tutor at the door is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video. For mathematics specifically that works better than a dining table: the student's attempt, the mark scheme and the tutor's working can share one screen, the whiteboard is saved, and the session is recorded so a worked solution can be replayed rather than half-remembered. It also means a Bur Dubai student is matched to someone who has taught Higher Level calculus rather than to whoever teaches maths nearby.

One more thing worth saying before the detail. Bur Dubai families are often weighing a tutor against a group revision course, and the two solve different problems: a course covers content at a fixed pace for everyone in the room, while one-to-one work exists to find the specific thing costing this student marks and fix it. If the diagnostic says the problem is pace, a course may genuinely be the better buy, and we will say so.

programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May session, with November functioning mainly as a resit route in this hemisphere. The exploration deadline is set by your school rather than by the IB, usually in DP2 with a draft date months earlier, and that internal date is the one a tutoring plan has to work back from.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme mathematics components

The difference is the surrounding load rather than the mathematics, which means subject tutoring works exactly the same way.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-bur-dubai.subjectsIntro: Mathematics requests from Bur Dubai are specific, and so are the failure points. Each entry below names a part of the course and what reliably goes wrong in it.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The heaviest mathematics in the Diploma. Calculus to a depth no IGCSE course approaches, proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, and vectors. Marks leave on unwritten method lines, on differentiation of composite functions, and on integration techniques chosen by trial rather than by recognition of the form.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, functions, sequences, basic calculus and probability. The usual weakness is algebra carried in from Year 11: a student who cannot rearrange confidently will lose marks across every topic regardless of how well they understand the new content sitting on top of it.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams, with heavy technology use. The late topics unsettle students who coasted through the earlier modelling work. Marks go on interpreting calculator output in context rather than on obtaining it.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial mathematics, modelling and geometry. Often chosen as the lighter option and then underestimated: the statistics component rewards careful interpretation and precise language, and students who treat it as arithmetic sit in the middle bands.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: HL and SL in both routes
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, with HL extending into techniques, kinematics and differential equations. The commonest HL failure is integration by substitution attempted without recognising the form, which burns ten minutes and earns nothing. Chain rule errors inside a longer question cascade through every subsequent mark.

subjects.name: Algebra, functions and proof
subjects.description: Sequences, logarithms, binomial expansion, and at HL proof by induction and contradiction. Proof questions are the most teachable marks in the course because they follow a fixed structure, and they are also the ones students most often leave blank.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: HL and SL in both routes
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and regression, weighted much more heavily in the Applications route. Students lose marks stating a conclusion without reference to the significance level, and on confusing correlation with a causal claim in an interpretation question.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and geometry
subjects.levels: HL and SL in both routes
subjects.description: Identities, equations and, at HL in Analysis, compound angle work. Solving trigonometric equations over a given domain is a reliable source of lost marks because students find one solution and stop, missing the others the question wanted.

subjects.name: Vectors and matrices
subjects.description: Vectors in Analysis HL, matrices and graph theory in Applications HL. Both arrive late in DP2 and compete with revision for everything else, which is why a planned block in Term 1 of DP2 is worth more than extra hours in April.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: An assessed skill, not a convenience. Students lose marks by producing a correct value and failing to state what they did, by using the wrong mode, and by not knowing the shortcuts for intersections, solvers and distributions. Practice must be on the student's own model to be worth anything.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A 12-to-20-page internally assessed investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade, marked against five criteria. It stalls on topic choice: too broad and there is no mathematics, too narrow and there is nothing to explore. A tutor may coach the question and the method and must not write any of it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge links in mathematics
subjects.description: Mathematics supplies some of the most usable Theory of Knowledge material in the Diploma, from the status of proof to the limits of modelling. Students who notice this early find the Theory of Knowledge essay substantially easier to write than those who look only at the humanities.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Bur Dubai is actually being asked to fix
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor working one-to-one online in the Dubai market costs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and a tutor travelling to a Bur Dubai address is quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 with the drive included. Before spending either, it is worth establishing which of four problems you have, because the same hourly rate buys very different value depending on the answer.

Route error is the first and the most expensive to leave alone. A student in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level who needed Applications and Interpretation will grind through two years for a grade below what they could have had elsewhere. Schools place students in Year 11, often from one set of results, and the deadline for moving is early. If this is your problem, the first action is a meeting with the school and not a tutoring contract.

Content pace is the second, and it is what tutoring is genuinely good at. Higher Level mathematics moves faster than anything in IGCSE or MYP, and students who got strong results by learning procedures run out of procedures somewhere in the calculus. Weekly work alongside the teaching fixes this; blocks in April do not, because by then the content is behind them and the gap has compounded.

The third is the exploration and the fourth is technique, and both are short, targeted engagements rather than long ones. The exploration stalls on topic choice, which three sessions can settle. Technique is method marks, command terms and pacing, which a marked paper exposes in an hour. Diagnosing which problem is in front of you is therefore the single highest-value thing the first session does, and ours is free.
bullets: Route error needs the school, not a tutor, and the window is narrow

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that shapes two years, and it is made on thin evidence more often than it should be. Both routes are full IB mathematics courses, both are available at Higher and Standard Level, and both are accepted for university entry in most subjects. They are not interchangeable in content or in what they demand of a student, and the difference is not simply that one is harder.

Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and abstraction. It carries proof at Higher Level, deeper calculus, and a general expectation that a student can manipulate symbols confidently without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistical reasoning and the disciplined use of technology, and its Higher Level content includes matrices, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams that Analysis students never see.

The honest selection signal is prior attainment in algebra rather than overall mathematics grades. A student who found Cambridge 0580 Extended algebra or MYP criterion A straightforward will cope with Analysis. A student who was strong in mathematics but relied on context and on a calculator is usually better served by Applications, and will frequently achieve a higher grade there while learning more.

Where this interacts with university plans, check specific requirements rather than assuming. Some engineering, physics and economics programmes state Analysis or its equivalent; many others accept either route; several UAE universities publish their own requirements that differ from the UK pattern families often assume. Check the published entry requirements for the actual programme and the actual intake year, because departmental practice changes.

sections.heading: The papers, what each assesses and where the marks go
paragraphs: Students revise topics. Examiners set papers. The gap between those two statements explains a large share of disappointing results, because a student can know every topic and still lose twenty marks to paper-specific habits. Knowing what each component asks for changes how revision is organised.

At Higher Level both routes sit three written papers plus the exploration; at Standard Level, two papers plus the exploration. One paper is sat without a calculator in the Analysis route, which makes algebraic fluency directly assessable, and the Applications route leans on technology throughout. The exploration is worth 20 per cent in every route and at both levels, which makes it the single largest component a student has direct control over.

The table sets out what each component rewards and where marks reliably leave. The pattern across all of them is method. IB mark schemes award method marks generously and students routinely forfeit them by writing only answers, particularly on calculator papers where the working feels redundant. Showing the substitution, naming the rule applied, and stating what the calculator was asked to do converts several marks per paper.

Confirm the current component structure and weightings against your school's own subject documentation, because the IB revises course guides and this page is an orientation rather than a specification. Published IB exam and results dates should come from your Diploma coordinator or from the IB directly; we do not publish them here because they could not be verified from the source for this project.

sections.heading: Where marks actually leave an IB maths paper, topic by topic
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma student which topic is costing them and they will name the one they dislike. Mark a paper against the scheme and a different list appears, usually shorter and more fixable. That is why no sensible plan starts before a full paper has been sat to time and marked properly, with losses recorded by topic and by question type.

The recurring entries on that list are consistent across Bur Dubai students. In the Analysis route: chain rule errors inside composite functions, integration attempted by trial rather than by recognising the form, trigonometric equations solved for one value in a domain that wanted three, and proof questions left blank despite following a fixed structure. In the Applications route: statistical conclusions stated without reference to a significance level, regression treated as causation, and calculator results quoted without the method.

Common to both and to every level is accuracy discipline. Rounding applied partway through a multi-step calculation produces an answer that is almost right, and almost right scores nothing on the final mark while often still earning the method. Students who adopt a single convention — carry full accuracy, round once at the end, state the rounding — pick up marks across every paper without learning any new mathematics.

The practical consequence is that short targeted blocks outperform long general ones. Thirty marks lost across chain rule, integration recognition and trigonometric domains is four sessions of work with a measurable result. The same hours spread across the full syllabus mostly revisit topics the student was already scoring on, which is why the second marked paper matters as much as the first.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is worth 20 per cent of the mathematics grade and it is the component a student controls most directly. It is also where Bur Dubai families most often ask for help, usually about six weeks before a school draft deadline, which is the most expensive moment to start. The marks are decided by the topic and the aim, both of which are settled in the first week.

Five criteria are assessed by letter, and students who have read them score better than students who have not — which sounds obvious and is routinely skipped. The commonest failure is a topic with no mathematics in it: a survey, a set of statistics copied from a website, and a conclusion. The second commonest is the reverse, a topic whose mathematics the student cannot actually carry, which produces a report describing somebody else's work.

A tutor's legitimate role here is well defined and worth stating precisely. A tutor may explain each criterion and what it rewards, help the student narrow a topic into a workable mathematical aim, discuss method and the mathematics required, read a draft the student has written and say where it loses marks against the criteria, and teach citation convention. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite paragraphs, supply a dataset, or produce a plan so detailed that the student is transcribing.

That line matters commercially as well as ethically in this market. One operator found in this search results page sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. Buying one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student: a withheld grade, or the Diploma itself. No agency carries that risk on a candidate's behalf, whatever it implies.

sections.heading: What IB maths tutoring costs in Dubai, and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Every figure in this section is checkable, which is the point of publishing it. A parent can open each source and read the rate, which is more than can be said for most pages ranking for this search: three of the six measured for this project publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams.

At the bottom of the market, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. That band buys supervised study rather than Higher Level mathematics teaching, and for a Diploma student it is rarely the right purchase. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, and home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500. The highest published figure found in this market is AED 650 at a premium named-tutor agency.

Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Higher Level mathematics sits towards the specialist end of that spread for a straightforward reason: the number of people who can teach it well is smaller than the number who advertise it.

None of these are IB Gram prices. They are what the Dubai market charges, each attributed, and they are here so a parent can calibrate a quote before accepting it. sections.heading: An in-home maths tutor in Bur Dubai against one-to-one online
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where parents most often want somebody in the room, and the instinct is understandable: working through a problem on paper feels like it needs a shared table. In practice a shared screen does the same job and leaves a record, which matters more in mathematics than in any other subject because a worked solution is only useful if it can be revisited.

The arithmetic of the two options in this district is straightforward. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 500 an hour with travel priced in; qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300. The travel premium over a twenty-session Higher Level block is a four-figure sum, and it buys proximity rather than calculus expertise. It also narrows the pool to whoever can reach Al Mankhool or Karama before 7pm, which for Higher Level Analysis is a short list.

Timing compounds this. An in-home session in Old Dubai rarely starts before 6pm because of the tutor's own commute, and mathematics at 7.30pm after a full school day and Arabic homework is not where a student does their best thinking. An online session can run at 4.30pm. Across an eight-week block the difference between alert and tired work is larger than any difference in teaching style.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE, and the table below is the case for why we think that is the right side of the trade for a Diploma mathematics student in this district. For a younger child who will not begin work without an adult present, the honest answer is different and we will say so.

sections.heading: KHDA, the timetable and what else is competing for the hours
paragraphs: A Diploma student's week is fuller than the subject list suggests, and a mathematics plan that ignores this fails. Dubai private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum.

Those requirements occupy real timetable hours. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes, and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes for both groups prohibited. Material for those subjects cannot be substituted without prior Ministry of Education permission.

Add Creativity, Activity, Service, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and five other subjects' internal assessments, and the hours available for mathematics practice are finite. The useful response is to be honest about the budget. Two hours of mathematics practice a week, done properly, beats five hours nominally scheduled and half-attended, and a plan built around what the student will actually do holds up better than one built around what they should.

Reading your school's published KHDA inspection report is also worth twenty minutes before buying anything. The reports comment at department level, so if mathematics attainment is flagged as weaker than other subjects you have learned something specific about where the problem starts — and whether a tutor is addressing a teaching gap or a student one.

faqs.question: Should my child in Bur Dubai take IB Maths Analysis or Applications?
faqs.answer: The honest selection signal is prior attainment in algebra rather than in mathematics generally. A student who handled Cambridge 0580 Extended algebra or MYP criterion A comfortably will cope with Analysis and Approaches, which rewards symbol fluency, calculus and proof. A student who was strong in context and data but leaned on a calculator usually achieves more in Applications and Interpretation, which is a full mathematics course and not a soft option. Check the published entry requirements for the specific degree programme and intake year, because some engineering and physics courses name Analysis and many others accept either.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade does the exploration carry?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in both routes and at both levels, which makes it the largest single component a student controls directly. It is also the one most often left until six weeks before a school draft deadline, which is the most expensive point to start. The marks are largely decided in the first week by the topic and the mathematical aim: too broad and there is no mathematics in it, too narrow and there is nothing to explore. Three sessions early are worth more than ten late.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work on the exploration with my child without it becoming malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a defined boundary. A tutor may explain what each of the five criteria rewards, help narrow a topic into a workable mathematical aim, discuss the mathematics and the method required, read a draft the student wrote and say where it loses marks, and teach citation convention. A tutor may not write or rewrite any part of it, supply a dataset, or hand over a plan detailed enough that the student is transcribing. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments at around AED 3,750; that is malpractice and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the maths but still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Almost always method and accuracy rather than understanding. IB mark schemes award method generously and students forfeit those marks by writing answers without working, particularly on calculator papers where the working feels redundant. The other recurring loss is rounding applied partway through a multi-step calculation, which produces an answer that is almost right and scores nothing. Adopting one convention — carry full accuracy, round once at the end, state the rounding — and writing the substitution and the rule applied converts several marks per paper without learning new mathematics.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Analysis much harder than Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and the gap is in depth rather than breadth. Higher Level adds a third written paper, proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, vectors and considerably harder calculus, and it expects confident algebraic manipulation without a calculator. Students who reached strong IGCSE or MYP results by learning procedures tend to meet the limit of that approach in the calculus. The practical implication is that Higher Level needs weekly work from early in DP1 rather than a block in DP2, because the content compounds.

faqs.question: My child came from MYP and is lost in DP1 maths. What actually needs fixing?
faqs.answer: Usually exam technique rather than content. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria in school-set tasks, often with no timed external paper, so a student with level 7s may never have sat a two-hour paper under mark-scheme conditions. The gaps that show up are showing method, working to time, reading command terms, and algebraic fluency without a calculator. Eight to twelve weeks of focused technique work early in DP1 generally resets this, and it is far cheaper than the rescue block families buy in DP2 instead.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Higher Level IB maths usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week through DP1, kept up consistently, with a short intensive block before mocks if the paper work needs it. Two a week from the start is rarely the right answer, because each session generates two or three hours of practice and a student who cannot service that is paying for the same topics twice. The exception is a student arriving from MYP who needs technique rebuilt, where two shorter sessions a week for eight weeks sets up the remainder of the course properly.

faqs.question: Does the graphic display calculator really need teaching?
faqs.answer: Yes, because its use is assessed rather than incidental. Students lose marks by producing a correct value and never stating what they asked the calculator to do, by working in the wrong mode, and by not knowing the shortcuts for intersections, solvers, regression and distributions. The teaching has to happen on the student's own model, since menus differ, and screen-sharing that model is more practical than looking over a shoulder. In the Applications route it is central to the whole assessment rather than a convenience.

faqs.question: Do you send an IB maths tutor to our home in Bur Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For Diploma mathematics that is the better arrangement in this district: a travelling tutor cannot usually start before 6pm, which is the worst time of day to attempt calculus, and the pool narrows to whoever can reach your street. Online, worked solutions are saved and replayable, calculator technique can be screen-shared on your child's own model, and the match is made on route and level.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level maths tutoring cost in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sits towards the specialist end of the published range because the pool of people who teach it well is small. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai figures put specialists at AED 200 to 450 an hour and upwards, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and Unitors quotes IB tuition from AED 200. Monthly, a weekly specialist hour in an exam year is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices; our own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson and a diagnosis.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start IB maths tutoring eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Not for technique, and probably too late for content. Eight weeks can fix method marks, accuracy discipline, pacing, calculator shortcuts and two or three specific topics, which together are often worth a grade boundary. What eight weeks cannot do is teach two years of Higher Level calculus or rescue an exploration already submitted and moderated. Establish which of those you are dealing with in the first session, from a marked timed paper, rather than buying a block and discovering it in week five.

faqs.question: Which maths topics cost Bur Dubai Diploma students the most marks?
faqs.answer: In the Analysis route: chain rule errors inside composite functions, integration attempted by trial rather than by recognising the form, trigonometric equations solved for one value where the domain wanted several, and proof questions left blank even though they follow a fixed structure. In the Applications route: statistical conclusions stated without reference to the significance level, regression treated as a causal claim, and calculator output quoted with no statement of method. Accuracy discipline costs marks in both, at every level.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both IB maths and IB physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The quantitative overlap is real: kinematics, graph interpretation, logarithmic scales and uncertainty handling appear in both. What matters is whether the tutor has actually taught both syllabuses at the level required, because Higher Level physics is not a mathematics course with context added. Where one person covers both well it saves scheduling and lets the quantitative skills be taught once; where they do not, two specialists on consecutive slots is the better arrangement.

faqs.question: When will my child in Dubai sit the IB maths papers?
faqs.answer: Dubai schools sit the May session, with November functioning mainly as a resit route in this hemisphere. We do not publish specific IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site could not be verified as a source for this project and a wrong date is worse than no date. Confirm the exact window, the results date and any enquiry-upon-results deadline with your school's Diploma coordinator or directly with the IB before planning travel, revision blocks or anything else around them.

intro.heading: Four courses wearing one name, and why the match has to be exact
paragraphs: Parents searching for an IB maths tutor in Business Bay are usually searching for a single thing. There are four. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation each run at Higher and Standard Level, and the four combinations are not variations in difficulty of one course. They assess different content, weight their papers differently, and reward different habits of working. A tutor who teaches Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level confidently may be of limited use to a student sitting Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the student will not be able to tell for several weeks.

This page is written from the subject rather than from the neighbourhood, because the subject is where the marks are. It sets out the components and their weightings, the five topic areas and the teaching hours each course is built around, the Exploration criteria by letter with the marks attached, and the mark-scheme notation that decides whether a half-right answer scores two marks or none. That last item is the one families almost never see, and it changes how a student writes a solution within about three sessions.

Business Bay matters to the logistics rather than the mathematics. There is no IB school inside the district, so every Diploma student living in the towers along the Dubai Water Canal commutes out, most often towards Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf, Al Quoz or Al Barsha. A 3.15pm school finish with a canal crossing in it means a realistic session start of 4.30pm. We schedule after that, not into it, because a Higher Level Paper 3 question is not a thing to attempt from the back seat of a car.

On delivery, we are direct. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and we do not operate a centre you can drive to; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For mathematics specifically this is close to an advantage rather than a concession, because written working shared live on a whiteboard is visible to the tutor as it forms, which is exactly where mark-scheme errors are caught. A photograph of finished working sent afterwards shows the answer and hides the mistake.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics, Years 12-13
programmes.description: Two years on one of four courses. Every course covers the same five topic areas with different depth and emphasis.

It is not continuous in mathematics: criterion-based coursework and a timed unseen Paper 1 reward different preparation almost entirely.

Extended tier Cambridge 0580 or Higher tier Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is the realistic prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Additional Mathematics is better preparation still. Mathematics suffers from this disproportionately because it is the subject where skipped practice compounds silently. A student who stops working problems for three weeks during an Extended Essay push does not notice the loss until a timed Paper 1 arrives.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-business-bay.subjectsIntro: The five topic areas every IB maths course covers, plus the components that sit around them. What differs between courses is depth, emphasis and the proportion of each paper, which is why a tutor matched to the wrong course teaches the right mathematics at the wrong level of abstraction.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level complex numbers, proof and matrices depending on course. Marks go missing on log manipulation and on binomial terms where the index is negative or fractional. Algebraic fluency here is the hidden prerequisite for everything in calculus later.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations, quadratics and rational functions. Analysis and Approaches pushes further into algebraic manipulation of functions; Applications and Interpretation leans towards modelling with them. The common error is treating a transformation question as a sketching exercise and losing the algebraic justification marks.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations, radian measure, vectors at Higher Level, and three-dimensional geometry. Radians are the single largest source of silent calculator errors in this topic: a calculator left in degrees produces plausible wrong answers that a student will not flag. Checking calculator mode is a habit, not a skill.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability distributions, the binomial and normal distributions, and at Higher Level hypothesis testing in Applications and Interpretation. This topic carries much more weight in Applications and Interpretation, where statistical technique with a calculator is a core skill rather than a module.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, kinematics, and at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches considerably more technique including implicit differentiation, integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. This is where Higher Level Analysis and Approaches separates decisively from the other three courses in volume of required practice.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Short and extended response questions. In Analysis and Approaches no graphical display calculator is permitted, which turns algebraic fluency into the whole examination. In Applications and Interpretation a calculator is allowed. Students who revise by working calculator-permitted past papers are preparing for the wrong paper, and this is a surprisingly common waste of a term.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Calculator permitted in both courses. The failure mode is not inability but accuracy: answers must be given to three significant figures unless otherwise stated, and a correct method followed by an unrounded or over-rounded answer loses the final accuracy mark. This is the cheapest set of marks on any IB maths paper to recover.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions, each building through parts towards an unfamiliar result. It rewards reading the whole question before starting and using earlier parts in later ones, which is a technique rather than knowledge. Students who have never seen a Paper 3 before the examination almost always mismanage the time.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: An individual written piece of mathematical work, internally assessed and externally moderated, marked on five criteria for a total of twenty marks. It is the component where a tutor's role is most constrained and most useful: criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own draft are legitimate, writing any part of it is not.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The course for students heading towards mathematics, engineering, physics, economics at quantitative universities and most medicine routes. It emphasises algebraic manipulation, proof and analytical calculus technique. The Higher Level version is the most demanding of the four by volume of technique required.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The course for students heading towards business, social sciences, design, architecture and biology-led routes. It emphasises modelling, statistics and technology use. It is not an easier course; at Higher Level it carries substantial statistical content that Analysis and Approaches students never meet.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator skills
subjects.description: A taught skill treated as incidental by most schemes of work. Solving equations numerically, finding intersections, working with distributions and using regression functions are each worth marks, and students who use the calculator only as an arithmetic device leave those marks behind. Practising the device is practising the subject.

sections.heading: The four courses, component by component
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Business Bay has to know which of four courses a student is on before the first problem is worked. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation each run at Higher and Standard Level. Standard Level is built around 150 recommended teaching hours and Higher Level around 240. Standard Level students sit two written papers; Higher Level students sit three. All four courses include the Exploration at twenty per cent.

The structural consequence is that the same overall grade is reached by different routes. At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry forty per cent, so a weakness in one paper can be substantially offset by the other. At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry thirty per cent each and Paper 3 carries twenty, so the grade is spread across three unfamiliar formats instead of two. A Higher Level student who ignores Paper 3 until the final term has left a fifth of the grade unpractised.

The content consequence is sharper still. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a graphical display calculator, so every mark on that paper depends on algebraic manipulation done by hand. In Applications and Interpretation, a calculator is permitted throughout. A student revising Analysis and Approaches by working through calculator-permitted questions is practising a skill that will not be available in the examination hall, and it is a mistake that survives a whole term because the mathematics looks identical on the page.

Confirm your child's course and level against the school's own documentation rather than relying on memory, and confirm every assessment detail in the table below against the current IB subject guide your school holds. The IB revises subject guides on a cycle, ibo.org does not permit automated verification, and this page will not publish an IB examination date or results date that has not been read from an official source.

sections.heading: Reading a mark scheme: M, A, R and the follow-through mark
paragraphs: This is the section that changes a grade fastest and the one no competitor page in this market publishes. IB mathematics mark schemes award marks by type, and a student who does not know the types writes solutions that throw marks away while arriving at correct answers. Method marks reward a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails. Accuracy marks reward the correct value. Reasoning marks reward a stated justification. Follow-through marks allow a later answer to earn credit from an earlier wrong value, provided the subsequent method is sound.

The practical effects are immediate and slightly counterintuitive. A student who writes only a final answer and gets it wrong scores nothing, even where their method was entirely correct, because there is no visible method to award. A student who shows the substitution, makes an arithmetic slip, and continues correctly can score most of the marks available. This is why "show your working" is not a teacher's preference in IB mathematics; it is the mechanism by which partial credit exists at all.

Three rules follow. First, write the method line before the calculator line, always, including on calculator-permitted papers where the temptation to produce only a numeric answer is strongest. Second, when a question says "hence", use the previous part; a correct answer obtained by an independent method can fail to earn the mark the question was testing. Third, on Paper 2 and Paper 3 give answers to three significant figures unless the question states otherwise, because the final accuracy mark is lost to rounding more often than to mathematics.

A tutor can teach this in three or four sessions, and the effect is visible in the next set of marked papers. It is also the clearest demonstration of why a student needs a tutor who has taught their exact course: the notation is shared across IB mathematics, but what counts as a sufficient method line in a Higher Level Paper 3 question is not the same as in a Standard Level Paper 1 question, and only somebody who has marked both knows the difference.

sections.heading: The Exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of every IB mathematics grade comes from a single piece of individual written work, and it is assessed on five criteria with different mark allocations. In the current structure, Criterion A covers presentation, Criterion B mathematical communication, Criterion C personal engagement, Criterion D reflection and Criterion E use of mathematics, for a total of twenty marks. Criterion E carries the largest allocation and Criteria C and D the smallest. Confirm the exact current descriptors and allocations with your child's teacher, because the IB revises them.

Where Business Bay students lose Exploration marks is predictable. Criterion E suffers when the mathematics chosen sits below the level of the course: a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Exploration built on Standard Level statistics cannot reach the upper bands however well written it is. Criterion D suffers because reflection is confused with summary; a paragraph restating what was done earns little, while a paragraph explaining what a result implies and what the model's limitations are earns the band. Criterion C suffers when the topic is generic, because personal engagement has to be visible in the choices made rather than asserted in the introduction.

The single most useful intervention is also the earliest one: a conversation about topic viability before weeks have been spent. A student who has invested four weeks in a topic that cannot support Higher Level mathematics has a problem no amount of writing fixes. Twenty minutes of discussion at the proposal stage routinely saves a month, and it is entirely within the academic-honesty boundary because the question being answered is whether a topic can reach the criteria, not what the student should write.

What a tutor must not do is equally clear. No part of the Exploration may be written, drafted, completed or edited to completion by anybody other than the student. Feedback on a student's own draft is legitimate. Supplying sentences, restructuring the text, or performing the calculations is not. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the Diploma, so this boundary protects your child rather than us. IB Gram will not write any part of an Exploration and will not accept the work if it is offered.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, topic by topic
paragraphs: Diagnosis beats effort in IB mathematics, because the topics that cost marks are a short and stable list. Across the four courses, the recurring losses cluster in six places, and a tutor who starts by identifying which of the six is active can usually plan a term in one session rather than three.

Logarithms and exponents come first. Students can state the laws and cannot apply them in reverse, so an equation requiring a change of base or the combination of two log terms stalls. Second, radian measure: a calculator left in degree mode produces answers that look reasonable and are wrong, and because nothing flags the error, students repeat it across a whole paper. Third, binomial expansion with negative or fractional indices, where the general term is misremembered and the validity condition is omitted.

Fourth, calculus technique at Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, specifically integration by substitution and by parts, where the issue is choosing the substitution rather than executing it. Fifth, probability distributions in Applications and Interpretation, where students know the distribution and misread which tail the question wants. Sixth, and most costly in aggregate, three-significant-figure rounding on Papers 2 and 3, which loses a mark per question without touching the mathematics at all.

The reason this list is useful is that four of the six are habits rather than knowledge. Calculator mode, rounding discipline, writing the method line, and reading which tail is wanted are all behaviours that change inside a month with deliberate practice. Only the calculus technique and the log manipulation require substantial teaching time. A family in Business Bay deciding whether a tutor is worth the money should ask for a diagnosis against this list first, because if the losses are habitual the intervention is short and if they are technical it is a term.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the route decision and what it closes
paragraphs: The choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is made in DP1 and has consequences in university applications two years later. It is not a difficulty choice, and describing Applications and Interpretation as the easier course is both inaccurate and unhelpful to a Business Bay family trying to decide.

Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic manipulation, proof and analytical calculus. It is the course that quantitative degree programmes most often expect, including mathematics, engineering, physics and economics at research universities, and it is the usual expectation for competitive medicine routes. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology use, and is well matched to business, social sciences, design, architecture and biology-led pathways. At Higher Level it carries statistical content that Analysis and Approaches students never encounter.

The decision rule we give families is simple and unglamorous. Identify three or four degree programmes the student might plausibly apply to, read the published mathematics requirement for each on the university's own admissions page, and choose the course that satisfies all of them. Do not choose on which course the student currently finds comfortable, because the comfort gap at the start of DP1 is usually a fluency gap from IGCSE or MYP and is closeable. Do not choose on a teacher's informal advice without checking the requirement in writing.

Changing course after the start of DP1 is possible in some schools and difficult in all of them, and the window closes quickly. If there is doubt, resolve it in the first weeks rather than at the end of the first term. Where a student has already begun Applications and Interpretation and later discovers an engineering ambition, the honest conversation covers foundation-year routes and alternative entry rather than pretending the original requirement can be argued away.

sections.heading: The IGCSE and MYP gap that arrives in September
paragraphs: Most Business Bay families who look for an IB maths tutor do so between September and November of DP1, and the reason is almost always the same. The student arrived from MYP 5 or from Year 11 with strong grades and hit Higher Level content that assumes an algebraic fluency their previous course did not require them to demonstrate under time pressure.

From the MYP the mechanism is criterion-based assessment. An MYP 5 student is assessed on four criteria across coursework and tasks, which rewards process, investigation and communication. It does not require repeated timed manipulation of unseen algebra against the clock. A student holding 6s and 7s in MYP mathematics can therefore be genuinely strong and still find a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 unmanageable in October, because the demand is new rather than harder.

From IGCSE the mechanism is tier. Extended tier Cambridge 0580 or Higher tier Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 covers the algebra Higher Level assumes; Core and Foundation tier do not. Additional Mathematics, where a school offers it, closes the gap almost entirely. A Core-tier candidate entering Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is carrying a year's deficit into a two-year course, and the right advice is often to move to Standard Level or to Applications and Interpretation early rather than to buy two years of tutoring.

Either way the fix is diagnosable and time-limited. Six to ten weeks of targeted algebraic fluency work, done calculator-free, closes most of the September gap for a student who is otherwise capable. The mistake families make is treating it as a general confidence problem and buying open-ended weekly tutoring, when what is needed is a short specific block followed by a review against component marks.

sections.heading: What IB maths tuition costs in Dubai, and what a parent can verify alone
paragraphs: Prices in this market are easier to check than providers imply, and a Business Bay family can establish the whole picture in an afternoon without speaking to anybody. Open the published rate pages of four or five providers, note the figure and the date, and the bands become obvious. That exercise is the honest basis for the numbers below, every one of which belongs to the provider or publication named beside it.

At the budget end of online tutoring, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a qualified subject tutor online, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is included. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium named-tutor end. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Two observations a parent can make from that data without any help. First, the in-home band sits above the equivalent online band by roughly the cost of the travel, and the extra buys logistics rather than a better specialist. Second, Higher Level mathematics sits at the specialist end of every published scale, which means a rate at the budget end for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is a signal to ask who is teaching and what they have taught before.

IB Gram does not publish a UAE price list on these pages and does not present market rates as ours. The free trial lesson exists so that a family can see the teaching before discussing money, and the consultation exists so that the number of sessions is decided from component marks rather than from a package. We also do not publish satisfaction percentages, average score claims or any statistic we cannot support with n, date and method, which is why there are none on this page.

sections.heading: Planning a Diploma mathematics year backwards
paragraphs: A mathematics year is planned backwards from the examination session, and in the UAE the Diploma session that schools sit is May. This page does not publish an IB examination window or a results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator, who has the official timetable.

What can be planned without dates is the sequence, and the sequence is what families get wrong. The Exploration deadline is set internally by the school and usually falls well before the examination term, which means Exploration work competes with content teaching rather than following it. Mock examinations sit roughly a term before the session. Predicted grades are issued for university applications before the student has finished the course, which is why DP1 performance matters more than students expect.

The practical consequence for a Business Bay family is about load rather than content. The weeks when the Exploration deadline, the Extended Essay deadline and the mock examinations cluster are the weeks when a weekly tutoring session should reduce or pause, not intensify. Families who add hours in those weeks typically see attendance collapse and then conclude that tutoring did not work, when what failed was the calendar.

Ramadan also moves the shape of the term for many families in this corridor, with school days shortened and evening schedules reorganised around iftar. Sessions can be moved to post-iftar timings or to the early afternoon, and planning that in advance rather than improvising week by week keeps continuity through a period that otherwise costs three or four weeks of momentum.

sections.heading: Regulation, honesty and the limits of what we will claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page, titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so this page quotes no amount; a figure circulating online could not be verified against an official source. In Dubai, your child's school is regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific authorisation issued to institutes with premises.

IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, licence, approval or partnership, and we do not describe ourselves as endorsed by any of them. We have no office, branch or centre in the United Arab Emirates. We name regulators on these pages to explain what they do, because a parent who understands the regulatory map can check a provider's claims, and because almost nobody else in this market names them at all.

On academic honesty the position is short. A tutor teaches content, explains criteria, models technique on a different example, and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write, complete or edit assessed work to completion, and does not supply IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the Diploma. Any provider offering to produce an Exploration is disqualified by the offer itself, whatever else they do well.

sections.heading: Coverage, matching and what happens when the answer is no
paragraphs: No platform covers every course at every hour, and the honest move is to say where the gaps are. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are reliably covered. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is covered but fills first, because it is the course with the deepest technique requirement and therefore the smallest specialist pool. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, with its statistical content, is the narrowest of the four and the one most likely to require a wait or an alternative hour.

The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is the busiest of the week for the whole corridor, since every Dubai family wants the same slot. For a Business Bay student arriving home around 4.30pm, the hours that stay open longest are 4.30pm itself and anything after 7.30pm, plus weekend mornings. Where no UAE-based specialist covers a course, the match may be a specialist teaching into the Gulf timezone from elsewhere, and that is stated before the trial lesson rather than discovered later.

What we will not do is match a student to a tutor who teaches a different course and hope the overlap is enough. It is not enough, particularly between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, where the content diverges substantially. If the specialist is not available at the hour you need, you will be told at the enquiry and offered the hours that are open.

Bring three things to the consultation and the first session becomes a diagnosis instead of an introduction: which of the four courses your child is enrolled on, the most recent component-level marks rather than the overall grade, and the school's internal Exploration deadline. Those three pieces of information decide what the first four weeks should be, and all three are free to obtain.

faqs.question: My child is in Business Bay and does IB maths. Which course do I need a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Find out which of four courses they are enrolled on before you book anything: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. The school's course selection letter or the student's timetable will say. This matters more than any other detail, because the four courses assess different content and weight their papers differently. A tutor strong in Standard Level Applications and Interpretation may be of limited use to a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student, and it typically takes a family several weeks and several paid sessions to discover that.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why has nobody explained it to us?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level students, in both IB maths courses, and carries twenty per cent of the grade. It consists of extended problem-solving questions built in parts towards an unfamiliar result, with a calculator permitted. It rewards reading the whole question before starting and using earlier parts in later ones, which is a technique rather than a body of knowledge. Many schemes of work leave it until the final term, which is why students meet it late and mismanage the time. Confirm the current format with your child's teacher against the school's subject guide.

faqs.question: Why does my child need to revise Paper 1 without a calculator?
faqs.answer: Because in Analysis and Approaches no graphical display calculator is permitted in Paper 1, which carries forty per cent of the Standard Level grade and thirty per cent at Higher Level. Every mark on that paper depends on algebraic manipulation performed by hand. A student who revises by working calculator-permitted questions is practising a skill that will not be available in the examination hall. The mathematics looks identical on the page, which is why this error can survive an entire term unnoticed. In Applications and Interpretation a calculator is permitted throughout, so the rule does not apply.

faqs.question: What are M marks and A marks on an IB maths paper?
faqs.answer: They are the two main mark types in IB mathematics mark schemes. A method mark rewards a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails; an accuracy mark rewards the correct, correctly rounded value. There are also reasoning marks for explicit justification and follow-through marks that let a later answer earn credit from an earlier wrong value. The practical consequence is large: a bare wrong answer scores nothing even with a perfect unwritten method, while visible working with a slip in it can score most of the marks. Writing the method line is therefore mechanical mark protection.

faqs.question: Does it really cost marks if my child rounds to two significant figures?
faqs.answer: Yes, routinely, and it is the cheapest mark loss on any IB maths paper to fix. On calculator-permitted papers, answers should be given to three significant figures unless the question states otherwise. A correct method followed by an over-rounded or unrounded final answer loses the accuracy mark while the mathematics was entirely right. Across a full paper this can amount to several marks, which at a grade boundary is decisive. It takes about two weeks of deliberate practice to make correct rounding automatic, and it is usually the first thing a good diagnostic session identifies.

faqs.question: When a question says hence, can my child use a different method?
faqs.answer: They can, and they may still lose the mark. The word hence is an instruction to use the result of the previous part, and the question is testing whether the student can see the connection. A correct answer reached independently sometimes fails to earn the credit the question was designed to award. The related variant, hence or otherwise, does permit an independent method. Teaching a student to read command terms as instructions rather than as connecting words is a short piece of work with a disproportionate effect on marks across a whole paper.

faqs.question: How are the Exploration marks divided up?
faqs.answer: The Exploration is worth twenty per cent of every IB maths grade and is marked on five criteria for a total of twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation, and personal engagement and reflection the smallest. Confirm the current descriptors and allocations with your child's teacher, since the IB revises subject guides on a cycle. The practical point for a parent is that the largest single criterion depends on the mathematics being at the level of the course, which is a decision made when the topic is chosen.

faqs.question: My child picked an Exploration topic a month ago. Can a tutor check it is viable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the most useful twenty minutes available. A tutor can judge whether the proposed mathematics is commensurate with the course level, because a Higher Level Exploration built on Standard Level statistics cannot reach the top bands however well it is written. That conversation is entirely within the academic-honesty boundary: the question being answered is whether a topic can meet the criteria, not what the student should write. Doing it at the proposal stage routinely saves a month of misdirected work, and a month is a lot in DP1.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child finish the Exploration before the school deadline?
faqs.answer: A tutor will explain each criterion, discuss the structure, and give feedback on your child's own draft. A tutor will not write any part of it, supply sentences, perform the calculations or edit it to completion. That boundary exists to protect your child: a malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the Diploma. If the deadline is genuinely unreachable, the conversation to have is with the school's coordinator rather than with a tutor. Any provider offering to produce an Exploration is disqualified by that offer, whatever else they appear to do well.

faqs.question: AA or AI: how do we decide without guessing at university requirements?
faqs.answer: Decide it from the destination, not from comfort. List three or four degree programmes the student might apply to, read the published mathematics requirement on each university's own admissions page, and pick the course that satisfies all of them. Analysis and Approaches suits mathematics, engineering, physics and quantitative economics, and is the usual expectation for competitive medicine routes. Applications and Interpretation suits business, social sciences, design, architecture and biology-led pathways, and at Higher Level carries statistics that Analysis and Approaches students never meet. It is a different course, not an easier one.

faqs.question: My child had strong MYP maths grades and is struggling in DP1. What changed?
faqs.answer: The demand changed rather than the difficulty. MYP mathematics is assessed on four criteria across coursework and tasks, which rewards investigation, process and communication. It does not require repeated timed manipulation of unseen algebra against a clock, which is exactly what a Diploma Paper 1 requires. A student holding 6s and 7s in MYP 5 can therefore be genuinely able and still find October of DP1 unmanageable. Six to ten weeks of calculator-free algebraic fluency work closes most of that gap, which is a short specific block rather than an open-ended year of tutoring.

faqs.question: Can a Core tier IGCSE student cope with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: It is a hard road and often the wrong one. Extended tier Cambridge 0580 or Higher tier Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 covers the algebra that Higher Level Analysis and Approaches assumes, and Additional Mathematics closes the gap almost completely. A Core or Foundation tier candidate is carrying roughly a year's algebraic deficit into a two-year course where the technique load is the heaviest of the four IB maths options. The honest advice is usually to move to Standard Level or to Applications and Interpretation within the first weeks of DP1, rather than buying two years of support to stay in place.

faqs.question: What does Higher Level IB maths tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Higher Level mathematics sits at the specialist end of every published scale in this market. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour online, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. Those are each provider's own published figures, read in October 2026. A Higher Level rate quoted at the budget end of the market is a prompt to ask which IB maths course the tutor has actually taught, and how recently.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Higher Level maths realistically need?
faqs.answer: One session a week sustained across a term usually beats two sessions a week that collapse by week five, and the Diploma workload makes collapse likely. The exception is a paper-specific block: four to eight weeks at two sessions a week aimed at Paper 1 fluency or Paper 3 technique, with a defined endpoint. Load should fall rather than rise in the weeks where the Exploration deadline, Extended Essay deadline and mock examinations cluster. Families who add hours in those weeks typically lose attendance and then conclude tutoring failed, when the calendar did.

faqs.question: How should we handle the Ramadan weeks without losing a term of maths momentum?
faqs.answer: Yes, and planning it in advance rather than week by week is what keeps momentum. School days shorten during Ramadan and evening routines reorganise around iftar, which for many Business Bay families makes the usual 5pm slot unworkable for several weeks. Sessions can move to the early afternoon or to a post-iftar time. Agreeing the alternative pattern before the month starts avoids the three or four weeks of lost continuity that otherwise happens, which matters most for a DP2 student working towards the May session.

faqs.question: When are the IB maths examinations, and can you confirm the dates?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session, and we will not publish a specific IB examination or results date on this page. The IB's own site does not permit automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a parent plans around has to be right. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the official timetable for your centre. What can be planned without dates is the sequence: Exploration deadline first, then mocks, then predicted grades, then the session itself.

faqs.question: Do you have a tutor who could come to our apartment in Business Bay?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch or tuition centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics specifically, the live shared whiteboard is arguably better than sitting beside a student, because the tutor sees written working as it forms rather than after it is finished, and that is precisely where mark-scheme errors are visible and correctable.

intro.heading: City Walk or Jumeirah 1 — the maths question does not change
paragraphs: City Walk is an apartment district, and that single fact changes how its families shop for tuition. Walk ten minutes north-west and you are in Jumeirah 1, where the housing is villas with a study and a spare room. Walk south and you hit Al Wasl and Al Safa, where the big British schools sit. A parent in a Jumeirah 1 villa has somewhere obvious to put a visiting tutor. A parent in a City Walk apartment often does not, and the sitting room is also where a younger sibling is doing homework. So City Walk families ask the home-tutor question earlier and more sceptically than their neighbours two streets over.

Here is the honest answer, and it is the same answer on both sides of Al Wasl Road. The thing that decides whether IB Mathematics tuition works is not the room. It is whether the tutor has taught the exact course your child sits. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are two separate courses with two separate syllabuses, four separate paper structures across HL and SL, and two very different ideas of what a good answer looks like. A tutor who is strong at one is not automatically useful at the other. There are not many of either within a twenty-minute drive of City Walk, and the ones who are get booked by whoever called first.

IB Gram does not solve that by sending someone to your building. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses at all — home visits are a service we run only in India. We solve it by removing the drive from the equation. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, so the pool you choose from is every Mathematics AA and AI specialist we work with rather than the three who happen to live near Al Safa. A City Walk student who needs Paper 3 practice at HL gets someone who has taught Paper 3, not someone who is free on Tuesdays.

That also fixes the thing City Walk parents complain about most, which is time. The school run from City Walk to Al Safa or Umm Suqeim is short in distance and unpredictable in minutes, and Al Wasl Road at 3.30pm does not care about your lesson slot. An online session starts when the clock says so. If your child walks in at 4.07pm, the lesson starts at 4.07pm and still runs its full hour. No travel fee, no tutor sitting in traffic on Sheikh Zayed Road, no lesson quietly shortened to let someone reach their next booking in Jumeirah 3.

This page is built as a comparison, because that is the decision a City Walk family is actually making. It sets this neighbourhood against the ones next to it on schools, commute and session timing. It sets Mathematics AA against AI, paper by paper, with the weightings written out. It sets online tuition against the in-home market using published AED figures with their sources named. And it counts the two years of the Diploma backwards from the May session, so you can see which eight weeks matter and which ones do not.

Everything factual below is either sourced to a named authority or framed as market observation. Where a figure belongs to a competitor, the competitor is named. Where a date belongs to Cambridge or Pearson, the official timetable is the reference rather than our restatement of it. And where something is genuinely not verifiable — IB session dates among them — this page says so instead of inventing a number your child would plan around.
