sections.heading: The week between sessions
paragraphs: If a single change had to be made to how maths tutoring is bought in this market, it would be to the days with no lesson on them. Fluency is built by short frequent repetition, and a weekly hour provides none of it. Ten minutes of written work four times between sessions is a trivial commitment and it changes the rate at which everything sticks.

The content of that daily work should be narrow and old rather than broad and current. Three rearrangements, two differentiations, one integral — material already taught, repeated for speed rather than for understanding. Students resist it because it feels like going backwards, and it is precisely the thing that stops the backwards slide that otherwise happens between Tuesdays.

The weekend task is different in kind: one longer piece, a paper section sat to time or a set of past questions on the current topic, marked by the student against the official scheme. That is the work that generates the material for the next session, and it is why the session has something to diagnose rather than something to explain again.

The table below is a template rather than a prescription, written for a student in DAMAC Hills who gets home after five and has two sessions a week. The point is that the four quiet days are doing work, and that work is small enough to survive a long school day.

The test of whether the pattern is working is speed rather than accuracy. Time three rearrangements at the start of a block and time the same three a month later. If the answers were right both times but took half as long on the second attempt, the drill is doing its job and the Paper 1 mark will follow. If the time has not changed, the daily work is not actually happening, which is a more common finding than any tutor would like to admit.

sections.heading: The exploration, handled as three checkpoints
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration does not need a weekly tutor and frequently gets one. It needs three decisions made at the right times, and a student working in between. Treating it as a weekly slot tends to produce a student who waits for the session to make progress, which is the opposite of what a piece of independent mathematical writing is supposed to develop.

Checkpoint one is feasibility, and it is the one that earns most. Students choose topics they find interesting and discover the mathematics is either trivial or beyond the course. The test is whether there is mathematics at their own level that can be done properly in the space available, and that judgement takes a single conversation. A tractable topic chosen early is worth more than four extra sessions later.

Checkpoint two is soundness, placed once the mathematics is drafted. Is it correct, is it at course level, and does it actually address the question posed? Errors found here are fixable. Errors found in the final fortnight are not, because the time needed to redo the mathematics no longer exists.

Checkpoint three is the criterion review. Roughly half the available marks concern presentation, communication, personal engagement and reflection rather than the mathematics. The student self-marks their own draft against each criterion, with the mark ceiling for each stated, and justifies the mark they have given themselves. The tutor gives feedback on what the student wrote and produces no part of it, which is an IB academic-honesty rule rather than a preference.

sections.heading: Reading the paper split after a mock
paragraphs: A mock in Diploma mathematics produces two or three paper marks, and the relationship between them is a diagnosis. Most families look at the overall grade and miss it entirely. The split takes five minutes to read and usually names the block without any professional help at all.

On the Analysis route, a solid Paper 2 with a weak Paper 1 is the classic signal: the mathematics is understood and the manipulation is not fluent, because Paper 1 removes the calculator that was concealing it. That student needs daily drill and non-calculator practice, not more teaching. The reverse pattern — Paper 1 solid, Paper 2 weak — points at calculator procedure and accuracy conventions rather than at mathematics.

On the Applications route both papers permit technology, so the split is less diagnostic and the loss pattern within each paper matters more. The common finding is outputs produced without interpretation: a regression with no comment, a test with no conclusion in context. That is a writing habit and it responds quickly.

At Higher Level, Paper 3 almost always sits below the others in a first mock, and that is structural rather than informative. It is the paper nobody has sat to time, and the remedy is exposure early in the second year rather than additional content. The table sets out what each pattern means and what it implies for the next eight weeks.

One further pattern deserves naming because it is the most misread. Where both papers sit low and the classroom work has been fine all year, the likely explanation is a foundation gap rather than a technique problem, and an eight-week technique block will produce a disappointing result. That student needs a longer rebuild and deserves to be told so before money changes hands, not in week six when nothing has moved.

sections.heading: What to do in each school break
paragraphs: Dubai schools give three breaks, and in mathematics each has a different best use. Treating all three as rest is the most common planning error available, because they are also the only periods in which a student has time without competing deadlines.

The winter break of the second Diploma year is the best exploration window there is. No new teaching, free days, and the opportunity to finish a draft before mock revision begins rather than alongside it. Three or four working days across the break removes the February collision that families in this belt describe every year.

The spring break sits close to the papers and belongs to timed practice. Two full papers sat properly, marked against the scheme, with the losses categorised, is worth more than a fortnight of reading notes. It is also the point at which the omissions should be written down: what will not be revised, decided deliberately rather than by running out of time.

The long summer between the two Diploma years is the highest-value break and the one most often wasted. First-year gaps are still cheap to close, and short daily manipulation work across July and August, with a handful of sessions to steer it, changes what the second year can be. Reading ahead instead usually leaves the gap in place with more content stacked on top.

The common objection is that a student needs a rest, and that is fair. The version of break work described here is deliberately small: ten or fifteen minutes a day with a handful of sessions to steer it, which leaves a holiday intact. The alternative is not rest followed by progress; it is rest followed by a term in which the same gap costs marks in every assessment, which is a worse holiday by the time February arrives.

sections.heading: What a maths block costs, by the term you buy it in
paragraphs: The published rates in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500 once travel is counted. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium named end.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list.

The twice-weekly pattern this page recommends costs more per month than a single weekly hour, which is worth stating plainly rather than buried. What it buys is a session structure that matches how fluency is actually built, and it is usually bought for a shorter total period: two months of twice-weekly work rather than two terms of once-weekly work that never quite moves the Paper 1 mark.

The table sets out the cost by the term in which a family starts. The pattern is the same as in every subject and more pronounced here, because mathematics compounds: the manipulation taught in the first term is used in every topic afterwards, so buying it early is both cheaper and more valuable than buying it late.

sections.heading: Limits, permits and claims not made
paragraphs: Three limits belong on a mathematics page. The first concerns assessed work: a tutor teaches the exploration criteria, questions whether the mathematics is sound, and gives feedback on the student's own draft, and does not write, complete or produce any part of it. Pages competing for these searches sell finished internal assessments; that is an academic-integrity breach and the finding lands on the candidate.

The second concerns outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place. What can be promised is a stated target per block, a written review at four sessions, and an honest answer when the target has not moved. Mathematics is unusually measurable, which makes that accountability easier here than in essay subjects and makes its absence less excusable.

The third concerns status. IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status is never used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

On the regulatory side, private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

process.title: Say the route, the level and the paper marks
process.description: 'Analysis HL, second year, Paper 1 a 3 and Paper 2 a 6' is a diagnosis in one line. The split between papers says more than the overall grade does, and it usually names the block before any tutor has looked at a script.

process.title: Agree the slot and the daily work
process.description: Sessions sit at 5.30pm or later, or on a weekend morning, and run sixty minutes. Ten minutes of written drill is set for four of the days in between. The daily work is part of the plan rather than optional homework, because fluency decays within days.

process.title: Diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: A full online session with the proposed specialist, spent on the student's own marked paper and on twenty minutes of non-calculator manipulation. It ends with a written target: a Paper 1 score, a rearrangement speed, a criterion to satisfy. Nothing is committed.

process.title: Work the strong paper less
process.description: Where the split identifies one paper, the block targets it and deliberately leaves the other. That feels uncomfortable and it is what makes an eight-week block produce a visible change rather than an even spread of small improvements.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target is measured on the same paper type, to the same time, against the same scheme. Mathematics makes this comparison clean. If the number has not moved, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes, at no cost and without awkwardness.

whyPoints.title: Built around decay, not coverage
whyPoints.description: Fluency fades within days, so a weekly hour with nothing in between produces a student who arrives each week slightly slower. Two shorter sessions plus ten minutes of daily drill is the pattern that matches how the skill is actually built, and it costs nothing extra to run.

whyPoints.title: The paper split read as a diagnosis
whyPoints.description: A solid Paper 2 with a weak Paper 1 on the Analysis route names the problem precisely: understanding present, manipulation not fluent. Families look at the overall grade and miss it. Reading the split takes five minutes and usually identifies the block without professional help.

whyPoints.title: Exploration run as checkpoints
whyPoints.description: Three decisions at the right times — feasibility, soundness, criterion review — with the student working in between. A weekly slot on an independent piece of mathematical writing tends to produce a student who waits for the session to make progress.

whyPoints.title: Routes matched separately
whyPoints.description: Analysis punishes weak manipulation; Applications punishes outputs produced without interpretation. A tutor strong in algebraic technique is not automatically right for an Applications student whose losses are all in contextual writing, and matching by route is the first filter applied.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for a student home after five
whyPoints.description: Sixty minutes rather than ninety, from 5.30pm or on a weekend morning, because concentration rather than teaching time is the constraint after a commute from Al Barsha or the Ranches. Online delivery is what makes that pattern choosable at all.

whyPoints.title: Measurable targets and stated limits
whyPoints.description: Every block carries a target comparable month to month under the same conditions, reviewed in writing at session four. No grade is promised, no accreditation is claimed, no UAE office exists, and no part of an exploration is produced for a student.

faqs.question: Why does my child seem to get slower at maths between lessons?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is partly a motor skill and it decays within days rather than weeks. A student can understand integration completely on a Tuesday and be measurably slower at it the following Tuesday without having forgotten the concept. That is why a weekly hour alone rarely moves a Paper 1 mark. Ten minutes of written drill on old material, four times between sessions, costs nothing and changes the rate at which everything else sticks.

faqs.question: Can an IB maths tutor come to a house in DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For mathematics the shared screen is arguably the better surface: the tutor reads the working line by line as it appears and can stop at the exact step where the method broke, rather than reading a finished page sideways across a table.

faqs.question: What does a weak Paper 1 with a strong Paper 2 actually mean?
faqs.answer: On the Analysis route it is the clearest diagnostic signal available. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so it removes the machine that was concealing slow manipulation. Understanding is present; fluency is not. That student needs daily drill and non-calculator practice rather than more teaching, and the improvement is measurable on a comparable paper within about six weeks. The reverse pattern points at calculator procedure and accuracy conventions instead.

faqs.question: How long should a maths session be after a long school run?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes. Secondary students in DAMAC Hills generally arrive home after five, and a ninety-minute session at that hour produces perhaps forty minutes of usable work plus fatigue that damages willingness to attend the next one. Two sixty-minute sessions a week, with short drill on the days between, produces more than one long weekly session and is more resilient when something in the week moves.

faqs.question: What should the daily ten minutes of maths actually contain?
faqs.answer: Old material, repeated for speed rather than for understanding. Three rearrangements, two differentiations, one integral — things already taught. Students resist it because it feels like going backwards, and that is exactly the point: it stops the backwards slide that otherwise happens between sessions. Keep it written rather than mental, rotate which operation leads, and do not extend it. Ten minutes done four times beats forty minutes done once.

faqs.question: Does the exploration need a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: No, and a weekly slot often makes it worse by training the student to wait for the session. It needs three checkpoints: feasibility of the topic, soundness of the mathematics once drafted, and a criterion-by-criterion review of the draft. Between those the student works alone, which is what an independent piece of mathematical writing is meant to develop. Roughly half the marks concern process and communication rather than mathematics.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should be chosen, and when?
faqs.answer: Decide in the term the option form is due, on two pieces of evidence. First, manipulation assessed under non-calculator conditions, which predicts Analysis performance better than any school report. Second, the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses under consideration, because some programmes in mathematics, engineering and physics expect Analysis by name. Neither route is the easy one: Analysis punishes weak manipulation, Applications punishes outputs with no interpretation.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 3 always the lowest mark in a first mock?
faqs.answer: Because almost nobody has sat one to time before. Paper 3 presents two extended tasks leading a candidate through unfamiliar mathematics, and the skill it tests is tolerance for the first ten minutes when nothing is obvious. That is exposure, not content. Attempting Paper 3 style tasks to time early in the second Diploma year, then again a few weeks later, moves a Higher Level profile more than any additional topic teaching at the same point.

faqs.question: How should the summer between the two Diploma years be used for maths?
faqs.answer: Short daily manipulation work across July and August, with a handful of sessions to steer it, aimed at the two topics the student already knows they never understood. It is the largest block of uncommitted time in the two years and it sits exactly where first-year gaps are still cheap to close. Reading ahead into new content instead usually leaves the gap in place with more material stacked on top of it.

faqs.question: Can the calculator really be costing marks?
faqs.answer: Regularly, and almost always through syntax rather than mathematics: a regression read from the wrong field, a distribution function given its arguments in the wrong order, an answer left in a display format the question did not request. Procedures learned once and never repeated are forgotten within weeks, so this is maintenance rather than a single lesson. One session on the exact model the school uses, revisited periodically, removes a recurring loss.

faqs.question: Is one term enough to fix slow algebra?
faqs.answer: Usually a term or two, and only with short frequent practice rather than long sessions. Fluency is built by repetition, so the limiting factor is how many days the student practises rather than how many hours a tutor teaches. That is also why the cost of fixing it rises sharply as the course progresses: in the first Diploma year there are enough weeks; in the final term there are not, and the honest plan becomes triage.

faqs.question: What does twice-weekly maths cost compared with once a week?
faqs.answer: More per month and often less in total, because it is bought for a shorter period. Using Bestimate's published monthly estimates, weekly hour-long sessions run AED 600 to 1,200 at the mid band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Two months of twice-weekly work costs more monthly than two terms of weekly work and frequently achieves what the longer arrangement does not, because it matches how fluency is built.

faqs.question: Should the stronger paper be revised at all in a short block?
faqs.answer: Barely, and that discomfort is the point. Where a mock split clearly identifies one paper as the problem, spreading eight sessions evenly across both produces small improvements in each and no visible change in either. Targeting the weak paper and deliberately leaving the strong one is what makes a short block move a number. The omission should be written down so the student follows the plan without guilt about it.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP and the grade looks fine. Is maths help premature?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. MYP marks four criteria out of eight each and converts them by published boundaries, so a student can hold a respectable grade for two years while manipulation stays slow and nothing in the reporting shows it. A block at the end of MYP 4 leaves a full year to build fluency before the Analysis or Applications decision has to be made, which changes what that decision can be rather than only how it goes.

intro.heading: Which IB maths course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that decides whether a maths tutor is useful or merely competent, and a surprising number of DAMAC Hills 2 parents do not know the answer. The IB runs two mathematics courses at two levels each. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, at Higher and Standard Level, is the algebraic and proof-oriented route. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, also at both levels, is the modelling, statistics and technology-oriented route. They are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. They are different syllabuses with different papers.

A tutor who teaches AA HL fluently and is handed an AI SL student will teach correct mathematics in the wrong proportions. They will reach for proof where the course wants a model, and for algebraic manipulation where the course wants a sensible use of the graphical calculator. The student will learn things. They will not necessarily learn the things their paper will ask for. So the first thing we establish, before proposing anybody, is which of the four routes your child is on.

The second question out here is the clock. DAMAC Hills 2 sits along the Al Qudra corridor and almost every Diploma student in the community is driven to school somewhere else — Motor City, Dubai Sports City, or deeper into the city for a specific IB programme. A day ending at half three becomes a 4:30pm arrival home once afternoon traffic on Hessa Street and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road is counted. A tutor who still has to drive here turns that into a half six start with a tired student.

IB Gram removes the travel from both ends. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. So a session can begin at 4:30pm for a Year 12 student, or at 8pm for a Year 13 student who works late anyway and is sharpest once the house is quiet. Both of those are better hours than any visiting arrangement can offer from this community.

The pool matters as much as the hour. Dubai had 387,441 private-school pupils in 2024-25 across 227 schools, with the IB at roughly 7% of enrolment spread across the whole emirate, and only the final two years sitting the Diploma. Narrow that to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and you have a small citywide cohort of students and a smaller group of teachers who have taken that course to final grade. The chance that one of them lives near DAMAC Hills 2 with a free Tuesday evening is not high.

The rest of this page is the detail that makes a maths tutoring decision sensible: how the two courses differ, what each paper is worth, where the marks actually go, what the Exploration is assessed on, and what the Dubai market charges with every figure attributed.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.programmesIntro: IB mathematics runs as a continuum, and the help that works at each stage is different. These are the stages we cover for DAMAC Hills 2 families, with what each actually demands.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Mathematics in the PYP sits inside units of inquiry and is assessed continuously by the class teacher rather than by examination. Number sense, pattern, measurement and the ability to explain a method in words are the real outputs. A child who can compute but cannot explain looks weaker here than their arithmetic suggests.
programmes.countryNote: DAMAC Hills 2 families arriving from a drill-based system often meet this as a shock: the child is quick at calculation and marked down for not showing reasoning. The fix is explanation practice rather than more sums, and it is far cheaper to do at nine than at sixteen.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria on a 0-8 scale: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B rewards generalising from a pattern and justifying it, which is unlike anything in a traditional maths exam, and criterion C marks the quality of mathematical communication rather than the answer.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP criteria are the honest preparation for whichever Diploma maths route follows. Criterion B work maps onto Analysis and Approaches thinking; criterion D maps onto Applications and Interpretation. A student strong in B and weak in D, or the reverse, has already told you something useful about the Year 11 choice.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses at two levels. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic methods, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and the use of technology. Both carry an Exploration worth 20% of the grade. Higher Level adds a third written paper and substantially more content than Standard Level in both courses.
programmes.countryNote: The choice between AA and AI is made at the end of Year 11 and it has consequences for university applications that are not always explained at the time. Some engineering and mathematics degrees specify AA, and some specify Higher Level. Decide against the intended degree rather than against which course looks more comfortable in Year 11.

programmes.name: The IGCSE or MYP to Diploma bridge
programmes.description: The single largest step in IB mathematics. A student arriving from IGCSE Extended or MYP maths into AA HL meets a jump in algebraic demand, abstraction and pace within the first term. Students who were comfortable at 16 can be genuinely struggling by November of Year 12, which is a curriculum step rather than a decline in ability.
programmes.countryNote: We see more DAMAC Hills 2 enquiries at this transition than at any other point. The useful intervention is a short summer or first-term block on algebraic fluency, functions and trigonometric identities, before the Year 12 content has built two storeys on an unstable foundation.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-damac-hills-2.subjectsIntro: These are the IB mathematics routes and components we cover for DAMAC Hills 2 students, with the specific place marks go in each. Availability varies by level and term and is confirmed at the trial lesson.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The most demanding route in IB maths. Proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, vectors, and calculus well beyond Standard Level. Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper that rewards sustained reasoning. Students with small algebraic weaknesses find them exposed within a term rather than a year.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and probability without the HL extensions or Paper 3. Marks are lost most often in calculus application questions and in the unstructured parts of Paper 2 where no scaffold indicates which technique is wanted.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics taken seriously, plus matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, which surprises students who chose AI expecting less abstraction. Paper 3 demands extended modelling with technology. Statistical vocabulary is the commonest gap.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Modelling, descriptive and inferential statistics, financial mathematics and confident calculator use. The usual failure is choosing it as the lighter option and then meeting regression and hypothesis testing without any statistical language to think in.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: The internal assessment, worth 20% of the final grade in every IB maths course. Assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is strong mathematics with no genuine personal engagement, which caps the mark regardless of the algebra.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration techniques, kinematics, related rates and, at HL, differential equations and Maclaurin series. Students can usually differentiate and struggle to recognise which technique a worded problem requires, which is a pattern-recognition gap rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Distributions, correlation, regression, hypothesis testing and, at AI HL, more advanced inference. The marks are in interpretation: a student who can produce a p-value and cannot say what it means about the claim will lose most of the available credit.

subjects.name: Proof and algebraic technique
subjects.description: Induction, contradiction, algebraic manipulation of rational and surd expressions, binomial expansion and identities. This is the foundation layer, and it is where almost every AA student who is struggling in Year 13 actually needs the work rather than in the topic they named.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator technique
subjects.description: Both courses assume fluent use of the permitted technology, and students lose marks daily on avoidable things: wrong window settings, failing to state the model they fitted, or doing by hand what the calculator was there for. This is quick to fix and rarely taught explicitly.

subjects.name: MYP mathematics criteria work
subjects.description: Criterion-by-criterion support against knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Working to the criteria rather than to a general grade is the only honest preparation for either Diploma route.

subjects.name: IGCSE and Additional Mathematics bridging
subjects.description: A short, targeted block on the algebra, functions and trigonometry that AA HL assumes and IGCSE does not fully build. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 covers some of it; students who did not take it arrive with a visible gap.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
paragraphs: This choice is made at the end of Year 11 and it is the most consequential maths decision in the Diploma. It is often made on the wrong basis — which course the student finds more comfortable now, or which their friends are taking — rather than on what the intended degree expects. Reversing it after the first term of Year 12 is possible in some schools and painful in all of them.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route. Proof, functions, calculus, and at Higher Level proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers and vectors. It rewards a student who likes manipulating symbols and following an argument. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling route. Statistics, regression, financial mathematics, and at Higher Level matrices and graph theory. It rewards a student who likes real data and is comfortable with technology.

The pitfall is treating AI as the easy option. It is not easier; it is different. AI Standard Level students who chose it to avoid difficulty regularly meet hypothesis testing and regression with no statistical vocabulary and find it harder than the algebra they were avoiding. AI Higher Level, meanwhile, contains matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, which is a genuine surprise to anyone who picked it expecting less abstraction.

The university question is the one to resolve first. Some mathematics, physics and engineering degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, and many specify Higher Level in a mathematics course. Check the actual published entry requirements of the actual universities your child is considering, including UAE institutions, before the choice is made rather than after. The table below sets out what each route involves so the conversation can be concrete.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Students revise topics. Examiners mark papers. Those are not the same organising principle, and a student who knows the content but has never thought about paper structure will underperform what they know.

Every IB maths route has written papers plus the Exploration at 20%. Higher Level adds a third paper that Standard Level does not sit, and that paper is a different kind of task: longer, less scaffolded, and rewarding sustained reasoning across a single extended problem rather than quick recall across many. Students meet it late in the course and often meet it unprepared, because school practice naturally concentrates on the papers that exist at both levels.

The paper-by-paper losses are consistent. On the non-calculator paper, arithmetic slips and incomplete algebraic manipulation. On the calculator paper, failing to state a model or a method, so the marks for reasoning are unavailable even when the answer is right. On HL Paper 3, abandoning a question after the first unfamiliar part rather than working the later parts that were accessible. Each of those is a technique fault with a specific fix, and none of them is solved by learning more content.
The table below is the structure to plan practice around. The last column is the useful one: it names the thing to actually work on, which is almost never the topic the student says is the problem.

Notation is the quiet one on that list. Marks for correct mathematical communication are available on every component and are lost habitually rather than dramatically: a symbol used without definition, a line of working with no equals sign, an answer given to a precision the question did not ask for. Across a full paper that adds up to a meaningful fraction of a grade boundary, and unlike content it can be fixed in a fortnight.

sections.heading: The Exploration: twenty per cent, and the part nobody coaches properly
paragraphs: A fifth of the final maths grade comes from a piece of independent work, and it is assessed on criteria most students never read carefully. That combination makes the Exploration the single most recoverable block of marks in the course, and also the one most commonly left until it is too late to recover.

The criteria reward presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Note what is not on that list: difficulty for its own sake. A student who takes a topic they genuinely care about and handles it with mathematics appropriate to their course will outscore a student who attempts something ambitious, half understands it, and shows no sign of caring. We see the second pattern constantly, usually from strong students who assumed harder meant better.

Personal engagement is where DAMAC Hills 2 students lose the most. It cannot be added at the end; it has to be visible in the choice of question and in the way the work is conducted. Reflection is the next biggest loss — written as a summary of what was done rather than as genuine evaluation of what the mathematics showed and what its limitations were.

What a tutor can do here is coach and only coach. Help find a topic with real engagement and workable mathematics. Check the mathematical level fits the course. Explain what each criterion asks for and what it is worth. Read a draft the student has written and give feedback against the criteria. What a tutor may not do is write any of it, supply the calculations, rewrite the prose, or edit it to a finish. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own.

sections.heading: Fitting maths sessions into a DAMAC Hills 2 week
paragraphs: Maths is the subject families most often try to tutor at the wrong hour, because it is the one they worry about most and so they book whatever slot is available. That is a mistake with maths specifically, because the work is cognitively dense: a tired student can read a history chapter and absorb something, and cannot follow a calculus derivation at all.

The timetable out here is tight. A school day ending at half three in Motor City or Dubai Sports City means a 4:30pm arrival home once the afternoon traffic is counted; from an inner-city IB school it is closer to five. Because nobody is driving to you, a session can start at 4:30pm, which for a Year 12 student is usually the best available hour. For a Year 13 student the better slot is often 8pm or 8:30pm, ninety minutes long, once the house is quiet and a full paper section plus marking can be done without rushing.

There is a third option that DAMAC Hills 2 families underuse: weekend mornings. Two hours on a Friday or Saturday morning is worth more for maths than three separate weekday hours, because the subject rewards sustained work on one thread. During a term with an Exploration deadline it is often the only honest answer, and it competes with nothing.

What we try to avoid is the slot that moves. A maths arrangement that drifts — cancelled, rescheduled, cancelled — loses continuity faster than any other subject, because each session builds directly on the last. Pick the window, protect it, and plan the Ramadan change deliberately rather than discovering it.

For maths specifically there is a clear place where money is wasted, and it is the bottom band. A budget generalist can genuinely help a Year 8 student with homework. Handed an AA HL student in Year 13, they will teach plausible mathematics that is not the course, and the term will pass pleasantly with no change in the paper performance. That is the most common expensive mistake in this market, and it is expensive precisely because it felt cheap.

sections.heading: The Diploma maths year, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and a maths year planned backwards from there looks different from one planned forwards. Almost everything that decides the grade has an internal school deadline months earlier, and the Exploration is the clearest example: it is worth 20% and it is finished long before any exam revision begins.

One honesty note. The IB's own site blocks automated retrieval, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org. We write about the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publish no specific date. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org, which are the only sources worth planning around. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we use them: Cambridge runs June and November series, with February/March offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

The backwards sequence for maths runs roughly like this. Course and level chosen at the end of Year 11, against the intended degree. Algebraic foundations secured early in Year 12, because everything afterwards sits on them. Exploration topic chosen in the second half of Year 12, while there is still time for it to be a good topic rather than an available one. Exploration drafted and finished to the school's internal deadline. Mocks. Then a final term that is almost entirely paper technique, including HL Paper 3 if the student sits it.

The practical consequence for a DAMAC Hills 2 family is that the best time to start maths tutoring is early Year 12 and the worst is March of Year 13. In March the only thing left to move is technique, which is worth real marks but is a smaller lever than foundations plus Exploration plus technique together.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a mathematics context
paragraphs: The honesty question sounds abstract until it meets an Exploration deadline. Then it becomes very concrete: can the tutor just check these calculations, or rewrite this section, or send a worked version to compare against? The answer is no to all three, and it is worth knowing why before the week it matters.

The permitted ground is wide. A tutor may teach any content in the syllabus. They may explain what each Exploration criterion asks for and what it is worth. They may help narrow a topic until the mathematics is appropriate and the engagement is real. They may read a draft the student has written and say that the notation is inconsistent, that the reflection is a summary rather than an evaluation, or that a step does not follow. All of that is teaching.

What is not permitted is producing the work. Not writing a section. Not supplying the calculations the student then transcribes. Not providing a model Exploration to be adapted. Not editing a draft to a finish so the submitted piece is substantially the tutor's. The student signs a declaration of authorship and the supervisor signs alongside, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice.

This matters more in this search result than it should, because it contains operators selling finished coursework — one advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. We also do not supply IB past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because they belong to the IB. We cite them, link the official source and teach from them.
bullets: Permitted: teaching content, explaining criteria, coaching a topic, feedback on the student's own draft
Not permitted: writing sections, supplying calculations, model Explorations, editing to a finish

sections.heading: What we will not promise about a maths grade
paragraphs: No grade guarantee. Not a 7, not a specific points improvement, not a particular paper score. Anyone offering one in this market is either not serious or is relying on a refund clause nobody reads, and in maths specifically the offer is especially hollow because the variables — the student's prior algebra, how many weeks remain, which paper structure they are meeting for the first time — are not under a tutor's control.

No invented statistics either. No average score achieved by students we have taught, no percentage who improved, no satisfaction figure. Competitors publish numbers like these routinely and almost none states a sample size, a date or a method. A statistic without those three is decoration. We would rather publish nothing than publish decoration dressed as evidence.

No regulator or awarding-body claim. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, has no office or centre anywhere in the UAE, and does not describe tutors as IB examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced — which in practice means we do not describe them that way at all. Examiner status is also not access to marking or boundaries, whatever anyone implies.

What we will say is narrower and more useful. After a diagnostic we will tell you whether the gap is foundations, technique or the Exploration, roughly how long each of those takes to move, and whether the time available is enough. Sometimes the answer is that it is not, and that the better plan is to concentrate on two components rather than three. That is the conversation worth having.

process.title: Tell us the course and the level
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. If you are not sure, the school will confirm it in one email. This single fact determines which specialists are even candidates, and getting it wrong wastes a term on correct mathematics in the wrong proportions.

process.title: Diagnostic on real past-paper questions
process.description: The student works through questions at their own level while a specialist watches, including non-calculator work. This is where the real gap appears, and in maths it is usually underneath the named topic: algebraic manipulation rather than calculus, statistical vocabulary rather than regression.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: Not a sales call and not a different person. The specialist who would continue teaches a full session, and you and your child judge the fit. If the explanation style does not land, nothing has been spent and we propose someone else. In maths, explanation style matters more than in any other subject.

process.title: Set the slot where your child can still think
process.description: Around the DAMAC Hills 2 school run and prayer times, usually 4:30pm for Year 12 and 8pm for Year 13, with weekend mornings as the alternative. Maths does not survive a tired hour, so we would rather propose a weekend block than a weekday slot that will not work.

process.title: Review by paper and by criterion
process.description: Every few weeks the tutor reports against something checkable: which paper technique is now reliable, which Exploration criterion the draft is weak on, whether the algebraic foundation has moved. If nothing has shifted, that is where the plan or the tutor changes.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the route, not to the word maths
whyPoints.description: AA HL, AA SL, AI HL and AI SL are four different jobs. We establish which one before proposing anybody, because a tutor teaching the wrong route will teach correct mathematics in the wrong proportions and the paper will not reward it.

whyPoints.title: We look underneath the named topic
whyPoints.description: Students name calculus; the diagnostic usually finds algebra. Students name regression; it is usually the absence of statistical vocabulary. Starting the plan from a marked past paper rather than from the school report is what makes the difference measurable.

whyPoints.title: The Exploration treated as 20% of the grade
whyPoints.description: Because it is. We coach topic choice early, when it can still be a good topic, and give criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft. The mathematics and the writing stay theirs, and we state that boundary plainly rather than leaving it vague.

whyPoints.title: Sessions at an hour maths can survive
whyPoints.description: A calculus derivation cannot be followed by a tired student, so we plan from your school's finish time rather than from our availability. No travel either side means a 4:30pm start exists at all, which from the Al Qudra corridor it otherwise would not.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with their publisher and date
whyPoints.description: Three of six ranking competitors publish no price and two quote US dollars. Every rate here names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and none is presented as an IB Gram price.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, no decorative numbers
whyPoints.description: No promised grade, no improvement percentage, no satisfaction figure, no claimed regulator approval, and no home visits anywhere in the UAE. What you get instead is a diagnostic verdict that may say the time available is not enough.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child takes AA or AI maths?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, and ask for the level as well — the full answer is one of four: Analysis and Approaches Higher or Standard, or Applications and Interpretation Higher or Standard. It is usually on the subject choice form from Year 11 and on the Diploma timetable. It matters because the two courses have different syllabuses and different papers, so a tutor matched to the wrong one teaches correct mathematics in proportions the paper will not reward. We will not propose a tutor before we know which of the four it is.

faqs.question: Should we pick Applications and Interpretation because it looks lighter?
faqs.answer: No, it is different. AI emphasises modelling, statistics, financial mathematics and the use of technology, where Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebra, proof and calculus. Students who choose AI to avoid difficulty frequently find hypothesis testing and regression harder than the algebra they were avoiding, because they arrive with no statistical vocabulary. AI at Higher Level also contains matrices, graph theory and complex numbers, which surprises almost everyone who picked it expecting less abstraction. Choose on what the intended degree expects, not on which looks lighter.

faqs.question: Which maths route do universities expect from an IB student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the course and you must check the published requirement rather than rely on general advice. Many mathematics, physics and engineering degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, and many specify Higher Level in a mathematics subject. Business, social science and design programmes are generally comfortable with Applications and Interpretation. UAE institutions publish their own requirements and they are not identical to UK or US ones. Do this before the Year 11 choice is confirmed, because reversing it after a term of Year 12 is painful where it is possible at all.

faqs.question: How much does the Exploration count towards a DAMAC Hills 2 student IB maths grade?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in every IB maths course at both levels. It is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest pattern we see is a strong student attempting ambitious mathematics they half understand, with no visible personal engagement, scoring below a student who handled a modest topic they genuinely cared about correctly. Difficulty is not on the criteria list. Because it is worth a fifth of the grade and is finished before exam revision begins, it is the most recoverable block of marks in the course.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check the calculations in my child's Exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor can tell your child that a step does not follow, that notation is inconsistent, or that a conclusion is not supported by the working — feedback on a draft the student has written is permitted and useful. What a tutor may not do is supply the calculations, write a section, provide a model Exploration to adapt, or edit the piece to a finish so it is substantially theirs. The student signs an authorship declaration and the supervisor signs alongside, and the IB withdraws awards for malpractice, so the distinction is practical rather than procedural.

faqs.question: Why does my child suddenly struggle with maths in Year 12?
faqs.answer: Usually because the step from IGCSE Extended or MYP maths into Diploma maths — especially Analysis and Approaches Higher Level — is the largest jump in the whole curriculum, in abstraction, pace and algebraic demand all at once. A student who was comfortable at sixteen can be genuinely lost by November of Year 12, and that is a curriculum step rather than a decline in ability. The effective intervention is a short block on algebraic fluency, functions and trigonometric identities, done early, before the Year 12 content builds two storeys on it.

faqs.question: What is HL Paper 3 and why do students lose marks on it?
faqs.answer: It is the third written paper that only Higher Level candidates sit, and it is a different task from the other two: longer, less scaffolded, rewarding sustained reasoning across a single extended problem in Analysis and Approaches or extended modelling in Applications and Interpretation. The commonest loss is abandoning the whole question after the first unfamiliar part, when the later parts were accessible. Schools meet it late because practice naturally concentrates on the papers both levels sit, so it benefits from explicit, separate preparation.

faqs.question: What time should a maths session be scheduled from DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: At an hour the student can still think in, which for maths matters more than for any other subject — nobody follows a calculus derivation while tired. For Year 12 that is usually 4:30pm, straight off the school run from Motor City or Dubai Sports City, which only exists as an option because nobody is driving to you. For Year 13 it is often 8pm for ninety minutes, once the house is quiet and a full paper section plus marking fits without rushing. Weekend mornings suit maths better than scattered weekday hours.

faqs.question: Is there an AA Higher Level specialist living near DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Frequently not. The IB is roughly 7% of Dubai's 387,441 private-school pupils spread across the whole emirate, only the final two years sit the Diploma, and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is one route of four. The pool of people who have taught it to final grade is therefore small citywide, and most of them are serving school teachers whose permit code of conduct bars tutoring students enrolled at their own school. Online matching removes distance from a problem where distance was never the binding constraint.

faqs.question: What do IB maths tutors charge in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026: budget online from AED 33-65 an hour (Tutopiya, EdFlik), qualified online subject tutors AED 150-300 with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200, IB specialists AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase at AED 270, in-home visits AED 180-500 including travel, and BartyED at AED 650 premium. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work. Those belong to the providers named. We quote after the free trial, because route, level and weeks remaining change the answer.

faqs.question: Where is maths tutoring money most often wasted here?
faqs.answer: In the bottom band, applied to the top of the course. A budget generalist at AED 33-65 an hour can genuinely help a Year 8 student with homework. Handed an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student in Year 13, the same tutor will teach plausible mathematics that is not the course, and a term passes pleasantly with no change in paper performance. It felt cheap, which is exactly what makes it the most expensive mistake available in this market. The second commonest waste is paying an in-home travel premium for presence rather than course knowledge.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start IB maths support?
faqs.answer: Early Year 12, because that is when foundations, Exploration and technique are all still movable. Everything in the Diploma maths year sits on algebraic fluency, so securing that first makes the rest cheaper. The Exploration topic should be chosen in the second half of Year 12, while it can still be a good topic rather than an available one. By March of Year 13 the only remaining lever is paper technique, which is worth real marks but is a smaller lever than all three together. We will say so rather than imply otherwise.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover maths and physics for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and there is a real argument for it in these two subjects specifically: the algebraic and graphical demands overlap heavily, and a tutor who sees both can stop a student from treating them as unrelated. It also lets one person weigh a Physics Internal Assessment deadline against a maths mock instead of two tutors each optimising for their own subject. What we will not do is stretch a tutor across subjects they do not genuinely teach to save you a second match.

faqs.question: Can any tutor promise my child a top grade in IB maths?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. The variables that decide a maths grade — prior algebraic fluency, how many weeks remain, whether the student has ever been taught paper technique, whether the Exploration was started early — are not all under a tutor's control. We publish no grade guarantees, no improvement percentages, no average scores achieved by students we have taught and no satisfaction figures, because every one of those would need a sample size, a date and a method we could show you. A promise of a specific top grade tells you something about the provider making it.

faqs.question: When do IB exams happen for DAMAC Hills 2 students?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no specific IB date, and the reason is worth stating: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, and we will not put an unverified date in front of a family that will plan around it. Get exact dates from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. For IGCSE siblings, Cambridge runs June and November series, with February/March offered to India only, and Pearson runs May/June and November.

intro.heading: Mathematics is the subject where timing is everything
paragraphs: Deira families come to IB Mathematics with one of four problems, and all four are really about the calendar. A student is in the wrong course and it is nearly too late to move. An exploration has no viable topic and the draft date is in three weeks. A mock paper came back with a 3 and the real session is in two terms. Or the content stopped making sense somewhere in the first year and nobody noticed until the second. Each needs a different plan, and the only way to pick the right one is to know what week of the Diploma you are in.

The structure of the subject makes timing matter more here than anywhere else in the Diploma. Mathematics is cumulative in a way History is not: a gap in functions in the first term of DP1 is still costing marks in Paper 2 eighteen months later, because every later topic assumes it. The exploration — the internally assessed piece worth a fifth of the grade — has to be topic-settled roughly a year before submission if it is to have enough mathematical substance to score well. And the two course routes diverge early, so the decision between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is effectively made before the Diploma begins.

There is also a local dimension. Deira is dense apartment housing north of the Creek with two Metro lines running through it, and most Diploma students here travel across the water to Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City for school, arriving home around 4pm to 4:30pm. The IB accounts for roughly 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment against 37 per cent for the UK curriculum, so Mathematics specialists who have actually taught Higher Level Analysis and Approaches are not thick on the ground in any single district, and they are thinner in this one.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a mathematics session that format is not a compromise: working on a shared whiteboard where both people write, with the previous session's annotated working saved and retrievable, suits the subject better than a single sheet of paper on a kitchen table.

What follows is the subject on a timeline. The exploration counted backwards from submission. The course decision and when it closes. Paper structure and weightings at both levels, with the calculator rules, because families routinely do not know them. What eight weeks before a mock can and cannot achieve. A table of where marks are actually lost, topic by topic. What the Dubai market charges, with sources. And the honesty boundary on the exploration, because it is the piece of coursework most often outsourced in this subject.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-deira.programmesIntro: Two routes, two levels and a core piece of coursework. The combination a student is on determines what the calendar looks like for them, so establish it before anything else.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebraic, proof-oriented route. Functions, calculus, trigonometry and, at Higher Level, substantial additional content including a third examination paper. Standard Level sits a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper. It is the usual prerequisite for engineering, physics and quantitative economics degrees.
programmes.countryNote: Deira students heading for engineering at a UAE or overseas university are frequently told they need this route and told late. Check the entry requirements of two or three target courses before DP1 begins, because some universities specify Analysis and Approaches by name.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling and statistics route, with heavier technology use throughout and calculators permitted in both papers. Suits business, design, medicine-adjacent and social science pathways. Higher Level adds content and a third paper in the same pattern as Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: This is not an easier course; it is a different one, and treating it as a downgrade produces students who are poorly placed for a quantitative degree. A small number of regional and international universities accept it for courses others restrict to Analysis and Approaches, so verify course by course.

programmes.name: The mathematical exploration
programmes.description: An internally assessed piece of individual mathematical work carrying 20 per cent of the final grade in both routes and at both levels. It is marked on criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: This is the single most commonly outsourced piece of work in the Diploma and the one with the clearest malpractice exposure. A tutor may question a topic, teach the mathematics and mark a draft against criteria; a tutor may not write it. The section further down this page states the line precisely.

programmes.name: Higher Level, in either route
programmes.description: Additional content on top of the Standard Level syllabus, materially more timetabled teaching, and a third examination paper. The weighting shifts: at Standard Level the two papers carry 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20; at Higher Level the three papers carry 30, 30 and 20 with the exploration at 20.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm the weightings for your child's cohort with their teacher, since subject guides are revised periodically. Higher Level specialists are the scarcest mathematics tutors in Dubai, so a Deira family needing one should request weeks before the need becomes urgent.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on the timetable and about eight distinct problems in practice. Below are the topic areas Deira students most often need help with, and when in the two years each tends to surface.

subjects.name: Functions and graph transformations
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Taught early in DP1 and assumed by everything afterwards, which makes it the highest-leverage repair in the whole course. Students who cannot move fluently between a function, its graph and its transformations lose marks in calculus, trigonometry and modelling questions without ever recognising the common cause.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Rules of differentiation are learned quickly; the application to optimisation and kinematics is where marks go. Written justification is assessed, so a correct derivative with no statement of what it represents scores below a correct derivative that is interpreted. Surfaces in DP1 term two and never leaves.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.levels: AA SL and HL; AI HL
subjects.description: The hardest topic in Analysis and Approaches for most students, because it rewards pattern recognition rather than procedure. Higher Level adds substitution and parts, and the step up is steep. Best addressed with a term of weekly work rather than a late block.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and identities
subjects.description: Identities, equations and, at Higher Level, compound angle work. Non-calculator Paper 1 questions in Analysis and Approaches concentrate marks here, and students who have always leaned on a calculator discover the gap in their first mock rather than before it.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Heavier in Applications and Interpretation, where it carries much of the course. Marks are lost in interpretation rather than calculation: a correct regression line with no comment on validity, or a hypothesis test with no conclusion in context. Highly improvable in a short block.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and exponentials
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Compact, formulaic and frequently the easiest marks on a paper to recover, because the question types repeat across sessions. A good target for a student who needs visible progress quickly, since a few sessions can reliably convert near-misses into full marks.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometry
subjects.levels: AA HL; AI SL and HL
subjects.description: Conceptually demanding and often taught late, which means it is still unfamiliar when mocks arrive. Diagram discipline carries real marks, and students who attempt vector questions without drawing lose them systematically.

subjects.name: Modelling with technology
subjects.description: Central to Applications and Interpretation: selecting a model, fitting it, and judging whether it is appropriate. Students treat the calculator output as the answer rather than the evidence, which is exactly the habit the mark scheme penalises.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: An extended problem-solving paper at Higher Level, worth 20 per cent, which rewards sustained reasoning across a long structured question rather than topic recall. It needs its own practice, and students who revise topics without ever attempting a full Paper 3 are unprepared for it.

subjects.name: The exploration itself
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade for a piece of individual work, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Topic feasibility is the whole game: a topic with too little mathematical substance cannot score well no matter how well it is written.

sections.heading: The exploration, counted backwards from submission
paragraphs: The exploration carries 20 per cent of the mathematics grade and is the piece of the course most often left too late. It is not a long document, which misleads families into thinking it is a short job; what it needs is a topic with enough mathematical substance to show genuine engagement, and that cannot be manufactured in a fortnight.

The timeline that works runs roughly a year. Topic brainstorming in the second term of DP1, when the student has seen enough of the syllabus to know what mathematics they can actually handle. A question agreed and tested for feasibility by the end of DP1 — tested meaning somebody has checked that the mathematics required is within reach and substantial enough to score. The mathematics itself done over the summer between the two years, when there are no competing deadlines. A complete draft early in DP2 term one, before university applications take over the autumn. Then feedback, revision and the school's internal submission date.

The internal date is the one that binds, and it is set by the teacher who has to mark and moderate, so it falls well before any external window. Ask the Diploma coordinator for it in writing at the start of DP1 and put it on a wall calendar. Families who track only the external submission consistently find they have three weeks less than they thought.

What goes wrong, in order of frequency: a topic chosen for interest with insufficient mathematics in it; a topic requiring mathematics the student has not yet met and will not meet in time; data that cannot support the analysis proposed; and a draft written without the criteria open, which loses marks on communication and reflection that have nothing to do with the mathematics. All four are preventable, and all four are prevented by one session early rather than three late.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and when that closes
paragraphs: This is the decision with the longest consequences in Diploma mathematics and it is usually made in a single conversation before DP1 begins, often on the wrong basis. The wrong basis is which course looks easier. The right basis is what the student's intended degree requires and which kind of mathematics they actually do well.

Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with a non-calculator paper at Standard Level, and it is the route most commonly specified for engineering, physics and quantitative economics. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics-led with technology permitted throughout, and it suits business, design and several social science pathways. Some universities name Analysis and Approaches explicitly in their entry requirements, which is why the check has to be course-specific rather than general.

The practical closing date is the start of DP1, because the two syllabuses diverge quickly and a student who moves after a term has missed foundational material in whichever course they transfer into. Schools will sometimes permit a move during the first term; after that it becomes a question of whether the student can self-teach the gap, and the answer is usually no.

The best early evidence of fit, for a student still in MYP 5 or Year 11, is their performance on investigation and pattern-generalisation tasks against their performance on procedural ones. A student who finds and justifies a general rule well is suited to Analysis and Approaches; one who applies named techniques accurately to real contexts and interprets the result is suited to Applications and Interpretation. Ask the current teacher for that read rather than for an overall grade.

sections.heading: Paper structure, weightings and the calculator rules
paragraphs: Families routinely do not know how their child's mathematics grade is assembled, which makes it impossible to judge whether tutoring is targeting the right thing. The structure is worth learning once, and it is the same in both routes.

At Standard Level a student sits two papers, each carrying 40 per cent, with the exploration carrying the remaining 20. At Higher Level there are three papers, carrying 30, 30 and 20 per cent, with the exploration again at 20. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended problem-solving paper rather than a topic test, which means it rewards sustained reasoning across a long structured question. In Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 2 with one; in Applications and Interpretation, technology is permitted throughout. Confirm the precise weightings for your child's cohort with their teacher, since subject guides are periodically revised.

Three consequences follow for a revision plan. First, the exploration is worth as much as a whole paper at Higher Level, which is why leaving it until the last term is irrational however urgent the examination feels. Second, non-calculator fluency in Analysis and Approaches is not optional: a student who has always had technology available will lose marks across a fifth of the course unless that is practised deliberately. Third, Paper 3 needs its own preparation, and a student who revises topics without attempting a complete Paper 3 under timed conditions will meet the format for the first time in the real session.

The table lays it out. Use it to check what your child's tutoring is actually aimed at: if a Higher Level student is being taught topics and has never sat a Paper 3, a fifth of the grade is going unaddressed.

sections.heading: What eight weeks before a mock can achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is roughly a Dubai school term and it is the window most families actually buy. It is enough to do one thing properly in mathematics and not enough to do three, so the choice of the one thing is the whole decision.

What eight weeks reliably achieves: one topic area repaired from the ground up, or one examination behaviour trained to the point of being automatic. Repairing functions and graph transformations in eight weeks is realistic and pays across the rest of the course. Training a student to show working in a form the mark scheme can credit is realistic and recovers marks immediately. Building non-calculator fluency for Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is realistic if it is the only target. Getting a Higher Level student through four complete Paper 3 attempts with full marking is realistic and almost nobody does it.

What eight weeks does not achieve: covering a year of missed content, raising every topic a little, or rescuing an exploration whose topic has no mathematics in it. Families who ask for all three get a tutor who skims, and skimming in mathematics produces a student who recognises everything and can do nothing. If the gap is genuinely a year wide, the honest advice is to pick the two topic areas with the heaviest examination weighting and accept the rest.

The sequencing that works inside eight weeks: two sessions diagnosing from the last marked paper, four teaching and drilling the single target, and two applying it under timed conditions. The last two are the ones families cut when time is short, and they are the ones that convert understanding into marks.

sections.heading: Where marks are actually lost in IB Mathematics
paragraphs: Mark loss in this subject is unusually diagnosable, because the same errors recur across cohorts and because mark schemes award method as well as answer. A student who knows which of these patterns is theirs can fix it; a student revising generally cannot.

The first and largest category is working that the mark scheme cannot credit. A student reaches a correct answer with three lines of unexplained manipulation and scores the answer mark while losing the method marks, or reaches a wrong answer with sound method and scores nothing because the method was never written down. This is a habit, not a knowledge gap, and it is trainable in a few weeks.

The second is interpretation. In Paper 2 and throughout Applications and Interpretation, a correct calculator output with no statement of what it means scores below its potential. Regression lines without a validity comment, hypothesis tests without a conclusion in context, derivatives without a statement of what the rate represents — all common, all cheap to fix.

The third is abandonment on long questions, which is specifically a Paper 3 problem at Higher Level. A structured problem has later parts that can be attempted without completing earlier ones, and students who get stuck at part b and stop leave marks on the table in parts d and e. Teaching a student to move on and come back is worth more than another topic. The table sets the patterns out with what each costs and what fixes it.

sections.heading: What mathematics support costs, and what AED 2,000 buys
paragraphs: A useful way to think about cost is to fix the budget and ask what it buys, since that is the decision a Deira household is actually making. Take AED 2,000. At the published budget band, where Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, that is upwards of thirty hours of generalist supervision. At the qualified band of AED 150 to 300, where Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, it is roughly seven to thirteen hours with a subject tutor. At the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range, it is about four to ten hours with somebody who has taught the course.

Now apply the subject. Thirty hours of generalist supervision will not move a Higher Level mathematics grade, because the skill required is mark-scheme literacy and the ability to test an exploration topic for mathematical substance. Four to ten specialist hours, spent on exploration feasibility and then on marked draft feedback, protects 20 per cent of the grade. Seven to thirteen qualified-band hours is a term of weekly work on one topic area. All three are defensible purchases; only one of them matches each problem.

The band to avoid, in this subject specifically, is the in-home premium. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 350 an hour per Bestimate and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors, with monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Mathematics is the subject where a shared digital whiteboard with saved annotated working is genuinely better than paper, so paying a travel premium here buys a worse working environment as well as a smaller pool. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end, which is rarely necessary below Higher Level.
All figures read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers. They are not IB Gram's prices; we quote after a free trial lesson, before any payment, against a written plan with a total on it.
