sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma mathematics gap
paragraphs: Most Deira Diploma students arrive from an IGCSE background, often from a school in Al Qusais or Bur Dubai, and the transition into Diploma mathematics is steeper than the transition in most other subjects. Knowing what the gap consists of lets a family fix it in DP1 term one, which is the cheapest moment there is.

Three things change. The first is written justification: an IGCSE answer that reaches the right number scores; a Diploma answer is expected to show reasoning a reader can follow and, in many questions, to state what the result means. Students who were strong at IGCSE because they were fast and accurate find this unfamiliar and interpret the mark loss as the course being harder, when it is the expectation that has changed.

The second is algebraic stamina. Diploma questions chain several steps where IGCSE questions chained two, so an algebra base that was adequate becomes a bottleneck. This is why functions and graph transformations is the highest-leverage repair: it is the base that the chaining rests on. The third is the exploration, which has no IGCSE equivalent at all — students arrive with no experience of producing an extended independent mathematical piece, and nobody tells them that it is worth a fifth of the grade.

The practical sequence for a student arriving from IGCSE: diagnose the algebra base in the first weeks of DP1 rather than waiting for a report, build written-justification habits on ordinary homework rather than on special exercises, and start thinking about the exploration in DP1 term two when there is still a year of runway. A family who does those three things in the first year usually needs nothing in the second except mock-driven paper work.

sections.heading: The exploration honesty boundary
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is the most commonly outsourced piece of Diploma coursework, and at least one operation competing for searches like this sells completed internal assessments. The asymmetry is worth stating plainly: the fee is paid once, the malpractice finding attaches to the student, and the possible consequence is the loss of the Diploma. The seller carries nothing.

Legitimate help is substantial and bounded. A tutor may challenge whether a proposed topic contains enough mathematics to score, and whether that mathematics is within the student's reach in the time available. They may teach the mathematics the exploration requires. They may read the assessment criteria with the student so they know what reflection and personal engagement actually mean in marking terms. They may mark a complete draft against those criteria and explain what a supervisor's comment means. They may insist on a timeline and hold the student to it.

A tutor may not write any part of the exploration, draft its sections, dictate sentences for transcription, produce the calculations or graphs for the student to insert, supply data the student did not generate, or edit the text until the final version is the tutor's prose rather than the student's. The working test is whether the student can explain, unprompted, why each step and each sentence is there. If they cannot, it should not be in the document.

This boundary is a genuine differentiator rather than a disclaimer, because the alternative on offer in this search result is a product that puts a student's Diploma at risk. It is also better teaching: a student who has been made to defend their own topic choice and their own reflection has learned something that transfers to the Extended Essay and to a university dissertation. A student handed a finished exploration has learned how to buy one.

sections.heading: Mathematics online, and why the whiteboard matters
paragraphs: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics specifically, the online format is not a trade-off we are apologising for, and it is worth explaining why rather than asserting it.

A mathematics session needs three things visible at once: the question, the student's working, and the correction. On a shared digital whiteboard where both people write, all three are visible, in colour, with the student's own working preserved rather than erased, and the whole board is saved so the next session opens on the last one. A student can be asked to work a question while the tutor watches the pen move, which is the moment the misconception becomes visible. On paper at a kitchen table, the page fills, the earlier working is gone, and nothing is retrievable next week.

The practical gains matter too, especially in Deira. A session does not depend on a tutor crossing the Creek at 5pm. A student who finishes a mock at 11am can take a session at noon. The slot can move to a weekend morning when the flat is quieter, which in dense apartment housing is often the only genuinely quiet academic hour of the week. And because specialists are matched from the whole market rather than from those willing to travel into the district, a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches request can actually be filled.

Where a tutor in the room is better — a young child, a household with no quiet corner, a student who cannot engage with a screen at all — the Dubai market provides it at the rates published above and a family should use it. We would rather be clear about not being that provider than let anyone discover it after paying.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the week
process.description: Analysis and Approaches HL in DP1 term two is a different request from Applications and Interpretation SL three weeks before an exploration deadline. Tell us the route, the level, the year and the next deadline, and the reply can be specific rather than generic.

process.title: Send the last marked paper
process.description: The most recent marked paper is the brief. We read it for pattern rather than score: working not shown, output not interpreted, long questions abandoned, or a genuine content gap. Those four need different work, and the paper usually says which.

process.title: Free trial lesson before payment
process.description: One free trial lesson before any payment, taken with the marked paper open and the exploration topic to hand if there is one. Ask the tutor to mark a page aloud and to say whether the exploration topic has enough mathematics in it; both answers are revealing.

process.title: One target, written down
process.description: The plan names one target — a topic area, an examination behaviour, or the exploration — the school deadline it is aimed at, and the evidence that will show it worked. If the gap is a year wide we will say which two topic areas we would prioritise and which we would accept losing.

process.title: Reviewed on a timed paper
process.description: The review point is a paper sat to time and marked, not a session count. For Higher Level students at least one of those is a complete Paper 3, because a fifth of the grade sits in a format most students never practise.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as 20 per cent
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the mathematics grade sits in a piece of coursework most families leave until the last term. We publish the backwards timeline and will spend an early session testing whether a topic has enough mathematics in it, which is the cheapest protection available.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 actually practised
whyPoints.description: Higher Level students lose marks on an extended problem-solving paper they have usually never sat complete and to time. Our post-mock blocks include full Paper 3 attempts with marking, because revising topics does not prepare anybody for that format.

whyPoints.title: Weightings and calculator rules published
whyPoints.description: Two papers at 40 per cent each at Standard Level, three at 30, 30 and 20 at Higher Level, exploration at 20, with Analysis and Approaches SL Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Families cannot judge whether tutoring is aimed correctly without knowing that.

whyPoints.title: The route decision taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation should be decided against named university requirements and the student's actual mathematical strengths, not against which looks easier. We will say when we think a student is in the wrong course, including when it is too late to move.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources, and what they buy
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names its publisher and is dated October 2026, and the fixed-budget table says what each band actually achieves in this subject. Thirty hours of generalist supervision will not move a Higher Level grade, and we would rather say so.

whyPoints.title: A whiteboard, not a kitchen table
whyPoints.description: Mathematics needs the question, the working and the correction visible at once, preserved between sessions. A shared digital whiteboard does that; a single sheet of paper does not. This is the one subject where the online format is a pedagogical advantage rather than a convenience.

faqs.question: When does my child need to have the maths exploration topic settled?
faqs.answer: By the end of DP1, with brainstorming starting in DP1 term two. The exploration carries 20 per cent of the grade and needs a topic with enough mathematical substance to show genuine engagement, which cannot be manufactured late. The workable timeline is topic ideas in DP1 term two, a question agreed and tested for feasibility by the end of DP1, the mathematics done over the summer between the years, and a complete draft early in DP2 term one before applications take over the autumn.

faqs.question: How much of the IB Mathematics grade is the exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both levels and in both routes, which is as much as a whole examination paper at Higher Level. At Standard Level the two papers carry 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20; at Higher Level the three papers carry 30, 30 and 20 with the exploration again at 20. Confirm the weightings for your child's cohort with their teacher, since subject guides are periodically revised. The practical point stands either way: leaving it until the last term is irrational.

faqs.question: Is it too late to move from Applications and Interpretation to Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Realistically the window is the first term of DP1. The two syllabuses diverge quickly, and a student transferring after that has missed foundational material in the course they are joining, which they would then have to self-teach alongside everything else. Schools sometimes permit an early move. If the window has closed and a target degree specifies Analysis and Approaches, the conversation to have is with the universities about alternatives rather than with a tutor about catching up.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does my child keep scoring badly on it?
faqs.answer: It is an extended problem-solving paper sat only at Higher Level, worth 20 per cent, which presents long structured problems rather than topic-by-topic questions. Students score badly because they revise topics and never attempt a complete Paper 3 under timed conditions, so they meet the format for the first time in the real session. The other common cause is abandonment: getting stuck at an early part and stopping, when later parts are often attemptable independently. Both are fixed by practice with triage, not by more content.

faqs.question: My child reaches the right answers but loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly because the working is not written in a form the mark scheme can credit. IB Mathematics awards method marks as well as answer marks, so three lines of unexplained manipulation to a correct result scores below a fully shown solution, and sound method with an arithmetic slip at the end can still earn most of the marks if it is visible. This is a habit rather than a knowledge gap and is trainable in two to four weeks of deliberate layout practice on ordinary homework.

faqs.question: How important is non-calculator practice for Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Essential at Standard Level, where Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries 40 per cent of the grade. Students who have always had technology available often do not discover the gap until their first mock, by which point it affects a fifth or more of the course. The fix is short daily drills over six to eight weeks rather than long sessions: algebraic manipulation, exact trigonometric values, surds and index work, done frequently enough to become automatic rather than reconstructed each time.

faqs.question: Which single topic is worth repairing first?
faqs.answer: Functions and graph transformations, in almost every case. It is taught early in DP1 and assumed by calculus, trigonometry and modelling, so a weak base there costs marks across several topics while looking like several separate problems. Repairing it from the ground up takes about a term and pays for the rest of the course. A student who cannot move fluently between a function, its graph and its transformations should be working on that before anything else is attempted.

faqs.question: What does AED 2,000 buy in IB maths support in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At published October 2026 rates: roughly thirty to sixty hours of budget online generalist supervision at AED 33 to 65 an hour, about seven to thirteen hours with a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, or about four to ten hours with a specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. The specialist hours spent on exploration feasibility and marked draft feedback protect a fifth of the grade. Thirty hours of generalist supervision will not move a Higher Level grade, whatever it costs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration without it becoming malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may challenge whether a topic has enough mathematics in it and whether it is reachable in the time available, teach the mathematics required, read the assessment criteria with the student, mark a complete draft against them, explain what a supervisor comment means, and enforce a timeline. A tutor may not write or draft any part of it, produce the calculations or graphs, supply data, or edit the prose until it is theirs. The test is whether the student can explain every step unprompted.

faqs.question: What changes between IGCSE maths and Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Three things. Written justification becomes assessed, so a right answer with no visible reasoning no longer scores fully. Algebraic stamina matters more, because Diploma questions chain several steps where IGCSE chained two. And the exploration has no IGCSE equivalent at all, so students arrive with no experience of an extended independent mathematical piece worth a fifth of the grade. Students who were strong at IGCSE because they were fast and accurate feel the first of those most sharply, usually in their first DP1 report.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find a Maths AA HL tutor for a Deira student?
faqs.answer: Up to a week in normal conditions, longer in the weeks around mock season. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists are among the scarcest mathematics tutors in Dubai, because the course contains material no A Level or IGCSE teacher will have taught and because the exploration criteria require someone who has supervised one. If your deadline is tight, say so in the first message; we will give you a date rather than substitute a Standard Level tutor and hope.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come to our apartment in Deira?
faqs.answer: Not from us. All UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. For mathematics the online format is genuinely better: a shared whiteboard keeps the question, the student's working and the correction visible at once and saves the board between sessions, which paper cannot. In-home tutoring exists in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel for families who need that format.

faqs.question: Eight weeks to the mock. What should we target?
faqs.answer: One thing. Eight weeks reliably achieves one topic area repaired properly or one examination behaviour trained to automatic — not three topics raised a little. Pick from the last marked paper: if working is not shown creditably, drill layout; if calculator output is not interpreted, build sentence frames; if long questions are abandoned, do timed papers with triage; if the content gap is real, repair functions first. Keep the final two sessions for timed practice, which is where understanding turns into marks.

faqs.question: Should a Standard Level student use a specialist or a qualified tutor?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor in the AED 150 to 300 band is usually the right fit for Standard Level content teaching, and a strong graduate who has read the syllabus does it well. Where the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 earns its premium is in two specific jobs: deciding whether an exploration topic can score, and diagnosing why a student has plateaued at a particular grade. Buy fewer specialist hours for those two and qualified hours for the content.

faqs.question: Does the Maths route affect university applications in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It can, and the check has to be course by course rather than general. Analysis and Approaches is the route most often specified for engineering, physics and quantitative economics, while Applications and Interpretation suits business, design and several social science pathways. Some institutions name Analysis and Approaches explicitly. Look up the entry requirements for two or three target courses before DP1 begins. Separately, for Ministry of Education equivalency there is no published IB points figure in the sources we can cite, so confirm that on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Is one weekly maths session enough alongside five other subjects?
faqs.answer: In DP1, yes, and it is the best-value purchase in the programme because the content compounds. A Diploma week already contains six subjects, coursework in all of them, Theory of Knowledge, CAS and for a Deira student a long commute each way. One protected weekly mathematics slot through DP1, plus a short exploration block and a post-mock paper block in DP2, is a complete plan. Two weekly subjects is manageable in the final year if the evenings are genuinely free.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-deira.closingHeading: Tell us the route, the level and the next date
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-deira.closingBody: Send the course — Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation — the level, the year of study and the next deadline, along with the most recent marked paper and the exploration topic if there is one. You will get one target, a written plan aimed at a specific school date, and an honest answer about what cannot be achieved in the time available. If the exploration is still open, that is where we would start, because a fifth of the grade is sitting in it. The first lesson is free, before any payment. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video, on a shared whiteboard, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics one-to-one over live video. Each is matched to one course and one level, which is the thing a rate should be buying and the thing most quotes in this market never specify.

intro.heading: The same budget, pointed at four different things
paragraphs: A DIFC family deciding what to spend on Diploma mathematics is working almost blind. Three of the six largest providers in this market publish no price at all. Two quote in US dollars. One publishes an hourly figure in its page copy that contradicts the price range in its own structured data. And none of them tells you the thing that actually determines value, which is that IB mathematics is four separate courses with four different support profiles, and that a fifth of every grade sits in a component most tutoring is never pointed at.

So this page is written from cost. It asks where a Diploma mathematics dirham produces the most grade movement, which components respond fastest to paid hours, why Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is genuinely more expensive to support than Standard Level Applications and Interpretation, and what no budget in this market can buy at any price. The published Dubai rates are here too, each attributed to the provider or publication that stated it and the month it was read, because a sourced band in dirhams is useful on its own whoever you end up buying from.

The structural point first, because everything else follows from it. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation each run at Higher and Standard Level. Standard Level is built around 150 recommended teaching hours and Higher Level around 240. Standard Level students sit two written papers; Higher Level students sit three. All four courses carry the Exploration at twenty per cent. A budget aimed at the wrong course teaches the right mathematics at the wrong level of abstraction, and nobody notices for several weeks.

DIFC adds one cost variable worth naming. The district has no school inside it, so every Diploma student here commutes out, most often towards Al Safa, Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf or Al Barsha. Any in-home arrangement is therefore charging for a drive across central Dubai in the evening peak, into a district with structured parking and tower reception procedures. That is the most expensive logistics in the emirate and it buys nothing that would show on a marked script.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE and we have no office, branch or centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. We publish no UAE rate card on these pages, no satisfaction percentage, no average-score claim and no statistic we cannot support with a number, a date and a method. The free trial lesson exists so a DIFC family can see the teaching before any money is discussed. No IB examination or results date appears on this page either, because ibo.org does not permit automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be right.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: Spending on Diploma mathematics splits across three distinct decisions, each with a different price and a different return. These are the ones in play for a DIFC family.

programmes.name: DP1 mathematics, the cheap year
programmes.description: The year where support is cheapest per unit of effect, because content is being met for the first time and gaps have not compounded. It is also the year in which the course and level decision can still be changed, which is the largest financial variable in the whole two years. A student in the wrong course discovered in October has options; the same student discovered in May of DP2 does not.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma sits under KHDA inspection. A DIFC family's DP1 student commutes to campuses in Al Safa, Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf or Al Barsha, and the short westward run means a 4pm session is genuinely achievable here, which is the cheapest hour to secure because the rest of the emirate is competing for 5pm to 7pm.

programmes.name: DP2 mathematics, the expensive year
programmes.description: Where most families actually spend, and where each dirham buys less. Content teaching is complete, the Exploration deadline has usually passed, predicted grades have been issued, and the work is converting existing knowledge into marks under time pressure. That is valuable and it is narrower than it sounds, which is why a DP2 budget should be sized as a block rather than a retainer.
programmes.countryNote: DP2 in Dubai contains the mock window, the university application cycle and the predicted-grade decision, all before the May session. For a DIFC family the practical consequence is that DP2 evenings are the most contested of the two years and the slots that hold for a full term are 4pm, after 7.30pm and weekend mornings.

programmes.name: The Exploration, bought separately
programmes.description: Twenty per cent of the grade in all four courses, assessed on five criteria out of twenty marks. It is the component where a small number of paid hours produces the largest proportional movement, because most students approach it without having read the criteria. It is also the component with the hardest boundary: a tutor may explain, discuss and give feedback, and may not write, draft or complete any part of it.
programmes.countryNote: The Exploration deadline is set internally by the school and typically falls well before the examination term, which means it competes with content teaching rather than following it. Confirm your own school's internal date, because it determines when this spending is useful and when it is too late to be.

programmes.name: Before DP1: the IGCSE and MYP foundation
programmes.description: The cheapest point in the entire sequence and the one almost nobody buys. Extended tier Cambridge 0580 or Higher tier Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 is the realistic prerequisite for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; Additional Mathematics is better preparation again. A term of algebraic fluency work before DP1 costs a fraction of two years of catch-up afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A wider sixth-form choice makes the IGCSE mathematics tier more consequential rather than less, because more doors are open to be closed by it.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.subjectsIntro: Not every part of a Diploma mathematics course responds equally to paid hours. The list below runs roughly from the best to the worst value for a constrained budget, which is a different ordering from the one a syllabus would give.

subjects.name: Mark-scheme literacy
subjects.description: Method marks, accuracy marks, reasoning marks and follow-through. The best value item in the whole course: three or four sessions, and it recovers marks the student was already earning mathematically and discarding on the page. A bare wrong answer scores nothing even with a perfect unwritten method, which is the mechanism nobody explains.

subjects.name: Three-significant-figure discipline
subjects.description: Answers given to three significant figures unless the question states otherwise. A correct method followed by an over-rounded answer loses the accuracy mark with the mathematics entirely right. Across a full paper this is several marks, it costs about two weeks of deliberate practice, and it is the cheapest grade movement available anywhere in the Diploma.

subjects.name: The Exploration criteria
subjects.description: Five criteria, twenty marks, and most students have never read the descriptors. A small number of hours spent on what each criterion actually rewards, plus a topic-viability conversation before weeks are invested, produces the largest proportional movement per dirham in the course. Confirm the current descriptors with the school.

subjects.name: Paper 1 non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: No graphical display calculator is permitted in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, which carries forty per cent at Standard Level and thirty at Higher. Students who revise with a calculator are practising an unavailable skill. Rebuilding by-hand fluency is six to ten weeks, which is a real cost but a well-defined one.

subjects.name: Command-term reading
subjects.description: Hence is an instruction to use the previous part, not a transition word; write down means no working is wanted; show that constrains the method. Teaching a student to read these as instructions is short work with a disproportionate effect across a whole paper, which makes it high value per session.

subjects.name: Higher Level Paper 3 technique
subjects.description: Two extended multi-part problems building towards an unfamiliar result. It rewards reading the whole question first and using earlier parts in later ones, which is technique rather than knowledge. Moderate cost because it needs real papers worked to time, and high value because a fifth of the grade is usually unpractised.

subjects.name: Logarithms, exponents and binomial expansion
subjects.description: Students can state the laws and cannot apply them in reverse, and the binomial general term is misremembered with negative or fractional indices. A genuine teaching block rather than a technique fix, so the cost is weeks rather than sessions, but the marks are reliable and recur every series.

subjects.name: Radian measure and calculator mode
subjects.description: A calculator left in degree mode produces plausible wrong answers that nothing flags, so students repeat the error across a whole paper. Checking mode is a habit, not a skill, which makes this one of the cheapest repairs in the course and one of the most commonly ignored.

subjects.name: Calculus technique at Higher Level AA
subjects.description: Integration by substitution and by parts, implicit differentiation, differential equations. The genuinely expensive part of IB mathematics to support, because the difficulty is in choosing the approach rather than executing it, and that judgement is built over weeks of worked problems rather than taught in a session.

subjects.name: Statistics in Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Substantial statistical content that Analysis and Approaches students never meet, including hypothesis testing. Expensive to support not because it is hard but because the specialist pool is the narrowest of the four courses, which affects availability and therefore what a family ends up paying.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator skill
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections, working with distributions and regression functions. Each is worth marks and students who use the device only for arithmetic leave them behind. Low cost to teach, rarely taught, and almost never the thing a family thinks they are buying.

subjects.name: General content revision
subjects.description: Listed last deliberately. Open-ended content revision with no diagnosis behind it is the lowest-value purchase in this market, because it spends paid hours on material the school is already covering and a textbook already contains. It is also what most untargeted weekly retainers quietly become.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.regionsTitle: DIFC and the journey an in-home premium pays for
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.regionsIntro: The in-home rate in this district is priced against a specific drive. These are the directions a DIFC Diploma family travels, with what each does to the cost and to the usable evening.

regions.name: DIFC
regions.note: A financial district with residential towers and no school inside it. Structured parking and tower reception procedures add minutes that are billed inside any in-home hour. The short westward run makes a 4pm session achievable here.

regions.name: Al Safa and Al Wasl
regions.note: The nearest established cluster west of the canal, fifteen to twenty minutes outside peak. The cheapest direction in time terms and the one that makes the early session slot genuinely usable.

regions.name: Sobha Hartland
regions.note: Creek-side and home to North London Collegiate School Dubai and Hartland International School. Five to twelve minutes from DIFC outside peak, which is the shortest Diploma school run available in the central corridor.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf
regions.note: Home to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai and a genuinely mixed curriculum catchment. Confirming the exact IB maths course a student is enrolled on matters more here than anywhere else nearby before money is committed.

regions.name: Downtown Dubai
regions.note: Immediately adjacent and operationally identical for school-run purposes. A tutor driving from Downtown to DIFC in the evening peak is charging a premium for a journey short in distance and long in minutes.

regions.name: Al Quoz
regions.note: Several campuses inside a district that is slow to cross in the evening. Later arrival home, a shorter usable evening, and therefore a higher effective cost per usable hour.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Umm Al Sheif
regions.note: A longer run west along Sheikh Zayed Road to several established IB campuses. The highest travel component any DIFC in-home arrangement would attract and the clearest case of paying for logistics.

regions.name: Business Bay
regions.note: One canal crossing away, also without a school inside the district. DIFC and Business Bay face the same thin local specialist pool for any single IB maths course and level.

schoolClusters.city: Sobha Hartland, Al Jaddaf and the Creek side
schoolClusters.note: The closest Diploma provision to DIFC and the shortest return journeys, which is the one place where an in-home arrangement would carry a genuinely modest travel component. Mixed curricula, so the course must be confirmed rather than assumed.
schools: GEMS Our Own Indian School, Al Quoz

schoolClusters.city: Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah
schoolClusters.note: The established cluster west of the canal, where a large share of DIFC's sixth-form students sit their Diploma or A Levels. Fifteen to thirty minutes depending on the hour, with the return slower than the outbound run.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha, Al Quoz and the western corridor
schoolClusters.note: The longest journeys from DIFC and therefore the highest travel component in any in-home quote. Also the widest spread of courses and levels, which makes a generic rate quote least meaningful in this direction.

modes.title: A short high-yield block
modes.description: Six to ten sessions aimed at the items that move fastest: mark-scheme literacy, rounding discipline, command-term reading, calculator mode and the Exploration criteria. None of these is content, all of them are worth marks on every paper, and together they often account for a grade boundary. This is the highest return per dirham available in Diploma mathematics and almost nobody buys it as a distinct product.

It also keeps the course and level decision reviewable during the weeks when it can still be changed, which is the largest single financial variable across the two years.

sections.heading: Where a Diploma mathematics dirham buys the most
paragraphs: The most useful thing a cost-focused page can publish is a ranking of components by grade movement per paid hour, because no provider in this market publishes one and the ranking is not what families assume. The expensive items are not the hard ones. They are the cumulative ones.

At the top sit the mark-type items. Method marks reward a correct approach even where the arithmetic fails; accuracy marks reward the correctly rounded value; reasoning marks reward an explicit justification; follow-through marks let a later answer earn credit from an earlier wrong value. A student who does not know this writes solutions that discard marks while arriving at correct answers. Three or four sessions, and the effect appears in the next marked paper. Nothing else in the course comes close on return.

Then rounding discipline, command-term reading and calculator mode, each a habit rather than a skill, each worth marks on nearly every paper, each repairable in weeks. Then the Exploration criteria, where a handful of hours produces the largest proportional movement in the course because most students have never read the descriptors. Only after all of that do the genuine teaching blocks appear: logarithm manipulation, binomial expansion with awkward indices, and at Higher Level Analysis and Approaches the calculus technique, which is the one genuinely expensive thing in IB mathematics.

The practical consequence for a DIFC family with a limited budget is counterintuitive. Spend the first ten sessions on things that are not mathematics, then reassess. If the marks have moved a grade boundary's worth, which happens more often than this market admits, the expensive teaching block may not be needed at all. A provider that proposes a year of content revision before reading a marked paper is not advising you.

sections.heading: Four courses, four different price profiles
paragraphs: Supply explains more about IB maths pricing in Dubai than quality does. Standard Level Applications and Interpretation has the largest tutor pool of the four courses, because the content is the most widely taught and the most transferable from other systems. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches has a substantially smaller pool, because it requires sustained calculus technique and a Paper 3 nobody teaches casually. Higher Level Applications and Interpretation has the smallest pool of all, because its statistical content is met by almost nobody outside that course.

That is why the same provider can quote the same hourly rate for all four and deliver very different matches. A rate card that does not distinguish between the four courses is telling you that the provider matches on subject rather than on course, which is the single most expensive assumption a DIFC family can make. The right question to any provider is not what they charge but which of the four courses the named tutor has actually taught, and how recently.

The second cost driver is the recommended teaching hours. Standard Level is built around 150 and Higher Level around 240, which is roughly sixty per cent more taught content. A Higher Level student needing content support therefore needs proportionally more of it, and a family budgeting for Higher Level on a Standard Level estimate will run out partway through. Confirm every assessment detail against the current IB subject guide your school holds, because the IB revises them on a cycle.

The third is Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level and carries twenty per cent. It needs real papers worked to time and marked, which is session-expensive rather than explanation-expensive. A Higher Level budget that has not allocated sessions to Paper 3 has left a fifth of the grade unpractised while paying for the other four fifths, and in our experience that is the most common structural error in Diploma mathematics spending.

sections.heading: The Exploration is the cheapest twenty per cent in the Diploma
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of every IB mathematics grade comes from one piece of individual written work, assessed on five criteria for a total of twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation; personal engagement and reflection the smallest. Confirm the current descriptors with your child's teacher, since the IB revises them.

The reason this is the best value component in the course is that most students arrive at it without having read the descriptors, so the gap between their work and the upper bands is informational rather than mathematical. Three to five sessions on what each criterion actually rewards, plus one conversation about whether a proposed topic can support the level of mathematics the course requires, routinely produces more movement than ten sessions of content revision. A fifth of the grade, addressed for the price of a short block.

The predictable losses are worth naming because they are all avoidable. Use of mathematics suffers when the chosen mathematics sits below the course level, and a Higher Level Exploration built on Standard Level statistics cannot reach the top bands however well written. Reflection suffers because students summarise what they did instead of explaining what a result implies and where the model fails. Personal engagement suffers when the topic is generic, since engagement has to be visible in the choices made rather than asserted in an introduction.

The boundary is absolute and it protects your child rather than us. A tutor may explain each criterion, discuss structure, judge topic viability and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write the text, supply sentences, perform the calculations or edit the piece to completion. A malpractice finding falls on the student and can cost the Diploma. There is a provider operating in this market that sells completed Internal Assessments; that offer is the most expensive thing a family can buy here, whatever the invoice says.

sections.heading: DP1 money against DP2 money
paragraphs: The same amount spent in DP1 and in DP2 does different work, and families overwhelmingly spend in DP2. The reasons are understandable: the exams are visible, the predicted grades have landed, and anxiety is a better salesman than foresight. But the arithmetic favours the earlier year substantially.

In DP1, support is consolidation in real time. The topic taught this week is practised with a specialist this week, so gaps never compound. The course and level decision is still reviewable, which means a student in the wrong course can move rather than be supported indefinitely in the wrong place. And the Exploration can be addressed at the proposal stage, when a twenty-minute conversation about topic viability saves a month of misdirected work.

In DP2, content teaching is finished, the Exploration deadline has usually passed, and the available work is conversion: timing, mark types, rounding, Paper 3 technique. That work is genuinely valuable and it is narrower. It also sits in the most contested evenings of the two years, competing with five other subjects, the core, and the university application cycle. A DP2 budget should therefore be sized as a defined block with a review date, not as a retainer that runs to the examination.

One practical consequence for DIFC families specifically. If you are reading this in DP1, the cheapest effective purchase is a short high-yield block now plus a small Exploration block at the proposal stage, and then a decision at six weeks. If you are reading this in DP2, the cheapest effective purchase is a diagnosis from marked papers followed by a block aimed at mark types and Paper 3. In neither case is the answer an open-ended weekly arrangement with no diagnosis behind it, which is nonetheless what most of this market sells.
bullets: DP1 spending is cheaper per unit of effect and keeps the course decision open
DP2 spending is conversion work: narrower, valuable, and best bought as a block
The Exploration is addressable in DP1 and usually past help by DP2
An open-ended retainer with no diagnosis is the default and the worst option

sections.heading: What no budget in this market can buy
paragraphs: A cost page should be honest about the ceiling. Several things are sold in this market that cannot be delivered, and knowing them protects a family more than any rate comparison.

A grade cannot be bought. No provider can guarantee a 7, a points total, a grade improvement or university admission, and any offer of that kind should end the conversation. Nor can access to marking, grade boundaries or unseen paper content be bought: tutors described as examiners are frequently described that way without evidence of current status, and examiner status in any case confers no access to material a student could use. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence, and we do not imply such access exists.

A completed Exploration cannot legitimately be bought, and the fact that it can be purchased somewhere does not make it available to you safely. The consequence of that purchase falls on the student as a malpractice finding and can cost the Diploma. Published syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables also cannot be bought from us, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to all of them, free.

Nor can regulatory standing be bought in the way this market implies. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation, licence, approval or partnership, and we would never describe ourselves as approved by any of them. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises, which we do not operate in the UAE. The phrase that should make a DIFC parent cautious is any claim of regulator approval for tutoring, because it is the easiest claim to make and the hardest to substantiate.
bullets: No grade, points total or admission can be guaranteed by anyone
Examiner status confers no usable access to marking or paper content
A completed Exploration is a malpractice risk carried by the student
No regulator approval for tutoring is held here, and none is claimed

sections.heading: The published Dubai rates, cheapest workable option first
paragraphs: Starting from the bottom is the right order for a cost page, because the useful question is the cheapest option that actually works rather than the best option available. At the budget end of online tutoring, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For a short high-yield block on mark types and rounding, a competent tutor at the lower bands can deliver real movement, provided they can name the course and level they have taught.

Above that, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150 for a qualified subject tutor online. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist tutoring at AED 200 to 450 or more per hour, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium named-tutor end. Monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Each figure belongs to the provider or publication named with it and was read in October 2026.

Where the budget bands stop working is Higher Level content teaching, particularly Analysis and Approaches calculus and Higher Level Applications and Interpretation statistics. Those sit at the specialist end of every published scale, and a Higher Level rate quoted at the budget end is a prompt to ask which of the four courses the tutor has taught and when. The scarcity is real rather than manufactured: the pools for those two courses are genuinely small in this market.

IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card on these pages and does not present any of these figures as ours. For wider budget context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion, with a total package value of AED 2.5 billion.

sections.heading: Provider models compared on what the money covers
paragraphs: Two quotes at the same hourly rate in Dubai are frequently not the same purchase, because the delivery model differs and almost nobody states the inclusions. Comparing models rather than brands is both fairer and more useful, and it is the comparison this market never publishes.

A specialist agency typically matches carefully and charges for it, and the questions worth asking are whether you get the same tutor each week and what the replacement policy is. An international marketplace offers breadth and price competition, with the trade-off that the match is often to a subject rather than to one of the four IB maths courses. A freelance tutor can be excellent value and carries the permit question directly rather than through an intermediary. A tuition centre with premises charges less per hour for a group and cannot diagnose from your child's marked papers or work to their specific course.

The permit position differs by model and is checkable. The MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge for two years and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A tuition centre with premises in Dubai is a different legal arrangement and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

The questions that make any two quotes comparable are short. Is the rate per clock hour or per session of unstated length? Is marking of full timed papers included? Is it the same named tutor each week, and what happens if the match is wrong? What is the cancellation window? Is the first session chargeable? And is the figure quoted the figure that will appear on the invoice? Those six answers, in writing, turn an incomparable set of quotes into a decision.

sections.heading: Coverage, matching and the cheapest honest first step
paragraphs: Coverage for Diploma mathematics is genuinely uneven across the four courses, and saying so is more useful than implying otherwise. Standard Level Applications and Interpretation and Standard Level Analysis and Approaches are reliably covered. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is covered and fills first. Higher Level Applications and Interpretation is the narrowest of the four and may require a wait or an alternative hour. We will not match a Higher Level Applications and Interpretation student to an Analysis and Approaches tutor on the theory that the overlap is sufficient, because at Higher Level it is not.

The scarce resource beyond that is the hour. The 5pm to 7pm Gulf Standard Time window is contested across the whole emirate. DIFC's short westward school run is a real advantage here: a 4pm or 4.30pm start is achievable from the Al Safa and Sobha Hartland clusters, and those are the easiest hours in the central corridor to hold for a full term. Taking an available slot immediately usually beats waiting three weeks for a preferred one.

The cheapest honest first step costs nothing. Confirm which of the four courses your child is enrolled on, from the school's course selection letter or the student's timetable. Ask the school for component-level marks rather than the overall grade. Note the school's internal Exploration deadline. Those three items turn a guess into a diagnosis, and a diagnosis is what decides whether the right purchase is six sessions or sixty.

Then take the free trial. It is a taught session rather than a sales call, no card is required, and it should end with a written note naming which mark types are being lost, which of the common loss points are active, and what the first four weeks would address. That note is useful to you whether or not you book, and it is the only way to compare two providers on something other than their rate card. If the honest conclusion is that your child does not need a tutor, we will say so.

process.title: Establish which of the four courses, free
process.description: The school's course selection letter or your child's timetable names it: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard Level. This determines who can teach them and therefore what the right rate is. A provider who does not ask this question before quoting is matching on subject rather than course.

process.title: Get component marks, not the overall grade
process.description: A 4 built on a weak Paper 1 and a solid Paper 2 needs a different and cheaper block than a 4 built evenly. Most Dubai schools report component marks. These numbers are free and they are what distinguish a ten-session purchase from a sixty-session one.

process.title: Note the school's internal Exploration deadline
process.description: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in the Exploration, and the cheapest point to address it is the proposal stage. If the deadline has passed, that spending option has closed and the budget should go elsewhere. One email establishes which situation you are in.

process.title: A short consultation on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Fifteen to twenty minutes to decide where the budget should point: mark types and technique, the Exploration, or a genuine content block. If the evidence says six sessions rather than a year, or says no tutoring at all, that is what we will tell you.

process.title: A free trial that ends in a written note
process.description: A taught session producing a written list of which mark types are being lost and what the first four weeks would address. No card required. The note is the only basis on which two providers can be compared on something other than their advertised rate.

process.title: Buy a block with a review date, not a retainer
process.description: Agree a session count and a six-week review before the first lesson rather than after the tenth. The quiet renewal of an unreviewed weekly arrangement is how most tutoring money leaves a family in this market, and a date in the diary is the whole defence.

whyPoints.title: Pointed at the components that move
whyPoints.description: The first block targets mark-type literacy, rounding discipline, command-term reading and the Exploration criteria, because those produce the most grade movement per paid hour in Diploma mathematics. Content teaching comes after a diagnosis says it is needed, not before.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here carries the provider or publication that stated it and the month it was read. Three of the six largest providers in this market publish no price, and two quote in US dollars, so a sourced band in dirhams is useful whoever you ultimately buy from.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one of four courses
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and Higher Level Applications and Interpretation diverge enough that an approximate match wastes a term. We match to the course and level and say so when the specialist is not available, rather than substituting quietly.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video to DIFC. No drive across central Dubai in the evening peak, no structured parking, no tower reception time inside the hour. Sessions also move in a message, which matters in a DP2 term full of mocks and deadlines.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the ceiling
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantee, no points promise, no examiner claim without evidence of current status, no implied access to marking or paper content, no completed coursework, and no regulator approval claimed. A page that states its limits is easier to check than one that has none.

whyPoints.title: Willing to recommend spending less
whyPoints.description: Where ten sessions on mark types would do what a year of content revision is being sold for, we will say so. A provider that never recommends a smaller purchase is selling rather than advising, and that is worth noticing before choosing one.

faqs.question: What should a DIFC family spend the first ten IB maths sessions on?
faqs.answer: On things that are not mathematics. Mark-type literacy, meaning method, accuracy, reasoning and follow-through marks, takes three or four sessions and recovers marks a student is already earning mathematically and discarding on the page. Three-significant-figure discipline takes two. Command-term reading takes two. Calculator mode takes one. Together these frequently account for a grade boundary's worth of marks on a Diploma paper. Reassess after that block: if the marks have moved, the expensive content teaching may not be needed at all, which is the cheapest possible outcome.

faqs.question: Why would a tutor charge the same rate for all four IB maths courses?
faqs.answer: Because they are matching on subject rather than on course, which is the most expensive assumption available in this purchase. Standard Level Applications and Interpretation has the largest specialist pool in this market; Higher Level Analysis and Approaches a noticeably smaller one; Higher Level Applications and Interpretation the smallest, because its statistical content is met by almost nobody outside that course. A single undifferentiated rate across all four tells you the provider has not thought about supply. Ask which of the four the named tutor has taught, and how recently.

faqs.question: Is the Exploration worth paying for separately?
faqs.answer: It is arguably the best value purchase in the whole course. The Exploration is twenty per cent of every IB maths grade and is assessed on five criteria for twenty marks, and most students approach it without having read the descriptors. That means the gap between their work and the upper bands is informational rather than mathematical, and three to five sessions on what each criterion rewards plus one topic-viability conversation produces more movement than ten sessions of content revision. Confirm the current descriptors with your child's teacher.

faqs.question: How early does Exploration support stop being useful?
faqs.answer: At the point the topic is locked in and weeks have been invested, the cheapest intervention has already passed. The highest-value conversation happens at the proposal stage, because a topic whose mathematics sits below the level of the course cannot reach the top bands however well the piece is written, and discovering that after four weeks of work is an expensive discovery. Ask your school for the internal deadline and work backwards from it. After the draft deadline, feedback on the student's own text is still legitimate and still useful, but the leverage is much smaller.

faqs.question: Does spending in Year 12 cost less than spending in Year 13?
faqs.answer: Per unit of effect, substantially less. In DP1 the work is consolidation in real time, so gaps never compound; the course and level decision is still reviewable, which is the largest financial variable across the two years; and the Exploration can be addressed at the proposal stage. In DP2, content teaching is complete, the Exploration deadline has usually passed, and the available work is conversion: timing, mark types, rounding and Paper 3. That is valuable and narrower, and it sits in the most contested evenings of the two years.

faqs.question: What makes Higher Level maths genuinely more expensive to support?
faqs.answer: Three things, all structural. Higher Level is built around 240 recommended teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, so content support needs proportionally more of it. Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and carries twenty per cent, and it needs real papers worked to time rather than explanation, which is session-expensive. And the specialist pools for the two Higher Level courses are smaller in this market, which affects availability and therefore price. Confirm all assessment detail against the current IB subject guide your school holds.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 something we need to budget sessions for?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families do not. Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level students and carries twenty per cent of the grade. It consists of extended multi-part problems building towards an unfamiliar result, and it rewards reading the whole question before starting and using earlier parts in later ones. Many schemes of work leave it until the final term, so students meet it late and mismanage the time. A Higher Level budget with no Paper 3 allocation has paid for four fifths of the grade and left the remaining fifth unpractised.

faqs.question: Can we buy access to IB grade boundaries or examiner knowledge?
faqs.answer: No, and the offer should end the conversation. Tutors are frequently described as examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status in any case confers no access to marking, boundaries or unseen paper content that a student could use. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence and do not imply such access exists. We also do not distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school has legitimate access to all of it.

faqs.question: What is the most expensive mistake a DIFC family can make in this market?
faqs.answer: Buying a completed Exploration. There is a provider operating in this space that sells finished assessed work, and the consequence of that purchase falls on the student as a malpractice finding, which can cost the Diploma. No invoice reflects that cost. The legitimate boundary is that a tutor may explain criteria, discuss structure, judge topic viability and give feedback on the student's own draft, and may not write text, supply sentences, perform the calculations or edit to completion. Any provider offering the second list is disqualified by the offer.

faqs.question: Does a cheaper online tutor work for IB maths, or is it a false economy?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what you point them at. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and a competent tutor at those bands can deliver genuine movement on mark types, rounding discipline and command terms, which is where the fastest grade movement sits anyway. Where the budget bands stop working is Higher Level content teaching, particularly Analysis and Approaches calculus and Higher Level Applications and Interpretation statistics. A Higher Level rate at the budget end is a prompt to ask what the tutor has actually taught.

faqs.question: How do we compare two Dubai quotes that show the same hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Ask six questions in writing. Is the rate per clock hour or per session of unstated length? Is marking of full timed papers included? Is it the same named tutor every week, and what happens if the match is wrong? What is the cancellation window? Is the first session chargeable? And is the figure quoted the figure that will appear on the invoice? Those answers routinely reveal that two identical-looking rates are different purchases, and they take about a day to collect from two or three providers.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class cheaper for Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, and the comparison is not only about price. A group cannot diagnose from your child's marked papers, cannot work to one of four courses if the room spans more than one, and cannot change pace for a single student. It suits a student who is close to a grade and needs structured practice. Note also that a centre with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry, which is part of its cost base.

faqs.question: Is any part of a Dubai tutor's rate a licensing cost?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. So no legitimate rate contains a permit fee, and a provider presenting one is misinforming you. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, which is why no amount appears here.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium buy for a family in a DIFC tower?
faqs.answer: The journey. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with independent home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in. In DIFC that premium covers a drive across central Dubai in the evening peak, structured parking and tower reception time. A tutor arriving for a 5pm session leaves somewhere else around 4.15pm and is not free again until after 7pm for one billed hour. It buys nothing visible on a marked script.

faqs.question: How many sessions before we can tell whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: Six weeks, measured against marked papers rather than impressions. Six weeks is long enough for mark-type and rounding repairs to show in a timed paper and short enough that a wrong match has not cost much. Agree the review date before the first session rather than after the tenth, because the quiet renewal of an unreviewed weekly arrangement is how most tutoring money leaves a family in this market. Stopping at the review is a legitimate outcome and sometimes the correct recommendation.

faqs.question: Is there an IB maths tutor we could hire to come to our DIFC apartment?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch or tuition centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics specifically there is a genuine advantage: a shared whiteboard shows the tutor written working as it forms, which is exactly where mark-scheme errors are catchable, whereas working photographed after the fact shows the destination and hides the wrong turn.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.closingHeading: Point the budget before you size it
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-difc.closingBody: Three free pieces of information decide this well: which of the four IB mathematics courses your child is enrolled on, the most recent component-level marks rather than the overall grade, and the school's internal Exploration deadline. With those, the right purchase is usually obvious and usually smaller than expected. Bring them to a short consultation on Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson is free, no card is required, and it ends with a written note of which mark types are being lost and what the first four weeks would address. If ten sessions on mark types and rounding would do what a year of content revision is being sold for elsewhere, that is what we will tell you.

intro.heading: Correct answers, poor marks
paragraphs: The most common complaint a Diploma mathematics parent brings is that the answers were right and the mark was low. It is not a misunderstanding on the student's part about mathematics. It is a misunderstanding about how the paper is marked. IB mathematics mark schemes award method marks and accuracy marks separately, and in a multi-step question the method marks usually outnumber the accuracy ones.

That means a student who reaches the correct value on a calculator and writes only the value has forfeited most of the question. It also means a student who makes an early arithmetic slip but shows a sound chain of reasoning can score most of it, through follow-through credit. Neither of those facts is obvious from classwork, where teachers often comment on whether the answer was right.

This page works at that level throughout. It sets out the five topics both IB mathematics courses are built from and what each actually demands, explains method and accuracy marks and follow-through, covers the mathematical communication errors that cost marks students believe are unfair, describes how to run a past paper so that it produces information, and names the topic traps that recur across Dubai cohorts.

Discovery Gardens shapes the logistics rather than the mathematics. It is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings in themed districts beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Diploma students travel out for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, so they are home from about 16:30 and sessions run at 18:00 or later. Study space is usually a desk in a shared room.

That setup suits mathematics particularly well online, which is worth saying because it is not true of every subject. A mathematics session is shared written working: the student writes, the tutor sees it, and both annotate the same page. Over a screen that is cleaner than two people leaning over one sheet, and it needs a desk and headphones rather than a spare room. IB Gram visits no UAE addresses; home visiting is a service we run only in India.

On dates: UAE schools sit the Diploma in the May session, and we publish no specific IB exam or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking. Your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal calendar, including the exploration deadline, and that is the document to ask for in September rather than in February. The exploration deadline in particular tends to arrive earlier than families expect, and twenty marks turn on a topic choice made well before it.

One last framing point. Nothing on this page is about working harder. Every item in it is about writing down something the student already knows in a form the mark scheme can credit, or about practising a component they have been avoiding. That is why mathematics support started early is so much cheaper than support started late: the habits cost a few sessions to build and then earn marks on every assessment for two years.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-discovery-garden.subjectsIntro: Mathematics at Diploma level is five topics and several distinct skills. These are the areas a Discovery Gardens family will hear about, with what each costs when it is weak.

subjects.name: Topic 1: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level proof, complex numbers and systems of equations. Everything else routes through algebraic fluency, so weakness here shows up as poor marks in topics the student genuinely understands.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, graphs, transformations, inverse and composite functions, and modelling with functions. Students who decode notation each time it appears rather than reading it fluently run out of time on papers they could otherwise complete.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric functions and identities, three-dimensional geometry, and at Higher Level vectors in Analysis and Approaches and matrices and graph theory in Applications. Diagram-first working is the habit that converts understanding into marks here.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data, distributions, probability, and at Higher Level hypothesis testing in Applications and more formal probability in Analysis. Interpretation in context is a separate mark from the calculation, and it is the one most commonly left unwritten.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration and their applications, with Higher Level Analysis and Approaches going considerably further into techniques and differential equations. Exact values and manual manipulation are examined directly where a non-calculator paper applies.

subjects.name: Proof
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction and proof by induction. The ambush is conceptual rather than technical: students arrive from a procedural background and have never been asked to establish that something is true in general rather than verify it in cases.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended problem solving
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade across two long scaffolded questions. Needs whole-question practice under timing, with discussion focused on where the thread was lost rather than on the topic the question happened to use.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks on five criteria. The highest scorers are often mathematically modest pieces on topics the student genuinely cares about, handled correctly and reflected on honestly. Ambition handled superficially scores poorly, and the topic cannot be changed late.

subjects.name: Mathematical communication
subjects.description: Correct notation, defined variables, logical layout and stated conclusions. Marked as communication rather than presentation, which is why students regard losses here as unfair. Among the fastest things in the whole syllabus to correct.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator competence
subjects.description: Model-specific menus, knowing when graphical solution is acceptable and when working is required, and stating what technology returned. Marks are available for using and reporting technology properly, and lost by presenting a bare number.

subjects.name: Mathematics supporting Physics and Chemistry
subjects.description: Rearrangement, logarithms, gradients and uncertainty handling are routine demands in the sciences. Where a student understands the science and stalls on the algebra, the correct purchase is mathematics support rather than more science teaching.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in mathematics
subjects.description: Four thousand words of supervised independent research. Essays fail where the research question has either no mathematics in it or far too much for the word count, and that is diagnosable in one early session rather than in the final term.

sections.heading: The five topics, and what each actually demands
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses are built from the same five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. What differs between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is the emphasis and depth within them, and what differs between Higher and Standard Level is how far each is taken. A tutor should be able to name all five without checking.

Knowing the structure matters because it exposes how the papers are built. Examiners do not ask questions inside a single topic. A calculus question will require algebraic manipulation from topic one and function notation from topic two before any differentiation happens. A statistics question will need interpretation written in the context of the scenario. Students who revised each topic as a sealed unit recognise all the content and cannot assemble it.

It also explains a pattern that confuses parents: a student can be strong in a topic and consistently lose marks on questions that use it. The failure is usually upstream, in algebraic fluency or in reading function notation, rather than in the topic the question is nominally about. That is why a diagnosis from a marked paper outperforms a diagnosis from the student's sense of which topics feel hard.

The practical consequence for revision is to work on the connective tissue: algebraic manipulation, function notation, and interpretation in context. Those three recur in every topic and are examined in every paper. A student who is fluent in all three can attempt almost any question; a student weak in one of them will lose marks in four topics out of five and will attribute it to the topics.

sections.heading: Method marks, accuracy marks and follow-through
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing a Diploma mathematics parent can understand, and almost no student has it explained properly. IB mathematics mark schemes distinguish method marks, awarded for a correct approach, from accuracy marks, awarded for correct values. In a question worth six marks, four might be method and two accuracy. The approach, written down, is worth more than the answer.

That produces two consequences students find counter-intuitive. First, a correct final answer with no visible working forfeits the method marks, because the scheme has nothing to award them against. A student who solves an equation on a calculator and writes the root has shown no method. Second, an early arithmetic slip need not be fatal: follow-through credit can award later marks for correct subsequent work on an incorrect value.

Together those mean the optimal behaviour is to write the chain of reasoning regardless of how the answer was obtained. State the equation being solved, the substitution being made, the rule being applied. If technology produced a value, say what was asked of it and what it returned. None of that is slower than the alternative once it is a habit, and it changes marks on every multi-step question in every paper.

Students resist this because it feels like padding, and because classwork rarely penalises its absence. A tutor who marks the student's own work against the real scheme, repeatedly, is the fastest way to change the behaviour, because the student sees marks appearing on identical mathematics. Three or four marked papers usually does it, which makes this the best-value work available early in a course.

sections.heading: Proof, and why it ambushes Analysis and Approaches students
paragraphs: Proof is where the Diploma most clearly asks for something a student's previous mathematics never did. Direct proof, proof by contradiction and proof by induction all require establishing that a statement holds in general. Students arriving from a procedural background, including Extended IGCSE, have spent years verifying statements in particular cases and reasonably believe that is what mathematical demonstration means.

The characteristic error is therefore not a technical one. A student asked to prove a result will check it for a few values, find it holds, and consider the job done. Nothing in that approach is careless; it is a different conception of what counts as sufficient. Correcting it is a conversation rather than a technique, and it has to happen before any induction practice is useful.

Induction specifically has a structure that rewards drilling once the conceptual point has landed. State the base case and verify it. State the inductive hypothesis precisely. Show the inductive step, making explicit where the hypothesis is used. Conclude. Students lose marks by assuming the result they are proving, by not stating where the hypothesis was applied, and by omitting the concluding sentence, which carries a mark.

For Discovery Gardens families the practical note is that proof is mostly an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level demand, so it is also one of the places a Standard Level tutor stretched upwards will be weakest. If your child sits Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, ask any prospective tutor how they teach induction. The answer separates specialists from generalists faster than almost any other question.
