sections.heading: Running a past paper so that it produces information
paragraphs: Most Diploma students do a great many past papers and learn very little from them. The familiar version is working through a paper with the answers beside it, checking what came out right, and feeling reassured. There is no timing, no marking against a scheme and no record of what kind of error occurred. It builds recognition of question types and that is all, which is why heavy past-paper use often coincides with a plateau.

The version that works has four steps and the fourth is the one everyone skips. Attempt the paper under timed conditions in one sitting without notes. Mark it against the real scheme, strictly, awarding method and accuracy marks separately. Categorise every loss by cause: method not shown, notation, arithmetic, misread question, topic gap, or ran out of time. Then target the two largest categories before the next paper.

The categorisation is what converts a score into a plan. A student who loses nine marks across a paper has two causes, not nine problems. Six marks lost to method not shown and three to timing is a completely different plan from six lost to a topic gap and three to notation. Students cannot usually do this for themselves, because they see the question they got wrong rather than the behaviour that caused it.

Keeping an error log across papers is the cheap extension of this, and it is the single habit that most reliably separates students who improve from students who practise. Three columns are enough: the paper, the loss type, and one sentence on what to do differently. After four papers the pattern is undeniable, and revision stops being a matter of opinion about which topics feel weak.

sections.heading: Paper 3, and holding a long question together
paragraphs: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level, in both courses, and carries twenty per cent of the grade. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions scaffolded across many parts, where each part builds on the one before and the whole thing is usually set in a context the student has not seen. It is the component most Discovery Gardens families discover after a mock, and the one least amenable to the revision they have been doing.

The reason topic revision does not prepare for it is that the difficulty is structural. The mathematics in any individual part is usually within reach. The demand is reading what the question is constructing, carrying results forward accurately, noticing when an intermediate value is implausible, and sustaining the argument for twenty minutes or more. An error in part three can collapse parts four to eight.

So the preparation is whole questions, under timing, with the discussion afterwards focused on where the thread was lost rather than on the topic the question happened to use. Recovery technique is teachable and almost never taught: checking intermediate results for plausibility, stating an assumption explicitly and continuing rather than stopping, and recognising which later parts are independent of the one that went wrong.

This is also the clearest dividing line between a mathematics specialist and a competent generalist. Teaching Paper 3 well requires having taught it before, because the guidance is about question structure rather than content. A tutor meeting Paper 3 for the first time alongside the student is learning the component, which is an expensive way for a family to fund someone's professional development.

sections.heading: Mathematical communication: the marks students call unfair
paragraphs: A recurring conversation in Diploma mathematics tutoring involves a student insisting that a lost mark was unjust. Usually they are describing a notation loss, and usually the mark scheme is clear. IB mathematics is marked as written communication alongside calculation: variables must be defined, notation must be correct, working must be laid out so a reader can follow it, and conclusions must be stated.

The specific losses are consistent. Equals signs used as connectives between unrelated lines. Differentials omitted from integrals. Limits left off definite integrals. Interval and set notation written loosely. Vectors written without indication that they are vectors. A final answer buried inside working rather than stated. None of these is a mathematical misunderstanding, and all of them are marked.

They are also among the fastest corrections available in the entire syllabus, which makes them excellent value in the first weeks of working with a student. Three or four marked pieces of work with notation flagged every time is usually enough to change the habit, and the gain then applies to every paper the student sits for the remaining two years.

The exploration raises the same issue in a more weighted form, because mathematical communication is one of its five criteria explicitly. A student whose notation is loose in papers will lose marks in the exploration for the same reason, except there the strand is named and worth marks in its own right. Fixing the habit early therefore protects both the written papers and twenty internally assessed marks.
bullets: Define variables; do not use equals signs as connectives
Include differentials and limits in integrals
State the final answer rather than leaving it inside working
Mathematical communication is also a named exploration criterion

sections.heading: Topic traps that recur across Dubai cohorts
paragraphs: Some losses are specific enough to list, and a tutor who knows the course can name them before seeing any work. They are worth knowing as a parent because they give you something concrete to ask about, and because almost all of them are quick to fix relative to the marks involved.

In functions, the trap is transformations applied in the wrong order and composite functions evaluated inside out. In trigonometry, it is identities used without checking the domain, and three-dimensional questions attempted without first identifying the relevant triangle. In statistics, it is giving a calculated value without interpreting it in the scenario, which is a separate mark that students leave unclaimed in almost every paper.

In calculus, the traps divide by course. For Analysis and Approaches, the losses concentrate in exact manual work: surds, exact trigonometric values, and integration by substitution without adjusting limits. For Applications and Interpretation, they concentrate in modelling: choosing a model without justifying the choice, and failing to comment on the model's limitations when asked.

In number and algebra, it is logarithm rules applied loosely and binomial expansion terms miscounted. The common thread across all of them is that the student knows the relevant mathematics and loses the mark on execution or on an unwritten step. That is also why these are the right first target in a short block of sessions rather than a syllabus review. A tutor who opens with a list of traps rather than a syllabus checklist has usually marked enough scripts to know where the marks go, and that is a reasonable thing to listen for in a first conversation.

sections.heading: What a mathematics tutor will not do, and where we fit
paragraphs: The boundary in this subject is stated at the first session and it is simple. A tutor teaches method, questions a student's reasoning, demonstrates technique, marks the student's own work against the real scheme and writes down the feedback given. A tutor does not complete set work, supply answers for submission, sit with a student during an assessed task, or write any part of the exploration.

That last point carries weight because at least one provider in this market advertises completed internal assessments at a fixed price. If a student submits an exploration they did not produce, the IB treats it as malpractice and the Diploma is what is at risk rather than the seller's revenue. Legitimate exploration support is reading the five criteria with the student, questioning the topic, teaching the mathematics required, and feeding back in writing on the student's own drafts.

On materials: we do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those are cited and linked, and sessions work from material the school has issued. A tutor offering a folder of downloaded papers and schemes is distributing something that is not theirs to give, and for unreleased material that is a malpractice exposure for the student.

On claims and delivery: we do not predict or guarantee grades, we do not describe tutors as IB examiners without evidence of current status, and we hold no approval or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address, and there is no IB Gram office in the UAE.

process.title: Confirm the course, the level and the paper
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, and the component where marks are going. Add the earliest time your child is at the desk; Diploma students in this community travel out for school and are usually home from about 16:30.

process.title: We match on course and level, and name the tutor
process.description: You are told who will teach, which of the four courses they specialise in, and whether they have taught whole Paper 3 questions and marked explorations. If the exact course cannot be matched at that level we say so rather than offering a mathematics generalist.

process.title: Free trial on a marked paper
process.description: Bring the most recent marked paper and ask what pattern connects the lost marks. A specialist separates method losses from accuracy, notation, reading and timing. A topic answer tells you nothing. No payment is taken for the trial and there is no obligation.

process.title: Start an error log in the first week
process.description: Three columns: the paper, the loss type, and one sentence on what to do differently. After four papers the pattern is undeniable and revision stops being a matter of opinion about which topics feel weak. It costs nothing and almost nobody does it.

process.title: Set the notation habit early
process.description: Define variables, state the equation being solved, say what was asked of the calculator and what it returned, state the conclusion. Three or four marked pieces with notation flagged every time usually changes the habit for the remaining two years.

process.title: Schedule the exploration and Paper 3 work in advance
process.description: The exploration topic session belongs months before the deadline, because twenty marks turn on a choice that cannot be changed late. Paper 3 practice needs whole questions under timing from the mock window onward, not topic revision relabelled.

whyPoints.title: Marked at the level of the mark scheme
whyPoints.description: Method marks and accuracy marks are awarded separately, and in multi-step questions method usually dominates. We teach writing the chain of reasoning as a habit from the first session, which changes marks on every paper rather than only at the end.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one of four courses
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation diverge considerably at Higher Level, in content, in calculator role and in Paper 3. We confirm which your child sits before the trial, because a generalist is specialist in neither.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 taught by someone who has taught it
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade sits in two long scaffolded questions where the difficulty is structural rather than topical. Teaching that well requires prior experience of the component, and we ask tutors about it before matching.

whyPoints.title: Proof treated as a conception, not a technique
whyPoints.description: Students arriving from a procedural background believe checking cases is proving. That has to be addressed before induction practice is useful, and it is one of the places a Standard Level tutor stretched upwards is weakest.

whyPoints.title: Online suits mathematics and suits an apartment
whyPoints.description: A session is shared written working: the student writes, the tutor sees it, both annotate the same page. That is cleaner on a screen than over one sheet of paper, and it needs a desk and headphones rather than a spare room.

whyPoints.title: Notation fixed early, because it is cheap
whyPoints.description: Loose notation costs marks in every paper and is a named exploration criterion too. Three or four marked pieces with it flagged each time usually changes the habit, which makes it the best-value early work in the subject.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose IB maths marks when the final answers are correct?
faqs.answer: Because method marks and accuracy marks are awarded separately, and in a multi-step question the method marks usually outnumber the accuracy ones. A correct value taken from a calculator and written alone forfeits the method marks, because the scheme has nothing to award them against. The fix is habitual: state the equation being solved, the rule being applied, and what was asked of the calculator and what it returned. Three or four marked papers usually establishes it permanently.

faqs.question: What is follow-through credit and does it really help?
faqs.answer: It is the awarding of later marks for correct subsequent work carried out on an earlier incorrect value, and it matters a great deal. It means an arithmetic slip early in a question need not be fatal, provided the student continues with sound method rather than stopping. Students who abandon a question after noticing an error forfeit marks that were still available. Knowing this changes exam behaviour, which is why it belongs in a first session rather than being discovered by accident.

faqs.question: What are the five topics in IB mathematics?
faqs.answer: Number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Both courses are built from all five, with Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation differing in emphasis and depth, and Higher Level taking each further. A tutor should name them without checking. The structure matters because examiners build questions across topics rather than inside them, so a student who revised each as a sealed unit recognises the content and cannot assemble it.

faqs.question: Why does proof cause so much trouble at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Because it asks for something previous mathematics never did. Students from a procedural background have spent years verifying statements in particular cases, so when asked to prove a result they check a few values, find it holds, and consider the job done. That is a different conception of sufficiency rather than carelessness, and it has to be addressed before any induction practice is useful. Induction itself then rewards strict structure, with marks for the base case, the hypothesis, the step and the conclusion.

faqs.question: How should a past paper be used to be worth doing?
faqs.answer: Four steps. Attempt it under timed conditions, in one sitting, without notes. Mark it against the real scheme, strictly, separating method and accuracy marks. Categorise every loss by cause: method not shown, notation, arithmetic, misread question, topic gap, timing. Then target the two largest categories before the next paper. The categorisation is the step everyone skips and the only one that converts a score into a plan, since nine lost marks usually come from two causes.

faqs.question: What is an error log and is it worth the effort?
faqs.answer: Three columns: which paper, what type of loss, and one sentence on what to do differently. It is the cheapest habit in Diploma mathematics and the one that most reliably separates students who improve from students who merely practise. After four papers the pattern is undeniable, and revision stops being a matter of opinion about which topics feel weak. It takes about five minutes per paper and almost no student does it unprompted.

faqs.question: Why can Paper 3 not be prepared by revising topics?
faqs.answer: Because its difficulty is structural rather than topical. It consists of two extended questions scaffolded across many parts, usually in an unfamiliar context, where each part builds on the one before. The mathematics in any individual part is normally within reach; the demand is reading what the question is constructing, carrying results forward, noticing implausible intermediate values, and sustaining the argument for twenty minutes or more. Only whole questions under timing develop that.

faqs.question: Which notation errors cost the most marks?
faqs.answer: Equals signs used as connectives between unrelated lines, differentials omitted from integrals, limits left off definite integrals, interval and set notation written loosely, vectors written without vector notation, and a final answer buried inside working rather than stated. None is a mathematical misunderstanding and all are marked, because IB mathematics is assessed as written communication alongside calculation. They are also among the fastest corrections in the whole syllabus, which makes them excellent early work.

faqs.question: How many marks is the exploration and what decides them?
faqs.answer: Twenty, internally assessed and moderated against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The mark depends far more on topic choice and the honesty of the reflection than on the difficulty of the mathematics attempted, so modest work on a topic the student genuinely cares about regularly outscores ambitious work handled superficially. The topic cannot be changed late, which is why the first session belongs months before the deadline.

faqs.question: Does the course my child sits change the kind of tutor we need?
faqs.answer: At Higher Level, substantially. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level examines proof, complex numbers and deeper calculus, while Applications and Interpretation Higher Level examines hypothesis testing, matrices and extended modelling. Paper 3 differs completely between them. A tutor comfortable in one is often rusty in the other, and a mathematics generalist is specialist in neither. At Standard Level the gap is narrower and a strong general teacher can usually cover either, given the exploration criteria.

faqs.question: What time can maths sessions run for a Discovery Gardens student?
faqs.answer: Usually 18:00 or later for Diploma students, who travel out of the community for school, mostly to Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Al Khail, and are home from about 16:30. Middle Years students are often home by 16:00, so a 16:30 start works for them. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, seven days a week, and a session missed to a late bus or a fixture can move to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: Does online work for maths in a shared apartment?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is among the easiest subjects to deliver well online, because a session is shared written working rather than discussion: the student writes, the tutor sees it, and both annotate the same page. That is cleaner on a screen than two people over one sheet of paper. What it needs is a desk, over-ear headphones with a microphone and the marked work to hand, rather than a room with a door, which suits the housing stock here.

faqs.question: My child is strong in a topic but loses marks on questions that use it. Why?
faqs.answer: The failure is usually upstream. A calculus question needs algebraic manipulation and function notation before any differentiation happens, so a student fluent in calculus and shaky in algebra loses marks on calculus questions and attributes it to calculus. That is why a diagnosis from a marked paper beats a diagnosis from the student's sense of which topics feel hard. The connective tissue, algebraic fluency, notation reading and interpretation in context, is what repays work.

faqs.question: Is the interpretation mark in statistics really separate from the calculation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most consistently unclaimed marks in the subject. A calculated value is not a complete answer where the question asks what it means: a gradient expressed as a rate of change in the units of the scenario is, a bare number is not. Students leave this unwritten in almost every paper because the mark is invisible to them. It takes part of one session to establish and then applies across statistics and modelling questions in both courses.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of the exploration if time is short?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may read the five criteria with the student, question whether the topic carries real mathematics at the right level, teach the technique the investigation needs, show how published work structures an argument, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write it, rewrite it, supply the mathematics, or outline it for completion. That is stated at the first session of any exploration block and feedback is given in writing for the school to see.

faqs.question: What is the best-value first purchase in IB maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Marked work with method and notation flagged, which costs three or four sessions and changes marks on every paper for the rest of the course. The second best is the exploration topic session, because twenty marks turn on a choice that cannot be revisited. What is poor value is a syllabus review bought because a report card was disappointing, since it treats a mark-scheme problem as a content problem and a term passes with everyone working hard and nothing moving.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels, plus the Mathematics Internal Assessment. Each one is matched to the route your child's school actually teaches, not to whichever maths teacher is free that week.

intro.heading: What the money buys, line by line
paragraphs: Downtown Dubai families are rarely short of maths tutors. They are short of a way to tell one AED 180 hour from another AED 180 hour. The quotes arrive by WhatsApp with no scope attached: no route named, no paper named, no statement about whether the Internal Assessment is included or billed separately. Six weeks later the invoice total is clear and the progress is not. This page starts from the money because that is the part parents can actually audit before committing.

The published market in Dubai splits into five bands. University-student and budget online tutors advertise from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A tutor who drives to a Downtown address bills AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is priced in, per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table and the independent home-tutor market. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase published at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-badged tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, where BartyED sits. Those are market figures from the providers named, not an IB Gram price list.

The band matters less than the match. A Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student six weeks from the May session needs someone who can set a Paper 3 investigation, watch the student fail it, and diagnose whether the failure was in the modelling, the notation or the time. A budget tutor can mark Paper 1 answers correctly and still never touch that. The AED 120 difference per hour buys diagnosis, and diagnosis is the only thing that changes a grade.

The route decision is the second place money disappears. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is examined across three papers, with Paper 3 carrying twenty per cent of the grade in two extended problem-solving questions. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level also sits three papers, but Paper 3 there is data-led and rewards a different skill entirely. Families who book twenty hours of general maths support before anyone has confirmed which route the school entered their child for are paying for coverage they will not use.

The third leak is scheduling. Downtown Dubai, Business Bay and DIFC families commonly finish school between 14:45 and 15:30, then sit in Sheikh Zayed Road traffic until well past 16:30. An in-home tutor billing from the moment they leave Jumeirah is being paid for Al Khail Road. Online delivery removes that line from the invoice entirely, which is a large part of why the same specialist costs less over video than in a car.

What follows is the detail: the rate table with sources, the AA versus AI comparison, the paper weightings, what a tutor may and may not do with a Maths IA under IB academic-honesty rules, the Cambridge and Pearson calendar counted backwards, and the regulatory position on who may legally tutor in Dubai. Read the cost sections first if the budget is the live question.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.programmesIntro: Downtown Dubai sits inside the densest school catchment in the UAE, and the IB continuum runs through it at three levels. Each one prices differently because each one assesses differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level. Mathematics is compulsory in Group 5, so every Diploma student in Downtown Dubai sits either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. The Internal Assessment, a mathematical exploration, carries twenty per cent at both routes and both levels. Higher Level adds a third paper; Standard Level does not.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma maths is where Downtown spending concentrates, because the route is fixed in Year 11 and cannot be changed cheaply in Year 13. Families in Business Bay and Sobha Hartland typically book from January of Year 12 once mock results land, which is also when the market rate firms up. Booking before the route is confirmed is the most common way to waste a package in this area.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. MYP maths splits into standard and extended in the final years, and the extended pathway is what feeds Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where most marks are lost.
programmes.countryNote: MYP tutoring in Downtown Dubai is cheaper per hour than Diploma work and far cheaper in total, because it is preventative. A student who enters MYP Year 5 on the standard pathway and wants Analysis and Approaches Higher Level has a gap to close, and closing it over two years costs a fraction of a Year 13 rescue at specialist rates.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with mathematics organised across number, pattern and function, data handling, measurement, and shape and space. There is no external examination. Support here is about fluency and confidence rather than assessment technique, and sessions are shorter.
programmes.countryNote: Primary maths support in the Downtown and Meydan corridor is usually booked for one of two reasons: a mid-year arrival from a non-IB system, or a Year 6 student heading into an MYP school with a visible arithmetic gap. Both are short engagements. Neither needs a specialist rate, and paying one is money spent on the wrong band.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where mathematics appears it is usually a Diploma Standard Level course, most often Applications and Interpretation, alongside personal and professional skills.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is offered by only a handful of Dubai schools, so Downtown families reaching it are usually travelling to a specific campus rather than a neighbourhood one. Maths support here is scoped tightly to the single Standard Level course carried forward, which keeps the booking small.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-downtown-dubai.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the page, but it does not arrive alone. These are the courses Downtown Dubai and Business Bay families book alongside it, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route. Higher Level sits Papers 1, 2 and 3; Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, and Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions worth twenty per cent. Marks are lost most often in proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, and the unstructured nature of Paper 3 itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling-and-statistics route, calculator-permitted throughout. Higher Level adds graph theory, matrices and complex numbers in a modelling context. The common failure is treating statistics questions as arithmetic and omitting the interpretation sentence that carries the final mark.

subjects.name: Mathematics Internal Assessment
subjects.description: A twelve to twenty page mathematical exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade, marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Criterion E, use of mathematics, is where Higher Level candidates are most often capped by choosing a topic below their level.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Booked with maths more often than any other subject in this area, because the mechanics and fields topics assume calculus fluency the Physics syllabus does not teach. Students who are weak on differentiation lose marks in Physics Paper 2 before they lose them in maths.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The quantitative chemistry, energetics and equilibrium topics are arithmetic-heavy, and the Higher Level Paper 2 calculation questions punish rounding errors. Students carrying a maths weakness into Chemistry usually present as careless rather than confused.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics adds quantitative questions on elasticity, market failure and the Keynesian multiplier. The maths is not hard but the notation is unfamiliar, and Paper 3 at Higher Level is where the two subjects collide most visibly.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Covers abstract data structures, resource management and the internal assessment solution. Students who find Analysis and Approaches notation difficult often find pseudocode equally difficult, because both reward precision over intuition.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The finance and accounts unit requires break-even analysis, investment appraisal and ratio calculation. Downtown and DIFC families commonly book maths and Business Management together once the Year 12 finance papers are returned.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by exhibition and a 1,600-word essay. Mathematics appears regularly as an area of knowledge, and students who can explain why a mathematical proof differs from scientific evidence write stronger essays.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent research piece. Mathematics Extended Essays are fewer in number and are marked hard on the mathematical content criterion, so the topic choice conversation matters more here than in most subjects.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Required in all Dubai private schools regardless of licensed curriculum, under KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes are prohibited. This runs alongside the IB timetable rather than inside it.

subjects.name: UAE Social Studies and Moral Education
subjects.description: Mandatory in Dubai private schools, with Arabic as the primary language of instruction for Arab students and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises a minimum of 25 minutes per mandatory-subject lesson.

sections.heading: Where the money goes wrong
paragraphs: The expensive mistake in this market is not paying too much per hour. It is paying the right hourly rate for the wrong hours. Four patterns account for most of the waste we see in enquiries from Downtown Dubai, Business Bay and DIFC, and all four are avoidable before any money changes hands.

The first is buying a package before the route is confirmed. A family books twenty hours of Diploma maths in October, then discovers in November that the school entered their child for Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches. Half the content taught does not appear on the papers the student will sit. Confirming the route takes one email to the Diploma coordinator.

The second is paying a specialist rate for consolidation work. A Year 10 MYP student who cannot reliably rearrange a formula does not need a Higher Level examiner at AED 450. That student needs eight patient hours at AED 150 and then a reassessment. Buying the top band early usually means running out of budget in the term where the top band would actually have mattered.

The third is paying for travel. An in-home tutor crossing Al Khail Road at 16:00 is billing for the journey whether the invoice itemises it or not, and Bestimate's own in-home band sits AED 30 to AED 150 above the equivalent online band for precisely that reason. The fourth is the open-ended booking with no end date, no stated target and no halfway review, which drifts until someone notices the total.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that sets the bill
paragraphs: Every Diploma student takes a Group 5 mathematics course, and the two routes are genuinely different subjects rather than two difficulties of the same one. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic rigour, proof and calculus, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and technology, with a calculator permitted throughout. A tutor who treats them as interchangeable will teach the wrong half of the syllabus.

The route also sets how many hours a student is likely to need. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level carries proof by induction, complex numbers in both Cartesian and polar form, and a Paper 3 that gives two extended unstructured problems worth twenty per cent of the grade. There is no efficient shortcut through Paper 3; it is practised or it is lost. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level has its own Paper 3, data-led and equally unstructured, but the preparation is different in kind and students who read well often progress faster on it.

University entry is the part parents most often get wrong. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, and will say so in their prerequisites. Business, psychology, design and most social sciences accept Applications and Interpretation without comment. Check the specific programme pages for the universities your child is actually applying to rather than relying on a general rule, because the requirement is set by the department and not by the country.

Where a route change is still possible, it is a Year 12 conversation and not a Year 13 one. Switching late means relearning a different Paper 1 discipline with months rather than terms, and that is the single most expensive tutoring scenario in this catchment.

sections.heading: Paper by paper: where the marks actually go
paragraphs: Parents are told their child is weak at maths. The useful version of that statement names a component. An IB Mathematics grade is assembled from external papers plus the Internal Assessment, and the loss pattern differs sharply by paper. A student who scores well on Paper 1 and badly on Paper 2 has a technology problem, not a mathematics problem, and the two need different sessions.

The Internal Assessment is twenty per cent at both routes and both levels, which makes it the single largest component a student fully controls. It is also the component most often left to the last three weeks. A student who submits a rushed exploration has capped their grade before sitting a paper, and no amount of specialist revision afterwards recovers that twenty per cent.

The table below sets out the structure and the characteristic failure for each component. Use it to turn a vague school report into a specific tutoring brief: if the mock showed Paper 2 method marks lost to calculator misuse, say that in the first message rather than asking for general maths help, and the first session will be worth more.

Command terms deserve their own mention because they cost marks invisibly. A question that begins 'hence' is instructing the candidate to use the previous result, and a student who starts again from first principles can reach the right answer and still lose the dependent marks. 'Show that' requires the working to be visible even where the answer is given. 'Justify' requires a reason attached to the statement. These are mechanical habits, teachable in two or three sessions, and they recur in every paper at both levels.

Confirm the current component structure and timings against your child's Diploma coordinator or the official IB subject page before planning around them, since the IB revises course structures between syllabus cycles.

sections.heading: The Maths IA: what a tutor may do, and what would get your child withdrawn
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration must be the student's own work. That is not a house rule, it is an IB academic-honesty requirement, and a breach is a malpractice finding against the student rather than against the tutor. Some providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright. One advertises them at AED 3,750. Buying one risks the whole Diploma.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. A tutor can teach the mathematics a student has chosen to explore, including content beyond the taught syllabus. A tutor can read a draft and ask why a step follows, where the reflection sits, and whether Criterion E is satisfied at the candidate's level. A tutor can point out that a topic is below Higher Level and explain what raising it would involve. A tutor can set deadlines against the school's own calendar and hold the student to them.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite, restructure or edit the text into its final state, supply a topic ready-made with the mathematics already worked, or produce the graphs and calculations the student then presents. The boundary in practice is simple: feedback arrives as questions and taught content, never as replacement prose. If a provider offers to 'handle' the IA, that is the answer to whether to use them.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. Both are assessed as independent work, both carry supervisor declarations, and both are checked. A student who has been coached properly can explain every line of their own exploration under questioning, which is also what the viva-style conversations with a supervisor are designed to surface.

May question a draft, criterion by criterion, without supplying replacement wording

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Entry deadlines sit months before the exams, and families who plan from the exam date backwards discover the registration date has already passed. The honest way to present this is as a sequence of milestones with the body that sets each one, so a parent can check the live source rather than trust a date on a tutoring page.

For Cambridge International, UAE centres sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to candidates in Dubai. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone; Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in before reading any timetable PDF.

For Pearson Edexcel, International GCSE exams run in May or June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

IB Diploma dates are deliberately not published on this page. The IB revises session windows and results dates, and we will not put a date in front of a parent that we have not read on ibo.org on the day. Dubai schools sit the May session; confirm the exact window and the results date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages, and plan the tutoring block from that confirmed date.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to tutor your child in Dubai
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is quoting something unverified; Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties. The practical point for a parent is that a permit exists, it is free, and a tutor who cannot explain their position on it has told you something.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor: it requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, operates no centre or office in the UAE, and is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. Any provider claiming otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

In Abu Dhabi there is an additional restriction worth knowing even from Dubai, since families move between emirates. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

And Dubai's private sector is growing rather than tightening: 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with enrolment up six per cent during 2025-26 and seven new schools opening for 2026-27.

The same family buying specialist exam-year support from January is adding AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for the final stretch. sections.heading: Why lessons run online to Downtown Dubai, stated plainly
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the UAE. That is the position, stated before any benefit is claimed for it, because a family planning around a tutor arriving in Downtown Dubai should know within the first screen that this is not what is being sold.

The case for video delivery here is specific rather than general. A Downtown or Business Bay family choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from the pool willing to drive to that address at that hour, which in practice means a generalist. Choosing online widens the pool to a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist who has taught Paper 3 repeatedly, and narrows the cost by removing the travel the in-home band exists to cover.

The practical gains are equally specific. A shared screen holds the working, so a student can revisit exactly how a proof was set out rather than relying on a photographed page. Sessions survive a sandstorm, a closed road and a school trip. A 19:30 slot is actually available, because nobody has to drive home afterwards. And a missed week can be rescheduled to a Friday without anyone crossing the city twice.

What video does not do is supervise. A student who needs someone physically present to stay at the desk needs that, and no amount of screen-sharing substitutes for it. If that is the real requirement, an in-home tutor from the local market is the honest answer, and the rate table above shows what that costs.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths tutor in Downtown Dubai cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai put qualified one-to-one IB maths support online between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, and specialist Higher Level support between AED 200 and AED 450 or above. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table gives AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialists. An in-home tutor driving to a Downtown address bills AED 180 to AED 500 because travel sits inside the rate. Those are market figures as read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our first lesson is free, and the rate after it depends on the route, level and number of weeks agreed.

faqs.question: Is Maths Applications and Interpretation cheaper to tutor than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Not per hour, but often in total. The hourly band is the same because the tutor's qualification is the same. The difference is the number of hours. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level carries proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, and a non-calculator Paper 1, all of which take repeated timed practice to secure. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-permitted throughout and rewards interpretation, which many students reach faster. The exception is Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, where graph theory and statistical inference are unfamiliar enough to absorb as many hours as the Analysis route. Confirm your child's route with the Diploma coordinator before estimating anything.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week do Downtown Dubai Diploma families usually start with?
faqs.answer: One sixty-minute session a week is the normal starting point during term, which Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates put at AED 600 to AED 1,200 a month at the mid band. Families move to two sessions a week in the final two terms, or earlier if a mock has exposed a specific component failure such as Paper 3. We would rather start at one and add a second when the evidence justifies it than sell two from the outset. Business Bay and DIFC households often prefer two shorter sessions over one long one, because a single ninety-minute evening slot is easier to lose to work.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Mathematics Internal Assessment without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is worth stating precisely. A tutor may teach the mathematics your child's chosen topic requires, including content beyond the taught syllabus, read a draft and ask why each step follows, check that Criterion E is satisfied at the candidate's level, and hold the student to the school's own deadlines. A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or edit the exploration into its final state, nor supply a pre-worked topic, dataset or set of graphs. Feedback arrives as questions and taught content, never as replacement prose. Some providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright; that is an IB malpractice risk carried by your child.

faqs.question: Which IB maths paper carries the most risk for a Higher Level student?
faqs.answer: Paper 3. It is twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade and consists of two extended, unstructured investigations rather than the shorter questions students practise all year. Candidates lose marks there by running out of time, by failing to state a conjecture, and by never reaching the generalisation the question is built towards. Nothing in ordinary revision prepares a student for it, which is why it needs its own sessions rather than a mention inside general preparation. Standard Level students do not sit Paper 3, so for them the equivalent risk sits in the Internal Assessment, which is also twenty per cent and equally often left late.

faqs.question: Do tutoring rates in Dubai rise closer to the exam season?
faqs.answer: Specialist availability tightens rather than the advertised rate changing. From January onwards, tutors with Higher Level Paper 3 experience fill their timetables, and what a family actually loses is choice of tutor and choice of slot rather than money. The practical consequence is that a booking made in October gets the specialist at the ordinary band, and the same request in March gets whoever remains. If the budget is the constraint, the cheaper decision is an earlier start at the mid band rather than a later start at the specialist band, because earlier work needs fewer hours.

faqs.question: Why would online maths tutoring cost less than a tutor coming to Downtown Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because travel is inside the in-home rate whether the invoice names it or not. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one in Dubai at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to AED 500, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified tutor working online. The gap is the car. For a Downtown or Business Bay address, a tutor arriving after a 15:00 school finish is crossing Sheikh Zayed Road or Al Khail Road in peak traffic, and that hour is paid for by somebody. IB Gram delivers to UAE families over live video and does not offer home visits in Dubai, so that cost is simply absent.

faqs.question: Which schools do Downtown Dubai and Business Bay students actually attend?
faqs.answer: Almost none sit inside Downtown itself, which has no villa stock and very little school provision. Families commute out to campuses in Al Safa, Al Barsha, Al Jaddaf, Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland, including Jumeirah English Speaking School, Dubai International Academy, Swiss International Scientific School, GEMS Modern Academy, Kent College Dubai and Hartland International School. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 curricula. Named schools here are context for the catchment only; IB Gram claims no affiliation, partnership or endorsement with any of them.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student maths tutor a false economy?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the task. For arithmetic fluency, homework structure and MYP consolidation, a tutor at the AED 45 to AED 150 band does the job and the money is well spent. For diagnosing why a Higher Level candidate loses method marks on Paper 2, or for Paper 3 technique, it usually is a false economy: the sessions are pleasant, the homework gets done, and the component failure is untouched because nobody identified it. The expensive mistake is the reverse too, paying AED 450 for work a mid-band tutor would have handled. Match the band to the diagnosed task.

faqs.question: Does a private maths tutor in Dubai need a permit, and is it expensive?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it is free. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include school-registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page is 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted is unverified.

faqs.question: What does the free trial maths lesson include, and what are the conditions?
faqs.answer: It is a full one-to-one session on a real topic from your child's current syllabus, delivered over live video, with written feedback afterwards naming the specific gap found. No card details are taken and nothing is owed if you stop there. The only condition is that we need the route and level before it starts, so the tutor matched is the right one: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. One trial per student. If the match is wrong we will say so and offer a different tutor rather than proceed.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level maths matter for UAE university applications?
faqs.answer: It matters for the programme rather than the country. Engineering, physics, mathematics and quantitative economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, and state so in their entry requirements. Business, psychology and design programmes generally accept Applications and Interpretation. Check the named programme's own page at the university your child is applying to, because the requirement is set departmentally. Separately, UAE Ministry of Education equivalency is its own process with its own criteria; we will not publish an IB points threshold for it, because that figure has not been verified on a Ministry source. Confirm it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for an IB maths tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Five things make a quote accurate rather than approximate: the route and level, the school and year group, the most recent mock or report grade with the component breakdown if you have it, the date of the next school assessment, and the days and times that genuinely work after the school run. With those, a specialist can tell you how many hours the gap looks like and which band of tutor it needs. Without them, any figure quoted is a placeholder that will be revised upwards once the real position becomes clear in the first session.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or around school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ramadan sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing, and families in Downtown Dubai and Business Bay often reduce to one session a week during that period and add it back afterwards. Summer and half-term work differently: with no school assessments running, the useful work is syllabus consolidation or Internal Assessment scoping rather than exam technique, and sessions can be longer because there is no school day in front of them. We pause rather than bill through mock weeks, and a block paused for travel resumes at the same rate.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level maths specialist is free when we enquire?

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academic-c.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at both Higher and Standard Level, plus the MYP mathematics that leads into them and Internal Assessment coaching on the student's own exploration.

intro.heading: Two different courses, four neighbourhoods, one tutoring problem
paragraphs: The first thing to establish is which mathematics your child is actually taking, because 'IB maths' describes two courses that share a name and very little else. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-based route: calculus, functions, trigonometric identities, and at Higher Level proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, built around technology use, regression, and interpreting results in context. They are examined separately and they suit different students.

Families in this cluster get this wrong more often than families in older Dubai neighbourhoods, for a practical reason. Dubai International Academic City is a university free zone; its own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route to A Level. The Diploma schools this cluster uses are elsewhere - GEMS Wellington Academy in Silicon Oasis, Uptown International School in Mirdif, Universal American School in Al Warqa, GEMS Modern Academy and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Nad Al Sheba - and course availability varies between them.

So a parent in Academic City comparing notes with a neighbour in Silicon Oasis may be discussing two different qualifications. One child is doing AA HL at one school; the other is doing AI SL at another; the tutoring each needs has almost nothing in common. Before booking anything, get the course name, the level and the school from the Diploma coordinator, in writing. It takes one email and it prevents a term of mismatched teaching.

The second thing to establish is where the marks are going. In both courses the commonest loss is not conceptual. It is method: answers presented without working, so that a correct final number earns a fraction of the available marks; rounding applied too early in a multi-step problem, so accuracy marks fall away through the rest of it; and calculator methods used where the question demanded an analytic one. These are habits, and habits are faster to change than understanding is to build.

The third is the Internal Assessment, the mathematical exploration, worth 20 marks against five published criteria. Almost no competitor page in this market names a single criterion, which is strange, because knowing that personal engagement carries three marks and use of mathematics carries six tells a student exactly where to spend their effort. The criteria table further down this page is the most immediately useful thing on it.

IB Gram delivers all of this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service. For mathematics specifically that matters, because the pool of people within a twenty-minute drive of Academic City who teach AA HL is very small, and the pool who can coach an exploration against criterion E is smaller still.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academic-c.programmesIntro: Mathematics tutoring requests from this cluster arrive at four distinct points, and the right work is different at each one.

programmes.name: MYP mathematics, standard and extended
programmes.description: Graded 1-8 against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Many schools split into standard and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5, and that split influences which Diploma course a student is steered towards. Marks are lost on investigating patterns, because generalising and justifying a rule is a skill nobody teaches directly.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster the MYP runs at Uptown International School in Mirdif and Universal American School in Al Warqa. If your child is in MYP 4 or 5 and may want Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the extended route matters: AA HL assumes algebraic fluency that standard MYP mathematics does not build to the same depth. Ask the school which route they intend and why.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and statistics, assessed across two papers plus the exploration. It is a demanding course for a student who was comfortable rather than strong in MYP mathematics, principally because it moves quickly and assumes prior fluency. Students who relied on a calculator through MYP meet the limits of that approach in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: AA SL is the most commonly requested tutoring combination from families in Academic City, Silicon Oasis and Mirdif, and the usual presenting problem is identical: the content is understood in the lesson and collapses in the test. That is a method and timing problem rather than a comprehension problem, and it is diagnosable from one marked paper.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
programmes.description: The most demanding mathematics in the Diploma: everything in SL plus proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors, and substantially heavier calculus including further integration techniques. Three papers rather than two, and a grade distribution that reflects a self-selecting cohort. It is the usual requirement for engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics degrees.
programmes.countryNote: This is the hardest combination to staff locally in the eastern suburbs, and the one where online matching makes the clearest difference. A family in Al Khawaneej or International City looking for an AA HL specialist within driving distance is usually looking at an empty list. We also say plainly when an AA HL slot is not available at short notice rather than offering a Standard Level tutor for it.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation, SL and HL
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics, probability and technology use, with HL adding matrices, graph theory, vectors and more demanding statistical inference. The content is not easier than AA, it is different: less algebraic manipulation, far more interpretation. The characteristic failure is a student who computes a regression line correctly and then says nothing about what the gradient means.
programmes.countryNote: AI is growing in Dubai schools and is often the better fit for students heading towards business, social sciences, design or medicine-adjacent routes. The caution is university prerequisites: some courses specify AA, and a few specify AA at Higher Level. Check the target universities' published requirements before DP1 rather than in DP2, because the switch between courses is difficult once teaching has begun.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academic-c.subjectsIntro: Mathematics tutoring is topic work, not subject work. These are the areas families in this cluster ask about, with what each actually demands.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency and manipulation
subjects.description: The foundation everything else rests on: indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging, and factorising without hesitation. A student who can do these slowly cannot do the rest of the course at all, because the algebra is the step inside a longer problem rather than the problem itself.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, and the effect of each transformation on a graph. Marks go missing when students memorise transformation rules rather than understanding them, because examination questions combine two or three transformations at once.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, optimisation and kinematics. HL extends to implicit differentiation and related rates. The recurring loss is in optimisation problems where the student differentiates correctly and never justifies that the stationary point is a maximum.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, areas and volumes of revolution. HL adds substitution, integration by parts and partial fractions. Students lose marks on limits, on forgetting the constant, and on setting up the integral with the wrong variable of integration.

subjects.name: Proof, including induction
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, counterexample and proof by mathematical induction. Induction is heavily examined and heavily botched: the inductive step is often asserted rather than derived, and the conclusion is omitted. It is formulaic enough to be taught reliably in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Complex numbers and vectors
subjects.description: Cartesian, polar and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem, and vector geometry including lines and planes. Marks go on argument conventions and on diagrams that are not drawn. Vector questions in particular reward sketching before calculating, which almost no student does unprompted.

subjects.name: Statistics, probability and distributions
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous distributions, the binomial and normal, correlation and regression. In AI this is the heart of the course. The common loss is in conditional probability and in stating conclusions without reference to the context the question established.

subjects.name: Modelling and interpretation
subjects.description: Choosing a model, fitting it, and saying what it means. The computation is rarely the problem; the interpretation is. A student who writes the gradient of a regression line without a sentence on what it represents in the context of the data has lost the marks that distinguish the top bands.

subjects.name: Matrices and graph theory
subjects.description: Matrix operations, eigenvalues, transition matrices, and graph theory including minimum spanning trees and Chinese postman problems. Unfamiliar to most parents and highly teachable, because the question types repeat with great regularity across sessions.

subjects.name: Mathematics Internal Assessment, the exploration
subjects.description: An individual exploration of 12 to 20 pages, worth 20 marks against five criteria. Coaching covers topic viability, structure, mathematical communication and the reflection the criteria reward. The student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes every word.

subjects.name: MYP to Diploma mathematics bridge
subjects.description: A short programme on exactly what the Diploma assumes from day one: indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation and basic differentiation. Six to eight sessions in the summer before DP1 removes most of the first-term shock, and it is the cheapest useful mathematics tutoring a family in this cluster can buy.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: Knowing which paper permits the calculator and what it is for. In AI it is central; in AA it is a tool that must not replace analytic method. Specific skills - solving numerically, finding intersections, working with distributions, storing values to avoid rounding error - are worth marks and take two sessions to teach.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that shapes two years of mathematics and it is frequently made on a sentence at a parents' evening. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led; Applications and Interpretation is model-led and statistical. A student who finds algebraic manipulation painful but reads data well is genuinely better served by AI, and will score higher there.

The constraint is university entry. Some courses specify Analysis and Approaches, and a number of engineering, mathematics and physics programmes specify it at Higher Level. Others accept either. The only reliable way to settle it is to read the published entry requirements for the specific universities and courses your child is considering, including the UAE institutions, and to do that in the first Diploma year rather than the second, because switching after teaching has started is difficult.

The second constraint is school provision. Not every Diploma school in this part of Dubai offers both courses at both levels in every cohort, and timetable blocking can rule a combination out even when the course exists. Ask the Diploma coordinator which of the four combinations will actually run for your child's year group before building a plan on one of them.

For tutoring the practical point is that AA and AI tutors are not interchangeable. Somebody strong on calculus and proof may be weak on statistical inference and graph theory, and the reverse is equally true. We match on the course and level, which is why the first question we ask is which of the four your child is in.

sections.heading: The Internal Assessment criteria, letter by letter
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is worth 20 marks, assessed against five criteria, and almost no page competing for this search names a single one of them. That omission is expensive for students, because the mark allocations tell you precisely where effort pays. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks - more than any other - and it is the criterion most often undermined by a topic that simply does not contain enough mathematics at the right level.

So the topic decision is the single highest-leverage moment in the whole exploration, and it happens before any writing. A topic that reduces to arithmetic and a graph cannot score well on criterion E no matter how neatly it is presented. A topic that requires mathematics commensurate with the course, used correctly and with understanding shown, can. Testing a proposed topic against criterion E before the student commits is the main thing a tutor is for here.

The other criteria reward things students systematically neglect. Personal engagement is three marks for genuine involvement with the material rather than a sentence saying the student finds the topic interesting. Reflection is three marks for considering the significance and limitations of the results, which is usually squeezed into a final paragraph when it should run through the work. Mathematical communication is four marks for notation, terminology and consistent use of symbols.

On process, this is coaching rather than production. We question the topic, explain the criteria, and comment on the student's own drafts. We do not supply mathematics, write sections or choose topics. One operator in these search results sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate, not the seller.

sections.heading: Where mathematics marks actually go, by habit rather than by topic
paragraphs: Marking a Diploma mathematics paper properly produces a short and repetitive list. Working not shown, so a correct final answer scores one mark out of four. Rounding applied at an intermediate step, so every subsequent accuracy mark falls. A calculator used on a paper that required an analytic method. A stationary point found and never classified. A vector question attempted without a sketch. An optimisation answer given without units or context.

None of those is a failure of understanding and all of them are expensive. That is the good news, because habits change faster than comprehension grows. A student who loses eight marks a paper to method can usually recover most of them in six to eight sessions of deliberate practice, which is a far better return than the same hours spent re-explaining differentiation.

The way to find your own child's list is to have one timed paper marked properly against the published mark scheme, question by question, with the reason for each lost mark written down. Most students have three or four recurring reasons rather than twenty. That list becomes the lesson plan, and the student keeps it as an error log that gets checked for recurrence each session.

The topic-level gaps are real too and they are usually narrower than they feel. In Analysis and Approaches the recurring weak areas are integration technique, proof by induction and vector geometry. In Applications and Interpretation they are conditional probability, statistical inference and the interpretation sentences the mark scheme asks for. Those are nameable and schedulable, which is the opposite of 'my child is bad at maths'.

sections.heading: Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif, International City: what actually differs
paragraphs: Families in this cluster compare neighbourhoods constantly, so here is the comparison done properly for a mathematics student. What differs between the four is the school run, the time a session can start, and which Diploma courses the local school actually runs. What does not differ is the supply of Higher Level mathematics specialists, because that is set across the emirate rather than district by district.

Mirdif and Silicon Oasis have Diploma schools inside the district, so a 4.45pm session is realistic and a student can sustain two a week in the second year. Academic City's own secondary is on the British route, so Diploma families travel and 5pm is the practical floor. International City has no international school at all within the district, which pushes weekday sessions past six and makes the weekend morning the slot where serious paper practice happens.

The column that matters is the last one. In none of these four neighbourhoods is there a usable local choice of Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutors. A family in Mirdif has a marginally better chance than a family in Al Khawaneej, and neither has a shortlist. Removing travel from the equation gives all four the same pool, which is larger than any of them had alone - and that, rather than convenience, is the argument for online delivery in this district.

One practical consequence of the timings in the table: book the slot against the worst-case journey rather than the average one. A session set for 4.30pm from a Nad Al Sheba school becomes a 4.50pm start twice a week, and in mathematics the lost ten minutes are usually the ones where last week's error log would have been reviewed.
