sections.heading: The MYP mathematics to Diploma step, and how to close it cheaply
paragraphs: The most predictable mathematics problem in this cluster is the transition from MYP 5 into the first Diploma year. MYP mathematics is graded 1-8 against criteria that reward investigation and communication; Diploma mathematics assumes algebraic operations are automatic and then builds quickly on top of them. A student can hold a strong MYP grade and still be slow at the operations the Diploma treats as given.

The gap is specific rather than general, which is what makes it cheap to close. Indices and surds. Algebraic fractions. Rearranging formulae with the unknown in more than one place. Function notation and composite functions. Expanding and factorising without pausing. Basic differentiation, for students heading to Analysis and Approaches. That is a list, not a syllabus, and six to eight sessions over a summer covers it.

Families who do this in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 report a quieter first term and buy fewer hours in total across the two years. Families who wait until the first Diploma report card are buying the same sessions in competition with new content arriving weekly, which is harder and takes longer. The MYP-to-Diploma bridge is the single best-value mathematics tutoring available to a student in this cluster.

One further note for Al Warqa and International City families specifically, where many students arrive from Indian-curriculum schools. The shift there is different again: CBSE mathematics builds strong procedural fluency and less interpretive writing, so the transition issue is usually the modelling and communication demands of MYP criteria and of Applications and Interpretation, rather than the algebra.

sections.heading: What mathematics tutoring costs in this market
paragraphs: Lead with what a parent can verify rather than with a price. Every figure below was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram rate. Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote United States dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in.

Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500.

Monthly, which is how families actually budget: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

For Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specifically, the honest market observation is that the budget band rarely contains anybody who can teach it. A tutor at AED 60 an hour is almost certainly not an AA HL specialist, and paying AED 300 for a generalist is worse value than paying AED 250 for somebody who teaches the course. For our own rates, the free trial lesson comes first and the figure is quoted against your child's actual course and level.

sections.heading: The Diploma mathematics year, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May examination session, and for mathematics the internal calendar matters as much as the external one. The exploration has a school deadline, usually in the second half of the first Diploma year or early in the second, and it competes directly with mock examinations and with the Extended Essay in a crowded January and February window.

Counting backwards from that window changes the plan. Exploration topic chosen and tested against criterion E by the end of the first year. Mathematics drafted while there is still slack in the timetable, not alongside mock revision. Timed paper practice begun in the first term of the second year rather than saved for after the mocks, which is the commonest planning error in Diploma mathematics.

We publish no specific IB session or results dates on this site. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than no date at all, so confirm every IB date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dates are sourced: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, the February and March series being offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November.

Ramadan sits inside the revision period in most years. School days shorten, late-afternoon concentration is poor, and a mathematics session booked for 4pm during the month is usually wasted. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work better. Because no tutor is travelling, changing the pattern is a scheduling decision rather than a logistical one, and it is worth fixing before the month begins.

sections.heading: Finding somebody who actually teaches your child's course
paragraphs: Matching for mathematics is narrower than for most subjects. You are not looking for a maths tutor; you are looking for somebody who teaches Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, routinely enough to know which question types appear where and what the mark scheme credits. In the eastern suburbs of Dubai, the number of such people within driving distance of Academic City is not a shortlist.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any figure quoted at you. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit, and ask to see it.

There is one arrangement to decline. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. If somebody offers you your child's own mathematics teacher privately, that is a problem for the teacher and potentially for your child.

And where we cannot staff a combination properly - Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level at short notice in the weeks before mocks is the recurring case - we say so, give a realistic wait, and let you look elsewhere. We also state what we are not: no UAE office or centre, no KHDA Educational Services Permit, and no approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the school
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, which school, and what the last marked assessment came back as. Get it from the Diploma coordinator in writing if you are unsure, because the four combinations need four different tutors.

process.title: One marked paper as the diagnosis
process.description: Before planning anything, the tutor has the student sit a timed paper at the correct level and marks it against the published mark scheme, writing down the reason for every lost mark. That produces three or four recurring reasons, which becomes the plan for the first six sessions.

process.title: Free trial lesson and a written note
process.description: A real lesson on real mathematics, with the student working and the tutor diagnosing. Afterwards a plain written summary: the error habits found, the topic gaps, and what eight weeks would target. Say no and nothing further is owed.

process.title: Weekly rhythm with an error log
process.description: One session a week in the first Diploma year, often two in the second for Higher Level. The student keeps the error log and it is checked for recurrence every session. Short written reviews every few weeks on what has moved and what has not.

process.title: Exploration block timed to the school deadline
process.description: Four to six sessions when the Internal Assessment is live, starting with whether the chosen topic can carry criterion E at all. The student chooses, calculates and writes; the tutor questions and gives feedback on drafts. That boundary holds regardless of the deadline.

whyPoints.title: Matched to one of four combinations, not to 'IB maths'
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation SL are different qualifications needing different tutors. Strength in calculus and proof does not imply strength in statistical inference and graph theory. We ask which course before we match, every time.

whyPoints.title: Method marks taught as a subject in their own right
whyPoints.description: Working shown, rounding controlled, stationary points classified, vectors sketched, interpretation sentences written. Most mathematics mark loss at Diploma level is habit rather than understanding, and habits move faster than comprehension does.

whyPoints.title: The exploration criteria named, with their marks
whyPoints.description: Presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, use of mathematics 6. No competitor page in this market names a single criterion. Knowing the allocation tells a student exactly where the effort belongs.

whyPoints.title: The transition nobody budgets for
whyPoints.description: Six to eight sessions in the summer between MYP 5 and the first Diploma year, on indices, surds, algebraic fractions, function notation and basic differentiation. It is the cheapest useful mathematics tutoring available in this cluster and almost nobody buys it.

whyPoints.title: Rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider who published it and the month it was read. Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote dollars, which is not the currency UAE families pay in.

whyPoints.title: We say when we cannot help
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level at short notice before mocks is the combination we most often cannot staff well. You hear that at the enquiry stage with a realistic wait, rather than meeting a generalist at specialist rates in session three.

faqs.question: Can I get an IB maths tutor in Dubai International Academic City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor arriving at your address. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is an India-only service for us. For Diploma mathematics the online route has a concrete advantage here beyond convenience: the pool of people within driving distance of Academic City who teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is effectively empty, and matching online replaces proximity with the thing that actually decides the grade.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-led course: functions, trigonometry, calculus, and at Higher Level proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics, built around technology use, regression and interpreting results in context, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Neither is the easy version. The decision should rest on how your child thinks and on the published entry requirements for the courses they want, since some degrees specify AA and a few specify it at Higher Level.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Maths exploration worth and how is it split?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks across five criteria. Criterion A, presentation, carries four. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries four. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries three. Criterion D, reflection, carries three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six and is the largest single allocation. That split is why the topic choice matters more than the writing: a topic that does not contain mathematics commensurate with the course cannot score well on criterion E however neatly it is presented.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's maths exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor can test whether her proposed topic contains enough mathematics at her level, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, question her structure, and read her own drafts and comment on them. A tutor cannot choose her topic, do the mathematics, write sections, or supply text or working that ends up in the submission. The test is whether she could explain, without notes, why every line says what it says. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: My son understands maths in lessons but collapses in tests. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always method and timing rather than comprehension, and it is the most common presenting problem from this cluster. The specific habits are working omitted so a correct answer scores one mark out of four, rounding applied at an intermediate step so later accuracy marks fall away, stationary points found but never classified, and the final long question abandoned rather than attempted partially. One timed paper marked properly against the published mark scheme will name his three or four recurring reasons.

faqs.question: Will AI Higher Level be accepted for an engineering degree application?
faqs.answer: Read the published entry requirements for the specific institutions and courses rather than relying on a general answer, because they differ and they change. The pattern across engineering, mathematics and physics programmes internationally is a preference or requirement for Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while Applications and Interpretation is accepted widely but can be insufficient for mathematical degrees. Check this during the first Diploma year, because switching course after teaching has begun is difficult and sometimes impossible on the timetable.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level realistic for an average MYP mathematician?
faqs.answer: It depends on fluency rather than on grade. AA HL assumes algebraic operations are automatic and builds quickly on top of them, so a student who can factorise and rearrange accurately but slowly will find the first term very hard, regardless of a solid MYP 5 result. The honest test is two marked Higher Level past-paper questions early on. A short bridging block over the summer on indices, surds, algebraic fractions and function notation changes the answer for a lot of students.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor for the graphic display calculator?
faqs.answer: Often two sessions rather than a course. The useful skills are knowing which paper permits the calculator and what it is legitimately for, solving numerically, finding intersections, working with distributions, and storing intermediate values to avoid rounding error. In Applications and Interpretation the calculator is central to the course; in Analysis and Approaches it is a tool that must not replace analytic method, and students who lean on it lose marks on exactly the questions designed to test the method.

faqs.question: How much does IB maths tutoring cost around Academic City?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026, attributed to whoever published them: qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one with travel runs AED 180 to 500. For Higher Level work the budget band under AED 100 rarely contains anybody who teaches the course.

faqs.question: Is Mirdif or Silicon Oasis better for finding a Diploma maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Marginally Mirdif, because Uptown International School runs the full IB continuum inside the district and the school run is short enough for a 4.45pm session. But the difference is logistical. Neither neighbourhood contains a usable local choice of Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists, because that supply is set across the emirate rather than district by district. Once lessons are online, Mirdif, Silicon Oasis, Academic City and International City all draw from the same pool, which is larger than any of them had locally.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Higher Level maths student need?
faqs.answer: One a week through the first Diploma year is the usual starting point, moving to two in the second year for Higher Level students, particularly through the mock period and the exploration deadline. Two sessions a week is a real commitment from International City, where weekday starts slip towards six; one weekday evening plus a weekend morning usually works better there. The weekend slot is also where a full timed paper can actually be sat, which cannot be done properly at seven in the evening.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both maths and physics for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming, because the overlap in calculus and mechanics makes the combination efficient when it works. Where we would not combine is Higher Level in both, or where the tutor's depth is clearly in one and nominal in the other. Ask for the specific cohorts they have taught in each: a tutor who can walk a student through a Higher Level mark scheme in both subjects, question by question, is the real thing and will not mind proving it.

faqs.question: When should the exploration be finished to avoid the February crush?
faqs.answer: Topic chosen and tested against criterion E by the end of the first Diploma year, and the mathematics drafted before mock preparation begins. In most schools here the exploration deadline, the Extended Essay submission, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the mocks collide in a few weeks in January and February, and the exploration is the piece that gets sacrificed because it feels furthest from the examination. It is worth twenty marks in a subject, which is not a small thing to sacrifice.

faqs.question: Is a maths tutor working in Academic City required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can price it into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified. Ask the person teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

faqs.question: What if my child's exact maths combination is not available?
faqs.answer: You hear it at the enquiry stage. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the weeks before mock examinations is the combination we most often cannot staff well, because every Diploma family in the emirate wants the same specialists in the same fortnight. In that case we give a realistic wait, or we say no. What we will not do is assign a Standard Level tutor to a Higher Level student and let a pleasant trial lesson sell the arrangement for us.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-academic-c.closingBody: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, which school, and what the last marked assessment said. With those four facts we can tell you honestly whether a specialist in that exact combination is free, what one timed paper is likely to reveal, and whether the exploration needs attention before anything else. The trial lesson is free, it is a real lesson rather than a sales call, and you get a written note of what the tutor found. Lessons are one-to-one and online, on Gulf Standard Time, from Academic City to International City alike.

intro.heading: Does anyone near Dubai Creek Harbour actually know this syllabus?
paragraphs: That is the real question, so here is the real answer. IB Mathematics is not one subject. It is four courses: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. They have different content, different calculator rules, different paper structures, and a different kind of Exploration. A tutor who has taught A Level Mathematics for fifteen years and has never marked an IB Exploration against criterion E is a strong mathematician and a weak match. A parent in Dubai Creek Harbour cannot tell the difference from an advertisement, which is why the question gets asked in the first place.

The second part of the answer is about geography. Dubai Creek Harbour has no private school inside its boundary, so the IB students living there attend schools scattered from Dubai Festival City across to Sobha Hartland, Nad Al Sheba and Al Jaddaf. Within a practical driving radius of Ras Al Khor the pool of tutors who have genuinely taught Analysis and Approaches HL to completion is thin. Not absent, but thin enough that a family searching on proximity will usually be offered somebody adjacent rather than somebody exact. Removing travel from the equation is what widens that pool, and it is the only reason IB Gram's delivery model looks the way it does.

So tuition for UAE families is one-to-one, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Dubai Creek Harbour or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting exists only in our India service. Stated plainly rather than buried, because a family deciding between a visiting tutor and an online specialist deserves to know which one they are reading about. The comparison in the cost section below sets out what the visiting premium buys and what it costs in choice.

What a route-correct match looks like in practice is narrow and checkable. Before the first lesson we confirm whether your child sits Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, which Exploration stage they are at, and what their most recent internal assessment mark was out of what. Those four facts determine the work. A Standard Level Applications student struggling with statistical inference needs almost nothing in common with a Higher Level Analysis student stuck on the Maclaurin series, and a tutor who treats them the same is not a specialist.

The third thing worth saying before the detail starts: the Exploration is 20% of the grade in every one of the four courses, and it is the component where tutoring help is most useful and most easily misused. A tutor may read a draft, mark it against the published criteria, explain what criterion D actually rewards, and model reflection on a different investigation. A tutor may not write it, restructure it to a standard, or supply the mathematics. The boundary is not a formality; breaching it is a malpractice matter for the candidate, not for the tutor.

Everything below is specific: the AA against AI decision with its university consequences, the paper weightings and durations at both levels, the Exploration criteria by letter with their mark allocations, where marks actually go missing, what the Dubai market charges, and the schools around Creek Harbour whose timetables we schedule around.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harb.programmesIntro: Creek Harbour families meet IB mathematics at three points, and the useful tutoring looks different at each. These are the programmes we cover and what the maths actually demands in each one.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two years, one of four course and level combinations, assessed by written papers plus a mathematical Exploration worth 20%. Standard Level sits two papers of ninety minutes each; Higher Level sits two papers of two hours plus a third paper of one hour. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is taken without technology; Applications and Interpretation permits a graphic display calculator throughout.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the main May session, and that is the one Creek Harbour families plan around. No specific IB session or results date is published on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a landing page is worse than no date. Confirm every deadline with your school's IB coordinator, who holds the internal timetable for Exploration drafts as well as the external one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment across knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There are no external papers in most MYP years, so the grade comes from internal tasks. The investigating-patterns criterion is the one that prepares a student for the Exploration, and it is the one most often taught lightly.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving Creek Harbour run MYP to Year 11 and then move into the Diploma, which means a student arrives in Year 12 having never sat a timed written maths paper. That transition is the single most common reason a Creek Harbour family contacts us in the autumn term of Year 12, and it is a technique problem more than a content problem.

programmes.name: The IGCSE route into Diploma maths
programmes.description: Many Creek Harbour pupils sit Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 at sixteen and then enter the Diploma. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 is the strongest bridge into Analysis and Approaches, because it introduces differentiation, integration and binomial expansion a year early.
programmes.countryNote: A student entering Analysis and Approaches HL from 0580 Extended alone, without 0606, usually has a real gap in algebraic fluency and in function manipulation. It is closable in a term if it is identified in Year 11 rather than in Year 12. Where a family is choosing options now, this is the decision with the longest shadow.

programmes.name: What universities do with the maths grade
programmes.description: Engineering, mathematics, physics, economics and computer science courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and some will not accept Applications and Interpretation as a substitute. Courses in the social sciences, business and design are frequently satisfied by Applications at either level.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, no IB points threshold is published on this page, because no figure could be read on the Ministry's own site and an unsourced number would be a liability on every page carrying it. Check your own case with the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority. Nothing here implies tutoring is needed for equivalency or admission.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-creek-harb.subjectsIntro: Within IB Mathematics the requests from Creek Harbour families cluster around the same topics, and they cluster for structural reasons rather than random ones. These are the ones we are asked for most, with what each actually demands.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL — calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration techniques, implicit differentiation, related rates, volumes of revolution, differential equations and the Maclaurin series. This is where the HL grade is decided and where Paper 3 most often draws its extended investigation. Students lose marks on notation and on unjustified steps rather than on the method itself.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL — proof and complex numbers
subjects.description: Proof by induction, proof by contradiction, counterexamples, and complex numbers in Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential form including De Moivre's theorem. Induction is a technique question: the structure earns marks, so a student who writes the inductive step as a template scores above one who improvises it.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL — functions and algebra
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, transformations of graphs, quadratics, exponentials and logarithms, and sequences and series. Paper 1 is sat without technology, so algebraic fluency is not optional. Most lost marks here are sign errors inside a correct method.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL — statistics and probability
subjects.description: Sampling, correlation and regression, probability distributions, hypothesis testing including chi-squared and t-tests, and the interpretation that follows the calculation. The discriminator is not the test statistic; it is stating the conclusion in context with reference to the significance level.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL — modelling
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic, exponential and trigonometric models, piecewise functions, and the choice of model to fit a dataset. Technology is permitted throughout, which moves the marks from computation to justification: why this model, what the parameters mean, where it stops being valid.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and geometry, both routes
subjects.description: Radian measure, identities, equations, the ambiguous case of the sine rule, and in Applications the use of Voronoi diagrams and three-dimensional geometry. The reliable failure is a calculator left in degrees for a radian question, which costs a correct method its answer mark.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Vector equations of lines and planes, scalar and vector products, intersections and angles between lines and planes, and distance problems. Students who can sketch the configuration before computing outperform those who go straight to the algebra, because most errors here are geometric misreadings.

subjects.name: The mathematical Exploration
subjects.levels: All four courses · 20% of the grade
subjects.description: An individual written investigation, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic too large to carry genuine personal engagement, chosen late. Topic choice is where tutoring earns the most and is most clearly legitimate.

subjects.name: Paper 3 technique, Higher Level only
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions over one hour, worth 20% of the HL grade, requiring a student to follow an unfamiliar investigation through guided stages. It cannot be revised by topic. It is practised by doing past Paper 3 questions and learning to read the scaffolding.

subjects.name: Calculator technique and the GDC
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections, statistical functions, distributions and regression on the graphic display calculator. On Applications papers and on AA Paper 2 this is marked skill, not a convenience, and a student who navigates menus slowly loses marks to the clock rather than to the mathematics.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: which one is your child on?
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Creek Harbour is useless until this is settled, and a surprising number of families do not know. The two routes diverge in content and in purpose. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented course: function manipulation, calculus technique, induction, complex numbers at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics course: regression, hypothesis testing, Voronoi diagrams, financial mathematics, and the interpretation that follows a calculation made with technology.

The calculator rule is the quickest way to tell them apart in practice. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without technology, which means algebraic fluency is a scored skill rather than a convenience. Applications and Interpretation permits a graphic display calculator in both papers, which moves the marks away from computation and towards justification: why this model, what do the parameters mean, where does the model stop being valid. A student who is strong at arithmetic and weak at explanation often scores better on AA than on AI, which is the opposite of what families assume.

The consequence that matters most is university entry. Engineering, mathematics, physics, computer science and many economics courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a number of them will not accept Applications as an equivalent. Social science, business, design and health-related courses are frequently satisfied by Applications at either level. A Creek Harbour student in Year 11 choosing between the two is making a decision about which degrees remain open, and the school's own university guidance counsellor is the right person to confirm a specific course requirement.
The table below sets the two routes against each other on the things that change the tutoring, rather than on the things that make a nice brochure.

sections.heading: The papers, the durations and the weightings at both levels
paragraphs: Here is the assessment structure a Creek Harbour parent should be able to recite, because every planning decision follows from it. At Standard Level there are two written papers of ninety minutes each, carrying forty per cent of the grade apiece, plus the Exploration at twenty per cent. At Higher Level there are two papers of two hours each at thirty per cent apiece, a third paper of one hour at twenty per cent, and the Exploration at twenty per cent. That is the whole of it, and it is published by the IB.

Two things fall out immediately. First, the Exploration is one fifth of the grade in every version of the course, and it is the only component a student controls entirely. A Standard Level student who leaves the Exploration to the last fortnight has gambled twenty per cent of their grade on a bad week. Second, Higher Level Paper 3 is also twenty per cent, and it is the component least amenable to topic revision, because it presents an unfamiliar extended investigation in guided stages. Those two components together are forty per cent of an HL grade and neither is improved by re-reading notes.

The planning consequence for a Creek Harbour family is a sequencing one. The Exploration work belongs in the quieter part of the two-year cycle, not in the term where mock papers and other subjects' internal assessments are due. Paper 3 practice belongs in the final stretch, after the content is substantially complete, because it draws on all of it. A tutoring plan that treats the whole two years as undifferentiated weekly maths misses both of these.

We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and an unverified exam date on a landing page is a date a family might act on. UAE schools sit the main May session; for every deadline that matters, including Exploration draft deadlines, your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative internal calendar.

sections.heading: The Exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes the Exploration criteria with their mark allocations, which is strange, because they are the specification for twenty per cent of the grade and they are the single most actionable thing a family can read. There are five criteria. Presentation carries four marks. Mathematical communication carries four. Personal engagement carries three. Reflection carries three. Use of mathematics carries six, and it is the largest single block. Twenty marks in total.

Read that allocation again and a pattern appears. Use of mathematics is the biggest criterion, but presentation and mathematical communication together carry eight marks, more than any single criterion, and they are awarded for structure, notation, consistent use of symbols, defined variables and a coherent line of reasoning. Those are marks a competent student loses by carelessness rather than by ignorance. Reflection, at three marks, is the criterion most often left as a closing paragraph when it should be present throughout the investigation, commenting on choices as they are made.

Personal engagement, also three marks, is where topic choice decides the outcome before any mathematics is written. A topic that is genuinely the student's own produces engagement naturally; a topic chosen from a list of safe ideas produces a document that reads like a textbook extract. This is why topic coaching is the highest-value legitimate help a tutor can give on the Exploration, and why it should happen early rather than after a first draft exists.

The boundary on all of this is firm. A tutor reads the student's draft and marks it against these criteria. A tutor explains what a criterion rewards. A tutor models reflection on an unrelated investigation. A tutor does not write the Exploration, does not restructure it to a standard, and does not supply the mathematics. There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright. That is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Ask a Creek Harbour parent why their child's maths grade dropped and the answer is usually that the topics got harder. Ask the mark scheme and the answer is often different. A large share of lost marks on IB maths papers are not knowledge failures. They are notation failures, timing failures, calculator-mode failures and failures to claim method marks that were already earned.

The clearest example is the unjustified step. A student arrives at a correct answer in three lines where the mark scheme expects five, and loses two method marks on a question they fully understood. This is epidemic on Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, where no technology is available and the working is the entire evidence of reasoning. The fix is mechanical and fast: write the line you would be tempted to do in your head. It takes a fortnight of enforced practice and it is worth more than a month of new content.

The second is the calculator left in degrees for a radian question, or a graphic display calculator the student can use but not navigate quickly. On Paper 2 and on Applications papers, calculator fluency is assessed, and a student who takes ninety seconds to find a regression function has lost the question to the clock rather than to the mathematics. The third, specific to Applications, is the conclusion stated as a number instead of as a statement in context with reference to the significance level. The statistics were right; the answer mark went elsewhere.

This is why a diagnostic paper comes before any teaching plan. We ask the student to sit a timed paper on their exact course and level, mark it against the published scheme question by question, and let the marking choose the topic list. A list built that way shortens week by week. A list built from the syllabus contents page never does.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor costs around Dubai Creek Harbour
paragraphs: Take the cheapest end first, because it is the end most families start at and the one with the widest quality spread. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya, which usually means a university student teaching a subject they sat recently. For general homework support in a Standard Level course that can work. For Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or for Exploration feedback against five published criteria, it generally does not, and the reason is specificity rather than ability.

A qualified subject tutor working online in Dubai is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. IB specialist rates run from around AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 or more. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650. Those are each provider's own published figures, read in October 2026, and they are the market, not IB Gram's price list.

The in-home comparison is where Creek Harbour geography becomes a line item. Visiting one-to-one rates in Dubai are quoted from AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and from AED 200 to AED 500 by home-tutor providers. What it costs is the size of the pool you can select from, and for Analysis and Approaches HL that pool is already narrow.

IB Gram publishes no hourly figure here. The right number depends on route, level, Exploration stage and how close the May session is, and a single printed rate would be wrong for most people reading this. One free trial lesson per student comes first, with the quote given after a tutor has seen the work. No payment and no card details are required to book it.

sections.heading: The MYP to Diploma jump in maths, and why it bites in Year 12
paragraphs: Several schools serving Dubai Creek Harbour run the Middle Years Programme through Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma. MYP mathematics is criterion-assessed through internal tasks: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no external timed paper in most MYP years. A student can therefore reach Year 12 with a strong maths record and no experience of a ninety-minute written examination.

The gap that opens is rarely about content. It is about pace under timed conditions, about writing method for a marker rather than for a teacher who knows the student, and about the absence of a second attempt. MYP tasks are often revisited and resubmitted; Diploma papers are not. The first Year 12 assessment is where this becomes visible, and it is the most common reason a Creek Harbour family contacts us in the autumn term rather than in the spring.

The one piece of MYP that genuinely prepares a student for the Diploma is the investigating-patterns criterion, and it maps almost directly onto the Exploration. A student who learned to generalise a pattern, justify a rule and reflect on its limits in Year 10 has a head start on criterion D and criterion E. A student whose MYP investigations were completed quickly to a template does not, and will meet those criteria for the first time with twenty per cent of a grade attached.

The fix is not more content teaching. It is timed-paper exposure early in Year 12, marked strictly to the published scheme, plus one Exploration-style investigation attempted before the real one is chosen. Both are cheap in hours and both are usually skipped, because they feel like a detour from the syllabus.

sections.heading: Schools, KHDA and what a Creek Harbour parent can verify
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai had 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25, offering seventeen curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent on UK curricula. Seven more private schools join the market for the 2026-27 intake, three of them IB, creating 16,846 new places. KHDA also confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

What a parent should take from that is scale and context, not endorsement. A KHDA inspection rating is a judgement about a school. It says nothing about any tutor, and no tutoring provider inherits it. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes with premises and staff, with initial approval first and annual renewal, and we do not hold one. Any provider implying regulator endorsement is making a claim worth checking before you buy.

Tutoring itself is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, with no fee and a stated two working days. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount appears here.

One further point specific to maths. A Creek Harbour family may be tempted to ask their child's own maths teacher for private lessons. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The person who teaches the class and moderates the Exploration should not be paid separately by one family in it.

sections.heading: Getting matched from Dubai Creek Harbour, and what we do when nobody is free
paragraphs: The sequence is deliberately short. Send the course and level, the Exploration stage, the most recent internal mark out of what, and two or three evening windows that genuinely survive a normal week after the school run. We match a route specialist, run one free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and give you a plan afterwards. Nothing is charged before the trial and no card details are needed to book it.

Then the part other pages omit. Specialists in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level are genuinely scarce, and the scarcity concentrates in the weeks before the May session, which is exactly when demand peaks. If nobody with the right route and level has a slot in your window, we will say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing a general maths tutor and calling it an IB match. The alternatives are a different time slot, a shorter weekly commitment with a specialist whose availability is limited, or paper-technique work while the subject slot is pending.

There is a scheduling lever worth knowing about. The weekday window between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time is the busiest hour in the UAE tutoring day, and it is also the only window a Creek Harbour family with a Nad Al Sheba commute can realistically use on a school night. Families able to offer a weekend morning have materially more choice of tutor, and for Higher Level routes that often decides whether the match is exact or approximate.

Finally, the limits. Nobody can promise a grade and this page does not. Nothing here implies that tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission, or for progression at school; those are regulatory and institutional processes with their own published rules, and the authority rather than a tutoring provider is where to verify them. What a route-correct match can do is turn hours the student is already spending into marks the mark scheme will actually award.

faqs.question: Is there really an IB maths tutor near me in Dubai Creek Harbour who knows Analysis and Approaches HL?
faqs.answer: Within a short drive of Ras Al Khor, the pool of tutors who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to completion is small. Not empty, but small enough that a proximity search usually returns someone adjacent: a strong A Level mathematician, or an IB tutor whose experience is Standard Level or the Applications route. IB Gram solves it by removing travel. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to your child's exact route and level. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, which is precisely what makes the national specialist pool available to a Creek Harbour family.

faqs.question: Creek Harbour schools offer two IB maths routes — which one does a parent need to understand first?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented course: function manipulation, calculus technique, and at Higher Level induction, complex numbers and the Maclaurin series. Its Paper 1 is sat without technology. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics course: regression, hypothesis testing, Voronoi diagrams and financial mathematics, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. Neither is simply harder. They are differently harder, and the practical difference is university entry: engineering, mathematics, physics and computer science courses commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and some will not accept Applications instead.

faqs.question: Out of the final maths grade, what proportion rests on the Exploration rather than the papers?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four course and level combinations. It is assessed on five criteria: presentation at four marks, mathematical communication at four, personal engagement at three, reflection at three, and use of mathematics at six, for twenty marks in total. The practical significance is that one fifth of the grade is the only component a student fully controls, and it rewards planning rather than revision. A student who leaves it to the final fortnight has gambled that proportion of their grade on one difficult week, usually the week other subjects' deadlines also land.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 3 test, and can it be revised by topic?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat at Higher Level only, lasts one hour, and carries twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade. It presents two extended problem-solving questions that walk a student through an unfamiliar investigation in guided stages. It cannot be revised by topic, because its content is drawn from across the course and its difficulty lies in reading the scaffolding and following it. It is practised as a format: attempt past Paper 3 questions, read how each one is structured before answering, and learn to use the earlier parts as the route into the later ones.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my child's maths Exploration?
faqs.answer: No, and you should decline any offer to do so. A tutor may read the student's own draft and mark it against the five published criteria, explain what a criterion rewards, help narrow a topic until genuine personal engagement is possible, and model reflection on an unrelated investigation. A tutor may not write it, restructure it to a standard, or supply the mathematics. There are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments. That is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the seller. We record whose work was in front of us at each session.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 12 after MYP and suddenly struggling with timed maths papers. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is common and it is usually a technique gap rather than a content gap. Middle Years Programme mathematics is criterion-assessed through internal tasks, often revisited and resubmitted, with no external timed paper in most years. Diploma papers are timed, marked by someone who does not know the student, and offer no second attempt. The fix is exposure: timed papers early in Year 12, marked strictly to the published scheme, plus one practice investigation before the real Exploration topic is chosen. Both are inexpensive in hours and both are routinely skipped as a detour from the syllabus.

faqs.question: What should a Dubai Creek Harbour family expect to pay for IB maths tuition each month?
faqs.answer: Working from the market's own published figures rather than from an hourly rate in isolation: Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those were read in October 2026 and belong to other providers, not to IB Gram. Our quote follows the free trial lesson, because it depends on route, level and how close the session is.

faqs.question: Is a cheap online tutor at AED 50 an hour good enough for Standard Level maths?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, for a narrow purpose. Budget online tutoring in Dubai is advertised from AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya and from AED 45 to AED 65 by EdFlik, which typically means a university student teaching a subject they sat recently. For unblocking homework in a Standard Level course that can genuinely work. For Exploration feedback against five published criteria, for Paper 3 technique, or for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, it usually does not, and the reason is specificity rather than ability. Match the tier to the job rather than to the budget alone.

faqs.question: Which schools near Dubai Creek Harbour run the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: No private school sits inside Dubai Creek Harbour, so students commute. Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is immediately across the Creek in Al Jaddaf. Universal American School Dubai sits in Dubai Festival City, the nearest cluster. South along Al Khail Road, North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland and GEMS Modern Academy in Nad Al Sheba both run Diploma programmes. KHDA reported the International Baccalaureate at seven per cent of Dubai private enrolment in 2024-25, and three of the seven new schools for the 2026-27 intake are IB. Schools are named as market context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: When can an IB maths session start if my child commutes to Nad Al Sheba?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect. Secondary schools in the Nad Al Sheba and Meydan corridor finish in the mid-afternoon, and the run back to Creek Harbour puts a student on Al Khail Road at the school-run hour, so 17:15 is a realistic first slot on a normal weekday and later on a co-curricular day. Choose the slot for your worst normal weekday rather than your best. If any part of the weekend is available, a Saturday or Sunday morning session is worth more than the same hour at 18:30, and it widens the choice of Higher Level specialist considerably.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. KHDA is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority and is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; it regulates and inspects schools, and a school's inspection rating is a judgement about that school rather than about any tutor. A KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes with premises and staff. Treat any provider implying regulator endorsement as a reason to check their other claims.

faqs.question: Does the tutor teaching my child need a UAE permit, and can I check it?
faqs.answer: An individual providing private tutoring in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own Private Tutor Licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask for the permit category. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the IB exam dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the IB's own site, which blocks automated checking. An unverified exam date on a landing page is a date a family might plan a term of revision around, and getting it wrong is worse than omitting it. UAE schools sit the main May session. For every date that matters, including internal Exploration draft deadlines, your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative calendar. By contrast, the Cambridge and Pearson dates referenced elsewhere on this site come from those boards' own published timetable pages and are cited accordingly.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an IB maths student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: Most Creek Harbour families start with one weekly hour and raise it only for a reason. One hour a week suits a student who follows lessons but makes consistent errors; two suits a Higher Level student carrying both a content gap and an Exploration deadline. Beyond two weekly hours, the limiting factor is usually the student's own practice time rather than tuition. We would rather schedule one well-placed session the school run can survive than two the family cancels by the third week, and the plan is reviewed at the school's next assessment.

faqs.question: Would pairing maths and physics with the same tutor save us an evening on the Creek Harbour schedule?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and we would not optimise for it. The overlap in content is real, particularly in mechanics and in calculus applications, so a tutor comfortable with both exists. But the Exploration in maths and the Internal Assessment in physics are assessed against different criteria and need different coaching, and Paper 3 at Higher Level maths is a distinct format. If one specialist genuinely covers both at the right level, the scheduling convenience is a real benefit. If not, two exact matches beat one approximate one.

intro.heading: What an IB maths tutor is actually being paid to fix
paragraphs: Break the cost down by job rather than by month, because IB mathematics is four separate problems wearing one subject name. The first is Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, which is sat without a calculator and which exposes any student who has been leaning on a graphic display calculator for routine algebra. The second is Paper 3, which exists only at Higher Level and asks for sustained reasoning across an extended problem rather than recall. The third is the exploration, worth a fifth of the final grade. The fourth is a route decision taken before Year 12 that is now the wrong one.

Each of those costs a different amount to address, and that is the useful way to think about a budget. A Paper 1 algebra weakness is a procedural fix: six to eight focused sessions of non-calculator practice, marked, with the errors classified. A Paper 3 weakness is slower, because sustained reasoning is a habit rather than a technique. Exploration support is short and front-loaded by design. A route mismatch is not a tutoring problem at all in the first instance; it is a conversation with the school.

The market bands are the ones published across Dubai and read in October 2026. Unitors advertises IB tuition from AED 200 an hour. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and TutorChase publishes AED 270. The budget online band sits at AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the figure. None of these is an IB Gram price.

Where Dubai Festival City families most often waste money in this subject is on the wrong course. A tutor advertising IB maths who is strong in Applications and Interpretation will teach an Analysis and Approaches student competently for weeks before the mismatch shows, because the two courses share plenty of content. What they do not share is the emphasis: AA leans on algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof, AI on modelling, statistics and technology-led reasoning. Ask which one before you book, and ask the tutor to say how they differ.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Al Badia and the eastern suburbs, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For mathematics specifically that format is better rather than merely cheaper: a shared screen shows the same working to both people at the same size, a non-calculator question can be annotated line by line as the error appears, and the graphic display calculator screen can be shown directly rather than described.

The rest of this page sets out what each paper is worth, where marks actually go missing by topic, what the exploration criteria reward, what each of those fixes costs against the market bands, and which route UAE and overseas admissions expect. It is written to be used, so take the paper weightings to your child's maths teacher and check them against the school's own copy of the subject guide.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-festival-c.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through every IB programme and changes shape at each transition, which is where most Dubai Festival City families discover a gap. These are the three stages and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Number, pattern, shape, space and data handling taught through units of inquiry, with no external examination. The mathematical content is modest; the valuable habit built here is explaining a method out loud, which is exactly what criterion-based marking will ask for three years later.
programmes.countryNote: For Dubai Festival City families this is where times-table and mental-arithmetic fluency should be settled. A student who reaches Middle Years without automatic recall will spend Diploma Paper 1 preparation relearning it under time pressure, at four or five times the hourly rate. The cheapest maths tuition anyone ever buys is in Year 4.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, A to D, each on a 1 to 8 scale, with the totals converted to a 1 to 7 grade. Criterion A is knowing and understanding, and it is the one most parents assume is the whole subject. The investigating-patterns and applying-in-context criteria are where students with good arithmetic routinely lose bands.
programmes.countryNote: MYP mathematics in Dubai is also where the Diploma route is effectively decided, because standard and extended mathematics in Years 9 and 10 feed naturally into AI and AA respectively. A family thinking about Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level should be asking about this in Year 9, not Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses, each at Higher and Standard Level. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology, with the calculator permitted throughout. Both carry a mathematical exploration worth 20 per cent, and Higher Level in both adds a Paper 3.
programmes.countryNote: Deira International School runs the IB continuum through to Diploma, so a Dubai Festival City student may make this choice inside the same campus they have attended for years. dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-festival-c.subjectsIntro: This grid is the IB mathematics syllabus broken into the topics tuition is actually bought for, with where the marks go in each. Take it to a prospective tutor and ask them to talk about any three.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, binomial expansion, and at AA HL proof and complex numbers. This is the topic that decides Paper 1 in AA, because every manipulation has to be exact without a calculator. Errors here are almost always procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations, and rational functions at Higher Level. Marks are lost on domain restrictions that students treat as decoration, and on sketches drawn without the asymptotes that carry the marks.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Triangles, circular functions, identities and equations, with vectors at AA HL. Trigonometric equations are the commonest place a student finds some of the solutions and loses the rest by not considering the full interval required.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA SL and HL, AI at a lighter weighting
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at AA HL, techniques including substitution and parts plus differential equations. The AA HL calculus questions in Paper 2 are where the long structured marks sit, and where untidy intermediate working costs method marks.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI SL and HL heavily; AA more lightly
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability distributions and hypothesis testing in AI. The AI student's commonest loss is interpretation: a correctly computed regression described in words that say nothing about the context earns the calculation and loses the rest.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An independent piece of mathematics on a topic of the student's choosing, marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic too large to handle properly in the space available.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, AA
subjects.description: Sat without a calculator, which is a separate skill from doing the mathematics. Exact values, surds, fractions and clean algebraic steps. Students who have practised only with a calculator in hand lose marks they could do, which makes this the highest-return thing to drill.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level only
subjects.description: An extended problem-solving paper where each part builds on the last, so an early error propagates. The skill is sustained reasoning and reading ahead, and it is the component that responds least well to last-minute preparation.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: Solving equations, finding intersections, regression, distributions and numerical calculus on the device. Weak calculator skills cost marks in AI and in AA Paper 2, and over-reliance on the device hides the algebra gap that then surfaces in AA Paper 1.

subjects.name: MYP to DP transition mathematics
subjects.description: The step into either Diploma course assumes fluent algebraic manipulation, confident handling of indices and surds, and comfort rearranging formulae. A student who met those topics but never automated them will feel the Diploma as a sudden difficulty rather than a gradual one.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that determines everything else, and it is made in Year 11 by students who often cannot articulate the difference. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving, with the calculator permitted throughout both papers. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and both carry a mathematical exploration worth a fifth of the grade.

The common error is treating AI as the easier course. It is not easier; it is different. An AI Higher Level student handles substantial statistics, regression and distributions, and has to interpret results in context, which is a demanding and distinct skill. What AI does not demand is the exact non-calculator manipulation that AA Paper 1 lives on. A student with weak algebra and strong interpretive instincts may genuinely be better served by AI and should not be talked out of it.

The reverse error is choosing AI to avoid difficulty and discovering a closed door later. Some university programmes, particularly in engineering, mathematics, physics and economics at competitive institutions, specify Analysis and Approaches or set a Higher Level mathematics requirement that AI Standard Level does not meet. Requirements vary by institution and change, so the only reliable method is to read the admissions page for the specific course and the specific year, and to involve the school's university counsellor early.

For a Dubai Festival City family the practical sequence is: ask the school which course the student is currently tracked towards, ask why, and then test the assumption against two or three target degree subjects rather than against a general sense of ambition. If a change is warranted, the window is the end of Year 11 and the very start of Year 12. After that the cost of switching rises sharply, in both tuition and lost ground.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth and how long it runs
paragraphs: Weightings are the most useful thing a parent can know and the thing almost no tutoring page states. At Standard Level in both courses, Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 40 per cent of the final grade and the exploration carries 20 per cent. At Higher Level in both courses, Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 30 per cent, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and the exploration carries 20 per cent. Check those against your child's school copy of the subject guide, because the guide is the authority and we do not reproduce it.

Durations follow the same pattern. Standard Level Papers 1 and 2 run for ninety minutes each. Higher Level Papers 1 and 2 run for two hours each, and Paper 3 for one hour. The arithmetic worth doing is this: at Higher Level, Paper 3 and the exploration together carry 40 per cent of the grade and occupy one hour of examination plus a piece of coursework. That is a very large share of the grade sitting in the two components students prepare for least.

This is where a cost argument becomes concrete. If 20 per cent of the grade sits in a sixty-minute paper that responds to strategy and practice, then a block of sessions aimed at Paper 3 is better value than the same number of sessions spread across general revision. The same logic applies to the exploration, where a handful of well-timed hours at the question-setting stage can move a criterion band that an entire term of content teaching will not touch.

For many students the correct conclusion is that Paper 2 is already fine, that Paper 1 needs a short drilling block, and that nobody has yet thought about Paper 3 at all. That is a cheaper plan than weekly cover across everything, and a better one.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Most lost marks in Diploma mathematics are not caused by not knowing the mathematics. They are caused by four repeatable habits, and naming them is most of the fix. The first is sign and index slips under time pressure, which is a Paper 1 problem in Analysis and Approaches specifically. The second is working shown so compressed that method marks cannot be awarded, which is a Paper 2 problem at both levels.

The third is answering less than the question asked. A trigonometric equation question that specifies an interval wants every solution in that interval; a student who finds two and stops has done the mathematics and lost the marks. A function sketch wants the asymptotes and intercepts, not a plausible curve. These are reading habits, and they respond to marked practice rather than to explanation.

The fourth is interpretation, which is the AI student's version of the same problem. A regression is computed correctly, a correlation coefficient is quoted, and then the written answer says nothing about what it means for the context in the question. The calculation marks arrive and the interpretation marks do not. Teaching a student to write one honest sentence about context after every statistical result is a cheap intervention with a visible effect.

The diagnostic method that works is unglamorous. Take the student's last two marked papers, classify every lost mark into one of those four buckets plus a fifth for genuine content gaps, and count. Most students produce a strongly skewed distribution, and the plan then writes itself. A tutor who starts by doing this rather than by teaching topic one is a tutor who intends to make the hours count.

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration: a fifth of the grade, marked on five criteria
paragraphs: The exploration is an independent piece of mathematics written by the student on a topic of their own choosing, and it carries 20 per cent of the final grade in all four courses. It is marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. Your child's teacher holds the current criteria and mark allocations in the subject guide; ask for them and work from the school's copy, because we do not reproduce board documents.

The commonest failure has nothing to do with mathematical ability. It is a topic too large to handle properly in the space available, chosen because it sounded impressive. A narrow question answered thoroughly outscores a grand question answered superficially, every time, because the criteria reward depth of engagement and quality of reflection rather than ambition of subject matter. Fixing a topic choice takes one conversation and saves a term of frustration.

The second commonest failure is reflection treated as a conclusion. Criterion-based reflection means engaging honestly with what the mathematics did and did not show, what assumptions were made, and what a further investigation would change. A paragraph that restates the result in different words scores in the lowest band. This is teachable quickly and almost never taught, because it does not feel like mathematics.

The boundary matters more here than anywhere else in the course. A tutor may discuss topic choice, explain each criterion, model a comparable exploration on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The work is declared as the student's own and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else lands on your child.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs, priced by the job
paragraphs: Hourly bands are the market's language and jobs are the parent's, so here is the translation. The bands first: budget online tuition at AED 33 to 52 from Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 from EdFlik; a qualified online subject tutor across the market at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IB from AED 200; specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 with travel included; and a premium tier at AED 650 from BartyED. All published by those providers and read in October 2026.

Now the jobs. A non-calculator drilling block for AA Paper 1 is six to eight sessions and does not need the top of the market, because the work is repetitive marked practice with error classification. Paper 3 strategy does need a specialist, because a tutor who has not worked through extended problem-solving papers cannot teach reading ahead. Exploration support is three or four hours total but wants someone who knows the criteria. Route advice is usually free and belongs with the school.

That breakdown is why a monthly subscription is the wrong default for mathematics. Bestimate's monthly estimate for an exam-year specialist at one weekly hour is AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above, and a two-year weekly commitment at that level is a serious sum. Several students need exactly that. Many need a block, a gap, another block and an intensive, which costs considerably less and is pointed at the components carrying the marks.

None of the figures above is an IB Gram rate. Our terms follow the free trial lesson and a diagnostic conversation, because quoting one hourly number across MYP number work and AA Higher Level Paper 3 would be misleading in both directions. What the table does is let you price a plan before you talk to anybody, and check any quote you already hold against what the market publishes.

sections.heading: Which maths route universities actually want
paragraphs: This is where a cost decision becomes a consequence decision, and where honesty is more useful than reassurance. Requirements are set by individual institutions and courses, they differ between countries, and they change between admissions cycles. So nobody should be telling a Dubai Festival City family a general rule. What we can say is which questions to ask and where the answers live.

For UAE universities, the first thing to establish is Ministry of Education equivalency, which is separate from a university's own entry requirements. For the British track the sourced requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the IB Diploma we publish no points figure, because none has been read on an official Ministry source, and verification belongs on moe.gov.ae.

For overseas admissions, maths-heavy degrees in engineering, mathematics, physics, computer science and economics are the ones most likely to specify Analysis and Approaches or a Higher Level mathematics grade. Medicine, life sciences and most humanities subjects are usually more flexible. The reliable method is to open the admissions page for the specific course, in the specific year, and to check whether AI Standard Level satisfies it. The school's university counsellor does this for a living.

The practical point for tuition spending is sequencing. If a target degree requires Higher Level mathematics, the money belongs in DP1 building the fluency to survive it, not in DP2 rescuing a student who should have switched. If no target degree requires it, then Higher Level AA chosen for prestige is an expensive decision that will consume tutoring hours for two years. Ask the question before the route is locked, because afterwards every answer costs more.
