whyPoints.title: An honest answer when tutoring is the wrong spend
whyPoints.description: Sometimes the right move is a level change, a conversation with the DP coordinator, or the school's own support sessions, which cost nothing. We say that in the first lesson. A family told the truth in October is a family that comes back in January.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session is it too late to start IB maths tutoring in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: It is never too late to improve paper technique, but what can change narrows sharply. With twelve weeks or more, topic repair and timed-paper work both fit. With six to eight weeks, choose one: either two or three topics taught properly, or full-paper technique and method recording. With under four weeks, the only realistic work is examination technique, command terms and calculator discipline, which can still be worth several marks a paper. What cannot be rescued late is the exploration, because that deadline is set by the school months earlier and will not move.

faqs.question: My son is in DP2 near Dubai Hills Estate and still has no exploration topic. What should happen this week?
faqs.answer: Topic choice this week, not next. The viable topics are the ones where he can get real data or a real model and apply mathematics at the level of his course. Criterion C rewards personal engagement, which cannot be added later, so the topic should connect to something he actually does. Criterion E carries six of the twenty marks and needs mathematics commensurate with the course, which rules out anything that ends at a mean and a bar chart. Book a single session to test two or three candidate topics against the criteria before he commits to one.

faqs.question: Can an IB maths tutor help with the exploration without writing any part of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the only version we offer. A tutor can teach mathematics the exploration needs beyond the class syllabus, check whether the aim is answerable, ask the questions a moderator would ask, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write, redraft, edit to completion or supply text, data or analysis. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic malpractice under IB rules and the penalty falls on the student. Any service offering a completed Internal Assessment is selling your child a disciplinary risk.

faqs.question: Should my daughter move from Analysis and Approaches HL to SL, and when is the last sensible moment?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to your daughter and her DP coordinator, because the school holds the entry and the timetable. What a tutor can contribute is evidence: whether the marks lost are knowledge gaps that a term of teaching closes, or whether the HL calculus and proof content is genuinely out of reach alongside her other five subjects. Make the call early in DP2 rather than after the mocks, because option changes get harder once final entries are submitted. A student scoring consistently at a 3 in HL in January is usually better served by a strong SL grade.

faqs.question: How many IB maths sessions a week does a DP2 student in this part of Dubai usually take?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour is the normal starting point and is enough when the problem is a specific topic or technique. Two sessions a week make sense in two situations: an exploration deadline inside the next month, where one session handles the exploration and the other keeps pace with class content, or the run into mocks, where one session sits a paper and the other marks and repairs it. More than two weekly hours in one subject rarely helps, because the limiting factor becomes the student's own practice time rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tuition cost per hour around Dubai Hills Estate in 2026?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market figures as of October 2026: budget online platforms from roughly AED 33 to 150, with Tutopiya advertising AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik AED 45 to 65; qualified online subject tutors AED 150 to 300, with Unitors pricing IB from AED 200; IB and IGCSE specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and the Bestimate Dubai survey at 200 to 450+; premium named tutors up to AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because the rate carries travel. Those are market rates, not ours; our quote follows the free first lesson and the written plan.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a villa in Dubai Hills Estate?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one and live over video, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own working on camera and written notes afterwards. The practical gain is specialism: instead of choosing among mathematics teachers who live a short drive from Dubai Hills Estate and have that evening free, you choose an Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation specialist at the exact level your child sits, and the 16:30 slot is actually reachable.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson start if the bus gets back to Dubai Hills Estate at 15:50?
faqs.answer: Most families here settle on 16:30 or 17:00. That leaves time to eat and change, and it finishes early enough that homework still gets done and the student is not working at 21:00. Slots run to about 21:00 on school nights for older students who have co-curricular commitments, and weekend mornings work well for exploration sessions that need a longer unbroken block. During Ramadan the same lesson usually moves to after Iftar. Because delivery is online, none of these times depends on anyone completing a drive through the Al Quoz corridor at rush hour.

faqs.question: For engineering at a UAE university, is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation the right course?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme's published entry requirements rather than relying on a general rule, because UAE universities set their own. The broad pattern is that engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, because of the calculus and algebra content, while Applications and Interpretation suits business, design, social sciences and health routes. Ask the admissions page of each target university and ask your DP coordinator what the school can timetable, then decide. A tutor can explain the content difference; only the university can tell you what it accepts.

faqs.question: How is Paper 3 different from Paper 1 and Paper 2 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sixty minutes long, worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade, and consists of two compulsory extended problems rather than a spread of shorter questions. Each problem builds in stages, so part (c) usually depends on part (b) being right. A calculator is required. The skill it tests is sustaining an unfamiliar argument across twenty or thirty minutes, which is different from recognising a question type. It is also the component schools often reach last, which makes a full timed Paper 3 under examination conditions one of the highest-yield tutoring hours available at HL.

faqs.question: Can lessons shift to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we ask about it before the month starts rather than waiting for a cancellation. School days compress during Ramadan and the household's evening moves entirely, so a lesson that worked at 17:00 generally works better after Iftar. Many families switch from one long weekly session to two shorter ones for the month, because concentration is better in shorter blocks during fasting. The slot returns to its usual time afterwards. Eid and the spring break are planned around in the same conversation, so the plan absorbs the month instead of losing it.

faqs.question: My child's calculator work keeps losing method marks. Can that be fixed in a term?
faqs.answer: Usually in about three weeks. The cause is almost always the same: on Paper 2 and Paper 3 the graphic display calculator produces the number, the student writes the number, and the method that earned the marks never appears on the page. An examiner can only award what is written. The fix is mechanical, not conceptual: define the variables, write the equation or command being solved, then the result, then the answer in context. Practised on five timed papers it becomes automatic, and it is often worth more marks than any new topic taught in the same three weeks.

faqs.question: Do you follow my child's school scheme of work or the IB subject guide?
faqs.answer: Both, in that order of priority. The school's sequence decides what gets taught when, because a lesson that runs three topics ahead of the class is of little use in Thursday's test. The IB subject guide decides the standard and the assessment objectives, which is what keeps the work aimed at the examination rather than at the test. Where they conflict, the school wins on timing and the subject guide wins on depth. Bring the school's scheme of work and the published internal deadlines to the first lesson and the plan is built around them.

faqs.question: Is a maths tutor needed for Ministry of Education equivalency in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is an administrative process you complete with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority, and no tutoring service performs, influences or speeds it up. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. For the British track the published requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at AS Level. For the IB, verify the requirement on moe.gov.ae directly, because we have found no official source stating a points threshold.

faqs.question: What actually happens in the first three lessons?
faqs.answer: Lesson one is a diagnostic: two marked mock papers are reviewed and each lost mark is sorted into a category, which is knowledge, method recording, command-term misreading, sketching or timing. Lesson two begins the highest-yield category and sets a short written exercise. Lesson three starts by marking that exercise, which is the first real evidence of whether the change is sticking. By the end of lesson three you have a written plan dated back from the examination session and a clear view of whether this tutor is the right match. If not, we change the tutor.

intro.heading: Four courses wear the name "IB maths". Only one of them is your child's
paragraphs: A parent in Dubai Internet City asking for help with IB maths is almost never asking about one thing. The Diploma Programme splits mathematics into Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, and each runs at Higher and Standard Level. Those are four distinct courses with four distinct assessment profiles, and a tutor who treats them as variations on a theme will spend your money on the wrong practice.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route. It leans on proof, calculus, trigonometric manipulation and the kind of question where the path to the answer is the point. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling route. It leans on statistics, regression, financial mathematics and interpreting a result in context, and it assumes constant technology use. Both are respectable. They suit different students and they open slightly different university doors, which is the part families in this cluster most often discover too late.

Then the level. Higher Level in either course adds a third paper, and Paper 3 is a different animal: an extended, scaffolded problem-solving paper where a student is led through an unfamiliar investigation. Students who can do every topic in isolation still lose heavily here, because the paper tests whether they can follow an argument they have not seen before. It cannot be prepared for by revising topics. It has to be practised as a genre, by sitting whole investigations and then working out where the thread was dropped.

On top of all four sits the Exploration, the internally assessed piece worth a fifth of the grade in every one of the four courses. It is marked against five criteria, A to E, and the marks are not distributed the way students assume. Most of the loss in Dubai schools is not mathematical; it is in presentation, in the reflection criterion, and in choosing a topic that cannot generate enough genuine mathematics to be worth writing about. A student who picks their topic carelessly in DP1 has capped their grade before writing a line, and nobody will tell them for weeks.

One practical point before anything else. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is a service offered only in India. Mathematics for a Dubai Internet City family is taught one-to-one over live video, with a shared screen and a tablet the tutor writes on, which for this subject is close to ideal: working appears line by line, calculator screens can be shared directly, and the whole session can be reviewed afterwards. It also means the match is made on the course and level rather than on who happens to live near the Al Sufouh tram, which for a Higher Level mathematician is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-internet-c.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs as a continuous strand through the IB programmes offered by schools around Dubai Internet City, and the place a student joins it changes what support looks like. programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP mathematics is taught through units of inquiry rather than as a separate timetabled subject with a textbook sequence. Number, pattern, measurement, shape and data handling all appear, but they surface inside transdisciplinary units, which means a gap can sit unnoticed for a year. Tutoring at this stage is about securing number fluency and the language of mathematical reasoning, not about exam technique.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Al Sufouh and Marina belt run PYP before switching to a British middle school, so a child here may meet formal written methods later than a cousin in a straight IGCSE school. That is a sequencing difference rather than a deficit, but it does mean the Year 7 transition deserves a look rather than an assumption.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-world contexts. Most schools stream into standard and extended routes by MYP 4. The extended route is the one that leads comfortably into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who sits in standard through MYP 5 will find AA HL a steep first term.
programmes.countryNote: In this cluster MYP 5 maths is where the real decision gets made, because it sets the realistic DP options. Parents often think the choice happens in Year 11; in practice it is being narrowed by the streaming decision a year or more earlier. That is the moment worth a conversation, and it is a cheaper moment to act on than the one after it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one of the four maths courses, so maths is the only group where there is no opting out. The assessment is two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher Level, plus the Exploration at 20 per cent. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator in AA; AI assumes technology throughout. Those structural differences change what a revision programme has to contain.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Internet City, Knowledge Park and Emirates Hills vary in which courses they can actually timetable. A school with a small cohort may offer AA SL and AI SL but not AA HL, and a student who needs AA HL for an engineering application has a problem that is administrative rather than mathematical. Checking that in MYP 5 rather than in Year 12 is the whole point.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-internet-c.subjectsIntro: The four maths courses and the Diploma subjects whose grades depend most directly on mathematical fluency. Families around Internet City most often ask about the first four, then discover the fifth and sixth were the real problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers plus the Exploration. Proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and the harder calculus are where grades separate. Paper 3 is the component students underprepare for, because it rewards following an unfamiliar argument rather than recalling a method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers plus the Exploration, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. The non-calculator paper is the recurring shock for students who have relied on technology since MYP; exact-value trigonometry and surd manipulation need rebuilding from scratch.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics, regression, matrices, graph theory and financial mathematics, all with technology assumed. Marks go missing in interpretation rather than calculation: a correct regression equation with no comment on what it means scores a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: The most-taken course in many Dubai cohorts. Modelling, probability distributions and interpreting statistical output dominate. Students who treat it as easier maths rather than different maths are the ones who stall at a 4 or 5.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, marked on five criteria. Presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics each carry marks, and topic choice decides the ceiling before a word is written.

subjects.name: Physics HL
subjects.description: Mathematically the most demanding of the sciences at Higher Level. Students whose algebra is shaky lose physics marks they believe are physics gaps — rearranging before substituting, and handling units through a derivation, are the two habits that transfer.

subjects.name: Chemistry HL
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and kinetics all rest on proportional reasoning and logarithms. A student who cannot move confidently between a ratio and a logarithm will plateau in chemistry regardless of how well they know the content.

subjects.name: Economics HL
subjects.description: Higher Level economics adds quantitative work that catches out strong essay writers. Elasticity calculations, cost and revenue curves and the diagrammatic work all need the same precision a maths paper demands, and diagrams lose marks for unlabelled axes.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Popular with families working in the free zone. Algorithm analysis and recursion lean on the same reasoning habits as discrete maths, and students who enjoy AI HL's graph theory often find this the stronger pairing.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, extended route
subjects.description: The route that leads into AA at Higher Level. Assessed against four criteria rather than by exam, which means a student can have good report grades and still be unprepared for the pace of DP1 algebra.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the decision that shapes everything after it
paragraphs: Ask first which course your child is in, then which level. That single answer determines what a tutor should be doing for the next two years, and a surprising number of families in this cluster are not certain. School reports often say "Mathematics" and nothing more, and students themselves sometimes describe AI as "the easier one", which is not what it is.

Analysis and Approaches is built around algebraic reasoning. Proof, calculus, trigonometric identities and the manipulation of exact values dominate, and at Standard Level one of the two papers is sat without a calculator. A student who likes the mechanics of a method and wants to know why it works belongs here. A student who has leaned on a calculator since MYP 4 will find the non-calculator paper a genuine shock in DP1.

Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling and statistics. Regression, probability distributions, financial mathematics and, at Higher Level, matrices and graph theory. Technology is assumed throughout. The marks sit as much in interpreting an output as in producing it, which rewards students who can write a clear sentence about what a number means. It is not easier; it is differently difficult, and the loss pattern is entirely different.

The table sets the two against each other on the things that actually change a tutoring plan. Course descriptions should be checked against the IB's own subject briefs through your school's coordinator, because this page can only point at the structure.

sections.heading: The papers, and why Paper 3 is a separate problem
paragraphs: Standard Level candidates sit two papers; Higher Level candidates sit three. In both courses the Exploration carries twenty per cent, which means the written papers carry eighty between them. Parents often assume the Exploration is a small internal piece. It is a fifth of the grade and it is the only component the student controls entirely.

Paper 1 and Paper 2 are the recognisable ones: structured short questions followed by longer multi-part questions, spread across the syllabus. In AA, Paper 1 is the non-calculator paper, which makes exact-value trigonometry, surd manipulation and logarithm laws non-negotiable rather than optional. In AI, both papers assume technology, so calculator fluency itself is assessed — a student who cannot find a regression line quickly is losing time, not just marks.

Paper 3 at Higher Level is different in kind. It presents an extended problem, often an unfamiliar investigation, and leads the candidate through it in stages. Each stage builds on the last, which has two consequences: an early error can propagate, and a student who cannot follow a mathematical argument they have not seen before will stall no matter how well they know the topics. There is no topic list to revise for this. It is practised by sitting whole investigations and then unpicking where the thread was dropped.

The practical implication for a DP2 programme is sequencing. Content revision first, then paper-specific technique, then Paper 3 as its own strand with its own hours. Families who revise topics right up to the final weeks and never sit a full Paper 3 are leaving the most recoverable marks on the table.

sections.heading: The Exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Five criteria, A to E, and the mark allocations are the single most useful thing a Diploma maths student can know early. Most of the loss in this cluster is not mathematical. It is in presentation, in the reflection criterion, and in a topic chosen because it sounded interesting rather than because it could generate enough genuine mathematics to be marked.

Topic viability is the first gate and the cheapest place to intervene. An Exploration on a subject the student loves, which produces three lines of arithmetic and a graph, cannot reach the upper bands however well it is written. One that generates a real mathematical process — something to derive, model, test and then reflect on — can. Testing viability takes one conversation. Discovering the problem in week six costs a month.

Personal engagement and reflection are where students from strong schools in this cluster often underscore, because they write like textbooks. The criteria reward a student thinking in their own voice about why a result is surprising, what the model fails to capture, and what they would do differently. That is a writing habit, and it can be taught without anyone writing a word on the student's behalf.

The boundary here is absolute. A tutor explains the criteria, questions the mathematics, and gives feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor does not write, redraft to completion or supply text. An operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; the student is the one who would lose the qualification, and no responsible tutor goes near it.

sections.heading: Calculator fluency is assessed, not assumed
paragraphs: The graphic display calculator is part of the assessment, and in AI it is part of nearly every question. Students arrive in DP1 able to use a calculator for arithmetic and then discover that the papers expect something else: solving numerically, finding intersections, running regressions, reading distribution values, and producing a result quickly enough to leave time for the interpretation that carries the marks.

In AI this is decisive. A regression question where the student can produce the line of best fit in twenty seconds has time left to comment on the correlation and the limitations of the model, which is where the marks are. A student who takes four minutes navigating menus has the right answer and no time to say anything about it. That is a pure efficiency problem and it responds very quickly to practice.

In AA the calculator matters on Paper 2 and matters enormously on Paper 3, where numerical confirmation of an algebraic result is often the step that opens up the next part. It also has to be switched off entirely for Paper 1, which is why AA students need two separate practice habits rather than one. Mixing them produces a student who reaches for technology on a non-calculator paper out of muscle memory.

This is one area where an online lesson is genuinely better than a person in the room. The student shares their calculator screen or emulator directly, so the tutor sees exactly which keystrokes are being used rather than watching a device from across a table. Fixing a menu habit takes minutes when you can see it.

sections.heading: The MYP 5 to DP1 maths gap, and how to close it
paragraphs: This is the most common hidden cause of a disappointing DP1 maths grade in this cluster, and it is structural rather than about any individual child. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria through tasks and investigations. Diploma mathematics is assessed by timed written papers. A student can hold strong MYP criterion grades and still be unready for the first DP1 test, because the two systems reward different things.

Three specific gaps recur. Speed, because MYP tasks rarely run to a clock and DP papers always do. Method presentation, because MYP communication criteria reward explanation in words while a DP mark scheme rewards visible algebraic steps. And unscaffolded problem entry, because MYP tasks usually tell the student what approach to take and a DP question does not.

A student arriving from IGCSE has a different gap again. The algebra is usually more fluent and the exam habits better formed, because IGCSE has trained them on timed written papers for two years. But the breadth is narrower and the expectation of independent reasoning lower. An IGCSE Extended candidate moving into AA Higher Level typically needs calculus and proof rather than technique work, which is a content job and a reassuring one.

sections.heading: What IB maths tuition costs in Dubai, read as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market quotes and monthly totals are how families actually budget, so start there. Bestimate's Dubai rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages circulating in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Convert those back to the hour and the bands are visible. Budget online tuition, usually delivered by university students, is published from AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik and from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between roughly AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one with travel priced into the hour is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, and independent home tutors ask AED 200 to 500. Specialist IB work runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and BartyED AED 650.

For a two-year Diploma that arithmetic is worth doing honestly before committing. One 90-minute session a week at the qualified-online rate, through both DP years with breaks, is a different order of commitment from a six-week Paper 3 block. Many families in this cluster would be better served by the second, and will be told so.

None of these figures are IB Gram's prices; they are the market, attributed to whoever published them so you can check. For what a specific match costs in AA HL or AI SL, the route is the free trial lesson and the conversation after it, because the answer depends on level, on the papers being targeted and on how many weeks remain before the session.

sections.heading: Why online suits mathematics particularly well here
paragraphs: Some subjects lose something on a screen. Mathematics mostly gains. The working is the lesson, and a shared digital whiteboard preserves every line of it, which a sheet of paper on a dining table does not. The student can scroll back to what was written forty minutes earlier, and so can the tutor in the following week's session.

Calculator work is the clearest gain, as above: a shared screen shows the actual keystrokes. Graph work is the second. Dragging a parameter and watching a curve respond, live, while the tutor talks through what is happening, is a better explanation of a transformation than any static diagram. And a photographed handwritten attempt can be annotated on screen in real time, which is how most marking in this subject should happen.

The pool argument matters as much. Across Dubai Internet City, Knowledge Park and Al Sufouh there are not many people who have taught AA Higher Level Paper 3 to a high standard and happen to be free at 19:30 on a Tuesday. On Gulf Standard Time there are considerably more. For AI Standard Level the difference is modest; for AA HL Paper 3 it is the entire decision.

The honest counter-argument stands too. A student who will not engage with a screen, or who has nowhere quiet in a shared tower apartment, will do better with a person in the room. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE — that service exists only in India — so if that describes your child, a local in-home tutor is the right answer and we will say so rather than sell around it.

sections.heading: Which maths route the universities in play actually want
paragraphs: Families in this cluster apply widely — the UK, North America, Europe, and increasingly universities inside the UAE — and the maths route interacts with all of it. The general pattern is that engineering, mathematics, physics and most economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while business, social sciences, design and many life-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation.

The important discipline is to check the requirement on the university's own admissions page for the year of entry, by name, rather than relying on a general rule. Requirements differ between institutions and are revised, and a page like this one cannot be the authority. What a tutor can do is help a DP1 student work backwards from a shortlist to a defensible course choice while a change is still administratively possible.

For a UAE destination there is a separate thread: the Ministry of Education equivalency process. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in that published source, so none is stated here — verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions worth stating plainly. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation; it is a Ministry process with an official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency or admission. It helps a student reach a grade. Anyone framing it as a procedural necessity is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Timing a maths programme around the Dubai school year
paragraphs: The Diploma runs on a two-year clock and the useful intervention points are fixed. DP1 term one is when the algebraic debts from MYP or IGCSE show up, and it is the cheapest term in the whole programme to buy. DP1 term three is when the Exploration topic is usually chosen, which makes it the highest-leverage conversation of the year for a component worth a fifth of the grade.

DP2 term one is mocks and the Exploration draft running at the same time, which is the pinch point every Dubai cohort hits. Term two is paper technique, and at Higher Level that is when Paper 3 needs to become its own strand rather than something squeezed in after topic revision. UAE schools sit the May session; specific IB session and results dates should come from your school's IB coordinator or ibo.org rather than from a page like this, because they are not independently confirmed here.

Ramadan shifts the working day and the family routine, and sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing for those weeks. That is worth planning rather than improvising, particularly in a DP2 year, because the weeks before and after carry the heaviest assessment load. Summer is the other structural opportunity: a six-session algebra block in July changes the start of DP1 more than the same six sessions in October.

The one date discipline that matters: name a session by its month. The May session and the November session are true every year. A page that stamps a specific future year onto an exam window is wrong twelve months later with nobody having touched it, and a parent who acts on it loses real time.

sections.heading: What the first fortnight of a maths engagement should look like
paragraphs: Four facts make a sensible plan possible: the course, the level, the papers already sat with their marks, and whether the Exploration topic is chosen. With those, a tutor can tell you in fifteen minutes what the next eight weeks should contain. Without them, any programme you are quoted is a template with your child's name on it.

The trial lesson should open with a real question from the correct course, attempted live. For maths this is unusually diagnostic, because the pause tells you more than the error. A student who stalls before starting has a problem with unscaffolded entry. One who sets up correctly and abandons the manipulation has an algebra problem. One who reaches the right answer and writes nothing about it has an interpretation problem. Three different programmes follow from three different pauses.

After that, an error log, kept by cause rather than by topic. Content gap, method not shown, algebra slip, calculator inefficiency, interpretation missing, ran out of time. Counting the causes is what turns a sequence of test scores into a plan, and it is the step families skip because a topic checklist feels more like progress.

And a willingness to stop. Some students need four sessions on logarithm manipulation and nothing else at all. When the re-test on the same question set shows the gap has closed, that is what will be said, in writing. A platform that cannot recommend less than it sells is not advising you, it is subscribing you.

whyPoints.description: AA HL, AA SL, AI HL and AI SL are different qualifications with different loss patterns. The match is made on the course and level before anything else, because a capable tutor working on the wrong paper is still the wrong tutor for your child.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own discipline
whyPoints.description: Higher Level Paper 3 rewards following an unfamiliar argument, which no amount of topic revision prepares a student for. It gets its own hours, its own practice material and its own place in the error log, which is uncommon in this market.

whyPoints.title: Calculator work actually watched

faqs.question: Which of the four IB maths courses does my child actually need a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Start by confirming the course and level with the school's IB coordinator, because reports often say only "Mathematics". There are four: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at the same two levels. AA is algebra, calculus and proof, with one paper sat without a calculator. AI is statistics, modelling and financial mathematics with technology assumed. Each has a different loss pattern, so the right practice differs from the first week. A tutor matched to "IB maths" in general is matched to nothing in particular.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier route, as students in Year 11 tend to claim?
faqs.answer: No — it is differently difficult. AI drops much of the algebraic manipulation and proof that makes AA demanding, and replaces it with statistics, regression, modelling and financial mathematics, all requiring confident technology use. The marks sit heavily in interpretation: a correct regression line with no comment on what it means or where the model fails scores a fraction of what is available. Students who treat AI as lighter work are the ones who stall at a 4 or 5. Students who can write clearly about what a number means often do better here than in AA.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why do Higher Level students lose so much on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level and it is structurally different from Papers 1 and 2. Instead of questions across the syllabus, it presents one extended, often unfamiliar investigation and leads the candidate through it in stages. Each stage builds on the previous one, so an early error can propagate through the rest. Students lose marks here despite knowing every topic, because the paper tests whether they can follow a mathematical argument they have not met before. It cannot be revised from a topic list; it is practised by sitting whole investigations and unpicking where the thread dropped.

faqs.question: How much of the maths grade does the Exploration carry, and what is it marked on?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four courses, and it is marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Most loss in Dubai cohorts is not mathematical. It is a topic that cannot generate enough genuine mathematics to be marked well, a textbook register that scores nothing on personal engagement, and a conclusion that restates instead of evaluating. Topic viability is the cheapest thing to get right, because testing it takes one conversation and discovering the problem in week six costs a month of DP1.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Exploration support stop being legitimate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards and how the marks are allocated, test whether a topic can sustain enough mathematics, question the student's reasoning, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, redraft it to completion, or supply text for submission. That boundary protects the student: the IB's academic-honesty rules put the consequence on the candidate, not the helper. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is exactly what responsible support is not.

faqs.question: My child was fine at MYP maths and is struggling in DP1. Why the sudden drop?
faqs.answer: This is structural and very common in this cluster. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria through tasks and investigations; Diploma mathematics is assessed by timed written papers. A student can hold strong MYP grades and still be unready, because the systems reward different things. Three gaps recur: speed, since MYP tasks rarely run to a clock; method presentation, since a DP mark scheme wants visible algebraic steps; and unscaffolded problem entry, since MYP tasks usually name the approach and DP questions do not. Six to ten weeks of focused work usually closes it.

faqs.question: How important is the graphic display calculator, and can that be taught remotely?
faqs.answer: It is assessed, not assumed, and remote teaching is actually better for it. In AI nearly every question involves technology, and speed is marks: a student who produces a regression line in twenty seconds has time to comment on correlation and limitations, where the marks sit. One who spends four minutes in menus has the answer and no time to interpret. Online, the student shares their calculator screen or emulator so the tutor sees the exact keystrokes rather than watching a device across a table. Inefficient habits are visible and usually fixable in a session or two.

faqs.question: Does AA Higher Level matter for engineering applications, or will AI do?
faqs.answer: Engineering, mathematics and physics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while business, social sciences and design routes frequently accept Applications and Interpretation. But requirements vary by institution and are revised, so check the university's own admissions page for the year of entry by name rather than relying on a general rule. What matters practically is timing: a DP1 student can still change course while it remains a timetable question. By DP2, it rarely is. That is the conversation to have in term one of DP1.

faqs.question: What does a monthly budget for IB maths tuition in Dubai look like?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages seen in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Hourly, qualified online tutors sit around AED 150 to 300 and specialists AED 200 to 450 and above. Those are published market figures from the providers named, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Why is there no tutor who can come to our tower in Internet City?
faqs.answer: Because IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE — that service exists only in India. Lessons here are one-to-one over live video, and for mathematics that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: the working is saved on a shared whiteboard and can be revisited next week, calculator screens are shared directly, and graphs can be manipulated live while the tutor explains. It also widens the pool from whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of Al Sufouh to every AA HL specialist on Gulf Standard Time, and removes travel from the hourly rate.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma mathematician usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, at 60 or 90 minutes. A single weekly session that consolidates what the school has just taught, with set work marked properly in between, does more than two sessions covering ground twice. Two a week makes sense in two situations: a DP2 student running separate strands for paper technique and Paper 3 at Higher Level, and a student with a substantial algebraic debt to clear quickly in DP1 term one. Starting at two out of caution usually produces a tired student and a plan nobody is following by week five.

faqs.question: Is a six-week block before the May session worth booking, or is that too late?
faqs.answer: Six weeks changes a grade when the losses are technique rather than content, which at that range they usually are. Non-calculator fluency for AA Paper 1, calculator efficiency for Paper 2, and whole Paper 3 investigations sat to the clock all move marks quickly. What six weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of missing algebra, and anybody promising that is selling rather than advising. One marked paper settles it: if the lost marks cluster in timing, method and interpretation, there is real ground to recover.

faqs.question: Can maths sessions move during Ramadan and around the Dubai school calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better planned than improvised. Sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan, which matters most in a DP2 year because the weeks either side carry heavy assessment. Summer is the other structural opportunity: a six-session algebra block in July changes the start of DP1 considerably more than the same six sessions in October. Because no tutor is travelling to Al Sufouh, a slot can also be moved and moved back without losing it to someone who lives closer, which is the quiet practical benefit of the online format.

faqs.question: What should we send before the first maths session so it is not wasted?
faqs.answer: Four things. The course and level, confirmed by the school. The most recent marked paper or test with its actual score, not a predicted grade. Which papers are being targeted, since Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3 need different work. And whether the Exploration topic has been chosen. With those four a tutor can propose a defensible eight weeks in a quarter of an hour. Without them, any programme quoted is a template, and the first three sessions get spent finding out what should already have been known.

faqs.question: If nobody is free for AA Higher Level at our preferred evening time, are we told?
faqs.answer: Before you book, yes. For AI Standard Level and AA Standard Level a specialist on Gulf Standard Time is usually available within a few days. For AA Higher Level with Paper 3 as the target, in a crowded evening slot, in the term before the May session, there may be a wait, or the only available specialist may be working from outside the UAE on the same time zone. Which applies is stated in advance. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and that silence is itself informative.

faqs.question: Should we use the same person for maths and physics, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Many Higher Level physics problems are algebra problems wearing a physics costume — rearranging before substituting, carrying units through a derivation, reading a gradient as a rate. A tutor comfortable in both can fix the shared cause once instead of twice. But a single tutor who is strong in one and adequate in the other is worse than two specialists. The honest answer depends on the individual, and the trial lesson in each subject is how to find out rather than taking the convenience on trust.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-internet-c.closingHeading: Name the course, then the paper, then the plan
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-internet-c.closingBody: Everything on this page reduces to a sequence. Confirm which of the four courses your child is in and at what level. Identify which paper is costing marks, and why — content, method, calculator speed or interpretation. Decide whether the Exploration is a live problem or already handled. Then buy the specific hours that address those answers rather than a general subscription to maths. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the course and the paper rather than to the distance between two New Dubai addresses. The first lesson is free and starts with a question, and if the right recommendation is four sessions and a stop, that is what you will hear.

intro.heading: Mathematics needs an unbroken hour, and this corridor rarely offers one by accident
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. A British-curriculum school and two IB schools sit inside the district; most secondary students travel out to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Dubai South or further north.

That matters more for mathematics than for any other Diploma subject, because mathematics does not divide neatly into fragments. A derivation half-completed is not half-learnt, it is abandoned. A Paper 3 investigation attempted in forty minutes teaches a student that Paper 3 is impossible. Most Diploma subjects tolerate a short or interrupted session; mathematics punishes one, and in a household where a child arrives home at six the risk of booking a session that cannot work is real.

So the practical question for a DIP family is not just who teaches the route, but what length of session the week can actually sustain and what work belongs in each length. Forty minutes is enough for marking a script against the scheme, drilling notation or practising one question type. A full hour is the minimum for a derivation or a worked exploration section. A Paper 3 attempt needs the weekend.

The subject questions matter too and they are quickly stated. Which route: Analysis and Approaches is the proof, calculus and algebra course; Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and calculator-led interpretation. Which level, because Higher Level adds Paper 3 and 20 per cent of the grade with it. And which component is losing marks, because method marks lost to omitted working, calculator results reported without reasoning, angular mode errors and simple timing all produce the same grade and need different plans.

There is one more scheduling fact worth stating before the mathematics. The hours a long run consumes are the same hours in which a student would otherwise attempt practice questions on their own, and in mathematics that independent attempt is where the learning actually lands. A session diagnoses; the practice consolidates. So a commute does not only delay the lesson, it removes the work that was meant to follow it, which is why fewer well-aimed sessions with protected practice time beat more sessions with none.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one mathematics tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For mathematics the shared screen is a genuine improvement rather than a substitute, because both people see the same working the same way up, and the session can stop on one line until it is understood.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-investment.programmesIntro: Mathematics support in this corridor is requested at four points, and the scheduling demands differ as much as the content does. Each is described below by what the assessment requires.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The proof, calculus and algebraic route at Higher and Standard Level, with Paper 3 at Higher Level as a two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent. Algebraic fluency is assumed rather than taught, so a student slow at manipulation spends working memory on mechanics and has none left for the problem in front of them.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route DIP families most often need help with, and it is also the least forgiving of a short session. Proof and calculus work requires continuous attention, which in a long-commute household means the substantive sessions usually belong at the weekend with weekday evenings used for consolidation.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use at Higher and Standard Level, with Paper 3 again at Higher Level. Fluent graphical display calculator work is assumed, and the marks sit heavily on interpreting output in context rather than on producing it.
programmes.countryNote: Applications divides into discrete tasks more readily than Analysis does, which makes it the better fit for a household that can only offer forty-minute weekday slots. A hypothesis test or a regression interpretation can be taught and practised in one short session; a calculus derivation cannot.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria covering knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where levels go, because generalising a rule and then justifying it is a distinct skill most students treat as optional.
programmes.countryNote: The IB schools inside DIP run the continuum, so middle-years mathematics support here is often criterion work rather than content teaching. It is also the cheapest intervention available and the one most affected by bus fatigue, so a weekend morning usually produces more than a weekday evening.

programmes.name: IGCSE or MYP to Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: The gap between IGCSE Extended or MYP extended mathematics and Diploma Higher Level is wider than the content list suggests, because what is rewarded changes. Prior courses pay for correct method; the Diploma pays for justified reasoning, correct notation and the ability to say why a method is valid.
programmes.countryNote: A summer block between Year 11 and DP1 is the single best use of a holiday for a prospective Higher Level Analysis student in this corridor, precisely because the summer has no school run in it. Four to six sessions on notation, proof conventions and algebraic speed prevents the first-term drop.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-investment.subjectsIntro: Mathematics support is organised by topic and component, because that is how the marks are allocated. Each entry below names what the area demands and, where it matters, how much unbroken time it needs.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, and at Higher Level in Analysis proof and complex numbers. Fluency decides everything downstream, and fluency work divides well into short sessions, which makes it ideal weekday material.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Transformations, inverses, rational and composite functions, with heavier treatment of function behaviour in Analysis. Marks go on domain and range stated carelessly and on sketches missing the labelled features the question specified.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Identities and equations in Analysis with vectors at Higher Level, more applied and three-dimensional work in Applications. The recurring error is working in the wrong angular measure, which yields a confidently wrong answer that looks like a slip.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Lighter in Analysis, central in Applications where distributions, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing carry heavy weight. Runs well in short sessions because each technique is a self-contained task.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, far deeper in Analysis Higher Level with techniques of integration and differential equations. This is the material that genuinely needs an unbroken hour, because the reasoning chains are long.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Method and reasoning across the syllabus, with technology permitted or not depending on route and current specification. Timing rather than knowledge is usually the limiting factor, and the fix is timed practice marked to scheme wording.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Longer structured questions with the graphical display calculator central. The characteristic loss is a correct calculator result reported with no supporting line of reasoning, which forfeits method marks even where the value is right.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: A two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade, needing sustained reasoning in an unfamiliar context. It requires a full unbroken session, which in this corridor means a weekend, and schools usually reach it late.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Internally assessed coursework carrying 20 marks across lettered criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic with no mathematics available to develop.

subjects.name: Calculator and toolkit skills
subjects.description: Not a topic and worth marks throughout: which function to use, how to report what it returned, and when a sketch is required rather than a value. Trainable, usually left to accident, and perfectly suited to a short weekday slot.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor needs to establish for a DIP household
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Investments Park means one-to-one Diploma mathematics teaching at home on a weekday evening or at the weekend. IB Gram delivers that as a live online session into DIP homes on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen. No tutor is sent to a UAE address, because in-person home visits are a service we run only in India.

Four things have to be established, and in this corridor the fourth is as important as the first three. The route: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, which share five topic areas and weight them completely differently. The level, because Higher Level carries Paper 3 at 20 per cent. The failing component, taken from marked scripts rather than from the grade. And the session length the household can genuinely sustain on a weekday.

That fourth question is the one nobody asks and it changes the plan materially. A family that can only offer forty minutes on a weekday is not short-changed; they simply cannot do calculus derivations midweek, and should not be sold a plan that assumes they can. Their derivation work belongs at the weekend and their weekday slot should carry technique work, which happens to be where most of the recoverable marks are anyway.

A tutor who takes a booking without asking about arrival time is making an assumption that will fail in week three, and the failure will be attributed to the format or the tutor rather than to the schedule. Mathematics is where this shows up fastest, because an interrupted derivation is visibly useless in a way that an interrupted biology discussion is not.

sections.heading: Matching mathematics work to the session length available
paragraphs: This is the table a long-commute household actually needs, and no competitor page in this market publishes anything like it. It sets out what each length of session can usefully carry, so a family can see immediately that a constrained week is not a lost cause but does require a different allocation.

The organising principle is continuity. Some mathematics divides into discrete tasks with natural stopping points: a hypothesis test, a notation drill, marking three answers against a scheme, a calculator technique. Other mathematics does not: a calculus derivation, a proof, a Paper 3 investigation, an exploration section being developed. Putting the second kind into a forty-minute slot wastes both the slot and the student's confidence.

The useful consequence is that the highest-value-per-hour work happens to be the divisible kind. Method marks lost to omitted working, calculator results reported without reasoning, angular mode errors and timing all respond to short, repeated, self-contained practice, and together they account for more lost marks in Diploma mathematics than any content topic does. A household with only short weekday slots is therefore well placed to recover most of what is recoverable.

What such a household must protect is one longer slot a week, usually a weekend morning, for the continuous work. If that slot does not exist, Paper 3 and the exploration will not get the attention their weightings deserve, and those two together are a large share of a Higher Level grade.

One caution about the table: it describes capacity, not ambition. A household that can offer only short weekday slots should say so plainly rather than agreeing to an hour that becomes forty minutes in practice, because a plan built on the longer figure will quietly underdeliver and nobody will be able to say exactly where it went wrong.

sections.heading: The two routes, and the decision that cannot be revisited
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses are built from the same five topic areas, which is why the names sound interchangeable and the experience is not. Analysis and Approaches concentrates on number and algebra, functions, trigonometry and calculus, with statistics present but lighter, and Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers, vectors and substantially harder integration. Applications and Interpretation inverts the balance, with statistics and probability carrying heavy weight and the calculator functioning as a working tool rather than a checking device.

The decision is taken at the end of Year 11 to a school deadline and is effectively fixed afterwards. It reaches forward in a specific way: engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses commonly expect the Analysis route at Higher Level, and a student arriving with Applications can find a prerequisite unmet after offers have been made. Those are patterns rather than rules, so verify with the specific programmes on your child's list, including UAE universities, because requirements differ by course and change.

The honest test is not which course sounds harder. It is which one the student can work in fluently, read against the subjects they want to study. A student who enjoys structure, proof and algebraic manipulation is in the wrong place in Applications even if the grade looks better; a student who thinks in data and context is often stronger in Applications and will produce a better exploration there.

In this corridor there is one additional practical consideration. Diploma cohorts at the schools inside DIP are moderate in size, which can mean fewer set options and occasionally a route that is only viable if enough students choose it. If the route your child needs is marginal at their school, that is worth raising early with the mathematics department rather than discovering at the point of confirmation.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go in Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Marked mathematics scripts are repetitive, and almost none of the repetition is a failure of mathematical ability. The dominant loss is method marks forfeited by omitted working: a student who can see the answer writes the answer, and the scheme pays for the steps. Across a paper this is usually worth more than any single weak topic, and it is a four-session fix.

Second is calculator work reported without reasoning. In Paper 2 a correct value produced by a calculator with no supporting line is frequently worth less than a wrong value with correct method shown. Students find this unjust, which is exactly why it persists: they argue with it rather than adapting. Four sessions of marking their own work against the scheme ends the argument, and it fits a short weekday slot perfectly.

Third is angular measure, which sounds trivial and is not. Working in degrees where radians are required produces a confidently wrong answer that looks like carelessness and is a habit carried from IGCSE. Nobody corrects it because each instance looks like a slip. Fourth is timing, which masquerades as content weakness: a student who scores well untimed and poorly under examination conditions does not need more teaching.

Fifth, and specific to the exploration, is a topic chosen for interest rather than for mathematical content. Use of mathematics is the heaviest criterion, so a topic that offers nothing to develop caps the available marks before any writing happens. That one is free to avoid at the design stage and expensive to discover late, which is why it belongs in the first weekend session rather than the fifth.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the exploration: the two weightings schools reach last
paragraphs: At Higher Level, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent of the grade in both routes and is the component students have practised least relative to its weight. The cause is scheduling rather than difficulty: schools frequently arrive at it late in DP2 when every other deadline is competing for time, so students meet an extended two-part investigation for the first time within weeks of the session.

In a long-commute household this compounds, because a Paper 3 attempt cannot be done in a weekday evening. It needs a full unbroken session with a fresh student, which means the weekend, which means it has to be planned rather than fitted in. Two full attempts under timed conditions, started early, is a measurable advantage over none, and the only cost is deciding in advance which weekends they occupy.

The exploration is the other undervalued weighting, carrying 20 marks across lettered criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. It is marked by the school, moderated by the IB, and available months before the examinations at a point when the student has more time than they will ever have again. Families who treat it as an obligation to be discharged quickly leave marks on the table that cannot be recovered in the examination hall.

The honest boundary applies here as everywhere. A tutor may interrogate the topic for mathematical content, teach what each criterion rewards, demonstrate technique on unrelated examples, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion it currently fails. A tutor may not write, rewrite or complete any part of the exploration. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words. Confirm current criteria and weightings against the subject guide your school holds, since the IB revises its guides and we do not republish their documents.

sections.heading: The mathematics year, counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Mathematics has more hard internal deadlines than most Diploma subjects, and almost all of them are set by the school rather than the IB. Counting backwards is how a family finds out whether they are early, on time or in triage, and in this corridor it also determines which weekends need protecting.

The route decision sits furthest back and matters most, confirmed at the end of Year 11. Next comes DP1, where algebraic fluency is either built or quietly skipped. Then the exploration topic, which should be interrogated for mathematical content before a word is written, and the exploration draft, where most of the recoverable coursework marks sit. Then the mock window, then Paper 3 practice, then the session itself.

For a family deciding when to start, the rule is eight weeks of runway to change one component and a whole term to change a habit. Algebraic slowness is a habit; it needs a term of short regular work, which suits weekday slots. A pattern of reporting calculator results without reasoning is a technique; four sessions will shift it. Knowing which you have is the entire value of the first diagnostic session, and the script usually makes it obvious.

IB session and results dates are not independently verified in this project, because ibo.org blocks automated access. UAE schools sit the May session, and anything more specific should come from your child's IB coordinator. For siblings on the British curriculum: Cambridge runs June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June and November, with June 2026 results having reached centres on 19 August 2026.

faqs.question: Can IB maths tutoring work in a forty-minute weekday session?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right work, and that work happens to be where most recoverable marks are. Marking a script against the scheme, notation drills, calculator reporting discipline and angular mode checks are all self-contained tasks with natural stopping points, and together they address more lost marks than any content topic. What cannot be done in forty minutes is a calculus derivation, a proof or a Paper 3 attempt, and those belong in a protected weekend slot instead.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor come to our home in Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons are live one-to-one video sessions into DIP homes on Gulf Standard Time, with working shared and annotated on screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For mathematics the shared screen is better rather than merely equivalent, because both people see the same working the same way up and the session can stop on one line until it is understood.

faqs.question: Why does an interrupted maths session matter more than in other subjects?
faqs.answer: Because mathematics does not divide neatly into fragments. A derivation half-completed is not half-learnt; it is abandoned, and the student usually remembers the confusion rather than the method. Most Diploma subjects tolerate a short session, and mathematics punishes one. In a corridor where a child may arrive home at six, that means deciding in advance which work goes into a short weekday slot and which needs a longer weekend one.

faqs.question: Which maths route should our child take?
faqs.answer: Decide it with evidence rather than reputation. Take a recent timed paper from the route under consideration and mark it honestly. Analysis and Approaches is the proof, calculus and algebra route; Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and calculator-led interpretation, and both are real mathematics at both levels. Then verify prerequisites with the specific university programmes on your child's list, including UAE institutions, because requirements are set by course and change.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 3 the component that causes most trouble?
faqs.answer: A scheduling mismatch rather than a difficulty one. Paper 3 is a two-part extended investigation worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade in both routes, and schools frequently reach it late in DP2 when every other deadline competes for time. Students therefore meet it with the least practice relative to its weight. Two full attempts under timed conditions, started early, is a real advantage, and in this corridor it means deciding in advance which weekends they occupy.

faqs.question: Our child gets correct answers but low marks. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Method marks forfeited by omitted working, almost certainly, often alongside calculator results reported without a supporting line of reasoning. The scheme pays for steps, so a student who can see the answer writes the answer and collects one mark where four were available. In Paper 2 a correct calculator value with no method shown can score less than a wrong value with correct method. It is typically a four-session fix and it suits a short weekday slot.

faqs.question: How much maths work can realistically happen on the school bus?
faqs.answer: Recall work travels; written mathematics does not. Formula recall, definitions, notation conventions and command term lists can be reviewed on a journey. Anything requiring written working, a calculator or sustained reasoning cannot, and attempting it produces frustration. For a student losing seven or more hours a week to the journey, moving the recall component into it genuinely frees desk time for the work that needs a surface and a screen.

faqs.question: When should a prospective Higher Level maths student start support?
faqs.answer: The summer between Year 11 and DP1, which is also the least popular answer because nothing is wrong yet. Four to six sessions on notation, proof conventions and algebraic speed address exactly what the Diploma assumes and prior courses never had to teach, and the summer carries no school run so nothing competes with it. In this corridor that absence of a commute makes holiday blocks the most productive mathematics time available all year.

faqs.question: Is the exploration worth spending sessions on?
faqs.answer: Yes, and early rather than late. It carries 20 marks across lettered criteria, with use of mathematics the heaviest, so the decisive question is whether the chosen topic contains mathematics at the right level to develop. A topic chosen for interest that offers nothing to develop caps the available marks before any writing happens, and that is fixable in one session at the design stage and essentially unfixable six weeks later.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with the exploration?
faqs.answer: Interrogate the topic for mathematical content, teach what each criterion rewards, demonstrate technique on unrelated examples, and read the student's own draft and say which criterion it currently fails and why. What a tutor cannot do is write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The test after a session is whether your child could explain and defend every change in their own words; if not, the line has been crossed and the school's academic honesty policy governs what follows.

faqs.question: How do we tell a content problem from a timing problem?
faqs.answer: Give the same past paper twice at home, once under strict examination timing and once with unlimited time and no notes. A much higher untimed score means pacing, and the plan becomes a per-question time budget practised under pressure rather than more teaching. If both scores are low, the marked script shows whether it is content or technique. One evening of work at home, and it can redirect a whole term's plan before any money is spent.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Analysis hard to arrange at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: It is among the harder matches at peak early-evening times, particularly with genuine Paper 3 experience, and the constraint is sharpest in the weeks before the May session when much of Dubai's DP2 cohort wants the same slot. The practical response is to agree the pattern before mocks rather than after results. When nothing is available you will be told with a realistic date rather than offered a generalist described as a specialist.

faqs.question: What does a maths block actually cost?
faqs.answer: The market, dated October 2026: qualified online subject tutors run roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour and specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online provision starts at AED 33 to 65. Ours is set after the free trial, because the length depends on the diagnosis. The more useful figures are the blocks: four sessions for method marks, four to six for the exploration, four to eight for Paper 3 technique.

faqs.question: Should we add a second weekly maths session?
faqs.answer: Only if there is practice time between the two, which in a long-commute household usually means putting the second at the weekend rather than on another weekday evening. Mathematics gains come from the student's own attempts between sessions; without them each session restarts from cold. Two sessions with real practice between them outperform four without, and the weekend slot has the additional advantage of being the only one that can hold a full paper.

intro.heading: What the hour actually costs, and what it buys
paragraphs: Families in the Marina tend to arrive at maths tuition with a number already in their head, usually something another parent mentioned at a school gate in Al Sufouh or over coffee in JBR. The number is rarely wrong. It is incomplete. A rate of AED 180 an hour and a rate of AED 400 an hour both exist in this market, and they are not the same product. One is a graduate with a strong maths degree who has read the subject guide. The other is someone who has marked scripts at this level and can tell you inside twenty minutes whether your child is losing marks on method, on arithmetic, or on reading the command term.

The second thing worth saying early is that the price of maths tuition around Dubai Marina has less and less to do with where the tutor lives. It used to have everything to do with that, because a tutor driving from Mirdif to a tower on Marina Walk charged for the drive whether the invoice said so or not. Published rates for in-home visits in Dubai sit above online rates at every tier, and travel is the main reason. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, which is an India-only service, so what a Marina family pays covers teaching time rather than a car on Sheikh Zayed Road at six in the evening.

Where the money leaks is more specific than bad tutors. It leaks when a family buys a weekly hour for two years when the student needed a six-week block on sequences, series and binomial expansion before the Year 12 mock. It leaks when nobody checks whether the child sits Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and three sessions go on calculus that the second course does not assess to that depth. It leaks when the mathematics exploration is left until February of the final year and then needs six emergency hours that one conversation in September would have prevented. And it leaks when a general maths tutor is paid specialist rates for content that is really Year 10 algebra.

A Marina week makes some of this worse. Most schools these households attend finish between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and the drive back along Al Khail Road or Sheikh Zayed Road at that hour decides everything after it. A lesson booked at 4pm is a lesson the student arrives at hungry and flat. The same hour at 6:30pm or 7:30pm, after food, returns more per dirham, and over video it costs nothing extra to put it there. Households that travel over Eid or spend part of the summer abroad keep the same tutor and the same slot shifted by a few hours.

So the plan this page recommends is unglamorous. Find out which course and which paper pattern your child sits. Decide whether the problem is content, speed under timed conditions, or the exploration. Buy the smallest block that fits that problem, from someone who can name the criterion they are working on. Review at the end of term and cut it if the need has gone. That is a cheaper two years than a standing weekly order nobody re-examines, and it is usually a better grade as well.
