Asking the maths coordinator in Term 1 of Year 4 costs nothing and routinely saves a term of paid hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one of two mathematics courses, each available at Standard or Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebra, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and financial maths. Both carry an internally assessed exploration worth 20%. Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem solving. The four combinations are genuinely different subjects and need genuinely different tutors.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all paid maths tuition in the Marina is bought, and where most of it is bought badly. The common error is hiring on reputation rather than on course: a tutor who is excellent on Analysis and Approaches calculus can be mediocre on Applications and Interpretation statistical tests, because the content barely overlaps. Ask which of the four combinations the tutor has taught most recently.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.subjectsIntro: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Marina is most often asked for one of the four Diploma combinations, but the subjects that lean hardest on mathematics are booked alongside it almost as often. These are the courses our maths-side specialists cover for students in this area.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Marks go missing on unshown method, on differentiating a quotient under time pressure, and on candidates who can integrate but cannot say what the integral represents in the context the question set.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, probability distributions and financial mathematics, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. The usual failure is treating it as the easier course: the statistical tests and the modelling questions punish anyone who has not practised writing a conclusion in the language of the context.

subjects.name: Mathematics Higher Level Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended-response questions in one hour, each building across several parts so that an early slip propagates. It rewards stamina and structured working rather than new content, which is why it is best treated as a separate block of timed practice in the final two terms rather than as part of a general weekly hour.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: A written investigation of around twelve to twenty pages, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Supervision means helping a student choose a workable question and read the criteria honestly. The mathematics, the writing and the conclusions stay the student's own.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, Standard and Extended
subjects.description: Four criteria out of eight each, converted to a grade from one to seven. Investigating patterns is the criterion that most often drags a Marina student's grade down, because it asks for generalisation and proof of a rule rather than for correct arithmetic, and it is rarely practised at home.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Diploma subject most often paired with maths tuition, because the algebra of rearranging equations and the calculus in the fields theme are the real obstacle for many students rather than the physics itself. A maths-led session on logarithmic graph linearisation often moves a physics grade faster than more physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, dilution, equilibrium constants and energetics all collapse into proportional reasoning and unit handling. Students who lose marks consistently on calculation questions rarely have a chemistry problem; they have an arithmetic and significant-figures problem that a maths specialist can close in a short block.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds quantitative content that catches Applications and Interpretation students out less than it catches the ones who dropped maths to Standard Level. Elasticity, marginal analysis and diagram-reading all reward a student who is comfortable with gradients and rates of change.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Discrete structures, Boolean logic, complexity and the Higher Level content on abstract data types sit much closer to Analysis and Approaches than to anything else on the timetable. Students who find recursion opaque are usually missing the mathematical idea of a base case rather than the syntax.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The finance and accounts unit is where grades are won and lost, and it is arithmetic: investment appraisal, break-even, working capital and ratio analysis. A student who can set up a payback calculation cleanly picks up marks that a stronger essay writer with weaker numeracy leaves on the table.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsTitle: Where Marina maths students actually come from
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.regionsIntro: Dubai Marina does not sit on its own. The same towers, villas and school buses pull from a ring of communities along Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road, and the timing and cost of a session changes a little across that ring. These are the areas our Marina-side maths students live in.

regions.name: JBR
regions.note: A five-minute walk from much of the Marina and sharing the same school buses. Families here book the same 6:30pm and 7:30pm slots, and for the same reason: the beach-road traffic between 3pm and 5pm makes anything earlier unreliable.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: Across the tram line and a different parking proposition entirely. JLT households were the ones who most often paid a visiting tutor for the drive, and they are the quickest to see what moving the hour over video does to the rate.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Low-rise, short school runs, and within reach of a British-curriculum school on foot for some families. Maths tuition here skews younger: Years 7 to 9 bridging work rather than Diploma exam preparation.

regions.name: Al Sufouh
regions.note: Close enough to the Marina that the same households appear in both, and home to two of the schools these students attend. An Al Sufouh family can often get a 4:30pm slot to work, which is unusual in this cluster.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: One causeway in and out, which does for a visiting tutor's schedule what you would expect. Small student numbers, so a specialist in Applications and Interpretation Higher Level would never be found living on the island.

regions.name: The Springs and The Meadows
regions.note: Villa communities with a strong pull towards the IB school on the Meadows side. Sessions here often start later again, because co-curricular activities at school run to 5pm before anyone gets home.

regions.name: Emirates Hills
regions.note: A longer drive from the Marina than the map suggests once Al Khail Road is involved. Higher Level maths demand here is strong, and the pool of local tutors who can actually teach Paper 3 is not.

regions.name: Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens
regions.note: Newer communities on the far side of the Marina with a growing Year 10 and Year 11 population. Price sensitivity is higher here, which makes the block-versus-weekly decision on this page the most useful part of it.

schoolClusters.city: Schools on the Marina side of Al Khail Road
schoolClusters.note: These are the schools Marina, JBR and Bluewaters households most often name when they ask about maths support. The mix matters for pricing: a British-curriculum school moving into A Level needs different help from an IB continuum school running Analysis and Approaches from Year 12.

schoolClusters.city: Schools reached inland from the Marina
schoolClusters.note: The second ring, reached along Al Khail Road or Hessa Street. Pick-up times here are later and co-curricular programmes run longer, which is why the evening slots fill first and why an in-home tutor serving this ring is quoting for an hour of driving before any teaching happens.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.modesIntro: Three ways of buying maths support, priced by what the problem actually is. The point of separating them is that the weekly standing order is the right purchase far less often than it is the one families default to.

modes.title: A six-week block on one named topic
modes.description: The cheapest useful purchase in this market. You name the topic, the tutor runs a diagnostic in lesson one, teaches for four, and tests under timed conditions in the sixth. Sequences and series, trigonometric identities, integration by substitution and hypothesis testing are the four blocks Marina students buy most.
bullets: Six hours, with an end date written down before you start
A timed past-paper section at the end, marked against the real scheme
No commitment past the sixth lesson

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the exam year
modes.description: Appropriate when the gap is broad rather than topical, or when the student needs the external deadline that a standing appointment creates. Worth re-examining every term rather than renewing by default, because the commonest waste in the Marina is a weekly hour that outlived the problem it was bought for.
bullets: One fixed slot, usually 6:30pm or 7:30pm Gulf Standard Time
A written note of what was covered after each lesson
A term-end review that may recommend reducing or stopping

modes.title: Exploration supervision across a term
modes.description: Spread thin on purpose: a session to choose a question, one to check the mathematics is deep enough to score on use of mathematics, one on structure, one on reflection, and a last read before the school's internal deadline. The student writes it. The tutor reads criteria and asks awkward questions.
bullets: Four to six sessions spread over a full term, not a rescue week
Criteria read out loud with the student, not summarised for them

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs around Dubai Marina, tier by tier
paragraphs: Market rates for maths tuition in Dubai run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the bottom to AED 650 at the top, and the spread is not noise. Each band buys something different. The table below collects figures each provider published on its own site, recorded in October 2026, so you can see which part of the market a quote belongs to before you accept or refuse it. These are market rates and not an IB Gram price list; our own figure comes with the consultation, after the free first lesson.

The band that matters for most Diploma families is AED 200 to 450. Below it you are usually buying general maths help from someone who has not taught the course, which can be the right purchase for a Year 8 arithmetic gap and is the wrong one for Paper 3. Above it you are paying scarcity pricing. The premium tier is real and sometimes worth it in the last two terms of Higher Level, but a family paying it from Year 12 Term 1 is spending at the top of the market for work a mid-band specialist does equally well.

One figure in the table deserves separating out. In-home visits are quoted from around AED 180 to 500 an hour, and the gap between that and the equivalent online band is the drive. A tutor coming into a Marina tower spends time on Sheikh Zayed Road, then on parking, then in a lift. Nobody itemises it, but every family in this neighbourhood is paying for it somewhere in the rate. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which tells you the same story in a different unit.

sections.heading: The four places maths money leaks in a Marina household
paragraphs: The first leak is buying a subject instead of a problem. A parent who books maths tuition has usually diagnosed the symptom, a grade of 4 where a 6 was expected, and left the diagnosis there. Maths at this level fails in at least four distinguishable ways: missing prior content, correct method executed too slowly, correct work presented in a way the mark scheme cannot reward, and an exploration drifting without a question. Each needs a different number of hours and in two of the four cases the right answer is fewer hours, not more.

The second leak is the wrong course. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation share a name and little else at the margins where grades are decided. A tutor who has spent five years on algebraic proof and calculus can be genuinely weak on chi-squared tests and on writing a conclusion about a correlation coefficient. Families pay specialist rates for sessions that drift into content the student's course does not assess, which feels like progress and shows up nowhere in the final grade.

The third leak is timing, and it is the most expensive. An exploration started in September needs four or five calm sessions. The same exploration opened six weeks before the school's internal deadline needs ten anxious ones, and produces a weaker piece of work. The fourth leak is the standing order nobody cancels: a weekly hour booked in Year 11 for a genuine gap, still running in Year 13 after the gap closed, now functioning as supervised homework at AED 300 an hour. Review at the end of every term and the fourth leak closes itself.
bullets: Diagnose which of the four failure modes applies before booking a single hour
Confirm the exact course and level in writing: AA SL, AA HL, AI SL or AI HL
Open the exploration conversation in September of the final year, not February
Put a review date in the calendar at the same time as the first lesson

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets your bill
paragraphs: Most of the money a Marina family will spend on Diploma maths is determined by a decision made in Year 11, often in a ten-minute conversation about which course looks easier. It is not a question of difficulty. It is a question of which kind of mathematics the student can sustain for two years and which prerequisite their intended degree expects. Engineering and physics courses at competitive universities commonly ask for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Business, design and several life-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Checking the prerequisite before the choice is free; correcting it afterwards is not.

The tutoring consequence is sharper than the academic one. Because Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator, that course rewards drilled algebraic fluency in a way nothing else on the Diploma timetable does, and fluency is built by volume of short practice rather than by long explanatory lessons. Applications and Interpretation allows a graphic display calculator on every paper, which moves the difficulty from manipulation to interpretation: knowing which test to run, and writing what the output means in the context of the question.

That is why the same weekly hour produces different value on the two courses. An Analysis and Approaches student often does better with two short sessions a week than one long one. An Applications and Interpretation student usually needs the longer session, because a modelling question cannot be set up, solved and written up in twenty minutes. Ask a prospective tutor which of the four combinations they taught most recently and what they would do differently between them. The answer separates a specialist from a generalist faster than any qualification on a profile.

sections.heading: What each component is worth, and where the marks actually go
paragraphs: Nobody should be paying for maths tuition without knowing the weighting of the thing being tutored. A Standard Level student has two papers and an exploration. A Higher Level student has three papers and an exploration. The exploration is 20% of the grade in both cases, which means it is worth more than a full paper's difference in most grade boundaries and is the single most coachable component on the course, because it is written over months rather than performed in ninety minutes.

The papers fail in patterns, and the patterns are specific enough to buy against. On Paper 1 of Analysis and Approaches, the most common avoidable loss is unshown method: a candidate who knows the answer writes it, and the scheme awards nothing for a correct result reached invisibly. On Paper 2, it is premature rounding and a calculator left in the wrong angle mode, both of which cost accuracy marks across several questions rather than one. On Paper 3 it is time: the second extended question is routinely half-finished by candidates who could have completed it.

The exploration loses marks in a different way again. Presentation and mathematical communication are straightforward to secure with a structured draft. Personal engagement and reflection are where most of the lost marks sit, and they cannot be retrofitted in the last week, because reflection means commenting on decisions the student actually made while making them. Use of mathematics is the largest single block of marks and the one where an ambitious topic pays off, provided the student can genuinely handle the mathematics they have chosen.

sections.heading: One-to-one online against an in-home maths tutor in this area
paragraphs: This comparison is the one most Marina parents are actually making, and it deserves to be made on evidence rather than on instinct. The instinct is that a person in the room is better. Sometimes they are, particularly for a younger child who needs an adult physically redirecting their attention. For a Diploma maths candidate working through a Paper 3 question on a shared screen, the room adds very little and the constraint it imposes costs a great deal.

The constraint is the tutor pool. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is taught well by a small number of people. If the requirement is that one of them lives close enough to drive to a tower on the Marina on a weekday evening, the shortlist collapses to whoever is available within about twenty minutes, which in practice means whoever is left. Remove the driving requirement and the shortlist becomes everyone who teaches that course on a compatible timezone. That is the whole argument, and it is a stronger one than any claim about technology.

The cost side follows from it. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India, and every lesson for a Marina family runs one-to-one over live video. What that buys is a rate with no drive inside it, a slot that survives traffic and travel, and shared screen work that still exists the next morning when the student sits down to revise. The table sets the two side by side on the terms that matter in this specific neighbourhood.

sections.heading: Buying by the block instead of by the year
paragraphs: A block is six hours with a named topic and an end date. A year is thirty-odd hours with a direction of travel. The block is nearly always the better first purchase, and almost nobody sells it that way, because a standing weekly order is a more comfortable business than a six-week engagement that might not renew. Buy the block first anyway. If the problem survives it, the weekly hour has earned its place and you will know exactly what it is for.

The arithmetic is worth doing in dirhams. Six hours with a specialist in the AED 250 band is about AED 1,500 and a clear answer about whether the gap was content or confidence. A full year at the same rate is somewhere above AED 9,000, and families frequently commit to it without having established which of the four failure modes they are treating. Running the block first does not save money by being cheap. It saves money by telling you what to buy next.

There is one case where the block is wrong. A student who will not work without an external appointment needs the appointment, and the weekly slot is doing something real that no amount of good diagnosis replaces. That is a legitimate purchase, but it should be named for what it is, because it changes who you should hire. Supervised, structured practice does not need the top of the market. Paying premium specialist rates for accountability is the most expensive way to buy a habit.
bullets: Start with six hours and a named topic, not a term
Put the review date in the calendar before the first lesson
Price the year out in dirhams before committing to it
If the purchase is really accountability, hire for that and pay mid-band

sections.heading: The exploration: what a fee covers and what it never covers
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is 20% of the grade, written at home over a term, and it is the component where the boundary between teaching and malpractice has to be explicit. A tutor can help a student find a question that is both interesting and mathematically rich enough to score. A tutor can read the assessment criteria aloud with the student, ask what personal engagement would look like in their topic, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the data presented, and insist on a draft timeline that fits the school's internal deadline.

A tutor cannot author it. Not the mathematics, not the commentary, not the reflection, not a paragraph of it. The student types every word and performs every calculation, and anyone offering otherwise is selling an academic-honesty breach with an expulsion risk attached to the student rather than to the seller. This market has providers advertising finished internal assessments at four-figure prices. That is not a cheaper route to a grade; it is a route to no grade at all, and families should treat any such offer as disqualifying.

The practical consequence for a Marina family is that exploration support is thin and spread out rather than intense. Four to six sessions across a term, placed at the decision points: topic, mathematical depth, structure, reflection, and a final read before submission. Booking ten hours in the fortnight before the deadline buys panic. Booking five across a term buys a piece of work the student can talk about confidently if a teacher asks them to explain their own reasoning, which they will.

sections.heading: Checking that the tutor you are paying is permitted to teach here
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is a permitted activity with a permit attached. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. According to the federal government's own services portal, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through its app, website or e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent weighing a quote. The first is that the permit costs the tutor nothing, so a provider cannot reasonably present it as a cost that justifies a higher rate. The second is that operating without one carries consequences: the portal states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so any figure quoted to you as the fine should be treated with scepticism until you can find it on a government page.

A tutoring business with premises and employed staff in Dubai is a different legal animal, requiring an educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority for a training institute. IB Gram has no UAE premises and does not hold that permit, which is also why no page here describes its tutors with any regulator's name attached as a credential. In Abu Dhabi there is a further restriction worth knowing even from the Marina: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that school staff may not take paid private tuition with students enrolled at their own school.
bullets: Ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and for the category it was issued under
Treat any quoted fine amount as unverified unless you can read it on a government page
Be cautious of a provider using a regulator's name as a quality badge
Never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher at their own school

process.description: Tell us which of the four combinations your child sits: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher Level. If you are not certain, the school's maths coordinator can confirm it in a line. Everything after this step, including who we match and what it costs, depends on that answer being right.

process.title: Say what is actually failing
process.description: Missing content from earlier years, correct work that is too slow under timed conditions, method that is not written down in a form the scheme rewards, or an exploration with no question. These need different numbers of hours. Two of the four are solved with fewer sessions than families expect.

process.title: A free first lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One hour at no cost with the tutor we propose, who spends part of it running a diagnostic on a past-paper section rather than teaching. You get a written view of which failure mode applies and how many hours it should take. There is no obligation afterwards and no card required to book it.

process.title: Buy the smallest block that fits
process.description: Usually six hours on one named topic with an end date, sometimes a weekly slot through the exam year, sometimes exploration supervision spread across a term. We will say which, including when the honest recommendation is to buy less than you came for or to wait until after the mock.

process.title: Review at the end of term and cut what is finished
process.description: A standing weekly hour that has outlived its reason is the commonest waste in this market. At the end of each term we look at the mock marks and the school's feedback and say whether to continue, reduce, change tutor or stop. Stopping is a normal outcome, not a failure.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry their source and their currency
whyPoints.description: Every AED rate on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was recorded. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in. You should be able to check our numbers.

whyPoints.title: The specialist is chosen by paper, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run one-to-one over live video, the shortlist for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is everyone who teaches it well on a workable timezone rather than everyone who will drive to the Marina on a Tuesday. That is the entire practical case for online delivery at this level.

whyPoints.title: Recommendations to spend less, when that is right
whyPoints.description: A six-week block often closes a topic gap that a family arrived expecting to pay for across two years. We will say so, and we will say when the sensible move is to wait until the mock results are back before buying anything at all. A smaller correct purchase keeps families longer than a larger wrong one.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is written down
whyPoints.description: On the exploration a tutor helps with the question, the criteria, the structure and the honesty of the conclusions. The mathematics and the words stay the student's own. This market contains providers selling finished internal assessments; the boundary is stated here so there is no ambiguity about what you are buying.

whyPoints.title: No regulator's name is used as a badge
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK and MoHRE are named on this page to explain what they do and what a parent should check. None of them endorses IB Gram, and no page here says otherwise. A provider using a regulator's name as a quality claim is telling you something about itself rather than about its tutors.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths tutor in Dubai Marina charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB-level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, with a premium tier reaching AED 650. In-home visits are quoted from around AED 180 to 500 because the drive sits inside the rate. Those are market figures taken from each provider's own site in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. For Diploma maths most Marina families end up in the AED 200 to 450 band, and whether the top or the bottom of it is right depends on whether the student needs Paper 3 work or earlier content.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor quoted higher than an online one in the Marina?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is in the price even when it is not on the invoice. A tutor travelling to a Marina tower on a weekday evening spends time on Sheikh Zayed Road, then finding parking, then in a lift, and that time is paid for by somebody. Published in-home bands in Dubai sit above the equivalent online bands at every tier for this reason. The monthly packages make it clearer still: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four in-home visits. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so there is no drive to price.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 150 an hour a false economy for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but it depends on what you are buying. At that rate you are usually hiring a maths graduate rather than someone who has taught the course, and for closing a Year 10 algebra gap that is the correct purchase. For Paper 3, for the final two terms of Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, or for an exploration that needs its mathematical depth assessed honestly, it is the wrong one, and the saved dirhams come back as extra hours. Ask which of the four course combinations the tutor taught most recently. If the answer is vague, the rate is telling you something true.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week should a Marina Diploma student start with?
faqs.answer: One, in almost every case, and for six weeks rather than indefinitely. A student who takes two sessions a week from the start usually has not yet established which failure mode is costing the marks, so the second hour goes on general revision that would have happened anyway. The exception is an Analysis and Approaches candidate rebuilding algebraic fluency before Paper 1, where two short sessions beat one long one, because fluency responds to frequency. Add hours after the first mock, when you have evidence, rather than before it, when you only have a grade.

faqs.question: Do you charge the same for Applications and Interpretation as for Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: The market does not consistently distinguish them, and nor do we by default, but the hours needed often differ. Applications and Interpretation students tend to need longer single sessions, because setting up a modelling question, running the statistics and writing a contextual conclusion does not fit into twenty minutes. Analysis and Approaches students often get more from shorter, more frequent practice aimed at the non-calculator paper. So the hourly figure may match while the sensible total differs. We will say which pattern we think your child needs after the free first lesson.

faqs.question: Does the exploration need separate paid sessions, or is it covered in the weekly hour?
faqs.answer: Treat it separately. Folding it into a weekly hour means the exploration gets whatever time is left after the week's homework crisis, which is how it ends up started in February. Four to six sessions spread across a term, placed at the decision points, is the pattern that works: choosing the question, checking the mathematics is rich enough to score on use of mathematics, structure, reflection, and a final read before the school's internal deadline. That is fewer total hours than the rescue version and produces a piece of work the student can defend if asked to explain their reasoning.

faqs.question: My child sits Paper 3 in May and we have not started. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: No, and Paper 3 is unusually responsive late, because it tests stamina and structured working rather than new content. A focused block of timed extended questions, marked against the real scheme and then unpicked, moves that paper faster than general revision does. What is genuinely late is the exploration, which is written over months and cannot be compressed without the reflection marks suffering. So if time is short, spend it on timed Paper 3 practice and on the two or three topics the mock showed are weakest, and leave broad coverage alone.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics for the same Marina student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a good deal of what blocks physics students is mathematical rather than physical: rearranging equations under pressure, logarithmic linearisation of a graph, calculus in the fields theme. A maths specialist who has taught Diploma physics can close those in a short block. What does not work is one person covering Higher Level in both subjects across a whole year as a convenience. At that depth you want two specialists, and the scheduling cost of a second tutor is low when every lesson runs over video anyway.

faqs.question: What should I stop paying for once my child's maths grade is stable?
faqs.answer: The standing weekly hour, first. Once mock marks are where you want them and the school's feedback agrees, that hour usually converts into supervised homework, which is real but not worth specialist rates. Keep exploration supervision until it is submitted, because that is 20% of the grade and the deadline is fixed. Keep a short block of timed-paper practice in the final term, because speed decays. Drop general content coverage. Families who review each term rather than renewing by default spend a fraction of what a two-year standing order costs.

faqs.question: Do maths tuition rates in Dubai rise in the months before the May session?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens more than headline rates move. The specialists who teach Higher Level well fill their evening slots first, so by February the constraint is usually whether anyone good has a 7:30pm Gulf Standard Time slot left rather than what they charge for it. Some providers do run exam-season packages at the upper end of their published band. The practical implication for a Marina family is to book the slot in the autumn term even if you only intend to use it for a block, because the price you cannot negotiate is the one for an hour that no longer exists.

faqs.question: Is group maths tuition cheaper for a Marina family with two children?
faqs.answer: Per student, yes, and small-group rates in this market are quoted well below one-to-one. Whether it is good value depends on whether the two students have the same problem. Two siblings on the same course with the same weak topic can share an hour productively. A Year 11 and a Year 13, or an Analysis and Approaches student with an Applications and Interpretation one, cannot: the hour splits and each gets half a lesson at a discount. Where the courses differ, two short individual sessions usually beat one shared long one.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private maths tutor is permitted to work in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly whether they hold the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and under which eligibility category. The federal services portal states it is granted free of charge for two years and lists eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE handles the application through its app, website and e-services system. Because the permit costs nothing, no tutor can reasonably present it as a reason for a higher rate, and a vague answer about licensing is worth following up.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether a quoted maths rate includes VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask for it in writing. Tax treatment of tuition in the UAE depends on the provider's own status and registration, and this page will not tell you what it is because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's guidance and for the provider's own tax position rather than for a tutoring site. What you can reasonably insist on is clarity: whether the figure quoted is the figure you pay, whether it changes for a longer session, and whether a monthly package is billed differently from an hourly booking.

faqs.question: What does a maths tutor need to know about my child's school calendar in the Marina?
faqs.answer: Four dates, at minimum. The school's internal deadline for the exploration, which is usually months before anything the IB publishes. The mock window, because that is where diagnostic evidence comes from. The end-of-term assessment dates, because a block should finish before one rather than during it. And the co-curricular commitments that decide whether a session can start at 6:30pm or has to wait until 7:30pm. Schools in this area finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm, and after-school programmes often run to 5pm, which settles most scheduling arguments before they start.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book a block of maths hours than to pay week by week?
faqs.answer: The hourly figure is usually similar. The total is not, and that is the point of this page. Six hours on a named topic with an end date costs around AED 1,500 at mid-specialist rates and gives you a clear answer about what the problem was. A full year of weekly hours at the same rate runs well past AED 9,000, and most families commit to it before establishing which of the four failure modes they are treating. Buy the block, use what it tells you, then decide whether the year is justified.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingHeading: Price the problem, not the subject
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-marina.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the order of operations. Confirm the course and level. Work out which of the four failure modes is costing the marks. Buy six hours against that, with an end date written down, and review it when the term ends. A Marina family that does this spends a fraction of what a two-year standing weekly order costs and usually ends up with the better grade, because the hours went where the marks were. Book the free first lesson with a matched specialist, bring the last mock paper, and we will tell you honestly how many hours we think it needs, including when the answer is fewer than you expected.

intro.heading: Two courses, four combinations, one decision that gets made badly
paragraphs: IB mathematics is not one subject. It is two separate courses, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, each offered at Higher and Standard Level. That produces four combinations with different content, different papers, different calculator expectations and different university consequences. A parent in Dubai Media City asking for a maths tutor is asking for one of four things, and the four are not interchangeable.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route. At Higher Level it carries three papers and the heaviest calculus and proof content in the Diploma. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with a graphic display calculator used throughout and a different kind of question: interpret this output, justify this model, explain what the figure means in context. Students regularly choose Applications expecting relief and meet statistics at Higher Level that is genuinely demanding.

The decision is usually made at the end of Year 11 or MYP 5, on the basis of a predicted grade, in a conversation that lasts about ten minutes. Then it quietly determines what the student can study at university. Engineering, mathematics, physics, economics and many computer science courses commonly expect Analysis, often at Higher Level; social sciences, business and design routes are frequently content with Applications. Families discover this in DP2 while writing applications, which is late.

Around Media City this plays out in a specific way. The district is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh, with residential towers and no school inside it. Children travel out to GEMS Wellington International School next door, to the Al Barsha cluster, or to Dubai International Academy Emirates Hills and Emirates International School Meadows in the villa belt. Those schools offer different combinations of the four courses and set them up differently, so what your neighbour's child is doing is not a guide.

What a tutor can realistically change depends on which of the four a student is in and when you ask. In DP1 a route can still be reconsidered and a gap in algebraic fluency can still be closed properly. In DP2 the useful work is paper technique, Exploration quality and the specific topics the mock paper exposed. Both are worth buying; they are not the same purchase, and a provider who treats them identically is not paying attention.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm. For mathematics that arrangement is unusually strong, because the work is a shared screen, a worked solution built line by line and a past paper annotated live, all of which survive the medium without loss.

programmes.name: Diploma mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one mathematics course from the two available, at Higher or Standard Level. Assessment is by written papers plus the Exploration, an individual piece of mathematical writing that is internally assessed and externally moderated. The papers reward method and justification, so a correct answer with no visible reasoning scores below an incomplete answer with clear working.

programmes.name: Middle Years mathematics
programmes.ageRange: Ages 11-16 · MYP 1 to MYP 5, Standard and Extended
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B is where capable students stall, because it asks for a general rule justified rather than an answer produced. The Standard or Extended pathway chosen in MYP 4 shapes what is comfortable at Diploma level.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP Extended pathway is the natural feed into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. A student who took Standard and then aims at Analysis HL usually arrives in DP1 with a term of algebraic fluency to rebuild while new content is already arriving, which is the most common and most avoidable mathematics problem we see in this corridor.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics as the other feeder
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580 splits into Core and Extended; Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Specification A splits into Foundation and Higher. Both lower tiers omit the algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and function work that Diploma mathematics assumes from the first week. UAE candidates sit June and November with Cambridge and May/June and November with Pearson.
programmes.countryNote: Many children living in the Media City and Al Sufouh towers sit IGCSE before switching into the Diploma at a different school, which produces a predictable gap. Closing it in the summer between Year 11 and DP1 takes a short block; closing it in the autumn of DP1 while the course moves on takes a term and feels much worse.

programmes.name: A Level mathematics as the alternative
programmes.description: The route most of this corridor's British-school students take instead, with Further Mathematics available as a second qualification. It is narrower and deeper than the Diploma, with no equivalent of the Exploration and no requirement to carry five other subjects. Families comparing the two often ask which is harder, which is the wrong question.
programmes.countryNote: The useful comparison is fit rather than difficulty. A student who wants to specialise early and dislikes extended writing is usually better served by A Levels; a student who wants breadth and can handle six subjects plus the core is better served by the Diploma. Both exist within a short bus ride of Media City, which makes the decision a real one rather than theoretical.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-media-city.subjectsIntro: Mathematics requests from this corridor cluster in a small number of places. These are the topic areas and components, with what each actually assesses and where the marks tend to go.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponentials and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Analysis Higher Level complex numbers and proof. This is the foundation that decides whether the rest of the course is manageable. Students arriving from a lower IGCSE tier or MYP Standard almost always have gaps here, and they surface as slow, error-prone manipulation rather than as not knowing a topic.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational functions and, at Higher Level, more demanding graph sketching. The commonest loss is sketching from memory rather than from the function's features, which falls apart when the question asks for asymptotes and intercepts to be justified rather than drawn.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations, vectors at Analysis Higher Level, and three-dimensional work. Students handle right-angled trigonometry from IGCSE confidently and then lose marks on identities and on equations with multiple solutions in a given domain, which is a technique problem rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Both courses; the weight of Applications
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, with Applications Higher Level going considerably further than students expect. Marks are lost by reporting a calculator output without interpreting it in context, which is exactly what the Applications mark scheme is built to catch.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: Both courses; the weight of Analysis
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, with Analysis Higher Level extending to implicit differentiation, differential equations and Maclaurin series. This is where Analysis Higher Level students either consolidate or quietly fall behind, and where a weekly hour across DP1 pays for itself several times over.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction, induction and counterexample. Students who can perform every technique in the course still lose Paper 1 marks here, because proof is a written genre with conventions, and nobody teaches genres by accident. It responds very quickly to deliberate practice on marked examples.

subjects.name: Mathematical modelling
subjects.description: Choosing a model, fitting it, criticising it and explaining its limitations. The failure is answering the mathematics and ignoring the context, or the reverse. Mark schemes in Applications reward the sentence that says what the model implies, which students regard as optional and the examiner does not.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: Regression, distributions, numerical solving, graphing and table features, plus knowing which paper permits it. A substantial number of avoidable marks are lost to slow or incorrect calculator use under time pressure, and it is the easiest thing on this list to fix with structured practice.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing, internally assessed and externally moderated, marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The most common failure is a topic too broad to handle properly, chosen early and discovered late.

subjects.name: MYP Extended mathematics
subjects.description: The pre-Diploma pathway, marked against four criteria out of eight, with criterion B asking for a justified general rule. Students on the Standard pathway who intend to take Analysis at Higher Level need a bridging plan, and the cheapest time to build one is the summer before DP1 rather than the following November.

subjects.name: IGCSE Extended and Higher tier mathematics
subjects.description: The other common feeder into the Diploma. Students from Core or Foundation tiers have a visible gap in algebra, trigonometry and functions, all of which Diploma mathematics assumes immediately. A short structured block closes it; hoping it will resolve itself does not.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor search from Media City is really asking for
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Media City means, in practice, a specialist in one of four courses: Analysis and Approaches at Higher or Standard Level, or Applications and Interpretation at Higher or Standard. The first useful question is therefore not about experience. It is which course and which level, because a tutor fluent in Analysis Higher Level calculus may be a poor fit for an Applications student whose problem is interpreting regression output.

This matters more in mathematics than in most subjects, because the two courses reward different habits. Analysis rewards algebraic precision, proof convention and clean method presentation. Applications rewards model selection, calculator fluency and the written interpretation of a numerical result. A tutor who teaches the first style to an Applications student will produce technically strong work that misses the marks the scheme is actually awarding.

The second question is where the student sits in the course. In DP1, the high-value work is algebraic fluency and deciding honestly whether a Higher Level choice is sustainable. In DP2, it is Exploration quality and paper technique, with content reteaching limited to what the mocks expose. A parent who asks for maths help in general will be sold whichever of these the provider prefers to sell.

Geography is the least important variable. Media City has no school inside it, the nearest tuition centres are inland in Al Barsha, and the pool of people within a short drive who teach Applications Higher Level statistics is small enough to be effectively random. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and for mathematics the medium costs almost nothing: the work is a shared screen with a solution built line by line.

sections.heading: Analysis against Applications: choosing, and knowing when it is too late to switch
paragraphs: The route decision is usually made quickly and then lived with for two years. Making it well takes about an hour of honest conversation and one piece of evidence: how the student handles algebra under time pressure without a calculator. If that is fluent, Analysis is viable. If it is slow and error-prone, Analysis at Higher Level will consume the student's entire week and damage five other subjects.

Applications is not the easy option, and families who treat it as one are regularly surprised. At Higher Level it carries statistics and modelling content that many students find harder than the equivalent Analysis topics, and it demands written interpretation that mathematically confident students often resist. What it does not demand is the proof and abstract manipulation that Analysis Higher Level builds on, which is the real axis of the decision.

Switching is possible early in DP1 and progressively harder after that. A move from Higher to Standard Level within the same course is usually administratively simple and academically sensible when a student is drowning. A move between courses means a change of content and of style, and after the first term it means covering ground the class has already left behind. The table below sets out what each combination involves and what it costs to change.

The downstream point matters most. Engineering, mathematics, physics, economics and many computer science degrees commonly expect Analysis, often at Higher Level, while social sciences, business and design routes frequently accept Applications. Requirements vary by university and by year, so check the individual programme page rather than relying on a general rule, including for the Dubai campuses of overseas universities. Do not rely on a tutoring website for an admissions requirement, including this one.

sections.heading: Paper structure and weightings, and why Paper 1 is a different exam
paragraphs: Higher Level mathematics is assessed by three papers; Standard Level by two. The weightings differ between levels, and the rules about what is permitted in the room differ between papers, which is the single most commonly misunderstood thing about IB mathematics among parents and a surprising number of students.

The practical consequence is that Paper 1 and Paper 2 need different preparation. A paper sat without a calculator rewards algebraic fluency, clean manipulation and exact values; a paper sat with one rewards speed, correct use of the device's features and the discipline of writing down enough to earn method marks even when the answer came from a screen. Students who prepare for both identically tend to do noticeably better in one than the other, and the difference is technique rather than knowledge.

Paper 3 at Higher Level is different again: extended problem-solving in an unfamiliar context, where the mathematics is accessible and the challenge is sustaining a long chain of reasoning without losing the thread. It responds to practice more than to teaching. Most students have attempted fewer Paper 3 questions than any other component, which makes it the cheapest available improvement in a DP2 spring.

Weightings and durations are set by the current subject guide and can change between versions, so confirm the detail against your child's school and the official documentation. The shape in the table below is what matters for planning: where the marks are, what each paper is testing, and therefore how a term of tutoring should be divided. A tutor who cannot describe this from memory has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Where IB mathematics marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Ask a student why they lost marks and they will name a topic. Mark a paper and the pattern is almost always procedural. The largest single loss in both courses is unwritten working: a student reaches a correct answer by a route the examiner cannot see, and the method marks are gone. The second largest is answering a slightly different question from the one asked, usually because a command term was read as a synonym for something easier.

After those, the pattern splits by course. In Analysis, students lose marks on exact-value work in Paper 1, on proof convention, and on sketching graphs from memory instead of from the function's features. In Applications, the losses sit in calculator output reported without interpretation, in model criticism that never arrives, and in statistical conclusions stated without reference to the test that produced them.

Then there are the losses that belong to the whole Diploma rather than to mathematics. A student carrying three Higher Levels and an Extended Essay will run out of week, and mathematics is frequently the subject that absorbs the shortfall because its homework is finite and skippable in a way that essay drafting is not. A maths tutor who never asks about the other five subjects is missing the actual cause.

The reason this section is specific is that specific losses are fixable in a term and vague ones are not. A student who writes out method, reads command terms deliberately, practises exact values for Paper 1 and interprets every calculator output in a sentence has recovered most of the marks available to them without learning a single new topic.

sections.heading: The Exploration: five criteria, and the topic decision that decides the grade
paragraphs: The Exploration is the internally assessed component of both mathematics courses: an individual piece of mathematical writing, moderated externally, marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics used. It is the part of the course where a student has the most control and uses it worst.

Almost every weak Exploration fails for the same reason, and it is not mathematical ability. The topic was too broad, chosen in the first week from a list of ideas that sound impressive, and by the time the student discovers they cannot actually do the mathematics involved there is no time to start again. A narrower topic executed properly outscores an ambitious one executed partially, every time, and a tutor who spends the first session killing a bad topic has done the most valuable thing available.

The criteria that students neglect are reflection and personal engagement, because they look like presentation rather than mathematics. They are marked. Reflection means commenting on what the mathematics showed, what the limitations were and what a next step would be, at the point in the work where it arises rather than in a paragraph at the end. Personal engagement means the work reads as the student's own inquiry, which is also, usefully, what makes it defensible under academic honesty rules.

That boundary is worth stating plainly. A tutor may teach notation, structure, mathematical communication and what each criterion rewards, and may read the student's own draft and say where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure the Exploration, and may not supply a model to adapt. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; for the student, that is an academic honesty finding rather than a shortcut.

sections.heading: The graphic display calculator, and the marks hiding inside it
paragraphs: In Applications the calculator is part of the course rather than an aid to it, and in Analysis it is permitted in some papers and not others. Either way, a substantial number of avoidable marks live in how quickly and correctly a student drives the device, and almost nobody teaches it deliberately. Schools cover the features when the topic arrives and never return to them under time pressure.

The specific skills worth drilling are regression and correlation, distribution calculations, numerical solving, graphing with sensible window choices, and the table features that make a modelling question quick. Each is mechanical, each is examined, and each is faster with practice. A student who takes ninety seconds to set up a distribution calculation will lose several marks across a paper simply by running out of time.

There is a second, subtler point. Marks are awarded for method, and an answer produced entirely on a screen has no visible method unless the student writes down what they asked the calculator to do. In Applications particularly, the mark scheme expects the student to state the test or model used and then interpret the output in context. A student who writes only the number has thrown away the marks around it.

This is also where online delivery is at its most practical. A tutor can share a calculator emulator or watch the student's own screen, and correcting keystroke sequence in real time is considerably easier over video than leaning across a kitchen table. For the one part of mathematics that is genuinely mechanical, the medium is an advantage rather than a compromise.

sections.heading: From MYP or IGCSE into Diploma mathematics: closing the gap before it costs a term
paragraphs: Most mathematics problems in DP1 were created two years earlier. A student who took MYP Standard rather than Extended, or Cambridge 0580 Core rather than Extended, or Pearson 4MA1 Foundation rather than Higher, arrives in the Diploma without the algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and function work that the course assumes from the first week. The course does not pause to supply it.

The gap shows up as slowness rather than ignorance, which is why it is so often missed. The student can do the work; they take three times as long and make small errors under pressure. By November of DP1 they are behind on new content because the old content is eating their time, and by February they have concluded they are bad at mathematics, which is the expensive part.

The fix is unglamorous and cheap if taken early: a short block in the summer between the two phases, or a weekly hour through the first term of DP1, spent entirely on manipulation fluency rather than on the current topic. Six to ten sessions usually does it. The same repair attempted in the DP2 spring competes with the Exploration, five other subjects and revision, and does not work nearly as well.

This is also the point at which an honest conversation about Higher Level is worth having. A student with a real algebraic gap who insists on Analysis Higher Level is making a decision that will cost marks in five other subjects, and the kindest thing a tutor can do is say so in DP1 while a change is still administratively simple. A provider whose incentive is to sell more hours has a reason not to say it, which is worth remembering.

sections.heading: University routes, Ministry equivalency and what nobody should promise you
paragraphs: Mathematics route choice is the only Diploma decision that routinely closes doors. Engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, social science, humanities and design routes frequently accept Applications and Interpretation. Requirements differ between universities, between countries and between intake years, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions, so the only reliable source is the individual programme page.

Separately from admissions, there is the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency process, which is what allows a certificate to be used for local purposes. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test, and English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section.

For the IB, no points threshold appears in the source we were able to read, so no figure should be quoted to you by a tutoring provider, including this one. Verify it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring platform performs, accelerates or guarantees, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Describing the process is useful; implying involvement in it would not be honest.

The last word on promises. No tutor can guarantee a grade in IB mathematics, and anyone offering a guaranteed 7 is describing their marketing. What can be promised is specific: a diagnosis from the student's own work, a weekly hour that holds, an Exploration coached within the rules, and a re-match if the fit is wrong after the first paid session. Those are testable, which is the only kind of promise worth making.

faqs.question: Analysis or Applications: which one should a Media City student actually take?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with the heaviest calculus content at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with a graphic display calculator used throughout and written interpretation of results expected in almost every answer. The honest axis of the decision is whether the student's algebra is fluent under time pressure without a calculator. If it is, Analysis is viable. If it is slow and error-prone, Analysis at Higher Level will eat the week and damage five other subjects.

faqs.question: Everyone says Applications is the softer route. Is that true at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and families who choose it on that basis are often surprised. At Higher Level it carries statistics and modelling content that many students find harder than the equivalent Analysis material, and it demands written interpretation that mathematically confident students resist. What it does not demand is abstract proof and heavy algebraic manipulation. It is a different course rather than a lighter one, and the right question is fit to the student and to their intended degree.

faqs.question: Can my child switch from Higher to Standard Level maths partway through DP1?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and early is much better than late. A move within the same course from Higher to Standard is normally administratively straightforward and is often the right decision for a student who is drowning in one subject and losing marks in the other five. Check the prerequisite for the intended degree first, because some programmes specify Higher Level. A switch between courses, from Analysis to Applications or back, is harder after the first term because the content diverges.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course do universities expect for engineering?
faqs.answer: Engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Requirements vary by university, by country and by intake year, including at the Dubai campuses of overseas institutions, so the only reliable source is the individual programme page rather than a general rule. Do not take an admissions requirement from a tutoring website, including this one. Check it yourself, and check it in the year your child applies rather than two years earlier.

faqs.question: How long should my child's Exploration take, and when should it start?
faqs.answer: The decision that matters is the topic, and it should be narrowed much earlier than most students narrow it. Almost every weak Exploration fails because the topic was too broad, chosen from a list of impressive-sounding ideas, and by the time the student finds the mathematics is beyond them there is no time left. A narrower topic executed properly outscores an ambitious one left half-finished. Expect the writing to take several weeks of real work spread across a term rather than a fortnight.

faqs.question: What are the five Exploration criteria actually marking?
faqs.answer: Presentation marks coherence and organisation. Mathematical communication marks notation, terminology and representation, which is where calculator syntax left in the write-up costs marks. Personal engagement marks evidence that this was the student's own inquiry. Reflection marks critical commentary made at the point the mathematics raises it, not bolted on at the end. Use of mathematics marks correctness, sophistication and appropriateness to the level. Students consistently neglect reflection and personal engagement because they look decorative, and they are marked.

faqs.question: May a tutor help with the maths Exploration at all?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor may help narrow the topic, teach notation and mathematical communication, explain what each criterion rewards, and read the student's own draft and say precisely where it fails against a descriptor. A tutor may not write, redraft or restructure any part of it, and may not supply a model to adapt. The most valuable legitimate help arrives in the first session by replacing an unworkable topic, long before anything needs editing.

faqs.question: My child reaches the right answer yet the mark scheme still takes marks off. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the method is not visible. Marks are awarded for the reasoning as well as the result, and a student who reaches an answer by a route the examiner cannot see loses the method marks even when the final figure is correct. This is the largest single avoidable loss in both IB mathematics courses, and it is worse in calculator papers where an answer can come straight off a screen. The fix is a habit rather than a topic, and it responds within a few marked papers.

faqs.question: How should Paper 1 preparation differ from Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Treat them as separate examinations. One is sat without a calculator and rewards algebraic fluency, clean manipulation and exact values, so practice should be untimed first and then strictly timed, by hand. The other permits technology and rewards speed plus the discipline of writing down enough method to earn the marks around a calculator result. Students who prepare for both identically usually perform noticeably better in one, and the gap is technique rather than knowledge.

faqs.question: Does Paper 3 at Higher Level need separate practice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the cheapest improvement available in a DP2 spring. Paper 3 is extended problem-solving in an unfamiliar context, where the individual steps are accessible and the difficulty is sustaining a long chain of reasoning without losing the thread. Most students have attempted fewer questions of this type than of any other component, simply because there are fewer of them about. Working through several complete ones under time changes performance quickly.

faqs.question: My child came from IGCSE Core maths and is struggling in DP1. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the sooner the better. Core and Foundation tiers omit the algebraic manipulation, trigonometry and function work that Diploma mathematics assumes immediately, and the gap presents as slowness and small errors rather than as not knowing a topic. Six to ten sessions spent purely on manipulation fluency, rather than on the current week's content, usually closes it. Attempted in the DP2 spring instead, the same repair competes with the Exploration, revision and five other subjects.

faqs.question: How much calculator teaching should a maths tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: More than most do. Regression and correlation, distribution calculations, numerical solving, graphing with sensible windows and the table features are all examined, all mechanical, and all faster with practice. A student who takes ninety seconds to set up a distribution calculation loses marks simply by running out of paper time. Over a shared screen a tutor can watch the keystroke sequence and correct it live, which is more effective than describing it and far easier than leaning across a table.

faqs.question: Can a maths tutor based outside the UAE teach a Dubai student properly?
faqs.answer: For mathematics, yes, provided the timing works. The lesson is a shared screen with a solution built line by line and a past paper annotated live, which is how mathematics is taught at a table anyway. What matters is Gulf Standard Time scheduling and board familiarity, not the tutor's postcode. Where a match is a tutor based outside the UAE, we say so before you book rather than behind a local-sounding number, because two providers ranking for these searches do not.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a DP2 student need before the exams?
faqs.answer: Two or three a week for six to eight weeks is the usual shape of a pre-session block, and it should end when the session starts rather than drifting on. Before that, one held hour a week through DP1 and the first half of DP2 does considerably more for less money, because it prevents the emergency instead of managing it. Buying four hours a week in the final month mostly consumes the student's own practice time, which is where the remaining marks actually are.

faqs.question: Is an in-home maths tutor worth the extra cost in Al Sufouh?
faqs.answer: Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor and AED 200 to AED 450 for a specialist. The premium is the drive, not the teaching, and for mathematics the online medium costs almost nothing because the work is a shared screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India.

intro.heading: The route decision outranks the tutoring decision
paragraphs: There are four IB mathematics courses, not one. Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard. They share a title and almost nothing else. AA is built on proof, algebraic fluency and calculus. AI is built on statistics, modelling and technology use. A student who is strong at one is frequently weak at the other, and the choice is made at sixteen, usually in a hurry, often on the basis of which teacher the student liked.

That is the decision a Production City family most needs help with, and it is why this page leads with it rather than with tutoring. Universities in the United Kingdom, Europe and the UAE set prerequisites that distinguish between the routes, and engineering, physics, economics and most mathematics degrees expect AA. A student who takes AI HL and then applies for mechanical engineering can find themselves holding a strong grade in the wrong subject, and no number of tutoring hours in DP2 fixes that.

The second thing this page does is compare. Dubai Production City sits beside Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Dubai South, Emaar South, Jebel Ali and Green Community, and families in this cluster are routinely compared against one another when a tutor decides whether an evening journey is worth making. For mathematics specifically, the comparison is interesting because the feeder schools differ in which route they push, and a student's options are shaped by that before they ever choose.

There is no IB World School inside Production City. Students travel to Greenfield International School in Dubai Investments Park, to the Al Barsha ring, or to Fairgreen International School to the south. That means a family's maths options depend on which campus their child attends, and whether that campus offers all four routes or only two. Not every school runs AI HL, and that fact alone has decided more route choices in this cluster than any careers conversation.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics, the online format has a specific advantage beyond the obvious: a shared digital whiteboard produces a saved record of every worked solution, so a student revising in the spring is working from their own tutor's working rather than from a half-remembered page in a notebook.

Everything here was reviewed in October 2026. We do not publish IB session or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be correct. Confirm windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. Component structures and assessment criteria, which is what most of this page is about, are published in the subject guide your child's school already holds.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one of the four mathematics courses from group five. Higher Level has three papers; Standard Level has two. Both levels submit an exploration, an individual written report worth roughly twenty per cent and assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics.
