Before planning anything, confirm which of the four courses the school actually runs, because a student intending AA HL at a campus that only offers AA SL and AI SL is making a school decision rather than a subject one, and that is a conversation for Year 11 rather than DP1.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria scored one to eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is the one that prepares a student for the exploration, and it is the one most commonly treated as an optional extra by students chasing content marks.
programmes.countryNote: Because the MYP has no external examination, a Production City student entering DP1 has rarely sat a timed mathematics paper of any length. The first DP mock then looks like a content failure when it is a pacing and presentation failure. The final MYP term is the right place to introduce timed questions and the habit of writing visible method.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Mathematics in the PYP is embedded in transdisciplinary units with continuous assessment and no external examination. The things that matter later are narrow and specific: fluency with number facts, confidence with fractions and proportion, and the willingness to write down a working step rather than answering mentally. All three carry directly into MYP criteria.
programmes.countryNote: PYP children from Production City are on early buses out to Dubai Investments Park, Motor City or Al Barsha, and their evening attention is limited. Twenty-five minute sessions twice a week work better at this age than one long hour, and a parent sitting in for the first few minutes measurably improves how the session goes.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-production.subjectsIntro: The mathematics topics that generate the most requests from Production City and the surrounding communities, with the specific place marks go missing. Topic names follow the current subject guide structure.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation and related rates at HL. Marks are lost in notation rather than in technique: a student who differentiates correctly but does not state what is being differentiated with respect to loses method marks that were already earned.

subjects.name: Calculus: integration
subjects.description: Substitution, integration by parts and volumes of revolution at HL. The recurring failure is omitting the constant, or changing limits after a substitution without saying so. Both are mechanical habits and both are fixable in two or three sessions of deliberate practice.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample. Induction is the most formulaic proof in the course and the most frequently botched, because students write the inductive step without ever stating the assumption they are using. The structure is worth drilling until it is automatic.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity. Students manage the algebra and lose marks on the Argand diagram, where a sketch without labelled axes, moduli or arguments scores nothing it could have scored.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI HL and SL, AA SL
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. In AI the graphical calculator is assumed, and marks are lost for not naming the test used or the model fitted. Interpreting a result in context, rather than reporting a number, is where the upper band sits.

subjects.name: Modelling and functions
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric and piecewise models fitted to real data. The skill examined is judgement: choosing a model, justifying the choice, and stating what the model cannot do. Students fit and then fail to evaluate, which costs the final marks on most questions.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, compound angles, the double-angle formulae and solving in given domains. The most common lost mark in the whole course sits here: solutions outside the stated domain, or a student finding one solution where the domain contains three.

subjects.name: Vectors, matrices and graph theory
subjects.description: AA HL covers vector equations of lines and planes and intersections; AI HL covers matrices, transformations, graph theory and adjacency. Two genuinely different topic sets under one heading, which is why a tutor who teaches both routes interchangeably is a problem rather than a convenience.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: An individual written report of around twelve to twenty pages, worth roughly twenty per cent, assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Topic choice in DP1 constrains the achievable mark more than the writing does.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: Start with what the two courses contain, because the names tell a parent nothing. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route: proof, functions, calculus, trigonometric identities, and at Higher Level complex numbers and vectors. It assumes and develops symbolic fluency, and it is the course that resembles a traditional pure mathematics syllabus. Applications and Interpretation is the data route: statistics, probability distributions, hypothesis testing, modelling real datasets, and at Higher Level matrices and graph theory.

The technology position is the clearest practical difference. In AI, the graphical calculator is assumed throughout and a student who cannot run a regression or a chi-squared test on the device will lose marks that have nothing to do with mathematics. In AA, Paper 1 is a non-calculator paper, which rewards algebraic manipulation done by hand and punishes a student who has always reached for the device.

Then there are the prerequisites, which is where the decision becomes irreversible. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most quantitative economics degrees generally expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. AI HL is accepted for a narrower set of courses, and AI SL for a narrower set again. The right process is to list three or four target degrees, read the published entry requirements on each university's own site, and work backwards. Requirements change, so read them rather than trusting a summary.

The common failure in this cluster is a capable student choosing AI because it looks easier, then applying for engineering. AI HL is not easier than AA SL; it is different and in places harder. What it is not is a substitute for AA where AA is specified.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually sit, paper by paper
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject where component weighting is most often misunderstood, because the exploration is invisible in daily classwork and then turns out to be a fifth of the grade. A student who treats it as a holiday project has handed away twenty per cent before revision begins, and unlike a paper it cannot be re-sat.

At Higher Level in both routes, the external assessment is three papers rather than two. The third is the one that differentiates students, and it does so by examining something the first two do not: sustained work on an extended unfamiliar problem. In AA HL that means two long structured questions requiring several techniques in sequence. In AI HL it means two extended problems built around data and modelling, often with a context the student has never met.

At Standard Level there are two papers, one with a calculator and one without in AA, and both with calculator access in AI. The proportions mean that a Standard Level student cannot afford a weak exploration, because there is less external assessment to absorb it.

Across all four routes, method marks are the recurring issue. The mark scheme awards visible reasoning separately from the final answer, so a student who works mentally and writes only the result loses marks they genuinely earned. That single habit, writing the step, is worth more in a Standard Level paper than almost any content revision, and it takes two or three sessions to establish.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is assessed on five published criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Almost no competitor page in this market names any of them, which is strange, because they are the entire instruction and they are in the subject guide every school holds.

Use of mathematics is the heaviest criterion and the one where topic choice decides the outcome. A topic whose mathematics sits comfortably below the student's course level cannot reach the top band however well it is written, because the criterion rewards mathematics commensurate with the course. This is why a topic chosen in week two of DP1, before the student has met the harder content, so often caps the mark.

Personal engagement is the criterion students misread most. It does not mean choosing something they enjoy. It means visible evidence of their own thinking and their own decisions inside the work: a choice made and justified, an approach abandoned and replaced, an extension attempted. Reflection means saying what the result actually means and what the limitations are, not restating the conclusion in different words.

Our role is bounded and we state the boundary plainly. We teach what each criterion asks for, we interrogate whether a proposed topic can satisfy use of mathematics at the student's level, and we give feedback on the student's own drafts against the descriptors. We do not write, rewrite or complete any part of an exploration. One operator in our research sells completed internal assessments; the malpractice consequence of buying one falls on the student.

sections.heading: Production City against its neighbours, for mathematics specifically
paragraphs: Set Dubai Production City beside Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Dubai South, Emaar South, Jebel Ali and Green Community and the differences that matter for a maths student are not the ones a property listing would mention. They are which campus the bus goes to, which of the four group five routes that campus runs, and whether the student arrives in DP1 from an MYP background or an IGCSE one.

That last distinction shapes the first term more than anything else. An MYP entrant has met criterion-based assessment, including investigating patterns, which is direct preparation for the exploration. An IGCSE entrant has met timed papers and algebraic drill, which is direct preparation for Paper 1 but not for the exploration at all. Al Furjan and Jebel Ali send more IGCSE entrants; Dubai Investments Park and Green Community, feeding Greenfield, send more MYP entrants.

What does not differ is the depth of the local evening tutor pool for a specific route. An AA HL specialist is drawn from the small number of teachers delivering AA HL at campuses in Al Barsha, Dubai Investments Park and the southern corridor, and that person is thirty to forty minutes from any of these eight communities between five and seven. The Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour, visible in the gap between published online and in-home bands, is that drive expressed as money.

So the comparison resolves the same way everywhere, and for mathematics it resolves harder, because route-specific expertise is narrower than general subject expertise. There is no neighbourhood in this cluster where moving house would improve a student's access to an AA HL specialist.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the skill nobody teaches explicitly
paragraphs: Higher Level students in both routes sit a third paper, and it is the one that most reliably produces a lower mark than the student's ability suggests. The reason is that it examines something the rest of the course does not require: sustained independent work on a long, unfamiliar, multi-part problem where the first step is not signposted.

A student who has only met questions resembling their textbook has learned to recognise rather than to analyse. Faced with an unfamiliar structure, they read it twice and stop, because recognition fails and nothing replaces it. The paper is worth roughly a fifth of the Higher Level grade, so freezing for the first ten minutes is expensive in a way that a wrong answer is not.

The fix is specific and repetitive, and it is about the opening rather than the whole question. We practise reading an unfamiliar problem, identifying what is given, naming what kind of object is being asked for, and writing a first line even when the route to the answer is not visible. Writing something correct and relevant usually opens the next step, and it also earns method marks that a blank page cannot.

We do this with questions the student or school legitimately holds, because IB papers and mark schemes are copyright material and we do not reproduce or distribute them. Your child's mathematics teacher can supply past Paper 3 questions through the proper channel, and that is the route to use.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs in Dubai, and what the premium buys
paragraphs: Lead with the cheapest honest option rather than the premium one. Budget and university-student tutors in Dubai advertise from AED 45 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. For a Standard Level student who needs procedural practice and somebody to check their working, that band can genuinely be enough, and nobody in this market will tell you so.

Above that, qualified subject tutors online run roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. IB specialists sit at AED 200-450, with TutorChase quoting AED 270. Premium or examiner-led tutors reach AED 500-650 or more, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, rising to AED 500 at specialist levels. All figures read in October 2026 and attributed to their publishers.

What the step up actually buys in mathematics is route-specific mark-scheme knowledge. An AA HL student needs somebody who knows that an unjustified line costs method marks and what the Paper 3 examiner wants in the opening. A student needing drill on quadratics does not, and paying specialist rates for drill is the most common overspend in this market.

These are market rates, not IB Gram prices. We do not publish a price list on these pages. We start with a free trial lesson and an honest conversation about which band the actual problem sits in, which sometimes means telling a family that they need fewer hours and a cheaper tutor than they came expecting to buy.

sections.heading: Equivalency, universities and what to check before Year 12
paragraphs: A Dubai Diploma often needs a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency certificate before it can be used for a UAE university place or certain employment routes. Families meet this for the first time in DP2 under time pressure, and the mathematics route is occasionally relevant to it because some destination programmes specify quantitative prerequisites of their own.

The published British-track rule is specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. For the IB Diploma there is no points threshold we can responsibly publish, because the source setting out the British and American tracks states none. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority, and ask the school's university counsellor, who handles this annually.

On university prerequisites, the only reliable method is to read the requirement on each institution's own admissions page for the specific programme, in the year the student applies. Engineering and physics programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and some specify a minimum grade in it. Requirements are revised, so a summary from two years ago is a guess.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or admission for anybody, and tutoring is not a requirement for either. We will tell a family when the honest answer is that the route decision needs the school's university counsellor rather than a tutor.

sections.heading: Getting started on the right route
paragraphs: If the route is still open, start there. One or two sessions working through real questions from both courses tells you more than any amount of discussion, because a student's reaction to a proof by induction and to a regression interpretation is informative in a way their stated preference is not. You get a written summary to take to the school's university counsellor.

If the route is already fixed, send the course, the level, the school and a recent marked paper. A marked script is worth more than a report card, because it shows whether the problem is notation, content, pacing or the exploration. Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on the current sticking point rather than a sales call, with a short written note afterwards.

On availability we give dates rather than substitutes. AA HL and AI HL specialists in a specific evening slot are the thinnest part of our mathematics coverage, particularly in the weeks before mocks, and a wait of two to four days is normal. If the first opening is longer we say the date. If the specialist is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

Sessions for Production City households usually land at 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings better for exploration work. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots are a normal request and the slot is held. What we will not do, in IMPZ or anywhere in the UAE, is send a tutor to your address; that service runs in India only.

faqs.question: Which group five route fits a student aiming at engineering, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the degree, then check it against the student's actual strengths. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most quantitative economics programmes generally expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level and sometimes with a minimum grade. AI suits business, social sciences, design and many life science routes. Then test the student: somebody who handles proof by induction but struggles to interpret a regression belongs in AA, and the reverse belongs in AI. Read the requirement on each target university's own admissions page in the application year, because these are revised and a two-year-old summary is a guess.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier maths course?
faqs.answer: No, it is a different course, and AI HL is not easier than AA SL. AI replaces algebraic proof and calculus depth with statistics, modelling, matrices and graph theory, all of which are demanding in their own way, and it assumes calculator fluency throughout. The real risk is not difficulty but fit: a capable student who chooses AI because it sounds lighter and then applies for mechanical engineering can end up with a strong grade in a subject the programme does not accept. That is the error we most often catch too late in this cluster.

faqs.question: What proportion of a Production City student's maths grade is the exploration?
faqs.answer: Roughly twenty per cent in all four routes, as a single individual written report assessed on five published criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. It is the most controllable part of the grade and the easiest to cap by accident, because use of mathematics rewards work commensurate with the course level. A topic chosen in week two of DP1, before the student has met the harder content, frequently limits the achievable mark no matter how well the report is written afterwards.

faqs.question: What exactly does personal engagement mean in the exploration?
faqs.answer: Not choosing a topic the student enjoys, which is how almost everybody reads it. It means visible evidence of their own thinking and their own decisions inside the work: a choice made and justified, an approach tried and abandoned with the reason stated, an extension attempted beyond the obvious. Reflection is the companion criterion and means saying what the result actually means and what its limitations are, rather than restating the conclusion in different words. Both are teachable, and both are usually the difference between a middle and an upper band mark.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 pull Higher Level grades down?
faqs.answer: Because it examines something the other papers do not: sustained independent work on a long unfamiliar problem with no signposted first step. Students who have only met textbook-shaped questions have learned recognition rather than analysis, so when recognition fails they read the problem twice and stop. It is worth roughly a fifth of the Higher Level grade, so ten frozen minutes is expensive. The fix targets the opening rather than the whole question: read, identify what is given, name what is being asked for, and write a correct relevant first line, which is usually enough to see the second one.

faqs.question: Does my child really lose marks for not writing the working?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common avoidable loss in the subject. The mark scheme awards method marks for visible reasoning separately from the mark for the final answer, so a student who manipulates an expression mentally and writes only the result forfeits marks they genuinely earned. It is a habit rather than a knowledge problem, which means it can be established in two or three sessions of deliberate practice, and at Standard Level that single change is usually worth more than any amount of additional content revision.

faqs.question: Does every Dubai IB school offer all four maths routes?
faqs.answer: No, and this constrains more choices in this cluster than any careers conversation does. Some campuses run only two or three of AA HL, AA SL, AI HL and AI SL in a given year, depending on cohort size and staffing. Since Dubai Production City has no IB campus inside it, families here are often choosing between schools partly on group five provision without realising it. Ask the school directly which routes will be available in your child's year, in writing, before Year 11 choices are submitted.

faqs.question: Our son came from IGCSE and is drowning in AA HL calculus. Fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason it happened is structural rather than personal. IGCSE Extended does not cover the calculus that AA Higher Level assumes from early in DP1, so a strong IGCSE mathematician can arrive genuinely well prepared for Paper 1 algebra and completely unprepared for differentiation. The work is sequential: establish function notation and limits properly, then differentiation rules, then applications, in that order. Attempting the school's current topic without that foundation is why extra practice at the current point usually produces no improvement at all.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor enough for Standard Level maths practice?
faqs.answer: Often, and almost nobody in this market will say so. Budget and university-student tutors in Dubai advertise from AED 45 an hour, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. For a Standard Level student who mainly needs procedural practice and somebody to check their working, that band can be genuinely sufficient. What it does not cover is Paper 3 technique, exploration criteria work or route advice, which need specialist knowledge at AED 200-450. Paying specialist rates for drill is the most common overspend we see.

faqs.question: How does a graphical calculator affect the AI papers?
faqs.answer: Substantially, because the device is assumed throughout rather than permitted on one paper. An AI student who cannot run a regression, a chi-squared test or a distribution calculation fluently on their model loses marks that have nothing to do with their mathematics. Equally, marks go missing when a student produces a correct output and does not state which test was run or which model was fitted, since the mark scheme awards the stated method. We check device fluency explicitly in the first few sessions, because it is invisible in classwork until a paper exposes it.

faqs.question: Is there an AA HL specialist living near Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: Few, and the reason is structural. AA Higher Level is taught by a small number of teachers at the campuses that offer it, in Al Barsha, Dubai Investments Park and the southern corridor, and none of those is less than twenty minutes from IMPZ, closer to forty between five and seven when a Diploma student is actually free. The Dubai travel premium of roughly AED 50-150 an hour is that drive priced into the lesson. Online delivery removes the geographic filter and leaves route-specific expertise, which is the filter that affects the grade.

faqs.question: Would moving to Al Furjan or DIP improve access to maths tutors?
faqs.answer: No. It would change the school run and the entry route into DP1, which matters for what a student needs, but not the depth of the local specialist pool. AA HL teachers are drawn from the campuses that deliver AA HL, and those sit thirty to forty minutes from every community in this cluster in the evening. What does differ is preparation: Dubai Investments Park and Green Community send more MYP entrants, who are better prepared for the exploration, while Al Furjan and Jebel Ali send more IGCSE entrants, who are better prepared for Paper 1 algebra.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check over the exploration before my daughter submits it?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give feedback against the five published criteria on a draft your daughter wrote, explain what each descriptor actually rewards, and question whether the topic can reach the band she is aiming for. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, edit to completion or supply any part of the text, because the line is authorship and the consequence of crossing it sits on the student's record. Operators in this same search sell completed internal assessments; buying one is an academic malpractice risk and no tutoring arrangement is worth that.

faqs.question: When do UAE IB students sit maths papers, and when should we start?
faqs.answer: UAE IB schools sit the May session. We do not publish specific IB session or results dates because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a date a parent plans around has to be right, so confirm windows with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. On timing, mathematics is cumulative, which makes early work unusually valuable: a gap left in DP1 compounds for eighteen months rather than sitting still. The highest-return period is DP1 and the autumn of DP2, while the exploration is live and content gaps are still repairable.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to our home in IMPZ?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. For mathematics the online format has a specific benefit beyond cost: the shared whiteboard saves every worked solution, so spring revision starts from the student's own tutor's working rather than from a half-remembered notebook. Independent home tutors do operate in this area at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, and for a younger child who needs a hand kept on the page they can genuinely be the better option.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-production.closingBody: The single most consequential mathematics decision a Production City family makes is which of the four group five courses the student enters, and it is usually made quickly on weak information. List three or four target degrees, read their published prerequisites, confirm which routes the school actually runs, and test the student on real questions from both courses before committing. Then, and only then, worry about tutoring, which should be matched to the route and the level rather than to the word maths. Book a free trial lesson and start with one honest hour of teaching.

intro.heading: Comparing the corridor for IB maths, and finding the same answer
paragraphs: Dubai Silicon Oasis sits on the eastern side of the Dubai-Al Ain corridor, with Academic City immediately south, The Villa and Dubailand to the west, and Nad Al Sheba and Ras Al Khor to the north. Families weighing these areas for a Diploma student usually assume the maths tutoring market varies between them. It varies far less than the school offer does, and the reason is worth understanding before spending a weekend on local searches.

What genuinely differs is which courses the nearby schools actually run. Not every Diploma school offers all four maths courses at both levels in every cohort. A school may run Analysis and Approaches at both levels and Applications and Interpretation only at Standard Level, or combine small Higher Level groups across years. That is a real difference between schools in Silicon Oasis, Nad Al Sheba and Dubailand, and it is a question worth asking before enrolment rather than after.

What does not differ is the private tutoring pool. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of private school enrolment in Dubai in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on the UK curriculum and 26 per cent Indian. Divide that cohort across four maths courses and the pool of people who teach any one of them for a living is small, and it is small measured from Cedre Villas, from Nad Al Sheba or from The Villa equally.

Then add the third filter. A visiting tutor must reach your address between roughly 4pm and 6pm, which is the only window in which a Diploma student can hold a four-step rearrangement in their head. On a corridor where journeys run twenty-five to forty minutes in the late afternoon, that filter removes most of the remaining candidates for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. The intersection of course, level and driving distance is close to empty in every one of these communities.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis and the neighbouring areas, maths lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format is better rather than merely cheaper: the same working appears at the same size for both people, a non-calculator question can be annotated line by line as the error happens, and the graphic display calculator screen can be shown directly rather than described across a table.

The rest of this page does the comparison with tables. Which courses sit at which schools and how to ask. How deep local supply runs by course and level. What the AA and AI choice commits a family to. What each paper is worth. And where the marks actually go, which is the only comparison that changes a grade.

Criterion A is knowing and understanding; the investigating-patterns and applying-in-context criteria are where students with sound arithmetic routinely lose bands because generalising and justifying a rule is a different activity from calculating.

A family along this corridor thinking about Higher Level AA should be asking about the stream in Year 9.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses at two levels each. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology, with the calculator permitted throughout. Both carry a mathematical exploration worth 20 per cent, and Higher Level in both adds a Paper 3.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-silicon-oa.subjectsIntro: This grid is the Diploma maths syllabus split into the topics tuition actually gets bought for, with where the marks go in each. It is the comparison that matters: tutor against tutor on these specifics, rather than one postcode against another.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, binomial expansion, with proof and complex numbers at AA Higher Level. This topic decides Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, because every manipulation has to be exact without a calculator, and the errors are procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations, with rational functions at Higher Level. Marks are lost on domain restrictions treated as decoration, and on sketches drawn without the asymptotes and intercepts that carry the marks.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Triangles, circular functions, identities and equations, with vectors at AA Higher Level. Trigonometric equations are where a student finds some solutions and loses the rest by not considering the whole interval the question specified.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA SL and HL, lighter in AI
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at AA Higher Level, substitution, integration by parts and differential equations. The long structured questions in Paper 2 are where the method marks sit, and untidy intermediate working loses them.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability distributions and hypothesis testing in Applications and Interpretation. The AI student's characteristic loss is interpretation: a correct regression described in words that never mention the context in the question.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An independent piece of mathematics on a topic the student chooses, marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. A topic too large for the space available is the commonest failure.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique in AA
subjects.description: Sat without a calculator, which is a distinct skill from doing the mathematics. Exact values, surds, fractions and clean algebraic steps. Students who have practised only with a device in hand lose marks on questions they can genuinely do.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level only
subjects.description: An extended problem-solving paper where each part builds on the last, so an early error propagates through everything after it. Sustained reasoning and reading ahead are the skills, and this is the component that responds least well to late preparation.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: Solving equations, finding intersections, regression, distributions and numerical calculus on the device. Weak skills cost marks in AI and in AA Paper 2, while over-reliance conceals the algebra gap that then surfaces in AA Paper 1.

subjects.name: MYP and IGCSE to DP transition
subjects.description: Both Diploma courses assume fluent algebraic manipulation, confident indices and surds, and comfort rearranging formulae. A student who met those topics without automating them experiences the Diploma as a sudden difficulty rather than a gradual one.

sections.heading: Which maths courses the nearby schools actually run
paragraphs: This is the one part of the neighbourhood comparison that genuinely matters, and almost nobody asks it. Not every Diploma school offers all four maths courses in every cohort. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level requires a viable group and a teacher able to take it, and in smaller cohorts a school may run Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level only, or teach a combined Higher Level group across both courses, or set the stream in Year 11 with little room to change.

That has a direct consequence for a family choosing between Silicon Oasis, Nad Al Sheba, The Villa and Dubailand. If a student is heading for an engineering or mathematics degree that specifies Analysis and Approaches, the question to ask a prospective school is whether it has run AA Higher Level in each of the last three cohorts, not whether it offers it on paper. Those are different answers and the second one is the honest one.

Ask it in writing and ask it early. A school that offers a course in its prospectus and has not actually run it for two years is not being dishonest; it is describing capacity rather than history. But a student enrolled on that basis may find themselves in a combined group or steered towards a different course, and by then the alternative schools along the corridor have filled their places.

For a family already enrolled, the same question determines the tutoring plan. A student in a combined Higher Level group, or one taught Applications and Interpretation while aiming at a course that prefers Analysis and Approaches, needs a different kind of support from one in a well-staffed single-course group. That is a school-level fact rather than a neighbourhood one, which is the point of this section.

sections.heading: Local tutor supply by course, which is the same everywhere
paragraphs: Apply the three filters honestly. Course: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different enough that a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful for the other, particularly at Higher Level. Level: Higher Level adds content and, in both courses, a Paper 3. Geography: the tutor must reach your address between roughly 4pm and 6pm, which on this corridor means a twenty-five to forty minute journey in the worst hour.

Each filter alone leaves candidates. Together they do not. For Primary Years and most Middle Years mathematics the intersection is still populated, which is why hiring locally at those levels is a sensible choice rather than a compromise. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and for Paper 3 strategy specifically, the intersection in Silicon Oasis is close to empty, and so is the intersection in Nad Al Sheba, The Villa and Mirdif.

There is a particular local mismatch worth naming. Academic City's university campuses make this corridor unusually well supplied at the budget band of AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, both read in October 2026. Undergraduate mathematicians are genuinely good at drilling non-calculator algebra, which happens to be the single highest-return task in Analysis and Approaches. They are not the right people for exploration criteria or Paper 3 reasoning.

So the honest recommendation is split rather than uniform. Use the local budget band for repetitive marked practice where that is what the diagnosis calls for. Use a matched specialist for the exploration, for Paper 3 and for the interpretation work that Applications and Interpretation marks reward. And drop the distance filter for the second category, because it is the filter that makes the match fail.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: The choice is made in Year 11, often by students who cannot articulate the difference, and it determines everything afterwards. Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology-led problem solving, with the calculator permitted throughout both papers. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level and both carry an exploration worth a fifth of the grade.

The common error is treating AI as the easier course. It is different rather than easier. An AI Higher Level student handles substantial statistics, regression and distributions, and must interpret results in context, which is a demanding and distinct skill. What AI does not demand is the exact non-calculator manipulation that AA Paper 1 lives on, so a student with weak algebra and strong interpretive instincts may genuinely be better served by it and should not be argued out of it.

The reverse error is choosing AI to avoid difficulty and finding a door closed later. Some university programmes, particularly in engineering, mathematics, physics and economics at competitive institutions, specify Analysis and Approaches or set a Higher Level mathematics requirement that AI Standard Level does not meet. Requirements are set by individual institutions and courses and change between admissions cycles, so the only reliable method is to read the specific admissions page for the specific year.

For a family on this corridor the sequence is: ask the school which course the student is tracked towards and why, then test that assumption against two or three target degree subjects, then involve the school's university counsellor. If a change is warranted the window is the end of Year 11 and the very start of DP1. After that the cost of switching rises sharply in tuition and in lost ground.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth and how long it runs
paragraphs: Weightings are the most useful thing a parent can know and the thing almost no tutoring page states. At Standard Level in both courses, Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 40 per cent of the final grade and the exploration carries 20 per cent. At Higher Level in both courses, Paper 1 and Paper 2 each carry 30 per cent, Paper 3 carries 20 per cent and the exploration carries 20 per cent. Check these against your child's school copy of the subject guide, which is the authority.

Durations follow the same pattern. Standard Level Papers 1 and 2 run ninety minutes each. Higher Level Papers 1 and 2 run two hours each, and Paper 3 one hour. The arithmetic worth doing is that at Higher Level, Paper 3 and the exploration together carry 40 per cent of the grade while occupying one hour of examination plus a piece of coursework. That is a very large share sitting in the two components students prepare for least.

Read against the neighbourhood comparison that opened this page, that is the real finding. Whether you live in Silicon Oasis or Nad Al Sheba changes nothing about those weightings, and they are what determines where tuition money should go. A block aimed at Paper 3, or a handful of well-timed hours on the exploration at the question-setting stage, moves a larger share of the grade than general revision spread across two years.

The table below is the one to keep. Treat the final column as a priority list rather than a shopping list: for many students the honest conclusion is that Paper 2 is already fine, Paper 1 needs a short non-calculator block, and nobody has yet thought about Paper 3 at all. That is a cheaper plan than weekly cover across everything and a considerably better one.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, which is the only real comparison
paragraphs: Most lost marks in Diploma mathematics are not caused by not knowing the mathematics. They are caused by four repeatable habits, and naming them is most of the repair. Sign and index slips under time pressure, which is a Paper 1 problem in Analysis and Approaches specifically. Working shown so compressed that method marks cannot be awarded, which is a Paper 2 problem at both levels and in both courses.

Answering less than the question asked is the third. A trigonometric equation question that specifies an interval wants every solution inside it; a student who finds two and stops has done the mathematics and lost the marks. A function sketch wants the asymptotes and intercepts rather than a plausible curve. These are reading habits and they respond to marked practice rather than to further explanation.

The fourth is interpretation, which is the Applications and Interpretation student's version of the same problem. A regression is computed correctly, a correlation coefficient is quoted, and the written answer says nothing about what it means for the context in the question. The calculation marks arrive and the interpretation marks do not. Teaching a student to write one honest sentence of context after every statistical result is cheap and visibly effective.

The diagnostic that works is unglamorous and free. Take the student's last two marked papers, classify every lost mark into those four buckets plus a fifth for genuine content gaps, and count. Most students produce a strongly skewed distribution and the plan then writes itself. A tutor who starts there rather than at topic one is a tutor who intends the hours to count, and this is the test to apply regardless of where they live.

sections.heading: The exploration: a fifth of the grade on five criteria
paragraphs: The exploration is an independent piece of mathematics written on a topic the student chooses, and it carries 20 per cent of the final grade in all four courses. It is marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Your child's teacher holds the current criteria and mark allocations in the subject guide, and that is the copy to work from; we do not reproduce board documents.

The commonest failure has nothing to do with mathematical ability. It is a topic too large to handle properly in the space available, chosen because it sounded impressive. A narrow question answered thoroughly outscores a grand question answered superficially every time, because the criteria reward depth of engagement and quality of reflection rather than ambition of subject matter. Fixing the choice takes one conversation and saves a term of frustration.

The second commonest failure is reflection treated as a conclusion. Criterion-based reflection means engaging honestly with what the mathematics did and did not show, what assumptions were made, and what a further investigation would change. A paragraph restating the result in different words scores in the lowest band. This is teachable quickly and almost never taught, because it does not feel like mathematics.

The boundary matters more here than anywhere else in the course, and it is the same in every community on this corridor. A tutor may discuss topic choice, explain each criterion, model a comparable exploration on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The work is declared as the student's own and moderated by the IB.

sections.heading: The calculator, and why a shared screen helps
paragraphs: A graphic display calculator is required equipment in both Diploma mathematics courses, and how a student uses it predicts their Paper 1 grade in Analysis and Approaches better than almost anything else. Used well it solves equations, finds intersections, runs regressions and handles distributions quickly, which frees attention for reasoning. Used as a crutch it conceals an algebra gap for two years, and the gap then arrives fully grown in a paper where the device is not allowed.

The diagnostic is simple enough for a parent to run without any mathematics. Ask the student to expand and simplify a bracketed expression, rearrange a formula for a different variable, and add two algebraic fractions, all on paper. A fluent Analysis and Approaches student does those without hesitation. A student who reaches for the calculator or stalls has a Paper 1 problem regardless of their Paper 2 marks, and that is worth knowing in DP1 rather than in the spring of DP2.

The opposite failure is real too, particularly in Applications and Interpretation. Students who have never been taught the device properly lose marks in both papers because they cannot run a regression or read a distribution efficiently, and then spend time they do not have doing by hand what the calculator exists to do. Calculator technique is teachable in a few sessions and is among the clearest returns on a tutoring hour in AI.

This is where the delivery format stops being neutral. The calculator screen can be shown directly on a shared screen, so the tutor sees exactly which menu the student is in and which keystroke went wrong, rather than watching a device across a table and inferring. Several of the commonest calculator errors are invisible to somebody sitting beside the student and obvious to somebody looking at the same screen.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and the limits we state
paragraphs: Send four things: which of the four maths courses your child is in, which paper or component is going wrong, the last two marked papers if you have them, and the hour the student is realistically at a desk. The marked papers matter most, because the error classification can be done before any money changes hands. We then match a tutor to that exact course and level and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written note setting out where the marks are going, sorted into the four habit categories plus genuine content gaps, with a recommended shape and number of hours. For many students that is a short non-calculator block rather than a weekly booking. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the one course where a two-year weekly arrangement is frequently right, and we will say which situation you are in.

The limits. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none. We hold no IB, regulator or board approval. We publish no IB examination or results dates, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than silence; your child's IB coordinator holds the real calendar.

And the exploration boundary, once more, because it is the rule this market bends most often. A tutor may discuss the topic, explain each criterion, model a comparable piece on a different subject, read your child's own draft and say where it falls short, and teach citation. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or supply any part of it. Ask every provider you consider to put that in writing, and keep the reply.

faqs.question: Is IB maths tutoring easier to find in Silicon Oasis than in Nad Al Sheba?
faqs.answer: No. Those areas differ on school offer and commute, and the private tutoring pool is an emirate-level constraint rather than a neighbourhood one. The International Baccalaureate was 7 per cent of Dubai private school enrolment in 2024-25, and dividing that across four maths courses at two levels leaves a small pool measured from anywhere on this corridor. What does differ, and is worth asking, is which maths courses each nearby school has actually run recently.

faqs.question: Does every Diploma school near Dubai Silicon Oasis offer AA Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and this is the question worth asking before enrolment. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level needs a viable group and a teacher able to take it, so in smaller cohorts a school may run Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level only, teach a combined Higher Level group, or set the stream in Year 11 with little room to change. Ask whether the school has run AA Higher Level in each of the last three cohorts, not whether it appears in the prospectus.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI for a Silicon Oasis student?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches emphasises algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology, with the calculator permitted throughout. Both run at Higher and Standard Level and both carry an exploration worth 20 per cent. AI is not easier, it is different: it demands substantial statistics and genuine interpretation, and it does not demand exact non-calculator manipulation.

faqs.question: Do tutors travel to Cedre Villas for maths lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For mathematics the online format is genuinely better rather than merely cheaper. The same working appears at the same size for both people, a non-calculator question can be annotated line by line as the error happens, and the graphic display calculator screen can be displayed directly instead of described across a table.

faqs.question: Can we use the cheaper tutors near Academic City for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: For one specific task, yes, and it is a useful one. The budget band in this emirate runs AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik, sustained partly by the undergraduate population next door, and undergraduate mathematicians are genuinely effective at drilling non-calculator algebra, which is the highest-return task in Analysis and Approaches. They are not the right match for exploration criteria or Paper 3 reasoning, which need somebody who has taught the course.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and does my child sit it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is an extended problem-solving paper sat only at Higher Level, in both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation. It runs for one hour and carries 20 per cent of the final grade, and each part builds on the last so an early error propagates through everything after it. It responds least well of any component to late preparation, which is why strategy work belongs in DP1 rather than in the final weeks.

faqs.question: What share of the grade is the exploration, and which five criteria apply?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the final grade in all four Diploma mathematics courses. It is marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Your child's teacher holds the current criteria and mark allocations in the subject guide, and that is the copy to work from. The commonest failure is a topic too large to handle in the space available, which one conversation fixes.

faqs.question: Why is my child strong in Paper 2 and weak in Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Almost always because Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator and the student has been doing the mathematics with a device in hand for years. The underlying knowledge is sound; the exact manipulation is not automatic. Test it on paper yourself: expand a bracketed expression, rearrange a formula, add two algebraic fractions. Hesitation on any means a six to eight session non-calculator drilling block is the highest-return purchase available.

faqs.question: Which maths route do universities want from a Dubai Diploma student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the course and the institution, and requirements change between admissions cycles, so no tutoring page should offer a rule. Maths-heavy degrees in engineering, mathematics, physics, computer science and economics are the ones most likely to specify Analysis and Approaches or a Higher Level grade. Open the admissions page for the specific course and year, check whether AI Standard Level satisfies it, and involve the school's university counsellor early rather than late.

faqs.question: How far can a Silicon Oasis tutor go in supporting the exploration?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may discuss topic choice, explain each of the five criteria, model a comparable exploration on a different topic, read a draft your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach citation properly. A tutor may not write, draft, complete, rewrite or supply any part of it. The exploration is declared as the student's own work and moderated by the IB, so the consequence of anything else falls on your child rather than on whoever was paid.

faqs.question: Is it too late to switch between AA and AI in DP1?
faqs.answer: The realistic window is the end of Year 11 and the very start of DP1, and the decision sits with the school rather than with a tutor. Before that conversation, check what two or three target degrees actually require of mathematics, because a switch made to avoid difficulty can close a door and one made for prestige can consume two years of tutoring hours. After the window closes, the cost of switching rises sharply in both tuition and lost ground.

faqs.question: Can poor calculator technique alone pull down an AI grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, in both papers, and it is one of the clearest returns on a tutoring hour in that course. A student who cannot run a regression, read a distribution or find an intersection efficiently loses time they do not have and then attempts by hand what the device exists to do. Calculator technique is teachable in a few sessions, and on a shared screen a tutor can see exactly which menu the student is in, which is not possible across a table.

faqs.question: How many weekly maths sessions does a Higher Level student need?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, placed early enough in the afternoon that the student can still hold a four-step rearrangement in their head. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the one Diploma maths course where a weekly arrangement across both years is frequently right, because the subject builds cumulatively. Where a student is genuinely behind, a weekend block plus the weekday hour works better than three tired evenings, and the slot should be reviewed after mocks.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level maths worth taking if no target degree requires it?
faqs.answer: Often not, and almost nobody will say so. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches chosen for how it looks consumes tutoring hours across two years and risks a grade that helps nothing, while a confident Standard Level result in the right course leaves time for the subjects that carry the application. Check what two or three target degrees actually require before the route is locked. If none specifies Higher Level mathematics, that is a real finding worth acting on.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB maths session dates anywhere on this page?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a date a family plans around is the worst thing to get wrong. UAE schools sit the May examinations, and your child's IB coordinator holds the actual windows and the internal deadlines, including the exploration deadline, which is the date that affects tuition timing most.

intro.heading: Two clocks: the papers in May and the exploration a year earlier
paragraphs: Most parents arranging IB maths support in Dubai South are thinking about the papers. The papers matter, and they arrive in the May session of Year 13. But the deadline that catches more students is the exploration, worth 20% of the subject grade, whose internal school deadline typically falls in Year 12 or early Year 13 — months before anyone is thinking about examinations. A plan aimed only at the papers arrives after a fifth of the grade has already been settled by a piece of work written under panic.

That is the organising idea of this page. There are two clocks running in Diploma mathematics and they need different work. The exploration clock runs on choosing a question, gathering or generating data, doing mathematics that is genuinely at the level of the course, and writing to five published criteria of which two reward process rather than mathematics. The paper clock runs on technique: non-calculator algebra for Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, calculator discipline for Paper 2, and the stamina to finish.

Before either clock matters, the route has to be settled. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are not difficulty levels of the same course; they are different courses with different content and different university currency. Analysis and Approaches has a non-calculator Paper 1 and heavier algebra, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-permitted throughout with statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carrying the weight. Some university programmes specify Analysis and Approaches by name, which makes the Year 11 choice a long-range decision rather than a preference.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with their own marked script and the official markband shared on screen. For mathematics specifically the online arrangement has a practical edge: working is written on a shared digital surface and saved, so the algebra from week three is still legible in week nine when the same error reappears.

One compliance note. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai and publishes annual school inspection ratings. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and that is the document a parent can reasonably ask to see. It licenses somebody to teach privately; it says nothing about whether they have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is the second question and the one that actually decides whether the hours will be useful to your child.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-south.programmesIntro: Dubai South students reach Diploma mathematics from the Middle Years Programme or from IGCSE, and both routes leave characteristic gaps. The notes below are specific to mathematics rather than general programme descriptions.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics is compulsory in the Diploma, taken in one of two routes at Higher or Standard Level. Each route has two or three examination papers plus the exploration at 20%. Standard Level sits Papers 1 and 2; Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper that examines sustained reasoning rather than recall and is routinely prepared last. Grades run 1 to 7 with boundaries set after each session.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai South Diploma candidates sit the May session. The dates that actually govern the maths year are internal: the school's deadline for the exploration draft, the deadline for the final submission, and the mock paper window. Those are set by the school's IB coordinator and typically fall far earlier than families expect, which is the first thing worth asking about.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics is marked against four criteria from A to D, each 0 to 8, converted to a 1-7 grade. Criterion C rewards communication and criterion D rewards applying mathematics in real-life contexts, so a student can hold a strong Middle Years grade on the strength of presentation and investigation while procedural fluency lags. That gap only becomes visible in Diploma Paper 1.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma in the Dubai Investments Park cluster usually need a short block on notation and non-calculator technique rather than content. Four to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12 closes most of it. Left undone, the same gap takes a whole term of Year 12 to close while new content is also arriving.

programmes.name: International GCSE into the Diploma
programmes.description: An IGCSE Extended or Higher tier pass is the usual entry point to Diploma mathematics, and Additional Mathematics 0606 where a school offers it is a genuine advantage for the Analysis and Approaches route. The gap between IGCSE and Diploma mathematics is algebraic fluency and the expectation of justification: at Diploma level, show that and hence are instructions rather than suggestions.
programmes.countryNote: Several British-curriculum schools around Al Furjan and Jebel Ali feed Diploma cohorts elsewhere in Dubai, so a student may change school and system at sixteen. That transition needs the gap mapped in writing over the summer, because the new course assumes prior knowledge the old syllabus may not have covered to the same depth.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where mathematics is taken as one of the Diploma courses inside the Career-related Programme, it is examined identically to any other Diploma entry, including the exploration. Students on this route sometimes have fewer timetabled hours of contact for the same assessment, which makes independent practice between sessions more important rather than less.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is uncommon in this part of Dubai, so a family whose child takes maths within it has few local comparisons. The practical consequence is that nobody can tell the parent whether an exploration draft is on track, and a specialist who has supervised the component is the straightforward answer.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The components and topics a Dubai South maths student actually needs work on, broken out rather than listed as one subject. Each note names where marks go.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches Paper 1
subjects.description: Sat without a calculator, which is the single largest source of lost marks in the whole course. Students taught through a graphical display calculator cannot differentiate a quotient by hand, solve a logarithmic equation, or sketch a derivative from a function. The fix is drill, and it is unpopular and effective in roughly equal measure.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches Paper 2
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted, worth around 40% of the Standard Level grade, and the paper where method marks are available. Candidates lose marks by giving a calculator answer with no working where a question asks for justification, and by rounding prematurely so that a correct method produces a wrong final value.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation Paper 1
subjects.description: Short-response questions across statistics, modelling, geometry and finance, calculator-permitted. Marks leak on interpretation rather than calculation: stating a hypothesis, naming the test used, explaining what a correlation coefficient means for the context given rather than quoting its value.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation Paper 2
subjects.description: Extended-response questions built on longer contexts, where the mathematics is usually accessible and the reading is the obstacle. Candidates who do not extract the variables before starting end up modelling the wrong relationship accurately, which earns very little.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: A longer paper of two extended problem-solving questions that build in stages, examining sustained reasoning rather than topic recall. It is routinely left until last and routinely under-practised. It needs its own block of sessions, because the skill it tests is not improved by revising the content of Papers 1 and 2.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page piece of independent mathematics worth 20% of the grade, marked on five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Two of those reward process. Students who write technically correct mathematics with no reflection sit mid-band and cannot see why.

subjects.name: Non-calculator algebra
subjects.description: Index laws, surds, logarithm manipulation, partial fractions and rearrangement. Not a topic on the syllabus so much as the substrate everything else sits on. A student weak here will appear weak in calculus, in trigonometry and in proof, and treating those three separately wastes the term.

subjects.name: Calculus at Higher Level
subjects.description: Implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and by parts, and differential equations. The commonest failure is not technique but recognition: knowing which method a given integral calls for. That is a pattern-matching skill built by volume, which makes it well suited to set work between sessions.

subjects.name: Proof and proof by induction
subjects.description: Induction has a fixed structure and marks are awarded for the structure as much as for the algebra, so a student who learns the layout gains marks reliably. Proof by contradiction and direct proof appear less often but are short, high-yield topics that respond to two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Statistics and hypothesis testing
subjects.description: Chi-squared and t-tests, correlation, regression and the language of conclusions. Marks are lost on stating hypotheses in the wrong form, on concluding more than the test supports, and on failing to reference the significance level. All three are vocabulary problems and all three are quickly fixed.

subjects.name: Vectors and complex numbers
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes, and the Argand diagram with polar form and De Moivre's theorem. Geometry-heavy and reward sketching, which students under time pressure skip. A deliberate habit of drawing before calculating recovers marks across the whole topic.

subjects.name: Graph theory and matrices
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, walks and paths, minimum spanning trees and transition matrices. Procedural topics that reward drilled algorithm execution rather than insight, which makes them among the most improvable content on the Higher Level Applications syllabus in a short block.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications: settle the route first
paragraphs: No maths plan can be written before the route is confirmed, because the two courses examine different things. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebra, calculus and proof, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics, modelling and financial mathematics, and allows a calculator throughout. A student can be strong in one and genuinely weaker in the other, and neither is the easy option.

The deciding factor is not which course suits the student's temperament. It is what the universities on the shortlist require, because some programmes specify Analysis and Approaches by name and will not accept the other route however high the grade. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees are the usual cases. Business, social sciences, design and several medical routes commonly accept either. That requirement should be checked against the actual course pages for the actual universities before Year 12 subject choices close.

The second question is level. Higher Level adds content, adds Paper 3, and raises the analytical demand at the top of the markbands. A student taking Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because it looks impressive, without the algebraic fluency to support it, will spend two years at the bottom of a hard course. A student taking Applications at Standard Level when their target degree wants Analysis has closed a door quietly. The table sets the comparison out so the conversation can happen once, properly, in Year 11.

sections.heading: Where the maths marks sit, paper by paper
paragraphs: Mathematics distributes its marks across two or three papers plus the exploration, and the distribution is the reason a plan should name a component rather than a topic. A Standard Level candidate whose Paper 2 is weak is losing ground in the component carrying around 40% of the grade, while a candidate whose exploration is unstarted is risking 20% that nobody can recover in the final fortnight.

Higher Level redistributes further by adding Paper 3, which examines sustained problem-solving across two long staged questions. Because the skill is different from the one Papers 1 and 2 reward, revising the core content does not prepare a student for it. This is the most common structural error in Higher Level maths preparation in this cluster: a student who has worked hard on topics arrives at Paper 3 having never attempted one whole and loses marks that were available to them.

The table gives the structure for planning purposes. The honest caveat is that grade boundaries are set after each session and adjusted to the difficulty of that session's papers, so a percentage from a previous year is not a target. What transfers is the relative weight of each component, and that is what a plan should be aimed at. Reading the structure with a marked mock in hand is the fastest way to find out where the hours should go. One practical rule falls out of it: an unstarted exploration always outranks a weak paper in the priority order, because the exploration can still be secured in full while a paper can only be improved.

sections.heading: The exploration, counted backwards from the school deadline
paragraphs: The exploration is 20% of the grade and the only part of it a family can plan with certainty, because its deadline is known in advance. What makes it go wrong is not difficulty but sequencing. A student who chooses a question in the final month will choose one that is either too broad to answer or too shallow to show course-level mathematics, and both cap the mark before a word is written.

Counted backwards, the sequence is clear. The final submission deadline is set by the school coordinator. Before it sits the single permitted round of substantive feedback on a complete draft, which means the draft has to exist with time to act on comments. Before that sits the mathematics itself, which takes longer than students expect because the first approach often fails and a second has to be found. Before that sits data collection where the exploration needs data. And before all of it sits question selection, which is the step that determines the ceiling.

The table sets out that sequence with the months typically available. The dates themselves come from the school's IB coordinator rather than from the IB, and they differ between schools in this cluster by several weeks, so the first action is to ask. A plan built on an assumed deadline tends to discover the real one about three weeks too late, which is the single most expensive avoidable error in Diploma mathematics. Ask once, in writing, in the first term of Year 12, and put both dates in the family calendar rather than relying on the student to relay them.

sections.heading: Where Dubai South maths students actually lose marks
paragraphs: The losses are consistent and they are nearly all technique. In Analysis and Approaches the largest single one is non-calculator algebra. Students who learned the course with a graphical display calculator present can describe what a derivative means and cannot differentiate a quotient by hand. Paper 1 forbids the calculator entirely, so the gap is fully exposed in a component worth around 40% of the Standard Level grade.

The second is premature rounding. A multi-step calculation with a value rounded to three significant figures in line two produces a final answer that is wrong by enough to lose the accuracy marks even though every step was correct. The third is working: a correct calculator answer with no method shown earns nothing where a question asks for justification, and candidates who are used to short-answer formats routinely omit it. The fourth is instruction words — show that, hence, deduce and verify each demand something specific, and hence in particular requires the previous result to be used rather than the question restarted.

In Applications and Interpretation the pattern shifts. The calculation is usually within reach; the interpretation is not. Marks go on failing to state a hypothesis in the correct form, on quoting a correlation coefficient without saying what it means for the context, and on concluding more than a test supports. Those are vocabulary problems rather than mathematics problems, which is good news: a student can fix them in three or four sessions, and almost nobody teaches them deliberately.

sections.heading: The two-year maths calendar for a Dubai South student
paragraphs: The two years of the Diploma hold different work, and most plans treat them as one long run-up to May. Year 12 is where content arrives, where the exploration question should be chosen, and where a route or level change is still possible without damage. Year 13 is where the papers are prepared and where the exploration is submitted, usually early enough that it feels like an interruption to revision rather than a fifth of the grade.

The decision points matter more than the revision. A student struggling with Analysis and Approaches Higher Level in the autumn of Year 12 can change to Standard Level or to the other route with little cost. The same student in the spring of Year 13 cannot. Families who treat the first year as warm-up lose the only window in which the structural decisions are cheap, and in this cluster that is the commonest regret parents report when they come to us in Year 13.

The table sets out what each period is for. Place it against your own school's calendar rather than reading it in the abstract, because exploration deadlines and mock windows differ by weeks between the Dubai Investments Park and Dubailand schools. The spring break of Year 13 is the pivot: everything before it is preparation and everything after it is pacing, and a plan that has not begun timed whole papers by then is behind. The second pivot is the summer between the two years, which is the last stretch of time in which catching up happens without new content arriving on top of it.

sections.heading: Which maths route the universities actually want
paragraphs: This is the part of the route decision families most often get wrong, because general advice is not specific enough to act on. Some programmes name Analysis and Approaches explicitly in their entry requirements. Others accept either route. A few state a Higher Level requirement regardless of route. The only reliable source is the entry requirements page of the specific course at the specific university, read in the year the student applies, because requirements are revised.

The pattern across published requirements is broadly predictable. Engineering, physics, mathematics, computer science and many economics programmes lean towards Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Business, management, social sciences, design, architecture and many life-science routes accept Applications. Medicine varies by country and by institution more than any other subject, so it deserves checking individually rather than assuming.

For UAE-based families there is a second process worth knowing about: Ministry of Education equivalency, which recognises a school-leaving certificate for use in the UAE. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at E. For the IB no points threshold appears in any source this page can verify, so none is published here — check it on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not required for it.
