sections.heading: What two years of Dubai maths support costs, in AED
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject families most often support across both Diploma years, so the useful figure is the two-year one rather than the hourly one. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 a month for budget provision, AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The hourly bands behind those come from the providers that publish them. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online and both at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 for qualified subject tutors. TutorChase quotes AED 270. BartyED quotes AED 650 for premium named tutors. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the price.

The sensible way to budget a Diploma maths plan is not a flat weekly rate for two years. It is a lighter load in Year 12 with a concentrated block around the exploration, then a heavier load in the spring of Year 13 for timed papers and, at Higher Level, for Paper 3. That shape costs less than a constant weekly commitment and produces more, because the hours land where the clocks are. Every figure above is attributed to the provider that published it; these are market bands rather than IB Gram prices, and our own conversation begins with a free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on an exploration, stated plainly
paragraphs: There are pages in this market selling completed Internal Assessments. An exploration bought or substantially written by somebody else is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student: a finding can mean no grade in the subject and, in serious cases, no Diploma. A parent paying for maths support is entitled to know exactly where the boundary sits, and any provider unwilling to state it is the wrong provider.

What a tutor may do covers almost everything useful. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration rests on. A tutor may discuss a proposed question and reject one that cannot be answered at course level in the page limit. A tutor may explain each of the five criteria and what distinguishes one band from the next. A tutor may read a complete draft the student has written and give feedback on it. A tutor may teach referencing, presentation and the conventions of mathematical communication.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work. Not writing a section, not rewriting the reflection into better English, not supplying a dataset, not choosing the question on the student's behalf, not editing the draft to completion. The practical test is whether every line in the submitted document was produced by the student. IB Gram tutors teach, question and give feedback, and that boundary is explained to the student in the first session rather than discovered when the school runs its authenticity check.

process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications, Higher or Standard, and which component is weak. Those three facts determine the entire plan. process.description: A mock or class paper with the marks on it tells a specialist whether the problem is non-calculator fluency, rounding, missing working, instruction words or interpretation. All five look the same from a grade and need different work. Without a script, the first session produces one from a timed section.

process.description: Higher Level candidates should attempt a whole Paper 3 question before the end of Year 12, not in the final fortnight. The skill it tests is staged reasoning rather than topic recall, so it needs its own practice. Students who meet it late lose marks that were straightforwardly within reach.

whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications examine different mathematics, and a tutor who teaches one fluently is not automatically useful for the other. Matching includes the route and the level from the first message, which means the correct past papers appear in session one rather than in week three.

Here the question is chosen early, the criteria are named by letter, and the reflection is planned rather than retrofitted. The deadline comes from the school coordinator, not from an assumption.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 gets its own block at Higher Level
whyPoints.description: Revising the content of Papers 1 and 2 does not prepare a student for staged problem solving. Higher Level candidates attempt whole Paper 3 questions well before the final weeks, with a deliberate partial-credit strategy for questions that cannot be completed. Most plans in this market skip it entirely.

whyPoints.title: Working is saved week to week
whyPoints.description: Sessions are written on a shared digital surface that persists, so the algebra from week three is still legible in week nine when the same slip reappears. That record is what makes a technique fault diagnosable rather than anecdotal, and it is not available when working is done on loose paper.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should a Dubai South student take?
faqs.answer: It is decided by the universities on the shortlist rather than by which course looks manageable. Some engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches by name and will not accept Applications however high the grade. Business, management, design and many life-science routes accept either. The only reliable source is the entry requirements page of the specific course at the specific institution, read in the year of application. Make that check before Year 12 subject choices close, because changing route in Year 13 is costly and sometimes impossible.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade is the exploration?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in both routes and at both levels. It is marked on five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Two of those reward process rather than mathematics, which is why technically strong explorations sit mid-band when the reflection is thin. The deadline is set by the school's IB coordinator rather than by the IB, usually far earlier than families expect, and it is the single most important date to establish at the start of Year 12 rather than at the end of it.

faqs.question: Why does my child struggle with Paper 1 but cope in class?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator and class work usually is not. A student taught with a graphical display calculator on the desk can explain what a derivative is and cannot differentiate a quotient by hand, solve a logarithmic equation, or sketch a derivative from a function. The gap is invisible until a non-calculator paper exposes it in a component carrying around 40% of the Standard Level grade. The fix is drill on hand algebra, which is unglamorous and reliably effective within a term.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why do students arrive unprepared for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is the Higher Level paper of two extended problem-solving questions that build in stages, and it examines sustained reasoning rather than topic recall. Students arrive unprepared because revising the content of Papers 1 and 2 does not develop that skill, so a plan built around topics never touches it. The remedy is to attempt whole Paper 3 questions well before the final weeks, with an explicit strategy for the parts that cannot be finished, since partial credit across stages is a real source of marks.

faqs.question: When should a Dubai South student choose their exploration question?
faqs.answer: In Year 12, with months to spare, because question selection sets the mark ceiling before any writing happens. A question chosen late is usually either too broad to answer in twelve to twenty pages or too shallow to demonstrate mathematics at course level, and neither can be rescued by good writing. After selection comes data gathering where the exploration needs it, then the mathematics itself, which routinely takes a second attempt because the first approach fails. Only then is there a draft to receive the one permitted round of substantive feedback.

faqs.question: What may a maths tutor do on an exploration in Dubai South, and what not?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the mathematics, discuss and reject an unworkable question, explain the five criteria and what separates the bands, and give feedback on one complete draft the student has written. A tutor may not write a section, rewrite the reflection, supply a dataset, choose the question on the student's behalf or edit the draft to completion. The test is whether every line in the submitted document was produced by the student. A malpractice finding falls on the student's Diploma, which is why any provider offering a finished exploration should be refused outright.

faqs.question: Is it too late to change from Higher to Standard Level maths?
faqs.answer: That depends almost entirely on when the question is asked. In the autumn of Year 12 a change is straightforward and costs very little. By the spring of Year 13 it is usually not available, and where it is, the student has spent most of two years at the bottom of a course they could have been comfortable in. Check the university requirement before changing, because some programmes specify Higher Level by name. The honest signal to watch for is weakness across every component rather than in one, which is a workload problem rather than a technique problem.

faqs.question: What does premature rounding actually cost in IB maths?
faqs.answer: The accuracy marks on an otherwise correct question. A multi-step calculation with a value rounded to three significant figures early produces a final answer far enough from the true value that the mark scheme will not accept it, even though every step of the method was right. Candidates do it because it feels tidy. The habit to build is carrying full calculator precision through the working and rounding only at the final answer, stated to the accuracy the question asks for. It is a two-session fix and it recovers marks across every paper.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 help before IB maths?
faqs.answer: For the Analysis and Approaches route, meaningfully. Cambridge Additional Mathematics covers calculus, trigonometry and vectors beyond the main 0580 syllabus, which means a student arrives at Diploma mathematics having already met differentiation and integration rather than meeting them in Year 12 alongside everything else. Several British-curriculum schools around Jebel Ali and Al Furjan offer it. It is not a requirement and its absence is closable with a summer block, but students who have taken it start Year 12 with a real advantage in hand algebra.

faqs.question: How often should a Dubai South Diploma student have maths sessions?
faqs.answer: One a week through Year 12 is usually right, rising to two or three in the spring of Year 13 and in the weeks before the May papers. The limiting factor is how much independent practice a student completes between sessions, not how much teaching they can sit through, so more than two in one subject rarely pays outside an examination run-in. The better shape is a lighter Year 12 with a concentrated block around the exploration, then a heavier spring in Year 13 when timed papers and Paper 3 both need attention.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session start in Dubai South during term?
faqs.answer: Around 16:30 for most households here, because school runs ending in Dubai Investments Park put families home between 16:00 and 16:30. Green Community families can manage 16:00 since the school is minutes away; Dubai Production City households driving to Motor City or Sports City are closer to 17:30. Mathematics after a full school day and a commute produces less than mathematics at 18:00 after a break, so the slot worth booking is the one a child can concentrate in rather than the first one free.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to homes in Dubai South?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with working written on a shared digital surface that is saved from week to week. For mathematics that persistence is a genuine advantage, because the same algebraic slip appearing in week three and week nine is visible rather than remembered. Independent in-home tutors do work in this part of Dubai if presence is your priority.

faqs.question: Why are IB maths grade boundaries different each year?
faqs.answer: Because they are set after each examination session and adjusted to the difficulty of that session's papers. A percentage that reached a 6 last May may not reach a 6 this May, and the reverse happens too. The planning consequence is that a previous year's threshold is not a target. What does carry across sessions is the relative weight of each component, so a plan should be aimed at components rather than at percentages. Aiming a clear band above the target rather than at it is the reasonable response.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP maths into the Diploma. What is the gap?
faqs.answer: Mostly notation and procedural fluency rather than content. Middle Years mathematics is marked against four criteria, two of which reward communication and real-life application, so a student can hold a strong grade while hand manipulation lags. Diploma Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches exposes that immediately. Four to eight sessions across the summer before Year 12, focused on index laws, surds, logarithms, rearrangement and the instruction words show that and hence, closes most of it. Left undone, the same gap consumes a whole term of Year 12.

faqs.question: What does a two-year IB maths plan cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends on the shape more than the rate. Using published Dubai figures, Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 600-1,200 for mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, and qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150-300 an hour with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. A plan that is lighter in Year 12 with a concentrated exploration block, then heavier in the spring of Year 13, costs less than a flat weekly commitment across both years. These are market bands, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: What do show that and hence actually require in an IB maths answer?
faqs.answer: Show that requires a demonstration ending at the given result, with every step visible, and a candidate who works backwards from the answer loses marks. Hence requires the previous part of the question to be used, so restarting from first principles loses method marks even when the final answer is correct. Deduce requires a conclusion drawn from something already established rather than fresh calculation. Verify requires substitution into a known result. These are published instruction words with fixed meanings, and most candidates have never been shown the list.

intro.heading: Three moments when maths help is actually needed
paragraphs: IB mathematics generates more tutoring requests in Dubai than any other Diploma subject, and almost all of them arrive at one of three points in the calendar. The first is late in Year 11, when a student has to choose between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and between Higher and Standard Level, without much information about what either feels like. The second is the term the exploration is due. The third is the fortnight after the first full paper comes back marked.

Those three moments need different work. The route decision is a diagnostic question: what does this student's algebraic fluency actually look like, and what do the universities they are considering require? The exploration is a process problem with a published set of criteria and a school-set deadline. The mock aftermath is a mark-recovery problem, and the useful first step is sorting lost marks by cause rather than by topic.

Treating all three as the same thing — a weekly maths hour — is how families spend two years and arrive at the same grade. A weekly hour with no target drifts towards whatever the student has homework on, which is reactive by design. A block with a stated objective and a review at four sessions can be judged, and if it is not working it can be changed while there is still time to change it.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For mathematics the online format has a specific advantage: the work is written, so a shared screen with the student's own working visible line by line is a better surface than a dining table where the tutor reads the page upside down.

It also widens the pool in a way that matters at Higher Level. A Sports City cohort may have a handful of students taking Analysis at Higher Level in a given year, and the number of local tutors who have taught Paper 3 is smaller still. Matching by route and level rather than by drive time is the difference between a specialist and a capable generalist.

What follows is a calendar for IB mathematics: the route decision and when it closes, the exploration counted backwards from the school deadline, when each paper should first be sat to time, what two Diploma years of maths look like term by term, and what the market charges at each stage. The section on first timed sittings is the one most families wish they had read a year earlier, because the order in which a student meets their papers is decided by default rather than on purpose, and the default is the expensive option.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Dubai Sports City is asked to fix
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Dubai Sports City is asked for one of four things, and they are not interchangeable. A route decision before the Diploma begins. Algebraic manipulation that was never fluent. An exploration with a deadline attached. Or paper marks that are lower than the student's classwork suggests they should be. IB Gram provides that teaching live online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time; no tutor is sent to a Sports City address and in-home visiting runs only in India.

The fourth of those is the most common and the most misdiagnosed. A student who understands the mathematics in class and scores poorly on papers has a technique problem, not a knowledge problem, and more teaching will not change it. What changes it is sitting papers to time, marking them against the published scheme, and naming the specific reason each mark was withheld — a missing reasoning line, a calculator result with no supporting algebra, an accuracy error carried forward.

The first is the most consequential and the least discussed. The Analysis and Applications routes lead to different places, and some degree programmes in engineering, mathematics, physics and economics expect the Analysis route specifically. A student who chooses on comfort in Year 11 and discovers the prerequisite in Year 13 has a problem that no amount of tutoring solves.

For mathematics, the online format earns its place rather than merely being acceptable. The work is written, so what matters is that the tutor can see the student's working appear line by line and interrupt at the point a step is skipped. A shared screen does that better than sitting across a table reading a page sideways, and the session can be rewatched when the student repeats the same error a fortnight later.

sections.heading: Analysis or Applications, and when the decision closes
paragraphs: The choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is made in the pre-Diploma year, usually alongside the rest of the subject selection, and it is frequently made on the wrong evidence. Students choose Applications because it sounds gentler, or Analysis because it sounds more respectable, and neither is a reason. The courses differ in content, in assessment style and in what they prepare a student for.

Analysis is the algebraic and calculus route, with proof and manipulation carrying the grade and a non-calculator paper that exposes any weakness in handling expressions. Applications is modelling and statistics led, with the graphic display calculator permitted throughout and marks attached to interpreting results in a real context. Neither is easy. The failure mode differs: Analysis punishes weak manipulation, Applications punishes students who produce outputs without commentary.

The decision rule that works is two-part. First, assess manipulation honestly under non-calculator conditions, because that single piece of evidence predicts Analysis performance better than any school report. Second, check the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses the student is considering, because prerequisites are set by course and change. Doing both takes two sessions and closes the question properly.

The deadline is the school's option-form date, and once the course is running a change is difficult and sometimes impossible. A family in Sports City or Arabian Ranches thinking about this should have the conversation a term before the form, not the week of it. The table below sets the two routes against each other on the dimensions that actually decide the choice.

sections.heading: The exploration, counted backwards from the school deadline
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is the component most improvable by planning, because its deadline is known in advance, its criteria are published, and roughly half of its marks are for process and communication rather than for the mathematics. Students who leave it late lose marks on criteria they could have satisfied with a fortnight's thought.

Counted backwards, the schedule is clear. The final week is for formatting, referencing and a last criterion check, and no mathematics should be happening then. The fortnight before that is for reflection and for writing the commentary that connects the mathematics to the question. Before that sits the mathematics itself, and before that the data or the worked examples. The topic choice sits at the very start and is the decision that determines whether the rest is possible.

Topic choice is where tutoring earns most. Students pick topics they find interesting and then discover the mathematics is either trivial or beyond them. The test is whether there is mathematics at the level of their course that can be done properly in the space available, and that is a judgement a specialist makes in one conversation. A tractable topic chosen in week one is worth more than four extra sessions in week eight.

The boundary on this work is firm and it is an IB rule rather than a preference. A tutor teaches the criteria, questions the method, discusses whether the mathematics is sound, and gives feedback on what the student has written. A tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of the exploration. Work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against the student, and the deadline pressure does not change that.

sections.heading: When each paper should first be sat to time
paragraphs: Most Diploma students in Dubai meet their papers in the wrong order and far too late. They do plenty of exercises, some past-paper questions, and then encounter a full paper under timed conditions for the first time in a mock. The mock then measures timing, stamina and question-order judgement as much as mathematics, and the grade reads as a content failure when it is not.

A better schedule is to sit each paper type to time long before it matters, accept that the first attempt will be poor, and treat the result as information. A first full Paper 1 in the back half of the first Diploma year costs ninety minutes of a weekend and tells a family more than a term of reports. For Higher Level students the priority is Paper 3, because it is the paper nobody has practised and the one that drops hardest in a mock.

Calculator setup belongs in this schedule too. Students lose marks to the syntax of their own machine rather than to mathematics: a regression run correctly but read from the wrong field, a distribution function given the arguments in the wrong order, an answer left in a display format the question did not ask for. One session on the specific model the school uses removes a recurring category of loss.

sections.heading: Two years of Diploma maths, term by term
paragraphs: Set out term by term, the two Diploma years in mathematics have a shape that makes planning obvious. The first term of the first year is for establishing manipulation at the level the course assumes. Students arriving from IGCSE or MYP without fluent algebra should be fixing that in this term and nowhere else, because every later topic sits on top of it.

The second and third terms of the first year are for content with an eye on the exploration. This is the stretch in which a topic for the exploration can be noticed rather than hunted, because a student working through functions or statistics will encounter something that could carry an investigation. Families who start thinking about the exploration in the second year are already compressing a process that wanted months.

The first term of the second year is the exploration's term, whatever the school's precise deadline, and it collides with internal deadlines in other subjects. The second term is mocks and the review that follows. The third is triage. By the final term the question is no longer what the student could learn but which marks are still reachable, and the honest answer usually excludes part of the syllabus.

Against that shape, the common Sports City pattern — first enquiry after second-year mock results — arrives at the start of the triage phase. It is workable, and a well-targeted eight-week block does real work there. It is simply more expensive per mark than the same money spent in the first year, which is the argument for having the conversation early even when nothing appears to be wrong.

sections.heading: What maths support costs at each stage, in AED
paragraphs: Cost is best read against the stage rather than per hour, because the stages differ in length. A route-decision diagnostic is two sessions. An exploration block is six to eight. A manipulation rebuild is a term or two of weekly work. A post-mock recovery block is eight sessions. The same hourly rate produces very different totals, and the cheapest intervention per mark recovered is almost always the earliest one.

The published rates in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and in-home visiting at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors between AED 200 and 500 once travel is counted. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium named end.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised locally include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. All of these are provider-published figures read in October 2026, and none is IB Gram's price list.

The stage-by-stage reading is the useful one for a maths budget. Two sessions on the route decision is the smallest spend with the largest consequence, because it affects two years of work and a university application. An exploration block is a fixed, bounded cost against a component worth a fixed share of the grade. A manipulation rebuild is the most expensive in total and the only thing that fixes the underlying problem. Triage is expensive per week and short.

sections.heading: Why Paper 3 produces the sharpest mock drop
paragraphs: Higher Level students in Dubai consistently underperform on Paper 3 relative to their other papers in a first mock, and the reason is structural rather than mathematical. Paper 3 presents two extended tasks that lead a candidate through unfamiliar material, and the skill it tests — staying in an unfamiliar problem long enough to make progress — is one that classroom teaching rarely has time to practise.

Students meet it for the first time in the mock, discover that the questions do not look like the exercises they have done, and lose marks partly to unfamiliarity and partly to morale. Nothing about that is a content failure, and a block that responds by teaching more content misses it entirely. What works is exposure: sitting Paper 3 style tasks to time, repeatedly, early in the second year, and building tolerance for the first ten minutes when nothing is obvious yet.

The technique has components that can be named. Read the whole task before starting, because later parts often reveal what the early ones are for. Write something for every part, because partial credit is available and a blank scores nothing. Carry the structure of the earlier parts into the later ones, since the task is usually a single thread. And expect to be told things in the question that have not been taught; that is the design.

For a Sports City family, the practical consequence is a scheduling one. If a student is taking Analysis or Applications at Higher Level, the first Paper 3 to time should happen early in the second Diploma year and not be left for the mock. That single change moves a mock profile more than any other intervention available at that point in the calendar.

sections.heading: Honest limits, permits and what is not on offer
paragraphs: Three limits are worth stating plainly on a page about mathematics tutoring. The first is on assessed work: a tutor teaches the exploration criteria, questions the mathematics, and gives feedback on the student's own draft, and does not write, complete or produce any part of it. Pages competing for these searches sell finished internal assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach and the finding lands on the candidate.

The second is on outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place, and a provider who does is selling something they cannot deliver. What can be promised is a stated target for a block, a written review at four sessions, and an honest answer when the target has not moved. Mathematics is unusually measurable, which makes that kind of accountability easier here than in most subjects.

The third is on status. IB Gram holds no International Baccalaureate, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Tutors are not described as examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and examiner status is never used to imply access to marking, boundaries or paper content.

On the regulatory side, private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years to school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any amount circulating online should be treated as unverified.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should a Sports City student pick, Analysis or Applications?
faqs.answer: Decide on two pieces of evidence rather than on reputation. First, assess algebraic manipulation under non-calculator conditions, because that predicts Analysis performance better than any school report. Second, read the admissions pages of the specific universities and courses the student is considering, since some programmes in mathematics, engineering and physics expect the Analysis route by name. Neither course is the easy one: Analysis punishes weak manipulation, Applications punishes students who produce calculator outputs without interpreting them in context.

faqs.question: Can an IB maths tutor come to a house in Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. All UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. For mathematics the online format is arguably the better surface anyway: the tutor watches the student's working appear line by line on a shared screen and can interrupt at the exact point a reasoning step is skipped, which is harder to do reading a page across a table.

faqs.question: When should my child start the mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: Topic selection at least eight weeks before the school deadline, and ideally with a candidate topic noticed during the first Diploma year. Working backwards, the final week should be formatting and referencing, the fortnight before that reflection and commentary, and the mathematics itself finished earlier still. The single most expensive mistake is choosing a topic on interest and then discovering the mathematics is either trivial or beyond the course level, which wastes weeks nobody has.

faqs.question: Why is my child's Paper 3 mark so much lower than Paper 1 and Paper 2?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 3 is the paper almost nobody has sat to time before their first mock. It presents two extended tasks that lead a candidate through unfamiliar material, and the skill it tests is staying in an unfamiliar problem long enough to make progress. That is exposure, not content. Sitting Paper 3 style tasks to time early in the second Diploma year, repeatedly, moves a Higher Level mock profile more than any additional topic teaching at the same point.

faqs.question: Is a weekly maths hour enough for a Higher Level student?
faqs.answer: It depends what the hour is doing. One session a week is right for a manipulation rebuild, where the limit is how much a student can absorb rather than how much teaching is available. It is not enough in the final weeks, when the work is whole papers sat to time and marked, and two or three sessions a week is the useful frequency. The failure mode is a weekly hour with no target that drifts towards whatever homework happens to be due.

faqs.question: How much of the exploration mark is actually mathematics?
faqs.answer: Roughly half. The published criteria cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics, and only the last of those is mathematics in the narrow sense. Students who produce competent mathematics and write two sentences of reflection leave marks on the table that no additional mathematics recovers. Reading the criteria and self-marking a draft against each one is the highest-return hour available on this component, and almost nobody does it.

faqs.question: My child arrived from IGCSE and is struggling with the first term of Analysis. What now?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a manipulation problem until proved otherwise. The step from IGCSE to Analysis is in abstraction rather than in topic coverage, and most early difficulty traces back to rearrangement, indices, surds and function notation rather than to the new content. A narrow block on those, in the first term rather than the second, is the cheapest fix available. Students who took Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics usually meet this step far more easily, which is itself informative.

faqs.question: Does the graphic display calculator really cost marks?
faqs.answer: Regularly, and almost always to syntax rather than to mathematics. A regression run correctly but read from the wrong field, a distribution function given its arguments in the wrong order, an answer left in a display format the question did not request. One session on the specific model the school uses removes a recurring loss across every calculator-permitted paper. It is the least glamorous session on any maths block and frequently the highest-yield one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration if the deadline is next week?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the criteria, question whether the mathematics is sound, and give feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor cannot write, complete or produce any part of it, whatever the deadline. That is an IB academic-honesty rule and work a student did not produce becomes a malpractice finding against them. Realistically, a final-week session is a criterion check and a presentation review, which is useful but much smaller than what an eight-week run would have achieved.

faqs.question: How does Standard Level maths differ in tutoring terms from Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Standard Level has two papers rather than three and less syllabus depth, so a block can cover proportionally more of the course in the same time. Higher Level adds Paper 3 and extra content in every topic, which means an eight-week block has to choose. In practice Standard Level blocks are often technique-led and can lift a grade quickly, while Higher Level blocks have to decide early between covering gaps and drilling the unfamiliar paper.

faqs.question: What is the earliest useful point to get maths help in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Before it starts. Two sessions in the term the option form is due, spent assessing manipulation and checking university prerequisites, is the smallest spend with the largest consequence available anywhere in the two years. After that, the first term of the first year, on fluency. Both are cheaper per mark than anything that happens after a second-year mock, which is when most Sports City families first enquire.

faqs.question: Do you teach MYP mathematics as preparation for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful window is the end of MYP 4 rather than MYP 5. MYP assesses four criteria out of eight each and converts them by published boundaries, so a student can hold a respectable grade for two years while manipulation stays weak and nothing in the reporting shows it. A block at the end of MYP 4 leaves a full year to build fluency before the Analysis or Applications decision has to be made, which changes what that decision can be.

faqs.question: What does a maths block cost over an eight-week period in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Applying Bestimate's published monthly estimates for weekly hour-long sessions, two months at the mid band of AED 600 to 1,200 a month is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400, and at the specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more it is roughly AED 2,000 to 4,000. The hourly figures behind those run from AED 33 to 65 at the university-student end to AED 650 for premium named tutors. These are provider-published market rates read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: How will I know the maths block is working rather than just pleasant?
faqs.answer: Compare a timed paper score under the same conditions a month apart. Mathematics is unusually measurable, so this is cleaner here than in essay subjects: sit the same paper type, to the same time, mark it against the published scheme, and look at the number. If the block is about the exploration instead, the measure is whether the student can self-mark their own draft against each criterion and justify the mark they give themselves.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubailand.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics to students across the Dubailand communities, and each profile states the route and the level. An Analysis and Approaches HL specialist and an Applications and Interpretation SL specialist are preparing students for genuinely different examinations.

intro.heading: Which IB maths course is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: A parent in Arabian Ranches or Motor City searching for an IB maths tutor is usually looking for somebody competent and nearby. The more urgent question is narrower. IB Mathematics is not one subject. It is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each offered at Higher and Standard Level, which makes four distinct courses with separate syllabuses, separate papers and separate expectations about what a calculator is for. A tutor who does not establish which of the four is involved in the first conversation is guessing, and the guess costs the family a term.

The two routes diverge in character rather than difficulty. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytical route, heavier on proof, functions and calculus, and it includes a paper where a graphical calculator is not permitted. Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-led, calculator-active throughout, with more emphasis on interpreting a context in words. Students who assume the second is the easy option frequently discover that modelling questions punish imprecise writing as harshly as algebra punishes careless manipulation.

The level matters as much as the route. Higher Level in either course adds a third paper, an extended problem-solving or investigative component sat under time pressure, and a markedly larger syllabus. The exploration, the internally assessed piece of individual mathematical work, carries the same 20 per cent weighting in all four courses, but what counts as sufficient mathematical depth differs sharply between HL and SL. A tutor working from an SL mental model on an HL exploration will approve work that is heading for a middling band.

There is a diagnostic consequence to all of this that parents rarely hear stated. The four most common ways an IB mathematics candidate loses marks are method communication, failure to interpret a result in context, slow or incorrect calculator operation, and mismanagement of the Higher Level third paper. Each belongs to a particular course and level, and none of them is fixed by covering the syllabus again. A tutor who has seen a piece of marked work can usually name which one is in play within a single session, and a tutor who cannot has nothing to offer beyond repetition.

Dubailand adds a practical layer on top of the academic one. The belt is a development zone rather than a neighbourhood, running south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and absorbing Arabian Ranches and its successors, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. A specialist in a specific HL route who also happens to live within a short drive of your villa is a narrow intersection, and insisting on it is how families end up with a competent general maths tutor instead. IB Gram removes distance from the match and delivers lessons one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service we run only in India, so nobody is sent to a Dubailand address.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics, standard and extended

The criterion on investigating patterns is the one students neglect, and it is the direct ancestor of the Diploma exploration.
programmes.countryNote: Dubailand families arriving mid-phase from a British curriculum often have strong procedural fluency and no experience of being marked on communication or investigation. That gap is visible within two sessions and closes in a term, provided the work is done against the actual criterion descriptors rather than a textbook.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebraic route. Paper 1 is sat without a graphical calculator, Paper 2 with one, and Higher Level adds Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper with fewer, longer questions. Proof, functions, trigonometric identities, sequences and calculus carry the load, and at Higher Level the calculus extends to techniques Standard Level never meets.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route most UAE engineering, physics, computer science and economics applicants are steered toward, and the one Dubailand parents most often request without naming. Confirm it with the school before any plan is built, because a term spent preparing Analysis technique for an Applications candidate is wasted.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The statistical and modelling route, with a graphical calculator permitted in every paper. Higher Level adds Paper 3 and a substantially heavier load of statistical inference, matrices, graph theory and modelling. Marks are lost where a student produces a correct numerical answer and then fails to interpret it in the context the question established.
programmes.countryNote: Students who chose this route to avoid algebra tend to underestimate the writing demand, and that shows up first in the exploration rather than in the papers. Check intended university courses early: some competitive quantitative degrees state a preference, and that preference is easier to accommodate in the first Diploma year than the second.

programmes.name: The International GCSE route into DP mathematics

An Extended or Higher tier grade is broadly the expected foundation for Analysis and Approaches, while a strong Core or Foundation result points toward Applications and Interpretation. The step up in abstraction is larger than the step up in content.

Targeted work in that first term is cheaper and more effective than remediation in the second Diploma year.

subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, and at Higher Level complex numbers, proof by induction and the binomial theorem in its general form. The recurring failure is algebraic slips under time pressure rather than conceptual gaps, which responds to drilled technique rather than re-teaching.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational and reciprocal forms. Students lose marks by sketching a graph without the asymptotes and intercepts the markscheme is looking for. Higher Level extends to more awkward rational functions and modulus work.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Identities, equations and, in Applications, substantial coordinate and vector-adjacent work. Trigonometric equations lose marks where solution ranges are mishandled. In Analysis Higher Level the identity manipulation is where candidates stall and run out of time.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Lighter in Analysis, central in Applications. Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Marks go missing at the final step: a calculated p-value is worth little without the sentence that interprets it against the stated hypothesis.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, with Analysis Higher Level reaching techniques such as integration by substitution and parts, implicit differentiation and differential equations. This is the strand where a weak foundation is most visible and most expensive to leave until the second year.

subjects.name: The toolkit and proof
subjects.description: Mathematical communication, reasoning and formal proof. Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample are examined in Analysis Higher Level. Students who can produce the right result and cannot set out an argument lose marks on content they genuinely understand.

subjects.name: Paper 3 technique
subjects.description: Two long investigative questions in a shorter paper, where each part depends on the last. The skill is reading ahead, managing time across a question that cannot be dipped into, and writing enough to collect method marks even when the final answer is wrong.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.levels: All four courses, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic with no mathematics of adequate depth, and that is decided before a word is written.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator fluency
subjects.description: Statistical functions, solvers, regression and graphing. Applications candidates are expected to use the technology efficiently, and marks are lost to slow or incorrect operation rather than to mathematical error. This is teachable in a small number of sessions.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision and its consequences
paragraphs: This choice is made in the first Diploma year and it reaches further than any other subject decision a student takes. Analysis and Approaches is built around algebraic manipulation, functions, proof and calculus, and it includes a paper sat without a graphical calculator. Applications and Interpretation is built around statistics, modelling and the interpretation of real contexts, with a calculator available throughout. Both are respectable mathematics and both are examined rigorously; they are simply different subjects wearing a shared name.

The consequence that matters most is admissions. Competitive quantitative degrees, particularly in engineering, physics, mathematics and parts of economics, commonly express a preference for the Analysis route, and some specify it. Students who intend to apply for those courses and find themselves on the Applications route in the second Diploma year have a problem that tutoring cannot fully solve, because the syllabus content differs rather than merely the difficulty. Checking published entry requirements for intended universities during the first year is the single cheapest piece of planning available to a Dubailand family.

The second consequence is about fit rather than ambition. A student with strong procedural algebra and weak writing often does better in Analysis, because the marks reward manipulation. A student who reasons well in context and makes careless algebraic slips often does better in Applications, provided they accept that the writing demand is real. Choosing on the basis of which looks easier is how families arrive at a mismatch, and the mismatch usually surfaces in the exploration.

The table below sets out where the four courses differ in structure. It is the document to take into a conversation with the school, because the decision belongs to the student and the coordinator rather than to a tutor.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Diagnosis is the part of tutoring that earns its fee, and in mathematics it is unusually tractable because the losses are visible on paper. Four patterns account for most of them, and all four are teachable. None of them is fixed by covering the syllabus again, which is what a generalist tutor tends to offer because it is the only plan available without seeing marked work.

The first is method communication. IB markschemes pay for intermediate steps, and a student who writes the correct final answer with nothing between the question and the result collects a fraction of the available marks. This is the single largest avoidable loss in Analysis and Approaches at both levels, and it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. It takes a handful of sessions with marked work in front of both people.

The second is interpretation. In Applications and Interpretation a correct calculation that is never translated back into the context of the question leaves marks on the table. A regression coefficient without a sentence saying what it means in the scenario is incomplete. The third is calculator inefficiency: Applications candidates expected to use statistical and graphing functions fluently lose time rather than understanding, and at Higher Level time is the binding constraint. The fourth is Paper 3 management at Higher Level, where questions build in parts and a candidate who stalls early forfeits everything downstream.

A good first session produces a named diagnosis rather than a plan. If a tutor finishes a trial lesson without being able to say which of these four is costing the most marks, the match is wrong and a second opinion is worth more than a discount.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty per cent that is decided before drafting starts
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics course carries an internally assessed exploration worth 20 per cent of the grade, and the single biggest determinant of the final band is the choice of topic. A topic that cannot support mathematics of appropriate depth for the level produces a capped mark however well it is written. That decision happens weeks before the first draft, which is why support concentrated at the drafting stage arrives too late to help most.

What depth means differs by level, and this is where a tutor working from the wrong mental model does damage. An investigation that is adequate for Standard Level may be thin for Higher Level in the same route. A topic drawn from a student's own interest is encouraged, but personal engagement is not a substitute for mathematical content, and explorations built around a hobby with arithmetic attached routinely disappoint students who enjoyed writing them.

The criteria reward specific things: presentation and structure, mathematical communication including correct notation, personal engagement, reflection that is genuinely critical rather than decorative, and the use of mathematics at a level commensurate with the course. Reflection is the criterion students most often treat as a concluding paragraph when it should be threaded through the work. Notation is where otherwise strong explorations leak marks, because informal writing of mathematics is penalised.

The boundary on this work is absolute and worth stating plainly. A tutor may test whether a topic will survive contact with real mathematics, explain what each criterion asks for, read a draft the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach notation and referencing properly. A tutor must never write the exploration, draft sections of it, or edit it to the point where the mathematics is no longer the student's. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: Is there an IB maths specialist near Dubailand, honestly?
paragraphs: Taken literally, the answer is uncomfortable. Dubailand is a planning zone covering a large wedge of inland Dubai, and the communities inside it do not share a school or an afternoon. Independent tutors cluster where journeys are short, which in this city means the coastal corridor, Al Barsha and Business Bay. The pool of people who both specialise in a particular Higher Level mathematics route and will drive to Town Square twice a week is small, and the ones who will are pricing the journey.

The arithmetic of a visiting tutor's week explains the rest. Forty minutes of driving at each end of a session means roughly half as many families served per week as in a dense area. The rate rises to cover the dead time, and the subject range widens so the diary fills with whoever is nearby. A tutor advertising all IB mathematics across both routes and both levels, plus International GCSE, is not necessarily weak; they are responding sensibly to a dispersed market. But a family that needs Analysis Higher Level Paper 3 technique is not well served by that breadth.

There is a further reason local supply is thin for this subject specifically. Higher Level mathematics cohorts at individual schools are often small, which means the number of teachers in Dubai who have taught Analysis Higher Level to completion recently is smaller than the number who have taught mathematics. Scarcity at that level is national rather than local, so a radius filter does not just narrow the pool; it narrows it on the wrong axis entirely.

Removing distance changes which question the match answers. Instead of who is free and close, it becomes who has taught Analysis Higher Level recently and can take a slot at half past six on a Tuesday. That has a real answer. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that is stated plainly rather than hidden; the service exists only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, and a parent should know that before paying rather than after.

sections.heading: What maths tutoring costs around the Dubailand belt
paragraphs: Mathematics is the best-supplied subject in this market, which means a family has more choice and more opportunity to misjudge value. The sourced bands first. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

The useful distinction in mathematics is not the band but the match. A tutor at AED 150 who has taught Applications Standard Level repeatedly is better value for an Applications student than one at AED 400 whose experience is all Analysis Higher Level, and the reverse holds just as firmly. Rate is a weak proxy for fit in a subject with four distinct courses, which is why asking which of the four a tutor has taught most recently is worth more than comparing two numbers.

For budgeting, Bestimate's Dubai monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Packages circulate at roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, which is approximately double the cost for half the number of contacts.

Two notes on honesty. None of these figures is an IB Gram price; each is attributed to the provider or source that published it, and three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all. And the MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a licensing or registration line item in any quote is charging for something that costs nothing.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the session for a maths candidate
paragraphs: Mathematics has a calendar of its own inside the Diploma, because the exploration deadline sits well before the papers and the two require different kinds of work. A plan that treats the whole year as revision will miss the exploration window entirely, and that is 20 per cent of the grade.

The sequence that works runs roughly like this. In the first Diploma year, consolidate as topics are taught, with particular attention to calculus and functions because the second year builds directly on them. Toward the end of that year or early in the second, settle the exploration topic and test it for mathematical depth before any writing. Draft, receive feedback, redraft, and submit to the school's internal deadline, which the coordinator sets months ahead of the board's window. Only then does the work become paper technique, and that is where the final months belong.

On series and dates, the rules for a UAE page are firm. IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. For Cambridge qualifications, which many Dubailand siblings are sitting alongside, the UAE series are June and November; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan quoting it is using a date that does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. No specific IB examination or results date is published on this page, because ibo.org could not be verified by automated checking for this project and an unsourced date on a tutoring page is a liability; confirm every IB date with the school's coordinator.

Checkable backward anchors exist for the Cambridge and Pearson side and are worth citing because they can be verified. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the official timetable is the document to check rather than any figure restated here.

sections.heading: The regulatory and legal frame a Dubailand parent should know
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the detail is simple enough to check. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is speculating. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate matter and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, inspecting on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

What none of that licenses is a claim. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We explain what each body does and link to it. Nor do we reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which are the board's copyright; the correct move is to cite the official source and work from what the school has legitimately issued.

process.title: Confirm the route and the level
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. One email to the school settles it. Everything else in the plan depends on this answer, and a tutor who does not ask for it in the first exchange is working from assumption.

process.title: Send a marked paper if you have one
process.description: A recent paper with the mark breakdown tells a specialist more in two minutes than a paragraph of description. It usually makes the diagnosis obvious before the first session: method communication, interpretation, calculator inefficiency or Paper 3 management.

process.title: Take the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: A full session with a specialist in the right route and level, no charge and no card. The test is whether the tutor can name the specific failure mode by the end. If they cannot, the match is wrong and we will find another rather than ask you to persist.

process.title: Separate the exploration from the papers
process.description: These are two different pieces of work with two different calendars. Plan the exploration block around the school's internal deadline and keep the weekly slot for course content, then convert the final months into paper technique.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the diagnosis
process.description: Movement in method shows before movement in grades. Compare marked work against the first paper rather than against an impression, and pause cleanly for school examination weeks and travel.

whyPoints.title: Four courses, matched as four courses
whyPoints.description: We ask which of AA and AI, at which level, before matching. A specialist in Applications Standard Level is better value for an Applications student than a more expensive Analysis Higher Level tutor, and the reverse is equally true. Rate is a weak proxy for fit here.

whyPoints.title: Higher Level Paper 3 treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: Paper 3 questions build in parts, so a candidate who stalls early loses everything downstream. Reading ahead, managing time across a single long question and collecting partial credit are drillable techniques, and they are not the same as knowing the syllabus.

whyPoints.title: The exploration handled at the topic stage
whyPoints.description: The band is largely decided by whether the topic can carry mathematics of appropriate depth for the level. That is tested before drafting rather than rescued afterwards, which is where most exploration support arrives and why it achieves little.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor tests a topic, explains criteria, reads the student's own draft and teaches notation. A tutor never writes or redrafts the exploration. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, and the penalty for that falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names who published it. Three of the six most prominent pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a Dubai family pays in. The MoHRE permit, meanwhile, is free of charge.

whyPoints.title: No approval or outcome claimed
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE office, no grade promise and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method behind it. Those claims are common in this market and none of them is evidenced.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI for a Dubailand student?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and analytical route, with proof, functions and heavier calculus, and it includes a paper sat without a graphical calculator. Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-led, with a calculator permitted throughout and more emphasis on interpreting results in context. Both are examined rigorously. The practical difference for a family is admissions: competitive engineering, physics and mathematics degrees commonly prefer or require the Analysis route, so intended university courses should be checked during the first Diploma year rather than the second.

faqs.question: How hard is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level really?
faqs.answer: It is the most demanding mathematics course in the Diploma, and the difficulty is concentrated in two places. The syllabus is large, extending into proof by induction, complex numbers and calculus techniques Standard Level never meets. And Paper 3 asks two long investigative questions where each part depends on the previous one, so time management matters as much as knowledge. Students with strong algebraic fluency and an appetite for setting out an argument cope well. Students who reach correct answers without showing reasoning struggle, because the markscheme pays for the steps.

faqs.question: How far may a Dubailand tutor go on the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may test whether a proposed topic can carry mathematics of appropriate depth for the level, explain what each assessment criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and identify where marks are being lost, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach correct notation and referencing. A tutor must never write the exploration, draft sections of it, or edit it until the mathematics is no longer the student's own. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the penalty for that lands on the student.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Dubailand student usually need for IB maths?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which of four failure modes is in play, which is why a diagnostic comes first. Method communication problems in Analysis often respond within six to eight sessions, because the fix is a habit rather than knowledge. Calculator inefficiency in Applications can take as few as three. A weak calculus foundation carried into the second Diploma year is a term of work, sometimes more. Paper 3 strategy at Higher Level is usually a focused block in the final months. Anyone quoting a number before seeing marked work is guessing.

faqs.question: Why are Higher Level maths specialists so scarce in the Dubailand belt?
faqs.answer: Two reasons compound. Higher Level cohorts at individual schools are often small, so the number of teachers anywhere in Dubai who have taught Analysis Higher Level to completion recently is smaller than the number who teach mathematics. And independent tutors cluster where journeys are short, which in Dubai means the coastal corridor and Al Barsha rather than a villa belt forty minutes inland. A radius filter therefore narrows an already thin pool on exactly the wrong axis, which is why distance-free matching widens choice rather than reducing it.

faqs.question: My child switched from Extended IGCSE maths to Analysis and is struggling. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Very. The step is about abstraction rather than content. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 reward reliable procedure, while Analysis rewards reasoning set out formally, and a student who was comfortable producing answers suddenly finds that answers alone score poorly. The transition term is where most ground is lost and where targeted work is cheapest. What usually needs rebuilding is not topic knowledge but the habit of writing mathematics as an argument, which responds quickly once somebody sits with marked work rather than a textbook.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Standard and Higher Level in each route?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we treat them as separate briefs rather than variants of one. Higher Level in either route adds a third paper and a substantially larger syllabus, and what counts as adequate mathematical depth in the exploration differs between the levels in the same course. A tutor working from a Standard Level mental model will approve Higher Level work heading for a middling band. The level is confirmed before matching for exactly that reason, alongside the route.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150. Monthly, Bestimate estimates AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. In mathematics specifically, match quality matters more than band, since there are four distinct courses.

faqs.question: Is a graphical calculator allowed in every IB maths paper?
faqs.answer: No, and this catches students out. In Analysis and Approaches one paper is sat without a graphical calculator, which rewards algebraic fluency and penalises reliance on technology. In Applications and Interpretation a calculator is permitted throughout, and candidates are expected to use statistical, regression and graphing functions efficiently, so marks are lost to slow or incorrect operation rather than to mathematical error. Calculator fluency is genuinely teachable in a small number of sessions, and it is among the fastest returns available in the Applications route.

faqs.question: Will a weekend morning session work better than a weekday one for maths?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and particularly for exploration work and full timed papers. Mathematics needs a student who can still concentrate, and in Dubai Sports City and Motor City the weekday five-to-seven window is usually occupied by training. Weekday slots suit consolidating material being taught that fortnight, while a weekend morning suits anything needing sustained attention. For a Diploma student in this belt the pattern that holds through a year is usually one weekday slot plus one longer weekend block.

faqs.question: Which exam session does a Dubailand IB maths candidate sit?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB examination or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unsourced date on a tutoring page is a liability; confirm dates with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications that siblings may be sitting alongside, the UAE series are June and November, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and its November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths for two children at different IB stages?
faqs.answer: They can, but two specialists usually serve a household better. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria including investigating patterns and communication, while Diploma work is about papers and the exploration. The person who gives excellent criterion feedback is not automatically the right Analysis Higher Level tutor. Two consecutive slots with two specialists adds no travel cost because there is none, and households in Mudon and Remraam request this arrangement more often than any other in the belt.

faqs.question: Do you supply IB past papers and mark schemes for maths practice?
faqs.answer: No. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the board's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty, which for mathematics is straightforward. Be cautious of any provider advertising a download library of papers: that is a copyright problem they have not thought through, and you would be using it.

faqs.question: Does an IB maths tutor in the UAE need a licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no amounts are published. Since it is free, any licensing charge in a quote deserves a question.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IB maths tutor in Dubailand is only useful once two things are settled: which of the four courses your child is sitting, and which of the four common failure modes is costing the marks. Both are answerable in a week, one by an email to the school and one by a diagnostic session with a specialist. Distance answers neither, which is why lessons run over live video rather than in your villa. Book a free trial lesson with a specialist in the right route and level, judge it on whether they can name the failure mode, and plan the exploration separately from the papers.
