dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hills.programmesIntro: Emirates Hills children reach IB Mathematics by several routes. Two of the schools on the edge of Emirates Living run the IB continuum from primary upwards; others run a British primary and secondary and only meet the IB at sixteen, or not at all. The programme your child is in changes what a maths tutor should be working on this term.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary with no external examinations and no prescribed mathematics scheme. Number, pattern, measurement, shape and data handling are taught through units of inquiry, so the sequence of topics varies more between schools than it would in a British primary. Assessment is largely teacher judgement against learning outcomes, reported in descriptive bands rather than percentages.
programmes.countryNote: In Emirates Hills the PYP question is almost always about continuity rather than content. A family moving a nine-year-old from a British primary nearby into a continuum school finds the written-method expectations different: column methods arrive later, mental strategies earlier. Tutoring at this stage is about keeping arithmetic fluency sharp while the child adapts to an inquiry format, not about pushing ahead.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Standard and extended mathematics diverge from around MYP 4. The extended course is the one that feeds Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and the decision is usually made a full year before anyone mentions the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma gap is the quietest risk in Emirates Living. Criterion B investigations reward pattern-finding and generalisation, which is excellent preparation for Paper 3 at Higher Level, but MYP marking does not demand the algebraic speed that AA Higher Level assumes from week one. A tutor working with an MYP 5 student in this area should be adding drill volume, not extra investigation practice.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes a mathematics course. The choice is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard or Higher Level. Analysis is the algebraic and proof-based route; Applications is modelling, statistics and technology-led. Both carry a 20-mark exploration. Higher Level in either route adds Paper 3, a long investigation sat in a single hour.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai universities and the UK engineering departments Emirates Hills families most often apply to treat these two routes differently. Several engineering and mathematics courses name Analysis and Approaches Higher Level explicitly and will not accept Applications Higher Level in its place. Check the exact wording on each university's entry page before the subject choice is locked in Year 11, because changing route in Year 12 costs a term.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller IB route combining two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills. Where mathematics is taken it is usually Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, assessed exactly as it is for Diploma candidates, with the same exploration requirement and the same papers.
programmes.countryNote: Few Dubai schools run the Career-related Programme and none of the schools immediately around Emirates Living is widely known for it, so most families here will meet it only if they move. If your child is on this route, tutoring load is lighter than a full Diploma but the exploration deadline is identical and tends to be forgotten, because the rest of the timetable has a different rhythm.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hills.subjectsIntro: IB Mathematics is one subject on a transcript and four syllabuses in practice. The list below names what each component actually assesses and where marks leave the page, so you can point a tutor at the right half of the course rather than booking general help and hoping.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Proof by induction, complex numbers in modulus-argument and Euler form, vectors in three dimensions, compound angle identities, Maclaurin series, differential equations. Paper 1 is sat without technology and is where most of the grade is lost. Marks go on unsimplified exact values, missing constants of integration and proofs that assert rather than show.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Sequences and series, functions and transformations, trigonometry in radians, differentiation and integration of standard functions, probability and statistics. The non-calculator paper still exists at Standard Level and still carries the losses. Students who met logarithms only briefly at IGCSE are routinely caught by log laws under exam pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistical modelling, regression and correlation, matrices and transition matrices, graph theory, complex numbers in a modelling context, numerical methods and differential equations solved with Euler's method. Technology is permitted throughout. Marks are lost on interpretation rather than computation: a correct number with no statement of what it means scores part credit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing with chi-squared and t-tests, linear and non-linear models, financial mathematics, basic calculus in applied contexts. The common failure is treating a modelling question as an algebra question and never returning to the context the question set up.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique
subjects.description: Non-calculator work is a distinct skill, not simply the same mathematics without a machine. It needs exact-value trigonometry held in memory, confident surd and index manipulation, and the discipline to leave an answer as a fraction. This is the single most trainable component in the whole course and the one most students never practise separately.

subjects.name: Paper 3 investigation
subjects.description: One hour, two extended problems, each building from a concrete case to a general result. It rewards students who can spot a pattern, state a conjecture, and then prove or justify it. Preparation is not more content; it is supervised practice at writing up a developing argument under time pressure.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A twelve to twenty page individual piece worth 20 marks, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The use-of-mathematics criterion carries the largest block of marks and is the one students most often leave underpowered by choosing a topic that cannot bear the level required.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator fluency
subjects.description: Paper 2 and Paper 3 assume a student can find an intersection, solve numerically, run a regression, use a distribution menu and store values without retyping. Schools teach the menus once in Year 12. Students who never rebuilt the skill lose minutes per question, and minutes are the scarce resource in a ninety-mark paper.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: Show, hence, verify, justify, determine and find each license different work. Hence means the previous part must be used; verify allows substitution where determine does not. A student who treats all six as instructions to get the answer will lose method marks they had already earned on the page.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hills.regionsIntro: Emirates Hills sits in the middle of the Emirates Living cluster, and IB mathematics demand around it is not evenly spread. Some neighbouring communities feed continuum IB schools where a child has been doing MYP mathematics since Year 7; others feed British schools where the IB appears only at sixteen. The notes below describe what that means for the mathematics specifically.

regions.name: The Meadows
regions.note: Shares the Emirates Living school edge with Emirates Hills and feeds the same continuum schools, so Meadows students more often arrive at Diploma mathematics from MYP extended rather than from IGCSE Extended. Their gap is algebraic speed rather than unfamiliar content.

regions.name: The Springs
regions.note: A younger demographic on average, with more primary and MYP enquiries than Diploma ones. The mathematics question here is usually about keeping a child on the extended MYP track so that Analysis and Approaches Higher Level stays available two years later.

regions.name: The Lakes
regions.note: Small, quiet and close enough to the same schools that scheduling is identical to Emirates Hills. Diploma enquiries from here skew towards Applications and Interpretation, often from families aiming at business, economics and design degrees rather than engineering.

regions.name: The Greens

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-emirates-hills.modesIntro: Mathematics tutoring works differently from essay subjects because the evidence is on the page in front of both people. The three formats below reflect what the work actually needs at different points in the two-year Diploma, and all three run online over live video with a shared annotated whiteboard.

modes.description: A fixed slot each week running alongside the school's scheme of work, pre-teaching the topic the class is about to meet or consolidating the one it has just left. The student brings the week's marked work; the tutor reads the method, not just the answer, and rebuilds the step where it broke.

sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Emirates Hills is actually being hired to fix
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Emirates Hills is hired to close a gap between the mathematics a student can do and the mathematics an IB paper asks for under timed conditions. Those are different things, and the difference is where almost every lost grade lives. A student who can integrate by substitution on a worksheet may still lose the marks in Paper 1 because the integral is disguised, the constant is forgotten, or the question wanted an exact value and got a decimal.

The first session should therefore not be a lesson. It should be a diagnosis run on the student's own evidence: the last two marked assessments, the most recent mock, and the class topic tests from the current term. A tutor who asks for these before the trial has read the course. One who proposes starting at the beginning of the syllabus has not, and will spend eight weeks reteaching material the student already holds while the actual gap stays open.

What the diagnosis is looking for is narrow and specific. Does the loss cluster in one paper? Does it cluster in one topic across papers? Does it appear only in questions carrying five or more marks, which would point at structure and stamina rather than content? Is the student losing method marks for unshown working, which is a writing habit, or final-answer marks after correct method, which is arithmetic under pressure? Each of those four findings leads to a different programme of work, and three of them can be fixed faster than a parent expects.

Emirates Hills adds one practical constraint worth naming early. The school day in this part of Dubai ends between two and three, but the drive home, an activity and a meal put the realistic start of serious mathematics somewhere after five for most households. An online session removes the tutor's travel from that equation entirely, which in practice is what makes a six o'clock weekday slot possible at all.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that shapes two years
paragraphs: The route decision is made in Year 11 and it is the single most consequential mathematics choice a Diploma student makes. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented course: it builds towards calculus, series and formal reasoning, and it keeps a non-calculator paper at both levels. Applications and Interpretation is a modelling course: statistics, regression, matrices, graph theory, financial mathematics, with technology permitted in every paper.

Neither is a soft option and the grade distributions do not support the common staffroom claim that one is easier. They demand different things. Analysis Higher Level rewards a student who enjoys manipulation and will sit with a proof for twenty minutes. Applications Higher Level rewards a student who can read a context, choose a model, run it and then say in a sentence what the number means for the situation described. A student placed in the wrong one by reputation rather than temperament loses more than a student placed one level too high in the right one.

The constraint that matters for Emirates Hills families is university entry. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics and computer science courses at UK and European universities name Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and will not substitute Applications Higher Level. Some UAE universities are more flexible, but the published prospectus is the only reliable source, and it changes between admissions cycles. Read the exact course page for every university on the list before Year 11 options close, and keep a dated screenshot.

The table below sets the two routes side by side on the dimensions that actually drive the decision. Treat it as a structure for the conversation with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than as a replacement for it, and confirm the current assessment model against the IB subject guide your school is teaching, since the IB revises its guides on a rolling cycle.

sections.heading: The papers, the marks, and how many minutes you get per mark
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics grade is assembled from external papers and one internal piece, and the arithmetic of that assembly is more useful to a parent than any general statement about difficulty. The externals carry four fifths of the grade; the exploration carries the remaining fifth and is the only component the student controls entirely. Higher Level students sit three papers, Standard Level students sit two.

The number to hold on to is minutes per mark. At Standard Level each paper runs ninety minutes for eighty marks, which is a touch over a minute a mark. At Higher Level the papers run two hours for one hundred and ten marks, which is almost exactly the same rate. Paper 3 at Higher Level is one hour for fifty-five marks and feels slower because the two questions are long, but the rate is identical. Students who run out of time are not usually slow at mathematics; they are spending four minutes on a two-mark opener because it looked unfamiliar.

That diagnosis changes what a tutor should do. If the error log shows marks lost at the end of the paper, the work is pacing and question triage, not content. If it shows marks lost evenly throughout on method, the work is content. If it shows full marks on parts a and b and nothing on part c across many questions, the work is extended reasoning, which is Paper 3 preparation whether or not the student sits Paper 3.

Confirm the component weightings and durations your child faces against the subject guide their school is teaching before you build a revision plan on them. The IB publishes guides on a rolling revision cycle and schools can be teaching different cohorts under different guides in the same building.

sections.heading: Where IB mathematics marks actually go missing, topic by topic
paragraphs: Mark loss in IB mathematics is not random and it is not spread evenly across the syllabus. A handful of topics account for a disproportionate share of the gap between a 5 and a 7, and they are the same topics year after year because they each sit at a join between two skills rather than inside one.

Trigonometry in radians is the clearest example. Students meet degrees at IGCSE, switch to radians in the Diploma, and then meet calculus questions where a derivative is only correct in radians. The error is invisible in a single question and fatal across a paper. Logarithms are the second: the laws are taught in a week, used for two months, and then needed again eighteen months later in an exponential modelling question that nobody connected back to them.

Integration is the third and the most expensive. A missing constant of integration is one mark; failing to recognise that a question wants a definite integral representing an area under a curve below the axis is three or four. Vectors at Higher Level are the fourth: students can compute a scalar product and cannot explain what it tells them about the angle, so the interpretation marks go. Probability distributions are the fifth, where a conditional probability question is answered with an unconditional calculation that was correct for a question nobody asked.

A tutor working from the student's own marked papers will find three or four of these in an afternoon. The value of naming them is that each has a short, specific remedy, and the student stops believing that they are bad at mathematics when in fact they are reliably losing marks in five identifiable places.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and the two nobody prepares for
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is a twelve to twenty page individual piece written across the second half of the first Diploma year and the start of the second. It is worth twenty marks in every one of the four mathematics courses, which makes it a fifth of the final grade, and it is the only part of the subject a student can work on without time pressure. Most students treat it as homework and lose marks they could not lose anywhere else.

The marks are split across five criteria. Presentation covers structure, coherence and whether a reader can follow the argument without rereading. Mathematical communication covers notation, defined variables, labelled graphs and consistent use of symbols. Personal engagement asks whether the student actually did something rather than reproducing a textbook treatment. Reflection asks whether the student evaluated what they found, considered limitations and extended the work. Use of mathematics carries the largest single block and asks whether the mathematics is correct, relevant to the course, and of a level appropriate to it.

Reflection and personal engagement are where Emirates Hills students most often leave marks on the table, and for a predictable reason: both reward the untidy parts of the process, and strong students write up the clean version. A student who tried a model, found it failed, and switched approach has material for high reflection marks and usually deletes it. A tutor's most useful intervention is often to make the student keep a dated working log from the first week, so the reflection section has something true to say.

The boundary matters as much as the technique. A tutor may discuss topic viability, point out that the mathematics chosen is below the level of the course, explain a method the student has not met, and give written feedback on a draft. A tutor may not write any part of the exploration, supply a structure for the student to fill in, or correct the mathematics directly on the student's page. The exploration carries the student's authenticity declaration and their school's; crossing that line risks the whole Diploma.

sections.heading: Calculator work Paper 2 assumes and most students were taught once
paragraphs: Paper 2 at both levels, and Paper 3 at Higher Level, are written on the assumption that the student has a graphic display calculator and can drive it without thinking. Schools teach the device in a block early in Year 12, usually in a single week, and then never return to it. By the mock season eighteen months later a sizeable share of students are navigating menus by memory of a lesson they half-attended.

The cost is measured in minutes, and minutes are what the paper is short of. Finding the intersection of two curves should take fifteen seconds; a student hunting for the right menu takes ninety and then retypes a value with a rounding error. Running a regression and reading off the coefficient of determination should be automatic for Applications students; so should using the distribution menus for binomial and normal probabilities, and the numerical solver for equations that cannot be solved analytically.

There is a second, subtler skill: knowing when not to use it. Paper 2 questions frequently have an analytic route that is faster than the calculator route, and a student who reaches for the device on every part burns time. Conversely some questions are written so that only a numerical method will work, and a student who insists on algebra will not finish. Teaching that judgement is unglamorous and it reliably moves a grade boundary.

An online lesson handles this better than most parents expect. The tutor can see the calculator screen on the student's camera or through a shared emulator, annotate the keystroke sequence on the whiteboard, and save the sequence as a reference card the student keeps. That artefact matters more than the lesson: the student reviews a one-page keystroke sheet the night before the paper rather than relearning menus in the exam hall.

sections.heading: What past-paper work should look like from October onwards
paragraphs: Past papers are the most misused resource in IB mathematics. A student who works through a paper, marks it, notes the score and moves to the next one is generating a number and no learning. The paper is a diagnostic instrument, and its value is almost entirely in what happens after the marking.

The structure that works is three-part and it takes longer than sitting the paper. First, sit it to time, in one piece, without notes, on paper rather than a screen. Second, mark it against the official mark scheme and record not the score but the reason for each lost mark in a log with a topic label and an error type: content, method, arithmetic, reading, or time. Third, and this is the part that gets skipped, reattempt only the questions that were lost for content or method, a week later, cold.

After four papers the log tells a story that no single paper does. Perhaps every loss labelled time sits in the last twenty marks, which is a pacing problem. Perhaps content losses cluster in two syllabus topics, which is three sessions of work. Perhaps arithmetic errors dominate, in which case the remedy is checking habits rather than more mathematics. Emirates Hills students sitting the May session usually have enough time to run this cycle properly if it starts in October and is not front-loaded into March.

On sourcing: use the papers your school provides and the official board material your school has licensed. We do not host, reproduce or distribute IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides or grade boundary tables, and neither should anyone selling you tutoring. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator which material the school holds and work from that.

sections.heading: What IB mathematics tutoring costs around Emirates Hills, in dirhams
paragraphs: Published pricing is scarce in this market. Of the tutoring companies ranking for Dubai IB queries, several publish no hourly figure at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below collects rates those providers published themselves, with the provider named, so you can see the shape of the market before anyone quotes you.

The pattern is consistent across sources. Online tuition from a general or university-student tutor sits at the bottom of the range. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the middle. A specialist in a named Diploma subject at Higher Level sits higher, and in-home visits add a premium that reflects travel time rather than teaching quality. Premium named or examiner-linked tutors sit above all of it. Monthly packages advertised in this market have included online blocks around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home blocks between AED 1,599 and AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions.

Two things are worth saying plainly about those figures. They are market rates published by other providers, not IB Gram's price list, and they date from the October 2026 research that built this page. And a higher rate buys a narrower specialist, not a different quality of hour: the reason an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist costs more than a general maths tutor is scarcity, not magic. For a student losing marks to arithmetic habits, the cheaper tutor is the correct purchase.

Against those numbers, context helps. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package, so a tutoring budget set last year has not been squeezed by a fee increase this year. For our own pricing, the honest answer is that it depends on the lane and the hours, and the free trial lesson exists so you can judge the hour before you commit to a figure.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in mathematics, and the permit question parents should ask
paragraphs: Two boundaries matter when you hire mathematics help in Dubai, and both are easy to check before money changes hands. The first is academic honesty. The exploration is submitted under an authenticity declaration signed by the student and countersigned by the school. Work produced by anyone else, including a tutor, is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor. Some providers in this market sell completed internal assessments outright. That is not a grey area and no responsible tutor goes near it.

What a mathematics tutor may legitimately do is wide and useful: teach the content, explain a method the student has not met, discuss whether a chosen exploration topic can carry the level of the course, read a student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and model the structure of a good write-up using a different example. What they may not do is write, rewrite, dictate, fill in, or correct mathematics directly on the student's submitted page. Ask any tutor to state that boundary in their own words before you book, and treat an evasive answer as an answer.

The second boundary is the work permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, valid for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so be wary of anyone quoting you a figure.

A related point that catches Abu Dhabi families more than Dubai ones, but is worth knowing either way: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. If a teacher at your child's school offers private lessons to your child, that is a question for the school, not a shortcut.

sections.heading: Starting with an IB maths tutor from an Emirates Hills address
paragraphs: The honest version of getting started is shorter than most providers make it sound. You send the course and level, the specific component where marks are being lost, your child's school and year, and two or three evening windows that genuinely work in your week. Within a working day or two you get a named tutor in that lane with their teaching background, and a free trial lesson to judge the hour by.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared whiteboard that both people can write on. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For an Emirates Hills family, that is less of a compromise than it sounds and often the opposite. The pool of tutors who teach Analysis and Approaches Higher Level to examination standard is small, and restricting it to people who can drive to a villa in Emirates Living by six o'clock shrinks it to almost nothing. Online, the constraint disappears and the specialist is available at the hour you need.

If no specialist is free in your window, we say so rather than substituting a general tutor and hoping. The usual outcome is a different evening slot with the right person, which almost always beats the right evening with the wrong one. For a Higher Level student eight weeks from a mock, the subject match matters more than the hour.

What to have ready for the trial: the last two marked papers with the teacher's annotations visible, the current topic list from the school, the exploration title if one exists, and a sentence from your child about which part of mathematics they would most like to stop dreading. That last one is more diagnostic than it sounds and it takes the pressure off the first fifteen minutes.

process.title: Tell us the lane, not just the subject
process.description: Analysis or Applications, Standard or Higher, and the component where the marks are going. Add the school, the year group and the exam session your child is working towards. This one message is what lets us match a specialist rather than a generalist, and it takes two minutes to write.

process.title: Send the evidence
process.description: The last two marked assessments and the most recent mock, with the teacher's annotations visible. Photographs are fine. A tutor who reads marked work before the trial arrives with a hypothesis about where the marks are going, which makes the first hour diagnostic instead of introductory.

process.title: Meet the tutor on a free trial
process.description: A full lesson, online, with no payment and no card details taken. Watch for whether the tutor works from your child's own errors or from a generic worksheet, and whether your child talks during the hour. A silent student in a trial lesson is a signal worth acting on.

process.title: Fix the slot and the cycle
process.description: Agree a weekly time that survives a normal Emirates Hills week, including the drive home and the activity that always overruns. Agree what happens between sessions: a short practice set, an error log entry, or a timed paper section. The cycle matters more than the length of the lesson.

process.title: Review against the error log, not the mood
process.description: Every four to six weeks, look at what the log says rather than at how the sessions felt. If content losses in a named topic have stopped appearing, the work is done and the focus should move. If nothing has changed in six weeks, change the tutor or change the approach rather than extending the booking.

whyPoints.title: A specialist for the exact course
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation Higher Level are different syllabuses with different assessment logic. We match on the course, not on the word mathematics, because a tutor strong in modelling and weak in proof will not move an AA Higher Level grade however good the rapport is.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from marked work
whyPoints.description: Tutoring that starts from the student's own lost marks closes the gap faster than tutoring that starts at the beginning of the syllabus. We ask for marked papers before the trial so the first session can test a hypothesis rather than survey the course from scratch.

whyPoints.title: Clear academic-honesty boundaries
whyPoints.description: Exploration support means teaching, topic discussion and written feedback on the student's own drafts. It never means writing, rewriting or correcting mathematics on the submitted page. We state that boundary in writing so the school can see the support was legitimate if it is ever asked.

whyPoints.title: Online removes the travel constraint
whyPoints.description: Lessons run over live video with a shared whiteboard. Nobody drives to an Emirates Hills villa, which means the tutor pool is not limited to people who can reach Emirates Living before six, and a six o'clock weekday slot with the right specialist is actually available.

whyPoints.title: Prices and facts you can check
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, with the research date stated. Every regulatory fact is drawn from a UAE government source. Nothing here is a statistic we invented about ourselves, because a figure nobody can check is worth nothing to you.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer when we cannot help
whyPoints.description: If no specialist in the right lane is free in your window, we say so and offer a different time rather than substituting a general tutor. A mismatched specialist wastes a term, and a term is the one thing a Diploma student cannot get back.

faqs.question: Should my child take IB Mathematics AA or AI for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Check the named course pages before deciding, because the requirement is set by the university rather than by the IB. Many engineering, mathematics and physics courses in the UK and Europe specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and will not accept Applications and Interpretation Higher Level in its place. Some UAE universities are more flexible. Read the exact entry requirements for every course on your child's list while they are still in Year 11, save a dated copy, and recheck in the application year, since admissions wording changes between cycles. Choosing by reputation rather than by the published requirement is the error we see most.

faqs.question: How is the IB mathematics exploration marked and what is it worth?
faqs.answer: It carries twenty marks and counts for a fifth of the final grade in all four mathematics courses. Those marks are split across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single block. Students most often lose marks in reflection and personal engagement, because both reward the messy parts of the process and strong students write up only the clean version. Keeping a dated working log from the first week gives the reflection section something true to say. Confirm the current criteria with your school's Diploma coordinator, since the IB revises its subject guides on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and how should a Higher Level student prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level, in both mathematics routes. It runs for an hour, carries fifty-five marks, and contains two long problems that build from a concrete case towards a general result. It is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade. Preparation is not additional content, because the syllabus is the same; it is supervised practice at writing a developing argument under time pressure. Students who routinely score well on parts a and b and nothing on part c are telling you exactly what to work on. Confirm the current format against the subject guide your school teaches.

faqs.question: My child is fine in Paper 2 and losing marks in Paper 1. What causes that?
faqs.answer: That split almost always points at non-calculator technique rather than at mathematics knowledge. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator, so it tests exact-value trigonometry held in memory, confident work with surds and indices, and the discipline to leave an answer as a fraction or a logarithm rather than converting it. Students who have leaned on the device for eighteen months lose two or three marks a question to arithmetic and form, not to method. A six to eight week block working only from past Paper 1 questions, timed, with every lost mark logged by error type, is the standard remedy.

faqs.question: Which IB maths topics cost Dubai Diploma students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Five recur. Radians inside calculus questions, where a derivative is only correct in radians and the error is invisible in a single answer. Logarithm laws, taught early and then needed eighteen months later in exponential modelling. Definite integrals where part of the region sits below the axis. Vectors at Higher Level, where students compute a scalar product correctly and never interpret it. And conditional probability answered as though it were unconditional. Each sits at a join between two skills rather than inside one, which is why they survive ordinary revision. A tutor reading marked papers finds three or four of them in an afternoon.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation Higher Level easier than Analysis Higher Level?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it as the soft option is how students end up in the wrong course. The two reward different things. Analysis Higher Level suits a student who enjoys manipulation and will sit with a proof for twenty minutes. Applications Higher Level suits a student who can read a context, choose a model, run it and then say in a sentence what the result means for the situation described. Applications also carries matrices, graph theory and advanced statistics, which are not light. The real difference for most Emirates Hills families is university fit, not difficulty, so start the decision there.

faqs.question: What can a maths tutor legitimately do with my child's exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the content, explain a method the student has not met, discuss whether a chosen topic carries enough mathematics for the level of the course, read the student's own draft and give written feedback against the criteria, and model good structure using a different example. A tutor may not write, rewrite, dictate or fill in any part of it, and may not correct mathematics directly on the page that will be submitted. The exploration is submitted under an authenticity declaration signed by the student and the school, so the consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Higher Level mathematics student need?
faqs.answer: One well-structured hour a week, used properly, moves more than three unstructured ones. The usual pattern is a weekly session alongside the school's scheme of work, plus a short block of concentrated work on one component when the error log identifies it. Students who are two grades below target in the second year sometimes run two sessions a week for a term, then drop back. What matters more than the count is what happens between sessions: a practice set attempted and logged beats an hour of passive revision. Judge by whether the error pattern changes, not by hours booked.

faqs.question: Does online maths tutoring work when the student needs to show working?
faqs.answer: It works well, because mathematics is the subject where the shared screen is genuinely better than a kitchen table. Both people write on the same annotated whiteboard, the tutor can see each line as it is produced rather than only the finished answer, and the annotated page is saved and sent afterwards so the student revises from the actual working rather than from memory. Students upload photographs of handwritten work before a session so the tutor arrives having already read the method. The one thing to check is a stable connection and a device with a decent camera angle on the paper.

faqs.question: My child moved from IGCSE Extended maths into AA Higher Level and is struggling. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the two syllabuses do not meet cleanly, and this is the steepest routine jump in the Dubai school calendar. IGCSE Extended finishes with the quadratic formula, a light touch of trigonometric graphs and, in some specifications, elementary differentiation. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level assumes proof by induction, binomial expansion with fractional and negative indices, compound angle identities and a working comfort with radians that IGCSE never required. A strong IGCSE candidate can look like a weak Diploma one within a term with nothing having changed except the demand. It is a bridging problem and it responds quickly to targeted work.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Dubai, collected from the providers that publish them, run roughly as follows. Budget online tutoring sits between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and AED 300. A named-subject IB or IGCSE specialist sits between AED 200 and AED 450 or above, and premium named tutors have advertised AED 650. In-home visits add a travel premium of roughly AED 180 to AED 500. Those are other providers' published figures from October 2026 research, not our price list. Ask us for a quote and take the free trial first.

faqs.question: How early before the May session should past-paper work start?
faqs.answer: October of the examination year is the sensible start, because the useful cycle takes longer than sitting the paper. Sit it to time in one piece on paper, mark it against the official scheme, then log every lost mark by topic and by error type rather than recording a score. A week later, reattempt cold only the questions lost for content or method. After four papers the log shows whether the problem is pacing, two syllabus topics, or arithmetic under pressure, and each of those has a different remedy. Starting in March leaves time to generate scores but not to act on them.

faqs.question: Do you supply IB past papers, mark schemes or subject guides?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be cautious of anyone who offers to. IB, Cambridge and Pearson assessment materials are copyright, and schools hold them under licence. We reference them, cite the official source, and work from the material your child's school already provides. Ask the Diploma coordinator which past papers and mark schemes the school holds and which online platform the school subscribes to; that is almost always more material than a student can get through. A tutor's value is in what happens after the paper is marked, not in supplying the paper.

faqs.question: Does my child need a particular maths grade for UAE Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education sets equivalency requirements by curriculum, and the published British-track rule covers IGCSE and A Level rather than the IB. For the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. No verified IB points threshold is published in the sources we could read, so check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. Equivalency is a process your family completes with the Ministry; it is not something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my children if they are on different maths routes?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not force it. A tutor comfortable across Standard Level in both routes can reasonably hold two students, and families often run back-to-back slots on the same evening. Higher Level is different: Analysis Higher Level and Applications Higher Level are genuinely separate specialisms and few tutors teach both to examination standard. If one child is on Higher Level Analysis and the other on Higher Level Applications, two tutors is the honest answer. Convenience that costs a grade is not convenience.

intro.heading: The first Diploma year is where the maths grade is decided
paragraphs: Almost every maths enquiry we receive from this catchment arrives in the second Diploma year, usually after the mocks. By then the useful work has narrowed to habit repair and timed papers, which is real but modest. The decisions that actually set the grade were taken a year earlier, quietly, and nobody was watching them.

Four of them. Which course the student is in, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and at which level. Whether they learned the graphic display calculator deliberately or by copying what the teacher pressed. Whether they write method lines as a matter of course or only when they remember. And what their exploration is about, which in most schools should be decided before the first year ends.

None of those four is urgent in the first year, which is exactly why they go unattended. There is no external paper, the internal assessments are a long way off, and a 4 in the first set of reports looks like settling in. A year later all four have hardened, and three of them cannot be changed at all.

So this page is organised around the first Diploma year and what it should produce, with the second year treated as the consequence rather than the subject. It maps the first-year terms, sets out the calculator skills that should exist by the end of each, explains how to source an exploration topic the student can actually handle, and compares the two courses against what degree programmes expect.

There is one more first-year item that costs nothing to address and a great deal to ignore, and it is arithmetic by hand. A graphic display calculator will quietly cover for weak fraction work, index manipulation and mental estimation for several years, and the Diploma's technology-free paper removes that cover at the worst possible moment. A short set of manipulations by hand, marked, every week, with no calculator in the room, prevents a problem that becomes close to unfixable once mocks are underway. It takes ten minutes of a session and it is the item most often dropped first when a term gets busy.

Green Community is a useful place to make this argument because the local maths tutoring market is reasonably deep at IGCSE level and very thin at Diploma level. Dubai's IB provision is 7% of private enrolment across 227 schools and 17 curricula, and this catchment is not where it concentrates. A radius search from Dubai Investments Park returns people who can teach Year 10 algebra and very few who have read an exploration against its criteria.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. One note on dates: IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session and publishes no specific IB examination or results date.

subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and statistics across two papers, one without technology. The first-year action is hand arithmetic, because a calculator has usually been covering for a gap since Year 8 and the non-technology paper exposes it.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial mathematics and modelling with technology throughout. The first-year action is writing interpretation sentences, since a correct statistic with no statement of meaning scores below what the student understands.

subjects.description: A student-chosen investigation assessed against lettered criteria. The first-year action is choosing a topic whose mathematics the student can genuinely handle, which removes most of the pressure from the second year.

subjects.description: Regression, distributions, numerical solving, graph analysis and table work. Learned by imitation it costs minutes per paper in menu-hunting; learned deliberately it saves them, and in maths minutes convert directly into marks.

subjects.name: Method-line discipline
subjects.description: Writing each step before the answer. The mark scheme awards method marks to lines that exist, so a wrong final answer with visible working still scores and a right one without it risks everything on arithmetic.

subjects.name: Paper 3 persistence
subjects.description: Long linked tasks on unfamiliar ground where the skill is carrying a partial result forward. First-year practice at not stopping is worth more than second-year practice at the content, because the behaviour is the harder thing to change.

subjects.name: Interpretation sentences
subjects.description: Stating what a model, coefficient or probability actually means in context. Marked explicitly, routinely skipped, and trainable in a handful of sessions at any point in the course.

sections.heading: The first Diploma year, term by term, and what should exist at the end
paragraphs: The first Diploma maths year has no external deadline, which makes it feel like preparation rather than performance. Treated properly it is the most productive year in the course, because everything it produces is permanent: a habit, a skill, a topic, a course placement that fits.

The first term should establish that method lines are written every time. This sounds trivial and it is the single highest-value behaviour in the subject, because Paper 1 marks are allocated to the working rather than to the answer. A student who writes the lines keeps the method marks when arithmetic fails; one who does not risks the whole question on a sign. Installing it while the content is still manageable costs almost nothing.

The second term should establish calculator control. Not familiarity, control: knowing which function to reach for, reaching for it without hunting, and knowing what the output means. Students who learned by watching the teacher's screen lose minutes per paper to menu navigation, and in a timed maths paper minutes are marks. This is also when hand arithmetic needs protecting, because the non-technology paper will expose a gap that a calculator has been hiding since Year 8.

The third term should produce an exploration topic and a first real diagnostic. By the end of the first year a student should have a topic whose mathematics they can genuinely do, and a marked assessment that tells the family honestly whether the course and level still fit. Both of those are decisions, and both become much harder to take once the second year starts.

sections.heading: Sourcing an exploration topic the student can actually handle
paragraphs: The exploration is assessed against lettered criteria including personal engagement and the use of mathematics commensurate with the course. Those two pull in opposite directions when a topic is chosen badly. A student picks something impressive, imports a technique they do not understand, and loses marks on the mathematics criterion while also failing to show genuine engagement, because nothing about the work is theirs.

The fix is to start from the student rather than from a list of topics. What do they actually do, watch, play, argue about? A sport, a game, a commute, a hobby, a family business. Then ask what measurable quantity sits inside it, and what mathematics from their own course would say something non-obvious about that quantity. The topic that survives those two questions is nearly always better than anything from a list of suggested explorations.

The third test is feasibility, and it is the one families skip. Can the data be obtained, in the time available, in a form the student can work with? Is the model something they can set up and criticise? An exploration whose data turns out to be unavailable in week five becomes a rushed substitute in week eight, and the reflection criterion is the first casualty because there is nothing left to reflect on.

The boundary matters as much here as anywhere. A tutor may question the topic, teach the mathematics it needs, explain what each criterion rewards and what it caps, check whether the data is obtainable, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not supply the topic wholesale, do the mathematics, write any part of the exploration, or edit it to a finished state. Services in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and submitting bought work risks the Diploma.

sections.heading: Calculator fluency as a syllabus item in its own right
paragraphs: Most Diploma students are issued a graphic display calculator, shown how to do a handful of things with it, and left to absorb the rest by watching. That produces a student who can reach the right answer given unlimited time and who loses several minutes per paper navigating menus to find a function they know exists. In a timed paper, that is a mark cost nobody attributes to the calculator.

Fluency is teachable and it decomposes cleanly. Graph analysis: plotting, windowing sensibly, finding intersections, zeros and extrema without guessing. Statistics: one and two-variable analysis, regression with the model stated, distributions both ways round. Numerical work: solving equations, evaluating integrals and derivatives at a point. Table work: generating values to test a conjecture quickly.

The discipline that goes with it is stating what was asked of the technology. Paper 2 and the Applications and Interpretation course both reward candidates who write the model, the variables and the meaning alongside the number. An unexplained value earns nothing even when it is correct, and students who learned the calculator by imitation are precisely the ones who produce unexplained values, because they never articulated what they were asking for.

This is also work that suits a shared screen unusually well. The tutor can see exactly what the student is pressing, which is the fastest way to find the habit that is costing time, and the student can be given a timed set of calculator tasks and watched doing them. An in-home tutor looking over a shoulder gets the same information; the difference is that the online session happens at 4.30pm rather than after a drive.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, read from the destination
paragraphs: The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of one subject. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with calculus at its centre and a paper without technology. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-oriented, with statistics, financial mathematics and integrated technology, and interpretation marks sitting alongside the computation. A student who thinks in symbols belongs in the first; one who thinks in data and context belongs in the second.

Aptitude is only half the decision, though, and the half families overweight. The other half is the destination. Some degree programmes in mathematics, engineering, physics and economics specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and will not accept Applications and Interpretation in its place. Others treat them as equivalent. The only reliable method is to read the entry requirements of two or three target programmes directly, including any UAE universities on the list, before the course is confirmed.

Separately, school-leaving certificates generally need Ministry of Education equivalency before a UAE university application, and the requirements differ by curriculum track. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. No IB points threshold appears in the source we have read, so we publish none and you should verify any figure on moe.gov.ae.

Where a student is already in the course that suits them less well, the work is adaptation rather than regret. A modelling thinker in Analysis and Approaches needs non-calculator algebra drilled hard. A symbolic thinker in Applications and Interpretation needs to stop treating interpretation sentences as decoration and start treating them as marked content, which they are.

paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent tutors to AED 500, specialists at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase around AED 270, and BartyED at AED 650.

Read monthly, Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Packages visible in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Now compare two plans. One weekly session through the three terms of the first Diploma year, in the mid band, is a sustained but ordinary household cost, and what it buys is permanent: method discipline, calculator control, a workable exploration topic and an honest level check. Two or three sessions a week through the final stretch, in the specialist band, costs more per month and buys habit repair only, because the content window has closed.

That comparison is the argument of this page expressed in dirhams, and it is why we raise the first year on a page most families reach in the second. None of the figures above are IB Gram prices and this page carries no rate card, because the fee depends on course and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. sections.heading: Online one-to-one maths from Green Community, limitations included
paragraphs: Maths transfers to video better than most subjects, for a mechanical reason: the work is a shared surface with mathematics appearing on it. The tutor writes a line, the student writes the next, and both see the same page. For calculator work the screen share is actively better than sitting alongside, because the tutor sees precisely which keys are being pressed and can stop a habit the moment it appears.

The scheduling gain matters more in maths than elsewhere. A 4.30pm session catches a student who can still hold an algebraic manipulation accurately. A 6.15pm session, after a tutor has crossed the city, catches one who makes sign and transposition errors. Parents routinely read those errors as weak mathematics when they are fatigue, and the misreading leads to buying content help for a timing problem.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, stated here near the top rather than left to be discovered, because two providers ranking for UAE searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote.

The limitations are specific. A student who will not begin work without an adult physically present does better in person. A weak home connection shortens the hour whatever the invoice says. A shared study space, more common in the apartment blocks here than in the villas, undermines the lesson because the tutor cannot manage the room. If one of those applies, hire locally and ask whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the claims to set aside
paragraphs: Mathematics attracts overclaiming because its results look objective, so three claims deserve setting aside before any money changes hands.

Promised outcomes first. No tutor can commit to a 7, a points total or a grade improvement. Grade boundaries are set after each session is marked, and the final mark depends on work done in an examination hall nobody else is in. We publish no outcome promise, no success percentage and no self-asserted rating, because a statistic without n, date and method is a liability rather than evidence.

Examiner claims second. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for individuals, and in this market examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content that nobody has. We also do not host or distribute IB papers, mark schemes, boundary tables or subject guides, which are copyright material; we reference the official sources and work from the school's licensed copies.

Regulatory endorsement third. IB Gram is not KHDA approved - a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and we hold none and operate no UAE office. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership. Separately, private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years, and tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

sections.heading: Starting, in whichever year you are actually in
paragraphs: If your child is in the first Diploma year, send the course and level, the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment. The first session will look at two things that sound unglamorous and decide the grade: whether method lines are being written, and whether the calculator is under control. Both are visible on a script within two questions.

If your child is in the second year, send the same plus whichever is the live pressure - the exploration draft or a marked paper. The first session is diagnostic and ends in one of three honest statements: habit marks recoverable in the weeks available, unmet content needing more time than remains, or both with a decision to make. The third is the answer families least want and most need.

Matching takes about a day for Standard Level in either course. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the second year takes two or three days, because the pool is narrow and a general maths tutor in front of a Paper 3 problem is worse than a short wait. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards.

The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist, and built on the document you sent, ending in a written note that is yours whether or not you continue. When nobody suitable has a slot at your hour we say so and offer a different weekday, a short block, or an honest recommendation to look locally. No competitor in this market publishes its unavailable case.

faqs.question: Is it too early to get a maths tutor in the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, and almost nobody does it. The first year has no external paper, which makes it feel like preparation rather than performance, and it is where four permanent things are settled: whether method lines get written, whether the calculator is under control, what the exploration is about, and whether the course and level actually fit. Three of those four cannot be reversed in the second year. A term of ordinary weekly work here buys more than an intensive final stretch does.

faqs.question: Why does the graphic display calculator need teaching at all?
faqs.answer: Because most students learn it by watching the teacher's screen, which produces someone who can find the right answer given unlimited time and loses minutes per paper hunting through menus. In a timed maths paper minutes are marks. Taught deliberately, the skills decompose cleanly: graphing and windowing, intersections and extrema, one and two-variable statistics, regression with the model stated, distributions in both directions, numerical solving. A screen-shared session is unusually good for this, because the tutor sees exactly which keys are being pressed.

faqs.question: How should my child choose an exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Start from what they actually do rather than from a list. A sport, a game, a commute, a hobby, a family business. Then find the measurable quantity inside it, and ask what mathematics from their own course would say something non-obvious about that quantity. Then test feasibility: can the data be obtained in time, in a usable form? A topic that survives those three questions beats anything imported from a suggested list, because the personal engagement criterion rewards work that is genuinely the student's own.

faqs.question: Will a Green Community student need AA at Higher Level for engineering?
faqs.answer: Requirements differ by university and by programme, and the only reliable method is to read the entry requirements for two or three specific courses directly rather than relying on a general rule. Some mathematics, engineering, physics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and will not accept Applications and Interpretation in its place; others treat the two as equivalent. Separately, school-leaving certificates generally need Ministry of Education equivalency, and no IB points threshold appears in the source we read, so verify that on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: My child is in Applications and Interpretation but wanted Analysis and Approaches. What now?
faqs.answer: If the change is still possible in the school's timetable, decide it on a marked assessment rather than on preference, and read the entry requirements of two or three target degree programmes first because that is often the real constraint. If it is not possible, the work is adaptation rather than regret: a symbolic thinker in Applications and Interpretation needs to stop treating interpretation sentences as decoration and start treating them as marked content, which they are, and to use the technology deliberately rather than reluctantly.

faqs.question: What does "method lines" mean and why does it cost so much?
faqs.answer: It means writing each step of a calculation before the answer rather than working partly in your head. The IB mark scheme allocates method marks to working that exists on the page, so a student who writes only answers keeps full marks when the arithmetic is right and loses everything on the question when it is not. Over a full Paper 1 that routinely accounts for the gap between two grades. It is a discipline rather than a concept, and three or four sessions of strict enforcement normally installs it for good.

faqs.question: Does the non-technology paper really expose a Year 8 gap?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes. A calculator will cover for weak fraction work, index manipulation and mental arithmetic for years without anyone noticing, and the Diploma's technology-free paper removes that cover at the worst possible moment. The useful first-year action is maintaining hand arithmetic deliberately: a short set of manipulations by hand every week, marked, with no calculator in the room. It is dull, it takes ten minutes of a session, and it prevents a problem that is close to unfixable once mocks are underway.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without crossing IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate space is wide. A tutor can question the topic, teach the mathematics it needs, explain what each lettered criterion rewards and what its mark ceiling is, check whether the data or model is obtainable, discuss how to structure the argument, check notation and referencing, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor cannot supply the topic wholesale, do the mathematics, write any part of it or edit it to completion. The test after each session is whether every sentence and every calculation was the student's own.

faqs.question: How much does IB maths tutoring cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published October 2026 figures, none of them ours: entry-level online tuition from about AED 33-65 an hour at Tutopiya and EdFlik; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300 with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200; in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 per Dubai rate guidance with independents to AED 500; specialists at AED 200-450 and above with TutorChase around AED 270; and BartyED at AED 650. Monthly, a weekly session runs roughly AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid and AED 1,000-2,000 plus for specialist exam-year work.

faqs.question: Is a weekly session through the first year better value than an intensive final push?
faqs.answer: On what it buys, yes. A weekly mid-band session across the three terms of the first Diploma year produces permanent things: method discipline, calculator control, a feasible exploration topic and an honest level check. Two or three specialist-band sessions a week through the final stretch cost more per month and buy habit repair only, because the content window has closed and new teaching there displaces the timed practice that converts knowledge into marks. The second plan is real and it is narrower.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an HL Analysis and Approaches tutor near Dubai Investments Park?
faqs.answer: Standard Level in either course usually matches within a day. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the second Diploma year takes two or three days, because the pool of tutors who can handle a Paper 3 problem properly is genuinely narrow and we will not substitute a general maths tutor. We state the expected wait at the enquiry. A radius search from here for the same specialism tends to return people who teach Year 10 algebra well and have never read an exploration against its criteria.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP 5 and starting Diploma maths. What is worth doing now?
faqs.answer: Deliberate algebraic manipulation by hand, every line written, plus a diagnostic at the standard the chosen course will demand in its first term. The Middle Years Programme assesses against four lettered criteria out of eight and rewards investigation and communication, which is genuinely useful for the exploration later. What it does not require is fast, accurate formal manipulation, and the Diploma assumes it from the first week. A summer of that removes most of the first-term shock, which is otherwise read as a capability problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram publish the IB maths examination dates?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and goes no further. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where relevant. For your child's actual dates, the school's Diploma coordinator holds both the external session dates and the internal exploration deadline, and the internal one usually drives the term plan more than the external one does.

faqs.question: How should maths sessions change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Keep the frequency and shorten the session. Fluency in mathematics decays faster than content knowledge does, so two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one while a student is fasting, and a complete pause usually means relearning in the first week back. The hour itself typically moves to early afternoon or post-iftar, since school hours shorten and the household evening reorganises around iftar. Because nobody is travelling to your address, that is a shared-diary change rather than a renegotiation of a commute.

intro.heading: Diploma maths is a two-year sequence of decisions, and most of them close quietly
paragraphs: Families contact us about Diploma maths at four predictable moments. The first is in the spring of Year 11, when the choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation has to be made, often with very little information. The second is October of the first Diploma year, when a student who chose higher level discovers what higher level means. The third is the start of the second year, when the exploration deadline appears alongside everything else. The fourth is the final term, when a mock result turns a worry into a number.

The point in the course matters more than almost anything else, because it determines what is still possible. In the spring of Year 11 the decision itself is the intervention, and getting it right is worth more than a year of tutoring afterwards. In October of the first year the right work is foundational and cheap. At the start of the second year it is project management as much as mathematics. In the final term it is paper technique, and introducing new content actively costs marks.

Hor Al Anz sits in Deira, next to Abu Hail and Al Muteena and inland from Al Mamzar, with the Green Line of the Metro running through it. The Diploma provision used by families here mostly sits across the Creek or towards Al Mamzar and Festival City, so a Diploma student in this district usually commutes. That has a real effect on what a tutoring plan can ask of a weekday evening, and it is why we treat session length and weekend slots as part of the plan rather than as scheduling detail.

The exploration deserves its own warning at the top of the page. It is the internal assessment in both maths routes, it carries twenty per cent of the grade under the current guide, and its deadlines are set by the school rather than by the board. It is also the component families most often ask for the wrong help with. A tutor can teach a student how to choose a question with genuine mathematics in it, how to handle real data, and how to write up reasoning properly, and must never write, draft or rewrite any part of it.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. For maths specifically the screen suits the subject: the student writes on paper with the camera on the page, the tutor watches each line appear, and a graphing display or a shared whiteboard sits alongside it without anybody carrying equipment across Dubai.

What follows is the calendar in detail, the route and level decision, the exploration, the paper structures and where marks actually go. If you read one section, read the one on the exploration, because its deadline does more to shape a second Diploma year than any topic does.

sections.heading: The two-year maths calendar, decision by decision
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is not a syllabus to be covered evenly across two years. It is a sequence of points at which something is decided, and after each of them the range of available outcomes narrows. Families who see the sequence act earlier and spend less. Families who meet it as a series of surprises end up buying intensive support in the final term to compensate for a choice made by default eighteen months earlier.

The first point is the route and level choice, taken in the spring of Year 11. The second is the first term of the first Diploma year, where the gap between what a student can do and what the course assumes becomes visible. The third is the exploration, whose school-set deadlines usually arrive in the second year alongside everything else. The fourth is the mock series, which produces the only document worth planning the final term from. The fifth is the final fortnight, where the only rule that matters is to add nothing new.

The table below sets this out with what support should be doing in each window and which decision closes there. None of it requires a parent to understand the mathematics. All of it requires asking the school a specific question at a specific time, which is why the right-hand column is written as a closing decision rather than as information.

One local note. For a student commuting out of Hor Al Anz to a Diploma school, every window in this table is tighter than it would be for a student living next to their school. That is an argument for acting earlier at each point rather than for working harder later, and it is the single most useful piece of advice on this page.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice and its deadline
paragraphs: This is the decision with the longest shadow in Diploma mathematics and it is routinely made on the worst available information. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-focused route, with calculus at its centre and a first paper sat without technology, which means fluency and exact-form working carry real weight. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and the use of technology, with written justification of models carrying marks that students frequently treat as presentation.

Neither is a soft option and neither is universally harder. They are different, and the right question is not which is easier but which fits the student and the intended destination. Many engineering, physical-science and economics courses specify a route and sometimes a level, and those requirements are published on each university's own admissions pages. Reading two or three of those pages before the option block closes is worth more than any amount of advice, including this page's.

The student's own profile is the second input and it should be tested rather than assumed. A student who is quick and accurate with algebra and enjoys a problem with a single right answer is usually better served by Analysis and Approaches. A student who reasons well about real situations, handles data comfortably and finds abstract manipulation a grind often does better in Applications and Interpretation, and will score higher there than in a route chosen for its reputation.

The table compares the two routes on the things that actually differ. Use it alongside the university requirements rather than instead of them, and have the conversation before the deadline rather than after it, because a route change once the course has begun is disruptive and a level change is easier but still costly.
