sections.heading: The exploration: the internal deadline that runs the second year
paragraphs: Both maths routes are assessed in part by the mathematical exploration, a piece of individual written work completed in school and marked against published criteria. It carries twenty per cent of the grade under the current guide, which makes it the largest single block of marks the student directly controls, and it is where the second Diploma year either stays manageable or stops being so.

The most common failure is topic choice. Students pick something that interests them and discover six weeks later that it contains almost no mathematics at the right level, or they pick something so ambitious that the mathematics cannot be handled properly in the available space. Both are fatal and both are visible in the first fortnight to anybody who asks the right question, which is simply: show me the mathematics you will actually do, and at what level. A tutor earns their fee here more clearly than anywhere else in the subject.

The second failure is write-up quality. The criteria reward mathematical communication, personal engagement and reflection as well as the mathematics itself, which means notation, structure and a genuine discussion of limitations all score. Students treat the write-up as a formality after the interesting part is done, and it is frequently where half the available marks sit. Planning the write-up before the work starts prevents the usual rushed conclusion.

On what support is permitted, the limit is firm and we publish it. A tutor may help a student narrow a topic until the mathematics is appropriate and achievable, teach the techniques involved, advise on data handling, and respond to the student's own draft with the questions a moderator would ask next. A tutor must never write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of the exploration. The school supervisor sets the rules for permitted support in your child's case, and the internal deadlines they publish are what the plan should be built backwards from.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3: what technology changes
paragraphs: The papers in Diploma mathematics make different demands, and the biggest single difference is technology. In Analysis and Approaches one paper is sat without technology, which means exact-form answers, algebraic fluency and confident manipulation are examined directly. In Applications and Interpretation technology is available across the papers, which shifts the examination towards interpretation, modelling and the written justification of what the technology produced. Higher level students in both routes also sit an additional problem-solving paper.

That has a practical consequence for revision that students routinely get wrong: they practise everything the same way. Preparing for a paper sat without technology means deliberately working without it, which is uncomfortable and necessary. Preparing for a paper where technology is available means practising with the actual device the student will use in the hall, to the point where its menus are not costing time. Those are different activities and a student who does only one of them is half prepared.

The additional higher level paper deserves specific attention because it is the one most students have practised least. It asks for sustained problem-solving across a longer question rather than recall of a technique, and the skill it tests is the willingness to make progress on a problem whose route is not obvious. That is trainable, and it trains through doing exactly those questions under time with somebody who can show where the entry points were missed.

Across all the papers, the one habit worth more than any topic is laying out working as formula, substitution and result on separate lines. Method marks are available on multi-step questions even when the final value is wrong, and a student who writes only answers forfeits marks they had already earned. Establishing that habit takes a fortnight and protects marks for the rest of the course.

sections.heading: Where Diploma maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Across marked Diploma maths scripts the losses cluster in a small number of places and almost none of them are exotic topics. The largest is working that is not laid out, so method marks disappear when a final value is wrong. The second is notation: an inequality written loosely, a function defined without its domain, an integral without its variable. Examiners mark what is written, and in mathematics notation is content rather than style.

The third is exact form and rounding instructions. A question that asks for an exact answer and receives a decimal is wrong, and a question specifying a degree of accuracy means it. On the paper sat without technology, exact-form work is a standing requirement rather than an occasional one, and students who have spent two years with a calculator in reach find this genuinely difficult until they practise it deliberately.

The fourth is justification. Both routes reward the written reasoning around a result: why this model, what its limitations are, why this step follows. Students trained in systems where the answer is the whole of the work supply the result and lose the marks attached to the argument. That is a learnable habit and it generalises, because the same demand appears in the exploration and in the sciences.

The fifth is time. Many students lose more marks to questions they never reached than to questions they got wrong, and the remedy is procedural: a known order of attack, a rule for abandoning a question and returning to it, and enough whole papers under time that the rule has become automatic. Pacing is measurable, trainable and almost never taught, which makes it the highest-return item on most final-term plans.

sections.heading: A commuting student's week, and the session that survives it
paragraphs: A Diploma student travelling from Hor Al Anz to a school across the Creek or towards Festival City loses a substantial part of the day to the journey. Those on the Green Line arrive more predictably than those on a bus in traffic, but neither arrives early. Most are home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts around 17:30. For a student carrying three higher level subjects, the core and an exploration, that window is contested before any tutoring is added.

Two adjustments make the difference between a plan that works and one that quietly fails. The first is session length: sixty focused minutes on a travel day beats ninety that drift, and the work set between sessions should be sized for someone who has already spent an hour commuting. The second is using weekend mornings, which are the best slot in the week for whole papers, long exploration sessions and anything requiring sustained attention, and which almost nobody requests.

The physical setup matters in a Deira apartment. A hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper, a ruler, the student's own graphing device rather than a phone, and headphones so the household is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page, because in mathematics the entire diagnostic method is watching the working appear line by line and catching the sign error as it happens rather than after it has propagated.

Ramadan shifts several weeks each year and schools adjust their hours. The arrangement that works is fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work between them, agreed before the month begins. For a second-year Diploma student those weeks often sit close to a mock series or an exploration deadline, which is exactly why planning the shift beats improvising through it.

sections.heading: Arriving in Diploma maths from IGCSE, CBSE or the MYP
paragraphs: Students in this district arrive into Diploma mathematics from three main places and each arrives with a different profile, which is why a single catch-up programme serves none of them well. From IGCSE Extended or Higher tier, students are usually competent with technique and unpractised at sustained multi-step reasoning and at the written justification the Diploma expects. The content gap is modest; the expectation gap is real.

From CBSE or ICSE, students typically bring stronger procedural fluency and more systematic practice than average, and less experience of open-ended problems where the route is not signposted. The higher level problem-solving paper is where this shows most clearly. The work needed is practice on unfamiliar problems with somebody discussing entry points, rather than more drilling of techniques the student already has.

From the Middle Years Programme, students arrive strong on investigation and communication, which genuinely helps with the exploration, and often short on the automatic algebraic fluency that higher level assumes from the first week. Six to eight short sessions in the summer before the course, aimed only at manipulation, standard form and function handling, removes most of the September shock.

In every case the right first step is an audit rather than teaching: what has been covered, to what depth, and which of the Diploma's particular demands the student has never actually practised. One session produces a short written list, usually three or four items. Selling a general revision programme to a transferring student is the standard offer in this market and it is almost always the wrong purchase, because it spends weeks on material the student already holds.

sections.heading: Permits, honest limits and what to verify yourself
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with the application made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any specific amount should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will claim one. We operate no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not enter candidates for examinations and we do not perform Ministry equivalency. Where this page names a regulator, it is to explain what that body does and point you at its own pages rather than to borrow its standing.

On figures: published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more, and in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the fee. Those come from published provider pages and the Bestimate Dubai rate table and are the market rather than our price list. We publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

What to verify independently: the examination session and any dates with the school's IB coordinator and the International Baccalaureate's own site, since we deliberately publish no IB examination or results dates; the exploration deadlines, in writing, from the maths department; what exploration support is permitted, from the supervisor; and the university entry requirements for the route and level, from each institution's own admissions pages. On every one of those we would rather be the page that tells you where to look.

process.title: Say where in the course you are
process.description: Year group, route, level and roughly how many weeks remain. Those four facts decide whether the right purchase is a route-choice diagnosis, weekly teaching, exploration coaching or final-term paper work. They also decide what we would not sell you, which is the part of a first conversation most enquiries never reach.

process.title: Send a marked script and the exploration brief
process.description: The marked paper shows where the marks go: unlaid-out working, notation, exact form, justification or timing. The exploration brief and its internal deadlines show what the second year actually looks like. Together they take twenty minutes to read and they determine the plan more reliably than any conversation.

process.title: Free trial lesson on real questions
process.description: The first session is free and runs on past-paper questions drawn from the student's own weak area, with the camera on the page so the tutor watches the working appear. A short written note follows naming the two priority items and their order, and the note is yours whether or not you continue.

process.title: Place the session where the commute allows
process.description: One weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, set after the journey home, usually 17:30 or later, with sixty focused minutes rather than ninety drifting ones. Longer work, including exploration sessions and whole papers, moves to a weekend morning, which is the most productive and least-booked slot in the week.

process.title: Review on marked evidence and finish when done
process.description: A second marked paper at week four with the error tally compared to the first. If the pattern has not moved we change the approach or the tutor. If the honest answer is that the student needs a better exploration plan rather than more teaching, we say that instead of selling extra hours.

whyPoints.title: The route choice treated as the real intervention
whyPoints.description: Two or three honest diagnostic sessions before the option block closes are worth more than a year of tutoring afterwards, because a route chosen on reputation rather than on fit costs marks for two years. We test the student's fluency rather than asking how they feel about maths.

whyPoints.title: The exploration planned from the school's dates
whyPoints.description: We ask for the internal deadlines in writing at the start and build backwards. Topic choice gets settled in the first fortnight with the actual mathematics named, because a topic without mathematics at the right level is the most common and most expensive failure in this component.

whyPoints.title: Papers revised differently, because they differ
whyPoints.description: A paper sat without technology requires deliberate non-calculator practice, which students avoid. A paper with technology requires fluency with the specific device. The additional higher level paper requires unfamiliar problems under time. Treating all three the same way is how capable students under-perform.

whyPoints.title: Working laid out so method marks survive
whyPoints.description: Formula, substitution and result on separate lines, as a standing habit. Method marks are available on multi-step questions even when the final value is wrong, and the single largest recoverable loss in marked Diploma maths scripts is working that was never written down.

whyPoints.title: Built for a student who commutes
whyPoints.description: Sixty-minute weekday sessions, work set sized for an evening that started at 17:30, and the heavy work moved to weekend mornings. A plan that assumes an empty weekday evening does not survive a daily journey across the Creek.

whyPoints.title: A published limit on the exploration
whyPoints.description: We coach topic choice, technique, data handling and write-up structure, and we write none of it. Feedback arrives as the questions a moderator would ask. The supervisor at school remains the authority on what support is permitted in your child's case.

faqs.question: Should our child take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the intended degree subject and on how the student actually thinks, not on which has the easier reputation. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-focused with calculus at its centre and one paper sat without technology. Applications and Interpretation emphasises modelling, statistics and technology use, with written justification of models carrying real marks. Many engineering, physical-science and economics courses specify a route and sometimes a level, and those requirements are on each university's own admissions pages. Read two or three of those before the option block closes.

faqs.question: When does the IB maths route decision actually close?
faqs.answer: Effectively when the option blocks are confirmed in the spring of Year 11, though some schools allow a change early in the first Diploma term. A level change from higher to standard is usually easier than a route change and is still disruptive. That timing is why two or three honest diagnostic sessions before the deadline are the highest-value maths work available in the whole Diploma: they cost a fraction of a year of tutoring and they prevent two years spent in the wrong course.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send maths tutors to homes in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Maths sessions are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For this subject the format genuinely suits the work: the student writes on paper with the camera angled at the page, the tutor watches each line appear and catches a sign error as it happens, and nobody adds a journey to an evening that already started late because of a commute.

faqs.question: What makes a mathematical exploration fail?
faqs.answer: Almost always topic choice. Students pick something interesting and find six weeks later that it contains very little mathematics at the right level, or they pick something so ambitious that the mathematics cannot be handled properly in the space available. Both are visible in the first fortnight to anybody who asks to see the actual mathematics that will be done and at what level. The second common failure is treating the write-up as a formality, when notation, structure, personal engagement and a genuine discussion of limitations all carry marks.

faqs.question: How much can a tutor help with the exploration?
faqs.answer: With the thinking and the technique, a great deal; with the writing, nothing. A tutor can help narrow a topic until the mathematics is appropriate and achievable, teach the techniques the investigation needs, advise on handling real data, and respond to the student's own draft with the questions a moderator would ask next. A tutor must never write, draft, rewrite or supply any part of it. Your child's school supervisor sets the rules for permitted support, and their internal deadlines are what the plan should be built backwards from.

faqs.question: Why does one paper not allow a calculator?
faqs.answer: Because it is examining something different. In Analysis and Approaches one paper is sat without technology, which tests algebraic fluency, exact-form working and confident manipulation directly rather than through a device. The practical consequence is that revision has to include deliberate non-calculator practice, which students avoid because it is uncomfortable. A student who has spent two years with a calculator within reach and then meets that paper for the first time in the hall is not under-prepared on content; they are under-practised on the exact skill being examined.

faqs.question: What is the extra higher level paper, and how is it revised for?
faqs.answer: Higher level students sit an additional problem-solving component that asks for sustained work on longer, less familiar problems rather than recall of a technique. It is the paper most students have practised least, partly because it is hard to self-study: the skill it tests is making progress when the route is not obvious, and that improves through attempting exactly those problems under time with somebody who can point out where the entry point was missed. It rewards persistence more than content coverage, which is why it is worth deliberate practice.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks when the final answer is right?
faqs.answer: Usually notation or missing working. In mathematics the notation is content: a function without its domain, an integral without its variable, a loosely written inequality. Examiners mark what is on the page. The other common cause is exact form and accuracy instructions, where a question asking for an exact answer and receiving a decimal is simply wrong. Both are mechanical to fix and hold under pressure, which is why a short technique block often moves a grade faster than another pass through a topic does.

faqs.question: Our child did well in IGCSE maths and is struggling in the first Diploma year. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma assumes something IGCSE did not require: sustained multi-step reasoning and written justification of each step. IGCSE rewards technique applied to a signposted question. The Diploma asks for a route to be chosen and for the reasoning to be visible, and higher level assumes algebraic manipulation is automatic from the first week rather than something to be worked out. The content gap is usually modest and the expectation gap is real, which is why the first useful session is diagnostic rather than a march through topics.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking before the Diploma?
faqs.answer: If the main IGCSE grade is already secure and higher level maths is the plan, yes. Cambridge 0606 brings calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities forward by a year, which removes most of the shock of the first higher level Diploma term. If it is competing for revision time with a main grade that is not yet safe, it is a liability rather than insurance, and the honest advice is to drop it. The decision is about the security of the main grade, not about ambition.

faqs.question: When should a commuting student book maths sessions?
faqs.answer: Weekdays from 17:30, in sixty-minute blocks rather than ninety, and weekend mornings for anything long. Students travelling from this district to Diploma schools across the Creek or towards Festival City are usually home between 16:00 and 17:00, and after food the usable window starts later than parents expect. Weekend mornings are the most productive slot available for whole papers and exploration work, because nothing competes and the student is not already tired from a journey. They are also consistently the least requested.

faqs.question: How many sessions does the final term usually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families expect, if the work is the right work. In the final term the productive activity is whole papers under time, marked against the published scheme, with every lost mark categorised and the tally driving the next session. That can be weekly rather than twice weekly for most students. The one firm rule is that the last fortnight introduces nothing new, because new content displaces revision of material the student half-knows, which is where the recoverable marks actually are.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB examination dates for maths?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The International Baccalaureate's own site is the authoritative source for session and results dates, and it should be checked directly or through your school's IB coordinator. We will say that UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, because that is stable. Publishing a specific date that later changes would be worse than publishing nothing, particularly on a page a parent might read a year after it was written. The dates that actually govern a student's year are the school's own exploration and coursework deadlines in any case.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tutoring cost for a family in Deira?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB specialists quoted from about AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the journey sits inside the fee. Monthly estimates from the Bestimate Dubai table run about AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-band weekly support and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an examination year. Those are market figures with sources rather than our price list; we quote after the free trial.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingHeading: Tell us the point in the course, not just the subject
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingBody: Diploma maths support is priced by timing. Two sessions before the option block closes can change which course a student spends two years in. A term of weekly work in the first year prevents the crisis that otherwise arrives in the second. Exploration coaching in the first fortnight of a project saves the whole thing. Paper work in the final term recovers technique marks and nothing else. Send us the year group, the route, the level and either a marked script or the exploration brief, and we will tell you which of those four you need and what we would not sell you. The trial lesson is free. Everything runs one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-international-ci.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level, plus the MYP mathematics that leads into them and exploration coaching on the student's own work.

intro.heading: Does anyone reachable actually know this syllabus?
paragraphs: This is the honest version of the question families in these clusters are asking, and the honest answer has two parts. First: within a short drive of International City, probably not. There is no IB World School inside the district, the nearest Diploma teaching is in Silicon Oasis with Al Warqa and Mirdif beyond, and the people who teach Diploma mathematics in Dubai mostly live near the schools that employ them. A proximity search here returns availability rather than specification knowledge.

Second: across the emirate and online, yes, but you should verify it rather than take it on trust. 'IB maths' describes four different qualifications. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led, with induction, complex numbers and vectors at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Each runs at two levels, examined separately, and a tutor strong in one can be genuinely out of their depth in another.

Nobody can tell which is which from a profile, which is why this page is built around verification instead of claims. There are four or five questions that distinguish somebody who teaches your child's exact course from somebody who did a mathematics degree and is willing. They take two minutes, any competent tutor answers them without hesitation, and they work just as well on us as on anybody else.

The questions matter more than usual in this market because some of the credential language used here does not survive checking. Tutors described as approved by KHDA, when that permit is issued to training institutes with premises. Examiner status asserted without evidence. Star ratings published with no countable reviews behind them. One competitor publishes two different ratings on the same page. These are not small things when you are handing somebody a two-year qualification.

IB Gram delivers mathematics tuition online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service - and for this subject in this district that is the arrangement that makes a specialist reachable at all. We also publish what we are not, further down, because a page that only lists strengths is not telling you enough to decide.

There is a second reason to insist on verification rather than reputation. Mathematics is the subject where a mismatch hides longest, because early Higher Level teaching overlaps with Standard Level content and the gap only appears when the genuinely harder material arrives. By then a term has gone and the household has paid for it. Two minutes of questions at the start is the cheapest insurance available in this market. What follows is practical. The verification questions and what good answers sound like. The four combinations and what each one demands. Which claims to distrust and how to check them. What a diagnostic session should tell you within an hour. And an honest statement of which mathematics combinations we cannot always staff.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-international-ci.programmesIntro: Four points at which mathematics help is asked for from these clusters, each needing a different kind of tutor.

programmes.name: MYP mathematics
programmes.description: Graded 1 to 8 against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the usual weak point, because generalising a rule in correct notation and then justifying it is rarely taught directly. A competent generalist can teach this well.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where verification matters least, because the work is skill-building rather than specification-specific. It is also where the local tutor pool is deepest. If your child is in the Middle Years Programme, the criterion breakdown from the school matters far more than the tutor's Diploma credentials.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and statistics across two papers plus the exploration. Demanding for a student who was comfortable rather than strong in Middle Years mathematics, mainly because it assumes prior fluency and moves quickly. Verification matters here: a general mathematics tutor will cope with the content and miss the examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: The most commonly requested combination from this district, and the presenting problem is almost always the same: the content makes sense in lessons and collapses in tests. That is method and timing rather than comprehension, and one marked paper identifies it. Ask any prospective tutor what they would look for in that paper before they answer.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
programmes.description: Everything at Standard Level plus proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and considerably heavier calculus. Three papers rather than two. The usual requirement for engineering, mathematics and physics degrees, and the combination where a mismatched tutor is most quickly exposed.
programmes.countryNote: This is the hardest mathematics combination to find within reach of these clusters and the one where online matching makes the most difference. It is also the one we most often cannot staff at short notice, particularly in the weeks around mock examinations. We say so at the enquiry stage rather than offering a Standard Level tutor instead.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation, SL and HL
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics, probability and technology use, with matrices, graph theory and deeper statistical inference at Higher Level. Not an easier course, a different one: less algebraic manipulation, far more interpretation. The characteristic failure is a correct calculation with nothing said about what it means.
programmes.countryNote: Verification is particularly worth doing for Applications and Interpretation, because many mathematics graduates have never taught graph theory or transition matrices and will say yes to the subject name without knowing the content. Ask specifically which Higher Level topics they have taught, and listen for whether the answer contains the words the syllabus uses.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-international-ci.subjectsIntro: The topics to name when you are testing whether a tutor knows the course, with what each actually demands.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency and manipulation
subjects.description: Indices, surds, algebraic fractions, rearranging and factorising without hesitation. The foundation everything else stands on. A student who does these slowly cannot complete the rest of a paper in the time available, whatever they understand.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, and the effect of each transformation on a graph. Examination questions combine two or three transformations at once, which defeats students who memorised rules rather than understanding them.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, optimisation and kinematics, with implicit differentiation and related rates at Higher Level. Marks go on optimisation answers where the stationary point is found and never classified as a maximum.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, areas and volumes of revolution, with substitution, integration by parts and partial fractions at Higher Level. Lost marks cluster on limits, the omitted constant, and the wrong variable of integration.

subjects.name: Proof, including induction
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, counterexample and proof by mathematical induction. Heavily examined and heavily botched: the inductive step asserted rather than derived and the conclusion omitted. Formulaic enough to teach reliably in a few sessions.

subjects.name: Complex numbers and vectors
subjects.description: Cartesian, polar and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem, and vector geometry including lines and planes. Marks go on argument conventions and on diagrams students do not draw. A useful topic to name when testing a tutor's depth.

subjects.name: Statistics, probability and distributions
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous distributions, the binomial and normal, correlation and regression. The heart of Applications and Interpretation. Lost marks concentrate on conditional probability and on conclusions stated without the question's context.

subjects.name: Modelling and interpretation
subjects.description: Choosing a model, fitting it and saying what it means. The computation is rarely the problem. A student who writes a regression gradient without a sentence on what it represents has forfeited the marks separating the top bands.

subjects.name: Matrices, eigenvalues and transition matrices
subjects.description: Matrix operations, eigenvalues, and transition matrices applied to long-run behaviour. Unfamiliar to many mathematics graduates who have never taught the course, which makes it one of the sharpest verification topics available to a parent.

subjects.name: Graph theory
subjects.description: Minimum spanning trees, shortest path, Chinese postman and travelling salesman problems. Highly teachable because the question types repeat, and almost never encountered by somebody who has not taught Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual exploration of 12 to 20 pages worth 20 marks against five criteria. Coaching covers topic viability, structure, mathematical communication and reflection. The student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes every word.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: Which paper permits the calculator and what it is legitimately for. Central in Applications and Interpretation; a tool in Analysis and Approaches that must not replace analytic method. Solving numerically, finding intersections, distributions, storing values to avoid rounding error.

sections.heading: Five questions that establish whether a tutor knows the course
paragraphs: These take two minutes and they are the most useful thing on this page. Ask them of any prospective tutor, including us. What you are listening for is not confidence but specificity: whether the answer uses the vocabulary the syllabus uses, and whether it distinguishes the four combinations rather than treating 'IB maths' as one subject.

Start with the simplest discriminator. Ask which of the four combinations they have taught and how many cohorts of each. A tutor who teaches Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level will say so and will usually volunteer which topics they find students struggle with. A tutor who answers 'all of them' without elaboration, or who does not distinguish the two courses, has told you something.

Then ask something only a course teacher would know. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, what they look for in a proof-by-induction answer, and where students lose the marks. For Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, how they teach transition matrices or the Chinese postman problem. Those are not trick questions; they are ordinary parts of the course that somebody who has not taught it will not have encountered.

The last two questions are about the exploration and the mark scheme. Ask which criterion carries the most marks in the exploration, and ask what they would look for in one marked past paper before planning anything. The first has a factual answer. The second separates a tutor who diagnoses from one who delivers a prepared course, and that distinction decides whether the first six sessions are targeted or generic.

sections.heading: Credential claims in this market that do not survive checking
paragraphs: Some of the language used to sell tutoring in Dubai means something specific, and some of it means nothing at all. Knowing which is which is worth more than any amount of browsing, and it applies to every provider in these results including this one.

The most common is approval by KHDA. KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that have premises and staff in the emirate. It does not approve or license individual private tutors - that is MoHRE's permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. A provider describing its tutors as approved by the authority is either misunderstanding the system or referring to a permit it should be able to show you.

The second is examiner status. An individual's current examiner status is not something a parent can verify independently, and it should not be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, which it does not confer. If examiner experience is being offered as a reason to pay more, ask what specifically it changes about the teaching, and treat a vague answer as the answer.

The third is ratings. One competitor publishes two different aggregate ratings on the same page; another shows a five-star average from twenty reviews beside a claim of a claim of several thousand students. Self-asserted review markup that does not match a visible, countable set of dated reviews is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. We publish no rating we cannot evidence that way.

sections.heading: The four combinations, and what each one actually needs
paragraphs: Before verifying anybody, establish what you are verifying them against. Get the course name and level from the Diploma coordinator in writing: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. Families in these clusters compare notes across schools constantly, and because school provision varies, two students in the same building can be taking different mathematics with nothing in common.

Analysis and Approaches needs a tutor comfortable with algebraic manipulation, calculus technique and proof, who teaches method presentation as a subject in its own right. The characteristic student problem is understanding the mathematics and losing method marks, so the tutor's value is in habits: working shown, rounding controlled, stationary points classified, vectors sketched.

Applications and Interpretation needs a tutor comfortable with statistics, modelling and the interpretive writing the mark scheme rewards, and at Higher Level with matrices and graph theory. The characteristic student problem is computing correctly and saying nothing about meaning, so the tutor's value is in teaching a sentence structure that connects a number to the context.

At Higher Level in either course the additional content is substantial rather than decorative, and a Standard Level tutor will not cover it adequately. That is the mismatch most likely to go undetected for a term, because early Higher Level teaching overlaps with Standard Level content and the gap appears later. It is also why the proof-by-induction and transition-matrix questions above are worth asking before the first session rather than after the third.

sections.heading: What one diagnostic session should tell you
paragraphs: A first session that teaches is a wasted first session. The hour should establish which of three things is wrong, because they lead to completely different plans and the wrong plan costs a term. The three are a content gap, a method habit, and a timing problem - and most students have one dominant cause rather than all three.

The method is simple and any competent tutor will do it: have the student work through questions at the correct level while the tutor watches, then mark a timed paper properly against the published mark scheme, writing down the reason for each lost mark. Marks lost with correct final answers point to method. Marks lost on one topic point to content. Marks lost in the final third of the paper point to pacing.

What you should receive afterwards is a written note, not a verbal reassurance. The three or four recurring reasons, what the first six sessions will target, and an honest statement of what that is likely to achieve. We publish no predicted grades and offer no guarantees, because nobody can honour either, and a realistic range with reasoning is a more useful document than a promise.

If the diagnosis says the problem is not teaching - that the student is not doing the work the school already sets, or that the difficulty is organisational - the right answer is to say so and not take the booking. That happens often enough to be worth stating, and for a household in these clusters already spending ten hours a week on a commute, being told the truth early is worth more than a package.

sections.heading: Testing an exploration topic before the student commits
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is worth 20 marks against five criteria, and the criterion carrying the most - use of mathematics, with six - depends almost entirely on a decision made before any writing: whether the chosen topic contains mathematics commensurate with the course. A topic that reduces to arithmetic and a graph cannot score well there however neatly it is presented.

So the highest-leverage half hour in the whole exploration is a viability conversation. Does the topic require mathematics at the level of the course? Can the student obtain or generate data if data is involved? Is there a result to reflect on, or does the work simply describe something? Can the whole thing be done in 12 to 20 pages without either padding or compression?

The table below sets out the test we apply. It is deliberately blunt, because the commonest outcome of skipping it is a student three weeks in with a topic that cannot score, and three weeks is not recoverable when the deadline collides with mock examinations and the Extended Essay in the second year.

On the boundary: the student chooses the topic, does the mathematics and writes every word. The tutor tests viability, explains the criteria, questions the structure and comments on drafts. One operator competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments at a published price; a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate, which in this case is a sixteen or seventeen year old.

sections.heading: Fitting mathematics into a week that includes a long commute
paragraphs: A Diploma student travelling from these clusters to Silicon Oasis or Mirdif loses something like ten hours a week to the journey. Mathematics is unusually sensitive to that, because the subject rewards short frequent practice rather than long sessions, and short frequent practice needs a student who is not exhausted.

The arrangement that works is one fixed weekday session from about six, with a named evening for the practice it sets, plus a weekend morning when a full timed paper is possible. A full mathematics paper plus the mark-scheme walkthrough takes two to three hours, and that is not available on a weekday evening at any price. Students who sit one a week through the final term practise the examination rather than revising for it.

There is a specific mathematical reason to protect the practice slot rather than the session. Method habits - working shown, rounding controlled, stationary points classified - change through repetition rather than through explanation. A session that explains them and is followed by no practice has moved nothing. Twenty minutes of questions on three evenings beats one long sitting at the weekend for this particular purpose.

In Ramadan the pattern should change deliberately. The school day shortens so the bus returns earlier, but late-afternoon concentration is poor and a mathematics session at four is often wasted. Weekend mornings and post-Iftar slots work. Because no tutor is travelling, changing the pattern is a scheduling decision, and it should be fixed before the month starts rather than renegotiated weekly.

sections.heading: What mathematics tutoring costs, and which band holds what
paragraphs: Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram rate. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For Middle Years mathematics that band contains usable help. For Higher Level Analysis and Approaches it very rarely does, and that is the most useful thing to know about it.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. IB specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutors reach AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and advertised home-tutor rates at 200 to 500.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, which is useful context for a household budgeting both.

The verification questions matter precisely because the rate does not tell you what you are getting. Paying AED 300 an hour for somebody who cannot teach proof by induction is worse value than paying AED 200 for somebody who can, and the price alone will never reveal which is which. That is the whole argument of this page.

sections.heading: What we cannot always staff, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the fortnight either side of mock examinations is the combination we most often cannot staff properly, because demand across the emirate concentrates on the same specialists in the same weeks. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is generally available but takes longer to match than Standard Level. Middle Years mathematics is straightforward within days.

When we cannot cover a combination well, there are three honest responses and we use all three: a realistic wait, adjacent support with the boundary stated plainly, or a refusal. The one thing we will not do is put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate, because the mismatch takes a term to surface and by then the year has gone.

What we do not claim, stated plainly. No office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. No KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the permit issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. No approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. No guaranteed grades and no published predicted scores. No star ratings we cannot evidence with countable, dated reviews. No syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes supplied as downloads - we cite and link the official sources.

And on the regulators themselves, since the claim language above depends on them: KHDA oversees private education quality in Dubai, ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. All of them regulate schools. None licenses an individual tutor.

faqs.question: Is there anyone near International City who knows the IB maths syllabus?
faqs.answer: Within a short drive, probably not. There is no IB World School in the district, the nearest Diploma teaching is in Silicon Oasis with Al Warqa and Mirdif beyond, and the people who teach Diploma mathematics in Dubai generally live near the schools employing them. Across the emirate and online, yes - but verify rather than trust. The five questions on this page take two minutes and distinguish somebody who teaches your child's exact course from a mathematics graduate who is available.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a tutor really teaches Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Ask what they look for in a proof-by-induction answer and where students lose the marks. A tutor who teaches the course will describe the base case, the inductive step being derived rather than asserted, and the conclusion being stated - and will usually volunteer that students omit the last of those. Somebody who has not taught it will speak vaguely about showing it works for the next case. It is ordinary course content, not a trick question.

faqs.question: What is the equivalent test for Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Ask how they teach transition matrices or the Chinese postman problem. Many mathematics graduates have never encountered either, because both belong specifically to Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level rather than to a general mathematics education. A tutor who teaches the course will describe the question types and the long-run behaviour reasoning. Somebody who says yes to the subject name and cannot discuss the content has answered your real question.

faqs.question: A tutoring company says its tutors are approved by the Dubai authority. Is that real?
faqs.answer: Probably not in the way it sounds. KHDA regulates private schools in Dubai and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes that have premises and staff in the emirate. It does not approve or license individual private tutors - that is the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask for the permit and the premises address. IB Gram holds no such permit and has no UAE premises.

faqs.question: Is examiner experience worth a higher hourly rate for IB maths?
faqs.answer: Ask what it changes about the teaching, specifically, and treat a vague answer as the answer. A parent cannot independently verify an individual's current examiner appointment, and examiner status confers no access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. It may indicate familiarity with mark schemes, which is genuinely useful - but so does being able to walk a student through one, which you can test directly in a trial lesson for nothing.

faqs.question: Which exploration criterion carries the most marks?
faqs.answer: Use of mathematics, with six of the twenty. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four each, and personal engagement and reflection three each. That split is the most actionable fact about the task, because it means the topic choice - made before any writing - determines the largest single allocation. A topic that reduces to arithmetic and one graph cannot score well on use of mathematics however neatly the report is produced.

faqs.question: How do we know an exploration topic will work before starting?
faqs.answer: Test five things. Does the topic require techniques from your child's own course, or does it reduce to arithmetic? Is the data obtainable, or would it have to be invented? Is there a result that can be questioned and evaluated, or only a description? Can it be done properly in 12 to 20 pages? And can your child explain why they chose it? Half an hour on those questions prevents the commonest failure in the task.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a maths tutor actually do?
faqs.answer: Diagnose, not teach. The hour should establish which of three causes dominates: a content gap, a method habit, or a timing problem. The method is to watch the student work at the correct level and then mark a timed paper against the published mark scheme, writing down the reason for every lost mark. Marks lost with correct final answers mean method; marks lost on one topic mean content; marks lost in the last third mean pacing.

faqs.question: My son understands maths but his test marks are poor. What is that?
faqs.answer: Almost always method, and it is the most common presenting problem from this district. The specific habits are working omitted so a correct answer scores one mark out of four, rounding applied at an intermediate step so later accuracy marks fall, stationary points found but never classified, vector questions attempted without a sketch, and the final long question abandoned rather than attempted for partial credit. One marked timed paper names his three or four reasons.

faqs.question: Can a Standard Level tutor teach my daughter at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Not adequately, and this is the mismatch most likely to go undetected for a term. Early Higher Level teaching overlaps with Standard Level content, so the gap does not appear immediately - it appears when proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors and the heavier integration arrive, or when matrices and graph theory do in Applications and Interpretation. Ask which level they have taught and for how many cohorts before the first session rather than after the third.

faqs.question: How does the commute affect maths tutoring from these clusters?
faqs.answer: Mathematics rewards short frequent practice, and short frequent practice needs a student who is not exhausted. From International City a Diploma student loses around ten hours a week to travel, so the arrangement that works is one fixed weekday session from about six, a named evening for the questions it sets, and a weekend morning when a full timed paper is possible. Method habits change through repetition, so protecting the practice slot matters more than lengthening the session.

faqs.question: What does Diploma maths tutoring cost here, and does price indicate quality?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200; IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270; premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650, with BartyED at AED 650. Price does not indicate course knowledge. Paying AED 300 for somebody who cannot teach proof by induction is worse value than AED 200 for somebody who can, and only the questions reveal which.

faqs.question: Are the star ratings on tutoring sites reliable?
faqs.answer: Treat them sceptically unless the reviews themselves are visible, countable and dated. One competitor in this market publishes two different aggregate ratings on the same page; another shows a five-star average from twenty reviews beside a claim of a claim of several thousand students. Self-asserted review markup that does not match a visible set of real reviews is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. We publish none we cannot evidence that way.

faqs.question: Is a permit required for private maths tuition in these clusters?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask to see it; somebody who holds one shows it without hesitation.

faqs.answer: We say so at the enquiry stage. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the fortnight either side of mock examinations is the hardest combination on our list, because demand across the emirate concentrates on the same specialists in the same weeks. In that case you get a realistic wait, or adjacent support with the boundary stated plainly, or a refusal. What you will not get is a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level candidate.

intro.heading: Four problems, one subject, and the hour the school run leaves open
paragraphs: Families in JBR do not ring about mathematics in general. They ring because something specific has gone wrong, and in two years of Diploma teaching it is nearly always one of four things. The student can do the work with a calculator and falls apart on Paper 1. The student is at Higher Level and has met Paper 3, which asks two long problems that reward sustained argument rather than recall. The exploration is due and the research question cannot be answered mathematically. Or the student is in the wrong course, having chosen Applications and Interpretation to avoid algebra and discovered algebra inside the modelling questions.

Each of those has a different fix and they are not interchangeable. Paper 1 technique is drilling written method until a student stops reaching for a graphic display calculator they are not allowed. Paper 3 is teaching a student to stay inside one problem for twenty minutes without panicking at part (d). The exploration is a question-design problem dressed up as a writing problem. The course mismatch is a decision about whether to move, and that decision has a deadline attached in most Dubai schools. A tutor matched to the subject heading rather than the component will spend four sessions working out which of these you have.

The second constraint on this page is geography, and it is specific. There is no IB World School inside the JBR towers. Students travel outward: to Al Sufouh and the Media City edge on a short run, to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South on a longer one, out to the villa belt around Emirates Hills and The Meadows on the longest. A maths hour is the worst hour in the week to put at the end of a long commute, because the subject needs working memory rather than attention, and a student who has sat on a bus until 16:40 has neither. Timing is not an administrative detail in this subject. It is part of the teaching plan.

There are four mathematics courses, not one. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation each run at Standard and Higher Level, with roughly 150 and 240 recommended teaching hours respectively. All four share five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. All four carry an exploration worth 20 per cent of the grade. Beyond that they diverge sharply, and the divergence starts with whether a calculator is permitted in Paper 1, which it is not in either Analysis course.

So this page does four jobs. It sets the four courses side by side so you can see which one your child is in and what it actually demands. It explains the route choice and where to verify what a degree programme requires rather than guessing. It names where marks go missing, topic by topic. And it schedules honestly around a JBR afternoon. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: Mathematics is the subject a JBR child is assessed on continuously from age five to eighteen, and the handover points are where difficulty accumulates. These are the four stages and what maths support is actually for at each.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Mathematics in the PYP sits inside units of inquiry rather than in a numbered syllabus, and there is no external examination. Number sense, fact fluency and the ability to explain a method out loud are what matter, and all three are visible to a parent long before a report is. Support at this stage is short, frequent and practical rather than remedial in any examination sense.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai primary schools serve a highly mobile population, so a JBR child may arrive having been taught column methods one way in one country and another way here. That mismatch, not ability, is what produces most apparent weakness in a Year 4 or Year 5 arriving mid-year. It is also the cheapest thing on this page to fix, and the one most often left until secondary school.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where most students lose the most, because it asks for a generalisation and a justification rather than a correct answer. Students who are quick at arithmetic routinely score lowest here.
programmes.countryNote: Around JBR the MYP competes with IGCSE for the same two years, and the maths consequence is real. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP mathematics has met investigation and justification; one arriving from IGCSE has met speed and accuracy under timing. The first group struggles with Paper 1 pace, the second with the exploration. Knowing which gap you have saves a term of general revision.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: One mathematics course is compulsory, chosen from Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Each is graded one to seven. The written papers carry 80 per cent and the exploration 20. At Higher Level the written load splits across three papers rather than two, with Paper 3 asking two extended problems worth 20 per cent of the total.
programmes.countryNote: This is the course almost every maths enquiry from a JBR address concerns. Dubai schools sit the May session, so the exploration deadline falls in the middle of DP2, typically weeks away from two or three other internal assessments. Families who treat the exploration as a DP1 summer task rather than a DP2 crisis get a better piece of work and a calmer final term.

programmes.name: Pre-Diploma and IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Many JBR students reach the Diploma through IGCSE rather than the MYP, sitting Cambridge 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. The choice matters for what follows: 0607 embeds graphical-calculator work and an investigation style closer to the IB, while 0580 Extended now includes a non-calculator paper that prepares a student well for Analysis Paper 1.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Al Barsha and the villa belt that run IGCSE then offer the Diploma usually publish a minimum IGCSE grade for Higher Level mathematics entry. That threshold is the real decision point for a JBR family, and it is set in Year 11 rather than at the start of DP1, which means the useful tutoring window is earlier than most parents assume.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Mathematics enquiries from JBR split across four courses and one component, and they arrive bundled with the subjects whose grades depend on maths. Below are the ten combinations we are asked for most, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each 90 minutes and each worth 40 per cent, plus the exploration at 20. The characteristic failure is a student who is fluent with technology and insecure on written algebra, which Paper 1 exposes immediately. Differentiation, trigonometric identities and algebraic manipulation under time pressure are where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each 120 minutes and each 30 per cent, Paper 3 at 60 minutes and 20 per cent, and the exploration at 20. Paper 3 sets two extended problems and is the component most students meet unprepared. Proof by induction, complex numbers and the harder calculus are the recurring trouble spots.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Both papers permit a calculator, each 90 minutes at 40 per cent, with the exploration at 20. Statistics, modelling and financial mathematics carry much more weight than in Analysis. Students chose it to avoid algebra and then meet algebra inside the modelling questions, which is why the apparent easy option often produces the same grade as the harder course would have.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Three papers as in Analysis Higher Level, calculator permitted throughout. The content includes matrices, graph theory, Voronoi diagrams and a demanding statistics strand, and the Paper 3 problems are long modelling investigations. It is not a soft Higher Level, and students who arrive expecting one lose ground in the first term of DP2.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematics written up over roughly twelve to twenty pages and marked out of 20 across five criteria. The most common fault is a research question that cannot be answered with the mathematics the student actually knows. The second is thin reflection, criterion D, which is worth three marks and is usually written in the final hour.

subjects.name: Higher Level Physics, where maths is the limiting factor
subjects.description: A substantial number of Physics enquiries from this neighbourhood are maths problems in disguise: rearranging, logarithms, gradients and the calculus inside the fields and circular motion topics. Fixing the mathematics usually moves the Physics grade more than another hour of Physics content does, which is worth testing before buying two tutors.

subjects.name: Economics HL, the quantitative paper
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics includes a quantitative paper that catches students who chose the subject expecting essays. The mathematics involved is not advanced, but it is unfamiliar in an economics context: elasticities, calculations around taxes and subsidies, and interpreting a diagram numerically rather than descriptively.

subjects.name: Chemistry calculation strands
subjects.description: Mole calculations, titration arithmetic, equilibrium and energetics sign conventions. Students who are secure in mathematics and insecure in chemistry present differently from students who are insecure in both, and the second group benefits from maths support before chemistry support. Diagnosing which one you have is a single session of work.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The mathematics appears in complexity, in abstract data structures at Higher Level and in the logic underlying the written papers. Students write functioning code and then lose marks in the developed-solution documentation, where the criteria sit. Support here is usually part mathematics, part structured technical writing.

subjects.name: MYP mathematics, criterion B
subjects.description: Investigating patterns, assessed out of eight, asking for a general rule and a justification rather than a worked answer. It is the criterion that most reliably separates a strong MYP mathematician from a fast one, and it is also the best possible preparation for the Diploma exploration two years later.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: For a mathematics session the only local fact that matters is what time the student is home and able to think. These notes set out the school runs JBR families actually make and what each one does to the weekday window.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and the Media City edge
regions.note: The shortest run from the towers, and the only one in this set where a 16:15 maths session is routinely workable. Families here can keep a weekday hour and an after-school activity in the same afternoon, which is why their Paper 1 drilling stays consistent through DP2.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where most JBR Diploma students study, and the run that matters most to a maths timetable. The return leg coincides with the wider Al Barsha exodus, so 16:45 is the earliest honest start and non-calculator practice is better placed at a weekend.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Across Al Mamsha Street on the same tram line and mostly the same buses, so Marina and JBR students share session windows almost exactly. The practical difference is parking rather than timing, and for an online maths hour parking is not a factor at all.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: A highway crossing away, which adds minutes at the worst possible point of the afternoon. JLT students attending the same Al Barsha schools as JBR students generally start fifteen minutes later, and that fifteen minutes is the difference between a rested Paper 1 session and a wasted one.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: The villa belt, with several Diploma schools and the longest commutes from JBR. For Higher Level mathematics these households do markedly better with a weekend double session than with two tired weekday hours, because Paper 3 work needs an unbroken stretch.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Newer schools absorbing New Dubai demand, with a return leg that runs against the afternoon flow and therefore holds its timing better than the morning run. A 16:45 maths start here is more reliable than the raw distance suggests.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: JBR timings plus one bridge. The bridge is the variable that turns a dependable weekday slot into an unpredictable one on a busy afternoon, which argues for booking the session fifteen minutes later rather than hoping.

regions.name: Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Established schools with long IGCSE histories feeding both A Level and the Diploma. Students coming into DP1 maths from these schools usually arrive with strong written method and need the exploration and investigation habits rather than more algebra.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South: the main Diploma destination
schoolClusters.note: Most JBR students taking IB mathematics study here, and the practical consequence for a maths plan is that non-calculator work should not be scheduled at the end of a 45-minute return leg. Weekend mornings carry Paper 1 and Paper 3 practice far better than weekday evenings do.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh, Media City and the short commute
schoolClusters.note: The one cluster where a weekday maths hour genuinely works at 16:15. Students here lose less of the afternoon to travel and can hold a consistent weekly slot across both Diploma years, which matters more for mathematics than for any other subject.

schoolClusters.city: The villa belt and Jumeirah Village
schoolClusters.note: Longer runs, larger cohorts and often broader option structures. Higher Level mathematics students from these schools tend to need an unbroken stretch for Paper 3 work, which is why weekend sessions dominate here from the January of DP2 onwards.

sections.heading: Four courses, not one: which maths is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in JBR needs to know the answer to this before anything else, and a surprising number of parents cannot give it. There are four courses. Analysis and Approaches at Standard and at Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard and at Higher Level. They share five topics and they share an exploration worth 20 per cent, and after that they part company on the things that decide a grade.

The sharpest difference is the calculator. In both Analysis courses, Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator. In both Applications courses, every paper permits one. That single rule changes what a student must be able to do with a pen, and it is the reason a student who scores well in school tests can collapse in a Paper 1 mock. The second difference is structure: Standard Level sits two papers at 40 per cent each, Higher Level sits three, with Paper 3 running an hour and carrying 20 per cent on two extended problems.

Content weighting is the third difference and the least understood. Analysis leans on algebra, functions, trigonometry and calculus. Applications leans on statistics, modelling, financial mathematics and, at Higher Level, matrices and graph theory. Neither is a soft option; they are differently shaped. A student who dislikes proof and enjoys data is genuinely better served by Applications, and a student who chose Applications to avoid algebra has usually made a mistake they will discover in the modelling questions.

Read the table below against your child's timetable and, if there is any doubt, against the school's course outline. Getting this one fact right is worth more than the first three tutoring sessions, because the four courses need four different teachers and the teaching sequence is not transferable between them.

sections.heading: Analysis or Applications, and where to check what a degree actually requires
paragraphs: This is the decision that most often brings a JBR family to a maths tutor, and it is usually framed wrongly. The question parents ask is which course is easier. The question that matters is which course the student can perform in across two years, and which one the intended degree route will accept. Those are two separate checks and both have to be done before the school's internal switching deadline, which in most Dubai schools falls early in DP1.

On the performance side, the diagnostic is quick. Give the student a Paper 1 question from Analysis and a modelling question from Applications, both unseen, and watch which one they can start. A student who cannot begin an algebraic manipulation without a calculator will find Analysis Paper 1 punishing for two years. A student who finds statistics tedious and proof interesting will find Applications a long slog for the same grade. One session of honest diagnosis is cheaper than a year in the wrong course.

On the admissions side, be careful with what you read on tutoring sites, including the claims made about UAE universities. Faculty requirements change, they differ by programme rather than by institution, and several UAE universities publish their mathematics expectations only inside the programme page. The reliable method is to open the admissions page for the specific degree at the specific university and read the mathematics line, then confirm it with the school's university counselling office. Engineering, physics and economics programmes are the ones where the course choice is most likely to be specified; business, life sciences and humanities programmes are generally more flexible.

The table sets out how to run that check by route rather than asserting what any named university requires. Treat the right-hand column as the instruction: verify, in writing, for the specific programme, before the switching deadline passes.

sections.heading: The five topics and how they land across the papers
paragraphs: All four courses are built from the same five topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. What differs is the proportion of teaching time each gets and the depth to which it is taken. A parent who knows this can read a school report usefully for the first time, because a comment about weakness in functions means something specific about which papers will suffer.

The practical point is that topics do not map neatly onto papers. A single Paper 2 question may require a function, a derivative and a statistical interpretation in sequence, and the mark is lost at whichever of the three the student cannot do. This is why topic-by-topic revision produces less improvement than mixed practice under timing, and why a tutor who only works through the textbook chapter the school is on is teaching the course rather than the examination.

The exploration draws on the same five topics and on nothing outside them, which is a constraint most students find out too late. A research question requiring mathematics beyond the course cannot earn high marks on criterion E, use of mathematics, because the assessment rewards mathematics commensurate with the level, correctly applied, not mathematics that is impressive and shaky. Choosing a question inside the five topics is the single best decision available in the exploration.

Read the table as a diagnostic rather than a syllabus. If a school report says one of these topics is weak, the right-hand column tells you which component will show it first and therefore what the tutoring hour should be doing.
