sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Marks leave in predictable places and almost none of them are a failure of intelligence. The largest single loss at Standard Level is written algebraic method in Analysis Paper 1, where a student who has done two years of work on a graphic display calculator cannot manipulate confidently with a pen. The loss is not partial; a question begun wrongly earns nothing, and Paper 1 is 40 per cent of the Standard Level grade and 30 per cent at Higher.

The second loss is command-term reading. Show that, hence, verify and deduce each require something specific, and hence in particular means the previous part must be used. Students who ignore that word solve the question again from first principles, run out of time and lose method marks they had already earned. A tutor can teach this in two sessions and it transfers across every paper.

The third is Paper 3 abandonment at Higher Level. The paper sets two long problems built in escalating parts, and the student who stops at part (d) because it looks unfamiliar leaves the remaining parts, which are often more accessible, untouched. Practising Paper 3 in isolated fragments teaches exactly the wrong habit. It has to be sat at full length, repeatedly, until staying in the problem is automatic.

The fourth is the exploration, and specifically criteria C and D, personal engagement and reflection, worth three marks each. They are written last, in a hurry, and they are the cheapest marks on the whole paper to secure if they are planned first. A student who records why the question interested them and what they would do differently as they go has those six marks largely banked before the mathematics is finished.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, two usually thrown away
paragraphs: The exploration is 20 per cent of the grade in all four courses, written up over roughly twelve to twenty pages, and marked out of 20 across five criteria. It is the component where a tutor adds most value and also the one where the boundary between help and malpractice has to be stated explicitly, so both things belong in the same section.

The criteria are presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries six marks and is the only criterion where level matters: the mathematics must be commensurate with the course and correctly applied. Presentation and mathematical communication carry four each and are about structure, notation and whether a reader can follow the argument. Personal engagement and reflection carry three each and are the ones students throw away by writing them at the end.

What a tutor can legitimately do here is substantial. Test the research question for answerability. Teach the mathematics the question requires. Explain, criterion by criterion, what the published descriptors reward. Read the student's own draft and return written comments. Teach notation and referencing. What a tutor may not do is write any part of the exploration, supply paragraphs or worked mathematics to be inserted, or edit a draft until the words and the working are no longer the student's. The IB treats that as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, not the tutor.

In this market that boundary is not theoretical. Completed internal assessments are openly advertised for sale in the UAE at four-figure prices. A family tempted by that is being offered a risk to their child's diploma dressed as a time saving, and any provider who treats the boundary as negotiable has told you what kind of provider they are.

sections.heading: Why maths is the worst subject to schedule at the end of a JBR commute
paragraphs: Mathematics is not like a humanities subject in how it uses a student. A history hour at 17:30 after a long bus ride can still be productive, because reading and discussion survive tiredness reasonably well. An Analysis Paper 1 hour at 17:30 after a forty-minute return leg from Al Barsha is largely wasted, because what the subject needs is working memory and the willingness to start a line of algebra without knowing where it ends. Tired students will not start.

This is why scheduling belongs in the teaching plan for this subject specifically. Families whose children attend the Al Sufouh schools can hold a 16:15 slot and often should, because that is the best hour available in their week. Families on the Al Barsha run should treat 16:45 as the floor and should put non-calculator work at a weekend rather than a weekday. Families out in the villa belt, where the return can reach fifty minutes, usually do better with one longer weekend session than two short weekday ones at the same total cost.

There is a second scheduling point peculiar to Higher Level. Paper 3 needs an unbroken stretch, because the skill being trained is sustained attention inside one problem. A fifty-minute slot squeezed between a commute and dinner cannot train that. From January of DP2 onwards, Higher Level students in this cluster are consistently better served by a ninety-minute weekend session than by a weekday hour, and the difference shows up in the mock rather than in how the sessions feel.

During Ramadan the pattern shifts again. School days shorten, and a post-Iftar slot is frequently the most productive hour of the day for a Diploma student, particularly for mathematics. Families who move the session rather than pausing it keep the sequence intact through the weeks closest to the May papers, which is when losing continuity is most expensive.

sections.heading: From MYP or IGCSE into DP1 maths: the gap in the first term
paragraphs: The handover into Diploma mathematics is where a lot of JBR families first meet a problem, and the shape of the problem depends entirely on where the student came from. The two feeder routes produce almost opposite gaps, and treating them the same wastes a term. Schools rarely diagnose this explicitly because a DP1 class contains students from both routes and from several countries.

A student arriving from the MYP has met investigation, pattern generalisation and justification through criterion B, and has usually written something resembling a small exploration already. What they often lack is speed and accuracy under timed conditions, because MYP assessment is not built around a ninety-minute paper. Their first-term difficulty is pace, and it shows in Paper 1 and Paper 2 mocks rather than in the coursework.

A student arriving from IGCSE, particularly from Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1, has the opposite profile: solid written technique, good timing, and no experience of an extended independent mathematical write-up. Their first-term difficulty is the exploration, and it surfaces late because the exploration deadline sits in DP2. Students from Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 sit between the two, having met graphical-calculator work and investigation in a form closer to the Diploma.

There is a third group in this neighbourhood: students arriving mid-year from another country's system entirely. For them the gap is notation and convention as much as content, and it is fixable quickly if it is named. The table sets the starting points side by side with the realistic amount of focused support each one needs, which is weeks rather than terms in every case where the work starts early.

sections.heading: What IB maths tuition costs around JBR, by the month rather than the hour
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market quotes and monthly totals are how a household actually decides, so start with the month. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a single weekly one-hour session come out at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Monthly packages visible in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Converting back to hours, the published figures read in October 2026 are these. Tutopiya's comparison panel opens at AED 33 to AED 52, carrying a revision date around twenty-one months old. EdFlik publishes an entry tier at AED 45 to AED 65. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to AED 500. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the examiner end. Each of those is on the provider's own page and can be checked.

For mathematics specifically the monthly arithmetic is worth doing carefully, because this is the subject families most often over-buy. A DP1 student needs continuity rather than volume: one well-matched hour a week from January, costing a mid-tier monthly figure, outperforms three hours a week bought in the spring of DP2 at a specialist rate. The exception is the exploration, where a short burst of concentrated hours in the DP1 summer is genuinely better value than the same hours spread across DP2.

Set this against one piece of context. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed part of the education budget this year; tutoring is the part still moving, which makes the monthly figure the number to control. IB Gram does not publish a price list here: the sequence is a free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, then a quote once the course and the component are known.

process.title: Name the course and the paper
process.description: Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, and which paper the marks are leaking from. Those three facts turn a vague request into a precise match, because Analysis Paper 1 technique and Applications Paper 2 modelling need different people. If you are not sure which course your child is in, the school's course outline will say, and it is worth five minutes to find out.

process.title: A diagnostic trial in your real weekday slot
process.description: One free trial per student, no card details taken, held at the time the school run actually leaves open. The tutor sets an unseen question from the relevant paper and watches where the student stops, which is more informative than any amount of discussion. You get a written read on which of the four common problems you have.

process.title: A sequence built around the school's dates
process.description: Before the second session the tutor writes down the topic order and the component targets, sequenced against the school's scheme of work, its mock window and its exploration deadline. For a Higher Level student that plan usually places Paper 3 practice at weekends from January of DP2, because the component needs an unbroken stretch.

process.title: Written notes, and a change of tutor if it is wrong
process.description: A short record after each session names what was covered, what the student completed unaided and what remains open, and it can be shared with the school. Use those notes to decide whether to continue. If the match is not working, changing tutor after two sessions is normal and costs nothing; carrying a mismatch for a term is the expensive option.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not the word maths
whyPoints.description: Four IB mathematics courses exist and they are not interchangeable. Analysis Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Applications Higher Level includes graph theory and matrices. A tutor fluent in one and improvising in the other teaches correct mathematics with the wrong examination technique, which is the most common wasted hour in this subject.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 taught as a non-calculator paper
whyPoints.description: The single largest loss in Analysis is written algebraic method, because two years of graphic display calculator work hides it until a mock. Sessions aimed at Paper 1 start with the calculator put away and stay that way, which is uncomfortable for a fortnight and then stops being the problem.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling treated as part of the teaching
whyPoints.description: Mathematics needs working memory, and a student home at 16:40 from Al Barsha does not have much left. We set the slot after we know the school run, which for villa-belt families usually means one longer weekend session rather than two tired weekday hours at the same price.

whyPoints.title: A stated limit on exploration help
whyPoints.description: Tutors test the research question, teach the mathematics it needs, explain what the five criteria reward and comment on the student's own draft. They do not write, supply or edit any part of what is submitted. Completed internal assessments are sold openly in this market; that is a risk to a diploma, not a shortcut.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check before you spend
whyPoints.description: Every AED number on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and the monthly estimates are attributed to the rate table they came from. Most pages ranking for Dubai maths tutoring publish no price at all, and a rate you cannot trace is not information.

faqs.question: Which of the four IB maths courses is my child actually taking?
faqs.answer: The school's course outline will name it, and it will be one of Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. The quickest test at home is the calculator: if a past paper labelled Paper 1 says no calculator is permitted, the course is Analysis. Standard Level sits two papers at 40 per cent each; Higher Level sits three, with Paper 3 running an hour and carrying 20 per cent. All four carry an exploration worth 20 per cent.

faqs.question: My son wants Applications because he says it avoids algebra. Is he right?
faqs.answer: It is differently shaped rather than easier, and at Higher Level it is not easy by any reading. Applications permits a calculator in every paper and weights statistics, modelling and financial mathematics heavily, while Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and a demanding statistics strand. Students who choose it to avoid algebra meet algebra inside the modelling questions. The honest basis for choosing is which paper the student can begin unaided, tested on unseen questions from both courses.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in school tests and badly in Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Almost always because school tests allow the graphic display calculator and Analysis Paper 1 does not. Two years of technology use conceals insecure written algebra until a mock exposes it, and the loss is total rather than partial because a question begun wrongly earns nothing. Paper 1 is 40 per cent of the Standard Level grade and 30 per cent at Higher Level. The fix is drilling written method with the calculator put away, which is unpleasant for about a fortnight.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does my Higher Level child find it so different?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a one-hour paper sat only at Higher Level, worth 20 per cent of the grade, containing two extended problems built in escalating parts. It rewards staying inside a single problem for twenty minutes rather than answering many short questions. Most students meet it having practised only fragments, so they abandon it at part (d) and leave the later parts, which are often more accessible, untouched. It has to be practised at full length, repeatedly, to fix that habit.

faqs.question: How long should the maths exploration be and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: Roughly twelve to twenty pages, marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation and mathematical communication at four marks each, personal engagement and reflection at three each, and use of mathematics at six. Use of mathematics is the only criterion where level matters, requiring mathematics commensurate with the course and correctly applied. The commonest fault is a research question needing mathematics the student has not met, which caps criterion E whatever else is done well.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child choose an exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where outside help is worth most. A tutor can test whether a proposed question is answerable with the mathematics of the course, suggest how to narrow it, teach the mathematics it requires and explain what each criterion rewards. A tutor can read the student's own draft and return written comments. A tutor cannot write any part of it, supply working to be inserted, or edit until the words are no longer the student's. That line is a malpractice line, not a policy preference.

faqs.question: My child is home at 16:40 from Al Barsha. When should the maths hour be?
faqs.answer: Treat 16:45 as the floor for any maths session and move non-calculator work to a weekend. Mathematics draws on working memory in a way that reading and discussion do not, so a tired student will not start a line of algebra without knowing where it ends. Families on the shorter Al Sufouh run can hold 16:15, which is usually the best hour in their week. Villa-belt families with a fifty-minute return do better with one longer weekend session.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level maths student need more than one session a week?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and continuity matters more than volume. One well-matched hour a week from January of DP1, sequenced against the school's scheme of work, outperforms three hours a week bought in the spring of DP2. The exceptions are two: a short concentrated block on the exploration in the DP1 summer, and a longer weekend session for Paper 3 practice from January of DP2, because that component needs an unbroken ninety minutes rather than a squeezed hour.

faqs.question: My child came from the MYP and is struggling with maths timing. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is the standard MYP-to-Diploma gap. MYP mathematics assesses against four criteria including investigating patterns, which builds generalisation and justification but not speed under a ninety-minute paper. So these students arrive strong on the exploration skills and weak on pace, and it shows in mocks rather than coursework. Six to ten focused hours across the first term, spent entirely on timed practice, closes it. Students arriving from IGCSE have the opposite profile and need the exploration work instead.

faqs.question: Does the formula booklet mean my child does not need to memorise formulae?
faqs.answer: It changes what is worth memorising rather than removing the need. A formula booklet is supplied for every paper, so recall of listed results earns nothing. What the booklet does not supply is the recognition of which result applies, the trigonometric identities students are expected to manipulate fluently, and the algebraic technique to use a formula once found. Students who rely on the booklet in Paper 1 lose time hunting rather than marks on recall, which is its own problem under timing.

faqs.question: Which maths course do UAE universities want for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Check the specific programme page rather than taking any tutoring site's word for it, including this one. Requirements are set by faculty and programme rather than by institution, they change between admission cycles, and several UAE universities publish the mathematics line only inside the degree page. Engineering, physics and economics programmes are the ones where the course choice is most often specified. Confirm it in writing with your school's university counselling office before the school's switching deadline in DP1.

faqs.question: Can we change from Higher Level to Standard Level maths partway through?
faqs.answer: Most Dubai schools allow it up to an internal deadline early in DP1, and after that it becomes difficult or impossible. The decision should be made on evidence rather than on how the student feels in the second week: an unseen Paper 1 question and an unseen Paper 2 question, marked honestly, tell you more than a term of reports. Ask the coordinator in writing for the switching deadline at the start of DP1, because families who ask in January have usually already missed it.

faqs.question: Does my child's maths tutor need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are all eligible. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come into the JBR towers for the session?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE maths lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard for working through algebra line by line, screen sharing for annotating the student's own script and saved worked solutions. The published in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour is quoted on this page so the formats can be compared honestly.

faqs.question: What does a month of IB maths tutoring typically cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for one weekly hour give AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Online packages around AED 799 for eight sessions appear widely in this market. Those figures were read in October 2026 and can be checked on the sources named. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, once the course and component are known.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for Higher Level Analysis in our slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you before anything is paid. Standard Level courses can usually be matched within the week. Higher Level Analysis with a Paper 3 focus, in one fixed weekday slot, is the combination most likely to be unavailable at short notice, and in that case we offer the nearest workable time, a weekend alternative, or we say we cannot staff it. An hour with a tutor who has not taught Paper 3 is worse value than no hour, so we do not sell it.

Lessons run one to one on live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the first one free, one per student, and no card details taken.

intro.heading: The Diploma maths year has a shape, and most tutoring ignores it
paragraphs: Maths tutoring usually starts when a topic goes wrong. The student struggles with integration, the family books a tutor, and the tutor teaches integration. That is reasonable and it is also why so much tutoring produces no grade movement: the work is organised around the symptom rather than around the calendar the student is actually living in.

The IB maths year has a shape. There is a point at which the exploration has to be chosen, a point at which it has to be drafted, a point at which it has to be finished, and those are set by the school rather than by the IB. There is a mock window a term before the papers. There is a final eight-week run in which nothing new should be taught. Each of those phases needs different work, and doing the right work in the wrong phase wastes the term.

This page is organised that way. It counts backwards from the session - the May session, which is what almost every UAE school enters its candidates for - through the mock window, the exploration deadline and the end of the first Diploma year, and names what should exist at each point. Then it gives the two tables that make the rest of the decisions: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation, and the AED market bands with their sources. Each table is there to settle one decision rather than to decorate the page.

Geography is the reason this page talks about delivery at all. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western end of Dubai, with its residential communities spread through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. A tutor driving to any of those for a 5pm session arrives at 5.45pm in term traffic, and the further south you live the fewer tutors will come at all.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For maths that format is a good fit, because the work is a shared screen with a worked solution on it and the student writing rather than watching. Starting at 4.30pm rather than 6pm matters more for maths than for most subjects, because tired students make arithmetic errors.

One honest note on dates before the tables. Cambridge and Pearson publish their timetables and we cite them. IB session and results dates are not confirmable from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and does not publish a specific IB examination or results date. Confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria lettered A to D, each worth up to eight marks, covering knowledge and understanding, investigating patterns, communication, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no external paper for most students, so the record is a set of criterion judgements rather than percentages.

programmes.name: The exploration and the Diploma core
programmes.description: The mathematics exploration is the internally assessed component of both courses, marked against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics used. The wider Diploma core - Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, Creativity, Activity, Service - competes for the same weeks.

A student who has not chosen an exploration topic by the end of the first year is compressing three jobs into one term, and the reflection criterion is the one that suffers.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: Below are the parts of IB Mathematics that generate requests from this catchment, with the specific loss of marks each one produces. Mathematics is unusually diagnosable: the mark scheme tells you where the method marks were.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Calculus, proof, complex numbers and extended algebraic work, with a third paper built on long problem-solving tasks. Marks go on method lines never written down and on questions abandoned after part (a) when the later parts were reachable.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and statistics across two papers, one with technology and one without. The non-calculator paper exposes arithmetic fluency that a calculator has been hiding since Year 9.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, matrices and graph theory, with a third paper of extended modelling tasks. Candidates lose marks by quoting technology output without naming the model, the variables or the limits of the fit.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial mathematics and modelling with the calculator central rather than incidental. Interpretation sentences carry marks: a correct correlation coefficient with no statement of what it means scores less than it should.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: A student-chosen investigation marked against lettered criteria. Reflection is the criterion most often misread, treated as a conclusion rather than as critical evaluation of what the mathematics did and did not show.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique
subjects.description: Short and structured questions where method marks dominate. The single most profitable habit in the whole course is writing the line before the answer, and it is a discipline rather than a concept.

subjects.name: Paper 2 technique
subjects.description: Technology-permitted, which changes the question style rather than making it easier. Marks go to candidates who state what they asked the calculator for; an unexplained number earns nothing even when it is right.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem-solving
subjects.description: Long linked tasks on unfamiliar ground. The skill is persistence with partial information, and the commonest failure is stopping at the first part that does not resolve cleanly rather than taking the result forward.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator fluency
subjects.description: Regression, distributions, numerical solving and graph analysis. Students who learned the calculator by imitation lose time in the exam hunting menus, and lost time in maths is lost marks.

subjects.name: MYP to Diploma transition
subjects.description: The gap is algebraic fluency and formal notation rather than topic coverage. Students who were strong on MYP criterion D often struggle with the notation discipline the Diploma papers assume from the first week.

sections.heading: The Diploma maths year counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: Start at the papers and walk backwards. In the final eight weeks nothing new should be taught, because new content at that point displaces the timed practice that converts knowledge into marks. Before that there is a mock window, which exists to generate data rather than to be survived. Before that the exploration has to be finished to a school deadline. Before that it has to be chosen, which means the first Diploma year has to end with a topic in hand.

Laid out that way, the usual pattern of family behaviour looks obviously wrong. Most tutoring enquiries from this catchment arrive after the mocks, which is the point at which the content window has closed. A student who has not covered a Higher Level topic by then cannot cover it properly and also do the timed practice, and something has to be sacrificed. The honest conversation is about which.

The second thing the backwards count exposes is the exploration collision. School deadlines for the mathematics exploration land in the same term as the Extended Essay deadline and the mocks. Three substantial pieces of independent work, one calendar. Students who chose an exploration topic in the first year sail through it; students who did not lose marks on the reflection criterion because there is no time left to think.

On dates: we name the May session as the one UAE schools sit and we do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page, because IB dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the real internal calendar, and it is the one that matters most anyway.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: deciding properly
paragraphs: This choice is made in MYP 5 or Year 11, often on the basis of which course sounds harder, and it is difficult to reverse once the Diploma has started. The two courses are not a hard version and an easy version of the same subject. They examine different mathematics and they suit different students, and a strong candidate can be in the wrong one.

Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with calculus at its centre and a non-calculator paper that rewards arithmetic and algebraic fluency. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-oriented, with statistics, financial mathematics and technology integrated throughout, and interpretation sentences carrying marks alongside the computation. A student who thinks clearly in symbols belongs in the first. A student who thinks clearly about data and context belongs in the second.

The destination matters as much as the aptitude. Some engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degree programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and some will not accept Applications and Interpretation in its place. Others treat them as equivalent. The only reliable method is to read the entry requirements for two or three target programmes directly, including any UAE universities on the list, before confirming the course.

Where a student is already enrolled in the wrong course, the useful work is not regret but adaptation: building the specific fluency the course assumes. For a modelling thinker stuck in Analysis and Approaches, that is non-calculator algebra. For a symbolic thinker in Applications and Interpretation, it is writing interpretation sentences that earn marks instead of treating them as decoration.

sections.heading: The exploration: what each criterion actually rewards
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics student writes an exploration, and it is internally assessed and externally moderated. It is also the component where the gap between effort and mark is widest, because students optimise for the thing they can see - length, neatness, impressive-looking mathematics - and the criteria reward something else.

Presentation rewards a reader being able to follow the argument: a structure, consistent notation, labelled diagrams, no stray algebra. Mathematical communication rewards precision in that notation, including the distinction between a variable and a label and the correct use of symbols the student may have been using loosely for years. Personal engagement rewards evidence of the student's own thinking, which is not the same as enthusiasm about the topic.

Reflection is the criterion that costs most marks in this catchment and it is almost always misread. Students write a conclusion: here is what I found. The criterion asks for evaluation: what did the mathematics show, what did it fail to show, what were the limitations of the model or the data, what would be done differently. That is a different kind of paragraph and it has to be planned rather than appended.

The use of mathematics criterion rewards mathematics that is commensurate with the course and genuinely understood. A Standard Level student who imports a technique they cannot explain scores worse than one who uses course-level mathematics correctly and discusses it well. The boundary is firm: a tutor explains criteria, teaches content, narrows the topic and marks drafts. A tutor does not write, rewrite or complete any part of it, because that is a malpractice matter for the student.
bullets: Presentation: can a reader follow the argument without re-reading?
Mathematical communication: notation used precisely, not loosely

sections.heading: Where maths marks actually go: three papers, three habits
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most diagnosable subject in the Diploma, because the mark scheme awards marks to specific lines rather than to overall impression. That means a marked script tells you almost exactly what went wrong, and it means the fixes are narrow and trainable rather than vague.

On Paper 1 the dominant loss is the unwritten method line. A student works a question partly on paper and partly in their head, arrives at the right answer and writes only the answer. Where the answer is wrong - a sign error, a transcription slip - every method mark that was available is lost too. Over a full paper this routinely accounts for the gap between two grades, and it is a discipline that can be installed in three or four sessions of enforcement.

On Paper 2 the dominant loss is the unexplained calculator result. Technology is permitted, which means the question is no longer about getting the number; it is about demonstrating what was asked of the technology and what the result means. A regression coefficient with no statement of the model, a solution with no indication of which equation was solved, a probability with no distribution named: all score below what the student's understanding deserves.

On Paper 3, at Higher Level, the dominant loss is abandonment. The paper is built from long linked tasks on unfamiliar ground, and a part that does not resolve cleanly causes students to stop, when the later parts are often reachable from a partial result. Practising persistence specifically - carrying an incomplete result forward and seeing which later parts it opens up - is a different exercise from practising topics.

sections.heading: What IB maths tutoring costs in Dubai, and what the travel premium buys
paragraphs: The interesting question in this catchment is not the headline rate but what the in-home premium is actually purchasing. Dubai rate guidance published for 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. A qualified subject tutor teaching online is published at AED 150-300, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200. The gap is the journey.

For a Jebel Ali or Emaar South address, that journey is substantial, and here is what the premium buys. It buys a person in the room, which matters for a student who will not start work unsupervised. It buys no additional subject knowledge. And it costs you the later start time and the narrower choice, because only the tutors willing to make that drive are in your list at all.

Across the wider market, the published October 2026 bands are these: budget online tuition from AED 33-52 at Tutopiya and AED 45-65 at EdFlik; qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300; specialists at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase around AED 270; and one premium provider, BartyED, at AED 650. Monthly packages seen include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

None of those are IB Gram prices. We publish no rate card here because the fee depends on course and level and is quoted after the free trial lesson. The bands exist so that any quote can be judged against something published - which is more than three of the pages currently ranking for this search provide, and two of the rest quote US dollars.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one maths from a Jebel Ali address, limitations included
paragraphs: Maths suits the online format better than most subjects, for a mechanical reason: the work is a shared surface with mathematics appearing on it. The tutor writes a line, the student writes the next, and both see the same page. For marking a script together - counting where the method marks were available and were not claimed - the shared screen is better than passing one paper copy back and forth.

The scheduling gain is larger here than elsewhere because of what maths demands from a student. A 4.30pm session catches a student who can still hold an algebraic manipulation in their head. A 6.15pm session, after a tutor has crossed Dubai, catches one who makes sign errors. Parents often read those sign errors as a knowledge problem when they are a fatigue problem.

IB Gram offers no home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and this page says so near the top rather than leaving it to be discovered. Two providers ranking for UAE tutoring searches route parents to an Indian phone number without disclosing that delivery is remote, and disclosure is the baseline a family is owed.

The genuine limitations: a student who needs an adult present to begin work is better served in person; a weak home connection shortens the lesson whatever the clock says; and a shared study space, common in Discovery Gardens apartments, undermines the hour because the tutor cannot manage the room. If that is your situation, hire locally and ask the tutor whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit before the first lesson.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and the claims worth checking in a maths tutor
paragraphs: Mathematics attracts a particular kind of overclaim, because results in it look objective. Be sceptical of three things in particular when hiring anyone for IB maths in Dubai.

First, promised outcomes. No tutor can guarantee a 7, a points total or a grade improvement, and anyone offering one is either misunderstanding the assessment or misrepresenting it. Grade boundaries are set after each session is marked, and a student's final mark depends on work done in an examination hall nobody else is in. We make no outcome promises and we publish no success statistics, because a statistic without n, date and method is a liability rather than evidence.

Second, examiner claims. We do not describe tutors as IB examiners, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence for individuals, and in this market examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content that nobody has. We also do not host or distribute IB papers, mark schemes, boundary tables or subject guides, all of which are copyright material; we link the official sources instead.

Third, regulatory endorsement. IB Gram is not KHDA approved - a KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with physical premises in Dubai, and we hold none and operate no UAE office. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, IB or Cambridge accreditation or partnership. Separately, private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which the UAE government states is granted free of charge for two years; tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

sections.heading: Starting mid-year, and what we say when we cannot help
paragraphs: Most families in this catchment start mid-year, which is fine as long as the plan accounts for where in the calendar they are. Send the course and level - Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard - the school, and a photograph of the most recent marked assessment. If the exploration is in progress, send the current draft instead.

The first session is diagnostic rather than introductory. The tutor reads the script against the mark scheme and tells you plainly which of three situations you are in: habit marks recoverable in weeks, content gaps needing a term, or both with a deadline too close to do justice to either. That third answer is the one families least want and most need, because it determines what gets sacrificed.

Matching takes a day or so for Standard Level and either course; Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the second Diploma year can take two or three days, because the pool is genuinely narrow and we will not put a general maths tutor in front of a Paper 3 problem. We tell you the expected wait before you start waiting.

When no suitable specialist has a slot at your hour, we say so and offer the real alternatives: a different weekday with the right tutor, a short block until a regular slot opens, or an honest recommendation to look locally. No competitor in this market publishes what happens when they cannot help, and a family planning a final term deserves to know that in advance rather than after a week of silence.

whyPoints.title: The plan runs backwards from the session
whyPoints.description: Phases determine the work: content in the first year, exploration around the school deadline, habits after the mocks, timed papers in the final eight weeks. Doing the right work in the wrong phase is why conscientious students see no movement.

whyPoints.title: AA and AI specialists matched separately
whyPoints.description: The two courses punish different habits - skipped method lines in one, uninterpreted technology output in the other - so we do not treat IB maths as a single subject with one tutor pool.

whyPoints.description: Tutors narrow the topic, explain each criterion and mark drafts. They never write, rewrite or complete any part of it. Services selling finished coursework in this market put the student's whole Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Marking by someone who is not the student
whyPoints.description: Self-marking over-rewards because the student knows what they meant to write. External marking against the official scheme converts a vague sense of underperformance into a short, ranked list of fixable habits.

whyPoints.title: Nothing promised that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: We publish no grade promises, no success percentages and no self-asserted ratings, and every AED band here is attributed to its publisher with the month we read it. A number without a source is not evidence.

whyPoints.description: Sessions start from about 4pm Gulf Standard Time because nobody is driving to Emaar South or Jebel Ali Village. For maths specifically that matters: fatigue produces sign errors that look exactly like gaps in understanding.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should a Jebel Ali student start maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and the reason is calendar rather than content. The first Diploma year is where notation discipline and method-line habits are cheap to build. By the time mocks are over, the content window has effectively closed, and a student who has not met a Higher Level topic cannot both learn it properly and do the timed practice that converts it into marks. If you are already past the mocks, the honest plan is habit repair and timed papers rather than new teaching.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should a Jebel Ali student pick, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: They are different rather than ranked. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with calculus at its centre and a non-calculator paper, so it rewards symbolic fluency. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led, with statistics, financial mathematics and integrated technology, and interpretation sentences carry marks alongside the computation. A student who thinks in symbols finds the first easier; one who thinks in data and context finds the second easier. Check the entry requirements of two or three target degree programmes before treating either as the safer choice.

faqs.question: How long does the IB mathematics exploration need to be?
faqs.answer: Length is not what the criteria reward, and treating it as the target is the commonest misdirection. The criteria ask for presentation a reader can follow, precise mathematical communication, visible personal engagement, reflection that evaluates rather than summarises, and mathematics commensurate with the course and genuinely understood. A concise exploration that addresses every criterion outscores a long one that neglects reflection. Your school publishes its own guidance on expected length, and that is the figure to work to rather than anything quoted on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their final answers are right?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme pays for method lines, and the lines were never written down. A student works part of a question in their head, writes the answer, and it happens to be correct - so nothing is lost. On the next question a sign error creeps in, the answer is wrong, and with no working on the page every method mark available is lost as well. Over a full Paper 1 this routinely accounts for a whole grade. It is a discipline rather than a concept, and three or four sessions of strict enforcement usually installs it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the legitimate space is wide enough to be genuinely useful. A tutor can help narrow the topic until the mathematics is within the student's own reach, teach the content the investigation needs, explain what each lettered criterion rewards and what its mark ceiling is, discuss how to structure the argument, check notation and referencing conventions, and mark a draft against the descriptors. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it, or supply the mathematics. The test after each session is whether every sentence was typed by your child.

faqs.question: What should the last eight weeks before the maths papers look like?
faqs.answer: Timed papers and marking, and nothing new. The student sits a full paper under real timing, including Paper 3 at Higher Level. Someone who is not the student marks it against the official scheme and produces a ranked list of repeated habits. The next session attacks those habits rather than moving to a fresh paper. Then repeat. Introducing new content in this window displaces the practice that converts existing knowledge into marks, which is why a late content push so often produces no change in the result.

faqs.question: My child is moving from MYP 5 into Diploma maths. What should we work on?
faqs.answer: Notation discipline and algebraic fluency rather than topic coverage. The MYP assesses against four lettered criteria out of eight and rewards investigation and communication; the Diploma papers assume formal notation and fast, accurate manipulation from the first term. Students who scored well on MYP criterion D frequently struggle with that assumption, because the MYP never required it. A summer of deliberate algebra - rearranging, simplifying, writing every line - plus a diagnostic at the standard the chosen course will demand is the highest-value preparation available.

faqs.question: Does my child need Higher Level maths for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the programme, and the only safe method is to read the entry requirements for two or three specific courses directly. Some engineering, mathematics, physics and economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and will not accept Applications and Interpretation in its place; others treat the two as equivalent. Separately, school-leaving certificates generally need Ministry of Education equivalency before a UAE university application, and no IB points threshold is published in the source we read, so verify that on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any figure quoted elsewhere.

faqs.question: Can online lessons work for a subject as visual as maths?
faqs.answer: Maths is one of the formats that transfers best, because the work is a shared surface with mathematics appearing on it. The tutor writes a line, the student writes the next, and both see the same page at the same moment. Marking a script together is actually easier than in person, since both people can annotate rather than passing one paper copy across a table. What it needs is a reliable connection and a quiet hour. What it does not do well is supervise a student who will not begin work without an adult in the room.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match an HL Analysis and Approaches tutor for Dubai South?
faqs.answer: Standard Level in either course usually matches within a day. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in the second Diploma year can take two or three days, because the pool of tutors who can handle a Paper 3 problem properly is genuinely narrow and we will not substitute a general maths tutor. We tell you the expected wait at the enquiry rather than afterwards. If nobody suitable has a slot at the hour you need, we say so and offer a different weekday, a short block, or an honest suggestion to look locally.

faqs.question: Is a calculator skill really worth tutoring time?
faqs.answer: In Applications and Interpretation, yes, and in Analysis and Approaches more than families expect. Technology is integral to one of the two papers at both levels and to the AI course throughout: regression, distributions, numerical solving, graph analysis. Students who learned the calculator by imitation lose exam time hunting through menus, and lost time converts directly into lost marks. Deliberate calculator work is also where the Paper 2 habit of stating the model and the variables gets built, because an unexplained number on a technology paper earns nothing.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB exam dates for the maths papers?
faqs.answer: No, and we would rather explain why than print something plausible. IB session and results dates cannot be confirmed from the IB by automated means, so this page names the May session as the one almost all UAE schools enter candidates for and stops there. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and we cite those where relevant. For your child's actual dates, the Diploma coordinator at the school holds both the external session dates and the internal deadlines, and the internal ones usually matter more to the term plan.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics for the same Diploma student?
faqs.answer: It is one of the few genuine overlaps, and it works when the student's problem is shared - algebraic manipulation that fails in both subjects, or formula rearrangement under time pressure. It works less well when the physics problem is really about the scientific investigation or about causal explanation, which is a different competency from mathematical method. Our default is one subject per tutor, because the match is for component-level knowledge of a specific mark scheme. Tell us both subjects and we will say honestly whether one tutor fits your child's case.

faqs.question: What happens to the maths plan during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the content plan does not. School hours shorten, households reorganise their evening around iftar, and a weekday 5pm slot usually becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For maths it is worth protecting the frequency rather than the length: two shorter sessions hold fluency better than one long one when a student is fasting. Because nobody is travelling to your address, shifting a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of a commute, and it moves back afterwards just as easily.

intro.heading: What an IB maths tutor in JLT is really being asked to fix
paragraphs: Almost every maths enquiry from the JLT towers arrives as a grade problem and turns out to be a route problem. A Year 12 student is sitting Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the first term's tests have come back at a 3 or a 4, and the family wants more hours. Sometimes more hours is the answer. Often the honest answer is that the course was chosen for a university subject the student no longer wants, and the cheapest intervention is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator rather than a weekly booking that runs until May.

The two courses are not easy and hard versions of each other. Analysis and Approaches is built around algebraic manipulation, functions, calculus and proof, and rewards technical fluency. Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling, statistics and the use of technology, and rewards interpretation. A student who is strong at pattern recognition and weak at algebra is not a weaker mathematician; they are frequently in the wrong course. Treating that as a work-rate problem is how a family spends two years of money on the wrong diagnosis.

Cost follows directly from that. Reckoned over the whole Diploma, the dearest thing a family can buy is a route switch late in Year 12: the student has lost a term, has to cover content the new course assumes, and needs intensive support in exactly the months when specialists are hardest to book. Reckoned over the first six weeks, the cheapest thing a family can buy is a short block that establishes whether the problem is the route, the algebra or the technique. Those two sentences are the entire argument of this page.

The market rates sit around that argument rather than above it. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing from AED 200 for IB. Specialist exam-year support runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. A visiting tutor in a JLT tower is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors, with premium named tutors at AED 650 at BartyED. Six well-aimed sessions in October costs less than any of those arrangements sustained to May, and it is the purchase most likely to change the outcome.

IB Gram delivers to JLT as one-to-one online tuition over live video, timed after the commute back from Al Barsha, Barsha South or Al Sufouh rather than during it. We do not offer home visits in Dubai; those run only in India. For Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in particular, that format is what makes a genuine specialist reachable, because the pool of people who have taught Paper 3 is not the same as the pool of people who will drive to Jumeirah Lakes Towers at 17:00 on a Tuesday.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: Maths support is bought at three points in a JLT family's route, and the price of being late rises sharply at each one. These are the stages and what each one is actually for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria out of 8 each: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. There is no external paper in most schools, so the grade is built across the year. The reason this matters for Diploma maths is that criterion A tells you almost nothing about Analysis and Approaches readiness, while fluency on unscaffolded algebraic manipulation tells you nearly everything.
programmes.countryNote: JLT students in MYP 5 are usually choosing their Diploma route in the spring, often before anyone has tested their algebra without a calculator. Six to ten weeks of focused work at that point costs a fraction of the same work in Year 12, and it is the only moment when the route decision can be made on evidence rather than on preference.

programmes.name: Diploma Standard Level mathematics
programmes.description: Two examination papers plus the exploration. Standard Level in either route is a real course rather than a reduced one, and students who move down from Higher Level in Year 13 often find the papers less forgiving than they expected because the shared content is examined to the same standard. Support at Standard Level is usually technique-led: question reading, method marks, and the exploration.
programmes.countryNote: For a JLT student aiming at a UAE or UK university course without a mathematics prerequisite, Standard Level in the right route is frequently the better total-score decision than Higher Level in the wrong one. Check the published entry requirements of the actual courses on the shortlist before treating Higher Level as automatically preferable.

programmes.name: Diploma Higher Level mathematics
programmes.description: Three examination papers, with a third paper carrying extended problem-solving tasks, plus the exploration. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the most demanding mathematics route in the Diploma and the one where tutoring plans run longest, because the content load sits on top of fluency assumptions that are rarely tested before entry. Higher Level Applications and Interpretation is demanding in a different way, with heavy statistical modelling.
programmes.countryNote: Higher Level maths is the single most requested subject from the JLT and Marina corridor, which means it is also the subject where evening slots fill first. A family deciding in March that Higher Level support is needed for May is competing for the smallest pool of the year, which is exactly when published rate bands stop predicting what you will pay.

programmes.name: The mathematical exploration
programmes.ageRange: Internal assessment, both routes and levels
programmes.description: An individual written exploration marked on five criteria, lettered A to E, worth 20 marks in total: presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, and use of mathematics 6. It is the component families most often leave unsupported and the one where structured coaching produces the clearest gain, because most of the lost marks are procedural rather than mathematical.
programmes.countryNote: School deadlines for the exploration cluster in Year 12 summer term and Year 13 autumn, which collides with the Extended Essay for many JLT students. Mapping those two deadlines before the year starts prevents the pattern where both arrive in the same fortnight and neither gets the attention it needed.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: The grid below runs through the content areas of both maths routes, naming what each one assesses and where marks go. It is organised by where tutoring time is actually spent rather than by the order a textbook uses.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and functions
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL; assumed in AI
subjects.description: The gate for Analysis and Approaches. Students who cannot rearrange, factorise and compose confidently without technology are slow on every paper regardless of understanding. This is drillable, predictable and the single most common reason a Year 12 Higher Level student sits at a 3.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL; AI HL and SL in applied form
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules at Standard Level; implicit differentiation and related rates at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches. Marks go on notation and on failing to state what is being differentiated with respect to, rather than on the technique itself.

subjects.name: Calculus: integration
subjects.description: Substitution, areas and volumes, and at Higher Level integration by parts and partial fractions. The common loss is limits of integration and lost constants, both of which are habits rather than knowledge, and both fixable in a small number of sessions.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction, and at Higher Level proof by induction. Students lose marks for writing a convincing explanation rather than a proof, which is a language problem as much as a mathematical one and responds quickly to explicit teaching of the form.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and circular functions
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL; AI in applied contexts
subjects.description: Identities, equations and transformations, with compound angle work at Higher Level. The losses concentrate on domain and range when solving equations, where students find a correct solution and miss the others in the interval.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI HL and SL heavily; AA to a lesser extent
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing and regression. In Applications and Interpretation this is the centre of the course and the marks sit in interpretation: a correct test with no conclusion in context scores poorly, which is a teachable habit.

subjects.name: Modelling with functions
subjects.description: Selecting a model, fitting it, and commenting on its limitations. The final comment is where most of the available credit is lost, because students treat the model as the answer rather than as an approximation with a stated domain of validity.

subjects.name: Technology and the graphic display calculator
subjects.levels: Both routes; one paper permits technology
subjects.description: Technology-permitted papers reward speed and the ability to show enough working that a method is visible. Students who use the calculator as a black box lose method marks even when the final answer is right, which is the single cheapest thing to fix in either route.

subjects.name: Vectors, matrices and discrete topics
subjects.description: Content differs between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, which is one reason a route switch is costly: the topic lists are not nested. Confirm the exact content your child's course covers from the school's scheme rather than from a general summary.

subjects.name: The exploration, criteria A to E
subjects.description: Presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, use of mathematics 6. A tutor may coach the process and give feedback on the student's own drafts. No tutor should write any part of an exploration, and a service offering one is a malpractice risk for the student.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, compared properly
paragraphs: This is the comparison most pages in this market reduce to one sentence about rigour. It deserves a table, because the decision has four dimensions and families usually weigh only one. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic, analytic and proof-aware. Applications and Interpretation is statistical, model-led and technology-heavy. Both exist at Standard and Higher Level, so there are four destinations, not two.

The common error in the JLT catchment is to treat Analysis and Approaches Higher Level as the prestigious choice and everything else as a step down. That costs money in two ways. A student with strong interpretation and weak algebra will underperform in Analysis and Approaches at either level while being capable of a high grade in Applications and Interpretation, and the Diploma total is what universities read. And a student taking Higher Level for a degree they will not apply to has bought the hardest route for no return.

The right way to settle it is evidence rather than preference. Give the student twenty minutes of unscaffolded algebra without technology and twenty minutes of a modelling task with it, and look at which one they can sustain. That is a single session's work and it is the cheapest decision-support available. Then check the published entry requirements of the actual university courses on the shortlist, because the requirement is set by the university and no tutoring page should be telling you what it is.

The last column of the table is the one that answers the cost question. The tutoring profile of each route is different: Analysis and Approaches concentrates hours on fluency and proof, Applications and Interpretation on interpretation and technology discipline. A tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other, which is why hiring against the route name rather than against 'IB maths' matters as much as hiring against a syllabus code does at IGCSE.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and where the marks sit
paragraphs: Standard Level in either route is examined by two papers plus the exploration. Higher Level is examined by three, the third carrying extended problem-solving or modelling tasks that require sustained work on a small number of contexts. The exact weightings are published in the subject guide for your child's cohort and should be read there rather than taken from a tutoring page, but the structural point is stable and useful: no single paper decides the grade, and the exploration is a fifth component that most families leave unmanaged.

What matters for a plan is that the papers reward different things. The technology-permitted paper rewards speed and the discipline of showing enough working that a method is visible, which is the cheapest marks a student is currently throwing away if they treat the calculator as a black box. The non-technology paper rewards algebraic fluency, where speed is a function of practice rather than understanding. The Higher Level third paper rewards stamina and the willingness to keep going on an unfamiliar context, which is the hardest of the three to teach and the most responsive to timed practice.

The table maps the components against what each one is really testing and where students in this corridor lose marks. Use it to decide which paper a block should target, because 'maths tutoring' aimed at everything will fix nothing in particular. A student at a 4 who is losing marks on the technology paper and holding their own on the analytic one needs two or three sessions on calculator method, not a term of algebra.

Ask the school for the mark breakdown by paper from the most recent mocks, not just the overall grade. Most Dubai Diploma schools record it and will share it when asked precisely. With that in hand the conversation with a tutor takes four sentences, and the block you buy is the one the evidence points at.

sections.heading: The exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, by letter
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this project names a single internal assessment criterion, which is remarkable given that this component is a fifth of what a maths student is judged on and the most coachable part of the course. The mathematical exploration is marked on five criteria: presentation worth 4 marks, mathematical communication worth 4, personal engagement worth 3, reflection worth 3, and use of mathematics worth 6. Twenty marks in total.

Read that allocation again, because it explains most of the lost marks. Fourteen of the twenty are not about the mathematics itself. Presentation and communication together are worth 8 and are won by structure, notation, labelled graphs and consistent definitions. Personal engagement and reflection are worth 6 and are won by showing why this question, and what the results actually mean, including where the approach failed. Students who choose an ambitious topic and write it up carelessly routinely score below students who choose a modest topic and write it up properly.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, is the 6 marks where level matters. The expectation is mathematics commensurate with the course, which means a Higher Level exploration using only Standard Level techniques is capped regardless of how neatly it is presented. That single sentence is the most useful thing a tutor can say to a Higher Level student in the first exploration conversation, and it is said far too late in most schools' timelines.

The coaching boundary is absolute and worth stating next to the criteria. A tutor may interrogate the question, explain what each criterion rewards, suggest that a technique is under-ambitious for the level, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written. No tutor writes any part of an exploration. One page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments; buying one triggers a malpractice process against the student, and the mathematics in a bought exploration is usually the giveaway.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go, topic by topic
paragraphs: Grades in both routes are lost in a small number of repeatable places, and naming them converts an open budget into a short block. In Analysis and Approaches, the recurring losses are incomplete rearrangement under time, notation in calculus, solutions missed outside the first interval in trigonometric equations, and proofs written as explanations. Each of those is a habit, and habits move in sessions rather than terms.

In Applications and Interpretation, the pattern is almost inverted. The computation is usually right and the credit is lost at the end: a hypothesis test with no conclusion in context, a regression with no comment on validity, a model presented without its domain of validity or limitations. Students find this frustrating because they did the work; the answer is that the work was only part of what the mark scheme pays for.

Both routes share the technology losses. A student who produces a correct figure from a calculator without showing what was entered or what was being found loses method marks across every technology-permitted paper, and this is the single cheapest thing to repair in the whole subject. It usually takes two sessions and then practice. Families regularly pay for months of content teaching while this particular leak stays open.

The table below is a planning tool rather than a diagnosis. Take it to the mock breakdown and look for the row your child's lost marks actually sit in. If more than two rows apply, the problem is probably the route or the level rather than the topic, and the route-decision block above is the right purchase instead.

sections.heading: What IB maths support costs around JLT, in two different units
paragraphs: Price this subject in two units at once, because the hourly figure alone misleads. The first unit is the first six weeks: what it costs to establish whether the problem is the route, the fluency or the technique. At a qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour, five sessions is a known and modest total, and it is the purchase that most often prevents the expensive one. The second unit is the whole course: one weekly hour across both Diploma years at a mid-market AED 220 is roughly AED 14,000 for mathematics alone.

Between those two numbers sits every decision worth making. A fluency block of ten sessions in Year 12 is a fraction of the two-year figure and addresses the commonest single cause of a Higher Level 3. Exploration coaching of six fortnightly sessions is smaller again and targets a component worth a fifth of the assessment. A standing weekly slot from September of Year 12 to May of Year 13 is occasionally right and should be entered deliberately, with a termly decision point, rather than renewed by habit.

The market figures for context, all published by the providers named: budget online from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors from AED 200 for IB; in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's 2026 table and AED 200 to 500 from independent home tutors; specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270; and premium named tutors at AED 650 at BartyED. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward in a specialist exam year.

None of these is an IB Gram rate. For Higher Level Analysis and Approaches in particular, the variable that moves your actual price is not the band but the month: evening slots for that subject fill first across the whole Marina corridor, so a family deciding in March is choosing from the smallest pool of the year. The cheapest version of this subject is the one planned in September.

sections.heading: University requirements: what to check, and where
paragraphs: The route decision is often framed as a university decision, and it genuinely can be, but the requirement belongs to the university and not to a tutoring page. Some degree courses specify Higher Level mathematics, some specify Analysis and Approaches specifically, some accept either route at Higher Level, and some set no mathematics requirement at all. Those positions differ between institutions and change between admission cycles, which is why the only safe instruction is to read the course page for the actual course.

Do it in a particular order. List the five or six courses the student is realistically applying to, including UAE institutions and whichever overseas systems are in play. Find each course's published entry requirements on the institution's own admissions pages. Note whether the requirement names a route, a level, and a grade. Then compare that list against the route the school has placed the student in. The mismatch, if there is one, is the thing worth spending money on.

Two practical cautions for a JLT family. Engineering, mathematics, physics and economics courses are the ones most likely to specify a route and a level, so check those first and earliest. And where a student is undecided, the cost of keeping options open is not symmetric: moving from Higher Level to Standard Level within a route is usually simpler than moving between routes, because the content lists of Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are not nested.

Nothing on this page is a substitute for the institution's own statement, and nobody should tell you that tutoring is required to meet a requirement. Equivalency and admissions are regulatory and institutional processes; IB Gram neither performs nor guarantees any part of them. What a tutor can do is tell you honestly whether the route your child is in is reachable from where they currently are.

sections.heading: Honesty, the exploration and what a tutor will refuse
paragraphs: The exploration is the point in this subject where the pressure to cross a line becomes concrete, because it is written at home over weeks and it is worth 20 marks. The boundary is clear and worth agreeing in the first session rather than in the last week. A tutor may interrogate the research question, explain each criterion, point out that a technique is under-ambitious for Higher Level, question whether a conclusion follows, and give written feedback on drafts the student has written themselves.

A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite it to completion, supply text that appears in the submission, or produce the mathematics for the student to copy. The same applies to any modelling work taken from a source: a model used in an exploration must be cited, and an uncited one is a plagiarism finding rather than a presentational slip. Where generative tools have been used, the school's own policy governs, and a reflection that is not the student's thinking is visible to a moderator in exactly the way a parent would expect.

There is a materials boundary too. Official IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are referenced and linked from the IB's own channels, not reproduced or supplied as downloads, and unreleased material is not something a legitimate tutor holds. A provider who sends a folder of scans has told you how it treats rules in general, which matters most in the term when the exploration is due.

The screening question for any maths tutor is simple and cheap. Ask what they would do if your child sent a finished exploration draft and asked them to fix the mathematics. A teacher describes feedback, a conversation and a redraft by the student. A service describes a turnaround. That answer is worth more than a list of qualifications and costs nothing to obtain before the first paid session.
