sections.heading: Starting with maths from a JLT address
paragraphs: Send four things: the school, the route and level your child is currently in, the mark breakdown by paper from the most recent mocks, and the school's exploration deadline. We propose a tutor who teaches that route at that level, with a slot set after the commute back to Jumeirah Lakes Towers, and you take a free trial lesson that costs nothing and requires no card details.

For most Year 12 enquiries we will propose the route-decision block or the fluency block rather than a standing weekly slot, because those two address the two commonest causes of a disappointing first term and both have a defined end. For Year 13 enquiries arriving after the exploration is submitted, a Paper 3 or timed-practice block is usually the right shape. In either case the review point is the next real school assessment compared with the mock breakdown you sent us.

Availability for this subject is tighter than for any other in the Diploma, and we disclose it rather than discovering it with you in March. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches evening slots fill first across the whole corridor from JLT to Al Sufouh. Where we cannot staff the route and level you need in UAE evening hours this term, we say so at the enquiry stage and you should approach someone else, rather than being placed with a tutor who teaches the other route.

Three things we will decline: producing any part of an exploration, claiming a board or regulator relationship we do not hold, and promising a particular grade or points total. What we will give you is a session count, a target component, and a point at which you decide whether it worked.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course is the more expensive mistake to choose, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Whichever one does not match the student. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, calculus and proof; Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and interpretation. A student strong in interpretation and weak in algebra will underperform in Analysis and Approaches at either level while being capable of a high grade in the other route, and universities read the Diploma total. The expensive version is discovering this in Year 13. One session of diagnosis, twenty minutes of unscaffolded algebra and twenty of a modelling task, settles it for a fraction of the cost.

faqs.question: How are the marks split across the papers in IB Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Standard Level in either route is examined by two written papers plus the exploration; Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem solving or modelling. The exact weightings are published in the subject guide for your child's cohort and should be read there rather than taken from a tutoring page. The structural point for planning is that no single paper decides the grade, and the exploration is a fifth component carrying 20 marks that many families never manage at all. Ask the school for the mock mark breakdown by paper.

faqs.question: What are the five exploration criteria worth, in marks?
faqs.answer: Presentation 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, and use of mathematics 6, giving 20 in total. Fourteen of those twenty sit outside the mathematics itself, which explains why a modest topic written up carefully routinely outscores an ambitious one written up carelessly. Criterion E expects mathematics commensurate with the course, so a Higher Level exploration relying on Standard Level techniques is capped however neat it is. That is the first thing worth saying to a Higher Level student, and it is usually said far too late.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level Analysis and Approaches realistic after a Core IGCSE maths course?
faqs.answer: It is a long way, and the honest answer depends on evidence rather than ambition. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes fluent, fast algebraic manipulation without technology, which a Core or Foundation tier IGCSE course does not develop to that standard. The practical route is a diagnosis session on unscaffolded algebra, then a decision with the Diploma coordinator. Where the school supports the attempt, expect a fluency block of eight to twelve sessions early in Year 12, and expect to review it honestly at the first real assessment.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a student switching between the two routes need?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, because the content lists are not nested. Moving from Analysis and Approaches to Applications and Interpretation means picking up statistical content and technology discipline that the first course does not cover in the same depth; moving the other way means picking up algebraic and calculus fluency. Either way the student has also lost the term already spent. That is why the route-decision block of three to five sessions, bought in MYP 5 or the first weeks of Year 12, is the cheapest purchase on this page.

faqs.question: Which IB maths topics cost students in this corridor the most marks?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches: unfinished algebraic rearrangement under time, calculus notation, trigonometric equations where only the first solution in the interval is found, and proofs written as explanations. In Applications and Interpretation: hypothesis tests with no conclusion in context, regressions with no comment on validity, and models presented without their limitations. Shared across both routes is the technology paper, where a right answer with no visible method forfeits method marks. That last one takes about two sessions to repair and is the cheapest leak in the subject.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the help is mostly interrogation rather than suggestion. A tutor can ask why this question, whether the mathematics involved is commensurate with the course, whether data is actually obtainable, and whether there is anything genuine to reflect on at the end. Those four questions eliminate most doomed topics in one conversation. What a tutor must not do is write any part of the exploration, supply mathematics to be copied, or hand over text. Any model or source used has to be cited; an uncited one is a plagiarism finding, not a presentational slip.

faqs.question: Does our child need Analysis and Approaches for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Check the institution, because the requirement belongs to them and changes between cycles. Engineering, mathematics, physics and economics courses are the ones most likely to specify a route and a level, so read the published entry requirements on the actual course pages for the five or six courses on the shortlist. Then compare that against the route the school has placed the student in. No tutoring page should be telling you what a university requires, and nobody should suggest tutoring is needed to satisfy an admissions rule.

faqs.question: What does IB maths tutoring cost around Jumeirah Lakes Towers?
faqs.answer: Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing from AED 200 for IB, and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors. Price it as blocks rather than hours: a route-decision block of three to five sessions, a fluency block of eight to twelve, exploration coaching of six fortnightly. A continuous weekly hour across both years at AED 220 is roughly AED 14,000.

faqs.question: When in the two Diploma years should maths support be bought?
faqs.answer: September and October of Year 12 is the cheapest and most effective window, because every assessment is still ahead and the route decision can still be revisited. The second useful window is the exploration term, where six fortnightly sessions target 20 marks that most families leave unmanaged. The most expensive window is the spring of Year 13, when Higher Level Analysis and Approaches evening slots across the whole Marina corridor are full, availability rather than the published band sets your price, and little remains in the calendar to influence.

faqs.question: What does the third Higher Level paper actually add?
faqs.answer: Extended tasks on unfamiliar contexts, which test stamina and the willingness to keep going when the route through a problem is not visible in the first line. It is the hardest of the three papers to teach and the most responsive to timed practice on whole tasks rather than on topic exercises. Students lose marks there by abandoning a question part-way or by finishing the mathematics and never interpreting the result. A block of six to ten timed sessions is the usual shape of support for it.

faqs.question: Is the calculator paper easier than the non-calculator one?
faqs.answer: Different rather than easier, and it is where students throw marks away most casually. The technology-permitted paper rewards speed and the discipline of showing enough working that a method is visible; a correct figure lifted from a calculator with nothing written down forfeits method marks. The non-technology paper rewards algebraic fluency, where speed comes from practice rather than understanding. A student can be comfortable on one and losing most of their marks on the other, which is why the mock breakdown by paper matters more than the overall grade.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two siblings on different maths routes?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be checked rather than assumed. The two routes share some content but reward different habits, and a tutor strong in Analysis and Approaches fluency work is not automatically strong in statistical interpretation. Ask directly which routes and levels they teach and how recently. Two consecutive online slots with two specialists in one evening is straightforward and often costs the same as one generalist covering both, which is the arrangement most JLT households with two Diploma students end up preferring.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level AA tutor is free at the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the enquiry stage. This is the tightest subject in the Diploma for evening availability across the corridor from JLT to Al Sufouh, and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches fills first. Where we cannot staff the route and level in UAE evening hours this term, we say so rather than placing a tutor who teaches the other route. Two workarounds often help: a weekend session, or a later weekday start for students commuting from Barsha South who are home after 17:30 anyway.

faqs.question: Should we wait for the mock results before hiring anyone?
faqs.answer: No, but do collect the first real assessment data before committing to a long plan. The mock breakdown by paper is the most useful document in this process, and waiting for a full mock season to pass costs a term you cannot get back. A reasonable compromise is a short diagnostic block now, aimed at establishing whether the issue is the route, the fluency or the technique, and then a properly scoped block once the mock breakdown arrives. Buying the big plan before any evidence exists is the mistake to avoid.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jlt.closingHeading: Settle the route, then buy the block the evidence points at
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jlt.closingBody: An IB maths tutor in JLT earns their fee twice over by answering the route question honestly before the hours question. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation reward different mathematicians, the exploration is 20 marks across five criteria that most families never manage, and the technology paper leaks method marks that two sessions can close. Collect the route, the level and the mock breakdown by paper, then buy a block with a stated finish rather than a standing weekly slot. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is free with no card details required.

Matching starts from the course, the level, the term your child is in and which component is currently costing the most: a paper, the exploration, or the pace.

intro.heading: The same subject, four different jobs, depending on the week
paragraphs: There is no single answer to what an IB maths tutor should do, because the right work changes completely with the calendar. A DP1 student in the first term needs the Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation decision settled on evidence, and the algebraic fluency that the Diploma assumes and IGCSE does not always deliver. A DP1 student in the summer term needs an exploration topic that will survive contact with actual mathematics. A DP2 student in the autumn needs the exploration finished and Paper 3 technique started. A DP2 student in the spring needs timed papers and nothing else.

Families in Jumeirah 1 usually arrive at tutoring in one of two moments: October of DP1, when the first set of marks lands and the course feels harder than IGCSE ever did, or January of DP2, after mocks. Both are good moments and they require different purchases. The October arrival should buy foundations and a route decision. The January arrival should buy marking cycles and timed practice, and should not buy a tutor who wants to start at the beginning of the syllabus.

Mathematics in the Diploma is also four distinct courses rather than one. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level share topic headings and almost nothing else in character. The weightings differ, the calculator rules differ, Higher Level carries a third paper, and only one of the four has a substantial non-calculator component at Standard Level. A tutor who teaches maths in general will be competent; a tutor who has taught your child's exact course and level will be useful.

One thing this page will not do is state an IB examination or results date. The IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project, and publishing a date we cannot source across a set of pages this size would be a liability rather than a service. Confirm every date with your child's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org. What this page does instead is count the calendar backwards in terms of school terms and internal deadlines, which is the version a family can actually act on.

On delivery, the position is simple. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, and nothing here will promise a tutor at a UAE address; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Jumeirah 1 families are one-to-one over live video, with the student's own work on screen and written work marked between sessions. For a Higher Level maths requirement that trade is strongly in your favour, because the specialist pool for that course is narrow and a driving radius along Jumeirah Beach Road is a blunt way to search it.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.programmesIntro: Diploma mathematics sits at the end of a sequence, and the preparation behind it determines how the first term goes. These are the programmes Jumeirah 1 families ask about, with what each contributes to the maths outcome.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one mathematics course from Group 5, at Higher or Standard Level. Higher Level is recommended at 240 teaching hours and Standard Level at 150, which is the clearest single indicator of the difference. Both courses cover number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, with an exploration worth a fifth of the grade.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools sit the May session, and some also enter candidates in November. No IB session or results date appears on this page because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated fetching for this project. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the session dates, the school's internal exploration deadlines and the mock window, all three of which matter more to planning than the external dates do.

programmes.name: IB MYP Mathematics, Standard and Extended
programmes.description: The IB route into Diploma maths, assessed against four criteria out of eight rather than by paper. MYP Extended Mathematics keeps Higher Level a realistic choice; MYP Standard does not close it but makes it a genuine climb. The transition is partly technical and partly a change in assessment culture, since MYP rarely requires timed written work and the Diploma requires it constantly.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from Jumeirah 1 sits mainly in Al Safa, Umm Al Sheif and the Al Barsha campuses. Some of those schools also enter MYP students for Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607, which is the graphics-calculator route and feeds both Diploma maths courses more smoothly than Cambridge 0580 does.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics before the Diploma
programmes.description: The most common entry route in this district. A student finishing Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher with strong algebra has both Diploma doors open; one finishing Core or Foundation has neither Higher Level door open. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics 0606 is the clearest preparation for Higher Level, because it introduces calculus, logarithms and identities a year early.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For families with a younger sibling on Cambridge papers, the exams officer is the person to ask for the zone, the codes and the tier.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics and Further Mathematics
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in Jumeirah 1, and a useful comparison when a family is deciding between the Diploma and A Levels. A Level Mathematics goes deeper in fewer areas and has no equivalent of the exploration; Diploma maths is broader and carries the internal assessment. Students who prefer sustained independent work often do better with the exploration than they expect.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. A student entering the Diploma after a November IGCSE retake starts DP1 with an exam series immediately behind them, which is worth factoring into the first term's workload.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Diploma maths is five topic areas, two courses, two levels and an exploration. These are the parts Jumeirah 1 families ask about, with what each assesses and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The algebraic route at full depth, recommended at 240 teaching hours. Three papers plus the exploration, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Proof, calculus, complex numbers and series carry most of the lost marks, and Paper 3's extended problem-solving format is unlike anything in the other components.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers plus the exploration, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator and carrying 40% of the grade. That single fact shapes revision: exact values, surds, index laws and differentiation by hand all have to be fluent. Students arriving from a calculator-heavy IGCSE find Paper 1 the harder of the two by a clear margin.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route at Higher Level, with the graphic display calculator used throughout and a third paper. Students choose it expecting an easier course and meet statistical inference, matrices, graph theory and modelling that punishes imprecision. It is not the soft option, and some engineering courses still prefer the analysis route.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two papers plus the exploration, calculator permitted throughout. Statistics, financial mathematics, modelling and basic calculus. The commonest loss is context: students calculate correctly and then fail to interpret the result in the terms the question set, which the mark scheme explicitly asks for.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.levels: HL and SL, all four courses
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematics worth 20% of the grade, marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. The last of those carries the most marks and is where explorations with safe topics lose them, because safe topics do not permit mathematics of sufficient sophistication.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level proof by induction, complex numbers and systems of equations. This is the area where a weak IGCSE foundation shows first, usually in the second half of DP1 rather than in the first weeks.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Linear, quadratic, rational, exponential and logarithmic functions, transformations and inverse functions, with polynomial work and further transformations at Higher Level. Students who can solve equations but cannot read a graph lose marks across every paper, because function behaviour underpins the calculus questions too.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Three-dimensional geometry, trigonometric functions and identities, the sine and cosine rules, radian measure, and at Higher Level vectors, planes and more demanding identities. Radians are a persistent source of avoidable loss, usually because a calculator is left in the wrong mode under time pressure.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, correlation and regression, probability distributions, the normal and binomial distributions, with statistical inference and further distributions at Higher Level in Applications and Interpretation. Marks are lost to interpretation rather than calculation: the number is right and the sentence about what it means is missing.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and optimisation, extending at Higher Level to implicit differentiation, differential equations and Maclaurin series in Analysis and Approaches. It is the topic area that most rewards early work, because everything after it assumes it and because it arrives in DP1 term two when students are still adjusting.

sections.heading: What term is it, and what does that make urgent?
paragraphs: The most useful question a maths tutor can ask a Jumeirah 1 family is not what grade your child is getting. It is which term they are in and what their school's internal deadlines look like. The Diploma is a two-year structure with a fixed shape, and the same weakness has a different price depending on where in that structure it is found. Weak algebra discovered in October of DP1 costs six sessions. The same weak algebra discovered in January of DP2 costs three times that, because by then it is competing with timed practice, the exploration and five other subjects.

There are four moments in the two years where a decision is effectively taken, whether or not anybody notices. The first is the route and level choice, which most schools settle in the autumn of DP1 and which constrains everything after it. The second is the exploration topic, usually chosen in the summer term of DP1, where a safe topic quietly caps the mark. The third is the exploration draft deadline in DP2, after which the work is largely fixed. The fourth is the mock window, which is where a student discovers whether they can produce mathematics under time pressure rather than merely understand it.

None of those four is an external examination date and all four are more actionable, which is why this page is organised around them. Ask your child's Diploma coordinator for three dates in one email: the internal exploration deadlines, the mock window, and the school's deadline for any level change. Those three shape the next year more than the published session dates do, and they vary between Dubai schools by several weeks.

This page states no IB examination or results dates. The IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project, so publishing a date here would mean repeating somebody else's figure without a source. Confirm every IB date with your coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat with caution any tutoring website that states them confidently without saying where they came from.

sections.heading: Four courses, and where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: Group 5 is not one subject. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are distinct courses, each offered at Higher and Standard Level, and the four combinations differ in weighting, calculator use and number of papers. Knowing which one your child sits is the minimum entry ticket for any tutoring conversation, and a surprising number of parents discover halfway through DP1 that they had assumed the wrong one.

The structural facts matter for revision planning. Both Higher Level courses carry three papers plus the exploration, with Papers 1 and 2 at 30% each, Paper 3 at 20% and the exploration at 20%. Both Standard Level courses carry two papers at 40% each plus the exploration at 20%. The single biggest practical difference is the calculator: Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without one at both levels, while Applications and Interpretation permits the graphic display calculator throughout.

That calculator rule changes what revision has to contain. An Analysis and Approaches Standard Level student has 40% of the grade in a paper where exact values, surds, index laws, trigonometric exact ratios and differentiation by hand must be fluent. A student who arrived from a calculator-heavy IGCSE and has not rebuilt that fluency will underperform on Paper 1 by a visible margin while doing perfectly well on Paper 2, and the pattern is diagnosable from a single mock.

The table below is the reference version. Durations are the published shape of each paper, and the last column is the practical consequence a revision plan should respond to. Check it against your child's actual course on the school's subject list, because families and students sometimes use the shorthand names loosely and the four courses are genuinely different.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This choice is made in DP1 and lived with for two years, and it is made badly more often than any other Diploma decision. The common error is to treat Applications and Interpretation as the easier course. At Standard Level it suits a different student rather than a weaker one, and at Higher Level it is demanding in its own direction, with statistical inference, matrices, graph theory and modelling that punishes imprecise interpretation.

The real question is what the student is good at and what the degree plan needs. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic manipulation, proof and abstraction. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, data handling and the ability to explain what a result means in context. A student who enjoyed IGCSE algebra and found statistics tedious belongs in the first; a student who was strong on data and disliked proof belongs in the second, and will do better there than they would have done struggling through the other.

The degree-plan question has to be checked rather than assumed. Some engineering, mathematics and physics courses, in the UAE and overseas, specify Analysis and Approaches or expect Higher Level in it, while others accept either. Course requirements change and vary by institution, so the only reliable method is to read the entry requirements for two or three target universities directly on their own pages during DP1 rather than relying on what the year group believes.

Level is the second half of the decision. Higher Level is recommended at 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and the difference shows in the depth of every topic area plus the third paper. A student taking Higher Level maths because it looks better on a form, while finding DP1 term two genuinely hard, is usually better served by a strong Standard Level grade. Ask the coordinator for the school's deadline for a level change, because it exists and it is earlier than most families expect.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion, with its marks
paragraphs: The exploration carries 20% of the maths grade in all four courses and it is marked out of 20 across five criteria. Those criteria and their mark allocations are published by the IB and almost never set out on a tutoring page, which is why so many explorations are written as though presentation and personal engagement were the whole task. They are worth seven of the twenty marks between them. Use of mathematics is worth six on its own, and it is the criterion a safe topic cannot reach.

That single fact should drive topic choice. An exploration about a personally interesting subject that permits only routine mathematics is capped before a word is written, because the top band of use of mathematics requires work that is sophisticated relative to the course and is demonstrably correct and relevant throughout. A student in Higher Level Analysis and Approaches writing about compound interest has chosen a topic that cannot score in the top band of the criterion that carries the most marks.

Reflection is the criterion most often lost by accident. It rewards critical reflection on the mathematics and the process as the work develops, which means it has to be written while the work happens rather than added in a final paragraph. Explorations where every reflective sentence appears in the conclusion read exactly as they were written, and the mark reflects that. Mathematical communication is the other quiet loss: notation used consistently, variables defined, graphs labelled, terminology correct.

On what a tutor may do: coach topic choice, explain what each criterion's top band requires, ask the questions that produce genuine reflection, and give feedback on drafts the student has written. A tutor may not write the exploration or any section of it, and nobody at IB Gram will. The school supervisor remains the formal supervisor throughout, and the IB's rules about how many drafts a teacher may comment on are the school's to apply.

sections.heading: The two Diploma years, counted backwards
paragraphs: Counting backwards is the only way to see which deadlines have already bound a decision. Working forwards, a family in DP1 believes everything is open and then discovers in DP2 that the level change closed in the autumn and the exploration topic was effectively fixed in June. Working backwards from the final papers, the sequence becomes obvious and each term acquires a job.

The table below is that sequence in school terms rather than in dates, because Dubai schools run their internal deadlines on their own calendars and those differ by several weeks. Take it to your child's Diploma coordinator and fill in the actual dates for the three internal milestones that matter: the exploration draft and final deadlines, the mock window, and the cut-off for a level change. With those in place the plan becomes specific.

Two features of the sequence are worth naming. The first is that DP1 term two, when calculus arrives, is the heaviest teaching term in the two years and the cheapest place to intervene. The second is that DP2 term one is when the exploration and new Higher Level content compete directly, which is why explorations written in that term are so often thinner than the student was capable of. Finishing the exploration early is the single most effective scheduling decision available in Diploma maths.

The final term is not a teaching term. By the spring of DP2 the work is timed papers, marking and correction, with non-calculator drilling running alongside for Analysis and Approaches students and separate Paper 3 sessions for Higher Level. A tutor who wants to teach new content in that window has misread the calendar, and a family who hires one in March expecting foundations to be rebuilt has bought the wrong product at the worst moment.

sections.heading: What the next eight weeks actually have to achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the standard unit of serious Diploma revision, and it works whether it runs up to mocks or to the final papers. What it cannot do is teach two years of content, and a plan that pretends otherwise collapses in week three. What it can do is convert understanding into marks, which is a different and more achievable job: fix the two weakest topic areas, build the habit of writing method, drill the non-calculator skills, and sit enough whole papers to make timing automatic.

The block has a shape and the shape matters. Weeks one and two are diagnostic and foundational: a full past paper sat to time, every lost mark classified by topic and by cause, and the two weakest topic areas addressed directly. Weeks three to five are timed questions by topic, because a student who can do a question slowly cannot necessarily do it in the time the paper allows. Weeks six and seven are whole papers under examination conditions. Week eight is the correction of everything found in weeks six and seven, plus the logistics.

Two sessions a week is the right frequency, and the reason is marking rather than teaching time. Two sessions mean two rounds of written work marked, corrected and re-tested, and that cycle predicts movement better than hours taught. A third weekly session usually displaces the independent practice that the sessions are meant to be improving, and past that point a family is buying reassurance rather than marks.

The table sets the eight weeks out with a deliverable for each one, because a block without deliverables becomes a block of conversations. Note the last column: each week has a way of telling whether it worked. If week five's timed questions are still running fifty per cent over time, the plan changes rather than continuing. That is the difference between a revision programme and a standing appointment.

sections.heading: Paper 1 without a calculator, and Paper 3 at Higher Level
paragraphs: Two components in Diploma maths need their own treatment and rarely get it. The first is Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches, sat without a calculator at both levels and carrying 40% of the Standard Level grade and 30% at Higher Level. Students arriving from a calculator-permitted IGCSE often have no recent experience of working by hand, and the result is a visible gap between their Paper 1 and Paper 2 performance in every mock.

The skills involved are specific and drillable: exact trigonometric ratios, surd manipulation, index and logarithm laws, differentiating and integrating by hand, exact-form answers, and recognising when an expression simplifies before it is expanded. None of them is conceptually hard and all of them decay without use. The format that works is short and frequent: fifteen minutes four times a week beats ninety minutes once, because the aim is automaticity rather than understanding.

The second component is Paper 3, sat only at Higher Level and worth 20%. It presents extended problem-solving questions that build through linked parts, often in unfamiliar contexts, and it rewards a different skill from Papers 1 and 2: reading a long stem, extracting the structure, and following a chain of reasoning where each part depends on the last. Students who are strong on Papers 1 and 2 can still be caught by it, because nothing else in the course looks like it.

Paper 3 needs separate practice sessions rather than inclusion in general revision, and it needs them earlier than most students start. The useful work is attempting past Paper 3 questions in full, with the mark scheme discussed afterwards, paying attention to how a part that was answered wrongly affected everything after it. Six to eight of those, spread through DP2, usually converts Paper 3 from a liability into a component where the extended format works in a strong student's favour.

sections.heading: What exam-year maths support costs in this market
paragraphs: Start at the top, because that is where exam-year Diploma maths sits and because it makes the rest of the market legible. The highest published figure found in this market in October 2026 was AED 650 an hour from a named-tutor service. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, with a UK agency operating in the Gulf publishing AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for weekly sessions.

Work down from there. A qualified subject tutor working online is published in a band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, and one Dubai agency's rate card listed IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Bestimate estimates that mid-range tier at AED 600 to 1,200 a month for weekly one-hour sessions. At the bottom, budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour inside a band of roughly AED 45 to 150, estimated monthly at AED 240 to 600. In-home one-to-one across Dubai is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is included.

For a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches student in DP2 the relevant arithmetic is not the hourly rate but the eight-week block. Two sessions a week for eight weeks is sixteen hours. At the specialist band that is a defined, visible number, and it buys sixteen marking cycles at the only point in the two years when marking cycles convert directly into marks. The same budget spread as one unmarked hour a week across both years usually buys less movement, which is a scheduling result rather than a pricing one.

None of these figures is an IB Gram price and this page publishes none; the free trial lesson and the consultation are where our own fees are discussed. Two context notes. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. And no tutor at any price can promise a grade: a provider who offers one is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child's mathematics.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Beach Road and holding the slot through the year
paragraphs: A two-year plan survives or fails on whether the weekly slot holds, and in this district two things threaten it. The first is Jumeirah Beach Road in the afternoon, which is slower than its distance suggests and which makes any slot before 16:45 optimistic for families on the coastal side. Students in Al Hudaiba and the Al Wasl corridor often get home earlier, because the journey runs away from the coast. Set the slot from arrival time in September and it will still be there in March.

The second is Ramadan. School days shorten, afternoons compress and the productive study window moves to the evening after Iftar. Families who shift the maths slot two to three hours later and keep the frequency hold the marking cycle through the month. Families who pause usually lose six weeks rather than four, because restarting takes a fortnight of re-finding the thread. For a DP2 student, Ramadan often falls close enough to the final session that losing six weeks is not recoverable.

School holidays cut the other way and are underused. The winter and spring breaks in a DP2 year are the only blocks of uninterrupted time available, and they are where whole timed papers belong, because two hours of examination conditions is not available at 17:30 on a Tuesday for anybody. Three papers sat properly over a holiday is worth more than six weeks of weekday question sets, and it costs the student less in total time.

One practical note on logistics, which belongs in week eight of any block. Check the graphic display calculator model against the school's requirement, make sure it is the one the student has practised on, clear its memory as the school instructs, and have a spare set of batteries. A Higher Level student who meets an unfamiliar calculator interface in a calculator-permitted paper has lost marks to something entirely preventable, and it happens every session somewhere.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, permits and what we will not claim
paragraphs: The exploration is the place where academic honesty in Diploma maths is tested, and the boundary is worth stating precisely. A tutor may discuss candidate topics, explain what each criterion's top band requires, suggest mathematical techniques the student might investigate, ask the questions that produce genuine reflection, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced. A tutor may not write the exploration, produce any section of it, or carry out the mathematics on the student's behalf, and nobody at IB Gram will.

That is not a formality. Academic honesty breaches in the IB fall on the student, and an exploration that does not match the student's demonstrated ability is visible to a supervisor who has taught them for a year. One provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Buying that risks a student's entire Diploma to save a few weeks of work, and the school supervisor remains the formal supervisor whatever anybody else is paid to do.

Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit, and the detail is checkable rather than vague. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here.

Three claims this page does not make. No tutor is described as a current IB examiner unless that status can be evidenced, because the claim is widespread in this market and the evidence rarely is. No individual tutor is KHDA approved, because the KHDA Educational Services Permit is issued to training institutes with premises and IB Gram operates none in the UAE. And no grade or score is promised, at any level or any price, because no honest provider can promise one. Official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to the IB, so this page cites and links rather than hosting them.

process.title: Say which course, which level, which term
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard Level, and where your child is in the two years. Those three facts determine almost everything about the right plan, and the first is the one families most often get wrong because the shorthand names are used loosely.

process.title: Get three internal dates from the coordinator
process.description: The exploration draft and final deadlines, the mock window, and the school's cut-off for a level change. Dubai schools run these on their own calendars and they differ by several weeks, so a plan built on a general Diploma timeline will be wrong for your child by a fortnight or more.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a marked assessment
process.description: One trial lesson, one subject, before any paid block is booked. The tutor works through the most recent marked paper, separates topic weakness from timing weakness from method-mark loss, and says what eight weeks would target. You decide afterwards whether to continue.

process.title: Run the eight-week block with deliverables
process.description: Diagnostic and the two weakest topic areas first, then timed questions by topic, then whole papers with marking between them. Each week has something to show, so by week five it is clear whether the plan is working rather than whether everybody is trying hard.

process.title: Hold the exploration to its own timeline
process.description: Fortnightly check-ins from the DP1 summer term: a topic that permits sophisticated mathematics, a scope that can be finished, reflection written as the work develops, and all five criteria evidenced deliberately. Finishing early is the single most effective scheduling decision in the two years.

process.title: Protect the slot through Ramadan and the holidays
process.description: Move the weekly session two to three hours later for Ramadan rather than pausing, and use the winter and spring breaks for whole timed papers, which cannot be sat properly on a weekday evening. Both decisions should be made in September, not in the week they arrive.

whyPoints.title: The plan is built from the term, not from the grade
whyPoints.description: A DP1 October problem and a DP2 January problem are different purchases even when the grade is identical. We ask which term and which internal deadlines before anything else, because the same weakness costs three times as much to fix a year later.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as 20% of the grade
whyPoints.description: Five criteria, twenty marks, with use of mathematics worth six of them. We coach topic choice against that mark allocation rather than against personal interest alone, and we give feedback on the student's own drafts without producing any part of the work.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 and Paper 3 practised separately
whyPoints.description: Non-calculator Paper 1 skills respond to short frequent drilling, and Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended linked format unlike anything else in the course. Folding either into general revision is why strong students are still surprised by them in a mock.

whyPoints.title: Two marking cycles a week, not two extra hours
whyPoints.description: Written work is marked between sessions and the next lesson starts from the corrections. In the final eight weeks the number of marking cycles predicts movement better than the number of hours taught, which is why frequency beats session length.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources and dates
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is somebody else's published number, read in October 2026 and attributed, including what a sixteen-hour block costs at each tier. We do not present market rates as ours, and we do not hide a figure behind a form.

whyPoints.title: No dates or claims we cannot source
whyPoints.description: No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project. No grade is promised, no examiner status is asserted without evidence, and we run no in-home service anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: It is the autumn term and my child is in DP2. What should maths work be doing right now?
faqs.answer: Two things in parallel and nothing else. The exploration should be moving towards a complete draft, with reflection written as the mathematics develops rather than added at the end, because an exploration finished in the autumn stops competing with mock revision in the new year. Alongside that, current Higher or Standard Level content needs to keep pace, with method written out in full on every question. New foundational teaching at this point is usually the wrong purchase; the exception is a genuine algebra gap, which has to be fixed now because it only gets more expensive.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade is the exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four courses and at both levels, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria. That makes it worth more than any single paper at Higher Level, where Papers 1 and 2 carry thirty per cent each and Paper 3 carries twenty. Families routinely treat it as a side task and then find they have conceded a fifth of the grade. The practical consequence is that the hours spent on exploration supervision in DP1 summer and DP2 autumn are among the best-value tutoring hours in the two years.

faqs.question: What are the five exploration criteria and what is each worth?
faqs.answer: Criterion A, presentation, is worth four marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, is worth four. Criterion C, personal engagement, is worth three. Criterion D, reflection, is worth three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, is worth six, making it the single largest component. Twenty marks in total. The allocation matters because it shows where the topic decision bites: a topic that permits only routine mathematics caps criterion E before anything is written, and criterion E is nearly a third of the exploration mark on its own.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on my child's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary worth being precise about. A tutor can discuss candidate topics, explain what each criterion's top band requires, suggest techniques worth investigating, ask the questions that produce genuine reflection, and give written feedback on drafts the student has produced themselves. A tutor must not write the exploration, produce any section of it, or carry out the mathematics for the student, and nobody at IB Gram will. The school supervisor remains the formal supervisor, and the school applies the IB's rules on how many drafts may be commented on.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches harder than Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than uniformly harder, and treating Applications and Interpretation as the easy option is the commonest error in this choice. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic manipulation, proof and abstraction, and sits Paper 1 without a calculator at both levels. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-permitted throughout and rewards modelling, data handling and interpretation in context, with statistical inference, matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. A student strong on data and weak on proof will achieve more in the second course than they would struggling through the first.

faqs.question: My child wants to move from Higher Level to Standard Level maths. When is the deadline?
faqs.answer: Ask the Diploma coordinator, because it is set by the school and it is earlier than most families expect, usually in the autumn or spring of DP1. The decision deserves evidence rather than feeling: a marked assessment, the pace in calculus, and the entry requirements of two or three target universities read on their own pages. Higher Level is recommended at 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard, and a strong Standard Level grade is frequently a better outcome than a struggling Higher Level one, including for applications.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 at Higher Level actually ask for?
faqs.answer: Extended problem-solving questions that build through linked parts, often in unfamiliar contexts, worth twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade. The skill it tests is different from Papers 1 and 2: reading a long stem, extracting the mathematical structure, and sustaining a chain of reasoning where each part depends on the one before. A wrong answer in an early part can cost everything after it. Students strong on the other papers are still caught by it, because nothing else in the course resembles it, which is why it needs its own practice sessions.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 without a calculator such a problem for Dubai students?
faqs.answer: Because most arrive from an IGCSE route where a calculator was permitted on at least one paper and often on both, so recent experience of working by hand is thin. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is non-calculator and carries forty per cent of the Standard Level grade. The specific skills are exact trigonometric ratios, surds, index and logarithm laws, differentiating and integrating by hand, and exact-form answers. They are drillable and they decay without use, so fifteen minutes four times a week works far better than one long session.

faqs.question: How long before the final session should intensive maths work start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks for a focused block, sixteen if two blocks with a gap are possible, and a full year earlier if there is a genuine foundational gap. Eight weeks is enough to convert understanding into marks: fix the two weakest topic areas, build the habit of writing method, drill the non-calculator skills and sit enough whole papers for timing to become automatic. What eight weeks cannot do is teach two years of content, so a plan that implies otherwise should be questioned before it is paid for.

faqs.question: What should the eight weeks before mocks achieve?
faqs.answer: A specific list rather than a general improvement. Weeks one and two produce a diagnosis naming the two weakest topic areas from a full paper sat to time. Weeks three to five produce accuracy on those topics and then pace, with method written out. Weeks six and seven produce two whole papers sat under examination conditions and marked strictly. Week eight produces a final list of three remaining weaknesses. If by week five timed questions still run far over time, the plan should change rather than continue.

faqs.question: Where can I check the IB examination dates for my child's session?
faqs.answer: With your child's Diploma coordinator, or on ibo.org directly. This page states no IB examination or results date, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project and repeating an unsourced date across a large set of pages would be a liability rather than a service. More useful for planning are the three internal dates the school controls: the exploration draft and final deadlines, the mock window and the cut-off for a level change. Those differ between Dubai schools by several weeks.

faqs.question: Does the November session work differently from the May session for maths?
faqs.answer: The components and weightings are the same; what changes is where the session sits in the school year, which changes the whole revision calendar. A November candidate's eight-week block falls in the first half of the autumn term, when school teaching is still delivering new content, so the competition for time is different from a May candidate's spring. Ask your coordinator which session your child is entered for and when the school's internal deadlines sit relative to it, because the plan on this page has to be shifted rather than simply reused.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a DP2 student need in the final term?
faqs.answer: Two, and the reason is marking cycles rather than hours. Two sessions mean two rounds of written work marked, corrected and re-tested each week, and that cycle predicts movement better than teaching time does. A third weekly session usually displaces the independent past-paper practice the sessions exist to improve, at which point a family is buying reassurance. One session a week remains worthwhile for maintenance, but in the final eight weeks it halves the number of cycles available.

faqs.question: What does exam-year IB maths support cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published figures read in October 2026 put specialist IB tutors at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with a UK agency in the Gulf publishing AED 270 and a named-tutor service publishing AED 650. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for weekly sessions. For a sixteen-hour eight-week block at the specialist band, that is a defined figure you can budget. None of these is our price list.

faqs.question: Should my child use the graphic display calculator for every paper?
faqs.answer: It depends on the course. Applications and Interpretation permits it on every paper at both levels. Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without it at both levels, so a student who has practised everything with the calculator in hand will be exposed there. Practical points for the week before any paper: confirm the model against the school's requirement, use the one the student has actually practised on, follow the school's instruction on clearing the memory, and carry spare batteries. Unfamiliar calculator interfaces cost marks for entirely preventable reasons.

faqs.question: How should a maths slot in Jumeirah 1 change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move it later and keep the frequency. School days shorten, afternoons compress and the productive window shifts to the evening after Iftar, so shifting the session two to three hours later keeps the marking cycle intact. Families who pause for the month usually lose six weeks rather than four, because restarting takes a fortnight of re-finding the thread, and for a DP2 student that can be unrecoverable. Decide the shift in September rather than in the week it arrives, and treat the school holidays as the place for whole timed papers.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingHeading: Work out which term it is, then plan backwards
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.closingBody: Before you buy any hours, establish three things: which of the four maths courses your child actually sits, which term they are in, and what the school's internal deadlines are for the exploration, the mocks and any level change. With those in hand the next eight weeks acquire a specific job, and the exploration stops being a fifth of the grade nobody is managing. Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and online, with one free trial lesson in one subject before any paid block, written work marked between sessions, no IB dates we cannot source, and no in-home service anywhere in the UAE.

intro.heading: Why the school run decides your IB maths timetable
paragraphs: Jumeirah 2 is a villa district squeezed between Jumeirah Beach Road and Al Wasl Road, with Jumeirah 1 on one side and Jumeirah 3 on the other. There is no metro station inside it. The nearest Red Line platforms sit over on Sheikh Zayed Road, which means almost every secondary pupil here is driven to school and driven home again. That single fact shapes tutoring more than any syllabus detail: the window between the car pulling in and homework starting is narrow, and it moves twice a year as school timetables change.

Most Dubai secondary schools release Years 10 to 13 somewhere between 14:45 and 15:30. Add the drive back along Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road at exactly the hour every other school empties, and a Jumeirah 2 pupil is rarely at a desk before 16:00. Families who book a tutor for 15:30 end up paying for the first ten minutes of a lesson their child spends arriving. Families who book for 19:45, after food and a break, usually get a full hour of work - but only if the tutor is sitting in a time zone where 19:45 in Dubai is a civilised hour to teach.

That is the practical case for online delivery here, and online is the only kind of delivery IB Gram offers in the UAE. Home visits in Dubai are not part of the service; they exist only in India. A UAE lesson runs live, one to one, over video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on and the board work saved afterwards. Nobody is charged for a tutor's drive from Mirdif, and nobody loses a session because Jumeirah Beach Road is closed for an event at the park.

The second thing the school run decides is which school your child attends, and therefore which version of IB Mathematics they are sitting. Jumeirah 2 feeds an unusually mixed set of schools: IB continuum schools in Al Safa and Jumeirah 1, British schools running IGCSE then A Level, and a number of families whose children cross Al Sufouh Road each morning. Two pupils on the same street can be sitting Analysis and Approaches HL and Applications and Interpretation SL - courses with different papers, different calculator rules and almost no shared revision material.

So the first job of an IB maths tutor in Jumeirah 2 is administrative before it is mathematical: establish the course route, the paper structure, the school's internal deadline for the exploration, and the exact day of the week on which the diary falls apart. Everything after that is teaching. The sections below set out the school-day clock for the clusters Jumeirah 2 families actually use, the Analysis-versus-Applications decision, how each paper is weighted, where marks leak, and what a tutor is allowed to do with an exploration draft under IB academic-honesty rules.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Jumeirah 2 children sit in three different IB programmes depending on their school, and maths looks nothing alike across them. One has no examinations at all, one is marked against four criteria out of eight, and one ends in a timed paper sat without a calculator. The notes below say what each stage assesses and what that means for a family living on this side of Al Wasl Road.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Maths in the PYP is taught inside transdisciplinary units rather than as a separate subject block, and there is no external examination. Number sense, pattern, measurement and data handling are assessed continuously by the class teacher. Because nothing is examined, a gap in fraction or place-value fluency can sit unnoticed for two or three years and only announce itself in Year 7, when written methods start to be marked.
programmes.countryNote: Several Jumeirah and Al Safa schools run the PYP, which is why so many Jumeirah 2 enquiries arrive at the start of Year 7 rather than during primary. The useful intervention at PYP age is short and specific: twenty-minute slots on times tables, written division and fraction equivalence, scheduled before the school run tightens up in secondary. Nothing about this stage needs a two-year plan.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most schools stream into standard and extended mathematics by MYP 4. The criteria matter more than the topic list, because a pupil can be fluent at calculation and still score poorly on criterion B, which rewards finding and justifying a general rule.
programmes.countryNote: In Jumeirah the MYP-to-Diploma step is the single most common reason a family starts tutoring. Extended MYP Mathematics prepares a pupil for Analysis and Approaches; standard mathematics usually does not, and the gap shows up in the first six weeks of DP1. A Jumeirah 2 pupil who is told in MYP 5 that they will take Analysis and Approaches HL needs algebraic manipulation drilled over the summer, not in September.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma offers two maths courses, each at Standard and Higher Level. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic method, proof and calculus done by hand; Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and the interpretation of data. Both finish with the mathematical exploration, an independent written investigation worth a fifth of the grade and marked against five criteria by the teacher before external moderation.
programmes.countryNote: Jumeirah 2 families choosing between the routes should check the target degree first, not the child's current grade. Engineering and economics courses at research universities frequently name Analysis and Approaches; some design, psychology and business courses accept either. Option blocks are set by the school, so the decision happens months before DP1 begins, and that is the right moment for one honest conversation rather than a year of rescue work.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: This page is about maths, so the list below is maths and the subjects that lean hardest on it. A Jumeirah 2 pupil struggling with Physics HL mechanics is often struggling with vectors and differentiation, and a pupil losing marks in Economics HL is often losing them on a diagram axis rather than on the theory.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The most algebraically demanding route in the Diploma. Proof, complex numbers, vectors and a long calculus strand, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Marks leak on manipulation under time pressure rather than on understanding, which is why timed non-calculator practice is the core of HL tutoring.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Same flavour, shorter syllabus: functions, trigonometry, differentiation and integration, probability and statistics. Standard Level pupils commonly arrive from extended MYP Mathematics or from IGCSE Extended and find the step is in notation and rigour rather than in topic difficulty.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, matrices, graph theory, regression and statistical inference, with a calculator allowed in every paper. The Higher Level course is widely under-estimated: the statistics strand is substantial and Paper 3 asks for an extended modelling investigation under exam conditions.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Built around real contexts: financial maths, trigonometry in applied settings, descriptive statistics, probability distributions and simple calculus. The common failure is not calculation but reading - pupils lose marks by answering a question the stimulus did not ask.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A written investigation of around twelve to twenty pages, marked against five criteria worth twenty marks in total and carrying a fifth of the grade. Support here is coaching on topic choice, structure and notation plus feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor who contributes written content has broken IB academic-honesty rules.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics (standard and extended)
subjects.description: Marked on four criteria out of eight each. Criterion B, investigating patterns, is where most Jumeirah pupils lose ground, because it asks for a general rule to be found, tested and justified rather than for an answer to be produced.

subjects.name: Physics HL and SL
subjects.description: Paired with maths more often than any other subject on this page. Mechanics, fields and circuits all depend on algebraic rearrangement, vector resolution and graph gradients, so a maths intervention frequently lifts physics marks as a side effect.

subjects.name: Economics HL and SL
subjects.description: The quantitative strand - elasticity calculations, cost and revenue curves, the HL numerical paper - sinks more Diploma economics grades in Dubai than the essay content does. Tutoring here is diagram discipline and arithmetic accuracy under time.

subjects.name: Computer Science HL and SL
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, complexity, binary arithmetic and data structures overlap with Applications and Interpretation. Pupils who chose Computer Science alongside a Standard Level maths course often need the discrete strand taught explicitly rather than assumed.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.regionsTitle: Jumeirah 2 and the streets either side of it
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.regionsIntro: Jumeirah 2 does not sit on its own. Children here go to school with children from Jumeirah 1, Jumeirah 3, Al Safa, Al Wasl and Umm Suqeim, and the practical question is always the same: how long is the drive home, and what time does that leave for maths. The notes below are written from the clock, not the postcode.

regions.name: Jumeirah 1
regions.note: The closest neighbour, and the one that shares the most schools. A pupil living on the Jumeirah 1 side is often home by 15:15, which is the one case where a 15:45 start is genuinely workable rather than theoretical.

regions.name: Jumeirah 3
regions.note: Lower-density villas running down towards Umm Suqeim, with Jumeirah Beach Park on the boundary. Families here more often use schools towards Al Sufouh, which adds fifteen minutes each way and pushes the first realistic slot to 16:30.

regions.name: Al Wasl
regions.note: Immediately inland across Al Wasl Road. Short drives in principle, but the road itself is the bottleneck at dismissal. Several Al Wasl families book the 19:30 slot purely to avoid making the journey a second time in a day.

regions.name: Al Safa
regions.note: Home to a cluster of British and IB schools used heavily by Jumeirah 2 families. Pupils are usually back before 15:30, and the Al Safa cluster produces more Analysis and Approaches enquiries than any other on this list.

regions.name: Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Further along the coast, with a longer run back to Jumeirah 2 if siblings are at different schools. Split pick-ups here regularly destroy the 16:00 slot, which is why evening sessions dominate in this group.

regions.name: Pearl Jumeira
regions.note: Reclaimed land off the Jumeirah coast with a single access route. Traffic is light but the detour is real, and families tend to prefer a 90-minute weekend block to two shorter weekday sessions.

regions.note: Inland and well placed for the Al Barsha and Al Quoz schools. Those runs can take half an hour at dismissal, so Al Manara enquiries almost always arrive asking about slots after 19:00.

regions.note: Apartment living closer to the city, with a shorter commute in the opposite direction. Pupils here often have more after-school activity scheduled, so the constraint is the activity calendar rather than the road.

The mix is the point: an IB continuum school and a British school running IGCSE can sit two streets apart, which is why neighbours end up on different maths courses with different calculator rules and different internal deadlines.

sections.heading: What a Jumeirah 2 search for an IB maths tutor usually means
paragraphs: Parents in Jumeirah 2 type this phrase for one of three reasons, and they need different answers. The first group has a DP1 pupil who was comfortable in MYP Mathematics and is now below their predicted grade six weeks into Analysis and Approaches. The second has a DP2 pupil whose exploration deadline is close and whose draft has no mathematics in it above course level. The third has a Year 11 family choosing option blocks and trying to work out whether Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation is the honest choice.

None of those three is solved by the same weekly hour. The DP1 case is a fluency problem and responds to short, frequent, drilled sessions. The exploration case is a single piece of coaching plus feedback on a draft the student writes themselves. The route case needs one conversation with somebody who has read both syllabuses, and then nothing at all until September. A tutoring arrangement that treats all three as 'weekly maths help' wastes money on at least two of them.

The word 'in Jumeirah 2' in the search is about availability rather than geography. Parents want to know that somebody can teach their child's exact course at the hour their child is actually free, and that the arrangement does not depend on who happens to live within driving distance of a villa off Jumeirah Beach Road. Delivering lessons online answers that: the constraint becomes the timetable instead of the traffic, and a Higher Level specialist is reachable whether or not anybody with that specialism lives in Jumeirah.

sections.heading: The Jumeirah 2 school-day clock, and the slot that survives it
paragraphs: Dismissal times are published by each school and they move between phases and between years, so treat the table below as the shape of the problem rather than as your child's timetable. The pattern holds across the Jumeirah clusters: secondary pupils come out between a quarter to three and half past three, the roads around Al Wasl Road and Jumeirah Beach Road absorb every school in the district at once, and the honest start time for a lesson is between thirty and ninety minutes after the bell depending on where the school sits.

Two things make the picture worse than the raw drive time suggests. The first is split pick-ups: a family with a primary child in Jumeirah and a secondary child in Al Sufouh is making two journeys, and the second one ends after four o'clock. The second is activity scheduling. Swimming, football and music in this part of Dubai cluster between five and seven in the evening, which means the slot that looked free at 17:00 in September is gone by October.

The practical answer is to pick a slot that cannot be destroyed by either, and then defend it. For families inside the Jumeirah and Al Safa ring, that is usually 16:00 on a fixed weekday. For everyone else it is 19:30. Once chosen, the slot should stay put for the term: a pupil who is taught at a different hour every week never builds the habit of arriving with questions, and the first ten minutes of every session go on remembering where the last one stopped.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets two years
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects how much tutoring a Jumeirah 2 family ends up buying, and it is usually made on the wrong evidence. Pupils choose the route their friends chose, or the one their MYP teacher expects, or the one with the reputation for being easier. The correct test is narrower: read the entry requirements of the degree courses your child is plausibly applying to, and see which route is named. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics courses at research universities frequently specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level.

The two courses are not a hard version and an easy version of the same subject. Analysis and Approaches is a methods course: proof, algebraic manipulation, trigonometric identities, calculus done by hand, and a Paper 1 sat with no calculator at all. Applications and Interpretation is an applied course: modelling, regression, statistical inference, matrices and graph theory, with a graphic display calculator permitted in every paper. A pupil who is strong at structured calculation and weak at interpreting a messy context will find Analysis and Approaches easier, and the reverse is just as true.

Getting this wrong costs more than a bad fit. A pupil on Analysis and Approaches HL who cannot manipulate algebra at speed spends two years on remediation and still loses marks on Paper 1. A pupil on Applications and Interpretation who then applies for engineering discovers in Year 13 that the prerequisite is missing. Both are expensive, and both are avoidable with one honest conversation in Year 11 - which is a single consultation, not a tutoring contract.

sections.heading: How IB Mathematics is weighted, paper by paper
paragraphs: Weightings decide where revision time should go, and most pupils do not know them. Standard Level on either route is two written papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty. Higher Level is three written papers - thirty, thirty and twenty per cent - plus the same exploration at twenty. That means a Higher Level pupil who ignores Paper 3 until April has left a fifth of the grade untouched, which is exactly as much as the exploration they have been worrying about since DP1.

The calculator rule is the other structural fact worth internalising. On Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so every piece of arithmetic, surd manipulation and exact trigonometric value has to be secure by hand. Pupils who have done all their practice with a graphic display calculator in front of them discover this in the first mock and lose marks that have nothing to do with understanding. On Applications and Interpretation the calculator is permitted throughout, and the failure mode flips: pupils lose marks on syntax, on rounding, and on not showing the method the mark scheme wants to see.

Confirm the current weightings and component structure with your child's Diploma coordinator before building a revision plan on them. The IB publishes and revises subject guides on its own site, and a tutoring page is not the right authority for an assessment detail that decides how a family spends four hundred hours. The structure below is the shape of the course as taught in Dubai schools this year; the coordinator holds the version that applies to your child's cohort.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually leak
paragraphs: Almost nobody loses an IB maths grade because of a topic they have never met. Grades go on four recurring, diagnosable failures, and all four are visible in a marked past paper within twenty minutes. The first is arithmetic and algebraic slips under time pressure: a sign lost in a rearrangement, a bracket expanded wrongly, a surd left unsimplified. Each costs one or two marks, and across a full paper they are the difference between a five and a six.

The second is method marks never claimed. The mark scheme rewards a stated method even where the final answer is wrong, and pupils who do their working on a separate sheet or in their head forfeit those marks silently. The third is command-word blindness: 'hence' means use the previous result, 'show that' means the answer is given and the working is the mark, and 'write down' means no working is expected. Pupils who treat all three the same way either waste minutes or leave marks on the table.

The fourth is pacing. Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward finishing, and a pupil who spends twelve minutes on a four-mark question has already lost more than that question is worth. Fixing pacing is not a teaching problem; it is a timed-practice problem, which is why the weekend block exists. A diagnostic session that marks one recent paper against these four categories tells a Jumeirah 2 family more about where the money should go than any amount of general revision.
