sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is worth a fifth of the grade, is marked by the class teacher against five criteria and is then externally moderated. The criteria total twenty marks and they are not evenly weighted, which matters enormously for how a pupil spends their time. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty marks on its own: an exploration with a tidy structure, careful notation and no mathematics above course level cannot score well, however pleasant it is to read.

The commonest Dubai failure pattern is a topic chosen for interest rather than for mathematical depth. A survey of classmates analysed with a mean and a bar chart is a perfectly nice piece of work that cannot reach the top band of criterion E on a Higher Level course. The fix happens at topic stage, months before any writing: test the idea by asking which techniques from the syllabus it will force the student to use, and whether those techniques sit at or above the level of the course.

What a tutor may do here is bounded by IB academic-honesty rules, and the boundary is worth stating plainly because the search results around this query are not all honest about it. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards, teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, reads the student's own draft and says where the argument breaks. A tutor who contributes written content, supplies a topic ready-made, or edits prose into its final state has produced work that is not the candidate's, which is malpractice and puts the student's whole Diploma at risk. IB Gram does not supply exploration content, and no tutor on the platform is permitted to.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the timetable hours KHDA requires
paragraphs: Parents weighing up a maths slot often ask why their child's school day is already so full. Part of the answer is regulatory. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA's published requirements had to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Those lessons occupy real timetable space alongside the Diploma or IGCSE programme, which is one reason a Higher Level maths pupil in Jumeirah has fewer free periods than their cousin in London.

The rules are specific. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson should run shorter than twenty-five minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for the two groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

For a tutoring plan, two consequences follow. First, the week has less slack in it than the published finishing time suggests, so a realistic plan books one defended slot rather than three hopeful ones. Second, mandatory-subject content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so a family wanting Arabic support should work from the school's own materials. IB Gram is not a party to any of this and holds no approval from KHDA or the Ministry of Education; the rules are described here because they shape your child's week.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the May session in a Jumeirah diary
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May Diploma session, and the single most useful planning habit is to count backwards from it rather than forwards from today. The IB publishes session and results dates on its own site and revises them, so confirm every date with your child's Diploma coordinator; no tutoring website should be the authority on when an examination falls. What can be planned without a date is the order of work, and that order is remarkably stable from cohort to cohort.

Eighteen months out, at the start of DP1, the jobs are structural: route confirmed, calculator bought and learned, notation habits established, one defended weekly slot in the diary. Twelve to fourteen months out, the exploration topic should be shortlisted and tested for mathematical depth against criterion E - the single highest-value hour of coaching in the whole two years. Eight to ten months out, a first draft exists and gets one round of feedback. From four to six months out, the work becomes timed papers and an error log, and in the final six to eight weeks it becomes Paper 1 without a calculator, Paper 3 technique for Higher Level, and nothing new at all.

For a Jumeirah 2 family the practical point is that the shape of the week changes across those phases. DP1 runs comfortably on a 16:00 weekday hour. DP2 does not: it needs the 19:30 slot or a weekend block, because a full Paper 2 cannot be sat in sixty minutes after a school run. Families who plan for that in advance keep the same tutor through both phases; families who do not tend to change tutor in January of DP2, which is the worst possible month to start again.

process.title: Tell us the course route and the clock
process.description: The enquiry form asks for two things most tutoring forms do not: which maths course your child is sitting, including level and route, and what time they are realistically free on a school day. Those two answers determine which tutors can be offered at all, so getting them right saves a wasted trial lesson.

process.title: A free trial lesson in the slot you actually want
process.description: One trial lesson per student, at no charge, booked before any fee is discussed. It runs in the slot you intend to keep rather than whenever a tutor happens to be free, because a trial at 15:30 tells you nothing about how your child works at 19:30 after the drive home from Al Sufouh.

process.title: A written plan against your school's deadlines
process.description: After the trial the tutor writes a short plan: the topics to repair in order, the internal exploration deadline from your child's school, which papers get timed and when. It is a page, not a brochure, and it is the thing to hold the arrangement against in six weeks' time.

process.title: Weekly notes, and a different tutor if the match is wrong
process.description: Each session ends with a note on what was covered, what was set and what is still weak. If the match is not working, say so and a different tutor is arranged; a pupil who does not want to talk to their tutor will not ask the questions that make a session worth paying for.

process.title: A change of shape when DP2 starts
process.description: The arrangement is reviewed when the pupil moves into the second Diploma year, because the sixty-minute weekday hour that suited DP1 cannot hold a full timed paper. Most Jumeirah 2 families move to a 19:30 session or a weekend block at that point and keep the same tutor.

whyPoints.title: Matching starts with the route, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different papers and different calculator rules. A tutor is proposed for your child only if they teach that route at that level, which is a narrower filter than 'maths tutor in Dubai' and the reason the first lesson is usually productive.

whyPoints.title: The tutor pool is not limited by driving distance
whyPoints.description: Because every UAE lesson runs online, the question is never whether a Higher Level specialist happens to live near Jumeirah Beach Road. It is whether one is free at your slot. A family in Jumeirah 2 gets the same choice of Analysis and Approaches HL teachers as a family anywhere else.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated in writing, not implied
whyPoints.description: The exploration is the student's work. Tutors teach the mathematics, explain the criteria and give feedback on drafts the student has written. Nobody on this platform supplies exploration content, and the limit is written into the plan you receive after the trial so there is no ambiguity later.

whyPoints.title: Sessions built around the Jumeirah school run
whyPoints.description: Slots are offered at 16:00, 16:30, 19:30 and weekend mornings on Gulf Standard Time, and they move after iftar during Ramadan without changing tutor. Nobody is asked to be ready at a time that assumes an empty Al Wasl Road.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our own fee quoted after the trial
whyPoints.description: The AED ranges on this site are what the Dubai market charges, taken from published provider rates and a 2026 Dubai rate survey, and they are shown so a family can judge a quote. IB Gram's own fee depends on level and session length and is quoted after the trial lesson rather than guessed at here.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths lesson start if my child finishes school at 3pm?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect. A 15:00 finish in Al Sufouh or Umm Suqeim means a fifteen to twenty-five minute drive back to Jumeirah 2 at the busiest hour of the school day, so the pupil is at a desk around 15:45 at the earliest and is not ready to think until 16:15. Booking 15:30 buys a session that starts with an arrival. For families inside the Jumeirah and Al Safa ring, 16:00 works. For everyone else, 19:30 after food is the slot that holds all term.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation the right route for my child?
faqs.answer: Check the degree before you check the child. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many quantitative economics courses at research universities name Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, and a pupil without it finds out in Year 13 when the prerequisite is missing. If the destination is open, the deciding question is whether your child is stronger at structured algebraic method or at reading a messy real context. Both courses are demanding. Neither is the easy one, and the choice is set by school option blocks months before the Diploma starts.

faqs.question: How many IB maths sessions a week do Jumeirah 2 families usually book?
faqs.answer: One in the first Diploma year and two in the second is the common pattern, but the pattern should follow the problem rather than the calendar. A fluency gap in algebra responds to short frequent sessions, so two half-hours can beat one full hour. An exploration needs a handful of sessions clustered around topic choice and the first draft, then nothing. Timed paper practice in the final term needs a block long enough to sit a complete paper, which rules out a sixty-minute weekday slot after the school run.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's mathematical exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain what each of the five criteria rewards, teach the mathematics your child has chosen to use, question a topic until its mathematical depth is clear, and give feedback on a draft your child has written. A tutor may not contribute written content, hand over a ready-made topic, or edit prose into a finished state. That boundary is an IB academic-honesty requirement, not a house style, and crossing it puts the whole Diploma at risk for the student rather than for the tutor.

faqs.question: My child cannot finish Paper 1 in the time allowed - what actually fixes that?
faqs.answer: Pacing is a practice problem rather than a teaching problem, so the fix is timed work with a stopwatch and a marked script, not more explanation. The usual diagnosis is that twelve minutes went on a four-mark question early in the paper. The repair is a rule the pupil applies under pressure: allocate roughly a minute and a half per mark, abandon a question that has overrun, and come back if time allows. On Analysis and Approaches add daily non-calculator arithmetic drill, because hesitation on surds and exact values is what eats the clock.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Standard Level and Higher Level IB Mathematics for Jumeirah pupils?
faqs.answer: Yes, on both routes. Standard Level on either route is two papers at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty. Higher Level adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade on its own, and extends the syllabus substantially. Matching is done at that level of detail: a tutor is offered for Analysis and Approaches HL only if they teach Analysis and Approaches HL, because Paper 3 technique and the non-calculator demands of Paper 1 are not things a generalist picks up from the Standard Level course.

faqs.question: What do IB maths tutors charge per hour in Dubai at the moment?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market splits into bands. Budget online tutoring, often by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. Qualified subject tutors working online sit around AED 150 to AED 300, with one agency publishing IB rates from AED 200 in October 2026. Diploma and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and named or examiner-led tutors are advertised at AED 500 to AED 650. In-home visits add travel and are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's; ours is quoted after the free trial.

faqs.question: Does a tutor come to our villa in Jumeirah 2, or is the lesson online?
faqs.answer: Online, always. IB Gram does not send anyone to a UAE address, and home visits are not a service offered anywhere in the Emirates; they exist only in our India operation. A lesson runs live and one to one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard your child writes on and the board work kept afterwards. The practical gain is specialist access: the tutor is chosen for teaching Analysis and Approaches HL rather than for living within a twenty-minute drive of Jumeirah Beach Road.

faqs.question: How do maths sessions work during Ramadan when the school day is shortened?
faqs.answer: Timings move and the arrangement does not. School hours are reduced during Ramadan and official working hours change, so the afternoon slot that worked in February is usually too early and too tiring. Most Jumeirah families shift to a post-iftar session, often around 21:00, and some drop from two sessions to one for the month and add a weekend block instead. The tutor stays the same, which matters more than the hour: continuity through a disrupted month is worth more than squeezing in the usual timetable.

faqs.question: My child moved from MYP Mathematics into Analysis and Approaches SL and is drowning - what now?
faqs.answer: This is the most common Jumeirah enquiry of the autumn term and it is usually one specific gap rather than general weakness. MYP Mathematics is marked on four criteria out of eight and rewards investigation and communication; Analysis and Approaches rewards fast, accurate algebraic manipulation and formal notation. A pupil who came through standard rather than extended MYP Mathematics has often never been drilled on surds, indices, rearrangement or exact trigonometric values. Six to eight weeks of short, frequent sessions on those mechanics usually closes it, which is a different purchase from a two-year arrangement.

faqs.question: Which calculator does my child need, and when is it not allowed?
faqs.answer: Both IB maths routes assume a graphic display calculator, and schools publish the models they permit, so buy from the school's list rather than from a general recommendation. The rule that catches pupils out is Paper 1 on Analysis and Approaches, which is sat with no calculator at Standard and Higher Level. Pupils who practise exclusively with the device in front of them lose marks on arithmetic, surds and exact values that have nothing to do with their understanding. On Applications and Interpretation the calculator is permitted throughout and the risk shifts to syntax and rounding.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start maths tutoring eight weeks before the May session?
faqs.answer: It is late for syllabus repair and perfectly timed for technique. Eight weeks is not enough to rebuild two years of calculus, but it is enough to mark three past papers against a fixed set of failure categories, close an error log, drill Paper 1 without a calculator, and teach Paper 3 technique to a Higher Level pupil who has been ignoring it. The honest version of the answer is that the gain comes from marks currently being dropped on method and pacing rather than from new content, and that should be said before any money changes hands.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit to teach my child?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers in government and private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you read with suspicion. Applications go through MoHRE's own service.

faqs.question: What happens in the first lesson, and is anything payable before it?
faqs.answer: Nothing is payable before the trial lesson, which is free, one per student, and booked through the enquiry form. The lesson itself is mostly diagnostic: the tutor works through a recent piece of your child's own school work or a section of a past paper, watches how your child sets out working, and identifies which of the four standard failure categories is costing marks. You receive a short written plan afterwards naming the topics to repair in order and the school deadlines it is built around, and only then is a fee discussed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover IB Maths and Physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is worth asking for. Diploma Physics leans heavily on the same skills as Analysis and Approaches: rearranging formulae, resolving vectors, reading gradients and areas off graphs, and handling exponentials. A tutor who teaches both can treat a mechanics problem as the algebra exercise it usually is, which saves a session a fortnight. Where the physics need is specialised - an investigation write-up, or the Higher Level fields and quantum content - a second specialist is the better answer, and we will say so rather than stretch one tutor across both.

intro.heading: Jumeirah 3 against the neighbours, and the one thing that does not change
paragraphs: There is a real difference between hiring a maths tutor from Jumeirah 3 and hiring one from Jumeirah 2, Al Safa or Umm Suqeim, and it is worth setting out honestly before dismissing it. The schools each area feeds are not the same. The run home from a 3pm finish is not the same. The first session time that holds up across a whole term is not the same, and on this coast the difference is around thirty minutes between the eastern end of the corridor and the western one. None of that is imaginary, and a parent comparing options is right to notice it.

What does not change from one street to the next is the part that decides an IB Mathematics grade. A student in Jumeirah 3 sitting Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has three written papers and an Exploration, with Paper 1 taken without a calculator. A student two kilometres away in Umm Suqeim sitting Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level has two written papers, both with a graphic display calculator, and the same Exploration weighting. Those are different courses with different mark schemes, and the distance between the two houses is irrelevant to either.

That is the argument this page makes. The variables families compare when they search for a tutor nearby are the ones with the least effect on the outcome, and the variables with the most effect are invisible from a postcode. A tutor who lives in Jumeirah 3 and has taught Applications and Interpretation for six years is the wrong hire for an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student, and no amount of convenience repairs that.

The published rates make the same point from the other direction. The Dubai market quotes online qualified tutors in a band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards; in-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Those bands are identical whether the address is Jumeirah 1, Jumeirah 3 or Al Manara. Geography moves the logistics and the travel surcharge. It does not move the teaching rate, and online it does not move anything at all.

Every lesson here is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. The practical result is that the comparison between neighbourhoods collapses: a family in Jumeirah 3 and a family in Umm Suqeim choose from the same pool of Analysis and Approaches specialists, at the same rate, and pick a time that suits their own school run rather than somebody's route.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are three different syllabuses at the same level. 0607 carries a graphic display calculator expectation and an investigation, which makes it the closer preparation for IB Mathematics; 0580 Extended is closer to a traditional algebraic course.

Check the code on the entry confirmation before assuming the preparation matched the course the child has now started.

programmes.name: A Level Mathematics, for comparison
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in Dubai's British-curriculum schools, with Further Mathematics as an extension. Compared with the IB, it concentrates on fewer subjects in more depth and carries no equivalent of the Exploration, so the written-mathematics skill set a student develops is narrower and deeper.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: IB Mathematics tutoring is organised by course, level and topic, because the mark scheme changes with all three. These are the areas Dubai families ask for, with the specific failure each one tends to produce.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers plus the Exploration. Proof, complex numbers, vectors and the extended calculus content are the sections that separate a 5 from a 7, and Paper 3 rewards sustained problem-solving across a long unstructured question. Most late marks are lost to algebraic slips in no-calculator work rather than to missing theory.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers plus the Exploration, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Students who have come through a calculator-heavy IGCSE course frequently arrive unable to manipulate surds, logarithms and trigonometric exact values by hand, which is a technique gap rather than a knowledge gap and responds quickly to drilling.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Three papers, all with a calculator, weighted towards statistics, modelling, graph theory and matrices. Paper 3 is a long investigation-style question that cannot be revised for by topic; it has to be practised as a format. Students lose marks by producing a correct model with no interpretation of what it means.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two papers with a calculator throughout, plus the Exploration. The statistics content is the bulk of the course and the regression and hypothesis-testing questions reward a disciplined calculator routine. The common failure is treating the course as easier rather than different, and skipping the written interpretation marks.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences and series, binomial expansion, exponents and logarithms, and at Higher Level proof and complex numbers. Marks are lost in presentation: a correct answer with no visible method forfeits the method marks the scheme allocates, and this is the single most common avoidable loss across both courses.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Domain and range, transformations, inverse and composite functions, and modelling with functions in Applications and Interpretation. Students handle the algebra and then misread the question's context, which costs the interpretation marks rather than the calculation marks.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations in Analysis and Approaches; three-dimensional geometry, vectors and, at AI Higher Level, graph theory and Voronoi diagrams. The non-calculator trigonometric work in AA Paper 1 is a reliable source of lost marks for students trained on a calculator.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: The dominant topic in Applications and Interpretation and a smaller strand in Analysis and Approaches. Distributions, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing at AI; binomial and normal distributions at AA. The calculator does the arithmetic, so the marks sit in choosing the right test and stating the conclusion properly.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, with AA Higher Level extending into implicit differentiation, differential equations and Maclaurin series. In AI the emphasis moves towards numerical methods and rates of change in context. Chain, product and quotient rules under no-calculator conditions are where AA students most often stall.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: An individual written investigation of roughly 12 to 20 pages, internally assessed and externally moderated, marked out of 20 across five criteria. It is the single largest block of marks a student fully controls, and it is routinely the least prepared part of the course because it has no paper date.

The second real difference is the mix of schools each area feeds, and it shows in what families ask for. sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision behind most of the trouble
paragraphs: More Diploma mathematics problems in Dubai trace back to the course choice than to the teaching. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of each other. Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic reasoning, proof and calculus, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator at both levels. Applications and Interpretation is built on modelling, statistics and technology, with a calculator available throughout. A student who is strong at algebra and weak at extended written interpretation belongs in one; a student with the reverse profile belongs in the other.

The complication is that the choice is often made for university reasons rather than for aptitude ones, and sometimes on hearsay. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the route more commonly specified by engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees, but the authoritative statement is always the university's own published entry requirement, and those differ between institutions and between years. Read the requirement for the actual course your child is interested in, from the university's own admissions page, before treating the matter as settled.

Where a student is already in the wrong course, the useful question is whether a change is still possible within the school's deadlines, and that is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator rather than a tutoring purchase. Where a change is no longer possible, tutoring has a clear job: build the specific technique the chosen course demands, which for Analysis and Approaches usually means no-calculator fluency and for Applications and Interpretation usually means written interpretation of a model.

The table compares the two courses on the things that decide marks, rather than on reputation. It is the comparison most Dubai families are never shown, and it is the one that would have prevented a good proportion of the mathematics difficulties we are asked to repair in DP2.

sections.heading: The four papers, their weightings, and where the marks go
paragraphs: Parents are rarely told how an IB mathematics grade is actually assembled, which makes it hard to know what a tutor should be working on. Each course has written papers plus the Exploration, and the Exploration is 20 per cent in all four. The written papers carry the rest, split differently at Standard and Higher Level, and the durations differ too, which changes what revision has to achieve.

At Standard Level there are two written papers, each worth 40 per cent and each ninety minutes. At Higher Level there are three: two longer papers at 30 per cent each and a shorter Paper 3 at 20 per cent, which presents one or two extended, unstructured problems rather than a set of questions. Paper 3 is the component Higher Level students most often neglect, because it cannot be revised topic by topic and no revision guide can substitute for having sat several.

The calculator rule is the detail that matters most in Analysis and Approaches. Paper 1 is taken without one, at both levels. A student trained through a calculator-dependent IGCSE course can lose a large number of marks there while being perfectly capable of the mathematics, and the fix is mechanical: exact trigonometric values, surd manipulation, logarithm laws and algebraic fractions drilled until they are automatic.

Read the table as an allocation of tutoring time. If the Exploration is worth 20 per cent and has had no attention, that is where the cheapest marks are. If Paper 3 is worth 20 per cent at Higher Level and the student has never sat one under timing, no amount of further topic revision is the right purchase.

sections.heading: The Exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Exploration is the largest block of marks an IB mathematics student completely controls, and it is the component Dubai families most often leave until it is too late to help. It is an individual written investigation of roughly twelve to twenty pages, internally assessed by the school and externally moderated, and it is marked out of twenty across five criteria rather than as a single piece of mathematics.

Those criteria are worth knowing by letter, because nobody ranking for these searches publishes them and they explain almost every disappointing mark. Criterion A, presentation, is worth four marks and rewards coherence and organisation. Criterion B, mathematical communication, is worth four and rewards correct notation, defined variables and appropriate use of forms of representation. Criterion C, personal engagement, is worth three. Criterion D, reflection, is worth three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, is worth six and is the only criterion where the sophistication of the mathematics itself is assessed.

Read those allocations and the usual failure becomes obvious. A student spends the whole effort on criterion E, produces competent mathematics, and loses most of criteria C and D because the writing contains no genuine engagement and no reflection on what the results meant or where the model broke down. Six marks out of twenty sit in two criteria that are about thinking aloud on paper, and they are the cheapest marks in the entire two-year course to recover.

The other common failure is topic choice. A question too large cannot be treated properly in twenty pages; a question too small cannot reach the top of criterion E. Checking feasibility before weeks have gone into it is the most valuable single hour of Exploration coaching available, and it has to happen early. What a tutor may do here is bounded, and the next section sets out exactly where that boundary sits.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the Exploration, stated plainly
paragraphs: The Exploration is the student's own work and carries an authorship declaration. That makes the boundary around tutoring support both important and simple, and worth putting in writing before any session is booked. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposed question is feasible, teach the mathematical technique the investigation requires, model notation on a different example, read a draft and say which criterion it is currently failing, and ask questions that make the student reconsider their own reasoning.

A tutor may not choose the research question, supply text to be copied into the report, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, carry out the mathematics and hand over the results, or edit a piece to the point where the writing is no longer the student's. No tutor on this platform produces an Exploration, an Internal Assessment or any part of an Extended Essay for a student. That is not a disclaimer; it is the difference between support that improves a grade and support that puts a candidate at risk of a malpractice finding.

This market contains providers who do cross the line. Research into the UAE tutoring search results found one selling completed Internal Assessments outright. A family offered finished work should understand where the exposure sits: the declaration is signed by the student, and the consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the student, not on whoever sold it.

The test a parent can apply after any Exploration session needs no mathematical knowledge at all. Ask your child to explain, in their own words, what they changed and which criterion required the change. A student who can do that has been taught. A student who cannot has been handed something, and the examiner will reach the same conclusion through the moderation process.

sections.heading: What IB maths tutoring costs on this coast, and why the postcode does not move it
paragraphs: A parent comparing Jumeirah 3 with Jumeirah 2 or Umm Suqeim will find the same published rates in all three, which is the clearest evidence that geography is not what you are paying for. What varies with distance is the travel surcharge, and that is a cost rather than a feature. Setting the bands out plainly makes the choice easier, and almost nobody ranking for these searches publishes any figure at all.

The market reads as follows. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes online rates from AED 150 for IGCSE and AED 200 for IB. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a qualified subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors as high as AED 500. BartyED publishes AED 650 at the premium end. All of those are the providers' own published figures, not an IB Gram price list.

For Diploma mathematics specifically, the scarcity premium is real and it sits on Higher Level Analysis and Approaches. There are not many teachers in any single Dubai neighbourhood who have taught that syllabus recently, which is why a search constrained to a short drive tends to return either a generalist or a very high quote. Removing the radius removes the premium that scarcity creates, because the constraint becomes a timetable rather than a map.

One piece of context for a household budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A year without a fee increase is the sensible moment to fund the Exploration coaching and the Paper 3 clinics that most families never buy, rather than extending an open-ended weekly booking.

sections.heading: The school run, and the half hour that separates these neighbourhoods
paragraphs: School days along this coast end between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm, and the journey home adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on direction and on whether the route crosses Al Wasl Road or Jumeirah Beach Road at the wrong moment. For a Jumeirah 3 family that puts the first dependable weekday session at about 5pm. For Jumeirah 2, half an hour earlier. For Palm Jumeirah, with one access route, later still and less predictable.

That half hour is the entire practical difference between these neighbourhoods, and it only matters if somebody has to travel. An online session can begin at 5.05pm because the student walks from the door to a desk; a travelling tutor cannot promise 5.05pm from any of these addresses in term time. Families who have tried both formats tend to describe the same experience: the online slot is the one that is still intact in week eight.

The later part of the evening is widely available and underused. Sessions at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time suit households where both parents commute from DIFC or Business Bay, and for DP2 students they sit after sport and after the first pass at homework, which usually produces better questions. For Higher Level work a later, longer slot is often more productive than an early, shorter one.

Ramadan rearranges all of it. School hours shorten and the usable window moves to the early afternoon or to after Iftar, both of which work over live video and neither of which works well for anyone driving in Dubai at those hours. Agreeing the Ramadan slot a fortnight in advance, with the same tutor and the same weekday, keeps a Paper 3 block intact through the month.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we will tell you honestly
paragraphs: The useful first step takes twenty minutes and no money. Write down the course and level exactly as the school has it: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. Find the most recent marked paper and note which paper it was. Check whether the Exploration has a school deadline and whether a topic has been approved. Those three facts turn a general request for a maths tutor in Jumeirah 3 into a brief a specialist can act on in the first session.

Then take the free trial lesson and use it to test one thing: whether the tutor can look at the marked paper and say precisely where the marks went, in the language of that paper's mark scheme. A tutor who talks about confidence and foundations without reference to the component is not the right hire for a Diploma student, whatever the rate.

We will be straightforward about availability. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists are not abundant at every hour, and for a narrow request close to a deadline the honest answer is sometimes a different weekday or a short wait. We would rather say that than fill a slot with a tutor who knows mathematics but not that paper, which is the failure mode of hiring by proximity.

Finally, be realistic about volume. One hour a week across DP1, with Exploration blocks timed to the school's deadlines and a paper clinic in the final term, is the shape that works and the shape that stays affordable. Booking three hours a week in DP2 after a poor mock is the most expensive way to learn what one hour a week in DP1 would have prevented.

process.title: Name the course and level
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard. These are four different sets of papers with different calculator rules, and starting work without knowing which one the student sits is the most common waste of a first month in Diploma mathematics tutoring.

process.title: Read the most recent marked paper
process.description: We work from a marked script rather than a description, question by question, and rank the losses by marks rather than by how difficult they felt. In mathematics this usually shows that presentation and method marks account for more of the gap than missing theory does.

process.title: Check where the Exploration stands
process.description: Twenty per cent of the grade sits in a component with no examination date, so we ask about it in the first conversation. If a topic has not been approved, that is the first job; if a draft exists, criterion-by-criterion feedback is usually the fastest available improvement.

process.title: Match on the paper, then the hour
process.description: Matching is done on who teaches that course and level at the time you want on Gulf Standard Time, not on who is nearest Jumeirah 3. If no suitable specialist is free in your window we say so and offer the alternatives rather than substituting a general mathematics tutor.

process.title: Take the free trial, then review on marks
process.description: The first lesson is free and commits you to nothing. After that, progress is reported as marks on timed questions against the published scheme, reviewed each term. A booking that is not moving the number should be changed or stopped, and we will say so first.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: An Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student needs a teacher who knows that paper, and inside a twenty-minute drive of any Jumeirah address there are few of them. Online delivery makes the constraint a timetable instead of a map, which is the whole argument of this page.

whyPoints.title: The Exploration treated as 20 per cent
whyPoints.description: Most mathematics tutoring in this market never touches the Exploration, despite it carrying a fifth of the grade and twenty marks across five named criteria. We coach it to the criteria, on the student's own draft, and produce no part of it ourselves.

whyPoints.title: Calculator discipline taken seriously
whyPoints.description: AA Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and students arriving from calculator-heavy IGCSE courses lose marks there on mathematics they understand. That is a drilling problem with a quick fix, and it is one of the first things we test for.

whyPoints.title: Rates published, with their sources

whyPoints.title: No travel, so no lost sessions
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video and start when they are scheduled. IB Gram provides no home visits in the UAE, since home visiting is a service we run only in India, which is why nothing in the rate pays for a car on Jumeirah Beach Road at 5pm.

whyPoints.title: Claims limited to what we can show
whyPoints.description: We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education. We publish no success statistic, no rating and no grade promise, and we do not reproduce or supply the boards' own assessment materials.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IB maths tutor lives near Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Only if someone has to travel, and in our model nobody does. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the tutor is chosen for teaching the student's exact course and level rather than for living nearby. The cost of insisting on proximity is that the pool of Higher Level Analysis and Approaches teachers within a twenty-minute drive of any Jumeirah address is small, so the search quietly becomes a search for the nearest available maths graduate instead of the right subject specialist.

faqs.question: Is IB maths tutoring more expensive in Jumeirah 3 than in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. The published Dubai bands are the same along the whole corridor: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget online end, Unitors from AED 200 for IB, TutorChase at AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 table at AED 200 to 450 and upwards for a specialist. What changes with distance is the travel surcharge inside in-home quotes, which Bestimate puts at AED 180 to 350 and independent tutors at up to AED 500. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should my child take, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on aptitude and on the university course they are aiming at, in that order. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic reasoning, proof and calculus, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and technology use, with a calculator throughout. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the route more commonly specified by engineering and mathematics degrees, but entry requirements differ between institutions and years, so read the university's own admissions page rather than relying on general advice.

faqs.question: What are the paper weightings in IB Mathematics at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level there are two written papers at 40 per cent each, both ninety minutes, plus the Exploration at 20 per cent. At Higher Level there are three written papers: two at 30 per cent each over 120 minutes, and Paper 3 at 20 per cent over 60 minutes, plus the same 20 per cent Exploration. Paper 3 presents extended unstructured problems rather than a set of standard questions, which is why it has to be practised as a format rather than revised topic by topic.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on Paper 1 despite understanding the topic?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, and students who came through a calculator-dependent IGCSE course often cannot manipulate surds, exact trigonometric values, logarithms or algebraic fractions quickly by hand. The mathematics is understood; the execution is slow and error-prone under time pressure. This is a mechanical gap rather than a conceptual one and it responds quickly to short, repeated drilling, which is usually the first thing we test for in a diagnostic session.

faqs.question: How is the IB Maths Exploration marked?
faqs.answer: Out of twenty, across five criteria. Criterion A, presentation, carries four marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries four. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries three. Criterion D, reflection, carries three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six and is the only one assessing the sophistication of the mathematics itself. It is internally assessed and externally moderated, and runs to roughly twelve to twenty pages. Most lost marks sit in criteria C and D, which reward thinking that students assume does not count.

faqs.question: How long should the IB Maths Exploration be, and when should it start?
faqs.answer: Roughly twelve to twenty pages, and it should start earlier than most Dubai students begin it. Because it has no examination date, it competes with components that do and routinely slips until the mathematics has to be rushed. The single most valuable early step is checking that the chosen question is the right size: too broad and it cannot be treated properly in the page allowance, too narrow and it cannot reach the upper band of criterion E. Your school sets the internal deadline, so ask for it in writing.

faqs.question: What exactly can a tutor do on the Exploration without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, test whether a proposed question is feasible, teach the mathematical technique involved, model notation on a different example, read a draft and name the criterion it is failing, and ask questions that force the student to re-examine their reasoning. A tutor may not choose the question, supply text to be copied, restructure the report, or carry out the mathematics and hand over results. The declaration of authorship is signed by the student, so the risk of crossing that line falls on them.

faqs.question: My child is in Applications and Interpretation but wants an engineering degree. What now?
faqs.answer: First, check the actual published entry requirement for the specific courses they are applying to, from each university's own admissions page, because the picture is less uniform than staffroom advice suggests. Second, ask the Diploma coordinator whether a change of course is still possible within the school's deadlines; that is a school conversation rather than a tutoring purchase. If a change is not available, tutoring should concentrate on the Higher Level statistical and modelling content and on building the algebraic fluency the destination course will assume.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a DP1 maths student in Dubai usually need?
faqs.answer: One hour a week is the common and generally sufficient starting point in DP1, with short additional blocks timed to the Exploration deadline and a paper clinic in the final term of DP2. Families who book two or three hours a week usually do so in DP2 after a poor mock, at which point the same total spend buys far less because the time has gone. If a single weekly hour is not moving marks on timed questions after six weeks, the plan needs changing rather than extending.

faqs.question: Should we book one tutor for maths and physics together, or two?
faqs.answer: Sometimes at Standard Level, rarely well at Higher Level. The overlap in content is real but the mark schemes and the internal assessments are different, and a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 has nothing in common with a physics investigation. If a combined booking is offered, ask the tutor directly which physics component they have taught most recently and which maths paper they would prioritise. A specific answer is a good sign; a general one is not.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session start from Jumeirah 3 in term time?
faqs.answer: School days along this coast end between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm, and the journey home adds twenty to fifty minutes, so around 5pm is the first dependable weekday start from Jumeirah 3. A Jumeirah 2 family can usually hold 4.30pm, and Palm Jumeirah is later and less predictable because of its single access route. Slots at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are widely available and often better for Higher Level work, when a longer session after sport produces sharper questions.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a maths tutor to our home in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: No. We deliver one-to-one tuition online over live video everywhere in the UAE, and we do not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors do operate in Dubai and are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, alongside monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. The gap between those and the online band is logistics rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching a Dubai student need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified. It is a MoHRE permit, not a KHDA school licence.

faqs.question: When are the IB mathematics examinations and results published?
faqs.answer: UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's IB coordinator holds the authoritative dates. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and a wrong date on a page like this is something a parent would act on. Ask the coordinator directly, or read the IB's own assessment pages, and plan the Exploration and paper clinics backwards from what they tell you.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingHeading: Compare the school run, not the tutor
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.closingBody: Jumeirah 3, Jumeirah 2 and Umm Suqeim differ by about half an hour on the school run and by the schools they feed. They do not differ in the published tutoring rates, in how thin the local pool of Higher Level Analysis and Approaches teachers is, or in how an IB mathematics grade is assembled. Write down the course and level, bring the most recent marked paper and the school's Exploration deadline, and take a free trial lesson with someone who can tell you where the marks went. Sessions run one-to-one online over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: The cost of IB maths tuition depends on which maths it is
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah Golf Estates ring about maths more than about any other subject, and the first question is almost always what it costs. The honest answer is that the hourly rate is the least interesting part. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and that band barely moves between subjects. What moves, sometimes by a factor of two, is how many hours the work takes — and that is decided by which Mathematics course your child is sitting.

There are two, and they are different subjects wearing the same name. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-driven route, running through calculus to the Higher Level Paper 3 investigation. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route, with technology use built into every paper. A student can be strong at one and genuinely weak at the other, and a tutor fluent in one can waste a term on the other.

The cost consequence is straightforward. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most hour-hungry mathematics course in the Diploma: the proof work, the calculus and the Paper 3 extended investigation each need separate attention, and twenty sessions over a year is a realistic rather than a cautious estimate. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, where the loss is usually interpretation rather than technique, often moves in eight. Same hourly rate, very different total.

The other place money disappears is the exploration, the internal assessment every Mathematics student writes. It is worth 20 per cent of the grade and marked out of 20 across five criteria, and it is the one part of the course where early help is worth several times as much as late help. A badly chosen topic cannot be rescued in the final fortnight, and plenty of families pay for sessions trying.

There is a third cost nobody quotes, which is the cost of starting late. Most of the expensive mathematics problems we are asked to fix in Year 13 began as a small algebraic gap in Year 11 that nobody closed. Six sessions in the summer before the Diploma starts, spent on manipulation, radian measure and the structure of a proof, routinely removes the need for a twenty-session repair job two years later. Nobody in this market sells that block, because selling the repair is considerably more profitable than preventing it.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Golf Estates students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is an India-only service. Our own fee is quoted after a free trial lesson, because the number of sessions is what determines the real cost and that is only knowable once somebody has read your child's marked work.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one mathematics course, either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level. Both cover five syllabus topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The depth and emphasis differ sharply, and so does the technology expectation. Confirm your child's exact route and level on the school's subject guide before buying any tuition.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We publish no IB examination or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification; take yours from your school's IB coordinator. The practical UAE point is the exploration deadline, which the school sets months ahead of the papers and which is where Jumeirah Golf Estates families most often need help earliest.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria rather than examined, with extended and standard mathematics streams in many schools from Year 9. The stream a student is placed in at 14 is a strong predictor of which Diploma route they will be offered at 16, which makes Year 10 the cheapest moment to intervene if Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the goal.
programmes.countryNote: Schools around Jumeirah Golf Estates are split between Middle Years Programme and Cambridge IGCSE at this age, so a family moving between campuses inside Dubai can find the assessment model changes completely. The gap that matters for Diploma mathematics is algebraic fluency, which the criteria-based model tests less visibly.

programmes.name: The Year 11 to Diploma handover
programmes.description: The single most expensive gap in IB mathematics, and the cheapest one to close early. Students arriving into Analysis and Approaches Higher Level from a standard Year 11 course meet proof, radians and formal function notation in the first term, having never been taught them. Six sessions in the summer before Year 12 routinely prevents twenty sessions of repair in Year 13.

If your child's school offers it in Year 11 and Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is the plan, taking it is cheaper than any tuition block.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-golf-es.subjectsIntro: What follows is the Mathematics syllabus broken into the parts tuition is actually bought for, with a note on which route each matters most in and what it typically costs in sessions.

subjects.name: Proof and number
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction, induction at Higher Level, and the binomial theorem. Marks are lost because the structure of a proof is never learned as a structure; students write true statements in an order that does not establish anything. Three or four sessions usually fixes the habit.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, rational functions and transformations. This is where weak algebra becomes visible, and where a Higher Level student who scraped through Year 11 starts to lose marks on questions that are not about functions at all.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration by substitution and parts at Higher Level, related rates and kinematics. The most hour-hungry topic in the course and the usual reason an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level block runs to fifteen sessions rather than eight.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and radians
subjects.description: Identities, equations, the unit circle and radian measure. The characteristic error is mode: a calculator left in degrees produces plausible wrong answers across a whole question, and the method marks go with them.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity. Content-heavy and self-contained, which makes it one of the more efficient topics to tutor: five focused sessions and it is usually secure.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes, intersections and angles. Students lose marks on presentation as much as on method, writing a correct calculation without stating what it shows about the geometry.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI HL and SL, AA both levels
subjects.description: Distributions, correlation and regression, hypothesis testing at Applications and Interpretation Higher Level. The Applications route failure is interpretation: a regression run correctly and then described in words that do not match the context of the question.

subjects.name: Modelling and financial mathematics
subjects.description: Functions as models, compound interest, amortisation and depreciation. Marks go on unjustified model choice. A student who fits a curve without saying why that function suits the data loses the reasoning marks regardless of the fit.

subjects.name: Graph theory and matrices
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees, Chinese postman and travelling salesman problems, and transition matrices. Rarely taught well from a textbook alone, and one of the few Applications and Interpretation topics that genuinely needs a specialist.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: A written mathematical investigation worth 20 per cent of the grade, marked out of 20 across five criteria. The highest-value help is at the topic and question stage, weeks before any writing. Support afterwards is feedback on the student's own draft, never writing or rewriting it.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the decision that sets the hours
paragraphs: Most of the cost difference in IB maths tuition is decided before any tutor is hired. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-driven route; Applications and Interpretation is the statistical and modelling route with technology use embedded throughout. Both cover the same five syllabus topics on paper. In practice they ask for different habits of mind and they fail in different ways.

Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most hour-hungry mathematics course in the Diploma. Proof, the full calculus toolkit, complex numbers, vectors and the Paper 3 investigation are each substantial, and a student arriving with shaky algebra will keep paying for that gap in every topic. A realistic block across Year 12 and 13 is fifteen to twenty sessions, and front-loading them is cheaper than spreading them.

Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level sits at the other end. The content is more approachable and the losses are usually interpretive rather than technical: the calculation is right and the sentence describing it does not answer the question asked. That is a technique problem, and it often moves in eight sessions or fewer. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level sits in between, with hypothesis testing and graph theory the two topics that genuinely need a specialist.

A note on choosing the route, for families still in Year 11. Pick on the mathematics, not on the perceived difficulty. A student who enjoys structure and manipulation will find Analysis and Approaches easier than its reputation; a student who thinks in data and context will do better and score higher on Applications and Interpretation. Then check the course requirement for the degrees being considered, because some engineering and mathematics programmes specify the Analysis and Approaches route.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth, and what that changes
paragraphs: Revision is usually spread evenly across a course, and the weightings say it should not be. At Standard Level, both Mathematics routes are assessed through two papers carrying 40 per cent each, with the exploration making up the remaining 20 per cent. At Higher Level the structure changes: three papers at 30, 30 and 20 per cent, plus the exploration at 20. Confirm the exact figures for your child's cohort against the school's subject guide, because the assessment model is periodically revised.

Two consequences follow. First, the exploration is worth as much as a whole paper at Standard Level and more than Paper 3 at Higher Level. A student who treats it as homework is leaving a fifth of the grade to chance, and it is the one component where the work is done in advance with full access to help.

Second, at Higher Level Paper 3 deserves separate preparation. It is a short paper of extended investigative questions, and it rewards a specific skill: following an unfamiliar line of mathematical reasoning across several parts where each answer feeds the next. Students who are strong on Papers 1 and 2 frequently underperform on it because nobody practised that skill as a skill.

For Analysis and Approaches there is a third consequence. Paper 1 is non-calculator, and non-calculator fluency decays fast when every piece of homework is done with a device on the desk. Drilling it deliberately in the final eight weeks is one of the highest-return activities available.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks across five criteria
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is the component families underestimate and then overpay to fix. It is worth 20 per cent of the Mathematics grade and it is marked out of 20 against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation, which is the single most useful fact about it.

That allocation explains most of the marks lost. A beautifully written exploration about a topic the student cares about, using mathematics well below the level of the course, cannot score well on the criterion worth the most. Conversely, an exploration using appropriate mathematics badly presented loses across presentation and communication but keeps its core. The topic choice, made in a single conversation months before any writing, determines which of those two a student is heading for.

This is why exploration help is worth several times as much early as late. Three sessions at the topic-and-question stage, testing whether the mathematics is of the right level and whether the chosen data can support the analysis, is a small block. Trying to rescue a finished exploration built on unsuitable mathematics in the final fortnight is expensive, stressful and usually unsuccessful.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else in the course. A tutor may discuss topic viability, explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the mathematics is appropriate, mark a draft against the criteria and teach referencing. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's prose, supply the topic as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit it to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line. Keep the written session notes: a dated record that the help given was feedback on the student's own drafts is the student's protection.

sections.heading: Where maths marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Examiners see patterns, not weaknesses in a subject. The commonest is method. On a five or six-mark question, most of the marks are for the steps, and a student who writes only a final answer loses nearly all of them when that answer is wrong. This is pure habit, costs nothing to fix, and in a Jumeirah Golf Estates student's mock paper it is usually worth several marks a page.

The second is rounding. An intermediate value rounded to three significant figures and then carried forward produces a final answer that is close but not correct, and the accuracy mark goes. Working to full calculator precision and rounding once at the end is a rule, not a preference, and students break it constantly.

The third is mode. A calculator left in degrees when a question is set in radians yields plausible wrong answers through an entire question, with no error visible to the student. Checking the mode before every paper is a thirty-second habit that nobody teaches.

The fourth is command terms. Show that requires a derivation, not a restatement of the result; hence means the previous part must be used; verify and prove are not interchangeable. And the fifth, specific to Applications and Interpretation, is interpretation: the regression runs, the correlation coefficient appears, and the sentence underneath does not say what it means for the context the question described. Each of these is diagnosable from one marked paper, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

sections.heading: Paper 3 at Higher Level, and why it is a separate job
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, carries 20 per cent of the grade, and is the component capable students most often underperform on. It is short, it has few questions, and each question runs across several parts where every answer feeds the next. A slip in part b propagates to part f, and there is no second question to recover on.

What it rewards is not more content. It is the ability to follow an unfamiliar line of mathematical reasoning that the paper sets up for you, and to keep going when you cannot see where it is heading. That is a trainable skill and it is trained by doing extended investigative questions under timed conditions, with somebody walking the reasoning back afterwards to show where it was lost.

Most school revision does not cover it well, for a practical reason: there are far fewer Paper 3 questions in existence than Paper 1 and 2 questions, so the material runs out quickly. A tutor who has taught the course for several years is the person most likely to have worked through what exists and to know which questions are worth the time.

For an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student in Jumeirah Golf Estates, the sensible shape is three or four dedicated Paper 3 sessions in the second half of Year 13, after the content is covered, sat under conditions and then marked line by line. Doing it earlier wastes the scarce material; doing it later leaves no time to change anything.

sections.heading: Which route do universities expect?
paragraphs: This is the question that should drive the route choice in Year 11, and it is routinely answered with rumour. The accurate position is that it depends on the degree and the institution, and that the only reliable source is the published entry requirement for the specific course a student is considering. Engineering, mathematics, physics and some economics programmes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Many other degrees accept either route.

For families looking at UAE universities, there is a separate process to understand and it is not a tutoring matter. The school-leaving certificate goes through Ministry of Education equivalency, which the Ministry performs. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. For the American track, mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is an equivalency figure circulating on tutoring sites, and we are not repeating it, because we have not read it on a Ministry of Education source. If anybody quotes you an IB points threshold for equivalency, ask where on moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority it appears. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees it.

The practical advice for a Jumeirah Golf Estates family in Year 11 is unglamorous. Write down the three or four degree subjects under consideration, find the published mathematics requirement for each at two or three universities, and choose the route from that list rather than from what the student's friends are taking.

sections.heading: Scheduling maths in a Jumeirah Golf Estates week
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where session timing matters most, because it needs a student who can still concentrate. In this community the afternoon runs late: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving depending on whether the school is in Al Barsha South or Arabian Ranches, and then clubs in Dubai Sports City for a good proportion of children.

That ordering matters: a student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what a specialist can resolve in forty minutes. A session scheduled before homework becomes supervised homework, which is an expensive way to build dependence.

Weekend mornings are the most underused slot in this community and the right one for exploration work and for timed Paper 3 practice, both of which need an uninterrupted ninety minutes that a weekday evening cannot reliably provide.

Online delivery is what makes any of this flexible. There is no tutor in a car, so a session can move within the week when a tournament or a school deadline collides, shift to post-Iftar during Ramadan, and pause through mock weeks. We also agree a stop date at the start, so a maths arrangement is reviewed deliberately rather than renewed out of habit through a second year.
