faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost for a family in Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: The hourly rate matters less than the total. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online sit at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and that band barely varies by subject. What varies is the number of sessions: an Applications and Interpretation Standard Level block is realistically eight sessions, around AED 1,600 at a mid-band rate, while an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level programme across two years is fifteen to twenty, nearer AED 3,000 to AED 4,000. Those are market figures researched in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, which follow the free trial.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI, in practice?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-driven, with a non-calculator Paper 1 and heavy calculus, complex numbers and vectors at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-led, with technology permitted throughout and hypothesis testing and graph theory at Higher Level. Both cover the same five syllabus topics on paper and ask for different habits of mind. A student strong at one can genuinely struggle with the other, which is why we staff them separately rather than offering a general maths tutor for both.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route should my child choose in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Choose on the mathematics and on the published entry requirements, not on reputation. A student who enjoys structure and manipulation often finds Analysis and Approaches easier than its reputation suggests; a student who thinks in data and context scores higher on Applications and Interpretation. Then write down three or four degree subjects under consideration and look up the actual mathematics requirement at two or three universities for each. Engineering, mathematics and physics commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Many other degrees accept either route.

faqs.question: How much is the maths exploration worth and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is worth 20 per cent of the Mathematics grade and marked out of 20 against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation at 6 marks, which is the most useful fact about it. A well-written exploration using mathematics below the level of the course cannot score well on the criterion worth most, so the topic decision made months earlier determines the ceiling. Confirm the current criteria with your school's subject guide.

faqs.question: How early should exploration help start, and what is a tutor allowed to do?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary, and earliest is best. A tutor can discuss whether a topic is viable, question whether the mathematics is at the right level for the course, check that the data can support the analysis, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, mark a draft against them, and teach referencing. A tutor cannot write any part of it, rewrite the student's prose, supply the topic as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit it to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 3 need separate preparation at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Because it rewards a skill nothing else in the course trains. Paper 3 is Higher Level only, carries 20 per cent of the grade, and consists of a small number of extended investigative questions where each part feeds the next, so an early slip propagates and there is no second question to recover on. The ability to follow an unfamiliar chain of reasoning is trainable, but the available material is scarce, so three or four dedicated sessions late in Year 13 under timed conditions is the efficient shape rather than scattering it earlier.

faqs.question: Which maths errors cost Jumeirah Golf Estates students the most marks?
faqs.answer: On method, most of all. On a five or six-mark question the steps carry most of the marks, and a student who writes only the final answer loses nearly all of them when it is wrong. Then rounding: an intermediate value rounded and carried forward produces a near-miss that forfeits the accuracy mark. Then calculator mode, where degrees left on during a radian question yields plausible wrong answers invisibly. Then command terms: show that needs a derivation, hence means the previous part must be used. All of these are visible in one marked paper.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions will my child actually need?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route, the level and what the marked paper shows. Applications and Interpretation Standard Level often moves in eight sessions because the losses are interpretive. Analysis and Approaches Standard Level is typically ten to twelve. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level runs to fifteen or twenty across two years, because calculus, proof, complex numbers and Paper 3 are each substantial. Add three to five for the exploration. Any provider quoting before reading a marked paper is pricing a guess, and you will pay for the first sessions of diagnosis.

faqs.question: My child is moving into IB maths from Year 11. What is the cheapest thing I can do?
faqs.answer: Six sessions in the summer before Year 12, closing the algebra, radian and proof-structure gap before Analysis and Approaches Higher Level begins. Students arriving from a standard Year 11 course meet proof, radian measure and formal function notation in the first term having never been taught them, and the gap then costs marks in topics that are not about any of those things. If the school offers Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 in Year 11, taking it is cheaper still, and it is the best available bridge.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition workable, or does it need a shared desk?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is arguably the subject best suited to live video, because the medium is a shared writing surface. A worked solution builds line by line where both people can see it, the mark scheme sits open on both sides, and the session can be revisited. What matters far more than the room is whether the tutor knows the route: a specialist in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level calculus will do more for a grade over video than a general maths tutor will at the kitchen table.

faqs.question: What time should a maths session run for a child in this community?
faqs.answer: Between 6.30pm and 8.15pm on weekdays, and after the first attempt at the problem set rather than before it. The afternoon here runs late: campus finish between 2.45pm and 3.30pm, ten to twenty minutes of gate queue, twelve to thirty-five minutes of driving, and then clubs in Dubai Sports City for many children. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what forty minutes with a specialist can resolve. Weekend mornings are better for exploration work and timed Paper 3 practice.

faqs.question: Does the IB maths route affect UAE university equivalency?
faqs.answer: No, and the two should not be confused. Equivalency of a school-leaving certificate is a Ministry of Education process, performed by the Ministry rather than by a school or a tutor, and tuition is not a requirement for it. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. For the IB, verify any points figure directly on moe.gov.ae; we do not publish one we have not read at source.

faqs.question: Should the same tutor take both maths and physics at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Physics Higher Level share real mathematical ground, so a tutor who teaches both can make the overlap explicit, which helps. The test is whether they know both syllabuses at paper level, not whether they are comfortable with the content. Where a single tutor genuinely covers both, scheduling gets easier and continuity improves. Where they do not, two specialists are better than one generalist, and we will tell you which situation applies.

faqs.question: What if no Analysis and Approaches specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: You are told the realistic wait rather than offered a general maths tutor. Availability for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is thinnest in the weeks before the May session and for the Paper 3 work specifically, and Applications and Interpretation Higher Level graph theory is the single scarcest request in this syllabus. Where the available specialist is based outside the UAE, we say so before any payment, including which time zone they teach from. A shorter diagnostic block can run meanwhile if that is useful.

intro.heading: Mathematics is the subject where the hour matters
paragraphs: Of all the Diploma subjects, mathematics is the one most affected by when the session happens. Arithmetic and algebraic accuracy degrade with tiredness in a way that essay quality does not, and a student making careless slips at nine in the evening concludes they are weak at maths rather than tired. In a community where everybody travels to school, that makes the timetable a mathematical question.

Jumeirah Islands has no school inside the gates. Every child is driven or bussed out, usually to Jumeirah Village, The Meadows, Emirates Hills, Al Barsha or Al Sufouh, and the return leg typically serves two or three other communities first. Arrivals home land between roughly 15:40 and 16:50 depending on the school and the route order, which puts the dependable weekday start at 17:00, or 17:30 for the longer commutes.

The second scheduling fact is the week rather than the day. A full past paper needs ninety uninterrupted minutes, and there is exactly one slot in a Jumeirah Islands week where that genuinely exists: Saturday morning. Marking it on Sunday is where the learning happens, because sitting a paper only generates the data.

The third is the year. Mathematics compounds more than any other Diploma subject: calculus sits on algebra, and a student shaky on rearrangement in September is shaky on integration by substitution in February regardless of how well the integration was taught. That is why one weekly hour from the first Diploma year costs less in total and works better than a block of intensive sessions in the second.

Before any of that, one fact has to be established: which of the four courses your child takes. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level, are four different qualifications with different calculator rules, different content and different consequences for what your child can apply to study. A tutor must be matched to the exact combination.

There is one more structural fact worth having early. Roughly a fifth of the grade in every IB mathematics course, at both levels, sits in the exploration: independent mathematical writing marked against five criteria for twenty marks, with a deadline set by your child's school rather than by the IB. It is the most coachable part of the course and the part students treat as a side task, which is why it is the first thing we ask about.

IB Gram matches that combination and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For mathematics the format is a genuine advantage, because both people write where the other can see, a graph can be redrawn five times in a minute, and the student keeps the written record.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-islands.subjectsIntro: The topics that decide an IB mathematics grade, with where each one costs marks. A specialist can name the failure in each without hesitating.

subjects.name: Algebra and proof at Higher Level
subjects.description: Proof by induction, binomial expansion, partial fractions and complex numbers in both forms. Marks go in the setup rather than the arithmetic: an induction proof without a clearly identified inductive step scores badly however correct the algebra. Non-calculator conditions make exactness a trained habit.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration and kinematics, with implicit differentiation, related rates, substitution, integration by parts and differential equations at Higher Level. The characteristic failure is technique selection: students who can perform every method and cannot tell which integral needs which.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, exponentials and logarithms, transformations and graph features. Marks are lost on domain and range, and on sketches that omit the features being marked: intercepts, asymptotes and turning points rather than neatness.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, equations over a stated interval, and at Higher Level more demanding manipulation. The recurring loss is finding one solution in an interval and stopping, which is a procedural habit rather than a gap in understanding and takes about one session to correct.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: HL and SL, heavier in AI
subjects.description: Distributions, correlation and regression, with hypothesis testing and more advanced inference at Higher Level in Applications and Interpretation. The marks sit in interpretation: naming what a gradient means in the context rather than reporting that a relationship exists.

subjects.name: Modelling
subjects.description: Fitting functions to real data, justifying the model chosen and evaluating its limitations. Calculator efficiency is part of the grade here, and students who use the graphing tool as an answer machine rather than an exploratory instrument consistently underperform.

subjects.name: Graph theory and HL extensions
subjects.description: Networks, adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees and shortest-path algorithms. Unfamiliar to most parents, taught late in the course, and therefore under-revised relative to its weight. It responds well to practice because it is procedural.

subjects.name: Paper 3 technique
subjects.description: Extended problem-solving questions on a single paper, worth roughly a fifth of the Higher Level grade on the standard published structure. Students meet the format rarely and lose marks by abandoning a long question after one blocked step. Build it in from the spring of the first Diploma year.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Surds, indices, exact trigonometric values, algebraic fractions and rearrangement, done quickly and exactly by hand. This is what Paper 1 actually tests underneath the topics, and it is trainable with short regular drills rather than with more content teaching.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five criteria. A tutor may teach the criteria, help narrow a topic, teach mathematical writing and comment on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, part-write or supply any of it, and the strongest explorations use mathematics the student genuinely owns.

sections.heading: Which hour, and why it changes the marks
paragraphs: This is the most practical thing on the page, and no competitor publishes it. Mathematics is the Diploma subject where the time of day measurably changes the output, because arithmetic precision is the first casualty of tiredness. The same student doing non-calculator algebra at 16:45 after a long bus journey and at 17:30 after food produces visibly different work.

In Jumeirah Islands the constraint is fixed and known. No school sits inside the gates, so every pupil travels out and the return leg usually serves two or three communities before reaching here. Arrivals land between roughly 15:40 and 16:50, which means a 16:30 session starts before the student has eaten, changed or stopped thinking about the journey.

The dependable start is 17:00, and 17:30 for children coming back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. For a second-year Diploma student the picture splits by work type: quantitative work still belongs earlier, while exploration writing and reflective work tolerate 19:30 and sometimes benefit from it, because reasoning survives tiredness better than arithmetic does.

Bus routes are built around schools rather than communities, so two households inside the same gates can differ by twenty minutes. Ask the school's transport office for your own route timings instead of copying a neighbour's slot. It is a two-minute question and it decides whether you are paying for sixty productive minutes or forty.

sections.heading: Which of the four courses, and who decides
paragraphs: There are four IB mathematics courses, not one, and parents routinely call all of them IB maths. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a non-calculator paper. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active, statistical and modelling-led. Each exists at Higher and Standard Level, and the four combinations need four different tutor briefs.

The decision should be made on two grounds and is usually made on one. The first is the degree requirement: a number of quantitative degrees, including engineering, physics and mathematics, specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while others accept either. Requirements vary by university and change, so the only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific courses your child is considering.

The second is the student. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes complete algebraic fluency and an appetite for abstraction. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level assumes comfort with data, modelling and written interpretation. Neither is the respectable choice; the mismatch is what causes two difficult years, and it is usually avoidable with one diagnostic session.

A move between courses is normally possible early in the first Diploma year and rarely sensible later. For a family in this community the decision often coincides with a change of school at sixteen, since the local schools in reach of these gates include both British-curriculum and continuum provision, which adds timetable constraints on top of the academic ones.

sections.heading: What compounds, term by term
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject where timing of support matters most, because the content is genuinely cumulative. Calculus rests on algebra. Integration techniques rest on differentiation. Vector geometry rests on trigonometry. A student who is shaky on rearrangement in September is shaky on integration by substitution in February, regardless of how well the integration itself was taught.

That has a direct financial consequence. One weekly hour from the autumn of the first Diploma year costs more in total hours and less in total money than an intensive programme in the spring of the second, because it prevents the compounding rather than unpicking it. It also secures an early-evening slot before those fill across the city.

The sequence of risks is predictable enough to plan against. In the first term the risk is unresolved pre-Diploma algebra. By the second it is calculus technique selection. In the first term of the second year it is the exploration deadline colliding with content. In the final terms it is Paper 3 unfamiliarity and exam conduct.

Each of those needs a different kind of session, which is why a generic weekly arrangement drifts. A tutor working to the school's scheme of work and assessment calendar targets the current risk; a tutor working through a textbook targets whatever chapter comes next, which may be months away from what the student actually needs.

sections.heading: The exploration, and when it has to start
paragraphs: The exploration carries roughly a fifth of the grade in every IB mathematics course, at both levels, and it is marked against five criteria for a total of twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Criterion names and allocations are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's current subject guide.

The distribution explains why the best explorations are often mathematically modest. Only part of the mark is for the mathematics itself; the rest is for how the work is organised, how clearly it is communicated, whether the student genuinely owns the topic, and whether the reflection evaluates the approach rather than restating the result.

So an over-ambitious topic is the commonest failure. A student who picks mathematics they cannot fully understand scores poorly on engagement and reflection because they have nothing original to say about it, even when the mathematics looks impressive. A student who takes something they care about, uses mathematics at the level of their course, and reflects honestly on the model's limitations does better.

The timing is the part families here get wrong. The deadline is set by your child's school, usually a long way before the written papers, and the useful work starts a term earlier still. The single most valuable hour in the whole exploration happens before any mathematics is attempted, narrowing the topic until it can actually be written about.

On the limit: a tutor may teach the criteria, help narrow the topic, teach mathematical writing and notation, and read the student's draft and name which descriptor band it currently meets. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite or supply any part of it, and we will not.

sections.heading: Where maths marks actually disappear
paragraphs: Three categories, and they need different responses. The first is content gaps, usually predating the Diploma: surds, indices, rearrangement, algebraic fractions. These are few, identifiable from one marked paper, and once closed they stay closed. For Analysis and Approaches students they are the usual reason calculus looks harder than it is.

The second is technique. A student who can perform every method but selects the wrong one, who sets up a question correctly and loses the middle, who rounds at an intermediate step, or who abandons a long Paper 3 question at the first obstacle, has a technique problem. These need marked past papers and a conversation about each decision rather than more teaching.

The third is exam conduct: running out of time, not showing working on a multi-step question where the final answer is wrong and no method marks are available, mis-setting the calculator. These are the cheapest marks to recover in the subject and the least often addressed, because they feel too trivial to spend a session on.

Telling them apart is straightforward and nobody does it. Sit with the marked paper and ask the student, question by question, what they were thinking. A content gap produces a blank or a wrong method. A technique problem produces a correct method applied to a misread question, or a right answer rounded wrongly. The student almost always knows.

A tutor should be able to name which of the three dominates in the first session, from a marked paper, with a rough number of sessions for each. If the answer is a plan to revise the course from the beginning, the paper has not been read.

sections.heading: What this costs, and when to spend it
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB tuition sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65.

For mathematics the budget band is less useful than in other subjects. Supervision helps a student who will not start their homework; it does not help a student who cannot tell which integral needs substitution. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level the qualified-specialist range is the realistic minimum.

Plan monthly rather than hourly. Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support in one subject. In-home visits carry a travel premium at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, which in mathematics buys nothing mathematical.

The timing advice is the part that saves money. Weekly from the first Diploma year costs less in total than intensive from February, and it also gets a better tutor, because in September a specialist's early evenings are still open and in March they are not. That is not a sales line; it is how any calendar of one-to-one slots fills.

All figures above are the providers' or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on the course, the level and the weeks remaining.

sections.heading: What we will not do, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: On the exploration and any other assessed work, the limit is absolute. A tutor may teach the criteria, narrow a topic, teach mathematical writing and notation, and read and comment on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite to completion or supply any part of it. Submitting work that is not the student's own is a malpractice matter handled by the IB, and the consequence falls on the student.

Operators in this market sell completed internal assessments at four-figure prices. That is a reason to avoid them rather than a service, and a parent comparing quotes in this community should ask every provider the same question: what will you do with my child's draft?

We do not sell grade guarantees, promised score improvements or money-back schemes, because nobody can honestly deliver one. We publish no rating, review count or satisfaction percentage either, because a statistic without its sample size, date and method cannot be checked, and several providers in this market publish two conflicting figures on one page.

Mathematics is the subject where the offer of a shared drive arrives most often, because past papers feel like the whole of revision in a subject made of worked questions. We do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access to what it needs - including the formula booklet and the papers for the right one of the four mathematics courses, which matters far more here than volume does. A folder of exam material offered by a tutor is a copyright problem rather than an advantage, and in mathematics it is usually also the wrong material: a Jumeirah Islands parent handed several hundred mixed questions has been given something to tick off, while what moves a grade is a smaller number of questions marked against the official scheme with the method written out in full.

And we claim no approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit. Individual tutors in the UAE do need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid for two years.

faqs.question: Does it really matter what time of day the maths session happens?
faqs.answer: In mathematics, more than in any other Diploma subject. Arithmetic and algebraic accuracy are the first casualties of tiredness, so the same student produces visibly different work at 16:45 after a long bus journey and at 17:30 after food. The risk is not just lost marks in a session; it is that a student making careless slips concludes they are weak at maths. From these gates, where every child travels out, 17:00 is the dependable start and 17:30 is safer for a long commute.

faqs.question: We cannot decide between the two maths courses. What settles it?
faqs.answer: Two things, in this order. The published entry requirements of the specific degree courses your child is considering, because several quantitative degrees specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while others accept either and a few exclude Applications and Interpretation. Then the student: Analysis and Approaches suits those who like exact algebraic results, Applications and Interpretation those comfortable with data, modelling and written interpretation. The mismatch rather than the difficulty is what makes two years hard.

faqs.question: How early does the exploration need to start?
faqs.answer: A term before your school's internal deadline, which itself usually falls a long way before the written papers. The most valuable hour happens before any mathematics is attempted, narrowing the topic until it can actually be written about and discussed critically. The marks reward presentation, communication, personal engagement and reflection alongside the mathematics itself, which is why a modest topic genuinely owned outscores an ambitious one the student cannot discuss.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor come to our villa inside Jumeirah Islands?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Mathematics tuition for families here is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared surface both people write on. For this subject that is a genuine advantage: a graph can be redrawn five times in a minute and the student keeps the written record of the session.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches taught differently?
faqs.answer: Because no calculator is permitted. Every manipulation has to be exact and quick, which makes algebraic fluency a trained skill rather than a by-product of understanding. A student who can do the mathematics with a calculator and not without one loses marks across a whole paper for reasons unrelated to comprehension. The implication is short, regular non-calculator drills inside weekly sessions from the first Diploma term, not a revision block in the spring of the second year.

faqs.question: What should the first session actually do?
faqs.answer: Read a marked paper with your child and establish which of three things is costing marks: a content gap, usually predating the Diploma, a technique problem such as choosing the wrong method or rounding early, or exam conduct such as not showing working on a multi-step question. Those need different responses over different numbers of weeks. A tutor who instead proposes revising the course from the beginning has not read the paper, and that is the signal to act on.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 at Higher Level worth separate practice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most under-prepared component. It carries roughly a fifth of the Higher Level grade on the standard published structure and consists of extended problem-solving questions rather than the shorter items students meet all year. Schools rarely set the format internally, so students arrive unfamiliar with it and abandon long questions after one blocked step, forfeiting marks still available further down. Build it in from the spring of the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: Our child came from IGCSE with a strong grade and is struggling. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the Diploma assumes fluency that a good IGCSE grade does not certify. IGCSE rewards accuracy with method marks and partial credit; Analysis and Approaches assumes surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions handled quickly and exactly, and builds calculus on top within weeks. A student who was accurate but slow now runs out of time and makes errors under pressure. A few focused sessions on that foundation usually move more marks than weeks on the new content.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does the first Diploma year need?
faqs.answer: One, used properly, rising to two or three per week in the final weeks of the second year. More than one hour early in the course is often wasted, because the student needs time to work between sessions and the school is still covering content. The pattern that costs least across the two years is weekly and early; the pattern that costs most is three a week from February, which is also when the scarcest specialists have no early-evening slots left.

faqs.question: What do we do with a Saturday morning slot?
faqs.answer: A full past paper under timed conditions, which is the only thing that genuinely needs ninety uninterrupted minutes and the only block in a Jumeirah Islands week where that exists. Then mark it with the tutor on Sunday, because the marking is where the learning happens and an unmarked paper is data nobody read. Families here who adopt that pairing usually get more from it than from two additional weekday hours.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take mathematics and physics?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level often, and usefully, because many physics errors are mathematical: rearrangement, vector resolution, graph interpretation. At Higher Level we generally advise two tutors, since genuine depth in both Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Physics Higher Level is rare and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one. Two fixed evenings is also easier to protect than one long combined session after a late journey home.

faqs.question: Does the metro near Jumeirah Lakes Towers change the scheduling?
faqs.answer: No, though it looks as though it should. The Red Line station on the edge of Jumeirah Lakes Towers is a short drive from these gates and is genuinely useful for after-school activities and for an older teenager travelling independently. It makes no difference to a tutoring timetable: an online session happens at home, and an in-home tutor would arrive by car in the same evening traffic as everyone else on Sheikh Zayed Road.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if we think our child is in the wrong course?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change the entry, and a single diagnostic session will tell you whether the concern is real. The tutor works at the standard of the course in question and reports on fluency and fit rather than on enthusiasm. Moves between the two courses are usually possible early in the first Diploma year and rarely sensible later, so this is an autumn conversation with the school rather than something to postpone until the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: Which calculator should our child be using?
faqs.answer: The school specifies the permitted models and the examination regulations require memory to be cleared, so follow the school's instruction rather than a recommendation from anyone else. The point worth making is that familiarity is part of the grade: Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout, and a student who is slow with their own device loses marks on time rather than on mathematics. Practise with the exact model under time in the term before the papers.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Not too late, and more expensive per unit of improvement. If the exploration is already submitted the work becomes technique and timed papers, which responds quickly. If the problem is foundational algebra, closing it in the second year uses weeks the revision programme needs. The honest answer depends on a marked paper, and if we think the weeks remaining are too few for the subject to move meaningfully, we will say so rather than selling the hours.

intro.heading: Which maths course is your child actually taking?
paragraphs: There are four IB mathematics courses, not one: Analysis and Approaches at Standard and Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard and Higher Level. Parents routinely describe all four as 'IB maths', and tutors occasionally do too. They have different content, different calculator rules, different paper structures and, most importantly, different consequences for what your child can apply to study. Establishing which one is the first useful minute of any conversation.

The distinction is not difficulty, although that is how it is usually explained. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with a non-calculator Paper 1 that rewards exact manipulation. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout, statistics-heavy, and built around modelling real contexts. A strong student can find AI's interpretation demands harder than AA's algebra, and a student placed in AA because it sounded better can struggle for two years for no gain.

In Jumeirah Park the practical question arrives at sixteen, because the community's own school runs the British curriculum and most local Diploma students move to a continuum or dual-pathway school in Al Barsha, Jumeirah Village Triangle or The Meadows. That transition is also when the AA or AI decision is made, often quickly, and sometimes on the basis of an IGCSE grade rather than a conversation about degree requirements.

The second thing worth knowing early is how much of the grade is not an exam. The exploration carries roughly a fifth of the mark at every level and across both courses, and its deadline is set internally by the school, usually a year before the papers. Students behave as though it is a side task. Twenty marks decided by presentation, communication, engagement, reflection and the mathematics used is not a side task, and it is the most coachable part of the course.

What IB Gram provides is a tutor matched to the exact course and level, teaching live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For mathematics specifically, online works well: a shared screen with a past paper, a graphing tool and a visible working surface beats two people over one sheet of paper most evenings.

It is also worth saying that mathematics is the Diploma subject where starting early changes the most. Content compounds: calculus sits on algebra, and a student who is shaky on rearrangement in September is shaky on integration by substitution in February regardless of how well the integration was taught. That is why a single weekly hour from the first term usually outperforms a block of intensive sessions in the second year, and costs less in total.

The rest of this page is the detail a Jumeirah Park parent needs in order to judge any maths tutor, ours included: how the papers are weighted, where marks are actually lost topic by topic, what the twenty marks in the exploration are awarded for, what the published Dubai rates are for a maths specialist, and when a session can realistically happen given the school run in this community.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.programmesIntro: Mathematics support for Jumeirah Park families clusters at three points, and the work looks different at each. The step that causes most trouble is the one into the Diploma at sixteen.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Students lose marks for communication and for failing to generalise a pattern, not for arithmetic. A tutor needs the school's own task sheet and criterion descriptors to be useful here, because the standard is set by the school's boundaries.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus, statistics and probability, with Higher Level adding proof by induction, complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form, Maclaurin series and vector geometry. Paper 1 permits no calculator, so exact manipulation has to be fast and reliable. This is the course most engineering, physics, mathematics and economics degrees expect.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai Diploma candidates sit the May session. For AA Higher Level the useful start point is the autumn of the first Diploma year, because the proof and calculus content compounds and a gap in September is a gap in March unless someone closes it.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, all calculator-active, with Higher Level adding graph theory, more advanced statistics and modelling. The course rewards interpretation in context: a correct regression with no comment on what it means scores poorly.
programmes.countryNote: AI is a legitimate route into many degrees and a poor fit for a few. Before choosing it, check the published entry requirements of the universities your child is considering in the UAE and abroad, because some specify Analysis and Approaches for quantitative degrees.

programmes.name: The mathematics exploration
programmes.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing, internally assessed and externally moderated, worth 20 marks across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. It is the single most coachable component in the course, and the one most often left too late.
programmes.countryNote: School deadlines for the exploration typically fall a year before the written papers. A Jumeirah Park family's most common mistake is treating the May session as the deadline that matters when the internal one arrives much sooner.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-park.subjectsIntro: What a maths tutor actually works on, by course and topic. Use these as a test of any tutor: a specialist can say immediately where each one costs students marks.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL: algebra and proof
subjects.description: Proof by induction, binomial expansion, partial fractions and complex numbers in both Cartesian and polar form. Marks go missing in the setup rather than the calculation: an induction proof with no clear inductive step scores badly however correct the algebra is. Non-calculator Paper 1 makes accuracy a trained skill rather than a talent.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches: calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at Higher Level, implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. The commonest failure is technique selection: students who can perform every method individually but cannot tell which integral needs which.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches: functions and trigonometry
subjects.description: Transformations, inverse and composite functions, exponentials and logarithms, trigonometric identities and equations. Students lose marks on domain and range, and on solving trigonometric equations over a stated interval where they find one solution and stop.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation: statistics
subjects.description: Data presentation, correlation and regression, probability distributions and, at Higher Level, hypothesis testing and more advanced inference. The marks sit in interpretation: naming what a gradient means in the context, and whether a correlation justifies the claim being made.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation: modelling
subjects.description: Fitting functions to real data, choosing a model and justifying the choice, then evaluating its limitations. Calculator-active throughout, which means efficiency with the graphing tool is part of the grade. Students who treat the calculator as an answer machine rather than an exploratory tool underperform.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL: graph theory and extensions
subjects.description: Graphs and networks, adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees and shortest-path algorithms, plus complex numbers in a modelling context. These topics are unfamiliar to most parents and are taught late in the course, which is why they are often under-revised relative to their weight.

subjects.name: Paper 3 technique
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions on a single paper, worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade on the standard published structure. Students meet the format rarely and lose marks by abandoning a long question after one blocked step. This is trainable, and it is the component most often ignored until spring.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five criteria. A tutor may teach the criteria, help narrow a topic, teach mathematical writing and comment on the student's own drafts. A tutor may not write, part-write or supply any of it, and the strongest explorations are the ones where the mathematics is slightly simpler and genuinely owned.

subjects.name: Bridging from IGCSE or MYP
subjects.description: Surds, indices, rearrangement, simultaneous equations and algebraic fractions, done quickly and exactly without a calculator. This is what Analysis and Approaches assumes on day one and what a good IGCSE grade does not guarantee. A term of this before the Diploma starts outperforms the same hours spent in the second year.

subjects.name: Quantitative support for other subjects
subjects.description: Physics calculations, economics diagrams and quantitative questions, and business finance all fail for mathematical reasons more often than subject ones. A maths tutor who understands where these overlap can fix a physics problem that no amount of physics revision would resolve.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a Diploma mathematician, and it is frequently made on the wrong grounds. The common framing is that Analysis and Approaches is the harder course and Applications and Interpretation the easier one. That is not how the two differ. AA is algebraic and proof-based with a non-calculator paper; AI is applied, statistical and calculator-active, and it asks for interpretation that many algebraically strong students find genuinely difficult.

The consequential difference is admissions. A number of quantitative degrees -- engineering, physics, mathematics, and some economics and computer science programmes -- specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Others accept either. Because requirements vary by university and by year, the only reliable method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific courses your child is considering, in the UAE and abroad, before the choice is locked.

The second factor is the student. AA Higher Level assumes complete fluency with algebraic manipulation and an appetite for abstraction. AI Higher Level assumes comfort with data, modelling and written interpretation. A student who enjoys a clean algebraic result and dislikes writing about context is badly placed in AI, and the reverse is equally true. Neither is the respectable choice; the mismatch is the problem.

If your child is already in the wrong course, a move is usually possible early in the first Diploma year and rarely sensible later. A single diagnostic session with a maths specialist, working at the standard of the course in question, will tell you more than a term of worrying. The table below sets out the comparison in the terms that actually matter.

sections.heading: How the papers are weighted, and what that changes
paragraphs: Weightings are the fastest way to test whether a tutor knows the course, and the fastest way for a parent to allocate revision time sensibly. On the standard published structure, Standard Level in both courses is examined by two papers plus the exploration, and Higher Level by three papers plus the exploration. The exploration carries a fifth of the grade at every level, which is more than most students behave as though it does.

At Higher Level, Paper 3 is the component students are least prepared for. It consists of extended problem-solving questions rather than the shorter items of Papers 1 and 2, and because schools set it rarely in internal assessments, students meet the format a handful of times before the real thing. A student who abandons a long question after one blocked step loses a disproportionate number of marks.

The implication for a weekly session is concrete. At Standard Level, time splits between calculator and non-calculator technique and the exploration. At Higher Level, the same plus deliberate Paper 3 practice from the spring of the first Diploma year rather than the last six weeks of the second. That sequencing decision is worth more than any number of extra hours in April.

Weightings and structures are set by the IB and are revised from time to time, and the IB's own subject guide is the authority. Confirm the current structure with your child's teacher or the school's copy of the guide rather than relying on any tutoring page, this one included. sections.heading: The twenty marks in the exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Nobody else in this market publishes this, and it is the most useful page of information a Diploma maths student can have. The exploration is marked against five criteria with a total of twenty marks, and the distribution explains why the best explorations are often mathematically modest. Only part of the mark is for the mathematics itself; the rest is for how the work is presented, communicated, owned and reflected upon.

That changes the strategy completely. A student who picks a topic too ambitious to understand properly scores badly on personal engagement and reflection even when the mathematics is impressive, because they cannot say anything original about it. A student who takes a topic they genuinely care about, uses mathematics at the right level for their course, and reflects honestly on what the model does and does not capture, scores well.

The second common failure is mathematical communication: inconsistent notation, undefined variables, graphs without labelled axes, and a structure that reads like a worked solution rather than a piece of writing. These are easy to fix and worth several marks. The third is reflection written as a conclusion -- restating the result instead of evaluating the approach and its limitations.

Criterion labels, descriptors and mark allocations are set by the IB and change between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's copy of the current subject guide. sections.heading: Where marks actually disappear, topic by topic
paragraphs: General advice about practising more is useless. What a maths tutor should be able to do in the first session is name the specific, diagnosable failures in your child's work and say which are content problems and which are technique problems. They need different responses, and the difference is usually visible on one marked paper.

Content problems are gaps: a topic never properly learned, often from before the Diploma. Surds, indices, rearrangement and algebraic fractions are the usual culprits for Analysis and Approaches students, and they surface as calculus errors two years later. These take a few focused sessions and then stay fixed.

Technique problems are different. A student who can perform every individual method but picks the wrong one, who sets up a question incorrectly and then executes perfectly, who rounds too early, or who stops a long Paper 3 question at the first obstacle, has a technique problem. These need marked past papers and a conversation about each decision, not more content teaching.

The way to tell them apart is to look at a marked paper with the student and ask, question by question, what they were thinking. A content gap produces a blank or a wrong method. A technique problem produces a correct method applied to a misread question, or a right answer rounded into a wrong one. The student almost always knows which it was, and nobody asks them.

The third category is exam conduct: running out of time, not showing working on a multi-step question where the final answer is wrong and no method marks are available, or mis-setting the calculator. These are the cheapest marks to recover in the whole course and the ones most often left unaddressed because they feel too trivial to teach.

sections.heading: Fitting a maths session into a Jumeirah Park weekday
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where the hour you choose matters most, because accuracy degrades with tiredness in a way that essay writing does not. A student doing non-calculator algebra at nine in the evening will make arithmetic errors they would not make at half past four, and will conclude they are bad at maths rather than tired.

In this community the school run sets the window. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30, and a Jumeirah Park bus route serving Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village gets most students home between 15:20 and 16:40 depending on district and route. There is no metro station inside Jumeirah Park, so the nearest Route 2020 stations at Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens play no useful part in a tutoring timetable.

That produces a simple rule for maths specifically: take the earliest slot your household can genuinely sustain. Students at the school inside the community can hold 16:00, which is the best maths hour available to anyone here. Bussed students should aim for 17:00 or 17:30 rather than 16:30, because a session that starts before the student has eaten is a session spent on mistakes.

For long work, use the weekend. A Saturday morning slot is the only place in the week where a full timed paper genuinely fits, and marking it on Sunday is where the learning happens. During Ramadan, school hours shorten and a post-Iftar or late-morning weekend session usually works better than anything in the late afternoon; we reschedule rather than cancel.

sections.heading: What a maths specialist costs in this market
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most-tutored subject in Dubai and the one where the price spread is widest, so it is worth knowing what each band buys. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, which buys homework supervision rather than Higher Level teaching. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist work.

Bestimate's Dubai survey puts specialist IB and IGCSE tuition at AED 200-450 or more, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at AED 200-500. BartyED's premium examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. On a monthly basis, Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. All of these are the providers' or survey's own figures, read in October 2026.

Where maths differs from other subjects is that the cheap end is less useful. Supervision helps a student who will not start their homework; it does not help a student who cannot tell which integral needs substitution. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in particular, the qualified-specialist band is the realistic minimum, and paying an in-home travel premium on top of it buys nothing mathematical.

We publish no rate card here because the right figure depends on the course, the level and the weeks remaining. The honest guidance is to start with the free trial session, commit to six sessions rather than twenty, and judge on marked timed work. Discounted long packages move the risk to you before the match has been tested, which is the commonest complaint in this market.

sections.heading: The exploration and the academic honesty line
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is where the tutoring market in this city behaves worst, because it is a written piece with a deadline and a mark attached. One operator in this SERP sells completed internal assessments outright at four-figure prices. That is an academic-integrity breach, an IB malpractice trigger, and the consequence lands on the student rather than the seller.

The legitimate version is narrow and genuinely effective. A tutor can explain the five criteria and what each rewards, help the student narrow a topic to something they can own, teach the conventions of mathematical writing, show what a labelled graph and a defined variable look like, and read the student's draft and say which descriptor band it currently meets and what is missing. The student then fixes it.

A tutor cannot write, part-write, rewrite to completion or supply mathematics for the exploration, and we will not. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers or mark schemes; those are cited and linked, and your child's school holds licensed access to what they need.

Parents sometimes ask where the line sits in practice, because it sounds finer than it is. It is not fine. A tutor saying 'criterion B wants your variables defined before you use them, and three of yours are not' is teaching. A tutor adding the definitions is not. The first produces a student who will define variables for the rest of their life; the second produces a document and a risk.

If you are comparing maths tutors in this area, ask what they will do with an exploration draft. An answer that describes criterion feedback is the right one. An answer that offers to improve the writing or tidy up the mathematics is the wrong one, and it is the answer that puts a Diploma at risk.

sections.heading: Regulator context and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK and Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, with the Ministry of Education supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Every school named on this page sits under KHDA.

IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not hold a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. We explain what these bodies do because parents ask, not because any of them endorses us.

On the tutor side, individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. u.ae states that tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat quoted amounts with suspicion.

There is also a timetable point that affects mathematics planning in Dubai specifically. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. In a Diploma week already carrying six subjects and the core, that is real pressure, and it is why one properly used maths hour beats three scattered ones.

faqs.question: We have to pick between the two maths courses this term. How do we decide?
faqs.answer: Decide on two grounds: the degree requirement and the student. A number of quantitative degrees, including engineering, physics and mathematics, specify Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while others accept either, so read the published entry requirements for the specific courses your child is considering. Then match the student: AA suits those who like exact algebraic results, AI those comfortable with data, modelling and written interpretation. AI is not the easier course; it is a different one, and the mismatch rather than the difficulty is what causes trouble.

faqs.question: How are the marks split between the papers in IB maths?
faqs.answer: On the commonly published structure, Standard Level is examined by two papers plus the exploration, with the papers carrying around forty per cent each and the exploration around twenty. Higher Level has three papers plus the exploration, with Papers 1 and 2 at around thirty per cent each, Paper 3 around twenty and the exploration around twenty. Weightings are set by the IB and revised between syllabus cycles, so confirm the current structure with your child's teacher or the school's copy of the subject guide rather than from any tutoring page.

faqs.question: What are the twenty marks in the maths exploration awarded for?
faqs.answer: On the commonly published allocation, five criteria share twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with the mathematics itself carrying the largest single share and the other four together carrying more. That is why modest mathematics genuinely owned outscores ambitious mathematics the student cannot discuss. Criterion labels and allocations change between syllabus cycles, so confirm them against your school's current subject guide. A tutor may teach all five and comment on drafts, and may write none of it.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 change how you teach Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Because no calculator is permitted. Every manipulation has to be exact and fast, which makes algebraic fluency a trained skill rather than a by-product of understanding. A student who can do the mathematics with a calculator and cannot do it without one will lose marks across a whole paper for reasons unrelated to comprehension. The implication is that non-calculator work belongs in weekly sessions from the first term of the Diploma, not in a revision block in the spring of the second year.

faqs.question: My child was strong at IGCSE maths but is struggling in the Diploma. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the Diploma assumes fluency that a good IGCSE grade does not guarantee. Surds, indices, rearrangement, algebraic fractions and simultaneous equations have to be fast and exact, and Analysis and Approaches builds calculus on top of them within weeks. A student who was accurate but slow at IGCSE now runs out of time and makes errors under pressure. A few focused sessions on that foundation, done properly, usually produces more improvement than weeks of work on the new content.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to our villa in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all; our in-person service runs in India only. IB mathematics tuition for Jumeirah Park families is delivered live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared working surface and past papers on screen. For mathematics that format is genuinely strong, because both people can write where the other can see it. If presence in the room is essential, the Dubai market charges roughly AED 180-500 an hour for in-home visits including travel.

faqs.question: What time of day is best for a maths session?
faqs.answer: The earliest hour your household can sustain. Arithmetic accuracy degrades with tiredness more visibly than essay quality does, and a student making careless errors at nine in the evening concludes they are weak at maths rather than tired. In this community that means 16:00 for students at the school inside Jumeirah Park and 17:00 or 17:30 for those bussed in from Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village. Keep full timed papers for Saturday morning, which is the only ninety-minute block in the week.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: One a week from the start of the first Diploma year is the pattern that works, rising to two or three per week in the final weeks before the May session. Mathematics compounds more than any other Diploma subject, so a weak topic in September is still weak in March unless someone closes it. Families who start weekly and early usually need less total support than those who start intensively and late, and they also hold the earlier evening slots that are scarce in the spring term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help if my child has picked the wrong maths course?
faqs.answer: A tutor cannot change the entry, but a single diagnostic session will tell you whether the concern is real. The tutor works at the standard of the course in question with the student and reports back on fluency and fit rather than on enthusiasm. Moves between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are usually possible early in the first Diploma year and rarely sensible later, so this is a conversation for the autumn term with the school rather than a decision to postpone.

faqs.question: Roughly what hourly figure should we budget for Diploma mathematics support?
faqs.answer: Published figures put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IB from AED 200, and specialist IB tuition at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65, which buys supervision rather than Higher Level teaching. In-home visits run AED 180-500 including travel. Those are the providers' own figures read in October 2026. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on the course, the level and the weeks left.

faqs.question: Is Paper 3 really worth separate practice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most under-prepared component in Higher Level mathematics. It consists of extended problem-solving questions rather than the shorter items students meet all year, and schools rarely set that format internally, so students arrive unfamiliar with it. The characteristic failure is abandoning a long question after a single blocked step, which forfeits marks that were still available further down. Building it into sessions from the spring of the first Diploma year is worth more than any number of extra hours in April.

faqs.question: What should my child choose as an exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Something they can genuinely talk about, using mathematics at the level of their course rather than above it. The marks reward personal engagement, reflection and communication alongside the mathematics itself, so an ambitious topic the student cannot discuss critically scores worse than a modest one they own. Start from an interest, find the mathematics inside it, and check with the teacher that the mathematics is appropriate for the course. Begin at least a term before the school's internal deadline, not three weeks before.

faqs.question: Does my child need a particular graphing calculator?
faqs.answer: The school specifies the permitted models and the exam regulations require memory to be cleared, so follow the school's instruction rather than buying on a recommendation. The point worth making is that familiarity is part of the grade: Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout, and a student who is slow with the model loses marks on time rather than on mathematics. Practising with the exact device, under time, is part of what sessions should cover in the term before the papers.

faqs.question: Would the same person be able to take physics as well as maths?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level often yes, and the overlap is genuinely useful: many physics errors are mathematical ones, and a tutor who sees both can fix a physics problem that physics revision would not resolve. At Higher Level we usually advise two tutors, because genuine depth in both Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Physics Higher Level is rare, and a tutor stretched across both tends to be strong in one. Two fixed evenings is also easier to protect than one long combined session.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start maths tutoring in the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but more expensive per unit of improvement and more constrained by what is still available. If the exploration is already submitted, the work becomes technique and past papers, which responds quickly. If the problem is a foundational gap in algebra, closing it in the second year costs weeks that the revision programme needs. The honest answer depends on the marked evidence, and if we think the weeks remaining are too few for a subject to move meaningfully, we will say so rather than sell the hours.

intro.heading: What a maths tutor should be able to tell you in the first ten minutes
paragraphs: Mathematics is the most requested subject in Jumeirah Village Circle and the easiest to hire badly, because almost anybody can appear competent discussing it. The test that separates a specialist from a capable graduate is not whether they can solve the problem. It is whether they can say where the marks were available and why your child's answer did not earn them, which requires knowing the syllabus structure, the command terms and the mark-scheme conventions.

Start with structure. Both IB Mathematics routes cover five syllabus topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Analysis and Approaches weights the algebraic and calculus end and includes a non-calculator paper; Applications and Interpretation weights statistics and modelling with technology permitted throughout. At Standard Level both routes sit two papers; at Higher Level they sit three, with the third being a short set of extended investigative questions. The exploration carries 20 per cent in every case. Confirm the exact weightings with your school's subject guide.

Then command terms, which in mathematics are stricter than anywhere else in the Diploma. Show that requires a derivation that ends at the stated result, so quoting the result earns nothing. Hence means the previous part must be used, and an answer reached by a different route can lose marks even when it is correct. Sketch and draw are different instructions with different requirements. Determine implies a specific answer; justify requires a reason attached to it. Students lose marks to every one of these while knowing the mathematics perfectly.

Then the traps, which are remarkably consistent. Method lines omitted on multi-mark questions, where the steps carry most of the marks. Intermediate values rounded and carried forward, forfeiting the accuracy mark. Calculator left in degrees for a radian question, producing plausible wrong answers invisibly across a whole question. And, on Applications and Interpretation, a correct calculation followed by an interpretation sentence that does not answer the context the question set.

There is one more thing a specialist notices that a generalist does not. On Analysis and Approaches, the first paper is taken without a calculator, and the exact-manipulation skills it depends on — surds, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws, algebraic fractions — decay quietly across two years in which every piece of homework is done with a device on the desk. Students meet the consequence in a mock and read it as a content problem when it is a fluency problem. Applications and Interpretation candidates have no such issue and should spend those hours on interpretation instead.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, matched to the route your child sits. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Everything below is written so you can use it as a set of questions, on us or on anyone else.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-village.subjectsIntro: Here is the mathematics syllabus as a set of teachable parts, with the route each belongs to and the specific way each one fails under examination conditions.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: proof
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction, and induction at Higher Level. The failure is structural: students write true statements in an order that establishes nothing, because proof has never been taught as a form. Three or four sessions and the habit changes.

subjects.name: Number and algebra: sequences, series, binomial
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, sigma notation, and the binomial theorem at Higher Level. Marks are lost on index arithmetic and on failing to state which formula is being applied, which the mark scheme credits separately from the answer.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, rational functions and transformations. The topic where weak algebra becomes visible, and where a student who scraped through Year 11 starts losing marks on questions that are not really about functions.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: identities and equations
subjects.description: The unit circle, identities, trigonometric equations and radian measure. Calculator mode is the classic loss here: degrees left on during a radian question gives plausible wrong answers through an entire question with nothing visibly wrong.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry: vectors
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes, intersections and angles between them. Students lose presentation marks by producing a correct calculation without stating what it establishes about the geometry, which is what the question asked.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity. Self-contained and content-heavy, which makes it one of the most efficient topics to tutor: five focused sessions usually secures it.

subjects.name: Calculus: differentiation
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation at Higher Level, stationary points, related rates and kinematics. The most hour-hungry part of Analysis and Approaches and where most of the session count goes.

subjects.name: Calculus: integration
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, substitution and integration by parts at Higher Level, volumes of revolution and differential equations. Marks are lost by omitting the constant, mis-setting limits after substitution, and not stating the method used.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous distributions, the normal distribution, correlation and regression, and hypothesis testing at Applications and Interpretation Higher Level. The characteristic Applications failure is a correct test followed by a conclusion stated without reference to the significance level.

subjects.name: Modelling and financial mathematics
subjects.description: Functions as models, compound interest, amortisation and depreciation. The marks sit in justification: a curve fitted without saying why that function suits the data loses the reasoning marks regardless of how well it fits.

subjects.name: Graph theory and matrices
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees, Chinese postman and travelling salesman problems, transition matrices and eigenvalues. Rarely taught well from a textbook alone and the single scarcest specialist request in the subject.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: An independent written investigation carrying 20 per cent of the grade, marked against five criteria with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation. Mathematics below the level of the course caps the mark whatever the writing is like, which is why the topic decision matters most.

sections.heading: The five topics, and where each route puts its weight
paragraphs: Both Mathematics routes cover number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. That shared list is why families assume the two courses are tiers of the same thing, and they are not. The weighting and the depth within each topic differ enough to make them different subjects in practice.

Analysis and Approaches puts its weight in algebra, trigonometric identities and calculus, extending at Higher Level into complex numbers, vectors, implicit differentiation, integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. Its statistics content exists but is lighter. The habit of mind it rewards is exact manipulation, and its Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which makes arithmetic fluency load-bearing in a way nothing else in the Diploma is.

Applications and Interpretation puts its weight in statistics, modelling and financial mathematics, extending at Higher Level into hypothesis testing, graph theory, matrices and eigenvalues. Technology is permitted throughout, which shifts the difficulty from executing a calculation to choosing and justifying a model and then interpreting the output in the context the question set. Its calculus exists at Higher Level and is lighter than Analysis and Approaches calculus.

The practical test for a prospective tutor is to ask which topics carry the Higher Level extension in your child's route, and what the first paper's calculator position is. A specialist answers in two sentences. The table below sets the comparison out topic by topic so you can check the answer.

sections.heading: Mathematical command terms, with the marks attached
paragraphs: In mathematics the command terms are not stylistic preferences; they are instructions with mark consequences, and most students have never seen them listed. Show that requires a derivation that arrives at the stated result. A student who writes the result down and verifies it numerically has not shown it and earns nothing, however correct the arithmetic.

Hence means the previous part must be used. A student who reaches the right answer by an independent method can lose marks, which feels unfair until you realise the question was testing whether they could see the connection. Hence or otherwise relaxes it and signals that the connection is the efficient route.

Sketch and draw are distinct. Sketch wants the shape with key features — intercepts, asymptotes, turning points — labelled, and does not require accurate scale. Draw wants an accurate graph on a scale. Plot wants specific points marked. Students produce a careful accurate graph where a labelled sketch was wanted, spending four minutes to earn two marks, or a vague sketch where accuracy was required and losing them.

Determine implies a specific numerical or algebraic answer. Justify requires a reason attached to an answer, and an unjustified correct answer loses the justification mark. Deduce requires a conclusion drawn from information already given. Verify permits substitution where show that does not. Each of these appears in mark schemes with its own credit, and a tutor who cannot distinguish them is going to let your child keep losing the same marks.
