sections.heading: The four mark-scheme traps, in order of cost
paragraphs: First and largest: missing method. On a four, five or six-mark question most of the marks are allocated to the steps, and a student who writes only a final answer loses nearly all of them if that answer is wrong. This is pure habit, costs nothing to fix, and in a typical marked mock from a Jumeirah Village Circle student it is worth several marks a page.

Second: rounding. An intermediate value rounded to three significant figures and carried into the next step produces a final answer that is close and not correct, and the accuracy mark goes. The rule is full calculator precision throughout and rounding once at the end. Students break it because partial rounding looks tidier, and nobody has told them it is an examined convention.

Third: calculator mode. Degrees left on during a radian question yields plausible wrong answers through an entire question with nothing visibly wrong to the student. Checking mode before every paper is a thirty-second habit that is almost never taught. The reverse error, radians during a degrees question, is rarer and equally expensive.

Fourth, and specific to Applications and Interpretation: interpretation. The regression runs, the correlation coefficient appears, the test statistic is correct, and the sentence underneath does not say what any of it means for the situation the question described. On that route the interpretation sentences carry real marks and they are the difference between a 5 and a 7. Every one of these four is visible in a single marked paper, which is why we ask for one before quoting anything.

sections.heading: Paper 3 at Higher Level, and how to practise it
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, carries a substantial weighting, and is the component where capable candidates most often underperform. It consists of a small number of extended investigative questions, each running across several parts where every answer feeds the next. A slip in an early part propagates all the way through, and there is no second question to recover on.

What it rewards is not more content. It is the ability to follow an unfamiliar line of mathematical reasoning that the paper itself constructs, and to keep going when the destination is not visible. Students who are strong on the first two papers often stall on it because they have never practised sustaining a chain of inference for twenty minutes.

The practice protocol matters more here than anywhere else in the course. The question must be sat under timed conditions, uninterrupted, with no notes. Then it is marked against the scheme. Then — and this is the part that is usually skipped — the reasoning is walked back from the point of failure to establish what the student could have noticed. Doing that once properly is worth more than working through three questions collaboratively.

There is a scarcity constraint. Far fewer Paper 3 questions exist than Paper 1 and 2 questions, and once a student has seen one it cannot serve as a genuine diagnostic again. So the sensible pattern is three or four dedicated sessions in the second half of Year 13, after content is covered, rather than scattering the material earlier. A tutor who has taught the course for several years is the person most likely to know which of the existing questions are worth the time.

sections.heading: Non-calculator fluency, and why it rots
paragraphs: This section applies to Analysis and Approaches candidates and it is the most overlooked part of their preparation. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, which means a substantial share of the available marks depends on exact manipulation: surds, exact trigonometric values, fraction arithmetic, logarithm laws, factorisation and recognising when an expression simplifies.

Those skills decay quietly. Every piece of homework a Year 11 and Year 12 student does has a device on the desk, so the muscle that handles exact forms is not used for two years and then is required for ninety minutes. Students discover this in a mock, where they can do the mathematics and cannot execute it without technology, and they interpret it as a content problem when it is a fluency problem.

The fix is deliberate and short. A set of exact-value questions done daily for a few weeks, with no device in the room, rebuilds it faster than anything else. Three sessions establishing which forms a student fumbles — surd rationalising, exact sine and cosine values, logarithm manipulation, algebraic fractions — plus daily practice between them is usually enough.

The timing is the useful part. This belongs in the final eight to ten weeks, because fluency rebuilt in Year 12 will decay again before the papers. Applications and Interpretation candidates can skip this entirely and spend the same hours on model justification and interpretation, which is where their marks actually sit. A tutor who prescribes non-calculator drilling to an Applications student has not asked which route they are on.

sections.heading: How past-paper work should actually run
paragraphs: Every provider claims to use past papers. The version worth paying for has three stages and most arrangements skip two. The student attempts the question or paper under genuine timed conditions, alone, without notes and without stopping when stuck. The tutor then marks it against the published scheme, with the scheme visible, annotating each place where a mark was available and not earned. The following session works on what was lost and nothing else.

What is not past-paper work: going through questions together as they arise, which removes both the timing and the independent attempt that make the exercise diagnostic. Handing over a folder of papers to be done alone, which produces unmarked work and false confidence. Or reworking questions the student has already seen the solutions to, which tests recall rather than skill.

There is a quantity point. Papers are finite, and for Paper 3 they are very finite. A paper spent untimed or unmarked is a diagnostic destroyed, because the questions cannot be unseen. The sensible allocation is a couple early for diagnosis and the bulk in the final eight to ten weeks under conditions.

One rule about materials, because this is where some providers overstep. We do not reproduce or distribute IB past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables, syllabus documents or subject guides as downloads. Tutors work from the copies the school provides and link to the official source. A provider offering a complete folder of everything is describing something they should not be doing, and it is a fair signal about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: The exploration, and the one thing that caps the mark
paragraphs: The exploration carries 20 per cent of the Mathematics grade and is marked against five criteria. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation, which is the most useful fact about it and the one students least often know when they choose a topic.

That allocation produces a specific failure mode. An exploration that is beautifully written, genuinely personal and mathematically trivial cannot score well, because the criterion worth the most is assessing whether the mathematics is commensurate with the level of the course. Conversely, appropriate mathematics presented badly loses across presentation and communication but retains its core. Topic choice therefore sets a ceiling, and it is made in a single conversation months before any writing.

So the help worth buying is early and short: three sessions testing whether the proposed mathematics is at the right level, whether the data or context can actually support it, and whether the question is narrow enough to finish. Trying to raise a finished exploration built on trivial mathematics in the final fortnight is expensive and rarely works, and families buy that far more often than they buy the early conversation.

The boundary applies here as firmly as anywhere. A tutor may discuss topic viability, question whether the mathematics is appropriate, explain what each criterion rewards, mark a draft against the criteria and teach referencing. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite the student's prose, supply the topic as a finished product, provide data the student has not collected, or edit it to completion. Our tutors decline requests that cross that line, and keeping dated session notes protects the student if authenticity is queried.

sections.heading: What it costs, and scheduling it in the Circle
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with one UK-based agency publishing AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150. In-home visits including travel run AED 180 to AED 500, with one provider publishing AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. All read from the providers' own pages in October 2026.

For the work on this page the specialist band is the right one, because the value is entirely in assessment knowledge. The blocks are modest: three sessions for command terms and technique, five to eight for a named topic, three or four for Paper 3, three for the exploration at the topic stage, and three for non-calculator rebuilding if your child is on Analysis and Approaches.

On timing: most Jumeirah Village Circle students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South and are home by 3.45pm, but Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. So mathematics sessions work around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one, with the later end for anybody commuting from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square.

Place the session after a first attempt at the problem set. That ordering matters more for this work than for content teaching, because command-term and mark-scheme work needs the student's own flawed answer to operate on. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers and for Paper 3, which need ninety uninterrupted minutes a weekday evening here rarely provides.

process.title: Name the route, the level and the topic
process.description: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level calculus and Applications and Interpretation Standard Level statistics are different jobs. The school's subject guide or the timetable states the route. Naming the topic as well turns a general request into a block with a defined end point.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A marked script shows which of the four traps is operating — missing method, rounding carried forward, calculator mode, or absent interpretation — and whether there is a genuine topic gap underneath. Those have different fixes and different session counts, and the script settles it in twenty minutes.

process.title: Test the tutor on command terms
process.description: Ask what show that requires and why quoting the result earns nothing, what hence obliges a candidate to do, and how sketch differs from draw. A specialist answers all three immediately. Somebody who treats them as stylistic variation will let your child keep losing the same marks all year.

process.title: Take the free trial on the lost question
process.description: You and your child meet the proposed route-specific tutor over live video. Hand them a question from the mock that was lost, with the mark scheme. Afterwards you get their read, a session count and the fee, and you decide. No payment is required to reach that point.

process.title: Insist on marking rather than discussion
process.description: Agree that work set between sessions comes back marked against the published scheme, with the scheme shown to the student. A question discussed produces agreement with a correct answer; a question marked produces a list of the specific marks their own writing failed to earn.

whyPoints.title: Route-specific staffing
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation reward different habits of mind and fail in different ways. We staff them separately, because a tutor who is excellent at proof and calculus can lose a term on model justification and hypothesis testing, and generalists rarely volunteer which one they know.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught as instructions
whyPoints.description: Show that, hence, sketch, draw, justify and verify carry separate credit in mark schemes, and most students have never had them explained. Three sessions on this improves every topic at once, which makes it the cheapest grade movement in the subject and the one nobody sells.

whyPoints.title: Marking with the scheme visible
whyPoints.description: Work set between sessions comes back marked against the published scheme rather than talked through. That is the difference between a student agreeing with a correct answer and a student seeing which available marks their own lines failed to earn.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own skill
whyPoints.description: At Higher Level it rewards sustaining an unfamiliar chain of reasoning, which nothing else in the course trains, and the available material is scarce. We spend it late, under timed conditions, and walk the reasoning back from the point of failure rather than solving it together.

whyPoints.title: Non-calculator work prescribed by route
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches candidates need deliberate exact-form drilling in the final weeks because fluency decays across two years of device-assisted homework. Applications candidates do not, and should spend those hours on interpretation instead. A tutor who prescribes it to both has not asked.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery and no invented claims
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, as in-person home tutoring exists only in our India service. No examiner claims we cannot evidence, no guaranteed grades, and every AED figure here credited to its published source.

faqs.question: What should an IB maths tutor be able to tell me straight away?
faqs.answer: Which route and level your child is on, which papers that means they sit, what the first paper's calculator position is, and which topics carry the Higher Level extension. Then, from a marked script, which of the four standard traps is costing marks: missing method lines, rounding carried forward, calculator mode, or absent interpretation sentences. A specialist covers all of that in ten minutes. Somebody who moves the conversation to confidence and study skills is offering a different and cheaper service.

faqs.question: What does "show that" actually require in an IB maths answer?
faqs.answer: A derivation that ends at the stated result. The question gives you the destination and asks you to build the road to it, so writing the result down and checking it numerically has not shown anything and earns nothing, however correct the arithmetic. This is one of the most expensive misunderstandings in the subject, because show that questions are often worth four or five marks and students who know the mathematics perfectly leave almost all of them unclaimed by verifying instead of deriving.

faqs.question: Why did my child lose marks when their answer was right?
faqs.answer: Three likely reasons. The question said hence, meaning the previous part had to be used, and an independent method does not earn the method marks even when the answer is correct. Or the working was not shown on a multi-mark question, where the steps carry most of the allocation. Or a justification was required and only the answer was given. All three are visible in a marked script, all three are habit rather than knowledge, and all three usually clear in about three sessions.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between sketch and draw in an IB maths question?
faqs.answer: Yes, and students lose time or marks in both directions. Sketch wants the shape with key features labelled — intercepts, asymptotes, turning points — and does not require an accurate scale. Draw wants an accurate graph on a scale. Plot wants specific points marked. A student who produces a careful scaled graph where a labelled sketch was wanted spends four minutes earning two marks; one who sketches vaguely where accuracy was required loses the accuracy marks outright.

faqs.question: Which maths topic needs the most tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Calculus, on the Analysis and Approaches route, by a clear margin: differentiation rules, implicit differentiation at Higher Level, integration by substitution and parts, related rates, volumes of revolution and differential equations are each substantial. On Applications and Interpretation the heaviest requests are hypothesis testing and graph theory, with graph theory the scarcest specialist need in the whole subject. The most efficient topics to tutor are the self-contained ones — complex numbers and vectors — where five focused sessions usually secures the topic.

faqs.question: Why does my child struggle on Paper 1 but not in class?
faqs.answer: If they are on Analysis and Approaches, almost certainly non-calculator fluency. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator, so exact manipulation carries a large share of the marks: surds, exact trigonometric values, logarithm laws, algebraic fractions. Those skills decay quietly across two years in which every piece of homework is done with a device on the desk. Students read the result as a content problem when it is a fluency problem. Three sessions plus short daily sets with no device in the room rebuilds it.

faqs.question: How should Paper 3 be practised at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: One question at a time, under genuine timed conditions, uninterrupted and without notes. Then marked against the scheme. Then — the stage usually skipped — the reasoning walked back from where it failed to establish what the student could have noticed. Doing that once properly beats working through three questions collaboratively. Available Paper 3 material is scarce and cannot be unseen, so spend it in the second half of Year 13 after content is covered rather than scattering it earlier.

faqs.question: What makes an exploration score badly even when it reads well?
faqs.answer: Mathematics below the level of the course. Use of mathematics carries the largest single criterion allocation, so an exploration that is beautifully written, genuinely personal and mathematically trivial cannot score well on the criterion worth most. Appropriate mathematics presented poorly loses on presentation and communication but keeps its core. That is why topic choice sets a ceiling and why three sessions at the topic stage, months before any writing, is worth several times what late help on a finished draft can achieve.

faqs.question: How do we pick between the two maths routes on the mathematics itself?
faqs.answer: Choose on the mathematics and on published entry requirements rather than on reputation. Analysis and Approaches rewards exact manipulation and abstraction and is often specified for engineering, mathematics and physics degrees, frequently at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, data handling and interpretation and suits students who think in context. Write down three or four degree subjects under consideration and check the actual mathematics requirement at two or three universities for each, then decide from that list.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both IB maths routes properly?
faqs.answer: Some can, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. The honest test is whether they can say which topics carry the Higher Level extension in each route and where each route's marks are typically lost — exact manipulation on one, interpretation sentences on the other. A tutor strong on proof and calculus who has never taught hypothesis testing or graph theory will lose a term on an Applications student. We staff the routes separately for that reason and will tell you which specialism we are proposing.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions does my child need?
faqs.answer: It depends what the marked script shows. Three sessions if the losses are command terms and method habits, which is the most common finding. Five to eight for one named syllabus topic. Three or four for Paper 3 at Higher Level. Three for the exploration at the topic stage. Three for non-calculator rebuilding on Analysis and Approaches. Those blocks are additive rather than alternatives, but they should be bought one at a time with a review between, not committed to as a year.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition suitable for this kind of work?
faqs.answer: Particularly suitable, because the medium is a shared writing surface. A derivation builds line by line where both people see it, the mark scheme sits open on both sides, and the session can be revisited. For marking work especially it is better than paper: the annotation appears on the student's own script while they watch. What matters far more than the room is whether the tutor knows the route and the mark-scheme conventions, which is the whole argument for matching by specialism rather than distance.

faqs.question: When should a maths session run for a student in Jumeirah Village Circle?
faqs.answer: Around 5.30pm for students without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm for those with one, with the later end for anybody commuting from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square. Most Circle students travel only five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South and are home by 3.45pm, but Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers and Paper 3 practice.

faqs.question: What if no Applications and Interpretation specialist is free?
faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait rather than an Analysis and Approaches tutor offered as a substitute. Graph theory and matrices at Applications and Interpretation Higher Level is the scarcest specialist request in this syllabus, and availability tightens further in the eight weeks before the May session. In the meantime a command-term and technique block can often run with a different specialist, which is genuinely useful work. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so, including the time zone, before any payment.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-village.closingBody: Almost anybody can solve an IB maths question. The useful tutor is the one who can look at your child's script and say which available marks their own lines failed to earn, and why — the missing method step, the value rounded too early, the calculator left in degrees, the interpretation sentence never written. Send us the route, the level, the topic and one marked paper, and we will propose a route-specific specialist you can test on exactly that in a free trial lesson over live video. No home visits in the UAE and no promised grades.

intro.heading: Three problems, and only one of them is about algebra
paragraphs: Almost every request for an IB maths tutor in Jumeirah Village Triangle traces back to one of three distinct problems, and they need different work. The first is course mismatch: a student placed on Analysis and Approaches who needed Applications and Interpretation, or the reverse, usually discovered three months into DP1 when the first set of marked papers comes back. The second is Paper 1, which both AA routes sit without a calculator. The third is the Exploration, the internally assessed report worth 20% of the grade at both levels, which students begin late and then cannot narrow.

Course mismatch is the most expensive of the three because it is the hardest to undo. AA assesses algebraic fluency, proof and calculus technique. AI is calculator-permitted throughout, statistics-led, and at Higher Level adds graph theory and matrices. Neither is the easy one. Students choose AI expecting relief and meet hypothesis testing, chi-squared and regression with no statistical vocabulary; students choose AA for university reasons and then discover Paper 1 punishes anybody who learned mathematics with a graphing display calculator in their hand. The decision should be driven by the degree prerequisite and by honest evidence of algebraic fluency, in that order.

Paper 1 is the most fixable. A student who can differentiate on a calculator but cannot sketch a cubic from its factors, find an exact value involving surds, or complete the square without prompting, is not short of understanding — they are short of fluency, and fluency responds to short daily practice better than to long weekly sessions. Six to eight weeks of twenty manipulations a day changes a Paper 1 score in a way that no amount of topic revision does.

The Exploration is the most leveraged. It is 20% of the grade, marked against five criteria worth 20 marks in total, and it is the one component where a student controls both the question and the timeline. Most Explorations lose marks not in the mathematics but in criteria that reward personal engagement, reflection and precise mathematical communication. A tutor can legitimately do a great deal here — interrogate the topic, check the mathematics is at the right level, explain what each criterion credits — while the student writes every word submitted. Started in DP1, it is a project with slack in it; started in the term it is due, it becomes a scramble in which the topic can no longer be changed and the ceiling is already fixed.

This page also does something the briefs for the neighbouring communities ask for: it compares Jumeirah Village Triangle with Dubai Sports City, Motor City and the Arabian Ranches cluster, because parents in all four ask whether the local answer differs. It does not, and the reason it does not is worth seeing laid out. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria: Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts, each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. The programme rewards reasoning and presentation rather than drilled manipulation, which produces students who can explain a method clearly and cannot execute it quickly. There are no external examinations unless the school uses MYP eAssessment.

A student arriving on Analysis and Approaches with strong MYP reasoning and weak algebraic fluency hits Paper 1 and stalls. Eight to twelve sessions of indices, surds, rearrangement, factorising and function notation before DP1 starts usually closes it; after the first DP1 assessment it takes longer.

programmes.description: The algebraic route. SL sits Papers 1 and 2; HL adds Paper 3, a two-question extended investigation worth 20% of the grade. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator at both levels, which is the defining feature of the course. The Exploration is 20% at both levels. Content runs through functions, sequences, trigonometry, calculus and, at HL, proof and complex numbers.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route most often required by engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees, and some programmes specify it at Higher Level. Students at JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai and Fairgreen International School take it in numbers, which means UAE evening cover for AA is deep and a match is usually quick.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling and statistics route, calculator-permitted on every paper. SL sits Papers 1 and 2; HL adds Paper 3 and extends into graph theory and matrices. Statistical inference is the heart of the course: hypothesis testing, chi-squared, correlation and regression, all of which demand precise vocabulary. Students who treat it as the undemanding option tend to find the statistics harder than the algebra they avoided.
programmes.countryNote: AI suits students heading for business, social sciences, design, psychology and many life-science routes, and it is a legitimate and well-designed course rather than a fallback. The caution for UAE families is prerequisite checking: confirm on the admissions page of each target university whether AA is specified, because a late discovery is very difficult to fix in DP2.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-village.subjectsIntro: The mathematics components and topics most often worked on from the Jumeirah Village Triangle area, with what each actually demands. Topic choice here is driven by where marks are lost rather than by syllabus order.

subjects.name: Paper 1, no calculator
subjects.description: Exact values, surds, completing the square, sketching from factorised form and differentiating by hand. Students who learned on a graphing display calculator lose marks they understand conceptually. Short daily fluency practice moves this score more reliably than weekly topic revision.

subjects.name: Paper 2, calculator permitted
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Longer multi-part questions where the calculator is a tool rather than the method. Marks go on premature rounding, unstated working and failing to interpret a result in context. Writing the full unrounded value and rounding once at the end recovers marks across the whole paper.

subjects.name: HL Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended investigation questions in one hour, worth 20% of the grade. The structure guides a student through unfamiliar mathematics, which rewards reading carefully and following the scaffold. School mock papers do not always include one, so it is frequently the least practised component in the course.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: An internally assessed mathematical report worth 20%, marked out of 20 across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The topic decides the ceiling; mathematics pitched below the course level caps the final criterion.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration techniques, with HL extending into implicit differentiation, related rates and differential equations. The recurring loss is chain-rule execution inside a product or quotient, and integration by substitution where the substitution is not stated.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample, plus proof of trigonometric identities. Students often produce a correct argument in the wrong form, which scores poorly. The structure of an inductive proof is mechanical once learned and is a reliable source of marks.

subjects.name: Statistical inference
subjects.description: Hypothesis testing, chi-squared tests for independence, correlation and regression. Marks are lost in the statement of hypotheses and wherever a conclusion asserts a causal relationship from a correlation. Vocabulary is assessed as much as computation here.

subjects.name: Graph theory and matrices
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, walks, trees, minimum spanning trees and transition matrices. Unfamiliar to most students arriving from MYP or IGCSE, and taught late in many schemes of work, so it often arrives shortly before mocks with little practice attached.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.description: Radian measure, identities, equations over a given domain and, at HL, compound angle work. The common error is losing solutions by dividing through by a trigonometric factor, and giving answers in degrees when the domain was set in radians.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and financial applications
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, sums to infinity, and in AI the financial applications including amortisation and annuities. Questions are often set in context, and the marks sit in translating the context into the right formula before any computation happens.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that determines whether the next two years are difficult in a productive way or in a wasteful one. The two courses are not tiers of the same subject. AA is the algebraic and analytic route: functions, calculus, trigonometric manipulation and, at Higher Level, proof and complex numbers. AI is the modelling and statistics route: data, inference, financial applications and, at Higher Level, graph theory and matrices. Both exist at SL and HL. Both are respectable. They suit different students and different degrees.

The order of reasoning should be prerequisite first, aptitude second. Several engineering, mathematics, physics and quantitative economics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches, some at Higher Level, and a student who takes AI and then applies to one of them has a problem that no tutor can solve in DP2. Check each target university's admissions page directly rather than relying on a school's general advice, and do it before the subject-choice form is signed rather than after.

Where the prerequisite permits either, aptitude decides. The honest test for AA is non-calculator algebra: can the student rearrange, factorise, handle surds and indices, and differentiate by hand with reasonable speed. The honest test for AI is statistical language: can they state a null hypothesis properly and describe a correlation without asserting cause. Most students are stronger on one of these than the other, and the diagnostic takes about forty minutes.

If the mismatch has already happened, say so early. A move between courses is usually possible in the first term of DP1 and progressively harder after that, and the school decides. The useful contribution a tutor makes is evidence: a few sessions of real questions from both courses, marked, so the conversation with the Diploma coordinator rests on something other than a parent's impression.

sections.heading: The Exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, twenty per cent
paragraphs: The Exploration is the most controllable mark in IB Mathematics and the one most often left to drift. It is internally assessed, worth 20% of the grade at both SL and HL on both courses, and marked out of 20 across five criteria. Unlike an examination, the student chooses the question, controls the timeline and can revise the work before submission. Unlike an examination, the marks lost are usually not mathematical.

The criteria reward different things. Presentation credits a coherent, organised piece with a clear aim. Mathematical communication credits correct notation, defined variables, labelled graphs and consistent terminology — and is where students who write in calculator syntax lose marks routinely. Personal engagement credits genuine interest and independent thinking, not enthusiasm declared in the introduction. Reflection credits critical discussion of limitations, assumptions and the significance of results. Use of mathematics credits work that is relevant, correct and commensurate with the level of the course.

That last criterion is where topic choice becomes decisive. An Exploration on a topic whose mathematics sits below the level of the course cannot score well on it however neatly it is written, and a Higher Level student modelling something with simple linear regression has capped themselves before writing a sentence. Equally, a topic requiring mathematics far beyond the course produces an essay the student cannot explain, which costs reflection and communication as well.

A tutor's legitimate role is substantial and precise. Interrogate the proposed topic until it carries appropriate mathematics. Check the data exists and can be obtained honestly. Explain what each criterion credits using the official descriptors. Read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. What the tutor must not do is choose the topic, write any part of the report, restructure it by rewriting, or produce the mathematics. The student writes every submitted word.

sections.heading: The Triangle against the communities next door
paragraphs: Families in Jumeirah Village Triangle, Dubai Sports City, Motor City and the Arabian Ranches cluster all ask whether the local answer is different, and the comparison is worth doing properly because the conclusion is useful. On the mathematics itself, the answer is identical in all four: the same two courses, the same Paper 1 without a calculator, the same Exploration criteria, the same HL Paper 3. The syllabus does not change across a roundabout.

What does change is the commute, and the commute decides the session time. No IB Diploma school sits inside the Triangle, Sports City or Motor City, so a Diploma mathematics student in any of them travels out to school and back. From the Triangle the realistic earliest start is around 17:30; from Motor City and DAMAC Hills, closer to 18:00 or 18:30. The Arabian Ranches cluster is the exception, because JESS Arabian Ranches is on the doorstep for some families there.

That single variable is what makes the in-home model awkward across this whole belt. A tutor driving in has to arrive after the student does, which pushes a two-hour minimum booking into the late evening, and the latest workable in-home start across these communities is roughly 18:30. Online sessions run to 21:00 and can be 45 minutes, which fits the actual shape of a Dubailand school night far better.

The practical conclusion for all four communities is the same, which is why the comparison is worth publishing rather than writing four different answers. Choose the tutor on the course and the component. Schedule around the drive. Treat the Exploration as a dated project rather than an eventual one.

sections.heading: What mathematics tutoring costs here, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because that is where a first search lands. Tutopiya publishes online tuition from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. For a Year 8 student consolidating arithmetic that may be entirely sufficient. For a DP2 student on AA Higher Level it is not, because the person teaching at that rate will not usually have taught Paper 3 or marked an Exploration against criterion E, and those are the two things the money is supposed to buy.

The specialist bands run higher. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table places qualified online subject tutors at AED 150-300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 or above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, and independent home tutors up to AED 500 with travel included. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work and BartyED AED 650 at the premium end. All of these are each provider's own published figure, read in October 2026.

For mathematics specifically there is a structural argument for spending less per hour and more often. Fluency on Paper 1 is built by frequency: twenty manipulations a day for six weeks beats one long session a week at any price. A sensible mathematics plan is therefore often a single weekly specialist hour to diagnose and set work, with the daily volume done by the student unpaid. A plan that is four expensive hours a week and no daily work is usually the wrong shape, whatever it costs.

On monthly numbers, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour come to roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate here because level, component and urgency move it; the free diagnostic lesson comes before any quote.

sections.heading: HL Paper 3, the component nobody practises
paragraphs: HL Paper 3 on both AA and AI is one hour, two questions, and 20% of the grade. It is an extended investigation rather than a set of topic questions: the paper leads a student through unfamiliar mathematics in scaffolded parts, where each part depends on the one before. Nothing in a textbook chapter looks like it, and school mock papers in Dubai do not always include one, which means a substantial number of students sit their first Paper 3 in the examination hall.

The skills it rewards are specific. Reading the whole question before starting, because the later parts reveal what the earlier notation is for. Following the scaffold rather than jumping to a general result. Writing down what has been established at each stage so the next part can use it. Accepting unfamiliar definitions and working with them rather than trying to translate them into something known. Students who are strong on Papers 1 and 2 and weak on Paper 3 are almost never short of content; they are short of this particular reading discipline.

It is also the cheapest component to improve, because the fix is practice on past Paper 3 questions with the mark scheme read afterwards. Four to six sessions will normally change the score materially, and the work transfers nowhere else in the course, which is precisely why it gets skipped in a general revision programme that is trying to cover everything.

A note on materials: past Paper 3 questions and their mark schemes are IB copyright. We work through them on screen in session and point to the official source. We do not distribute scanned papers or mark schemes, and a tutor who offers to send you a folder of them is creating a copyright problem rather than adding value.

sections.heading: The term, the calendar and when mathematics work should happen
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject where timing matters most, because fluency decays and the Exploration has a hard internal deadline. Working the year backwards is the only sensible planning order. For a Diploma student the fixed points are the school's Exploration deadlines, the school's mock window, and the external session. UAE candidates sit the May session; this page publishes no IB examination or results date because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unconfirmed date is worse than none. Your Diploma coordinator has the real calendar.

For students on the British route before the Diploma, the awarding bodies' published positions are concrete and worth knowing. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, plus Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so it is not available to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

One administrative rule applies to every Cambridge candidate in Dubai. Centres are allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Get the zone from the examinations officer before printing anything.

Practically, the mathematics year for a Diploma student looks like this: fluency work in the long holiday and the first term of DP1, Exploration topic agreed in DP1 with drafting through the year, Paper 3 practice from the start of DP2, and timed full papers from the mock window onwards. Starting the Exploration in the term it is due is the single most common planning error in this subject.

sections.heading: Getting a mathematics specialist, and the regulator footnotes
paragraphs: Send four things: the course, AA or AI; the level; which component is losing marks; and a marked script. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson and sends a written note within a working day naming the error patterns and estimating sessions. You read it before anything is charged. Where the problem is the AA or AI decision rather than a grade, the diagnostic uses real questions from both courses so the evidence is concrete.

Availability for mathematics is the best in the subject list. Both courses at both levels have deep cover for UAE evening slots, and a match normally takes one to three working days. The exception is a narrow combination at short notice — HL Paper 3 coaching requested a fortnight before the session, for instance — where the slot rather than the specialist is the constraint. If no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

Two regulator footnotes, because they belong on every page in this set rather than in terms nobody opens. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, no amount is quoted here.

And the claim nobody should make. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, issued to training institutes, with annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, occupies no UAE office or centre, and claims no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB. We explain what those bodies do; none of them endorses us.

process.title: Name the course and the level
process.description: AA and AI are different courses and HL and SL are different papers, so 'IB maths' is four possible answers. Give the course, the level and the component that is weak. If the real question is whether the course itself is wrong, say that instead and the diagnostic is built around it.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent on the student's own errors. For a fluency problem that means a short non-calculator set. For an Exploration problem it means reading the topic and the draft against the criteria. For a course-fit question it means questions from both AA and AI, marked.

process.title: Written diagnosis and the right plan shape
process.description: Within a working day, a note naming the error patterns and proposing a plan with the correct shape. Fluency needs daily volume and one weekly session; a component block needs six to ten sessions; an Exploration needs four to six spread across the drafting period. These are not interchangeable.

process.title: Weekly slot plus the work between sessions
process.description: Same tutor, same time, 45 or 60 minutes, scheduled after the drive home from school. For mathematics the work set between sessions matters as much as the session, and the written diagnosis says exactly what the daily volume should be and how it will be marked.

process.title: Reviewed on the school's own marks
process.description: Progress is judged on the next internal assessment or mock, read against the original diagnosis. If a Paper 1 score has not moved after six weeks of fluency work, the cause is usually that the daily work is not happening, and that is a more useful conversation than adding another paid hour.

whyPoints.title: The course decision treated as the first question
whyPoints.description: AA and AI suit different students and different degrees, and the mismatch is the most expensive problem in IB mathematics. We diagnose it with real questions from both courses and give you something markable to take to the Diploma coordinator rather than an opinion.

whyPoints.title: Exploration work against the published criteria
whyPoints.description: Twenty marks across five criteria, 20% of the grade, and most of the loss is in communication, reflection and a topic pitched below the level of the course. We test the topic before any writing starts, which is the point at which the ceiling is actually set.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 given its own block
whyPoints.description: HL Paper 3 is 20% of the grade, is unlike anything in the textbook, and is often missing from school mock papers. Four to six focused sessions on scaffolded investigation questions usually shifts it, and nothing in a general revision programme does the same job.

whyPoints.title: Plans shaped for how fluency is built
whyPoints.description: Non-calculator fluency responds to frequency rather than to duration, so the right plan is often one specialist hour a week plus daily unpaid volume. We will tell you that rather than sell four hours a week, because the four hours would not work as well.

whyPoints.title: One answer for the whole Dubailand belt
whyPoints.description: The Triangle, Sports City, Motor City and the Ranches cluster get the same mathematical answer because the syllabus does not change between them. What changes is the commute, and that is a scheduling question rather than a teaching one.

faqs.question: Does an IB maths tutor come to the house in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Not from us. Home visits exist across Dubai from independent tutors and agencies at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, rising to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included, but IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and runs home visits only in India. For mathematics the trade is clearly favourable: Paper 3 and Exploration experience are rare enough that choosing a tutor by driving distance from the Triangle is likely to cost more in match quality than it saves in convenience.

faqs.question: My child picked Maths AI and the degree needs AA. Can that be fixed?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window is early. A move between courses is usually possible in the first term of DP1 and gets progressively harder after that, and the school decides rather than the family. What helps is evidence: a few sessions of real AA questions, marked, showing the student can handle non-calculator algebra, so the conversation with the Diploma coordinator rests on something concrete. If the move is not possible, check whether the target universities accept AI with an additional qualification, because a small number do and the alternative is a changed destination.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 so much harder than my child's class work suggests?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 on both Analysis and Approaches routes is sat without a calculator, and most students learn mathematics with a graphing display calculator in their hand. A student who can differentiate perfectly on a screen may be unable to sketch a cubic from its factorised form, work with surds exactly, or complete the square unprompted. That is a fluency gap rather than an understanding gap, and it responds to short daily practice far better than to long weekly sessions. Six to eight weeks of about twenty manipulations a day typically changes the score.

faqs.question: How are marks distributed across the Exploration criteria?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks in total across five criteria. Presentation carries 4, mathematical communication 4, personal engagement 3, reflection 3, and use of mathematics 6. The whole Exploration is worth 20% of the final grade at both SL and HL on both courses. The pattern of loss is consistent: communication marks go to calculator syntax used as mathematical notation, reflection marks go to students describing what they did rather than evaluating it, and use-of-mathematics marks are capped when the topic's mathematics sits below the level of the course.

faqs.question: What makes a good Exploration topic for an HL student?
faqs.answer: One whose mathematics genuinely sits at Higher Level and whose data or model the student can obtain honestly. A Higher Level Exploration built on simple linear regression has capped the use-of-mathematics criterion before a word is written, and that criterion carries 6 of the 20 marks. Equally, a topic requiring mathematics well beyond the course produces work the student cannot explain, which costs reflection and communication too. The test is whether the student can talk through every step unaided. Topic selection is where a tutor adds the most legitimate value.

faqs.question: Is HL Paper 3 worth preparing for separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is frequently the best-value block in the course. Paper 3 is one hour, two questions and 20% of the Higher Level grade, structured as a scaffolded investigation into unfamiliar mathematics rather than as topic questions. School mock papers in Dubai do not always include one, so some students meet the format first in the examination. The skills are specific — read the whole question first, follow the scaffold, record what each part establishes — and four to six sessions of past questions with the mark schemes read afterwards usually moves the score.

faqs.question: Is the answer different in Motor City or Dubai Sports City?
faqs.answer: Not mathematically. The two courses, the no-calculator Paper 1, the Exploration criteria and HL Paper 3 are identical whichever side of Al Khail Road you live on. What differs is the commute and therefore the session time: from the Triangle and Sports City about 17:30 is realistic, from Motor City closer to 18:00 and from DAMAC Hills nearer 18:30, because no Diploma school sits inside any of those communities. That single variable is also why in-home visits sit awkwardly across this belt, since the latest workable in-home start is around 18:30.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a DP2 maths student actually have?
faqs.answer: Usually one paid specialist hour plus daily unpaid work, not four paid hours. Fluency is built by frequency: twenty short manipulations a day for six weeks beats one long weekly session at any price, and the specialist hour is best spent diagnosing, setting the right volume and marking it. Where a component block is running — HL Paper 3, or Exploration feedback — a second weekly session for a fixed number of weeks makes sense. A plan with many paid hours and no work between them is the wrong shape regardless of the hourly rate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Exploration without breaching IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may interrogate the topic until the mathematics is at the right level, check the data can be obtained honestly, explain what each criterion credits using the published descriptors, teach correct notation as a skill, and read a draft the student wrote and say which criterion a passage fails. A tutor may not choose the topic, write or rewrite any part of the report, restructure it by rewriting, or produce the mathematics. The test after every session is whether every word that will be submitted is still the student's own.

faqs.question: Which Dubai schools near JVT actually teach IB Mathematics?
faqs.answer: None inside the Triangle. Sunmarke School and Arcadia Global School are British curriculum, so IB mathematics students from JVT commute. The nearest Diploma cohorts are at JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, North London Collegiate School Dubai, Greenfield International School and Emirates International School Meadows. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them IB-curriculum, creating 16,846 places. We name schools as market context and claim no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: My child comes from MYP rather than IGCSE. Does that change the maths plan?
faqs.answer: It usually changes the starting point. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria — Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts — and rewards reasoning and presentation rather than drilled manipulation. Students arriving from MYP into Analysis and Approaches therefore often reason well and manipulate slowly, which Paper 1 punishes directly. Eight to twelve sessions on indices, surds, rearrangement, factorising and function notation before DP1 begins is the standard fix, and it is considerably harder once DP1 assessments have started.

faqs.question: Can we get past Paper 3 papers and mark schemes from you?
faqs.answer: We teach from them on screen and link the official source so you can obtain them legitimately, but we do not distribute copies. IB past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are copyright, and a tutor sending over a folder of scanned marking material is creating a copyright problem rather than adding value — and for unreleased material, something more serious than that. What a session does is work a real question through live, show precisely what the published scheme credits at each stage, and leave the student with notes they wrote themselves.

faqs.question: Why are there no IB exam dates on this page?
faqs.answer: Because none of them could be verified at source. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, and an examination date is something a family rearranges a term around, so an unconfirmed figure would be worse than none. UAE candidates sit the May session; for the window, the results date and the candidate release time, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly. For mathematics the deadlines that bite first are internal anyway — the school's Exploration dates, which fall far earlier in DP1 than most families expect.

faqs.question: How quickly can you start, and can sessions move for Ramadan?
faqs.answer: One to three working days for either mathematics course at either level, which is the deepest cover in our subject list. The constraint at short notice is usually the slot rather than the specialist. During Ramadan sessions shift to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time and often shortened to 45 minutes, which suits fluency work well because short and frequent is the right shape anyway. Through a school's mock week most families pause, then restart with a session spent reading the marked scripts rather than teaching new content.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-village.closingHeading: Course first, fluency second, Exploration on a date
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-jumeirah-village.closingBody: Three things decide an IB Mathematics grade for a student in Jumeirah Village Triangle, and none of them is which tutor lives nearest. Whether the course is the right one, which should be settled against the degree prerequisite and real marked evidence rather than a preference. Whether non-calculator fluency is good enough for Paper 1, which short daily practice fixes and long weekly sessions do not. And whether the Exploration has a date in the calendar rather than a vague intention, because twenty marks across five criteria is 20% of the grade and the topic sets the ceiling. Send the course, the level and a marked script, and take the free diagnostic lesson.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-karama.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels. Each works from the live subject guide, marks to the published criteria, and reports back in the language your child's school uses on its own reports.

intro.heading: Two maths courses, four routes, one grade that matters
paragraphs: A parent in Karama searching for an IB maths tutor is rarely searching for geography. The flats off Kuwait Street and Zabeel Road sit minutes from The Indian High School in Oud Metha and a short drive from St Mary's Catholic High School and Dubai Gem Private School. Distance is not the problem. The problem is that "IB maths" is not one subject. It is two separate courses, each taught at two levels, with different syllabus content, different papers, different calculator rules and different university consequences. A tutor who has taught one of the four well may be no use at all on another.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route. It leans on proof, calculus, trigonometric identities and the kind of manipulation a mathematics or engineering degree assumes. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling route: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, graph theory at Higher Level, and a far heavier reliance on the graphic display calculator throughout. Both are respectable. Both lead to good universities. They do not lead to the same ones, and a student who picked the wrong one in the first term of DP1 usually discovers it halfway through DP1 when the topic they cannot do turns out to be the topic the course is built on.

So the first job of a maths tutor working with a Karama family is diagnosis, not teaching. Which course is the school actually entered the student for? Which level? What did the last internal assessment look like, question by question? Where did the marks go: setting up, executing, or communicating? A student who loses marks on setting up needs topic teaching. A student who loses them on execution needs timed drilling. A student who loses them on communication needs to be taught what the mark scheme rewards, which is a different lesson entirely and the one most often skipped.

The second job is the Internal Assessment. The mathematical exploration carries twenty per cent of the final grade in every one of the four courses, it is marked against five criteria by letter, and it is the single component where a student can gain or lose a whole grade without ever sitting a paper. It is also the component where the boundary between teaching and malpractice matters most. A tutor may teach the statistics a student has chosen to use, challenge the aim, question whether the data supports the conclusion and point at a criterion the draft is not meeting. A tutor may not write it, restructure it into their own prose, or supply a topic the student then adopts wholesale.

The third job is the calculator. Both courses allow a graphic display calculator in two of the three papers, and the GDC is a mark-earning tool rather than a convenience. A student who can find a numerical solution in six keystrokes and write down the command used will bank marks a student doing it algebraically will lose to arithmetic slips. This is teachable in a handful of sessions and almost never taught properly in a class of twenty-four.

Everything below is the content of that work: the route comparison, the paper weightings, the specific places marks disappear in each topic, the IA criteria by letter, and what the Dubai market charges for all of it. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-karama.programmesIntro: Karama and the surrounding streets feed schools running the full IB continuum as well as British-curriculum schools that offer the Diploma at sixteen. These are the programme stages a maths tutor works across, and what each one actually demands.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses at two levels. Analysis and Approaches covers number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, with proof and rigour emphasised at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation covers the same five topic areas with the weight shifted towards statistics, modelling and, at Higher Level, graph theory and matrices. Both are assessed by two papers at SL and three at HL, plus the mathematical exploration.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools do not all offer all four routes. Several run AA and AI at Standard Level but only AA at Higher, which means a student wanting AI HL may need to negotiate or change school. Before booking tutoring, check the course code on the school's option block rather than assuming; families in the Karama and Oud Metha belt regularly arrive with the wrong one written on a report.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria, each marked out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Extended and standard mathematics diverge in MYP 4 and 5. The investigating-patterns criterion is the one that most closely resembles DP exploration work, and the students who handle the DP IA calmly are usually the ones who were taught to generalise a pattern properly at MYP 4.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP 5 report of 5 in mathematics is not a comfortable platform for AA HL, whatever the student's confidence. The gap is largest in algebraic fluency, because MYP rewards process and explanation while DP Paper 1 rewards accurate manipulation under time pressure with no calculator. Six weeks of targeted algebra over the summer closes most of it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics, as the route in
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools near Karama run Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 to sixteen, then offer the Diploma or A Level. For a student heading into DP maths, the IGCSE Extended or Higher-tier content is the assumed baseline: surds, indices, quadratics, simultaneous equations, trigonometry in two and three dimensions, and the basic calculus some boards include. Gaps here surface in DP1 within weeks.
programmes.countryNote: A grade 7 at IGCSE Extended is roughly the floor for AA HL in most Dubai schools' own guidance, and a 6 is workable for AA SL or AI HL. Schools vary, so ask the head of mathematics for the school's published entry guidance rather than relying on a national rule of thumb.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme numeracy
programmes.description: Inquiry-led numeracy with no external examination. Tutoring here is about number sense, times-table automaticity and written methods, because a child who cannot recall multiplication facts fluently will be slowed in every later topic that uses them. The useful measure at this stage is speed and accuracy on mental arithmetic, not whether the child enjoys the unit of inquiry.
programmes.countryNote: Karama households often have children at different schools and on different curricula at once — one in a PYP school, one at an Indian-board school, one in a British-curriculum Year 9. Scheduling one tutor across all three rarely works; matching each child to a specialist and staggering the slots across the week does.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-karama.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the page, but families here usually ask about the subjects that sit alongside it in a DP option block. These are the courses our IB specialists cover, with the parts that actually decide the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route. At HL the calculus extends to implicit differentiation, related rates, differential equations and Maclaurin series, and Paper 3 asks for extended problem-solving over two long questions. Marks go missing in proof writing and in unjustified steps that the mark scheme will not award without the reasoning shown.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route. Heavy on statistics, regression, hypothesis testing and financial mathematics, with graph theory, matrices and complex numbers added at HL. Students who find AA algebra punishing often thrive here, but AI HL statistics is genuinely demanding and the calculator work must be reported precisely.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most common companion to AA HL in Karama option blocks. Mechanics and electricity reward the same algebraic fluency as AA, so a student weak in rearrangement loses marks twice. Paper 1 is multiple choice, Paper 2 is structured and extended response, and the data booklet must be navigated at speed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Stoichiometry, energetics, equilibrium and organic chemistry at both levels, with the HL extension adding depth to each. Calculation marks are usually the recoverable ones; students lose them to significant figures, unit conversion and failing to state the state symbols the mark scheme expects.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than essay style. Labelled axes, correctly shifted curves and a stated direction of change earn the marks; a well-written paragraph around a wrong diagram does not. HL adds quantitative questions that reward the same arithmetic discipline a maths tutor drills.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The quantitative tools — break-even, investment appraisal, ratio analysis — are where maths-confident students pick up easy marks and maths-anxious ones give them away. The HL extension and the pre-released case study both reward structured calculation with a stated conclusion.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, data structures and algorithmic thinking. Students who can trace a loop on paper do well; those who only code by trial and error struggle with Paper 1. The internal assessment is a developed solution, which needs project discipline more than programming flair.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis under time pressure, which rewards a repeatable reading method rather than wide reading. The individual oral and the HL essay both need a defensible line of argument stated in the first minute, and both are coachable without any writing being done for the student.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The exhibition and the prescribed-title essay. Maths students often find TOK the hardest core element because it rewards exactly the opposite habit: holding two defensible positions open rather than closing on one answer. Coaching is about structuring a claim and a counterclaim, not supplying content.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words on a question the student chooses, supervised by a teacher at their own school. A mathematics EE is unforgiving because a vague question cannot be rescued by good prose. Tutoring here is question-shaping, method checking and feedback against the published criteria — the supervision itself stays with the school.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-karama.regionsTitle: Where our Karama students actually live
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-karama.regionsIntro: Karama is a dense, mid-rise residential grid in old Dubai, bounded by Zabeel, Oud Metha and Bur Dubai. Families come to us from across that belt, and the practical detail differs street by street more than the marketing in this market usually admits.

regions.name: Al Karama
regions.note: Apartment living, short walking distances, and a school-run radius measured in minutes rather than motorway junctions. The constraint on tutoring here is quiet study space inside the flat, not travel time.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: The school belt itself: The Indian High School, Dubai Gem, St Mary's and Pakistan Education Academy within a short radius. Day ends early enough that a 3:30pm or 4pm session is genuinely available here, which is rare in Dubai.

regions.note: Mixed apartment blocks with a strong Indian and Pakistani-board presence alongside British-curriculum families. Requests cluster around IGCSE mathematics and the transition into DP1.

regions.note: Older buildings, large households and frequent multi-child bookings. The usual request is two children at different stages, which works better as two short staggered sessions than one long shared one.

This is the format that fixes algebraic fluency, because fluency comes from spaced repetition rather than from intensive blocks. The tutor marks the school's own assessments alongside past-paper questions and reports which of the three mark-scheme stages is costing the marks.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: how the choice is actually made
paragraphs: A student should choose Analysis and Approaches if they intend to apply for mathematics, engineering, physics, computer science or economics at a university that lists a mathematics prerequisite, and Applications and Interpretation if their degree plans sit in business, social science, design, medicine-adjacent fields or the humanities. That is the short answer, and it is right most of the time. The longer answer is that the two courses reward different aptitudes, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years fighting the course instead of learning the subject.

Analysis and Approaches is built on algebraic manipulation and proof. A student who enjoys rearranging, who finds satisfaction in a clean derivation and who can hold a symbolic argument in their head without a calculator will do well. At Higher Level the calculus goes a long way: implicit differentiation, related rates, separable differential equations, Maclaurin series. Paper 1 is sat with no calculator at all, which means every arithmetic slip is unprotected. Students who scraped through IGCSE algebra by substituting numbers until something worked tend to find AA HL immediately punishing.

Applications and Interpretation looks easier from outside and is not. The statistics content at Higher Level — regression, chi-squared, hypothesis testing, Markov chains, graph theory — is substantial, and the calculator is assumed throughout rather than occasionally. The communication demand is higher than students expect: a correct numerical answer with no statement of the command used or the model assumed loses marks. The students who flourish in AI are the ones who like context, data and interpretation, and who are willing to write about numbers rather than only compute them.

The practical check for a Karama family is narrower than any of this. Ask the school which routes it is actually running this year, ask the head of mathematics what the entry guidance is from the student's current attainment, and then ask the student to attempt one past Paper 1 question from AA SL and one data-analysis question from AI SL. The answer is usually visible in twenty minutes, and it is more reliable than a preference stated in September.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings, and what each one is actually testing
paragraphs: A DP mathematics grade is built from a small number of components, and knowing their weights changes how revision time should be spent. At Standard Level the student sits two papers and submits the exploration. At Higher Level there is a third paper. The exploration is twenty per cent of the final grade in every route and at both levels, which makes it the largest single component a student has direct, unhurried control over.

Paper 1 is taken without a calculator. This is the component students neglect, because most of their classwork and almost all of their homework is done with a calculator to hand. The consequence is predictable: a student who can do the mathematics loses marks to arithmetic, to sign errors, to forgetting an exact value for a trigonometric ratio, or to spending four minutes on a computation that should have taken forty seconds. The fix is mechanical and it works — short, frequent, calculator-free sets from the first week of DP1, not from February of DP2.

Paper 2 allows the graphic display calculator and is designed around it. Here the marks are lost in the opposite direction: students compute correctly and then fail to communicate. A solution that gives a number without naming the function solved, the window used or the model assumed will be marked down even when the number is right. This is a twenty-minute lesson that is worth several marks a paper, and it is almost never taught because it feels like a formality rather than mathematics.

Paper 3, at Higher Level only, is two long questions that build. The early parts are accessible, the later parts depend on having understood what the earlier parts were establishing, and the whole thing rewards a student who will write something down before they can see the destination. Students who freeze on unfamiliar problems do badly on Paper 3 regardless of topic knowledge, and the remedy is exposure rather than revision: a steady diet of problems with no stated topic, attempted under time, discussed afterwards.

sections.heading: Topic by topic: where Karama students lose marks in IB mathematics
paragraphs: Diagnosis by topic is more useful than diagnosis by grade. A student at a 4 and a student at a 6 may be losing marks in entirely different places, and a tutor who starts by reteaching from the beginning wastes the hours that matter. The pattern across students arriving from IGCSE into DP1 in this belt is consistent enough to name.

Algebraic fluency is the first and biggest. Partial fractions, rearranging a formula where the subject appears twice, simplifying a rational expression, index laws with negative and fractional powers: these are IGCSE skills, they are assumed rather than taught in DP, and a student who is slow at them is slow at everything built on them. The second is trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles. Radians, the unit circle, identities, and solving equations over a stated interval rather than finding one answer. Students who learned SOHCAHTOA and stopped tend to lose a whole cluster of marks here.

Calculus is where the grade is usually decided at Higher Level, and the failure is rarely differentiation itself. It is knowing which technique a question wants, applying the chain rule inside a product, handling a definite integral that needs substitution, and interpreting the result in context when the question asks what the answer means. Statistics, in both routes but especially AI, fails on interpretation rather than calculation: a correct correlation coefficient followed by a sentence that overclaims causation loses the mark the sentence was there to earn.

The last category is not a topic. It is exam behaviour: starting with question one and running out of time, writing nothing when a question looks unfamiliar, rounding at every intermediate step, or giving an answer to two significant figures because that is what the calculator showed. Each of these is worth marks, each is fixable in a handful of sessions, and none of them requires any new mathematics to be learned.
