sections.heading: The mathematical exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, and a hard boundary
paragraphs: The exploration is a piece of independent mathematical writing, usually between twelve and twenty pages, in which the student investigates a question of their own choosing. It is marked internally by the school and moderated by the IB against five criteria identified by letter, and it carries twenty per cent of the final grade. A student who writes a competent exploration and a student who writes a thin one are separated by something closer to a grade boundary than most families expect.

The commonest failure is a weak aim. A student who writes "I will investigate the mathematics of basketball" has not posed a question, and no amount of good work afterwards fully recovers the criterion marks lost at the top. A student who writes "I will model the trajectory of a free throw to find the release angle that maximises the margin for error in release speed" has given themselves a structure, a method and a conclusion to reach. Getting the aim right is perhaps two sessions of work and it is the highest-leverage help a tutor can give.

The second commonest failure is mathematics below the level of the course. An AA HL exploration built on linear regression and a few means will lose marks for sophistication however neatly it is presented. The level has to match the course, which is not the same as being as hard as possible; an elegant use of a technique from the syllabus beats an undigested import from a university textbook, and the undigested import usually also fails the personal-engagement and reflection criteria.

The boundary matters. A tutor may teach the mathematics the student has chosen, question the aim, check whether the data supports the conclusion, point out that a criterion is unmet and explain what the criterion asks for. A tutor may not supply the topic, write any part of the document, rewrite the student's prose, or produce the analysis the student then presents. IB Gram tutors give feedback on the student's own work and nothing else. The school's supervisor remains the supervisor of record, and the authenticity declaration remains the student's.

sections.heading: Calculator discipline: the few marks a parent can see being left behind
paragraphs: The graphic display calculator is part of the assessment, not an aid to it. Two of the three Higher Level papers assume it, and the Standard Level Paper 2 is written on the expectation that a student will solve numerically rather than algebraically wherever that is faster. A student who does not know the machine well is slower on every question that involves one, and slower means marks lost at the end of the paper rather than in the middle.

The skills are specific and short to teach. Solving an equation numerically and reporting it to the required accuracy. Finding the intersection of two curves. Locating a maximum or a minimum and reading off both coordinates. Getting a definite integral without antidifferentiating. Running a regression, reading the coefficient, and knowing which of the regression outputs the question asked for. Storing a value rather than retyping a rounded version of it. None of these is difficult; all of them are routinely absent in students who have used the calculator only for arithmetic.

The reporting half matters as much as the operating half. A mark scheme will award a method mark for a stated approach even when the final number is wrong, and will withhold it when a correct number appears with no indication of how. Writing "solving 3 sin x = x on [0, 2π] with the GDC gives x = 2.279" earns more than writing "x = 2.279". Students resist this because it feels like padding. It is not padding; it is the only evidence the examiner has.

There is a second, duller discipline alongside it: rounding. Carry full precision through intermediate steps, round only at the end, and round to three significant figures unless the question says otherwise. A student who rounds early and then rounds again accumulates error and loses accuracy marks on questions they understood completely. Across a full paper this is worth more than any single topic a tutor could reteach.

sections.heading: What IB mathematics tutoring costs around Karama, and what the lower band buys
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most Karama families start. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students or by platform tutors working at volume, is advertised in Dubai from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik publishes rates from AED 45 to AED 65, and Tutopiya's panel quotes from AED 33 to AED 52. At that price a tutor can supervise homework, keep a student working and explain a method that has already been taught once. What the lower band does not reliably buy is someone who knows which of the four IB mathematics routes your child is on, or what the exploration criteria require.

The next band up is where IB-specific work actually sits. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table giving AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards. At the premium end, named or examiner-level tutors are advertised as high as AED 650 by BartyED. These are the market's published figures, not IB Gram's price list.

In-home visits are a separate band because the travel is priced in. Bestimate puts one-to-one home tutoring at AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to AED 500. Monthly packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work.

What a parent can verify for themselves is more useful than any of these numbers. Ask for the tutor's own IB mathematics teaching history, by route and level. Ask them to mark one of your child's existing scripts before you book anything, and read what they say about where the marks went. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tutor who can name the five exploration criteria by letter without looking them up is worth more at AED 250 than one who cannot at AED 120. For IB Gram's own arrangements, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation rather than a rate card.

sections.heading: An in-home maths tutor in a Karama flat against one-to-one online
paragraphs: Karama is one of the few parts of Dubai where the usual argument against in-home tutoring — the drive — barely applies. The schools are close, the streets are walkable, and a tutor living in Bur Dubai or Al Mankhool could reach a Karama flat in ten minutes. So the honest version of this comparison does not rest on travel time. It rests on the size of the pool you are choosing from, and on what a flat is like during the hours a session would run.

The pool is the real difference. A Karama family hiring someone who can physically attend is choosing from the tutors who live within a short drive and are free at the hour your child is free. For IGCSE mathematics that pool is large. For AA HL Paper 3 preparation, or for an AI HL exploration using Markov chains, it narrows to a handful of people, and the chance that one of them lives nearby and is free at 5pm on a Tuesday is small. Online removes the geography from that calculation entirely: the constraint becomes the tutor's diary rather than their postcode.

The flat is the second difference, and it cuts both ways. Karama apartments are busy, shared and often crowded in the early evening. An in-home tutor needs a table, a chair and a quiet hour, which in some households means displacing everyone else from the only usable room. An online session needs a laptop, headphones and a corner, and it can run at 3:45pm when the flat is empty rather than at 7pm when it is not. For a family with three children, the online version is also the only one that can realistically be staggered.

There is one genuine advantage to a person in the room, and it is worth stating: a younger or easily distracted student is harder to keep on task over video. For a DP mathematics student it rarely decides anything. For a Year 7 who will not sit still, it can. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE — home tutoring is a service we provide only in India — so where a family's child genuinely needs someone physically present, we will say so rather than sell an online session as a substitute.

sections.heading: KHDA, the school report, and what an inspection band does not tell you about maths
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which, on the UAE government's own description, is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA inspects annually and publishes a band from Outstanding down to Very Weak. In 2024-25 the Dubai private sector held 387,441 students across 227 schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7.

An inspection band is a whole-school judgement, and it is a poor proxy for the quality of one department in one year. A school rated Very Good may have an outstanding mathematics department and a weak one in sciences, or the reverse, and the one teacher who carried DP mathematics may have left in August. Parents in the Karama and Oud Metha belt sometimes choose or reject a school on the band alone. The more useful questions are narrower: how many students sat each mathematics route last year, which routes the school actually offers at Higher Level, and whether DP mathematics is taught by the same teacher across both years.

The school report is a better instrument than the inspection report, provided it is read properly. A predicted grade is a judgement, not a measurement, and it is usually built from internal assessments that were not sat under examination conditions. Ask for the raw marks on the last internal paper and the mark scheme alongside it. A 5 built from steady part-marks across every question is a different problem from a 5 built from three strong questions and two blanks, and the two need opposite responses.

Separately, every Dubai private school teaches the UAE mandatory subjects alongside its licensed curriculum. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all private schools regardless of curriculum, organised in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. This matters to a mathematics tutoring plan only in that it occupies timetable space: the week your child's school actually has free is smaller than the curriculum brochure implies.

sections.heading: Permits, honesty and what we will not do
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anybody.

A permit is a legal status, not a teaching qualification, and it is also not an endorsement. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and any tutoring service in this market that tells you otherwise is describing something it does not hold. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; we do not operate premises in the UAE and do not claim it. What we can tell you is which route and level a tutor has taught, and for how long.

On academic honesty the line is not negotiable and it is worth having in writing before you pay anyone. An IB Gram tutor will teach the mathematics, interrogate an exploration aim, check a method, mark a draft against the criteria and tell a student plainly when a section does not meet one. An IB Gram tutor will not write an exploration, an Extended Essay or a TOK essay, will not rewrite a student's prose into their own, and will not supply analysis the student then submits. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student, not on the tutor, and in the IB it can end a Diploma.

We also will not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those materials belong to the boards. A tutor will reference them, teach from them in a session and point you at the official source; a service that emails you a folder of them is handing you someone else's copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Nor will anyone here predict a grade. A specialist can tell you where the marks are currently going and what the realistic ceiling looks like from here; nobody can promise a 7.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent assessment with the marks on it is worth more than a paragraph of description. Our specialist reads it before the trial lesson and comes with a view on which of the three stages — setting up, executing, communicating — is actually costing the marks.

process.title: Free trial lesson, no card needed
process.description: One full session with the matched specialist, booked at a time that fits the school day, at no charge and with no payment details taken beforehand. You get a written note afterwards naming what the tutor found and what the first six weeks would target.

process.title: Agree the plan and the slot
process.description: Weekly through-course work, an exploration block, or a pre-session intensive. We confirm the cadence, the slot in Gulf Standard Time and what gets set between sessions, so the week is settled before any money changes hands.

process.title: Review against marks, not impressions
process.description: At six weeks we compare marks on comparable work rather than asking whether the sessions feel better. If the plan is not moving the marks, we change the plan or the tutor. If a specialism is not available, we say so rather than substituting someone who nearly fits.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course code, not to "IB maths"
whyPoints.description: AA HL and AI SL are different jobs. We match on the route and level your child is actually entered for, and a tutor who has taught the other one is not offered as a near-enough fit. This is the single most common mismatch in this market.

whyPoints.title: Mark-scheme literacy as a taught skill
whyPoints.description: A large share of recoverable marks sit in how an answer is written rather than whether it is right. Our tutors mark a student's own scripts line by line against the published scheme and teach what the examiner is permitted to award.

whyPoints.title: Calculator work treated as content
whyPoints.description: Six GDC commands, the habit of stating which one was used, and full precision carried through intermediate steps. Short to teach, rarely taught, and worth marks on every calculator paper your child sits.

whyPoints.title: Exploration coaching with the boundary stated
whyPoints.description: We help with the aim, the level of the mathematics and criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own draft. We do not write it, rewrite it or supply the analysis, and we put that in writing to parents before the block starts.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a scarce combination at the hour you need, we tell you instead of filling the slot. Published rates and availability in this market are often vaguer than they look, and a near-enough tutor costs a term.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Every session runs live over video, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India, and we would rather say that here than at the point of booking.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course is my child in, and how do I check from a Karama school report?
faqs.answer: Look for the full course title rather than the word maths. Reports and option blocks should say Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, followed by HL or SL. If the report only says Mathematics, ask the head of mathematics directly; the two courses have different syllabuses and a tutor matched to the wrong one wastes the term. Some schools near Oud Metha offer both routes at Standard Level but only Analysis and Approaches at Higher, so the available choice is narrower than the IB's full menu. Confirm the route before you book anything, including a free trial.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches harder than Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: They are hard in different directions. Analysis and Approaches HL is algebraically demanding: implicit differentiation, differential equations, Maclaurin series and proof, with a calculator-free Paper 1 that punishes arithmetic slips. Applications and Interpretation HL carries heavy statistics, graph theory, matrices and Markov chains, and expects the calculator throughout plus careful reporting of what was computed. Students who enjoy symbolic manipulation find Analysis more natural; students who prefer data and context find Applications more natural. Neither is a soft option, and a student placed by preference rather than by aptitude usually struggles whichever way the choice went.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP1 student in Karama usually need?
faqs.answer: One session a week is the normal starting point for a student who is coping with the course but losing marks in specific places. Two becomes sensible where the student is behind on the Higher Level extension content, where two subjects need support at once, or in the months before the May session. More than two a week rarely helps during term because the limiting factor is the work done between sessions, not the contact hours. We would rather start at one, see six weeks of marked work and increase if the marks say so than sell a heavier plan up front.

faqs.question: Where exactly does exploration coaching stop being allowed under IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can interrogate the aim, teach the mathematics the student has chosen to use, check whether the level of sophistication matches the course, mark a draft against criteria A to E and explain why a criterion is unmet. A tutor cannot supply the topic, write any section, rewrite the student's prose or produce the analysis. The supervisor at your child's school remains the supervisor and the authenticity declaration remains your child's. Any service offering to produce an exploration is offering malpractice, and the consequences land on the student, not on the service.

faqs.question: What does the exploration actually count for in the final maths grade?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four routes and at both levels. That makes it the largest single component a student controls without a clock running. It is marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the most marks. Confirm the current criterion weightings against your school's own copy of the subject guide each year, because the IB revises guides on a cycle. The practical point for a parent is that a weak exploration can cost a grade that no amount of examination performance comfortably recovers.

faqs.question: The working looks right but the marks are not there. Which of the three causes is it?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and they need opposite responses. Communication: the answer is right but the method is not shown in a form the mark scheme can award, which is fixed by marking the student's own scripts against the published scheme. Speed: the work is correct but unfinished, which is fixed by timed calculator-free practice and by question triage. Rounding: accuracy marks lost to early rounding, which is fixed by carrying full precision and rounding once at the end. A single diagnostic paper marked properly will usually show which of the three it is within one session.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 cause so much trouble if it covers the same syllabus?
faqs.answer: Because it is sat without a calculator and most students have practised almost everything with one. Exact trigonometric values, surd manipulation, index laws, mental arithmetic under pressure and sign discipline all become load-bearing, and a student who leaned on the calculator for two years is slow at all of them. The fix is mechanical: short calculator-free sets several times a week, started in DP1 rather than in the final term. It is the cheapest grade improvement available in IB mathematics and it requires no new content to be taught at all.

faqs.question: Which graphic display calculator skills are worth paying a tutor to teach?
faqs.answer: Six, and they take a session or two. Solving an equation numerically and reporting it accurately; finding the intersection of two curves; locating a maximum or minimum and reading both coordinates; evaluating a definite integral without antidifferentiating; running a regression and identifying which output the question wants; storing values instead of retyping rounded ones. Alongside the operating skill comes the reporting habit of naming the command used, because a mark scheme awards method marks for a stated approach. Check which calculator models your child's school permits in examinations before buying anything.

faqs.question: How much should a Karama family expect to pay for IB maths tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published market rates vary by tier rather than by neighbourhood. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to AED 300, IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced in. Those are other providers' published figures, sourced from EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED. For IB Gram's own arrangements, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation.

faqs.question: Is online tuition a real substitute for someone sitting at the table in our flat?
faqs.answer: For DP mathematics, generally yes, and often better. A shared screen with a writing tablet shows working more clearly than two people leaning over one exercise book, sessions are recorded or summarised in writing, and the tutor pool is not limited to people who live a short drive from Karama. The honest exception is a much younger or very distractible student, where physical presence helps. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, so where a child genuinely needs someone in the room we will tell you rather than sell the online version as equivalent.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE Extended maths into DP1. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, before anything else. Rearranging formulae where the subject appears more than once, index laws with negative and fractional powers, simplifying rational expressions, surds and quadratics by every available method. Then trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles: radians, the unit circle, identities, and solving over a stated interval. These are assumed in DP rather than taught, and a student who is slow at them is slow at everything built on top. Six weeks of short, frequent practice over a summer closes most of the gap and makes the first DP1 term far less punishing.

faqs.question: Does the school's KHDA inspection band tell us anything about its maths teaching?
faqs.answer: Less than parents assume. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually and publishes a whole-school band from Outstanding to Very Weak, which can hide a strong department sitting next to a weak one, and cannot reflect a teacher who left in August. More useful questions: which mathematics routes the school runs at Higher Level, how many students sat each one last year, and whether the same teacher carries DP mathematics across both years. The school's own internal mark schemes, read alongside the raw marks, tell you more about your child's position than any published band.

faqs.question: Does our tutor need a UAE permit, and how would we check?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths and physics for the same DP student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because the two subjects share a great deal of algebra and a single tutor can carry context between them. The test is whether the person has genuinely taught both at the level required, not whether they are comfortable with both. For a student taking Analysis and Approaches HL alongside Physics HL, a dual specialist saves scheduling and repetition. For Applications and Interpretation HL with Chemistry HL, the overlap is thinner and two specialists usually serve better. We will tell you which case yours is before matching rather than after.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks until the May papers. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. With eight weeks the work is built backwards from the papers rather than forwards through the syllabus: a diagnostic paper marked properly in week one, then topics ordered by marks available rather than by syllabus order, timed conditions from the second session, and no new content introduced in the final fortnight. Paper 1 technique comes first because it is usually the least practised. What eight weeks cannot do is rebuild two years of algebraic fluency, so the target is recovering accessible marks rather than moving the ceiling.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-knowledge-park.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach Diploma mathematics to students at schools around Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and the Marina. intro.heading: Four maths courses, and the first job is knowing which one you are in
paragraphs: The Diploma offers Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. That is four courses, with different content, different papers and different university consequences, and the single most common reason a Knowledge Park family searches for an IB maths tutor is that the course chosen in the spring of Year 11 has turned out to be the wrong one by the autumn of Year 12.

Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route. It carries a Paper 1 sat without a graphic display calculator, which is the component that separates students who understand a method from students who have learned to type it in. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with a calculator permitted in every paper, and it is a genuinely demanding course rather than an easy alternative - the statistics content at Higher Level defeats plenty of students who found algebra straightforward.

The weightings decide where tutoring time should go, and they are not what most families assume. At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40 per cent each and the exploration carries 20. At Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 30 per cent each, Paper 3 carries 20, and the exploration carries 20. That means a Higher Level student who has never attempted a Paper 3 has left a fifth of the grade untouched, and Paper 3 is a single extended problem rather than a set of short questions, so practising Papers 1 and 2 does not prepare for it.

Marks in this subject are lost in patterned, diagnosable ways. Method marks go unclaimed because nothing was written down. Exact-form answers are given as decimals on Paper 1, where the command 'give your answer in exact form' is doing real work. Calculator syntax produces a plausible wrong number on Paper 2 and the candidate does not notice because no estimate was made first. Proof questions are answered with examples rather than argument. Each of those is a habit, and habits respond faster to tutoring than content gaps do.

Knowledge Park itself is an education free zone off Al Sufouh Road, holding university campuses and training institutes rather than homes, so families searching for a maths tutor near it live in Al Sufouh, Media City, Barsha Heights, The Greens or the Marina towers. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai - sending a tutor to a UAE address is a service we run only in India - and for a subject this narrow that is an advantage rather than a compromise. The pool of people in this emirate who have taught AA Higher Level Paper 3 is small, and it does not overlap neatly with the pool willing to drive to Barsha Heights at 5pm.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-knowledge-park.programmesIntro: Diploma maths does not begin in Year 12. What a student can cope with at Higher Level is largely decided by what happened in the two years before, which is why the programmes below matter to a maths conversation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria - knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts - each on a 1 to 8 scale. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the realistic preparation for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level; standard mathematics is not, and the gap usually shows in the first term of Year 12 rather than at the point of choosing.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within reach of Al Sufouh run MYP before the Diploma, and the criterion-based reporting makes it hard for parents to compare against the British-curriculum grades their neighbours quote. A criterion 6 in investigating patterns and a criterion 4 in applying mathematics point at very different Diploma readiness, and the distinction is worth asking the teacher about directly.

programmes.name: IGCSE mathematics as the other entry route
programmes.description: Many students arriving in Diploma maths come from Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 rather than from MYP. Those who also took Additional Mathematics 0606 or Further Pure 4PM1 meet calculus, series and trigonometric identities a year early and cross into Analysis and Approaches comfortably. Those who took only the main syllabus meet differentiation for the first time in Year 12 alongside everything else.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools around Al Barsha and The Greens feed a steady flow of students into Diploma maths at schools elsewhere in the city, so a transfer between curricula at 16 is common in this catchment. The practical check is simple: has the student done any calculus at all? If not, the first six weeks of Higher Level will feel like a different subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two years, one of the four courses, sat in the May session that UAE schools use, with a November session also available. The exploration is drafted in Year 12 and finished early in Year 13, against an internal school deadline that sits well before the Diploma's own submission window. Students routinely underestimate how much of the final grade is settled before the examination papers are even printed.
programmes.countryNote: The route choice has consequences at UAE and overseas universities alike. Engineering, physics, economics and most mathematics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Check each target university's own published entry page rather than relying on a general rule, because the requirement is set course by course and changes between admission cycles.

programmes.name: After the Diploma: where the maths grade lands
programmes.description: A maths grade functions as a gate rather than a decoration. A 5 in AA Standard Level and a 5 in AI Standard Level are not treated the same way by every engineering faculty, and the difference is invisible in a transcript line. This is the part of the decision students make at 16 without information, and the part a tutor can usefully bring evidence to.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, no IB points threshold has been verified from the Ministry's own pages, so no figure is published here. The British-track rules are sourced; the IB figure is not. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and treat equivalency as separate from any university's academic offer.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-knowledge-park.subjectsIntro: Diploma maths is one subject on a timetable of six, and the maths problem is often entangled with a neighbouring one. These are the subjects Knowledge Park families most often pair with maths support, each with the component that usually decides the grade.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is where the course is really tested. HL Paper 3 is two extended problems in one hour and needs its own practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, and calculator-permitted papers throughout. HL statistics - hypothesis testing, regression, Markov chains, graph theory - is where most of the difficulty sits, and it rewards precise interpretation of output rather than manipulation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject most often failing alongside maths, and usually for the same reason. Students who cannot rearrange an equation under time pressure lose marks in both. Fixing algebraic fluency generally improves two grades rather than one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry, equilibrium and energetics all require confident arithmetic and unit handling. Students who treat chemistry as a memory subject hit a wall at the calculation questions on Paper 2 and interpret it as a chemistry problem.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries quantitative content that catches out students who chose it to avoid maths. Diagram accuracy and the command terms - explain, discuss, evaluate - decide more marks than the economics itself.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Popular in this catchment, where many parents work in technology roles in and around the free zone. Algorithmic thinking and the ability to trace code transfer directly from and to maths, and the two subjects reinforce each other if taught with that in mind.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The quantitative tools - ratio analysis, investment appraisal, break-even - are where marks are quietly lost by students who are strong on the written content. A few hours of focused numerical work shifts the grade more than more essay practice does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The statistics and data-analysis questions are a reliable mark drain for students who have not met standard deviation and error bars with any confidence, which again is a maths problem presenting as a biology one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Mathematics is one of the areas of knowledge, and students who take maths at Higher Level often write their best Theory of Knowledge work about it. Support here is on argument structure and the student's own examples, not on the content of the essay.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic is mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ. Any support has to match the pathway the school has placed the student in.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: making the decision on evidence
paragraphs: The route choice is made at sixteen, usually in a single conversation, and reversed far more often than schools would like. It deserves better evidence than it normally gets, because the two courses are not a hard and an easy version of the same thing. Analysis and Approaches is algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof, with a Paper 1 sat without a graphic display calculator. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with calculator access throughout, and its Higher Level statistics content is where many students meet their real difficulty.

The useful diagnostic is not which the student prefers but how they behave on an unfamiliar algebraic manipulation with no calculator in reach. A student who reaches for a method and writes down each step, even hesitantly, is an Analysis and Approaches student. A student who freezes without the calculator, but who reads a data set accurately and explains what it means, is far better served by Applications and Interpretation and will usually score higher there. Preference tends to follow what the previous teacher made feel possible, which is not the same signal.

University requirements then constrain the choice from the other side. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; the requirement is set course by course and changes between admission cycles, so check each target university's own published entry page rather than relying on a general rule or a school corridor consensus. Where the two pull in opposite directions - a student suited to Applications and Interpretation but aiming at engineering - that is a genuine problem to plan around in Year 12, not a thing to discover in Year 13.
bullets: Test the decision on a no-calculator manipulation, not on stated preference

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and where the hours should actually go
paragraphs: Tutoring time gets spent badly when nobody has looked at the weightings. A Higher Level student who spends every session on Paper 2 style questions is working on 30 per cent of the grade while 40 per cent - Paper 3 and the exploration - goes untouched. The table sets out what each component is and what it demands, so the hours can be allocated against the marks rather than against whatever felt most urgent last week.

Paper 1 is the component that most rewards tutoring on Analysis and Approaches, because it is sat without a graphic display calculator and therefore tests whether a method is understood rather than typed. Students who have learned the course through the calculator are exposed here, and the repair is a term of deliberate no-calculator practice rather than a week of revision. The commands matter too: 'give your answer in exact form' means a surd or a logarithm, and a decimal scores nothing however accurate.

Higher Level Paper 3 is the component families discover last. It is one hour, two extended problems, and it builds from a simple case towards a generalisation, so it tests whether a student can follow a chain of reasoning they have not seen before. Practising it is not the same as practising Papers 1 and 2, and the only way to prepare is to sit whole Paper 3 problems to time and then work through what the mark scheme rewarded. Two or three of those is usually enough to change how a student approaches the paper.

sections.heading: The twenty exploration marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is 20 per cent of the grade at both levels and is marked out of twenty across five criteria. Almost no page in this market names a single one of them, which is strange, because knowing where the marks sit changes how a student spends their time completely. Most students over-invest in content and under-invest in criteria C and D, which together carry six of the twenty marks and are the two most reliably recoverable.

Personal engagement, criterion C, is not decoration. It asks for evidence that the student thought independently about the topic - their own data, their own question, their own choice of approach - and a template exploration on a popular topic scores poorly here however correct the mathematics. Reflection, criterion D, asks the student to consider limitations, alternatives and implications as the work develops, not to summarise at the end. A single closing paragraph headed 'reflection' is the most common way to lose those marks.

Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks and rewards mathematics that is relevant, correct, and commensurate with the level of the course. A Higher Level exploration doing Standard Level mathematics flawlessly is capped there. The practical consequence for planning is that the topic decision is a mark-scoring decision, and it should be tested for viability before the student invests weeks in it. That is where a tutor earns their keep on this component - asking whether the chosen question can actually generate level-appropriate mathematics - and where the support has to stop, because the writing and the mathematics must be the student's own.

sections.heading: The mark-scheme traps that cost this catchment the most marks
paragraphs: Marks in Diploma maths are lost in patterns rather than at random, and the patterns are specific enough to be worth naming. The first is unwritten method. Mark schemes award method marks for a correct approach even when the arithmetic goes wrong, and a student who does the middle steps mentally forfeits those marks entirely. The habit is cheap to fix and worth several marks a paper, which at the grade boundaries is frequently a whole grade.

The second is command-term blindness. 'Show that' requires the argument, not the answer, and a student who verifies with a value has not shown anything. 'Hence' means the previous result must be used, and ignoring it can score zero on an otherwise correct solution. 'Justify' requires a reason, not a restatement. These are the cheapest marks available anywhere in the subject and they go uncollected because nobody taught the vocabulary explicitly.

The third is calculator over-trust. On Paper 2, a wrong window, a wrong angle mode or a mistyped bracket produces a number that looks fine, and the candidate writes it down because no mental estimate was made first. The fix is a routine - estimate, compute, compare - and it also protects Paper 1, where the device is absent. The fourth is proof by example on Analysis and Approaches: a student who checks three cases and concludes has demonstrated nothing, and proof questions appear reliably at both levels.

The fifth pattern is about order rather than content. Students in this catchment overwhelmingly work through a paper from question one to the end, which means the hardest question gets the least time and the easiest marks at the back of the paper go uncollected entirely. Reading the whole paper first and taking the accessible parts of every question before returning to the difficult ones is a two-minute change of habit that frequently recovers more marks than a month of additional teaching. It needs practising under timed conditions, though, because under pressure a student reverts to whatever they have always done.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine that works between October and the May session
paragraphs: Past papers are the most useful and most badly used resource in this subject. A student who works through a paper with the answers beside them has done an exercise, not an examination, and learns very little about what they can do unaided under time pressure. The routine below is the one that converts papers into marks, and it is not complicated - it is simply harder than the alternative.

Sit the paper whole, to time, without the textbook or the mark scheme, in one go. Then mark it against the official mark scheme, and mark it strictly, because a generous mark erases the information you were trying to collect. Then categorise every lost mark: content not known, method known but not written, command term misread, calculator error, or time ran out. The categories matter more than the total, because each points at a different intervention. A paper losing twelve marks to unwritten method needs a habit change; one losing twelve marks to unknown content needs teaching.

Build the rotation by paper rather than by topic once the course content is complete, usually from the spring of Year 13. Alternate Paper 1 and Paper 2, and for Higher Level insert whole Paper 3 problems every second or third week from the start of Year 13 rather than saving them. Keep a single sheet listing the recurring error categories and read it before each paper. Students who do this stop making the same four mistakes by about the fifth paper, which is a bigger gain than any additional content.

sections.heading: What Diploma maths tuition costs in Dubai, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because the bottom is where most families start and the limits are worth understanding. Published online rates in this city begin at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik. At those rates the tutor is usually a university student, and for building arithmetic fluency or working through routine exercises that can be entirely adequate. For Higher Level Paper 3, or for judging whether an exploration topic can generate level-appropriate mathematics, it generally is not.

The next band up is a qualified subject tutor working online, which Unitors publishes from AED 200 an hour for IB work and AED 150 for IGCSE. Specialist IB and IGCSE rates run higher: TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and Bestimate's specialist band sits at AED 200 to 450 and above. The top of the published market is examiner-led work at around AED 650 an hour with BartyED. Across that whole range the thing being bought is narrowness of expertise, and narrowness only pays when the need is narrow.

Visiting rates sit separately, at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour for in-home one-to-one with travel inside the price, and advertised in-home packages run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour sessions against roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. These are other providers' published figures, not ours. IB Gram publishes no rate card here, because a number given without knowing the course, the level and the frequency is not information. The trial lesson and the consultation are free. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: Why the tutor pool matters more than the postcode for this subject
paragraphs: For general maths support, a tutor who lives nearby is a reasonable choice and the pool around Al Sufouh is deep. For Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and particularly for Paper 3 and for exploration topic viability, the pool is a handful of people across the whole emirate. The probability that one of them lives within fifteen minutes of Barsha Heights, is free at 5pm on a Wednesday, and is willing to spend forty minutes in Al Khail Road traffic each way, is low.

That arithmetic is the whole argument for delivering this over live video, and it is an argument about matching rather than about technology being better. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. So the question is not whether online is preferable in the abstract, but whether a specialist on a screen beats a generalist in the room for this particular subject at this particular level. For a Higher Level student eight months from the papers, it usually does.

The honest costs are worth naming. Sketching a three-dimensional diagram together is slower on a shared whiteboard than on paper. A student who is going to disengage will do so faster on a call. Against that, the whiteboard is saved and revisited, two siblings can be taught in one evening without a second journey, and no session is lost to traffic on Sheikh Zayed Road. Where delivery genuinely fails - a younger student who needs a person present, or one who cannot settle on a screen - that is worth saying rather than selling around.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the exploration, stated plainly
paragraphs: The exploration is where academic honesty is most often tested in this subject, because it is coursework, it is worth a fifth of the grade, and it is produced under a deadline while five other subjects are also making demands. The boundary is clear even when the pressure is not. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion rewards, model a technique on a different problem, ask the questions that make a student notice an unjustified step, and give feedback on a draft the student has written.

A tutor may not produce the work. The mathematics, the data, the argument and the words have to be the student's own, and the school signs an authentication saying so. If that authentication is untrue, the consequence falls on the candidate, not on whoever helped. One site ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments at a published price; the entire risk of that transaction is transferred to the student, who is the only person the board can sanction.

The same principle governs materials. We reference the IB subject guide, past papers and mark schemes, cite them, and point to the official source. We do not reproduce or distribute them, because they are the board's copyright and, in the case of unreleased material, a malpractice exposure in themselves. Parents should also know that the IB has not confirmed any session or results date to us - ibo.org blocks automated access - so we write about the May session that UAE schools sit and the November session as the alternative, and we send families to their school's Diploma coordinator for exact dates.

faqs.question: Is an IB maths tutor near Dubai Knowledge Park likely to know Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specifically?
faqs.answer: Some will, but the pool is small. Plenty of competent maths tutors live within fifteen minutes of Al Sufouh; the number who have taught Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, and particularly Paper 3, is a handful across the emirate. Add the requirement that they be free at your preferred hour and willing to drive to Barsha Heights or The Greens at 5pm, and the overlap gets very thin. Online delivery removes the geography from the match, which is why we work that way rather than by home visit.

faqs.question: My daughter chose Applications and Interpretation and now wants engineering. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: It is a real problem rather than a formality, but how serious depends on the universities. Engineering faculties commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and the requirement is set course by course and revised between admission cycles. Check the published entry page for each target course rather than relying on a general rule. If a switch is still possible in the first term of Year 12, that is usually the cleanest answer. If it is not, build the application around the courses that do accept Applications and Interpretation and get the grade as high as it will go.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why has my son never done one?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a Higher Level only component, one hour, two extended problems, and it carries 20 per cent of the grade. It builds from a straightforward case towards a generalisation, so it tests sustained reasoning on something unfamiliar rather than recall of standard question types. Students rarely meet it until late because schools teach content first and because it does not slot neatly into a topic test. Sitting two or three whole Paper 3 problems to time, then working through what the mark scheme actually rewarded, changes how a student approaches it.

faqs.question: How much of the maths grade is settled before the examinations even start?
faqs.answer: A fifth. The exploration carries 20 per cent at both Higher and Standard Level and is finished months before the papers, usually against a school internal deadline well ahead of the board's own submission window. It is marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Students who treat it as an administrative task routinely lose six or seven of those twenty marks on criteria C and D alone, which is the most recoverable part of the whole subject.

faqs.question: Where do the twenty exploration marks sit, criterion by criterion?
faqs.answer: Criterion A, presentation, carries 4. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries 4. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries 3. Criterion D, reflection, carries 3. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries 6. Criterion E is capped if a Higher Level student does Standard Level mathematics, however accurately. Criteria C and D together are six marks and are lost most often, because personal engagement is treated as a style note and reflection is written as a closing paragraph rather than developed as the work proceeds.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on Paper 1 when he gets the same questions right at home?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the calculator is absent. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator at both levels, and a student who learned the course through the device can execute every method on screen and none on paper. The second reason is command terms: 'give your answer in exact form' wants a surd or a logarithm, and a correct decimal scores nothing. The repair is a term of deliberate no-calculator practice, not a week of revision, so it is worth starting as early in Year 12 as possible.

faqs.question: How much exploration help can a Knowledge Park family pay for before it stops being the student's own work?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can test whether a topic will generate mathematics at the right level, explain what each criterion rewards, model a technique on a different problem, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot produce the mathematics, the data, the argument or the words. The school signs an authentication that the work is the candidate's own, and if it is not the sanction falls on the student. A provider selling completed internal assessments is transferring all of that risk onto your child.

faqs.question: What should a past-paper session actually look like?
faqs.answer: The paper sat whole, to time, with no textbook and no mark scheme in reach. Then marked strictly against the official scheme, because generous marking destroys the information. Then every lost mark categorised: content not known, method known but not written, command term misread, calculator error, or time ran out. The categories matter more than the total, because each needs a different response. Students who keep one sheet of recurring error types and read it before each paper usually stop making the same mistakes within about five papers.

faqs.question: What does Diploma maths tuition cost in Dubai if we start at the cheapest end?
faqs.answer: Published online rates in this city start at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik, which generally means a university student and can be fine for routine practice. A qualified online subject tutor is published from around AED 150 to 300. Specialist IB work is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270 and examiner-led sessions at around AED 650. Those are other providers' figures. Our trial lesson and consultation are free, and a quote depends on course, level and frequency.

faqs.question: People near Al Sufouh keep calling Applications and Interpretation the soft maths option - is that fair?
faqs.answer: No, it is a different one. Applications and Interpretation replaces heavy algebra and proof with modelling and statistics, and at Higher Level that statistics content - hypothesis testing, regression, graph theory, Markov chains - defeats plenty of students who found manipulation straightforward. The reliable test of fit is behaviour rather than preference: a student who writes down steps on an unfamiliar manipulation without a calculator belongs in Analysis and Approaches; a student who freezes there but reads and interprets a data set accurately will usually score higher in Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: My son's school in Al Barsha finishes at 2.45pm. When can a maths session run?
faqs.answer: A 4.30pm start works for most students in this catchment who go straight home, because no travel time has to be added at either end of an online session. Households where a parent works in Media City or the free zone often prefer 7.30pm, after the evening has settled. The right answer is the slot that survives a whole term without being moved, and that is usually built around when the student can still think rather than when the diary looks tidiest in September.

faqs.question: How does a calculator error cost marks when the method was right?
faqs.answer: Because the answer looks plausible and nothing flags it. A wrong angle mode, a badly set window or a mistyped bracket produces a number of roughly the right size, the candidate writes it down, and the accuracy marks go. The fix is a routine rather than knowledge: estimate the answer mentally, compute it, then compare the two and investigate any mismatch. That habit protects Paper 2 and also builds the mental fluency that Paper 1 tests directly, so it earns marks twice.

faqs.question: Does a Middle Years Programme criterion score predict how a student will cope with Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the detail matters more than the average. Middle Years Programme mathematics is assessed on four criteria, each from 1 to 8: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. A strong score in investigating patterns alongside a weak one in applying mathematics suggests a different Diploma route from the reverse pattern. Whether the student took extended rather than standard mathematics in the final two years of the programme is the other signal worth asking the teacher about directly.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Dubai schools sit, and where do I get the exact dates?
faqs.answer: Schools in the UAE sit the May session, with a November session also available. We do not publish IB examination or results dates on these pages, because ibo.org blocks automated access and no date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Get the exact dates from your school's Diploma coordinator or from ibo.org directly. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the position is different: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free who teaches our exact course and level?
faqs.answer: We tell you, rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Some combinations are genuinely thin - Applications and Interpretation Higher Level statistics, or Paper 3 work at short notice in the weeks before the session. When that happens you get three honest answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist can cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route for now. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, so ask every provider the question directly.

intro.heading: What the maths decision costs before a single session is booked
paragraphs: There are four Diploma mathematics courses, not one. Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. They share a core and then diverge substantially: AA is algebraic and proof-led with calculus carrying the Higher Level weight, while AI is modelling and statistics led with technology assumed throughout. A tutor who is strong in one is not automatically strong in the other, and a family who hires without naming the route is buying a lottery ticket with a four-way draw.

The cost consequence is immediate. A student placed in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level on the strength of enthusiasm rather than attainment will need ninety minutes a week for two years and may still be short in the final term. The same student in Applications and Interpretation Standard Level might need twelve hours in total. Published Dubai market rates put specialist IB tuition at roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, with Unitors starting its IB tuition at AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270, from sources read in October 2026. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. Multiply the honest hour count by any of them and the route decision dwarfs the rate decision.

Then there is the premium a LA Mer address attracts. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a comparable tutor online. What that extra buys, specifically, is a car on the Jumeirah Road between five and seven in the evening. It does not buy better teaching, and for a subject where the shortlist of genuine Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists is already small, insisting on someone who can park near the beachfront by 6pm shrinks that shortlist to whoever is nearby and free. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

The second cost driver, after the route, is the exploration. Every Diploma mathematics student produces one internally assessed exploration, marked against named criteria and externally moderated. Capable mathematicians routinely score in the middle bands on it, not because the mathematics is wrong but because the communication, the reflection or the personal engagement was never addressed. That is the cheapest set of marks in the whole course to improve and the one most commonly left to chance, because it is nobody's examination revision and it has no past paper.

What follows is the detail a LA Mer family needs to spend sensibly: the AA and AI comparison set out properly, Higher against Standard Level by paper and weighting, the exploration counted backwards from the school's own internal deadline, a topic-by-topic account of where marks are actually lost and roughly how many hours each costs to fix, the technology the course assumes, the transition into Diploma maths from IGCSE and MYP, the honesty boundary on the exploration, and how session timing works around the Al Wasl and Al Safa school run.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.programmesIntro: Diploma mathematics sits at the end of a sequence, and where a LA Mer student is in that sequence determines what tutoring can usefully do. These are the stages and what each one actually requires.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebraic and proof-led route, with calculus carrying the Higher Level weight. Students who enjoyed Additional Mathematics at IGCSE generally belong here. The Higher Level course is the most demanding mathematics most Dubai school students will meet, and the one where a weak algebraic base is least survivable because every later topic compounds it.
programmes.countryNote: Universities in the UAE and abroad set their own prerequisites and change them, so confirm whether a target degree expects Analysis and Approaches specifically with the admissions office rather than with any tutoring site. This page names no university requirement, because none in this research was read from a university's own page.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Modelling and statistics led, with technology assumed throughout and statistical inference arriving at Higher Level. Chosen by students heading towards business, social sciences, design and many life science routes. It is not an easy option, and students who select it expecting one commonly find the statistics unfamiliar rather than undemanding.
programmes.countryNote: The route choice is a degree decision made two years early, and Dubai school students are frequently asked to make it in Year 11 with incomplete information. The useful intervention is a single session on course choice before Year 12 begins, which is worth more than many hours of remedial work later.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced mathematics across five years, reported on a one-to-eight scale per criterion rather than as a percentage. Strong MYP criterion scores do not predict Diploma grades, because the Diploma assesses different things in a different format. The transition into Analysis and Approaches is where that gap shows up, usually in algebraic fluency.
programmes.countryNote: At Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah, MYP mathematics runs alongside the KHDA mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies requirements, which is timetable time that a family new to the Dubai system does not budget for.

programmes.name: IGCSE and Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: The route most LA Mer students take if their school is British curriculum before switching to the Diploma. Cambridge 0580 Extended is the usual entry point and Additional Mathematics is the better one, because calculus notation and proof structure appear there first. Students who skip Additional Mathematics meet both unfamiliar in the first term of Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. Mathematics will normally be one of those five, which is worth knowing before dropping it to a lower tier.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics breaks into topic areas with distinct failure modes, and tutoring is efficient only when it targets the right one. These are the areas LA Mer students most often need, with where the marks go.

subjects.name: Algebra and sequences
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: The load-bearing wall. Binomial expansion, logarithms and series work are where an insecure base shows first, and every later topic rests on manipulation fluency. A student who cannot rearrange confidently will lose marks in calculus questions that have nothing to do with algebra, which is why diagnosis starts here.

subjects.name: Functions and graphing
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Transformations, inverse functions, domain and range. Marks are lost on stating a domain restriction rather than on the algebra, and on sketching without labelling the features the question asked for. Short, cheap to fix, and routinely dropped because the student believes they understand it.

subjects.name: Calculus, differentiation
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, then optimisation and kinematics. Higher Level adds implicit differentiation and related rates. The usual failure is not the rule but the setup: a correct derivative of an incorrectly formed expression. Teaching the modelling step before the differentiation step is the intervention that works.

subjects.name: Calculus, integration
subjects.levels: AA HL and SL, AI HL
subjects.description: Where Analysis and Approaches Higher Level separates students decisively. Substitution, parts and partial fractions at Higher Level, with volumes of revolution and differential equations beyond. This is the single largest consumer of tutoring hours in the whole Diploma maths syllabus and the topic most worth starting early rather than revising late.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and identities
subjects.description: Radians, identities, compound angles and solving in a specified interval. The commonest lost mark is giving a correct solution and missing the others inside the interval, which is a technique rather than a knowledge problem and takes two sessions to fix permanently.

subjects.name: Proof
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, and proof by induction. Students who have never been taught what counts as a complete argument write true statements that score nothing. The structure is learnable quickly and is one of the highest returns per hour available in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AI HL and SL, AA SL
subjects.description: Distributions, correlation, and at Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, statistical inference including hypothesis testing. Students coming from a British curriculum frequently meet inference for the first time here, and treating it as formula recall rather than as reasoning about evidence is why it costs them marks.

subjects.name: Vectors
subjects.description: Lines, planes, scalar and vector products at Higher Level. Geometric interpretation is where marks go: a student who can compute a vector product but cannot say what it means geometrically answers half the question. Worth four to six focused hours rather than a general sweep.

subjects.name: Technology and the graphing calculator
subjects.description: Applications and Interpretation assumes technology throughout and both routes examine calculator-permitted papers. Students lose marks by using the calculator where working is required, and by not using it where it would be faster. The school states the permitted model and the examination regulations; confirm both with the school rather than with any tutoring page.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: One internally assessed piece of work, marked against named criteria and externally moderated. Strong mathematicians commonly score mid-band because communication, reflection or visible personal engagement were never addressed. A tutor coaches the question, teaches the criteria and critiques drafts; the mathematics and the writing must be the student's own.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that sets the bill
paragraphs: This choice is made in Year 11 and paid for over two years. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led, with calculus carrying the Higher Level weight. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with technology assumed throughout and statistical inference at Higher Level. They are not a harder and an easier version of the same course; they are different courses that suit different students and different degrees.

Two mistakes dominate. The first is choosing Analysis and Approaches because it sounds more rigorous, without the algebraic fluency to carry it, which produces a two-year struggle and the largest tutoring bill available in the Diploma. The second is choosing Applications and Interpretation to avoid difficulty and discovering that statistical inference is genuinely demanding and entirely unfamiliar. Both mistakes are made because the decision is framed as a difficulty question when it is a fit and prerequisite question.

The prerequisite part has to be checked at source. Universities set their own entry requirements, revise them, and differ between countries and between faculties within a university. This page deliberately names no university requirement, because none was read from a university's own admissions page in this research, and a tutoring site that tells you which route a specific degree demands is guessing with your child's two years. Email the admissions office of two or three target universities in Year 11 and ask directly. It takes a week, it is free, and it is more reliable than any summary on any tutoring site.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, by paper and by hour
paragraphs: Level determines the hours more than route does. Higher Level adds content, adds an additional examination paper in both routes, and raises the analytical demand on the exploration without changing its criteria. A Standard Level student who is coping needs an hour a week and a block before the papers. A Higher Level student who is behind can absorb ninety minutes a week for two years and want more in the final term, which is the single largest tutoring commitment in the Diploma.

The structural point worth understanding is that the extra Higher Level paper carries its own technique, not merely more of the same content. A student who has practised only the shorter papers meets a different kind of question in the extended one and performs below their understanding. This is a teachable, finite problem and it is where a specialist earns the difference between the AED 200 and AED 450 ends of the published Dubai specialist band.

There is also a ceiling on usefulness. A Diploma candidate carries six subjects, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a service requirement. Past roughly ninety minutes a week in one subject, additional tutoring competes with the student's own study time and with the other five subjects rather than adding to them. Families buying four maths sessions a week are usually buying the thing that makes the rest of the Diploma worse, and a tutor who accepts that booking without saying so is not advising you.

sections.heading: The exploration, counted backwards from your school's deadline
paragraphs: Every Diploma mathematics student produces one exploration, internally assessed against named criteria and externally moderated. It is worth a meaningful share of the final grade and it is the only part of the course with no past paper, no mark scheme to practise against, and no revision guide that helps. It is therefore the part where a capable student most often loses marks they could easily have kept, and where tutoring money does the most work per hour.

The schedule is what fails, not the mathematics. A student with a vague topic in September has a vague topic in January, writes in a weekend, and submits something whose mathematics is sound and whose communication, reflection and visible engagement were never considered. Working backwards from the school's own internal deadline, rather than from the IB session, is the fix, because the school's dates are the binding ones and they arrive earlier than families expect.

A note on the criteria. Diploma internal assessments are marked criterion by criterion, each with its own descriptors, and a strong piece can be capped by one criterion that was never addressed. Criterion sets and mark allocations are revised by cohort, so read the current version in your child's own subject guide with them, and confirm anything uncertain with the school's maths teacher or IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring page, including this one. What a tutor contributes is the habit of reading the criteria before writing, which most students never do.

sections.heading: Where maths marks are actually lost, and what each costs to fix
paragraphs: Tutoring in mathematics is efficient only when aimed. A general weekly hour across a two-year Higher Level course covers everything and fixes nothing in particular, which is why families finish the year surprised that a substantial spend produced a modest change. The alternative is to start from a marked paper, identify the two or three failure modes that are actually costing marks, and buy hours against those.

The failure modes are more consistent than parents expect. Insecure algebraic manipulation showing up as calculus errors. Solving trigonometric equations and finding one solution instead of all of them in the interval. Writing true statements in a proof question that do not constitute an argument. Setting up an optimisation problem incorrectly and then differentiating the wrong expression flawlessly. Treating statistical inference as formula recall. Using the graphing calculator where working is required, or failing to use it where it saves four minutes.

Each of these is finite. The table gives rough hour counts, which exist so a family can calculate rather than guess. Multiply by the published Dubai specialist band of roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and you have a real budget for a real problem, instead of an open weekly commitment with no end condition. The discipline that matters is the end condition: a topic block should stop when the topic holds under timed conditions, not when the term does. A tutor who cannot describe what the end of the block looks like is describing an open commitment, and families on this coast have paid for several of those.
