sections.heading: Moving into Diploma maths from IGCSE or MYP
paragraphs: The first term of Diploma mathematics is where transfer gaps surface, and in LA Mer plenty of students transfer. A child who did Cambridge 0580 Extended and no Additional Mathematics meets calculus notation and formal proof for the first time at sixteen, alongside five other new subjects. A child arriving from MYP has criterion grades that say nothing predictive about Diploma performance, because the two systems assess different things in different formats.

The gap is almost always one of three things, and it is almost never general ability. It is algebraic fluency, which Additional Mathematics builds and Extended IGCSE only partly does. It is notation, where a student who understands a concept cannot read the way the Diploma writes it. Or it is the expectation of justification, where IGCSE often accepts an answer and the Diploma expects an argument. All three are closable in a short block, and all three are far cheaper to close in the summer before Year 12 than in the spring of Year 13.

The practical recommendation for a LA Mer family is a short diagnostic block in that summer: four to six sessions on algebraic fluency and notation for a student heading into Analysis and Approaches, or on data handling and modelling conventions for one heading into Applications and Interpretation. Nothing else is competing for the student's time, the rate is the same as it would be in term, and the hours do several times the work they would do once four internal assessments and an Extended Essay are running simultaneously.

sections.heading: The honesty line on a mathematics exploration
paragraphs: One of the sites competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments. For a mathematics exploration this is both a malpractice trigger and, practically, easy to detect, because a piece of work whose mathematical level does not match the student's examination performance invites exactly the scrutiny a family does not want. The consequence falls on the student's Diploma, not on the vendor, and no deadline justifies it.

Legitimate exploration support is specific and worth paying for. A tutor may test whether a candidate topic contains mathematics at the right level, challenge the research question until it can be completed within scope, teach what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and say precisely where it falls short of a criterion, and keep the student's chosen technique inside what they can genuinely justify. That last point is underrated: ambitious technique the student cannot explain loses more marks than modest technique they own completely.

What a tutor may not do is produce mathematics the student then presents, write or rewrite prose, edit a draft to a standard, or supply text or working that ends up in the submission. IB Gram tutors teach, review and give feedback on the student's own work. We also do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, because those belong to the IB; we reference and link the official source instead. Say this boundary to your child before the first exploration session, in those words.

sections.heading: Fitting sessions around the LA Mer school day
paragraphs: Mathematics is a poor subject to teach at the end of a long day, which makes session timing a real variable rather than an administrative one. Pickup for the schools most LA Mer students attend runs between roughly 2:40pm and 3:30pm depending on school and year group. That makes a 4pm or 4:30pm session genuinely available online, which is the single largest practical difference from a home visit, where the tutor's own drive across Dubai usually makes 6pm the earliest realistic slot.

For a Higher Level student, ninety minutes at 4:30pm reliably outperforms ninety minutes at 7:30pm, and parents who have tried both say so. Where an early slot is impossible, two shorter sessions in a week work better than one long evening one, because the limiting factor at that hour is attention rather than time. Online delivery makes splitting a weekly ninety minutes into two forty-five minute sessions trivial; a visiting tutor cannot absorb two drives for the same fee.

The two calendar features to build in are the school's own assessment weeks and Ramadan. Paying for sessions during a week of school examinations buys hours the student cannot use, so pause them. Ramadan shortens the school day, shifts routines later, and falls at a different point each year because it follows the lunar calendar, so a plan should assume disruption rather than a fixed date. Post-Iftar sessions work well for many families and are easy to schedule online, which is awkward for a tutor whose evening is already routed around other households.

process.description: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is a different booking from Applications and Interpretation Standard Level, and the four combinations need four different specialists. This single detail decides whether the hours you buy are useful, and it is the thing most enquiry forms never ask for.

process.description: Insecure algebra showing up as calculus errors needs a different block from missing solutions in an interval. A tutor who can name which one your child has, from the marked paper, in the first session, is a tutor worth the specialist end of the published rate band.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course should my child in LA Mer take, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on fit and on degree prerequisites, not on difficulty. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led with calculus carrying the Higher Level weight; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led with inference at Higher Level. A student who enjoyed Additional Mathematics at IGCSE usually belongs in Analysis and Approaches. Check prerequisites by emailing two or three target universities' admissions offices in Year 11. This page names no university requirement, because none was read from a university's own page in this research.

faqs.question: How many hours of IB maths tutoring does a Higher Level student actually need?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes a week from early in Year 12 is the realistic shape for a Higher Level student who is behind, running to the final paper. A Standard Level student who is coping needs about an hour a week plus a block before the papers. Beyond ninety minutes weekly in one subject, tutoring starts competing with the student's own study and with the other five Diploma subjects. At published Dubai specialist rates of roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, that arithmetic matters more than the rate itself.

faqs.question: What is a LA Mer tutor allowed to do on the mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may test whether a candidate topic has mathematics at the right level, challenge the research question until the piece is finishable, teach what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short, and keep the student's technique inside what they can justify. A tutor may not produce mathematics or prose that gets submitted, rewrite a draft, or edit it to a standard. One site competing for this search sells completed Internal Assessments; walk away from that.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class and badly on IB maths papers?
faqs.answer: Usually one of a short list of technique failures rather than a knowledge gap. Finding one solution to a trigonometric equation instead of all of them in the interval. Setting up an optimisation problem incorrectly and differentiating the wrong expression correctly, which still earns a method mark and hides the gap. Writing true statements in a proof question that do not form an argument. Using the graphing calculator where working is required. Each takes two to six focused sessions, and a marked paper identifies which one in a single session.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a LA Mer home?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video across the UAE and makes no home visits anywhere in the Emirates; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For Diploma mathematics the trade is clearly in your favour: the pool of genuine Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists is small, and requiring one who can reach Jumeirah 1 by 6pm reduces it further. Sessions use a shared whiteboard both tutor and student write on, with an optional recording.

faqs.question: What time can maths sessions start after school in Jumeirah 1?
faqs.answer: Pickup for the schools most LA Mer students attend runs between roughly 2:40pm and 3:30pm, so 4pm or 4:30pm is realistic online. That matters for mathematics specifically, because ninety minutes at 4:30pm reliably outperforms ninety minutes at 7:30pm. A home visit usually cannot start before 6pm, since the tutor's own drive across Dubai has to happen first. Where an early slot is impossible, two shorter sessions in a week work better than one long evening one.

faqs.question: My child did IGCSE maths without Additional Mathematics. Is that a problem for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: It is a known gap rather than a problem, and it is cheap to close at the right moment. Students who did Cambridge 0580 Extended without Additional Mathematics meet calculus notation and formal proof for the first time at sixteen, alongside five other new subjects. Four to six sessions in the summer before Year 12, on algebraic fluency and notation, does several times the work the same hours would do in the spring of Year 13, because nothing else is competing for the student's attention.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier route?
faqs.answer: No, and choosing it on that basis is a common and expensive error. Applications and Interpretation assumes technology throughout and brings statistical inference at Higher Level, which students arriving from a British curriculum frequently meet for the first time and find genuinely demanding. It is a different course for a different kind of student and a different set of degrees, not a reduced version of Analysis and Approaches. Decide on fit and prerequisites, checked with university admissions offices directly, rather than on perceived difficulty.

faqs.question: How do derivations and graph sketching work in an online maths session?
faqs.answer: Through a shared whiteboard both tutor and student write on, so a derivation is built in front of the student with them doing most of the writing, and a sketch is annotated live rather than described. The student's own marked paper or exploration draft is shared on screen and worked through directly. Sessions can be recorded, which students use heavily before papers and which a home visit never provides. This is the part parents doubt most and the part the free trial lesson settles fastest.

faqs.question: Which IB schools near LA Mer offer all four maths courses?
faqs.answer: Ask each school directly, because not every Dubai IB school runs all four combinations, and a student's route is sometimes set by the school's staffing rather than by their aptitude. The IB schools nearest this coast include Jumeira Baccalaureate School and Emirates International School Jumeirah, with Raffles World Academy, Kings' School Al Barsha and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai drawing from further out. Those schools are named as neighbourhood context; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: When should we start exploration coaching rather than examination work?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the school's own internal deadline, which is the binding date and arrives earlier than families expect. The useful sequence is a topic shortlist of three ideas, then narrowing to one answerable question, then attempting the mathematics before any prose is written, then reading the criteria with the student, then a full draft well before the deadline. Four to six sessions spread across that period is typically enough. A student with a vague topic in September still has one in January without this structure.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Dubai students sit, and what about dates?
faqs.answer: Dubai IB schools sit the May session, with November available at a small number of schools worldwide. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Any site quoting you an exact date should cite ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator. In practice, plan tutoring against the school's internal assessment deadlines, which are earlier and considerably more binding than the session itself.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle both maths and physics for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and wanting it usually costs more than it saves. The internal assessments are marked on different criteria, the papers reward different techniques, and insisting on one person shrinks an already small shortlist of Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialists. Online, two specialists can take back-to-back slots on the same evening with no travel gap between them, which is the arrangement most LA Mer Diploma families settle on once they stop looking for a single tutor to cover both.

faqs.question: What should the graphing calculator policy be in our planning?
faqs.answer: Confirm the permitted model and the examination regulations with your child's school, not with a tutoring page, because schools state this and regulations are revised. What tutoring addresses is the technique question: students lose marks by using the calculator where working is required, and by not using it where it would save several minutes on a permitted paper. That distinction is rarely taught explicitly by anyone, takes two or three sessions, and applies to both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: What end condition should we set on a Diploma maths topic block?
faqs.answer: Set an end condition at the start. A topic block ends when the topic holds under timed conditions, not when the term ends. A weekly commitment gets reviewed at six sessions against a named weakness, and again at the next school assessment. If the specific thing you bought help for has moved, continue or stop deliberately; if it has not, change the tutor or the plan. Open-ended maths tutoring with no end condition is the most reliable way a Diploma family overspends.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.closingHeading: Settle the route, then the failure mode, then the rate
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-la-mer.closingBody: Confirm with the school which of the four Diploma mathematics courses your child sits and at which level, and get the school's internal exploration deadline in writing. Find the most recent marked paper and let a specialist name the failure mode from it rather than describing the subject. Only then discuss hours and price, because the route and the hour count decide the bill and the hourly rate barely moves it. Then take the free trial lesson, one per family and before any payment, ideally in the 4pm slot that online delivery makes available on this coast.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-living-legends.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics to students in Living Legends and the neighbouring communities. Each profile states the route and the level, and availability is listed by hour, because in a commuting household the hour decides whether anything works.

intro.heading: Mathematics needs the best hour, and here the best hour is late
paragraphs: Most Diploma subjects survive a tired session. Mathematics does not. A calculus question requires the student to choose a method, carry it through several steps, and check whether the result makes sense, all without losing the thread. A student who walked in from a twenty-five minute journey fifteen minutes ago cannot do that, and the hour becomes a pleasant conversation about mathematics rather than an hour of doing it. In this community that is the first problem to solve, before any question of who teaches it.

Living Legends is a single gated community of villas and apartment towers off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, between Dubai Sports City, Motor City and Remraam, with no secondary school inside the gates. Every Diploma student therefore commutes, most often to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate or the Al Khail Road corridor. School finishes between half past two and half past three, the journey takes twenty to thirty minutes in free traffic and longer on a multi-community bus route, and the student is home between four and half past four. Add time to eat and settle and the first genuinely usable slot is around six.

The second constraint is what the evening already contains. Dubai Sports City sits immediately next door, and many households here have children in academy programmes training between five and seven on several weekdays. Where that applies, the weekday evening is effectively gone for mathematics, and the weekend morning becomes the serious slot. There is also the taught week to account for: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, so the homework load is larger than a six-subject list suggests.

The third constraint is the subject itself, and it is the one families underestimate. IB Mathematics is four courses, not one: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level, with different syllabuses, different papers and different rules about what a calculator is for. Those four do not place equal demands on a student's concentration. A non-calculator Analysis paper needs a sharp hour; interpretation work in Applications can survive a later one. Knowing which course is involved therefore changes the timetable as well as the teaching.

IB Gram's answer is to take travel out of the arrangement so the hour can be chosen rather than inherited. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can start minutes after the student is home, move to a Saturday morning for the harder work, and be matched on course and level rather than on who will drive to a gated community. Nobody is sent to a Living Legends address; home visits are a service we operate only in India.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-living-legends.programmesIntro: Three stages of IB mathematics matter in this community, plus the route most students arrive from. These notes describe what each stage asks of the student's time as well as their ability.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics, standard and extended
programmes.description: Marked against four criteria on a 0-8 scale: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the preparation route for Analysis and Approaches. Investigating patterns is the criterion students neglect, and it is the direct ancestor of the Diploma exploration.
programmes.countryNote: Younger students from this community attend nearby schools in Motor City, Sports City and Remraam, so journeys are short and afternoon sessions are realistic. That makes MYP mathematics the one stage where timing in Living Legends is straightforward rather than negotiated.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebraic route. One paper is sat without a graphical calculator, which rewards manipulation and penalises reliance on technology. Higher Level adds a third paper of extended problem solving and reaches calculus techniques Standard Level never meets, along with proof by induction and complex numbers.
programmes.countryNote: This is the route most engineering, physics and mathematics applicants need, and the one that demands the sharpest hour of the week. For a commuting student here that argues for a weekend morning as the main session rather than a weekday evening after a long journey.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The statistical and modelling route, with a graphical calculator permitted throughout. Higher Level adds a third paper and a heavier load of statistical inference, matrices and graph theory. Marks go missing where a correct calculation is never translated back into the context the question established.
programmes.countryNote: Applications tolerates a later weekday slot better than Analysis, because much of the work is interpretation rather than construction. That makes it the more schedulable of the two routes in a household with academy training in the early evening.

programmes.name: The International GCSE route in
programmes.description: Most students here enter the Diploma from Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 rather than from the MYP. An Extended or Higher tier grade is broadly the expected foundation for Analysis and Approaches; a strong Core or Foundation result points toward Applications. The step up is in abstraction rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: The transition term is where most ground is lost, because the school is teaching new content while the student is still adjusting to being marked on reasoning rather than answers. Work in that first term is cheaper and more effective than remediation in the second Diploma year.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-living-legends.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is best planned strand by strand, because each strand needs a different amount of concentration and therefore a different slot. These are the strands students here most often need rebuilt.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents and logarithms, with complex numbers and proof by induction at Higher Level in Analysis. Losses are algebraic slips under time pressure rather than conceptual gaps, which responds to short drilled sessions and suits a weekday slot.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, rational and reciprocal forms. Marks go missing on sketches drawn without the asymptotes and intercepts the markscheme wants, which is a checklist habit and quick to fix.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Identities and equations, with substantial coordinate work in Applications. Trigonometric equations lose marks on mishandled solution ranges. In Analysis Higher Level the identity manipulation is where candidates stall and lose time.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Light in Analysis and central in Applications: distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. The final interpreting sentence is where the marks sit, and omitting it is the standard loss across both levels.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, reaching substitution, parts, implicit differentiation and differential equations in Analysis Higher Level. The strand that most needs a long, undisturbed session, which in this community means a weekend morning.

subjects.name: Proof and mathematical communication
subjects.description: Induction, contradiction and counterexample, plus the discipline of setting out an argument. Students who reach correct results and cannot write them as an argument lose marks on material they genuinely understand.

subjects.name: Paper 3 technique
subjects.description: Two long investigative questions where each part depends on the last, so a candidate who stalls early forfeits everything downstream. Needs full-length practice, which rules out a 45-minute weekday slot entirely.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Individual mathematical writing assessed on presentation, communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The band is largely decided by whether the topic can carry mathematics of appropriate depth for the level.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator fluency
subjects.description: Statistical functions, solvers, regression and graphing. Applications candidates lose time rather than understanding when operation is slow, and this is among the fastest returns available in the whole course.

sections.heading: Which maths task belongs in which window
paragraphs: A commuting Diploma household in this community has perhaps three usable study windows a week after travel, training, mandatory subjects and homework. Mathematics is the subject where assigning those windows correctly produces the largest gain, because the difference between a sharp hour and a tired one is larger here than in any other Diploma subject.

The short weekday window handles consolidation. The school has taught a topic; the student works a few questions, sees a worked example, and has a misunderstanding corrected before it sets. That is genuinely valuable and it fits forty-five minutes after arrival. What it cannot do is build method communication on long questions or develop the stamina a Higher Level third paper requires, because both need a chain of reasoning longer than the slot.

The weekend morning window handles everything that decides grades at the margin: calculus problems with several stages, Paper 3 practice at full length, timed papers followed by a proper review of where the marks went, and exploration analysis with the student's own data on screen. Families who assign these to a weekday evening get a watered-down version of each and then wonder why progress stalled.

The third window is the school holiday, and it is the most underused asset in a Diploma year. The winter and spring breaks are the only periods with free daytime hours, and they fall at useful points relative to internal deadlines. A short intensive block then, particularly on the exploration, converts better than the same hours spread across term-time evenings. Families who travel can keep sessions running from wherever they are, which follows from lessons being delivered over video.

sections.heading: Four courses, and which of them survives a late slot
paragraphs: IB Mathematics is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. Those four are separate courses with separate syllabuses, separate papers and separate calculator rules, and a tutor who does not establish which one applies in the first conversation is planning for somebody else's child. That much is true anywhere. What is specific to a commuting household is that the four do not place equal demands on a depleted hour.

Analysis and Approaches is the least forgiving. One paper is sat without a graphical calculator, which rewards algebraic fluency, and Higher Level adds proof and extended calculus. This is construction work: the student has to build something rather than interpret it, and construction needs a sharp mind. For a student in this community, Analysis belongs in the weekend window as the primary session, with weekday slots used for consolidation.

Applications and Interpretation is more schedulable. A calculator is permitted throughout, much of the work is interpreting a context and writing a conclusion, and statistical procedures are repeatable in a way that proof is not. A student who is tired can still practise reading a regression output and writing the sentence that explains it, which means a weekday evening session retains most of its value.

The level then multiplies the effect. Higher Level in either route adds a third paper of extended investigation, and that paper cannot be practised in fragments because each part depends on the previous one. Any Higher Level plan in this community therefore needs at least one long window a week, and families who only have weekday evenings should know that before committing rather than discovering it in the second term.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, and the practice it actually needs
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches candidates sit one paper without a graphical calculator, and it is the paper that most reliably surprises students who have been taught with technology in the room. The difficulty is not conceptual. It is that habits built around checking a graph on a screen do not transfer, and a student who has always verified a solution visually has to learn to verify it algebraically instead.

The practice that works is specific and it is not simply doing more questions. It is short, frequent, timed sets with the calculator physically unavailable, where the student is required to show every manipulation. Exact values are the recurring theme: surds left as surds, trigonometric values given exactly rather than as decimals, logarithmic expressions simplified rather than evaluated. A student who writes 1.41 where the markscheme wants root two has given away a mark on a question they answered correctly.

There is a second habit to build, which is sanity checking without technology. Does this answer have the right sign? Is this magnitude plausible? Does the function behave as the algebra implies at the extremes? Students with a graphical calculator develop this instinct through the screen and lose access to it in the examination. It can be taught deliberately, and it is one of the better uses of a short weekday slot because it needs frequency rather than length.

Applications and Interpretation candidates have the mirror-image problem. A calculator is available throughout and they are expected to use it fluently, so marks are lost to slow or incorrect operation rather than to mathematical error. Statistical functions, regression, solvers and graphing all have to be automatic, and that is drillable in a small number of sessions. It is also, for a tired student at the end of a long day, one of the few genuinely productive things a weekday evening can deliver.

sections.heading: The exploration calendar, and why it belongs in a holiday
paragraphs: Every IB mathematics course carries an exploration worth 20 per cent of the grade, and the band is largely determined by the choice of topic rather than by the quality of the writing. A topic that cannot support mathematics of appropriate depth for the level produces a capped mark however carefully it is presented. That decision is made weeks before any drafting, which is why support concentrated at the drafting stage arrives too late to change much.

The timing problem in this community is acute. The school's internal deadline sits months before the board's window, and it falls in a term already crowded with subject deadlines. A student commuting an hour a day does not have spare weekday evenings in that period, and the exploration is the piece of work with no weekly lesson defending its place in the timetable. So it gets postponed until it is urgent, and then it is written in a rush.

The practical answer is to place the exploration block in a school holiday or across weekend mornings, and to do the topic testing early. One session well before the deadline, examining whether the proposed investigation has adequate mathematical depth for the level, a wide enough variable range, and an analysis that will support a meaningful conclusion, protects a term of work. Depth expectations differ between Higher and Standard Level in the same route, which is why the level has to be confirmed before anybody approves a topic.

The boundary is absolute. A tutor may test a topic, explain what each criterion rewards, read a draft the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach notation and referencing properly. A tutor must never write the exploration, draft sections of it, or edit it until the mathematics is no longer the student's own. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is an IB malpractice trigger and the penalty falls on the student.

sections.heading: Where maths marks go, and how long each fix takes
paragraphs: Diagnosis in mathematics is unusually tractable because the losses are visible on marked paper. A tutor who has seen one past paper with a mark breakdown can usually name the problem before the first session; a tutor who has not is offering general revision because that is the only plan available without evidence. General revision is also the slowest-converting and most expensive product in this market.

Four patterns account for most losses. Method not communicated, where a correct final answer with no intermediate steps collects a fraction of the available credit, and which is the largest avoidable loss in Analysis at both levels. Result not interpreted, where an Applications candidate computes correctly and never writes the sentence that explains what the number means in context. Calculator inefficiency, where an Applications candidate loses time rather than understanding. And Paper 3 collapse at Higher Level, where a candidate who stalls on an early part forfeits everything downstream.

A fifth is foundational rather than habitual: a student who never secured negative and fractional indices, or algebraic fraction manipulation, has a gap that touches every later topic. That is a term of work rather than a fortnight, and an honest diagnostic distinguishes it from the habit-level problems rather than treating everything as the same job.

The practical point for a family here is that the habit-level fixes are fast and the foundational one is not, so the diagnosis changes the plan and the budget. sections.heading: What IB maths support costs around this community
paragraphs: Mathematics is the best-supplied subject in this market, which gives a family more choice and more scope to misjudge value. The sourced bands first, since three of the six most visible pages competing for these searches publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate putting examination-year specialist support at AED 200 to 450 plus. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

In mathematics specifically, the match matters more than the band. A tutor at AED 150 who has taught Applications Standard Level repeatedly is better value for an Applications student than one at AED 400 whose recent experience is all Analysis Higher Level, and the reverse holds just as firmly. Because there are four distinct courses, asking which of them a tutor last taught is worth more than comparing two numbers.

For budgeting, Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session give AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Packages circulate at roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. In a gated community the in-home figure also loses minutes at the gate on every visit. None of these is an IB Gram price list, and the MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge, so no licensing cost belongs in any quote.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what may honestly be claimed
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit and the detail is short. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is speculating. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate matter, requiring a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

School regulation sits with the emirate. Dubai is KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

What none of that licenses is a claim of endorsement. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We publish no IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification; IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session and specific dates should come from the school's coordinator. We also do not reproduce IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, which are the organisation's copyright.

sections.heading: When the window you have is not the window available
paragraphs: Honest availability is part of planning rather than a disclaimer. In this community the constraint is almost always the hour. Half past five to seven on a weekday is what nearly every family in Dubai asks for, and weekend mornings are the second most contested slot, particularly among households whose weekday evenings are taken by training.

Three adjustments usually solve it. Shifting a weekday session fifteen or twenty minutes later opens options a 5.30pm request does not. Moving the main session to a Saturday rather than a Friday morning, or vice versa, often finds the specialist with space. And taking a less contested weekday, typically Sunday or Monday, resolves it immediately in many cases. For a Higher Level student needing one long window a week, booking that window early in the school year is worth more than negotiating it in February.

Where the request is narrow the answer may be a wait. Analysis Higher Level with Paper 3 specialism at short notice is the tightest mathematics request in this market, because Higher Level cohorts at individual schools are small and the pool of teachers who have taken the course to a final session recently is correspondingly thin across the whole emirate. In that case we give a date rather than offering an Applications specialist to an Analysis candidate.

No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is why families keep finding one in week three. Ours is stated alongside the delivery position: lessons run over live video, specialists may be based in the UAE or elsewhere including experienced IB teachers outside the Emirates, and nobody is sent to a UAE address because home visits exist only in our India service.

faqs.answer: Around six on a weekday, and the main session is often better on a weekend morning. There is no secondary school inside this community, so every Diploma student commutes to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills or the Al Khail corridor. School ends between half past two and half past three, the journey runs twenty to thirty minutes or longer on a multi-community bus, and the student is home between four and half past four. Mathematics specifically punishes a depleted hour, so the thirty or forty minutes to eat and settle is not optional.

faqs.question: Does Analysis and Approaches need a different slot from Applications?

Analysis is construction work: one paper is sat without a graphical calculator, and Higher Level adds proof and extended calculus, all of which need a sharp mind. All of that requires full-length practice followed by a proper review. faqs.question: What should the weekend maths session actually be used for?
faqs.answer: Calculus with multiple stages, Higher Level Paper 3 practice, full timed papers with a real review afterwards, and exploration analysis with the student's own data on screen. Those are the tasks that decide grades at the margin and the ones most likely to be squeezed out of a commuting week. Weekday slots suit consolidating the topic the school taught that fortnight, drilling algebra and indices, and improving calculator fluency. Assigning the windows deliberately usually helps more than adding a third session.

faqs.question: How do we prepare for a maths paper sat without a graphical calculator?
faqs.answer: With short, frequent, timed sets taken with the calculator physically unavailable, requiring every manipulation to be shown. Exact values are the recurring theme: surds left as surds, trigonometric values given exactly rather than as decimals, logarithms simplified rather than evaluated. A student writing 1.41 where the markscheme wants root two has given away a mark on a question they answered. The second habit is sanity checking algebraically rather than visually, which students with a calculator develop through the screen and lose in the examination room.

faqs.question: When should the maths exploration be started for a student here?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and the topic test matters more than the drafting. The band is largely determined by whether the investigation can support mathematics of appropriate depth for the level, and that is decided before a word is written. Shortlist topics well before the school's internal deadline, test each one for depth, variable range and whether the analysis will support a meaningful conclusion, and then place the drafting work in a school holiday or across weekend mornings where uninterrupted hours exist.

faqs.question: Do academy training evenings in Sports City rule out maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: They rule out the obvious slot, not the subject. Training next door routinely occupies five until seven on several weekdays, which removes the window every other family also wants. Two alternatives work: a short session immediately after school and before training, which suits calculator fluency and algebra drilling because those need repetition rather than length, and a weekend morning block for the heavier work. Most academy households in this community end up with exactly that combination, and it holds through a full year.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix unshown working in maths?
faqs.answer: Usually three or four sessions, because it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap. The work is simple and specific: marked papers in front of both people, line by line, identifying where the markscheme awarded credit for a stated principle, a substitution or a manipulation that the student omitted. Once a student sees that a correct answer with no visible method collects a fraction of the available marks, the behaviour changes quickly. This is the largest avoidable loss in Analysis at both levels and the fastest to address.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both maths routes if we have two children?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but two specialists usually serve a household better. Analysis and Applications diverge enough in content and emphasis that recent experience of one does not guarantee fluency in the other, particularly at Higher Level where the third papers differ substantially. Two consecutive online slots with two specialists costs nothing extra because nothing is travelling, and in a household where the children arrive home more than an hour apart the slots fall naturally in sequence anyway.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths specialist cost from this community?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150. In mathematics the match matters more than the band: a tutor who recently taught your child's actual course is better value than a more expensive specialist in the other route.

faqs.question: Which exam session does a Living Legends IB maths candidate sit?
faqs.answer: IB candidates at UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no specific IB examination or results date, because ibo.org returns an error to automated verification and an unsourced date a family plans around is a genuine harm; confirm those with the school's coordinator. For Cambridge qualifications a sibling may be taking, the UAE series are June and November, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November.

faqs.question: How do school holidays help a maths plan in this community?
faqs.answer: They provide the only free daytime hours in a Diploma year, and they fall at useful points relative to internal deadlines. A short intensive block in the winter or spring break, particularly on the exploration or on a calculus foundation that needs rebuilding, converts better than the same number of hours spread across squeezed term-time evenings. Households that travel can keep sessions running from wherever they are, which is a straightforward consequence of lessons being delivered over live video rather than in person.

faqs.question: Will you supply IB maths past papers for practice?
faqs.answer: No. IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are the organisation's copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from material the school has legitimately issued to the student, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty, which in mathematics is straightforward to do well. A provider advertising a paper library has an unresolved copyright problem a family using it would be sharing.

faqs.question: Is an Analysis Higher Level specialist hard to book at short notice?
faqs.answer: It is the tightest mathematics request in this market, and the reason is structural. Higher Level cohorts at individual Dubai schools are often small, so the number of teachers across the whole emirate who have taken Analysis Higher Level through to a final session recently is smaller than the number who teach mathematics. Combined with the contested evening window, short-notice requests can take longer. Where no suitable specialist is free we give a date rather than offering an Applications specialist to an Analysis candidate.

Confirm the route and the level, audit the week honestly, and identify one long window for calculus, Paper 3 and the exploration before you book anything. Then match on recent experience of that exact course. Book a free trial lesson at the hour you actually intend to use, and judge it on whether the tutor can name the loss pattern.

intro.heading: Price a maths tutor the way Dubai prices everything else: by the month
paragraphs: Ask what a maths tutor costs in Dubai and you get an hourly rate, if you get a number at all. Ask a Meydan parent what they can spend and they answer in months, because that is how the household runs. School fees are termly, the nursery is monthly, the car is monthly. An hourly rate is a unit nobody budgets in, and the gap between the two is where families overcommit in September and quietly stop in February.

So this page starts from the monthly figure. In the Dubai market, a weekly one-hour session with a budget tutor lands roughly between AED 240 and 600 a month on Bestimate's own estimates. A mid-tier qualified tutor runs about AED 600 to 1,200 a month on the same basis. A specialist working with a student in an examination year sits around AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Published packages exist too: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions is a real advertised figure, as is AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' numbers, read in October 2026, and they are the market rather than our price list.

What the monthly view exposes is that the hourly rate is rarely the expensive part. The expensive part is buying the wrong number of sessions for the wrong reason. Two sessions a week across two Diploma years, bought in a panic after one bad test, costs more than a house move and usually produces a student who waits to be taught rather than one who works. One well-used session a week for eight months, with marked practice between sessions, costs a third as much and does more. Where families in Meydan waste money is in duration and in diagnosis, not in the rate.

The second thing the monthly view exposes is the Analysis and Approaches versus Applications and Interpretation question, which is a cost question as much as an academic one. A student in the wrong course needs far more hours to reach the same grade, and no hourly rate makes that efficient. Getting the course right, or confirming it is right, is the cheapest intervention available in Diploma maths, and it is a single lesson's work.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online tuition to Meydan over live video, matched on the course the student is sitting rather than on who lives nearby. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. The sections below give the monthly bands with sources, the AA and AI comparison, the paper weightings your child is marked against, and the three specific ways tutoring money gets wasted in this city.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-meydan.programmesIntro: Meydan sits in the middle of a cluster of IB and British-curriculum schools, which means a family's route into Diploma maths varies. These are the three programme contexts that change what a first maths lesson should contain, and each one has a different cost profile over a year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, two maths courses to choose between, and an internal exploration worth a fifth of the grade. Standard Level sits two papers of ninety minutes each, both carrying 40%. Higher Level sits three papers, with Papers 1 and 2 at 30% apiece and the shorter Paper 3 at 20%. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator in Analysis and Approaches, which is the single structural fact that most surprises students arriving from other systems.
programmes.countryNote: In Meydan and along the central corridor, Diploma maths is taught at several schools within a short drive, but the courses offered differ: some run both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels, others only one combination. That constrains the choice before a tutor is ever involved, so the first question in a Meydan maths consultation is always which courses the school actually timetables.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria and includes extended investigation work, which builds the habits the Diploma exploration needs. What it does not build, on its own, is the algebraic speed Paper 1 demands without a calculator. The cheapest maths tutoring a Dubai family ever buys is a short block in Year 10 or 11 that secures algebraic manipulation before Diploma content arrives on top of it.
programmes.countryNote: Several central-corridor schools run MYP and then offer both the Diploma and A Levels at sixteen, so Meydan families face a genuine fork. For maths specifically, the Diploma suits students who want breadth and can carry the exploration; A Level Mathematics suits students who want depth in fewer subjects. Neither is harder in the abstract; they are hard in different places.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme course candidate
programmes.description: Individual Diploma subjects taken for certificates rather than the full Diploma. In maths this route appears when a student needs Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level for an engineering or economics application but cannot carry the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge load alongside it. The maths syllabus, the papers and the exploration are identical to the full-Diploma version, so the tutoring is identical too.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing in Meydan because the corridor sees a steady flow of mid-year arrivals from British, American and Indian systems. What a certificate route means for Ministry of Education equivalency is a question for the ministry's own attestation channel, not for a tutoring service, and we direct parents there rather than guessing on their behalf.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: Maths is the subject on this page, but the spend rarely stays in one subject. A Meydan family paying for Analysis and Approaches support often discovers the same algebra is costing marks in Physics or Economics. These are the courses our tutors cover, and what each one costs in time when maths is the underlying problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The page subject. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes algebraic fluency immediately. Marks are lost in proof, in calculus where the chain rule meets a product, and in trigonometric identities that students recognise but cannot manipulate under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The other Diploma maths course, heavier on statistics, modelling and graphic-display-calculator work. Students who move here from Analysis and Approaches to save effort are often surprised: the content is different rather than lighter, and the calculator skills are examinable.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject where weak maths shows up second. A student who cannot rearrange an equation confidently loses marks in Physics calculation questions that have nothing to do with physics. Fixing the algebra usually moves both grades, which changes the cost arithmetic.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries real quantitative work, and the internal assessment is a set of commentaries on published news articles. Students taking Applications and Interpretation alongside it benefit from shared statistics work rather than two separate tutoring arrangements.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Logarithms in pH calculations and the rearrangement in equilibrium problems are maths problems wearing a chemistry coat. We check for this pattern because it means one tutor can sometimes do the work two were booked for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Taken by a growing number of central-corridor students. The discrete maths and algorithmic reasoning overlap with Analysis and Approaches topics, so a student strong in one tends to find the other less alien than they expected.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A common pairing with Applications and Interpretation. The quantitative tools are modest but the interpretation demands are high, and students who treat the numbers as the whole answer lose the analysis marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Included here because extended-response marks in maths improve when written explanation improves. A student who can justify a method in words scores better on the exploration, which is a fifth of the maths grade.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The TOK exhibition and essay land in the same term as the maths exploration for most Diploma students. Our support is structural rather than content-based: reading the prescribed title, building an argument, finding where marks are awarded.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many non-Arab students in Dubai schools alongside the KHDA-mandated Arabic provision. Oral assessment carries real weight, so preparation is conversational and the session format differs from a maths session.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the costliest decision in Diploma maths
paragraphs: A student in the wrong maths course needs considerably more tutoring to reach the same grade, which makes course choice the highest-leverage spending decision a Meydan family makes. The two Diploma maths courses are not an easy version and a hard version. They are different mathematics with different assessment demands, and the decision should be made on what a student is good at and where they are going, not on which one a cousin found manageable.

Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. It suits students who like manipulation, who can hold a multi-step argument, and who are heading towards engineering, physical sciences, mathematics or competitive economics. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with calculator use expected throughout and a heavier emphasis on interpreting real data. It suits students heading towards business, social sciences, design and many life-science routes.

University expectations are where this gets expensive. Some degree programmes, particularly in engineering and mathematics, specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who discovers that in DP2 cannot switch. Admissions requirements vary by institution and by year, including among UAE universities, so the correct move is to read the stated requirement on the university's own admissions page for the intake year rather than relying on any tutoring website. A single session spent checking that, early, saves more money than any hourly discount.

The cost of getting it wrong is worth quantifying. A student placed in Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level without the algebraic base for it typically needs weekly support across both Diploma years just to stay at a 4, which at mid-tier monthly rates is a four-figure annual commitment producing a grade nobody is happy with. The same student in Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, or in Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, may need a single term of support and then nothing. That is the difference between a choice and an expense, and it is settled in one conversation with the student, the teacher and a marked paper on the table.

sections.heading: The three ways tutoring money gets wasted in Dubai
paragraphs: Having published the prices, the useful next step is saying where the spend fails. In our experience with Dubai families the waste is concentrated in three patterns, and all three are avoidable without spending less per hour. They are the reason two families with identical budgets get different results from the same market.

The first is buying duration instead of diagnosis. A parent panics after a poor test, books two sessions a week open-ended, and nobody ever establishes what is actually losing marks. Eight months later the spend is substantial and the student has become dependent on being talked through problems. The fix costs one lesson: mark the student's own paper with them, question by question, and name the pattern before buying anything.

The second is paying a specialist rate for work a cheaper tutor does equally well, and the reverse. Content recap and homework support genuinely do not need a Diploma specialist. Paper 3 technique, exploration feedback and no-calculator algebra genuinely do. Families often buy these the wrong way round, paying premium rates for homework supervision in DP1 and then economising in the term that actually decides the grade.

The third is the renewal that nobody questions. A block bought for a specific purpose keeps running after the purpose is met, because stopping feels like a risk. The honest version is a defined end date and a review, and a tutor who says the work is done. That conversation is uncomfortable to have and it is the single largest saving available on this page.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: what else a Meydan household is paying
paragraphs: A monthly tutoring figure means little in isolation, so here it is against the rest of the education budget. The anchor is a useful one this year: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For once, the fee line in a Dubai family's budget is flat.

That matters for how tutoring should be judged. With fees held, a family's discretionary education spend is more visible than usual, and the question becomes whether a given monthly tutoring figure is the best use of it. Sometimes it is not. A student whose problem is organisation rather than mathematics may be better served by a study-skills intervention at school than by a specialist maths tutor at the top of the market band.

The table below sets the figures side by side. Fee bands are deliberately described rather than quoted, because Dubai school fees vary enormously by school and KHDA publishes the current figures school by school. The tutoring rows use the market bands from earlier on this page. The point of the comparison is proportion: for most families, effective weekly maths tutoring is a small fraction of a termly fee invoice, and ineffective twice-weekly tutoring across two years is not.

There is one further line families forget to budget for, which is the examination entry cost if a student ever sits a paper as a private candidate rather than through their school. That is unusual in the Diploma and more common with IGCSE resits, but it belongs in the same column of the household spreadsheet, and the figure comes from the examination centre rather than from a tutor. Ask the school first, because a student enrolled at an IB World School sits through the school and the entry is part of the fee structure already paid.

sections.heading: What the money buys at each level, in actual teaching behaviour
paragraphs: Price bands are abstract until you know what changes inside the lesson. The difference between a tutor at AED 60 an hour and one at AED 300 is not enthusiasm or politeness. It is a set of specific behaviours that only come from having taught the course to examination standard several times, and they are observable in a single trial lesson if you know what to listen for.

A budget tutor will typically explain a question the student is stuck on, correctly, and move to the next one. That is useful and it is not nothing. What it does not include is any model of why this student got stuck, whether the same gap will reappear in Paper 2, or how the mark scheme would treat the working. The session is reactive: the homework sets the agenda.

A specialist works the other way round. They arrive having looked at the student's marked work, they name the pattern, and they choose what the session covers even if it is not what the homework is about. They talk about method marks. They stop a student mid-question to ask what they would write if they could not finish. They set practice that targets the gap rather than practice that covers the chapter. That is what the extra AED 150 an hour pays for, and in DP2 it is worth it.

You can test for this in the free trial lesson. Ask the tutor afterwards what is costing your child marks and listen to how specific the answer is. 'They need to practise more' is a budget answer. 'They are losing method marks in calculus because they stop showing working once they can see the answer' is what you are paying a specialist for.

sections.heading: The Diploma maths year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Spending decisions make more sense against a calendar. UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and planning backwards from it shows where the money should sit. The table below counts back through the milestones that matter for maths, naming who sets each one, because families routinely assume the IB sets every deadline when the school sets most of the ones that actually bite.

Two cautions. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, including the exploration deadlines, which are the ones that move. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one. And treat an internal deadline as firm the moment it is announced, because schools do pull them forward.

Read for cost, the calendar says something clear. The cheap, high-value window is early DP1, when algebraic foundations are still fixable in a short block and the exploration topic has not yet been chosen badly. The expensive window is the eight to twelve weeks after the DP2 mock, when the work is remedial and the clock is short. Families who spend in the first window usually spend less in the second, and families who spend in neither spend the most of all, because a resit or a retaken year dwarfs any tutoring figure on this page.

There is a second reason to work from the calendar rather than from the school's weekly homework. Diploma maths does not exist on its own in a student's week. The exploration deadline tends to sit near the Extended Essay deadline and near at least one other subject's internal assessment, so the weeks when maths needs the most attention are the weeks when the student has the least to give. Knowing that in advance lets you move the intensive block earlier rather than fighting for evenings that are already committed. Your coordinator can tell you where those collisions fall for your child's cohort, and it is worth asking in DP1 rather than discovering it in DP2.
