sections.heading: KHDA, the corridor's schools, and why the fee freeze matters here
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. It inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the results school by school. For a Meydan parent, those reports are the most useful free document in the market, and they are more useful read in sections than in headlines.

A school's overall band is an average across phases and subjects. A strong secondary mathematics department can sit inside a school rated Good, and a weak one inside a school rated Outstanding. What matters for this page is the secondary mathematics commentary and the attainment and progress judgements for the relevant phase. Families comparing central-corridor schools should read those parts side by side rather than comparing single words.

The sector is also growing, which affects supply. Dubai's private schools served 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More IB schools eventually means more IB teachers, which is the only thing that genuinely loosens the specialist supply this page keeps returning to.

To be plain about credentials: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or licensed by any UAE education authority, and does not claim to be. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence for training institutes with premises in Dubai. Any service advertising KHDA-approved tutors is describing something else or saying something untrue, and that is worth testing before paying anyone anything.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and the maths exploration
paragraphs: The exploration carries 20% of the maths grade and it is where tutoring most often crosses a line. At least one operator ranking for Dubai IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a pricing option, it is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the Diploma, not on the website that took the payment.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may explain the assessment criteria. They may question a topic until it carries enough mathematics to reach the top bands rather than reading as a school project. They may check the mathematical processes are at the right level for the course. They may read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin, where the notation is wrong, and where a conclusion outruns the working. They may teach the mathematics the exploration depends on.

What a tutor may not do is choose the topic, supply the mathematics, generate the data, or write or edit the report into its final form. Nor may they hand over a worked example so close to the student's exploration that copying it is the obvious next step. We state these boundaries to the student in the first session, because a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves to know where the line is before they are standing on it. The same applies to the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay, and we do not reproduce or supply IB past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we link to the official source instead.

sections.heading: Starting from Meydan, and what we do when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first step costs nothing and takes two minutes. Tell us the course, the level, the mock grade and the topics your child names as weak, and tell us what time the school day ends, because from Meydan that varies by school and it sets the window a session can occupy. Then say what you can spend monthly. A tutoring service that does not ask that is going to recommend more sessions than you need.

We propose a tutor and run a free trial lesson. The trial is a diagnosis. The tutor should finish it able to name what is costing marks, in the specific terms described earlier on this page, and you should finish it knowing whether your child will talk to this person weekly for two terms. If not, say so and we propose someone else. A match the student tolerates rather than respects does not survive to February.

The honest part, which this market generally omits: Diploma maths specialists are a limited resource, particularly for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and for Paper 3 work. When the right tutor is not free at the time you want, we say so. The resolution is usually a different slot, occasionally a short wait, and sometimes a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course to Gulf Standard Time. What we will not do is put a general maths tutor in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 student because the diary was tidier that way, and then charge the specialist rate for it.

process.title: Say the course and the monthly budget
process.description: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different jobs, and Higher Level Paper 3 is a third one. Tell us which, plus the mock grade and what you can spend a month. The budget shapes the recommendation honestly rather than after the fact.

process.title: We match on the course, not the commute
process.description: Lessons are online, so the shortlist is every maths specialist available rather than those who will drive to Meydan at 4pm. We tell you who the tutor is and why they fit this gap before anything is booked, and the travel premium in the market bands above never enters the price.

process.title: Free trial lesson as diagnosis
process.description: The first session costs nothing and its job is to find the problem. Ask the tutor afterwards what is costing your child marks. A specific answer about method marks or notation is what you are looking for; a general answer about practising more is not worth a specialist rate.

process.title: Agree a number of sessions and an end date
process.description: Blocks have a purpose and a finish. We agree how many sessions, for what, and when the review happens, so the monthly figure is a decision rather than a subscription nobody revisits. If the work is done early, we say so.

process.title: Practice between sessions, marked before the next
process.description: Each session ends with named practice, usually past-paper questions on the topic just covered, and the next session starts with it marked. This is the part that converts a monthly payment into a grade change, and it is also the part students skip when nobody checks.

process.title: Review against the calendar
process.description: Every few weeks the plan is checked against the Diploma year: exploration deadline, mock, final revision block. Intensity rises for a defined block before the examination session and falls afterwards, rather than sitting flat for two years at the same cost.

whyPoints.title: Monthly figures, not hourly ones
whyPoints.description: We publish the Dubai market in the unit families budget in, with each band attributed and dated. Most pages in this market publish nothing, and the two that publish anything quote US dollars. A monthly number is the one you can actually decide against.

whyPoints.title: The course question answered first
whyPoints.description: A student in the wrong maths course needs far more hours for the same grade, so the first lesson checks the fit against where they are heading. That single check saves more money than any discount, and it is work most tutoring arrangements never do.

whyPoints.title: Specialist hours where they count
whyPoints.description: Paper 3, no-calculator algebra and exploration feedback need a specialist. Homework supervision does not. We will tell you which you are buying, including when the cheaper option is genuinely sufficient for the term you are in.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Every block has a stated purpose and a review date. We would rather tell you the work is done than let a monthly payment run because stopping feels risky. That is the largest saving available in this market and nobody advertises it.

whyPoints.title: The exploration line stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the maths grade is the student's own work. We tell the student in the first session what we will and will not do with it: teaching, questioning and written feedback on their own draft, never the topic, the mathematics or the text.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed credentials
whyPoints.description: We explain what KHDA does and link to its own material. We do not describe IB Gram or any tutor as KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, because none of that is true of us, and in this market that phrase is the commonest untruth on a pricing page.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor in Meydan cost per month rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Converting the Dubai market into monthly figures: a weekly hour with a budget tutor runs roughly AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's own estimates, a mid-tier qualified tutor about AED 600 to 1,200, and a specialist working with a student in an examination year around AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Advertised packages exist at AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' published figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, which follow a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Where do Dubai families most often waste money on maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three places. First, buying duration before diagnosis: open-ended twice-weekly sessions booked after one bad test, with nobody ever naming what is losing marks. Second, paying specialist rates for homework supervision in DP1 and then economising in DP2, which is the reverse of what the calendar wants. Third, letting a block renew because stopping feels risky, long after its purpose was met. None of these is solved by finding a cheaper hourly rate. All three are solved by a diagnostic first lesson and an agreed end date.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course costs a Meydan family less in tutoring over two years?
faqs.answer: It is different rather than simply harder, and treating it as the harder one leads students into the wrong course. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator, which exposes manipulation skill immediately. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with calculator use expected throughout and examinable as a skill. Students who move to Applications and Interpretation expecting less work are often surprised. Choose on what the student is good at and on what their intended degree requires, then verify that requirement on the university's own admissions page.

faqs.question: How are the IB maths papers weighted at Standard and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 carry 40% each and the internal exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30% each, the shorter Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration carries 20%. The practical consequence is that Higher Level students have an entire additional paper with its own style of extended problem, which needs its own sessions rather than being treated as more of Paper 2. Confirm the current structure with your child's teacher, since course documents are revised periodically.

faqs.question: Does an in-home maths tutor coming to Meydan cost much more?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the premium is visible in the market bands. In-home one-to-one in Dubai runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure includes travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Advertised monthly packages show the same gap: around AED 799 a month online against AED 1,599 to 1,799 in-home. For a Meydan address in the middle of the corridor the travel component is moderate rather than extreme, but it buys logistics, not teaching. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions a month does a Diploma maths student actually need?
faqs.answer: Four, in most cases, meaning one a week. One well-used session with marked practice in between repairs topic gaps steadily and leaves time for five other subjects. Eight to twelve sessions a month make sense for a defined block: six to ten weeks before the examination session, or a short period around the exploration. Open-ended twice-weekly tutoring across both Diploma years tends to produce a student who waits to be taught, and it is also the most expensive version of the least effective plan.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the IB maths exploration without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is specific. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria, question a topic until it carries enough mathematics for the higher bands, check the mathematical processes suit the course, teach the mathematics involved, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the mathematics, generate data, or write or edit the report into its final form. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: My child cannot do Paper 1 without a calculator. Is that a content problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. It is almost always algebraic fluency, which is a speed and accuracy problem rather than a knowledge one. A student who understands differentiation perfectly but takes ninety seconds to simplify a fraction will run out of time on a paper where everyone else is thinking about the mathematics. The remedy is unglamorous and reliable: short, frequent no-calculator drill, every session, for a term. It is the cheapest grade movement available in Analysis and Approaches and the one students resist most strongly.

faqs.question: Which schools near Meydan teach IB Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: Several, with different course combinations, which is why the syllabus has to be asked about rather than assumed. The Meydan and Nad Al Sheba area includes established IB provision as well as British-curriculum schools running A Levels, and Sobha Hartland nearby has two well-known schools. Some schools timetable both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at both levels; others offer a narrower set, which constrains a student's choice before any tutor is involved. KHDA publishes current curricula for every Dubai private school on its own site, and that is where to confirm.

faqs.question: Are school fees in Dubai going up for 2026-27, and does that affect tutoring budgets?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For families that means the largest education line in the budget is flat this year, which makes discretionary spending such as tutoring more visible. It is a good year to judge a monthly tutoring figure on what it actually achieves rather than absorbing it into a general rise.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Dubai need a licence, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: They need a permit and it is free. MoHRE issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so any specific figure you see quoted is unverified.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class cheaper than one-to-one, and is it worth it?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per head, certainly, and sometimes worth it. A group class works when several students share the same gap and the pace suits all of them, which is most plausible for a single topic rather than for general Diploma maths. It works poorly when the problem is personal: a student losing method marks through their own particular habit will not have that noticed in a group of six. For a Meydan family the honest test is whether you can name the gap. If you can, a group class on that topic may be efficient.

faqs.question: We are starting tutoring in DP2 after a poor mock. Is it too late to be worth the money?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change. With eight to twelve weeks of usable time, the first session should be spent marking the mock with the student question by question, and the plan that follows should drop topics deliberately rather than attempting everything. That is uncomfortable and it is the correct use of the money. Expect a higher monthly figure for a short, defined block rather than a modest one spread thin. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or when the family travels?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a practical advantage of online delivery rather than a courtesy. During Ramadan sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, which is straightforward when there is no journey to renegotiate at either end. When a family travels, the lesson follows the student rather than the address, so two weeks away does not cost two weeks of maths. Agree in advance which time zone the session is pinned to, so a student abroad is not sitting a maths lesson at six in the morning.

faqs.question: What does the extra money actually buy in a lesson at the specialist rate?
faqs.answer: Specific behaviour you can observe. A specialist arrives having looked at the student's marked work, names the pattern, and chooses what the session covers even when that is not what the homework is about. They talk about method marks. They stop a student mid-question to ask what they would write if they could not finish. They set practice aimed at the gap rather than at the chapter. Test for it after the free trial lesson by asking what is costing your child marks, and judge how specific the answer is.

faqs.question: What happens if the maths specialist we want is fully booked?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting quietly. Diploma maths capacity is genuinely limited, particularly for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and for Paper 3 work. The options are a different slot, a short wait, or a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same course to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a general maths tutor in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 student and charge the specialist rate for it. If none of the alternatives suits, you have lost nothing, because the trial lesson is free and comes first.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-meydan.closingHeading: Get the monthly figure before you get the tutor
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-meydan.closingBody: Most families in Meydan decide on a maths tutor before they have worked out what they are spending across a term or what the spend is meant to achieve. Reverse the order. Tell us the course, the level, the mock grade and the monthly figure you are comfortable with, and we will say what that buys, how many sessions it implies and when the block should end. Then we run a trial lesson at no cost, and you judge the diagnosis before anything is booked. If the tutor cannot name what is costing marks, do not buy the block.

intro.heading: The next suburb over has the same answer
paragraphs: There is a particular search pattern in eastern Dubai and it is worth naming, because it wastes weeks. A parent in Mirdif looks for an IB maths tutor nearby, finds thin results, and concludes the problem is Mirdif. So they search Al Mizhar, then Al Warqa, then Al Khawaneej, then Al Rashidiya, widening the circle in the belief that somewhere in the eastern suburbs there is a Diploma mathematician who has simply not been found yet. There usually is not, and the reason has nothing to do with these neighbourhoods being underserved.

Diploma mathematics teachers are scarce everywhere. Dubai's private-school market in 2024-25 enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum taking 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and the International Baccalaureate 7%. Tutor supply follows enrolment, so IB-trained mathematicians are a small subset of a large pool in every part of the city - including the western school belt that eastern-suburb families sometimes imagine is better stocked. Mirdif is not short of maths teachers. It is short of Diploma maths teachers, like everywhere else.

What does vary between Mirdif and its neighbours is the geography, and it varies in a direction that makes the search worse rather than better. Mirdif sits in the eastern suburbs with Al Mizhar, Al Khawaneej, Al Warqa, Al Rashidiya and Nad Al Hamar around it, Dubai Festival City and International City to the south, and Dubai Silicon Oasis and Dubai International Academic City beyond that. It is a long way from the Jumeirah and Al Barsha school belt, which is where in-home tutors driving across the city are coming from - and that drive is priced into every in-home quote a Mirdif villa receives.

So the comparison that actually helps is not Mirdif against Al Mizhar. It is distance-based hiring against subject-based hiring. Once you stop filtering by neighbourhood, the pool becomes every Diploma maths specialist working on Gulf Standard Time, and the question becomes which course your child is taking rather than who happens to live near the Mirdif City Centre. That is a better question, and this page is built around it.

The course question is the expensive one. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are different courses, not difficulty tiers - Analysis is algebra, calculus and proof; Applications is modelling and statistics with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes generally expect Analysis, often at Higher Level. A student on the wrong route may find courses closed that nobody mentioned in Year 11, and that costs more than any amount of tuition.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India. For a Mirdif, Al Mizhar or Al Warqa family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is exactly how the eastern suburbs stop being a disadvantage.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: A Mirdif maths enquiry needs placing in the continuum first, because the same hour does very different work at each stage - and costs differently too.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one mathematics course from four options: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level. All four include the exploration, an independent piece of mathematics typically 12 to 20 pages, assessed against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Higher Level candidates also sit Paper 3.
programmes.countryNote: The bulk of Mirdif Diploma maths enquiries, usually triggered by the first substantial Year 12 assessment. The pattern is the same whether the family lives in Mirdif, Al Mizhar or Al Warqa: a student with a strong IGCSE grade meets Higher Level and finds that recognising question types no longer earns the marks.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Standard and Extended pathways assessed against four criteria scored 0-8: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is the one that matters for later, because generalising a rule and justifying it is exactly what the Diploma exploration will assess under a different name.
programmes.countryNote: The cheapest point in the pathway to build the skill the Diploma will charge specialist rates for later. Uptown International School runs the full IB continuum in Mirdif itself, which means some eastern-suburb families have MYP provision on their doorstep and a Diploma mathematics problem two years ahead of them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: No external assessment and no marks, reporting against conceptual understanding. What it builds is number sense and the habit of explaining why a method works, which every later criterion depends on. Fluency gaps that look harmless at this stage become the rearrangement failures that cost Higher Level marks.
programmes.countryNote: Mirdif and the eastern suburbs have substantial primary provision across several curricula, and families moving between them often find the adjustment is about justification rather than content level. That is a cheap thing to fix early and an expensive one to fix in Year 12.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme mathematics
programmes.description: CP students take at least two Diploma courses, which may include a mathematics course, assessed exactly as a Diploma student's would be with the same papers and the same exploration. Offered by a small number of UAE schools and often confused with the Diploma in post-16 conversations about workload and cost.
programmes.countryNote: Worth distinguishing because a CP certificate is not the Diploma. For any UAE university destination, check the Ministry of Education equivalency position directly with the authority - no IB points threshold appears in the sourced guidance, so no figure should be taken from a secondary source.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: IB mathematics is four courses rather than one. Below, the components a Mirdif family is actually buying help with, and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof at depth, with three papers including Paper 3. The scarcest teaching in Dubai and the most consequential. Marks go on unjustified steps, missing domains, and induction attempted without the inductive step written out properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same character of mathematics at reduced depth, two papers. Students lose marks on calculus technique and on questions that look familiar and are not. Assuming SL is simply HL with fewer topics misreads the assessment emphasis as well as the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, matrices and graph theory with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout, plus Paper 3. Chosen as the lighter route and frequently a surprise: the HL statistics content is demanding and modelling questions punish a number produced without interpretation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics at reduced depth, two papers. Marks go on reporting a regression coefficient without interpreting it in context, choosing a statistical test the data cannot support, and trusting calculator output without checking plausibility.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: Internally assessed, typically 12 to 20 pages, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Personal engagement and reflection are where marks are most often left on the table, because they reward something that is not mathematical skill.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: A pair of extended structured investigations that build across many parts, so an early error propagates. It cannot be topic-spotted and rewards stamina and structure. The single component where a non-specialist is least able to substitute, at any price.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency as a prerequisite
subjects.description: Rearrangement, indices, surds and multi-step manipulation under time. The most common real problem in Diploma mathematics and the one least often diagnosed, because it presents as a content problem on a report and as an arithmetic problem on a script.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator fluency
subjects.levels: Essential in AI, needed in AA
subjects.description: Assumed rather than taught in most classrooms and more consequential in Applications and Interpretation, where it is integral. Worth one or two sessions rather than a block, which makes it an easy place to overspend if somebody builds a term around it.

subjects.name: Statistical test selection
subjects.description: Choosing a test the data can actually support, and knowing its assumptions. Transfers well beyond mathematics, because explorations and internal assessments in sciences and individuals and societies frequently rest on the same decision.

subjects.name: Proof and mathematical argument
subjects.description: Induction, contradiction and direct proof, marked on the structure of the argument rather than on arriving at the result. Students lose whole questions by asserting what they were asked to show, and content revision never touches it.

subjects.name: MYP investigating patterns
subjects.description: Find a pattern, generalise it, justify the generalisation. Most lost marks are in the justification, which students treat as optional - and it is the exploration skill, two to four years early and at a lower rate tier.

subjects.name: IGCSE Extended or Higher maths
subjects.description: The foundation the Diploma assumes. A student who reached a strong grade by recognising question types rather than understanding methods meets a wall in the first Diploma term, and the fix is foundation work rather than Higher Level teaching.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mirdif.regionsIntro: The eastern suburbs are the comparison this page is about. Here is what each one actually offers a family looking for Diploma mathematics.

regions.name: Mirdif
regions.note: Villa and low-rise family suburb around Mirdif City Centre and Uptown Mirdif, with schools inside the neighbourhood across several curricula including an IB continuum school. A long way from the western school belt.

regions.name: Al Mizhar
regions.note: Directly north-east of Mirdif, villa territory with its own school provision. The same tutor pool quotes here, with the same curriculum profile and the same thin Diploma maths supply.

regions.name: Al Warqa

sections.heading: Mirdif, Al Mizhar, Al Warqa: what actually differs
paragraphs: Set the four suburbs side by side and the comparison is clarifying rather than discouraging. Housing stock differs. School provision differs a little - Mirdif has schools inside the neighbourhood across several curricula, including IB provision, while Al Khawaneej is lower-density and further out. Drive times into the Jumeirah and Al Barsha belt differ by fifteen or twenty minutes. What does not differ, in any way a Diploma family would notice, is the supply of people who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.

That is because specialist supply is a city-wide variable rather than a neighbourhood one. The relevant number is not how many teachers live near you but how many teachers anywhere in Dubai have taught the specific course and level your child is sitting. With the IB at 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment and four distinct maths courses inside that, the population of people who have taught Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level and marked explorations in it is small in absolute terms across the whole emirate.

Where the eastern suburbs genuinely are disadvantaged is in-home pricing, and the mechanism is simple. In-home quotes include travel, and the further a tutor has to come, the higher the quote or the fewer the available tutors. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. From Al Khawaneej or Al Mizhar, with the specialist pool concentrated in the west, that premium is at the top of the band rather than the bottom.

Which inverts the usual conclusion. Searching the next suburb over makes the problem worse, because each additional kilometre adds to the quote without adding to the expertise. sections.heading: The decision that outweighs every tutoring choice: AA or AI
paragraphs: Before an hour is bought, the course should be examined, because getting it wrong costs more than two years of tuition. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, functions, calculus and proof route. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the modelling and statistics route, with a graphical display calculator assumed throughout and Higher Level content including matrices and graph theory. They are separate courses with separate papers and separate consequences for university entry.

The belief that Applications is the easier option causes most of the harm. It is a different mathematics, not a lighter one, and its Higher Level statistics content defeats plenty of students who chose it to avoid calculus. Meanwhile competitive engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics programmes expect Analysis, typically at Higher Level, so a student who took Applications to protect a grade may have closed the degree the grade was being protected for.

The opposite error is equally expensive. A student heading for design, business, some health systems or the social sciences who takes Analysis Higher Level for appearances can spend two years fighting content they will never use while their other five subjects suffer. The right question is not which is harder but which is correct for the destination - and the only source worth acting on is each target university's own published admissions page, not general guidance including this page's.

Where a tutor genuinely adds value here is diagnosis rather than opinion. Looking at a marked piece of algebra done under time pressure and saying whether Analysis Higher Level is realistic for this student, inside the hours a full Diploma leaves them, is evidence-based advice. Get it in Year 11. Changing route in Year 12 is permitted at some schools and painful at all of them, and from Mirdif it is exactly as available as from anywhere else, because it is a conversation with the school rather than a journey.

sections.heading: The exploration, and why it is the cheapest thing to get right
paragraphs: Ask any prospective maths tutor to name the exploration criteria and what each is worth. It takes thirty seconds and it is the most reliable test available, because across the entire competitor corpus researched for this market not one page names a single IB assessment criterion. A teacher who has marked explorations answers immediately; one who has not will talk about originality and presentation in general terms.

The criteria cover presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Strong mathematicians already score on the last. The marks left on the table are usually in personal engagement and reflection, which reward something that is not mathematical skill at all - a technically impressive exploration with no evidenced engagement and a concluding paragraph that merely restates the result loses bands that a weaker piece of mathematics would have kept.

The timing is the financial point. The exploration is internally assessed, worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and completed and marked months before the written papers. The band is banked: it travels into the session and strong paper performance does not retrieve it. So a short block while the question is still being chosen buys a different outcome from the same money spent on a finished draft - and the second purchase is usually the larger one, bought in a panic.

The boundary is absolute and it protects your child rather than any provider. A tutor may explain each criterion, interrogate the question until the student can defend it in a sentence, teach the mathematics or the statistical test required, mark practice work, and give written questions and comments on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to demonstrate register, supply data or a question, or edit to completion. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the malpractice consequence falls on the student.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges, and what the eastern-suburb premium adds
paragraphs: Every figure here carries the name of whoever published it, because three of six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars. Tutopiya advertises from roughly AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted around AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Named IB specialists run AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase at AED 270, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table showing 200-450+ and BartyED publishing AED 650.

The in-home column is where Mirdif's geography bites. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 and independent home tutors at up to AED 500. Those are city-wide ranges, and where a household sits inside them is largely a function of distance from the tutor. From the eastern suburbs, with specialist supply concentrated in the west, an in-home Diploma maths quote is realistically at the upper end - and the pool willing to make that drive at five in the afternoon is small before any question of subject expertise arises.

Monthly comparisons make the trade clearer than hourly ones. Published packages run about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. For Higher Level mathematics in the exam year, plan on the top band if a specialist is genuinely involved.

Two honesty notes. Examiner framing often justifies the top of this range: current examiner status should be evidenced before it is charged for, and it must never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. And no IB Gram price appears on this page, because what a block costs depends on level, component and weeks remaining - the free trial lesson and the consultation after it are where a real figure is given. Household context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Where the marks sit: components by level
paragraphs: Spending should follow the mark allocation rather than the anxiety. All four IB maths courses carry the internally assessed exploration alongside externally marked papers, with Higher Level candidates sitting three papers where Standard Level candidates sit two. The exploration is worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and it is finished and marked months before the written session.

Higher Level Paper 3 deserves its own budget line. It is a pair of extended investigative questions that build across many parts, so an early error propagates through everything that follows, and it cannot be prepared by topic-spotting. It rewards mathematical stamina and structure, trained by working full investigations under time and then dissecting where the chain broke. That is several sessions rather than a mention inside general revision.

Underneath both sits algebraic fluency, which the courses assume rather than teach. This is the most common real problem in Diploma mathematics and it has a signature on a marked script: the method is right, the concept is understood, and the question is abandoned two lines in or finished with a wrong value because a sign flipped. No amount of Higher Level teaching fixes it, which is why families can spend a term at specialist rates and see the same marks.

Confirm the current weightings for your child's course and level with the school or the subject guide rather than with any summary, including this one, because the IB revises assessment structures between cycles and the school holds the version your child is assessed against. sections.heading: Why a long school run makes the slot matter more, not less
paragraphs: The eastern suburbs have one scheduling characteristic that genuinely differs from the western belt, and it works in favour of video delivery. Mirdif, Al Mizhar and Al Warqa children often attend schools inside the suburbs - which can mean a short run - or travel to Festival City, Garhoud, Silicon Oasis or further west, which can mean a long one. Households with two children frequently have both patterns at once, and two different arrival times.

A tutor who travels can serve one arrival time. A session set against the other means a student waiting an hour or a tutor waiting in a car, and both get resented by half-term. The practical fix is to set each slot against the actual arrival on a normal term-time day - timetabled finish, plus bus loop, plus the twenty minutes a teenager needs to eat and stop being a passenger - and then not renegotiate it weekly.

That arithmetic pushes most Mirdif slots later than parents first assume. A 4pm lesson for a child who walks in at 4.40pm loses its first twenty minutes every week, which across a thirty-week school year is roughly ten hours of tuition paid for and not received. At a mid-market Dubai rate of AED 150-300 an hour, that is the single cheapest improvement available to any tutoring arrangement, and almost nobody makes it deliberately.

Two Dubai-specific points to build in. School days shorten during Ramadan and the afternoon becomes the least productive part of the day, so a post-Iftar slot often works better than the usual hour - and an arrangement that can move survives the month where one that cannot tends not to restart. And over the long summer, a family travelling can keep the weekly hour running on Gulf Standard Time or shift it to another time zone, which is simply not available when somebody has to drive to a villa in Mirdif.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor, and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: Two free checks before the first paid hour. The permit: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anybody.

This check is the one item on the list that does not care where anybody lives, which makes it the right first question for a family that has spent a fortnight searching by neighbourhood. MoHRE titles the service "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing". That page lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and runs the application through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system - no counter to visit, nothing a tutor living in Al Warqa or Nad Al Hamar is any further from than one in Al Barsha. The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Two days and no fee is a low bar, so a tutor still working without one has decided against it.

The second check is the arrangement. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat it as press-reported and verify against current policy, but decline the arrangement where your child's own maths teacher is paid privately, however helpfully it is offered.

And the claims to refuse, which cluster at the top of the maths rate card. No individual tutor in Dubai is KHDA-approved, because that status does not exist for individuals - KHDA regulates schools and issues an Educational Services Permit to training institutes with premises. Nobody holds IB accreditation as a private tutor. Nobody should be described as an IB examiner without evidence of current status, and examiner status must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. No provider should supply IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads; those get referenced and linked. IB Gram holds no regulator or board accreditation and operates no premises in the UAE.

sections.heading: What a useful first month looks like from Mirdif
paragraphs: Four sessions with a shape. The first is diagnosis and nothing is taught in it: the marked paper or the exploration feedback is read together, and the lost marks are sorted into algebraic fluency, course content, exploration criteria and command-term or notation problems. Those are four different problems with four different price tags, and a plan proposed before any marked work has been read is guesswork however confident it sounds.

Sessions two and three attack the named problem on the student's own next piece of work rather than on a generic exercise. For fluency that means drilled rearrangement under time, in short bursts rather than whole lessons, because it improves with frequency. For an exploration it means making personal engagement visible in a piece the student actually cares about. For Paper 3 it means a full investigation worked under time and then dissected.

By session four the evidence has to come from outside the tutoring, because only the school's own marking counts. Your child's school marks the paper and awards the exploration criterion bands, so there are exactly two numbers to watch: the next marked maths paper, and the next criterion band. We do not set an internal test and then grade our own work against it - a provider reporting progress only against its own assessments is reporting on itself, and the admissions office reading this student's application in two years will see the school's grade and the IB's award, never a tutoring company's internal score.

Then a decision gets made rather than a subscription continuing. Some students need a second block. Some need nothing further this term. Some turn out to need a tier or course conversation with the school rather than tutoring, or foundation work at a lower rate tier - and a tutor who says so is reducing your bill. The free trial lesson means the diagnostic session costs nothing, and it works identically whether the family is in Mirdif, Al Mizhar or Al Khawaneej.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free at your hour
paragraphs: Availability transparency is a gap nobody in this market fills, and for Higher Level mathematics it is a real constraint rather than a disclaimer. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people and Paper 3 specialism narrows that further, so before the May session the right person may not have a slot at the hour a Mirdif family needs. Several competitors conceal non-UAE delivery behind a local-looking phone number instead of saying anything.

What happens here instead is a disclosure and a choice. Where the exact match is unavailable at your preferred time, the options are named: a different hour with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date, or an adjacent specialist - an Applications Higher Level teacher taking a statistics-heavy exploration, for instance - who can address the component you need now, with the limits of the match stated so you can judge.

Because delivery is online the specialist may sit outside the UAE, which is stated rather than disguised. Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the eastern-suburb school run, which varies by whether your child attends a school inside Mirdif or travels to Festival City, Silicon Oasis or further west. A family paying specialist rates deserves to know exactly what they are buying and from where.

The free trial lesson converts all of it from a promise into a check. One lesson at no cost, with the marked paper or the exploration draft on screen, and the tutor naming the course, the level and the criteria. Ask them which course your child is on before you tell them. If the fit is wrong, nothing is owed and no block has been bought.

faqs.answer: No, and that is the useful thing to know before spending another fortnight on it. Diploma mathematics teachers are scarce in every Dubai neighbourhood: the IB accounts for 7% of private-school enrolment across the emirate's 227 private schools, and there are four distinct maths courses inside that, so the population who have taught a specific one at a specific level is small city-wide. What changes between the eastern suburbs is the drive time, which pushes in-home quotes up rather than widening the pool. The thing to test for is whether a tutor has taught and marked the course, not whether they live near somewhere mathematical.

faqs.question: How much of the budget should Paper 3 get at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: A dedicated block rather than a mention inside general revision. Paper 3 is a pair of extended structured investigations that build across many parts, so an early error propagates and a familiar-looking topic gives no advantage. It cannot be topic-spotted and it rewards stamina and structure, trained by working full investigations under time and then dissecting where the chain broke. Several sessions, placed before the mock round rather than after it, and with a specialist - this is the component where distance-based hiring fails most completely, because the pool is small city-wide.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a house in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For a Mirdif, Al Mizhar or Al Warqa family, lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the marked paper, the exploration draft and the mark scheme are visible to both sides and the annotated work stays with the student. For the eastern suburbs specifically that is the point rather than a compromise: it is what makes the specialist pool identical to a Jumeirah family's.

faqs.question: What time should a Mirdif maths session start on a school night?
faqs.answer: After the real arrival time on a normal day, not after the timetabled finish. Eastern-suburb school runs vary enormously - a short hop to a school inside Mirdif, or a long westward drive - and households with two children often have both. Work out the timetabled finish, plus the bus loop, plus the twenty minutes a teenager needs to eat and stop being a passenger. A session losing its first twenty minutes weekly discards roughly ten hours of tuition across a thirty-week year, which at AED 150-300 an hour is the cheapest available improvement.

faqs.question: Can a university lecturer or an engineer tutor Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: The mathematics, yes; the assessment, often not. Diploma grades run 1-7, every course carries an internally assessed exploration with criteria published by letter, Higher Level candidates sit a Paper 3 with no equivalent in most other systems, and command terms carry mark-scheme consequences. Someone with deep mathematical knowledge and no exposure to those will teach correct mathematics and miss the marks, which is the part being bought. Ask them to name the exploration criteria; it separates mathematical competence from course experience in under a minute.

faqs.question: Should we pay a premium for a tutor described as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and never for what the title implies. Premium rates in this market reach AED 650, with BartyED publishing that figure, and examiner framing is frequently what justifies it. Current examiner status should be evidenced before it is charged for, and it must never be presented as access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because it is not. Ask what the evidence is and what concretely changes in the lesson. A specialist who has taught and marked your child's exact course at their level is the thing you actually need.

faqs.question: Why does this page give no IB exam or results dates?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified. ibo.org returns an error to automated fetching, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and handing an unverified exam date to a parent who will plan a revision budget around it does real harm. UAE candidates sit the May session, which is a pattern rather than a date. Confirm every specific date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are sourced and used elsewhere on this site with their framing intact.

faqs.question: What happens if the right specialist has no slot at our preferred hour?
faqs.answer: You are told, with options rather than a quiet substitution. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people and Paper 3 specialism narrows the pool further, so the weeks before the May session are tight. The honest alternatives are a different hour with the right specialist, a short wait with an actual date attached, or an adjacent specialist who can cover the component you need now with the limits of the match named. No competitor page researched in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Maths improves with frequency, and frequency is a timetable problem
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions are about who. In maths the more consequential decision is when, and it is the one households in this district almost never make deliberately. Mathematical fluency is built the way physical fitness is built: short, frequent, slightly uncomfortable repetitions. A student who does fifteen minutes of algebra six nights a week will be faster in ten weeks than a student who does ninety minutes every Saturday, and faster is what Paper 1 measures.

That makes the school run relevant in a way it is not for an essay subject. The schools serving this district finish between roughly 2:45pm and 3:30pm. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba is home within twenty minutes; a student travelling from Al Safa, Al Barsha or further west is in afternoon traffic, and the final stretch into a gated community adds to it, so arrival between 3:45pm and 4:15pm is routine. Subtract CAS, sport and the twenty minutes a sixteen-year-old needs to arrive properly, and the usable window is narrow.

Inside that window the hours are not equivalent, and maths is the subject where that matters most. Timed practice and non-calculator algebra need a student who is alert, because both measure speed as much as understanding. A student doing non-calculator drill at half past seven, after a full school day and two hours of other homework, is practising being slow. The exercise is still happening and it is no longer the exercise you paid for.

A near-me search makes this worse rather than better, which is the uncomfortable part. The tutors who answer it are the ones prepared to drive here, and a tutor leaving Al Barsha at four meets exactly the traffic your child just sat in, then the gated access at this end. Arrival between a quarter to five and a quarter past is normal. That pushes maths out of the hour it needs and into the hour it tolerates worst.

IB Gram delivers Diploma maths tuition to Mohammed Bin Rashid City as one-to-one lessons over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the session starts when the student is home and settled rather than when a tutor has cleared the gate. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The sections below set out the timing, what maths work survives which hour, how to build daily practice into a crowded week, and when each assessment component should be worked on.

sections.heading: What maths work survives which hour of the evening
paragraphs: A student's capacity falls across the evening in a predictable way, and maths exposes that more than any other Diploma subject because two of its components measure speed. Matching the kind of maths work to the hour costs nothing and produces more from the same number of sessions, which is why it belongs at the front of a scheduling page rather than as an afterthought.

The best hour is the one beginning twenty to thirty minutes after the student gets home, once they have eaten and stopped. That hour takes timed practice, non-calculator algebra and problem solving, which is to say the work that actually moves Paper 1. It is also the hour an in-home tutor driving from the city's teaching concentrations cannot reach, which is the single clearest practical argument on this page.

The middle of the window takes teaching: a new topic, worked examples, a marked script gone through question by question. Absorbing an explanation is easier than producing work against a clock, so this is where the session content should sit if the slot cannot be early. The last hour takes discussion: an exploration topic, criteria, why a method works. It does not take timed papers, and a tutor who sets one at half past seven has wasted the paper and part of your money.

Beyond eight o'clock, nothing in maths that requires concentration is worth doing, and pushing a student past ten costs sleep and then costs the grade the tutoring was meant to protect. If the only available slot is late, the honest answer is to change the subject in that slot rather than the hour, and to move the maths to a weekend morning where a rested student can do a whole timed paper properly.

sections.heading: Ten minutes a night against ninety minutes a week
paragraphs: This is the claim that most changes a maths plan, so it is worth setting out properly. Algebraic and arithmetic fluency is a motor skill as much as a conceptual one. It responds to repetition spread across days and responds poorly to the same total time delivered in one block, because what is being trained is retrieval speed rather than understanding.

The practical version: a student who does twelve minutes of mixed algebra on six nights has done seventy-two minutes and retrieved the same procedures six separate times. A student who does ninety minutes on a Saturday has done more total time and retrieved once. Ten weeks later the first student is measurably faster on Paper 1 question types, and speed on Paper 1 is marks, because the paper is timed and everybody else is thinking about the mathematics rather than the arithmetic.

This changes what a weekly session is for. It is not the place the practice happens; it is the place the practice is set, checked and corrected. A tutor who spends the hour working through problems with the student has done a pleasant and largely ineffective thing. A tutor who arrives having marked last week's six short pieces, names the pattern in the errors, teaches that pattern, and sets the next six is doing the job the hour exists for.

It also explains why a second weekly session rarely helps in maths and why daily drill does. The constraint is not contact time; it is the number of separate occasions the student retrieves a procedure. In a district where households can afford a second session, this is the single most useful thing to know, because the cheaper option is also the better one and almost nobody sells it that way.

sections.heading: When a maths session can start, school by school
paragraphs: Because maths needs the early window specifically, the timing chain matters more here than for a discursive subject. The table works through it: when the school day ends, how long the journey home takes at that hour, the twenty minutes a student needs to arrive properly, and therefore when timed practice is genuinely possible rather than nominally scheduled.

Read the two right-hand columns together. The online start is the earliest point at which the student is ready. The in-home start adds the tutor's own journey through the same traffic plus the gated access at this end, which in this district is consistently around forty-five minutes. For an essay subject that difference is tolerable. For non-calculator algebra it is the difference between practising speed and practising fatigue.

The bottom row is the one households forget. A CAS commitment, a sport fixture or a music lesson removes the early window entirely on that day, and a maths session pushed to half past six on a Tuesday is not a maths session in any useful sense. The right response is to move the maths to a different evening rather than to accept a later hour, and if no evening is free, to move it to a weekend morning.

Fix the hour before choosing the tutor. In maths more than anywhere else, an excellent tutor in the wrong hour produces an unimproved Paper 1 score and a household that concludes, reasonably and wrongly, that tutoring does not work for their child.

sections.heading: The components across a crowded week
paragraphs: Diploma maths has named components with published weightings, and they want different kinds of time rather than more time. Mapping each to the week is what converts a scheduling page into a plan. Standard Level carries Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 40% each with a 20% exploration; Higher Level carries Papers 1 and 2 at 30% each, Paper 3 at 20% and the exploration at 20%.

Paper 1 wants nightly minutes, especially in Analysis and Approaches where no calculator is permitted. Paper 2 wants weekly work on calculator efficiency and on showing method, which is a session task rather than a drill task. Paper 3, at Higher Level, wants long single sittings and therefore a weekend morning, because it is a structured investigation requiring a student to hold a line of reasoning across many parts.

The exploration wants discussion, which is the one maths component that genuinely fits a late evening slot. That is convenient, because it means exploration work can be placed on an evening that cannot take timed practice, freeing the early window for Paper 1 drill. Households who separate the two this way get both done; households who treat all maths as interchangeable usually get neither done properly.

The table sets out the mapping. One caution: course documents are revised periodically, so confirm the current component structure with your child's teacher rather than relying on this page, and confirm the school's internal exploration deadlines with the Diploma coordinator, because those are the dates that actually constrain the plan.

sections.heading: Mock season, Ramadan and travel in a maths plan
paragraphs: A weekly maths slot that works in October will not survive every week of the year untouched, and a plan that cannot bend gets abandoned rather than adjusted. Three periods reliably disrupt it in this district, and because all three are predictable they can be planned for in advance rather than reacted to in the week.

Mock season comes first. During mocks the evenings belong to the next morning's paper, so a general maths hour competes with revision that is more urgent and usually loses. What should be protected and booked months ahead is the week immediately after results, when there is a marked script to work from. One hour spent going through that script question by question with the student, naming whether the losses are method marks, pacing or content, aims every subsequent hour and every night's drill.

Ramadan is second, and online delivery handles it in a way an in-home arrangement cannot. Sessions commonly move to a post-Iftar slot, which works because no journey has to be renegotiated at either end, and a fasting student is better served later than in the afternoon. The daily drill is worth keeping during Ramadan even when the session moves, because five minutes is sustainable when fifteen is not, and frequency matters more than volume.

Travel is third. Households here travel for extended periods, and an online session follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight away need not cost a fortnight of maths. The thing to settle in advance is which time zone the session is pinned to. Drill travels better than sessions do: a student can keep the nightly minutes going anywhere, and that is the part of the plan that was doing most of the work.

sections.heading: Counted backwards from the May session, in usable weeks
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May examination session, and for a scheduling page the useful way to count backwards is in weeks the evenings can actually absorb. Remove the mock fortnight, the internal assessment deadline weeks, the final fortnight when nothing new sticks, and any holiday the family is travelling through, and the number of usable weeks is smaller and earlier than most households assume.

Two cautions. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on these pages. The IB holds those and your child's Diploma coordinator holds the school's internal versions, including the exploration deadlines, which are the ones that genuinely constrain an evening. Confirm every date with the coordinator rather than with a tutoring website, including this one, and treat an internal deadline as firm from the moment it is announced.

Read for maths specifically, the calendar produces a clear sequence. Start the nightly drill as early in DP1 as possible, because fluency takes months and cannot be compressed. Place the exploration discussion before the topic is fixed. Put Paper 3 work into weekend mornings in the first half of DP2. Save whole timed papers for the final six to ten weeks, when there is enough course covered for a whole paper to be meaningful.

The pattern that fails is the common one: no daily practice for two years, then an intensive block in the final term aimed at coverage. By then the pacing problem is structural and the only honest response is to abandon some topics and protect the ones that can still be secured. That works, and it produces a worse result than ten minutes a night would have done for free.
