sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and the free periods that are not free
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspection on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. For a household here the secondary mathematics commentary inside a report is worth more than the headline band, and it is a free second opinion on whether a weak grade reflects the student or the department.

The scheduling fact that matters is the mandatory UAE subjects, which run alongside the Diploma rather than instead of it. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

Instructional time for those subjects is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least twenty-five minutes. The effect on a Diploma student is fewer genuinely free periods in the school day, which means the nightly maths drill this page recommends has to be fitted into an evening that is already carrying more than a parent assumes.

That is an argument for ten minutes rather than thirty. A nightly commitment that is small enough to survive a bad day survives; one that is ambitious enough to feel like a second homework gets dropped in week three. On credentials, plainly: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved or IB accredited, and does not claim to be, since a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: The exploration: 20% of the grade a tutor may never write
paragraphs: The exploration carries a fifth of the maths grade and sits in a document the student controls entirely, which makes it both the highest-return component to support and the place tutoring most often goes wrong. At least one operator ranking for UAE IB queries sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the student, who can lose the Diploma.

What a tutor legitimately does is substantial. They may explain the criteria in the language the examiner uses. They may push a topic until it carries mathematics at the right level for the course rather than reading as a school project. They may warn that a planned approach will not generate enough mathematics to assess. They may teach the mathematics the exploration depends on, and they may read a draft the student has written and say where the reasoning is thin, where the notation is wrong and where a conclusion outruns the working.

What a tutor may not do is choose the topic, supply the mathematics, generate the data, or write or edit the report into its final form, nor hand over a worked example close enough to the student's own topic that copying becomes the obvious step. We state this to the student in the first session, not in small print, because a sixteen-year-old under deadline pressure deserves to know where the line is before they are standing on it.

There is a scheduling point here too. The decisive exploration session is the one before the topic is chosen, and it costs almost nothing in time. Leaving exploration support until the draft is due means the only honest help available is process advice, delivered in a week that is already full. Protect the deadline weeks and place the conversation early. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what we ask before proposing an hour
paragraphs: Three questions decide the slot and we ask them before proposing anyone. Which school your child attends and what time the day ends. What fixed commitments sit in the week, including CAS, sport and music. And which evening, in your judgement, your child could do timed work in rather than merely sit through. Parents answer the third accurately more often than this market assumes.

Then the course and level, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation and Higher or Standard, the latest grade, the teacher's last comment quoted rather than summarised, and a photograph of one marked paper. The script is the most useful item: blank later parts suggest pacing or Paper 3 strategy, right answers with no working suggest method marks, slow early arithmetic suggests the nightly drill has never happened.

We run the free trial lesson in the hour you would actually use rather than a convenient showcase slot, because the question is whether your child can do non-calculator work with this person at half past four on a Wednesday. Afterwards, ask what the week's drill will be and how it will be marked. A tutor with no answer to that is proposing to be the practice rather than to set it.

And the honest part. The early-evening Gulf Standard Time hours this district wants fill first, Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with genuine Paper 3 experience is thinner than Standard Level, and the week after mock results is the most contested booking of the year. When what you want is unavailable we say so and offer another hour, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time. We will not put a Standard Level tutor in front of a Higher Level Paper 3 student.

process.title: Tell us the school and the finishing time
process.description: The end of the school day plus the journey home decides whether timed maths practice is possible at all, and it varies by forty minutes or more between schools serving this district. Without it, any proposed hour is a guess.

process.title: Protect the early window for maths
process.description: Timed practice and non-calculator algebra need an alert student. If the only free hour is late, we would rather move maths to another evening or a weekend morning than bill you for practice done badly.

process.title: Set the drill, do not be the drill
process.description: The weekly session diagnoses, teaches and checks; ten to fifteen minutes on five or six nights does the work. Ask any prospective tutor what the week's practice will be and how it will be marked before the next hour.

process.title: Free trial in the real slot
process.description: We run the trial lesson in the hour you intend to book, because a Saturday morning says nothing about whether your child can do non-calculator work at half past four on a Wednesday after a long drive home.

process.title: Place each component where it fits
process.description: Paper 1 in nightly minutes, Paper 2 in the weekly hour, Paper 3 in weekend mornings at Higher Level, the exploration in a later slot that will not take timed work. Separating them is what gets all of them done.

process.title: Book the post-mock script hour months ahead
process.description: The week after mock results is the most valuable maths hour of the year, because for the first time there is marked evidence to aim the drill at. It is also the most contested, so reserve it long before you need it.

whyPoints.title: Frequency treated as the main lever
whyPoints.description: Maths fluency is built in nightly minutes, not weekly hours, so our weekly session exists to set and mark the drill rather than to be the practice. The cheaper pattern is also the more effective one, and almost nobody sells it that way.

whyPoints.title: The hour matched to the work
whyPoints.description: Timed and non-calculator practice in the early window, teaching mid-evening, exploration discussion late, nothing demanding after eight. It costs nothing to arrange and produces more from the same number of sessions.

whyPoints.title: No journey at either end
whyPoints.description: An online session begins when the student is settled rather than when a tutor has cleared afternoon traffic and gated access, which in this district is consistently about forty-five minutes of the best part of the evening.

whyPoints.title: Components placed, not blended
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 wants nightly minutes, Paper 3 wants long weekend sittings, the exploration wants discussion. Treating all maths as interchangeable is why crowded weeks produce no improvement in any of them.

whyPoints.title: Drill small enough to survive a bad day
whyPoints.description: Ten minutes a night survives a full timetable and the mandatory UAE subjects that make it fuller. Thirty minutes a night gets dropped in week three, which is worse than ten because the habit goes with it.

whyPoints.title: A trial at the real hour
whyPoints.description: We run the free trial lesson in the slot you would actually book, because the question is never whether a student can concentrate on a Saturday morning. It is whether they can on a Wednesday at half past four.

faqs.question: Does it really matter what time of day a maths session happens?
faqs.answer: In maths more than any other Diploma subject, yes, because two components measure speed as well as understanding. Timed practice and non-calculator algebra need a student who is alert, and one doing that work at half past seven after a full school day is practising being slow. The best hour begins twenty to thirty minutes after they get home, once they have eaten and stopped. Discussion work such as the exploration survives a later slot perfectly well, which is why the subject and the hour should be chosen together.

faqs.question: Is ten minutes a night really better than a long weekly session?
faqs.answer: For fluency, yes, and it is the most useful thing on this page. Algebraic and arithmetic speed is a retrieval skill: twelve minutes on six nights means six separate retrievals, while ninety minutes on a Saturday means one, despite more total time. Ten weeks later the first student is measurably faster on Paper 1 question types, and speed on a timed paper is marks. The weekly session still matters, but its job is to set, mark and correct the drill rather than to be the practice itself.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session start from this district?
faqs.answer: Online, between about 3:30pm and 4:50pm depending on the school, counting twenty minutes to arrive and eat. A student at a school inside the district or in Nad Al Sheba is ready by four; one travelling from Al Safa or Al Barsha is not ready until nearly half past four. With an in-home tutor add roughly forty-five minutes throughout, because the tutor is in the same school-run traffic and then the gated access at this end, which pushes timed practice out of the hour it needs.

faqs.question: Would a tutor travel to our home for maths?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition over live video throughout the UAE, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. For maths specifically the online structure is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise, because the session starts in the hour when timed practice is still possible. Local in-home arrangements exist here and in-home rates in Dubai run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, which is other providers' published market range rather than ours.

faqs.question: Should we book two maths sessions a week?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The constraint in maths is the number of separate occasions a student retrieves a procedure, not the number of contact hours, so a second session adds less than nightly drill does and costs more. A Diploma student carrying six subjects rarely has two spare hours of attention for one of them either, and the second session tends to become supervised homework. The exception is a bounded pre-examination block of six to ten weeks, where whole timed papers justify the intensity.

faqs.question: My child has CAS on the evening we wanted. What now?
faqs.answer: Move the maths rather than the hour. A session pushed to half past six after a club is not a maths session in any useful sense, because the work that needs doing is the work that needs alertness. Find a different evening with a free early window, or put the maths on a weekend morning where a rested student can sit a whole timed paper properly. Keep the nightly drill running on the club evening regardless; ten minutes survives a busy day in a way an hour does not.

faqs.question: What should the daily practice actually be?
faqs.answer: Mixed short pieces on the procedures the student is slow at, set by the tutor from the previous session and marked before the next one. For Analysis and Approaches that usually means no-calculator work: expanding, factorising, rearranging, fractions, indices, logarithm manipulation. Progress is tracked by timing the same question types across weeks so the student can see it rather than being told about it. Unmarked drill is worse than none, because it makes existing errors faster rather than correcting them.

faqs.question: When does Paper 3 work fit, and does my child need it?
faqs.answer: Only at Higher Level, where it carries a fifth of the grade, and it belongs in weekend mornings rather than weekday evenings because it needs long single sittings. Paper 3 is a structured investigation requiring a student to hold a line of reasoning across many parts, and most lose marks by stopping rather than by error. Six to eight bounded sessions in the first half of DP2 usually changes that. If your child is at Standard Level they do not sit it, and we will say so.

faqs.question: Where does the exploration fit in a full week?
faqs.answer: In the hours that will not take timed practice, which is convenient. Exploration work is discussion-led, so it sits perfectly well late in the evening, which frees the early window for Paper 1 drill. The decisive session is the one before the topic is chosen, and it costs almost nothing in time. Leaving it until the draft is due means the only honest help available is process advice, delivered in a week that already has three other deadlines in it.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a maths plan?
faqs.answer: The session usually moves to a post-Iftar slot, which online delivery makes straightforward because there is no journey to renegotiate at either end, and a fasting student is better served later than in the afternoon. School timings change too, so the chain from the end of the school day needs recalculating rather than assuming. Keep the nightly drill going but shorten it: five minutes is sustainable when fifteen is not, and in maths frequency matters considerably more than volume.

faqs.question: Can maths continue while we are travelling?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the drill travels better than the session does. An online lesson follows the student rather than the address, so a fortnight away need not cost a fortnight of maths, provided you settle in advance which time zone the session is pinned to so nobody is working at six in the morning. The nightly minutes can continue anywhere with a pencil, and since that is the part doing most of the work, a travelling student loses much less than a parent expects.

faqs.question: Why is the week after the mock the most important maths hour of the year?
faqs.answer: Because it is the first point with marked evidence. One hour spent going through the script question by question with the student establishes whether the losses are method marks not shown, pacing on the later questions, non-calculator slowness or genuinely unlearned content. Those are four different problems with four different remedies, and without that hour the plan is guesswork. It is also the most contested booking in this district, so reserve it in October rather than requesting it in February.

faqs.question: Does the school timetable leave room for daily practice?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect, which is an argument for ten minutes rather than thirty. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year and separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them, calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. The effect is fewer free periods, so more work comes home. A drill small enough to survive a bad day is a drill that lasts.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning session better than a weekday evening for maths?
faqs.answer: For whole timed papers and for Paper 3, clearly yes, because a rested student can sustain the concentration a long paper demands and there is no traffic at either end. For building fluency it is worse than nightly drill, because one long sitting means one retrieval. The sensible structure is nightly minutes through the week, a weekday session to set and mark them, and weekend mornings reserved for whole papers in the final six to ten weeks before the session.

faqs.question: What if the early slot we need is already booked?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than selling you a later hour for work that needs an early one. The options are a different evening with a free early window, a weekend morning, or a tutor based outside the UAE working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed as such. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with genuine Paper 3 experience is thinner than Standard Level, so that combination in a popular hour is the hardest to place. The trial lesson is free, so establishing what is possible costs nothing.

faqs.question: What single thing should I send to get a useful recommendation?
faqs.answer: A photograph of one marked maths paper, with the course, the level and the time the school day ends written alongside it. The script shows which component is leaking marks: blank later parts suggest pacing or Paper 3 strategy, right answers with no working suggest method marks, slow hesitant early arithmetic suggests the nightly drill has never happened. The finishing time tells us whether the hour that work needs is actually available, which is the other half of the recommendation.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-ras.closingHeading: Fix the hour, set the nightly minutes, then pick the tutor
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mohammed-bin-ras.closingBody: Diploma maths rewards frequency, so the plan that works is ten minutes a night with one weekly hour to set and mark it, placed early enough in the evening that timed work is still possible. Tell us the school and the finishing time, the fixed commitments, the course and level, and send a photograph of one marked paper. We will propose a tutor, run the trial in the hour you would really use, and tell you what the first week's drill should be. Then book the post-mock script hour early.

intro.heading: Marks are lost in the wording, the notation and the accuracy
paragraphs: There is a particular kind of maths student who understands the material and keeps scoring below what their teacher expects. They can do the differentiation. They know what a binomial distribution is. They can solve the equation. And they lose four or five marks a paper on things that are not mathematics at all: a final answer rounded to the wrong number of figures, a question that said 'hence' answered as though it said 'find', working done entirely on a calculator with nothing written down, a variable used without being defined.

That student does not need more content. They need the conventions, and the conventions are published and finite. The accuracy rule for a final answer is three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise or an exact value is required. A question asking for an exact value will not accept a decimal. 'Hence' obliges the student to use the previous result; 'hence or otherwise' permits a fresh start. Method marks require visible steps. A variable introduced in an answer has to be defined. None of that is mathematics, all of it is assessed, and all of it is learnable in a handful of sessions once somebody has pointed at it.

This page is built around those conventions and around the syllabus structure that sits underneath them. Both IB mathematics courses — Analysis and Approaches, and Applications and Interpretation — are organised into five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Knowing which of the five a paper failed on is a far better starting point than knowing the overall score, and a marked script gives that in about five minutes. The same script, read a second time for conventions alone, gives the other half of the diagnosis, and the two together are what a plan should be built on rather than a sense that maths is going badly.

Motor City's relationship to IB mathematics is worth stating because it shapes the practical side. GEMS Metropole School sits inside the community and runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so there is no Diploma cohort here. Students taking IB mathematics travel out across the Dubailand corridor — to JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School, Greenfield International School — and are home in time for a session from about 18:00.

Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard the student writes on, which matters in mathematics more than in any other subject because the working has to be visible to be marked. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. Sessions run 45 or 60 minutes, to 21:00, and every one is recorded.

Higher Level extends into graph theory and matrices. subjects.name: Topic 1: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem, and at Higher Level proof and complex numbers. Convention errors cluster here: exact values involving surds requested and given as decimals, and logarithm laws applied without stating the base.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Functions
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations and the quadratic family. Marks go on describing a transformation without a vector or a factor, and on domain restrictions omitted when an inverse is stated.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric ratios, identities and equations, radian measure, vectors at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches. Solutions lost by dividing through by a trigonometric factor, and answers given in degrees where the domain was set in radians, are the standing pattern.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, correlation and regression, probability distributions, and at Higher Level more inference. Heavier in Applications and Interpretation. Conclusions that assert causation from correlation, and hypotheses stated loosely, are where the marks go rather than in the computation.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration with applications, extending at Higher Level into implicit differentiation, related rates and differential equations. The recurring error is chain-rule execution inside a product or quotient, and substitution integrals where the substitution is not declared.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.levels: AA: no calculator; AI: calculator permitted
subjects.description: Shorter structured questions across the five topics. On the Analysis and Approaches route the absence of a calculator is the defining feature and the reason exact-value work matters. On Applications and Interpretation the calculator is available and the risk becomes invisible working.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Longer multi-part questions where part (a) sets up part (c), so an early error propagates. The calculator is permitted and is a tool rather than a method; writing intermediate values down is what preserves the method marks when the final figure is wrong.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level only
subjects.description: Two extended investigation questions in one hour, worth 20% of the grade, leading a student through unfamiliar mathematics in scaffolded parts. Reading the whole question before starting is the assessed skill as much as the mathematics is.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: An internally assessed mathematical report worth 20%, marked out of 20 across five criteria. Mathematical communication is where notation conventions pay off directly: defined variables, labelled axes, and mathematical notation rather than calculator syntax.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator skills
subjects.description: Solving, graphing, statistical functions and numerical calculus on the device. Treated as a skill in its own right, because a student who cannot find the right function quickly loses time on Paper 2 even when the mathematics is secure.

sections.heading: The five topic areas, and what each paper does with them
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses are organised into the same five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The content within each differs between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and between Standard and Higher Level, but the structure is shared. That makes the five areas the right unit for diagnosis, because a marked script can be scored against them in a few minutes and the result tells you what to teach.

What each paper does with a topic area differs, and this is the part that makes topic-based revision insufficient on its own. A shorter structured question asks a topic cleanly: one or two skills, three or four marks, minimal context. A longer structured question embeds the same topic in a multi-part problem where part (a) produces something part (c) needs, which means an early slip propagates and the later parts are lost even when the student could do them.

The practical implication is that revision has to include whole questions, not just topics. A student who works through exercises on integration will improve at integration. A student who works through multi-part past questions involving integration will improve at integration, at reading what a question is building towards, and at recovering when part (a) goes wrong — which is three skills rather than one, and the second and third are what separate a 5 from a 7.

At Higher Level the third paper adds another layer, because it presents unfamiliar mathematics in a scaffolded sequence where each part establishes something the next part uses. It is one hour, two questions, and 20% of the grade. The skill it rewards is reading the whole question before starting and recording what each part has established, and it is frequently absent from school mock papers, so a substantial number of students meet the format first in the examination.

sections.heading: Command terms in mathematics, and what each one obliges
paragraphs: IB mathematics command terms are not synonyms. They carry defined obligations, and a student who treats them as interchangeable loses marks on questions they could answer. This is the cheapest single intervention available in the subject: one session to learn the list, a fortnight of annotating the command term before writing, and the mark profile changes across every paper.

The most consequential pair is 'hence' and 'hence or otherwise'. 'Hence' obliges the student to use the result just established; a correct answer reached by an independent method does not earn the marks, because the question was testing whether the student could see the connection. 'Hence or otherwise' explicitly permits a fresh start, so any valid method is credited. Students who do not know the distinction either waste time re-deriving when they were handed the result, or lose marks by ignoring a result they were told to use.

'Show that' requires a derivation ending at the stated result, with each step visible — quoting the answer back is worth nothing. 'Verify' permits substitution into a given result. 'Find' and 'determine' want the value with sufficient working to support it. 'Write down' signals that no working is expected and the answer should be immediate, which is also a hint that a long calculation means the student has misread the question. 'Sketch' wants shape, intercepts and asymptotes rather than plotted accuracy; 'draw' wants accuracy.

'Justify' and 'explain' are where stronger students gain separation, because both require a reason expressed in mathematical language rather than a restatement. And 'state' wants the answer alone. A student who writes a paragraph for a question that said 'state' has lost time they will need for the multi-part question at the end of the paper, which is a cost that does not show up as a lost mark but shows up in the total.

sections.heading: The calculator rules, and what counts as working
paragraphs: On the Analysis and Approaches route, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and Paper 2 with one. On Applications and Interpretation, a calculator is permitted on every paper. Higher Level Paper 3 permits one on both courses. That distribution has two consequences that between them account for a large share of avoidable loss in this subject.

The first is the exact-value demand on Analysis and Approaches Paper 1. Without a calculator, a question can legitimately require a surd, a fraction, a logarithm left in exact form, or a trigonometric value from the standard set. A student who has learned mathematics with a graphing display calculator in their hand may understand the concept perfectly and be unable to produce the exact form, which reads as a content failure and is a fluency failure. It responds to short daily non-calculator practice over six to eight weeks and to nothing else.

The second is invisible working on the calculator-permitted papers. Method marks are awarded for visible steps. A student who computes a chain of operations on the device and writes only the final number has forfeited those marks if the answer is right and everything if it is wrong, because there is nothing on the page for an examiner to credit. The fix is procedural: write the expression being evaluated, then the value, on separate lines. It costs fifteen seconds a question and recovers marks across a whole paper.

There is also a positive calculator skill worth teaching deliberately, which most students acquire by accident. Knowing where the solver, the graph analysis functions, the statistical distributions and the numerical derivative and integral live on the specific model, and reaching them quickly, saves minutes on Paper 2. A student fumbling through menus under time pressure is losing marks to the interface rather than to the mathematics, and twenty minutes of deliberate practice fixes it.

sections.heading: Accuracy and notation: the marks that vanish silently
paragraphs: The accuracy convention is the single most common silent mark loss in IB mathematics. Unless a question specifies otherwise, a final answer is given to three significant figures, or exactly where an exact value is required or arises naturally. Students who write the full calculator output, or who round to two significant figures, or who give a decimal where an exact value was asked for, lose a mark on a question they answered correctly, and because the mathematics was right they often never find out why.

The related rule is about intermediate rounding. Full precision must be carried through intermediate steps and the rounding applied once, at the end. Rounding partway produces a final value outside the accepted tolerance, so the mark goes even though the method was sound. On a multi-part question the effect compounds, because part (c) inherits the imprecision from part (a).

Notation is the second category, and it is assessed directly in the Exploration through the mathematical communication criterion as well as incidentally in the papers. Variables used in an answer have to be defined. Axes on a sketch need labelling. Function notation should be used rather than calculator syntax — and a student who writes calculator output as though it were mathematical notation in their Exploration loses communication marks, which is four of the twenty available.

All of this is teachable in a short block and verifiable afterwards. Mark a student's past paper twice: once for the mathematics and once for the conventions alone. The difference between those two scores is the number of marks sitting on the table, and for a capable student who is underperforming it is routinely four or five marks a paper. That exercise is usually the most persuasive first session a tutor can run, because it turns a vague sense of underachievement into a specific number.

sections.heading: How to mine a past paper properly
paragraphs: Working through past papers is the most commonly recommended and most poorly executed revision activity in this subject. A student who attempts a paper, checks the answers, feels disappointed and moves on has spent two hours confirming what they already suspected. The value is in the marking, and specifically in the gap between what was written and what the published scheme credits.

The method is specific. Attempt the question under time. Then mark it against the scheme line by line, awarding yourself only what the scheme actually credits, which means reading the method marks rather than comparing final answers. Then classify every lost mark into one of four categories: content not known, method not shown, convention breached, or time. That classification is the whole point, because the four categories have completely different remedies and a student who does not separate them cannot act on the result.

Content not known is a teaching problem and the only one that needs new instruction. Method not shown is a habit and takes about two sessions to fix. Convention breached is the accuracy and command-term material above, and takes a block of four to six. Time is a selection and pacing problem that needs full papers under real conditions rather than topic work. Most underperforming students have far less content loss than they assume and far more of the other three.

On materials: IB past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are copyright. We work through them on screen in session, show exactly what the published scheme credits at each stage, and link the official sources so the family can obtain them legitimately. We do not distribute scanned papers or mark schemes, and a tutor offering a folder of them is creating a copyright problem rather than adding value.

paragraphs: A plan built on past papers and mark schemes has a different cost shape from one built on content teaching, and it is worth seeing the difference. Content teaching bills by the topic and expands to fill whatever time is bought. A past-paper plan has a natural length: a conventions block, a number of marked papers, and a timed-paper run before the session. It finishes.

Marking a paper against a published scheme and explaining what the scheme credits requires somebody who has read those schemes. A tutor at the entry band may teach the mathematics competently and be unable to tell a student why a correct answer scored two out of four, which is precisely the information the plan exists to produce. The money is buying scheme familiarity rather than subject knowledge.

sections.heading: Scheduling mathematics from Motor City
paragraphs: Mathematics needs two different session shapes and a Motor City Diploma family can get both. Non-calculator fluency work on the Analysis and Approaches route wants short frequent contact, because exact-value handling and algebraic speed are built by daily practice with regular marking. Marked past papers want a full hour, because a question attempted under time and then marked line by line against the scheme does not compress.

Diploma students from this postcode commute out of the community — GEMS Metropole School runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so there is no local cohort — and are generally home between 16:30 and 17:30. That puts the earliest realistic session at about 18:00. Online, two sessions a week at 18:00 and 20:00 on different evenings is routine, and a 45-minute fluency slot can sit alongside a 60-minute marking session rather than competing with it.

A visiting tutor cannot deliver that pairing. Forty to sixty minutes of travel each way means a two-hour minimum booking and a latest workable start of roughly 18:30, so the week becomes one long appointment rather than two differently shaped ones. The published premium for the visit is AED 30-150 an hour over the equivalent online band, and in mathematics what it buys is presence rather than a shared whiteboard, which is arguably a downgrade: the whiteboard produces a record of the working that both tutor and student can revisit.

Home visits remain the right choice for some students, particularly younger ones who need an adult in the room. IB Gram does not offer them anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so the comparison here is informational rather than persuasive. What we will not do is imply a local presence we lack: no UAE office, no centre, no branch.

sections.heading: Starting, with the Exploration and the honesty line
paragraphs: Send the course, the level, a marked paper and the school's Exploration deadline. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson in which the paper is marked twice — once for the mathematics and once for the conventions — and the difference becomes the starting number. A written note follows within a working day with the lost marks classified into content, method, convention and time, and a session estimate against each. Nothing is charged before you read it.

Availability for IB mathematics is the deepest in our subject list. Both courses at both levels have good UAE evening cover and a match normally takes one to three working days. The constraint when a family calls late in the year is the slot rather than the specialist, particularly for twice-weekly pairings at 18:00. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the match comes from our India-based IB faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

On the Exploration, the honesty line is strict. A tutor may interrogate the proposed topic until it carries mathematics at the right level, check that the data or model can support the planned analysis, explain what each of the five criteria credits using the published descriptors, teach mathematical notation as a skill, and read a draft the student wrote and name which criterion a passage fails. A tutor may not choose the topic, write any part of the report, restructure it by rewriting, or produce the mathematics. Every submitted word is the student's.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, is not an examination centre and has no UAE office. We do not describe tutors as current IB examiners, because that status cannot be evidenced here. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws — no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a description
process.description: A marked script shows which of the five topic areas is weak and, more usefully, how much of the loss is convention rather than content. A description of how the term went shows neither. If nothing recent is marked, the diagnostic session includes a short timed section instead.

process.title: Have it marked twice
process.description: Once for the mathematics and once for the conventions alone — accuracy, exact values, command terms, visible method, notation. The difference between the two scores is the number of marks available without learning any new content, and for a capable underperformer it is routinely four or five a paper.

process.title: Classify every lost mark
process.description: Content not known, method not shown, convention breached, or time. The four have different remedies and different timescales, and a student who has not separated them cannot act on a paper score. This classification is the output of the free diagnostic lesson.

process.title: Run the right session shape for each part
process.description: Short frequent sessions for non-calculator fluency, a full hour for marked past papers, a compressed block for Higher Level Paper 3, and four to six sessions before the Exploration deadline. These are different jobs and do not substitute for one another.

process.title: Re-mark a paper at the end of the block
process.description: The same double marking, on a fresh paper, at the end of the block. If the convention gap has closed, the block worked. If it has not, either the between-session work is not happening or the diagnosis was wrong, and both are better established before the session than after it.

whyPoints.title: The conventions treated as content
whyPoints.description: Three significant figures, exact values, visible method, defined variables, and what 'hence' obliges are all published, finite and assessed. We teach them as a block and verify the effect by marking a paper twice, which converts a vague underperformance into a number.

whyPoints.title: Command terms taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: 'Hence' and 'hence or otherwise' are different instructions. 'Show that' needs a derivation; 'verify' permits substitution; 'state' wants the answer alone. One session plus a fortnight of annotating changes a student's mark profile across every paper in the course.

whyPoints.title: Past papers marked to the scheme, line by line
whyPoints.description: The value in a past paper is the marking, not the attempting. We award only what the published scheme credits and then classify the gap, because comparing final answers tells a student nothing about the method marks they lost.

whyPoints.title: Calculator rules handled in both directions
whyPoints.description: Paper 1 on Analysis and Approaches demands exact values without a device; the calculator-permitted papers demand visible working despite one. We drill both, and we teach the device itself deliberately, because fumbling menus under time pressure costs marks that are nothing to do with mathematics.

whyPoints.title: Plans that finish
whyPoints.description: A conventions block, a run of marked papers, a Paper 3 block, a timed-paper run, Exploration supervision. Each has a stated length and a way to check it worked, rather than an open weekly commitment that expands to fill whatever is bought.

whyPoints.title: A whiteboard, because working has to be visible
whyPoints.description: Mathematics is marked on what reaches the page, so the session needs a shared surface the student writes on and both parties can revisit. Every session is recorded, which means a worked solution from October can be rewatched in April at no extra cost.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when the maths is right?
faqs.answer: Almost always conventions rather than content. The default accuracy rule is three significant figures unless the question specifies otherwise, and an exact value requested will not accept a decimal. Full precision has to be carried through intermediate steps and rounded once at the end. Method marks require visible working, so a chain of operations done on a calculator with only the final figure written down forfeits them. Variables used must be defined. Each of those is a mark on a question the student answered correctly, which is why they never find out.

faqs.question: What is the difference between "hence" and "hence or otherwise"?
faqs.answer: A significant one. 'Hence' obliges the student to use the result just established, and a correct answer reached by an independent method does not earn the marks, because the question was testing whether the connection was seen. 'Hence or otherwise' explicitly permits a fresh start, so any valid method is credited. Students who do not know the distinction either re-derive something they were handed, wasting time, or ignore a result they were instructed to use and lose the marks. It takes one session to learn the full command-term list.

faqs.question: Which of the five syllabus topics is my child actually weak in?
faqs.answer: A marked script answers that in about five minutes. Both IB mathematics courses are organised into number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, and scoring a paper against those five areas tells you where to teach. What a topic breakdown will not tell you is how much of the loss is convention rather than content, which is why the diagnostic session marks the paper twice — once for the mathematics, once for accuracy, command terms and visible method alone.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 on Analysis and Approaches so much harder than class work?
faqs.answer: Because it is sat without a calculator, and that changes what the questions can demand. A paper with no device can legitimately require a surd, a fraction, a logarithm in exact form or a standard trigonometric value. A student who has learned with a graphing display calculator in their hand may understand the concept perfectly and be unable to produce the exact form under pressure. That is a fluency problem, not an understanding one, and it responds to short daily non-calculator practice over six to eight weeks rather than to more explanation.

faqs.question: How do we actually get value out of past papers?
faqs.answer: By marking rather than attempting. Sit the question under time, then mark it against the published scheme line by line, awarding only what the scheme credits, which means reading the method marks instead of comparing final answers. Then classify every lost mark as content not known, method not shown, convention breached, or time. Those four have different remedies and different timescales, and most underperforming students have far less content loss than they assume and far more of the other three.

faqs.question: Can we get copies of IB past papers and mark schemes from you?
faqs.answer: We teach from them on screen and link the official sources so you can obtain them through the proper route, but we do not hand over copies. IB past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright, and a tutor distributing scanned folders of marking material is creating a copyright problem rather than adding value — and something more serious where unreleased material is involved. In session we work a real question through live and show exactly what the published scheme credits at each stage.

faqs.question: Is learning the calculator itself worth session time?
faqs.answer: A short amount of it, yes, and most students acquire the skill by accident instead. Knowing where the solver, the graph analysis functions, the statistical distributions and the numerical derivative and integral live on the specific model, and reaching them quickly, saves real minutes on a calculator-permitted paper. A student fumbling through menus under time pressure is losing marks to the interface rather than to the mathematics, and about twenty minutes of deliberate practice fixes it for the rest of the course.

faqs.question: How much notation detail does the Exploration actually assess?
faqs.answer: Four of the twenty marks, through the mathematical communication criterion, which is more than most students expect. It credits correct notation, defined variables, labelled graphs and consistent terminology. The commonest failure is writing calculator syntax as though it were mathematical notation, which reads immediately as a student working from a device rather than from mathematics. Since the Exploration is 20% of the grade at both levels and on both courses, four marks of notation is roughly one per cent of the final Diploma grade.

faqs.question: Does Higher Level Paper 3 need its own preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is frequently the best-value block in the course. Paper 3 is one hour, two questions and 20% of the Higher Level grade, structured as a scaffolded investigation into unfamiliar mathematics where each part establishes something the next part uses. School mock papers in Dubai do not always include one, so some students meet the format first in the examination. The assessed skills are reading the whole question before starting and recording what each part has established, and four to six sessions of past questions usually shifts the score.

faqs.question: Where do IB maths students from Motor City go to school?
faqs.answer: Out of the community. GEMS Metropole School is inside Motor City but runs a British curriculum through IGCSE, so there is no Diploma cohort here. Students taking IB mathematics travel to JESS Arabian Ranches, Nord Anglia International School Dubai, Fairgreen International School in The Sustainable City, Greenfield International School, North London Collegiate School Dubai or Emirates International School Meadows. That commute is why Diploma sessions from this postcode start at about 18:00. We name schools as market context and hold no relationship with any of them.

faqs.question: Can a session cover both fluency work and a marked paper?
faqs.answer: Badly, and it is better to separate them. Non-calculator fluency wants short frequent contact with marking between sessions, which suits a 45-minute slot three times a fortnight. A past paper attempted under time and then marked line by line against the scheme does not compress into part of a session; it wants a full hour. Online those two shapes can sit on different evenings in the same week, at 18:00 and 20:00. A visiting tutor needing a two-hour minimum has to combine them, which serves neither well.

faqs.question: Does an IB maths tutor travel to houses in Motor City?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For mathematics specifically the online format has a direct advantage beyond tutor choice: a shared whiteboard the student writes on produces a visible record of the working, which is what has to be marked, and every session is recorded so a worked solution can be rewatched during revision.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a conventions block take?
faqs.answer: Four to six, and it is the cheapest high-yield block in the subject. The work is accuracy rules, exact values, intermediate rounding, command term obligations, visible method and notation, practised on questions where the content is already secure so the only new thing is the convention. The effect is verifiable: mark a fresh paper twice at the end of the block, once for mathematics and once for conventions, and compare the gap with the one measured at the start. If it has not narrowed, the diagnosis was wrong.

faqs.question: What does a maths specialist need from us before the diagnostic lesson?
faqs.answer: The course — Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation — the level, a marked paper, and the school's deadline for the Exploration. The marked paper does most of the work: it identifies the weak topic areas, exposes how much of the loss is convention, and provides the baseline that the end-of-block comparison runs against. The school's Exploration deadline matters because that component is 20% of the grade and, once submitted, cannot be improved however the rest of the plan goes.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mudon.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. Each profile names the route and level, because the two courses have different topic lists and different paper structures and should not be treated as one subject.

intro.heading: A Diploma maths year has a sequence, and most tutoring ignores it
paragraphs: Maths tutoring usually starts after a disappointing report, which puts it at the wrong point in the cycle. The Diploma mathematics year has a shape that barely varies between schools. The route is chosen late in Year 11. The exploration topic is approved in the first half of Year 12 and a draft exists before mocks. Mocks happen roughly six months before the session. The final stretch is timed papers and nothing else. Work that fits the phase pays; work that ignores it duplicates the school day.

A Mudon family feels this more sharply than most, because the evening is short. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no secondary school inside its boundary, so Diploma students travel to Jumeirah English Speaking School in Arabian Ranches, GEMS International School Al Khail, Nord Anglia in Al Barsha South or Fairgreen International in The Sustainable City. By the time a Year 12 is home and fed, there are perhaps two usable hours, and they have to hold school homework as well.

That scarcity is an argument for sequencing rather than for volume. One well-aimed hour a week in the first term of Year 12, spent on the exploration and on non-calculator fluency, is worth more than three hours of panic in the spring of Year 13. The exploration alone carries roughly a fifth of the subject grade and has a deadline a family can still influence, which makes it the single most improvable component in the course.

The external papers divide the rest. Both routes examine two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher Level, with Paper 1 taken without a calculator in Analysis and Approaches and technology assumed throughout Applications and Interpretation. Higher Level adds a Paper 3 investigation in both routes, and that paper rewards rehearsed investigation structure rather than additional content. Exact weightings come from the current subject guide, so confirm them with the school's subject teacher rather than from a tutoring page.

One structural point about the route choice, because it is made before most families start thinking about tutoring at all. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are not a hard version and an easy version of the same course. They have different topic lists, different paper patterns and different university consequences, and a student placed in the wrong one spends two years working against their own strengths. That decision belongs with the school and the student's own fluency, checked against the entry profiles published by the universities they are actually considering.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time so a session can sit at 4.15pm for a student home early or after 8pm for a household where both parents commute. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Mudon door. What the online format buys is a maths specialist for the actual route and level, rather than whoever teaches maths and lives nearby.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-mudon.programmesIntro: Maths appears at three points in the IB continuum and the work looks different at each. Mudon families ask about all three, usually in this order as a child moves up.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

Entry requirements vary by institution and change, so the check belongs with the school's careers office and the university's own published entry profile rather than with a tutor.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling and statistics route, with technology assumed throughout. Content includes regression, probability distributions, financial mathematics and, at Higher Level, matrices, graph theory and complex numbers. Paper 3 at Higher Level is a modelling investigation rather than a content paper.

For Mudon students heading towards business, design or several social sciences it is a good fit, and the tutoring need is usually interpretation writing rather than manipulation.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics

Students who can do the mathematics still score poorly if they do not generalise, test and justify, and that is a teachable habit well before Year 11.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, kinetics and equilibrium carry the mathematical load, and students who are weak on logarithms and rearrangement lose marks in chemistry that look like chemistry failures. Diagnosing that correctly saves a term of misaimed work.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level involves calculation as well as diagrams, and students from Applications and Interpretation handle it comfortably. Marks sit in applying a diagram to the named market rather than describing it in the abstract.

sections.heading: The Diploma maths year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Take the session the student is working towards and count back from it. Eighteen months out, the route is being chosen in Year 11 on the strength of IGCSE or Middle Years work, and that choice sets the ceiling for university applications. Twelve months out, the exploration topic is being approved and the first content gaps from the autumn term are either closed or quietly carried forward. Nine months out, there should be a complete exploration draft and the first mock.

Six months out, the balance should tip. Content teaching stops being the main activity and timed papers start. This is the phase where students who have never practised Paper 1 without a calculator discover how much their fluency has degraded, because school classwork and homework are almost always done with technology to hand. Three months out, the only useful work is timed papers and marked-script repair, with topic work chosen from what the scripts show rather than from a syllabus order.

Six weeks out, the plan narrows to error patterns and exam logistics. At this point content revision has a poor return, because anything genuinely unlearned will not be secure enough to use under pressure, while a habit like showing working or checking a rearrangement can still be installed. Ramadan falls inside the final stretch in the current cycle, which is why evening slots after Iftar are worth fixing early rather than renegotiating late.

IB session and results dates are not published on this page. The IB's own site, through the school's Diploma coordinator, is the only reliable source for them, and a tutoring page that restates them without that check will eventually be wrong. What is safe to plan around is the sequence rather than the specific dates.

sections.heading: The exploration: a fifth of the grade with a movable deadline
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is the only part of a Diploma maths grade a family can still influence by acting early, which makes it the highest-return thing on this page. It is a piece of personal mathematical writing, not a long report, and schools publish the current page guidance from the subject guide. It is marked against criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics.

Students lose marks in a predictable place. They pour effort into the mathematics, which is one criterion, and neglect presentation, engagement and reflection, which are separately credited. A reflection that says the topic was interesting scores little. One that identifies a limitation in a model, considers what would change if an assumption were relaxed, and says why that matters for the conclusion scores properly. That is a writing skill, and it is teachable in two or three sessions.

Topic choice decides the ceiling before anything is written. A topic with no accessible mathematics at the student's level cannot be rescued by effort, and a topic so broad that the mathematics becomes a survey cannot show engagement. The useful test is whether the student can state, in one sentence, what mathematics they will do and why they personally chose this. If they cannot, the topic is not ready, however interesting it sounds.

The boundary here is strict and worth stating plainly. A tutor may explain the criteria, question the topic, critique the mathematics and mark the student's own draft against the descriptors. A tutor may not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, or supply a worked exploration to adapt. The work is authenticated by the teacher, and a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma rather than the marks.

sections.heading: Paper 1, Paper 2 and Paper 3, drilled separately
paragraphs: The most common mistake in maths revision is treating the papers as one thing. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is taken without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, and they reward different skills so completely that practising them together trains neither. A student who always has technology to hand loses non-calculator fluency silently, because nothing in school classwork exposes it until a mock.

Paper 1 rewards arithmetic resilience, exact-value work, surds, logarithms and the ability to carry an algebraic manipulation three or four lines without error. The drill is unglamorous and effective: short timed sets, no calculator, marked immediately, with every error classified as either a method problem or a slip. Slips respond to pace discipline. Method problems need teaching. Distinguishing them is the whole point of marking immediately.

Paper 2 rewards a different habit, which is reasoning first and confirming with technology second. Students who reach for the graphing calculator before deciding what they are looking for lose time and produce answers they cannot justify. The drill is to require a written plan line before any calculator use on each question, which feels slow for a fortnight and then becomes faster than the alternative.

At Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended investigation in Analysis and a modelling investigation in Applications. It rewards rehearsed structure rather than extra content: reading the whole question first, establishing notation, generalising carefully and justifying each step. Two or three full rehearsals change performance on it more than any amount of topic revision, and almost nobody does them.

sections.heading: What eight weeks before a session should contain
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most families ask for, and in maths it has a reliable shape. The first fortnight is diagnosis under time: two timed papers, marked by the student against the scheme, with every loss classified. Nothing else happens in those two weeks, because every later decision depends on what the classification shows.

Weeks three to five are repair aimed at the two or three topics carrying the heaviest recoverable loss, taught properly rather than revised, with a timed section in every session to keep the diagnosis honest. This is where most of the available marks move, and the selection matters more than the teaching: a topic worth four marks a paper is not worth three weeks however shaky it is.

Weeks six and seven return to whole papers under full conditions, alternating Paper 1 and Paper 2, with Paper 3 rehearsals added at Higher Level. The purpose shifts from learning to execution: pacing, question order, when to abandon a part and come back, and how to use the first five minutes. Students who have never practised question order lose marks they already earned by running out of time on the last page.

The final week is deliberately light. Formula booklet familiarity, calculator mode checks, one timed section to stay warm, sleep. A student who revises hard in the last week usually arrives tired, and tiredness costs more marks in a non-calculator paper than any remaining content gap.

sections.heading: Mocks and predicted grades in a Dubai school year
paragraphs: Mocks do two jobs and families usually only notice one. They produce a predicted grade, which matters for university applications, and they produce a marked script, which matters far more for the eventual result. The script is routinely filed and forgotten while the grade is discussed at length, which is the wrong way round.

Read properly, a maths mock separates four failures that feel identical. There is content absence, visible as questions untouched. There is method loss, where the approach was right and the presentation lost the marks. There is timing collapse, visible as a strong first half and an abandoned final page. And there is misreading, where a correct method answers a different question from the one asked.

Each has a different timescale. Timing collapse responds inside two weeks to papers sat with a clock and a question-order rule. Misreading responds to a fortnight of reading the question aloud before writing. Method loss responds to the student marking their own work against the scheme until the pattern is obvious to them. Content absence is the slow one and the only one that genuinely needs months.

On predicted grades, one caution. Schools set mocks at different severities, and a paper marked harshly to motivate a cohort is not a forecast. Treat the number as a position and the annotations as the information, and compare any school boundary against the board's most recent published boundaries for the same paper rather than assuming they match.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the Dubai academic calendar
paragraphs: A maths plan that ignores the UAE calendar fails for ordinary reasons. The academic year has long breaks in which nothing is set and short terms in which everything is, Ramadan shifts the shape of the day, and families in this belt travel. A plan written in September that assumes forty uninterrupted weekly sessions is fiction, and discovering that in March is expensive.

Ramadan is the clearest case. School days shorten, energy patterns change, and many Dubailand families prefer sessions after Iftar. Because an online session involves no travel, that change costs nothing to arrange and can be made week by week rather than negotiated once. Fixing those slots early in the month is easier than competing for them late.

School holidays work in the opposite direction and are underused. They are the only blocks in the year when a student can do three or four sessions in a week without competing homework, which makes them the natural window for closing a content gap or for exploration work that term time keeps interrupting. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is the cheapest useful window in the whole Diploma, and almost nobody uses it.

The practical move is to mark the fixed points once: term dates, mock windows, the exploration deadline, Ramadan, and any family travel. Everything else in the plan can then flex around them, and the review conversation every few weeks becomes a short one rather than a renegotiation.

sections.heading: What maths tuition costs in Dubai, priced per session
paragraphs: Most pages present rates per hour. For a maths plan it is more useful to think per session and per block, because that is how the work is actually bought: an eight-week block of sixteen sessions, or a three-session exploration push, or a weekly hour through a term.

Take the qualified online band first, which is where a competent Diploma maths tutor sits: roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A sixteen-session block at the middle of that band is a planning number a family can test against its budget. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's table giving AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

The cheaper end exists and has a use. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya at AED 33 to 52, and for working through exercise sets with an organised student that is defensible value. It is less suited to an eight-week block before a session, where the value lies in classifying losses from a marked script.

In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly, Bestimate puts a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more specialist. Packages seen include AED 799 monthly for eight online sessions. These are market figures with sources named, not IB Gram prices.

sections.heading: Honesty, permits and what to ask a maths tutor
paragraphs: Two boundaries matter in maths specifically. The first is the exploration, where a tutor teaches, questions and marks the student's own draft and does nothing else. The second is board material: IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to their publishers, and sessions reference and link to the official pages rather than circulating copies. Nobody has access to unreleased papers whatever is claimed.

On the tutor's side, the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

There is one arrangement to decline. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. A maths teacher offering to tutor your child privately is the first case to ask about.

The useful questions for a maths tutor are narrow. Which route and level have you taught, and for how many cohorts. Which papers have you marked. How do you drill non-calculator work. What will you do with an exploration draft, and what will you refuse to do. Four answers, and the choice usually makes itself.
