faqs.question: Which of the five IB Mathematics topic areas is my child most likely stuck in?
faqs.answer: Topic two, functions, or topic five, calculus, if the course is Analysis and Approaches, and topic four, statistics, if it is Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. Students are usually fluent in topic one and comfortable in topic three until a triangle stops being right-angled. The way to find out rather than guess is a short diagnostic spanning all five under timed conditions, which takes one session and routinely contradicts what a school report implied about general ability.

faqs.question: What does the Higher Level Paper 3 investigation actually ask for?
faqs.answer: A sustained argument in an unfamiliar context, worth twenty per cent of the grade, with later parts depending on earlier ones. Typically it opens with concrete cases, asks the student to notice a pattern, requires a precisely stated conjecture, then a proof or justification, then an extension to a wider context. The concrete cases are cheap marks; the justification stage carries the heaviest weighting. The key technique is carrying a doubtful earlier result forward rather than stopping, because blank pages score nothing.

faqs.question: Why is my child's working correct but the mark not full?
faqs.answer: Almost always command terms. Show that requires a complete forward argument to the stated result, hence requires the previous part to be used, deduce requires established work to be cited, verify asks for substitution rather than solving, and justify requires a reason attached to the answer. A student who reads all of these as solve forfeits the final mark on questions they otherwise answered. Look at the marked paper: if several such questions lost one mark each, three or four sessions fixes it.

faqs.question: How do we drill non-calculator technique for AA Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Short and frequent, with the calculator physically put away. Forty-five minutes twice a week beats one ninety-minute session, because hand fluency is a motor habit rather than a concept. The content is factorising, surds, logarithm laws, exact trigonometric values, differentiating products and quotients by hand, and simplifying before substituting. Measure it by the gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 scores: if Paper 2 is consistently eight to twelve marks higher, the gap is hand fluency and nothing else.

faqs.question: Is proof by induction teachable as a template without being dishonest?
faqs.answer: Yes, because the structure genuinely is fixed: establish the base case, assume the statement for an arbitrary case, prove it for the next, conclude. The marks sit in the inductive step and in the explicit statement of what was assumed, and the commonest loss is a student who does the algebra correctly without stating the assumption, leaving the argument incomplete. Proof by contradiction is harder because the student must choose what to negate. Counterexample is easy once a student accepts that one case suffices.

faqs.question: Can calculator skills really be taught over a video link?
faqs.answer: Better than in person, which surprises most parents. The tutor shares an emulator or the matching software on screen so the menu path appears at a readable size and can be repeated, while your child follows on the handheld model they will take into the examination hall. Sitting beside someone, the student watches a small screen at an awkward angle. We spend about ten minutes a session on it until it stops being a limiting factor, then stop, because an unfinished Paper 2 costs more than any topic gap.

faqs.question: What is the right way to mark and categorise a timed maths paper?
faqs.answer: Sit it timed, in the correct calculator condition, mark it against the scheme without charity, then categorise every lost mark as method not known, method misapplied, accuracy, command term or ran out of time. Count the categories. The largest sets the next three sessions and is usually not what the student expected. One paper a fortnight fully marked and reviewed beats three a week half-marked. For a weeknight slot, sit the paper at the weekend and use the session for review.

faqs.question: Will you send us a library of IB Mathematics assessment material?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB, and your child's school has legitimate access to the assessment material through its own channels. A tutor works from that material inside a session, which is ordinary practice; hosting a download library is distributing someone else's property, and for unreleased material it is worse. We cite the official sources and leave the material where it belongs rather than offering it as a free extra.

faqs.question: My child chose Applications and Interpretation to avoid calculus. Was that a mistake?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it was not the escape it looked like. Applications and Interpretation trims calculus to what a modelling course needs and in exchange loads topic four heavily, so at Higher Level the course runs into hypothesis testing and the chi-squared distribution. Students who chose it to avoid algebraic difficulty meet statistical difficulty instead. Whether it was right depends on the degree: engineering, mathematics and physics generally expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, while business and social sciences accept Applications and Interpretation.

faqs.question: Which schools would a Nad Al Hamar student sit Diploma maths at?
faqs.answer: Mostly the Dubai Festival City cluster, including Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai, and the Mirdif belt, including Uptown International School. Whether a school offers both mathematics courses at Higher Level in a given year depends on cohort size, so a course change may be constrained by the timetable rather than by your child's ability. Ask the coordinator directly. Schools are named here as local context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied.

faqs.question: Is paying an in-home maths rate worth it in the eastern suburbs?
faqs.answer: Examine what the premium buys. In-home visits in Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is absorbed, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor. The difference pays for travel, for scarcity within a twenty-minute radius, and for parent convenience. It does not pay for course specialism, and a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist probably does not live near Nad Al Hamar. We do not offer home visits in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: How early should a student heading into AA Higher Level start preparing?
faqs.answer: The summer before DP1, for six to eight weeks, on algebraic manipulation, trigonometric identities and function notation alone. It is the least-bought and highest-value block in the sequence, because Paper 1 demands hand fluency that neither IGCSE nor MYP required, and a student who arrives without it spends the autumn term behind. Families in this part of Dubai often travel for the summer, which makes the block awkward in person and straightforward over video across time zones.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do about the mathematical exploration?
faqs.answer: Explain what each of the five criteria rewards and in what proportion, screen a proposed topic for whether it can sustain mathematics at the level of the course, demonstrate a complete worked investigation on an entirely different topic, read your child's own draft and ask questions about assumptions, notation and depth, and say plainly where the mathematics falls short of the level claimed. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the mathematics, write any passage or edit the draft into shape.

faqs.question: How is the MYP standard or extended maths decision linked to all this?
faqs.answer: Directly. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the honest preparation for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and criterion B, investigating patterns, is the part of MYP assessment that predicts Diploma readiness because it tests generalisation rather than fluency. A student who takes standard mathematics and then chooses Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level arrives with an algebra gap that surfaces in the first term and costs far more to close then than it would have cost to pre-empt.

intro.heading: Two years of IB maths, and the four dates that shape them
paragraphs: An IB maths grade is decided across twenty-four months, and four dates inside that window do most of the deciding. The first is the course choice at the end of Year 11, when a Nad Al Sheba student picks Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation at Higher or Standard Level. The second is the exploration deadline in DP1 or early DP2, worth 20% of the grade. The third is the mock window. The fourth is the May session itself, which UAE schools sit. Everything a tutor can usefully do depends on which of those four is next.

That is why this page is organised as a calendar rather than as a syllabus tour. Parents here usually arrive at the question late — somewhere between a disappointing DP1 report and a mock result — and the single most useful thing at that point is an honest statement of what the remaining weeks can and cannot change. In maths more than in most subjects, the answer is specific: timing and method presentation are recoverable in weeks, missing calculus is not.

Nad Al Sheba sits in a dense school corridor. Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy are inside the district; Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai are in Sobha Hartland next door; Swiss International Scientific School Dubai is over at Al Jaddaf. Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with IB accounting for about 7% of enrolment across seventeen licensed curricula. The practical effect is that two students on the same street can both be doing IB maths and sit entirely different papers.

The second reason the course matters more than the subject label: Applications and Interpretation assumes a graphic display calculator on every paper, while Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 forbids one. A student who has spent two years leaning on a calculator and then meets AA Paper 1 is not weak at maths; they are untrained for that paper. A tutor who has never marked that paper will not spot the distinction, and distance from your villa says nothing about whether they have.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to addresses in the UAE — home visits are a service we run only in India. For maths specifically that has a practical upside beyond cost: a shared screen with a graphing tool and the official mark scheme open side by side beats one exercise book between two people, and every line of working stays visible to both people at once.

One practical note before the detail. The most useful thing a Nad Al Sheba parent can bring to a first conversation is not a report card but a marked script: a topic test, a mock paper, anything with the examiner's or teacher's annotations still on it. A grade tells you the size of the problem and a script tells you its shape, and the shape is what decides whether the next twelve weeks should be spent on calculus, on timing, or on the exploration sitting half-written in a folder.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.programmesIntro: Four stages feed an IB maths grade, and the preparation that matters most happens before the Diploma starts. These are the stages a Nad Al Sheba family passes through, described by the maths demand each one creates rather than by the programme's aims.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP maths is marked on four criteria out of 8 each: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The extended route in the final years is the one that prepares a student for Higher Level. Students who score well on investigation and poorly on communication are usually the ones who struggle most with the Diploma exploration, because the exploration is a communication task wearing a maths hat.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in and around Nad Al Sheba run MYP straight into the Diploma inside one building, which means the school controls the pacing and the transition is invisible from outside. The hidden cost is exam conditions: a student who has never sat a two-hour timed paper meets one in DP1, and the fix in the final MYP year is timed practice rather than more content.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Algebraic, proof-oriented and the route most competitive engineering and mathematics degrees expect. Standard Level sits Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, each worth 40%, plus the 20% exploration. Higher Level sits three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% alongside the exploration, and the Higher Level Paper 1 is where a two-year reliance on technology shows up most sharply.
programmes.countryNote: Nad Al Sheba students heading for engineering or economics at a UAE or overseas university are generally advised towards AA, and the entry requirement for Higher Level AA at most Dubai schools is a strong IGCSE Extended or Additional Mathematics result. Check the specific university's published prerequisite rather than assuming, because requirements differ between institutions and change.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Statistical, modelling-led and calculator-assumed throughout. Standard Level sits two papers at 40% each with the 20% exploration; Higher Level adds a Paper 3 of extended, data-driven problems. The content is not easier, it is different: the losses here are interpretation sentences left unwritten and modelling assumptions left unstated, rather than algebra left undone.
programmes.countryNote: AI suits students heading into business, design, social sciences and many health-science routes, and it is the course that more Dubai students should probably be on than currently are. Families sometimes choose AA for its reputation and then spend two years struggling with Paper 1. The decision should follow the degree, and it should be checked against the published prerequisite.

programmes.name: The pre-Diploma bridge year
programmes.description: The window in which the Diploma maths choice is still fully open and cheap to prepare for. A student taking IGCSE Additional Mathematics, or doing extra calculus and trigonometry alongside Extended Mathematics, arrives at AA Higher Level with the first term already partly covered. A student who does not is covering it while also learning how the Diploma works.
programmes.countryNote: In this corridor the bridge year is also when the A Level versus Diploma fork is decided, since several Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland schools offer both. A student who knows by the January mocks of Year 11 which way they are leaning can target the maths preparation; one who decides in July cannot.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.subjectsIntro: IB maths is one subject with four courses and five content strands, and tutoring decisions are made at that level rather than at the level of 'maths'. Below are the courses and strands Nad Al Sheba students bring, with where the marks actually go in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers at 30%, 30% and 20% plus the exploration. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and rewards fluent algebraic manipulation; Paper 3 is two extended investigations where partial credit is generous and abandoning a question is the costliest habit. Proof by induction and complex numbers are the usual content gaps.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers at 40% each plus the exploration. Paper 1 without a calculator is the paper most Standard Level students under-practise, because school homework is almost always done with one to hand. Differentiation and integration techniques carry the most recoverable marks here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Three papers plus the exploration, with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout and Paper 3 built on extended data-driven problems. Statistical tests, matrices and graph theory are the content most often missing, and the losses concentrate in the final interpretation sentence of each question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two papers at 40% each with a calculator on both, plus the exploration. The trap is treating calculator access as permission to skip the working, when method marks are awarded for the steps shown. Modelling questions want an assumption named before the model is built.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level proof and complex numbers. On AA Paper 1 this strand is where non-calculator fluency pays, and the common loss is a sign error early in a long manipulation that costs every mark downstream rather than one.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, rational and composite functions, inverse functions and at Higher Level more demanding graph work. Students lose marks by sketching without stating asymptotes or intercepts, and by solving algebraically when the question asked them to read a graph, or the reverse.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Triangle rules, radian measure, trigonometric identities and equations, and vectors at Higher Level AA. Radians are a reliable source of lost marks because calculators silently answer in degrees, and a correct method with the wrong mode produces a wrong answer that looks confident.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, correlation, distributions, conditional probability, and at AI Higher Level formal hypothesis testing. This strand carries more of the AI grade than of the AA grade, and the marks sit in the conclusion sentence: stating what the test result means in the context given, not just the number.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration, kinematics, and at AA Higher Level a substantially longer list of techniques including integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. This is the strand that cannot be rebuilt in eight weeks, which is why the term-by-term plan on this page front-loads it.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: One hour, two extended-response questions, calculator permitted, on both AA and AI. Marks are awarded through a long chain, so a student who stops at the part they cannot do forfeits later parts they could. Practising continuation after a block is more valuable here than practising the content.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing marked against five criteria over 20 marks, with no hard word limit and published guidance of roughly twelve to twenty pages. Personal engagement and reflection are the criteria most often scored lowest, and both are about the writing rather than the mathematics.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Not a syllabus strand but a decisive skill. AI assumes a graphic display calculator on every paper; AA Paper 1 forbids one. Knowing which functions the model offers, and practising both with and without, is worth more in the final term than another topic, and it is almost never taught explicitly.

sections.heading: The Diploma maths calendar, term by term
paragraphs: The useful way to look at IB maths is as six terms with different jobs. Term one of DP1 builds the foundations the rest depends on; by the end of it a student should be able to differentiate and integrate without hesitating. Term two adds breadth and, in most Nad Al Sheba schools, introduces the exploration as a concept. Term three is where the exploration topic gets chosen, and a bad choice made in June costs six months.

DP2 runs differently. Term four is the heaviest, because exploration drafting collides with new Higher Level content and with the internal assessments of two other subjects. Term five is the mock window and the fortnight after it, which is the single most informative data a parent receives in two years. Term six is the final run: no new content, only timed sections and question selection, ending at the May session that UAE schools sit.

The table below sets out that shape and what tutoring should be doing in each term. Dates are deliberately absent for the IB session itself: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB. Confirm every one with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it, and treat any page that publishes a precise IB date without a source with suspicion.

The reason to look at it this way is money as much as marks. Tutoring in term one is cheap and highly leveraged because it is building rather than repairing. Tutoring in term six is expensive per unit of grade movement because the only remaining levers are technique and selection. A family that starts in term five is not too late, but they are paying for a narrower set of possible outcomes, and they deserve to be told that rather than sold six months of hope.

sections.heading: AA or AI: a choice that closes in Year 11
paragraphs: This decision is taken at the end of Year 11, usually on a form, often in a hurry, and it is the most consequential maths decision a Diploma student makes. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented. Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-led, with a graphic display calculator assumed on every paper. Neither is the easy one; they reward different students.

Two patterns recur in this corridor. The first is a student choosing Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level because it carries more prestige, then spending two years losing marks on a non-calculator Paper 1 they were never trained for. The second is a student choosing Applications and Interpretation and later discovering that the engineering degree they want lists Analysis and Approaches as a prerequisite. The first is fixable with early technique work; the second is not fixable at all once DP1 is underway.

So the decision should run backwards from the degree, then forwards through the paper. Look up the published prerequisite for the actual course and institution — they differ, and they change, so read the admissions page rather than relying on a general rule. Then sit the student a past Paper 1 from the AA course under timed conditions, with no calculator, and mark it against the official scheme. That single exercise tells you more than a term of school reports.

Switching after DP1 begins is possible in some schools and painful in all of them, because the content diverges quickly and the exploration may already be underway. If a switch is being considered, it needs to happen in the first weeks rather than the first months, which means the evidence has to be gathered early. That is the whole argument for a diagnostic session in September rather than a rescue in February.

sections.heading: The papers, the weightings and what each one punishes
paragraphs: Parents are rarely shown the arithmetic of a maths grade, and it is worth having. At Standard Level, two papers carry 40% each and the exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30% each, Paper 3 carries 20%, and the exploration carries 20%. So a Higher Level student has already banked or lost a fifth of the grade before the exam hall, and a second fifth sits in a one-hour paper most students practise least.

Each paper punishes something specific. Paper 1 on Analysis and Approaches punishes reliance on technology: a student who can set up the integral but cannot evaluate it by hand loses the back half of the question. Paper 2 punishes poor calculator technique in the opposite direction, because answers given to the wrong accuracy or in the wrong angle mode are wrong answers arrived at correctly. Paper 3 punishes stopping.

That last one deserves a sentence of its own, because it is the most recoverable. Paper 3 questions run as long chains where later parts often depend on a structure rather than on the previous numerical answer. A student who hits a part they cannot do and puts the pen down forfeits everything after it. A student trained to write 'assume the result in part (b)' and continue picks up marks they would otherwise never see. That training takes about four sessions.

The practical reading of the table below is this: a Nad Al Sheba student eight weeks out should not be revising topics in proportion to their size in the syllabus. They should be revising in proportion to where their own marks are going, which is what mock scripts tell you and what a past paper marked against the official scheme tells you faster.

sections.heading: The exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, one draft
paragraphs: A fifth of the maths grade is a piece of writing, and most students treat it as an obstacle rather than as the most controllable marks in the course. It is marked against five criteria totalling 20 marks, there is no hard word limit, and the published guidance points at roughly twelve to twenty pages. Unlike a paper, it can be planned, drafted and improved in daylight.

The criteria are where the strategy sits. Presentation and mathematical communication reward structure, correct notation and a reader who can follow the argument without guessing. Personal engagement and reflection reward the student showing their own thinking — why this question, what surprised them, what the limitation of the approach was. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation and rewards mathematics that is appropriate to the level and actually used rather than displayed.

The two criteria most often scored low in this corridor are reflection and personal engagement, and both are writing problems rather than maths problems. A student who computes elegantly and then writes a conclusion saying 'the results were as expected' has left marks on the table that cost nothing to collect. Twenty minutes of a session spent reading the criteria wording aloud and translating it into a checklist is usually worth more than an hour on the mathematics.

The honesty line matters here and is worth stating plainly. A tutor may discuss whether a topic has enough mathematics in it for the level, point out that a scope is too wide, explain what a criterion is asking for, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not choose the topic, write any part of the text, produce the mathematics, or edit the piece to completion. The student signs a declaration that the work is their own, and a page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

sections.heading: What two years of IB maths tuition costs, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market and work up, because that is the direction the decision actually runs. The cheapest paid option in Dubai is a budget online tutor, usually a university student, at AED 45 to 150 an hour — EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For a Standard Level student with one specific topic gap, that can be the right purchase, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest.

Above it sits a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, where TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table gives 200 to 450 plus. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate putting them at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. The premium end runs AED 500 to 650 upwards, with BartyED publishing AED 650. All read in October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

The reason to climb the ladder rather than start at the top is that the bands buy different things, and Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is the point at which the difference stops being theoretical. An undergraduate who was good at maths can revise functions with a Standard Level student perfectly well. Marking a Paper 3 investigation against the official scheme, or judging whether an exploration topic carries enough mathematics for Higher Level, is specialist work and the bands reflect that.

Across a two-year Diploma the shape matters more than the rate. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and packages seen in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. A sensible plan spends lightly in DP1 term one, pauses, and concentrates spend in term four and term six. Ask any provider for the session length behind the rate and whether VAT is included before booking anything.

sections.heading: Why maths specifically works on a shared screen
paragraphs: The usual argument for online tutoring is cost and tutor choice. For maths there is a third argument that is actually stronger, and it is about the medium rather than the money: a shared screen holds more of the working, visibly, to both people at once, than a shared exercise book does.

In practice a maths session consists of a student attempting something, a tutor watching where the attempt goes wrong, and both looking at the official mark scheme afterwards. On a shared screen the question, the student's working and the examiner's wording sit side by side, and a graphing tool can be opened to show what the function actually does. Nothing has to be turned around, re-copied or held up to the light, and the whole session is reviewable afterwards because it was written on a surface that saves.

What online genuinely loses is presence. A tutor in the room notices a student drifting faster, and a parent can see the session happening. Those are real and this page is not going to pretend they are not. They are also what the market charges AED 50 to 150 an hour extra for, and in a two-year Diploma that premium is substantial.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India. The table below is therefore the reasoning behind an existing decision rather than a sales argument, and the last column is the part specific to this district — roads around Nad Al Sheba, Meydan and Mohammed Bin Rashid City at 15:00 decide what time a travelling tutor can actually start a maths session that needs concentration.

sections.heading: The eight weeks before papers, in maths
paragraphs: Eight weeks out, the honest statement is that content and technique are now different purchases. Technique is still fully available: timing, question selection, calculator accuracy, continuation on Paper 3, and the habit of showing method so partial credit lands. Content is only partly available, and attempting to cover everything in eight weeks produces thin recall across the whole syllabus instead of secure recall across most of it.

The sequence that works is narrow. Sit one timed section. Mark it against the official scheme line by line. Sort every lost mark into content not known, method not shown, arithmetic or mode slip, or ran out of time. Tally across three papers. In this corridor the dominant category in maths is almost always timing or method presentation rather than content, which is good news because those are the recoverable ones.

Then write the list of topics being abandoned, and show it to the student. Students resist this harder than parents do, because a written list of what they will not know feels like giving up. It is the opposite: it is what makes the remaining revision concentrated enough to move a boundary. A student revising nine topics lightly in eight weeks is choosing at random; a student revising four properly is choosing.

Papers come from the school's licensed access or the board's own platform. We do not host, reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, because they are copyright material and some of it is unreleased. Nobody can promise a grade from eight weeks of work, and any tutor who offers one has told you something useful about themselves at no charge.

sections.heading: Maths choice and UAE university entry
paragraphs: The maths course a Nad Al Sheba student picks interacts with where they intend to apply, and the interaction is specific rather than general. Competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, design, social science and several health-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation, and some prefer it because of the statistics content.

The right method is to read the published prerequisite for the specific programme at the specific institution, because requirements differ between universities and are revised. A general claim about what universities want is the sort of thing that is true on average and wrong for the one application that matters. A student applying in two directions should check both and take the more demanding requirement as the constraint.

There is a separate UAE step that is often confused with admissions. Ministry of Education equivalency converts a school-leaving qualification into something UAE authorities recognise, and it governs applications to universities inside the country. The British-track rules are published in detail: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the American track, English requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or SAT 450 in reading and writing, and mathematics requires SAT Math of at least 450.

For the IB there is deliberately no figure here. The source setting out those British and American requirements states no IB points threshold, so publishing one would be invention, and one ranking competitor already publishes the wrong subject count for the British track. Check the current IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the Dubai school week
paragraphs: A maths plan written without the UAE calendar in it will break in its second month. Ramadan shortens school hours and reorganises the day around Iftar and later sleep. Eid takes days out. Family travel in this corridor is long and frequent, and the spring half-term in Dubai sits differently from the pattern most online revision timetables assume.

The approach that survives is to decide in advance which weeks are low-intensity and protect them rather than discover them. During Ramadan, sessions generally move later or to post-Iftar timing and the productive length drops: 45 focused minutes of non-calculator practice beats 90 tired ones. Students sitting papers in the spring usually keep the cadence and change the clock, because a four-week gap in DP2 term five is expensive in term six.

There is also a standing claim on the timetable that international revision advice knows nothing about. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and schools advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Those minutes sit inside a week already holding six Diploma subjects, Theory of Knowledge and CAS.

Travel is the final factor and the one that favours live video most clearly. In-person tutoring stops when a family leaves the country, which in this corridor can be three or four weeks at a stretch. A session delivered over video follows the student, and in DP2 that continuity is the difference between a plan and a wish. Time zones are handled by moving the slot, not by cancelling the term.

sections.heading: What happens when no AA Higher Level specialist is free
paragraphs: Availability is the thing tutoring pages in this market conceal, and the researched set is consistent about it: a form, a promise of a fast match, and silence about the case where the specific course at the specific level has nobody free. Several route UAE parents to an Indian phone number without saying so. Disclosing a coverage limit is cheaper than being caught by one.

The honest shape for a Nad Al Sheba maths enquiry is this. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level are reliably covered, and a trial is usually arrangeable within a few days. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, specifically with Paper 3 marking experience, is a narrower pool and sometimes takes longer. A request for one tutor to cover Higher Level maths and Higher Level physics together is narrower still and occasionally cannot be met in a given term.

When it cannot, you get a date or a no rather than a generalist with the right label. A tutor who is strong at Standard Level and stretched at Higher Level is discovered in session three, by which time a term has gone and the money with it. The free trial lesson exists to put that judgement in your hands before anything is paid: a parent who watches a tutor mark a Paper 3 section can tell within twenty minutes whether they have done it before.

The same transparency applies to what a tutor will not do. Exploration support is feedback on the student's own draft, not drafting. Board materials are referenced and linked rather than reproduced. And no tutor, however experienced with AA Higher Level, can guarantee a grade, which is why no number of that kind appears anywhere on this page.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the next date
process.description: Say whether it is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, which school, and what is next: a topic test, the exploration proposal, mocks or the papers. Those four facts decide whether a specialist is free and what the term can realistically achieve. 'IB maths' on its own starts a conversation instead.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: One live session spent on a past-paper section from the correct course and paper, marked together rather than taught. For an Analysis and Approaches student that section is usually non-calculator, because that is where the hidden gap sits. You get a written note naming the dominant pattern in the lost marks. No payment is involved.

process.title: Build the plan against the six terms
process.description: Place the student on the term map, then decide what this term is for and what it is explicitly not for. In DP1 term one that means fluency and calculus. In DP2 term four it means sequencing the exploration against two other internal assessments. Writing down what is being left is what makes it a plan.

process.title: Weekly sessions tracking the school
process.description: The tutor asks for the current topic and the next assessment each week and works to those rather than to the textbook order. Session notes name the topic, what was set, and which paper or criterion the next session targets. Parents here tend to prefer that note to a progress percentage, which would be invented.

process.title: Rebuild on the mock scripts
process.description: When mocks come back, the plan is rewritten rather than continued. Lost marks are categorised into content, method not shown, slips and timing, the dominant category becomes the work for a fixed fortnight, and a stop-revising list is written. This is the most informative fortnight in two years and it has a short shelf life.

process.title: Switch to paper blocks for the final term
process.description: Content coverage stops and the sessions become timed sections marked against official schemes, with separate drilling for calculator and non-calculator papers and deliberate Paper 3 continuation practice at Higher Level. Cadence usually rises to two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: An Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutor and an Applications and Interpretation Standard Level tutor are different jobs with different marking experience. We ask which course and level before matching, and say so if the specialist you need is not free this term rather than filling the slot.

whyPoints.title: Non-calculator practice built in from the start
whyPoints.description: Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and school homework almost never is, which is why the gap stays hidden until a mock. Sessions on that course include deliberate non-calculator work from the first term rather than in the final eight weeks.

whyPoints.title: The exploration treated as marks, not admin
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade is a piece of writing marked on five criteria over 20 marks, and the two criteria usually scored lowest are about reflection and engagement rather than mathematics. Feedback is mapped to criteria letters, and nothing is written or redrafted for the student.

whyPoints.title: AED rates with their sources on the page
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it and dated to October 2026. Three of six researched competitors in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. You can check each band before speaking to anybody, including us.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates invented
whyPoints.description: UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page gets. The IB blocks automated checking of its own calendar, so no session or results date in this project is confirmed from the IB. Confirm every date with your school's coordinator or on ibo.org.

whyPoints.title: No regulator or board claimed as a credential
whyPoints.description: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge and Pearson are explained here where relevant. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of them and claims none.

faqs.question: Is the IB maths tutor near Nad Al Sheba actually local, or is this online?
faqs.answer: Sessions for UAE families run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For maths the format carries a specific advantage beyond cost: on a shared screen the question, the student's working and the official mark scheme sit side by side, and a graphing tool can be opened mid-explanation. Most of a maths session is two people reading working, and a screen holds more of it visibly than one exercise book passed between them.

faqs.question: Which maths course should my child take for the degree they want?
faqs.answer: Read the published prerequisite for the specific programme at the specific institution rather than relying on a general rule, because requirements differ and are revised. Competitive engineering, mathematics and physics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, design, social sciences and several health-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation, sometimes preferring its statistics content. If your child is applying in two directions, take the more demanding requirement as the constraint and plan the Year 11 preparation around it.

faqs.question: How is an IB maths grade actually made up?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, two papers carry 40% each and the exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30% each, Paper 3 carries 20% and the exploration carries 20%. So a Higher Level student has a fifth of the grade settled before any exam, and another fifth sitting in a one-hour paper most students practise least. Standard Level courses run 150 teaching hours and Higher Level 240, which is the real measure of the step up between them.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep losing marks on Paper 1 despite good class results?
faqs.answer: If the course is Analysis and Approaches, the likely reason is that Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and almost all school homework is done with one. The student can set up an integral and cannot evaluate it by hand, so the back half of each question disappears. It is a training gap rather than an ability gap, and it is recoverable in weeks of deliberate non-calculator practice. The usual sign is strong Paper 2 performance alongside weak Paper 1, which a mock script will show immediately.

faqs.question: What does the exploration need to score well on criteria C and D?
faqs.answer: Criterion C is personal engagement, worth 3 marks, and criterion D is reflection, also 3 marks. Both reward the student's own thinking made visible: why this question was chosen, what was surprising, what the approach could not account for. Students lose them by writing a competent report with a conclusion saying the results were as expected. The fix is a checklist built from the criteria wording and a conclusion that evaluates limitations rather than summarising. A tutor may give feedback on the draft; nothing may be written for the student.

faqs.question: How much input may a tutor have on the exploration topic?
faqs.answer: A tutor may discuss whether a proposed topic carries enough mathematics for the level and whether its scope is narrow enough to finish, and may explain what each criterion asks for. A tutor may not choose the topic, supply the mathematics or write any part of the piece. That boundary is stated to the student at the start, because the declaration on the submitted work is theirs. One page ranking in this market sells completed internal assessments outright, which is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does it matter so much at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a one-hour paper with two extended-response questions, calculator permitted, sat by Higher Level students on both courses and worth 20% of the grade. The questions run as long chains where later parts often depend on a structure rather than on the previous numerical answer. A student who stops at a part they cannot do forfeits everything after it. Training the habit of assuming a result and continuing takes roughly four sessions and is the most recoverable 20% in the course.

faqs.question: My child is in DP1 and already behind. What should this term do?
faqs.answer: DP1 is the only term in which calculus and the Higher Level technique list can be built properly rather than patched, so the answer is content, in the right order, starting with whatever the school's term-one assessments exposed. Working out what those assessments exposed is the first session's job. Fixing a DP1 gap costs a fraction of what the same gap costs in DP2 term six, because in term six the only remaining levers are timing and question selection.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week do Diploma families here usually book?
faqs.answer: One a week through DP1 is the normal starting point, rising to two or three during the exploration drafting window and again in the final term before papers. Spending evenly across two years is the common mistake: the hours bought in DP1 term one are highly leveraged because they are building, and the hours bought in term six are expensive per unit of grade movement because only technique remains. A plan that concentrates spend in term four and term six usually outperforms a flat one.

faqs.question: Can we switch from Analysis and Approaches to Applications and Interpretation mid-course?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, depending on the school, and it is painful in all cases because the content diverges quickly and the exploration may already be underway. If a switch is under consideration it needs to happen in the first weeks of DP1 rather than the first months, which means the evidence has to be gathered early. A past Paper 1 sat under timed conditions without a calculator and marked against the official scheme is the cheapest evidence available, and September is the right month for it.

faqs.question: Does a graphic display calculator model make a difference to the grade?
faqs.answer: It makes a difference to the marks available, which amounts to the same thing. Applications and Interpretation assumes a calculator on every paper, so knowing which statistical and graphing functions your model offers, and how fast you can reach them, converts directly into finished questions. On Analysis and Approaches the opposite skill matters for Paper 1. Angle mode is the quiet killer on both courses: a correct method in degrees when the question was in radians produces a confident wrong answer.

faqs.question: How much does IB maths tutoring cost per hour in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 start at AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, and the premium end reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Those are their figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Are the IB exam dates published anywhere reliable?
faqs.answer: Take them from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as this page will be, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate dates that then get republished, and a parent who books flights around one of those is acting on a number nobody has verified. Ask the coordinator; it takes one email.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle maths and physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, often yes, and it is worth asking because continuity helps and scheduling halves. At Higher Level in both subjects it is a narrow request, because genuine depth in Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 and in Physics Higher Level papers is rare in one person, and a tutor who stretches to cover both is a generalist with two labels. We will tell you which case you are in rather than filling the slot, and if the answer is two tutors we will say so.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and long family trips?
faqs.answer: During Ramadan sessions generally move later or to post-Iftar timing and the length shortens, because 45 focused minutes of non-calculator practice is worth more than 90 tired ones. Students sitting papers in the spring usually keep the weekly cadence and change the clock rather than pausing, since a four-week gap late in DP2 is expensive. Long family absences are normal in this corridor, and because delivery is over live video the session follows the student rather than stopping until they return.

faqs.question: What should we do in the fortnight after mock results?
faqs.answer: Get the script back, not just the grade, and sort every lost mark into four categories: content not known, method not shown, arithmetic or calculator-mode slip, and ran out of time. Tally across papers. One category usually dominates, and in maths in this corridor it is more often timing or method presentation than content, which is the recoverable kind. Work that category only for a fixed fortnight, write down the topics being abandoned, and show the list to the student.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingHeading: Tell us the course and the next date
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-nad-al-sheba.closingBody: An IB maths tutor in Nad Al Sheba is worth hiring once you know which of the four dates is next: the course choice, the exploration deadline, the mocks or the papers. Send the course and level, the school, and that date. From there we can say whether a specialist in that exact paper is free, what this term can change, and what it cannot — including the cases where the honest answer is a narrower target rather than more sessions. The first lesson is a free diagnostic on a past-paper section, marked together, with a written note afterwards.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level, for students at the Diploma schools reachable from Oud Metha, Al Jaddaf and Bur Dubai. Each session is held at a fixed hour chosen around the student's own school day rather than around a tutor's route.

intro.heading: A Diploma week in this belt, and where an hour of maths fits
paragraphs: Oud Metha is one of the few parts of Dubai where the school run is genuinely short. The Indian High School sits on the Oud Metha Road, St Mary's Catholic High School and Dubai Gem Private School are a few minutes away, Dubai English Speaking School and Pakistan Education Academy are inside the same loop, and the nearest IB continuum option, Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, is over in Al Jaddaf. Deira International School and Universal American School sit across the creek toward Festival City. A student living in Karama or Al Mankhool is not spending an hour in a car each way.

That short radius creates something valuable and badly used: an early slot. A Diploma student whose teaching day ends mid-afternoon and who is home fifteen minutes later can sit down to Mathematics at around half past three, which is a different student from the one starting at eight in the evening after ninety minutes of traffic from Dubai Silicon Oasis. Fresh working memory is worth more in Mathematics than in almost any other Diploma subject, because the work is sequential - a step missed early stops the rest of the question rather than merely weakening it.

Most families in this belt never take that slot. The default is to push tuition late, after dinner, when the parent is home and the evening feels clear. By then the student has done three hours of homework, and an hour of Analysis and Approaches Higher Level calculus is the last thing a tired fifteen-year-old can absorb. The session happens, the fee is paid, and very little lands. Nobody notices, because the alternative was never tried.

There is a second constraint that a generic tutoring diary ignores completely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates their instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student those periods are inside the school day, competing with six Diploma subjects and the Exploration. The week is tighter than the subject list suggests, and a Mathematics plan that assumes an empty evening is a plan built on a week that does not exist.

So this page is organised around time rather than around price. Which slot suits which school. What the Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation choice does to the number of hours needed. How the papers are weighted, so an hour can be pointed at the component that is actually losing marks. When the Exploration has to be worked on, and what a tutor is permitted to do with it. And how to count a Diploma Mathematics year backwards from the May session so that the hours land in the months where they still change something.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: Four programmes run inside reach of Oud Metha, and each one puts Mathematics in a different place in the week. The timetable consequence matters as much as the syllabus content when you are choosing a session slot.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three usually at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement. Mathematics is compulsory, taken as either Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. The Exploration is an internally assessed piece of the student's own work, and its internal deadline is set by the school rather than by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the Diploma sits inside a private sector of 227 schools and 387,441 pupils, with IB programmes accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. Diploma students in this belt frequently travel further to school than their IGCSE siblings, because the nearest Diploma provision is in Al Jaddaf or across the creek rather than on the Oud Metha Road itself. That extra travel is exactly what decides whether an early session is available.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year programme ahead of the Diploma, assessed against four criteria per subject on a 1-8 scale rather than by terminal papers. MYP Mathematics runs Standard and Extended routes in the final years, and the Extended route is the one that makes Analysis and Approaches Higher Level realistic later. Criterion A knowing and understanding is the one most reliably moved by targeted work.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 new places, with enrolment up 6 per cent during 2025-26. For Oud Metha families that means more continuum capacity arriving within reach, and more students arriving in Diploma year one from an MYP background rather than from IGCSE.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: The route most students in the Oud Metha school belt take to sixteen before splitting into the Diploma or A Level. Mathematics 0580 is tiered Core and Extended; Pearson Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher. Additional Mathematics 0606 is the optional extra that introduces calculus and logarithms early, and it is the single best predictor of a comfortable start in Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: Because so many schools in this belt run IGCSE while the Diploma schools sit slightly further out, a large share of local Diploma students arrive from a different campus to the one they spent Years 10 and 11 in. Their school day lengthens, the commute lengthens, and the family's old tuition slot stops working. That is usually the term when parents start searching.

programmes.name: A Level, the local alternative at sixteen
programmes.description: The other post-sixteen route taken by students from these schools, with Mathematics and Further Mathematics as separate qualifications rather than one compulsory subject at two routes and two levels. Students who find the Diploma's breadth unmanageable sometimes move across, and the mathematics content maps onto Analysis and Approaches more closely than onto Applications and Interpretation.
programmes.countryNote: Worth knowing when a family is weighing the two at the end of Year 11 in Oud Metha. A student who is strong at mathematics but stretched by six subjects plus Extended Essay plus Theory of Knowledge is making a timetable decision, not a mathematics decision, and the two are often confused in that conversation.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Mathematics in the Diploma is not one subject. It is two routes at two levels, with an internally assessed Exploration attached, and the number of hours a student needs depends far more on which combination they are sitting than on who is teaching it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The heaviest mathematics option in the Diploma. Calculus is the spine, with proof, complex numbers and series on top. Students who arrive without Additional Mathematics 0606 or MYP Extended Mathematics behind them typically need a front-loaded block of work in Diploma year one rather than a steady weekly hour.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency, functions, trigonometry, differentiation and integration, with a smaller statistics component. The common failure is procedural: a student who can differentiate cannot always tell from a worded question that differentiation is what is wanted. Question interpretation is the cheap fix here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, matrices and graph theory carry far more weight than in Analysis and Approaches, and technology use is assumed throughout. Students who choose it to avoid calculus are sometimes surprised by the statistical inference content, which rewards precision in interpretation rather than algebraic speed.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The route for students whose degree plans do not name mathematics, built around modelling real contexts and using technology properly. Marks are lost on communicating a model's limitations rather than on the arithmetic, which is a writing skill as much as a mathematical one.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: An internally assessed piece of the student's own mathematical writing, marked against published criteria. The two places students lose most are personal engagement and reflection, both of which require a topic the student genuinely owns. A tutor may coach the process and question the reasoning; a tutor may not write any of it.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, Extended route
subjects.description: The preparation that decides whether Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is realistic. The Extended route carries the algebraic depth the Diploma assumes. Students on the Standard route who want Higher Level later need the gap closed deliberately, usually across a summer rather than in a term.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: The optional IGCSE course that introduces calculus, logarithms and matrices before Year 12. Funding this at sixteen frequently removes the need for a remedial block in Diploma year one, which makes it the cheapest mathematics decision available to a family in this belt.

subjects.name: Mathematics for Physics HL
subjects.description: Physics Higher Level assumes mathematical handling that Applications and Interpretation Standard Level does not teach. Students taking both sometimes need a short bridging block on functions, graphs and algebraic rearrangement so that the physics is not limited by the maths.

subjects.name: Quantitative work in Economics HL
subjects.description: Economics Higher Level carries diagrammatic and calculation work that trips students who chose it as a non-mathematical subject. A handful of targeted sessions on graph interpretation and percentage reasoning usually resolves it without a separate mathematics plan.

subjects.name: Pre-Diploma bridging
subjects.description: A short block before the Diploma starts, aimed at the specific gap between the student's IGCSE or MYP route and the mathematics option they have chosen. It is the only mathematics work that reliably prevents a crisis in the October of Diploma year one, and it needs no timetable space at all.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.regionsTitle: The commute each neighbourhood actually has
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.regionsIntro: What time a Mathematics session can start depends on the journey, and in this part of Dubai the journeys differ more than the map suggests. Below is what each neighbourhood near Oud Metha does to a weekday afternoon.

regions.name: Oud Metha
regions.note: Walking distance or a few minutes by car to the main school belt. This is where the half-past-three Mathematics slot is genuinely available, and almost nobody uses it. A student home by three can work a full hour before fatigue sets in.

regions.name: Karama
regions.note: Dense and close, with short pick-up times and minimal traffic exposure on the way home. The practical constraint here is apartment noise and shared study space rather than travel, which argues for the early slot before siblings are home.

regions.name: Al Mankhool
regions.note: Just across the Al Mankhool Road, with Ambassador School and the Bur Dubai provision nearby. Afternoons work well; the difficulty is the 4pm to 6pm congestion on the approaches if a student is coming back from a Diploma school further out.

regions.name: Al Jaddaf and Dubai Healthcare City
regions.note: Home to Swiss International Scientific School Dubai, so some Diploma students here have no commute at all. Parents working clinic shifts in Healthcare City often need a slot that can move week to week, which online delivery handles and a fixed in-home visit does not.

regions.name: Bur Dubai
regions.note: Mixed provision and a high proportion of multi-child households. Where two children need different subjects, the workable pattern is back-to-back hours with two specialists rather than one tutor stretched across both, and that only works if the first hour starts early.

regions.note: The crossing toward Festival City and Deira International School. The 4pm to 6pm window on the creek approaches regularly adds twenty minutes to a journey that looks like ten, which is why a 4.30pm start quietly becomes a 4.50pm start.

regions.name: Al Nasr and Za'abeel
regions.note: Between Oud Metha and the Trade Centre, with a working-parent profile that pushes sessions toward seven o'clock. For Mathematics specifically that is the slot to resist if any earlier option exists, because the subject punishes tiredness harder than essay subjects do.

regions.name: Al Qusais and Al Nahda
regions.note: Further along the Green Line, with a large Indian-curriculum cohort and a longer run home. A student commuting from a Diploma school across town to Al Qusais realistically starts at five, and the plan should be built for five rather than pretending otherwise.

schoolClusters.city: Diploma and continuum schools within reach
schoolClusters.note: These are the campuses an Oud Metha Diploma student most often travels to. Their end-of-day times and their distance from this belt are what set the earliest workable Mathematics slot, so confirm your own school's time before locking an hour.

schoolClusters.city: The Oud Metha and Bur Dubai school belt
schoolClusters.note: The schools on the Oud Metha Road and immediately around it, feeding IGCSE and then splitting toward the Diploma or A Level. Students still at these campuses have the shortest journeys in the district and the best access to an early session.

sections.heading: Which slot each school actually leaves open
paragraphs: A Mathematics session in Oud Metha can realistically start between half past three and five o'clock, and which end of that range you get is decided by the school, not by the tutor. Students still at the Oud Metha Road campuses are home quickest. Students who travel to a Diploma school in Al Jaddaf, Festival City or Nad Al Sheba lose the early slot to the journey, and the family that keeps trying to book it ends up rescheduling every second week.

The most useful thing a parent can do before fixing an hour is write down three times: when the teaching day ends, when the student is actually through the front door, and when the school's own after-hours commitments fall. That third one catches most people out. Revision clinics, sports fixtures, Creativity Activity Service commitments and Extended Essay supervision meetings all land on specific weekdays, and a Mathematics hour booked on top of one of them will be cancelled before the term is out.

Then pick the subject to the slot rather than the slot to the subject. Mathematics is sequential and unforgiving of a missed step, so it belongs in the freshest hour available. An essay subject tolerates an eight o'clock session far better. Families with two tutors across two subjects should put Mathematics in the earlier of the two hours, every time, even if the other subject's grade is currently worse.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, and what each costs in hours
paragraphs: The choice between the two Mathematics routes is made at the end of Year 11, usually in a hurried conversation, and it determines more about the next two years than the choice of tutor does. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and calculus-led route. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology-led route. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and both are accepted as the Diploma's mathematics requirement, but they are not interchangeable where a degree names mathematics.

The practical question for a family in Oud Metha is what each route demands of the week. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level is front-loaded: the calculus arrives early and everything later depends on it, so a student who starts behind compounds the deficit through the whole of Diploma year one. Applications and Interpretation Higher Level distributes the difficulty more evenly but demands precision in interpretation and in the written communication of a model's limits, which some strong algebraists find harder than the algebra.

Where this becomes a timetable issue rather than a syllabus one: a student on the wrong route needs more hours than a student on the right route with a weaker start. Switching after the October of Diploma year one is possible at some schools and impossible at others, and the deadline is set by the school. If there is doubt, resolve it before Year 12 begins, using the summer bridging block to test both rather than guessing from an IGCSE grade.

Check the stated entry requirements of the universities your child is actually considering, including the UAE institutions, rather than relying on a general rule. Requirements are set by each institution and do change.

sections.heading: Pointing an hour at the component that is losing the marks
paragraphs: Diploma Mathematics is assessed through written papers plus the internally assessed Exploration, and the papers differ in what they reward. One is sat without technology, one with; Higher Level carries an additional paper that Standard Level does not. The exact weightings are published by the IB and are stated on your school's own subject outline, so confirm them there - this page names components and what each demands rather than restating percentages that a parent should read from the authoritative document.

What matters for an hour of tuition is that the components fail differently. A student who is strong on technique but slow loses marks on the technology-free paper through arithmetic under time pressure. A student who is fluent with a calculator but shaky on structure loses marks on the paper where a method has to be laid out to earn method marks. A student who understands the mathematics perfectly can still lose a third of the available marks on the Exploration by not addressing the criteria that are actually being marked.

So the first job of a Mathematics tutor is diagnostic and it takes one session, not a term. Put a past paper in front of the student under time, mark it honestly against the official mark scheme, and separate the losses into four buckets: content not known, method not shown, question misread, and time mismanaged. Three of those four are technique problems and move faster than content problems do. Families who skip this step buy content teaching for a technique failure and wonder why the grade sits still.

sections.heading: Counting a Diploma Mathematics year backwards
paragraphs: Mathematics work has a shape across the two years, and most families start it at the wrong point in that shape. The intuitive moment to hire a tutor is after a poor report, which usually means late in Diploma year one or early in year two. By then the Exploration deadline is close, the calculus that year two depends on is already assumed, and the hours available before the May session are finite.

Working backwards produces a different plan. The May session is the one UAE Diploma schools sit, so the final stretch is the spring of year two. Before that sits the mock window, which the school sets. Before that sits the Exploration's internal deadline, also set by the school and usually earlier than students expect. Before that sits the whole of year one, which is where the content that year two assumes is either secured or quietly skipped.

A word on dates, because this is where tutoring pages do real damage. No IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, because ibo.org blocks automated fetching. So no specific IB exam or results date is published here. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly, and treat any tutoring page that states a precise IB date without a source as unreliable on everything else too.

For the Cambridge and Pearson qualifications sat before the Diploma, the published position is firmer. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. sections.heading: The Exploration: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: The Mathematical Exploration is the part of the Diploma Mathematics grade that is entirely in the student's hands, and it is the part most exposed to bad help. It is written at home, over weeks, against published criteria, and the temptation to let somebody else shape it is obvious. IB academic-honesty rules make that a malpractice question, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever helped.

The boundary is clean and worth stating in plain terms. A tutor may explain what each assessment criterion rewards. A tutor may discuss whether a proposed topic can sustain the required mathematics. A tutor may model a technique on an entirely different example. A tutor may read the student's own draft and ask questions about reasoning that does not hold. A tutor may point out that a section does not address the criterion it is meant to address. IB Gram tutors do not write, rewrite, draft or complete any part of an Exploration, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or coursework.

In practice the marks students lose on the Exploration are not mathematical at all. They are lost on personal engagement, where a borrowed topic reads as borrowed, and on reflection, where a student describes what they did instead of evaluating what it showed. Both are fixed by choosing a topic the student actually cares about early enough to change it, which is a scheduling decision as much as an academic one - and it is why Exploration sessions belong in the calendar months before the school's internal deadline, not in the fortnight before it.

We also do not supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Those are published and owned by the IB, your school holds the current versions, and a tutor's work is to teach against them. Several operations ranking for these searches do otherwise, and one sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For the student, that is a malpractice finding.

sections.heading: What an hour costs here, and what the travel in it is worth
paragraphs: Start from minutes rather than dirhams, because in this district the minutes are the interesting part. An in-home Mathematics tutor arriving at an Oud Metha apartment at five o'clock has to be somewhere at four, cannot be anywhere else at six, and prices that constraint into the hour. The published Dubai range for in-home one-to-one tuition including travel is AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home at AED 180 to 350 and specialist provision at AED 200 to 450 or more; TutorChase publishes AED 270; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 at the budget end; BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tuition. All read in October 2026, all theirs rather than ours.

What the travel premium buys in Oud Metha is not distance - the drives here are short. It buys a committed arrival time from whichever qualified person is willing to sell one in this postcode at that hour. That pool is small, and a small pool prices itself. The parent is paying for scarcity rather than for mileage, and for Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specifically, the scarcity is severe: the number of people who can teach Higher Level calculus well and will drive to Karama at five o'clock is not large.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Mathematics sessions for Oud Metha students run one-to-one over live video, which is what makes an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist available to a family whose fifteen-minute radius contains none. The practical gain is not only the rate. It is that the session can be moved inside the same week when a school adds a mock, which is the week it matters most.

Monthly packages give a cleaner comparison than hourly rates. One Dubai provider publishes AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, roughly AED 100 an hour. In-home monthly packages in the same market are advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits, roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour for the same eight hours of teaching. Nothing in that gap is mathematics.
