sections.heading: The week nobody budgets for: mandatory subjects and Ramadan
paragraphs: A Diploma timetable looks like six subjects. In a Dubai private school it is six subjects plus a mandatory block that is not optional and not negotiable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose academic year begins in April.

KHDA is precise about how that block runs, and the detail affects when a student is actually free. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

The second thing a generic diary misses is Ramadan. School hours shorten, the shape of the day changes, and energy moves to after Iftar. A Mathematics slot that works in November does not work in Ramadan, and the families who plan for it keep their continuity while the ones who do not lose a month. The sensible approach is to agree in advance that the slot moves to a post-Iftar time for that period and then moves back, rather than cancelling and trying to restart.

The third is the school's own calendar. Mock weeks, Creativity Activity Service deadlines, Extended Essay supervision meetings and school trips all consume evenings. Ask for the term calendar at the start of term and book the Mathematics hour into a weekday that the school has not already claimed. It takes ten minutes and it is the difference between twelve sessions in a term and eight.

sections.heading: Regulators, permits and what you can check before the first session
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak. That report is published, it is free to read, and it tells you what the school is strong and weak at - which is useful information when deciding what to buy tuition for. If the inspection says mathematics attainment is a strength at your child's school, the school's own provision may already cover what you were about to pay for.

Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project, which is a reasonable measure of how thin the rest of this search result is.

On the tutor side, there is one check a parent can make directly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

One thing to be clear about: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific instrument with its own renewal cycle. Any page in this search result describing its tutors as approved by a regulator is making a claim worth asking it to evidence.

process.title: Send the timetable, not just the grade

A half-past-three session and an eight o'clock session are different products with the same name, and the trial is the cheap way to find out which one this student can work in.

process.description: A past paper under time, marked against the official mark scheme, sorted into content not known, method not shown, question misread and time mismanaged. Three of those four are technique and move faster than content. The plan is built from that split rather than from a guess.

process.title: Fix the hour and defend it
process.description: Same weekday, same time, through the term, chosen against the school calendar so nothing routinely collides with it. Agree in advance what happens in Ramadan and in mock weeks, so the slot moves deliberately rather than quietly disappearing.

process.title: Review against school marks, not impressions
process.description: Progress is judged on the student's own school assessments and mocks. If the marks have not moved across a block of sessions, the plan changes or the tutor does, and we would rather say that than sell another term on the strength of sessions that feel productive.

whyPoints.description: Oud Metha's short commute makes an early Mathematics hour genuinely available, and Mathematics is the subject that benefits most from it. We choose the slot from your child's timetable and the school's term calendar rather than from a tutor's route across Dubai.

We match on the route and level on your school's option form, because a tutor fluent in the other one looks convincing for about six weeks.

faqs.question: What time can an IB Maths session realistically start for a student in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Between about half past three and five o'clock, depending on where the school is. A student at one of the Oud Metha Road campuses can be at a desk by half past three, which is the strongest hour in the day for Mathematics. A student travelling back from Festival City or Nad Al Sheba at peak realistically starts at a quarter to five or five. Check three things before you fix the slot: when the teaching day ends, when your child is actually home, and which weekdays the school has already claimed with clinics or fixtures.

faqs.question: Why does the time of day matter more for Maths than for other Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Because the work is sequential. In an essay subject a tired student produces weaker writing but still follows the lesson. In Analysis and Approaches, a step missed early stops the rest of the question rather than merely weakening it, so a session on new calculus at eight in the evening after three hours of homework often transfers almost nothing. Families running two tutors across two subjects should put Mathematics in the earlier hour every time, even when the other subject's grade currently looks worse. The slot is a teaching decision, not a convenience one.

faqs.question: Which Diploma maths route leaves a student in this belt needing fewer hours?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the degree routes your child is actually considering and check each named institution's own published requirement, because they differ and they change. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and calculus route, front-loaded in Diploma year one. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route, spread more evenly but demanding precision in written interpretation. Preparation predicts comfort: Additional Mathematics 0606 or MYP Extended Mathematics behind a student makes Analysis and Approaches Higher Level realistic. Resolve any doubt before Year 12 starts, because switching deadlines are set by the school and are often early.

faqs.question: My child is moving from IGCSE to the Diploma. When should Maths support start?
faqs.answer: In the summer before Diploma year one, and it is the most useful mathematics money a family in this belt can spend. A short bridging block closes the specific gap between the IGCSE route taken and the Diploma option chosen, needs no term-time slot at all, and prevents the October crisis that sends most families searching in the first place. For Analysis and Approaches that means calculus, functions and algebraic fluency; for Applications and Interpretation it means statistics and modelling fundamentals. Scope it from what your child actually took rather than from a generic syllabus.

faqs.question: How many Maths sessions a week does a Diploma student in this area usually need?
faqs.answer: One well-placed hour a week carries most students through Diploma year one, provided it is in a fresh slot and the work set between sessions is actually done. Two a week makes sense in three situations: a student who started the route behind, a Higher Level student in the term before the mock window, and the final stretch before the May session where timed practice needs more volume than one hour allows. More than two a week usually signals a route or level problem rather than a teaching problem, and that is worth diagnosing before buying more hours.

faqs.question: Where exactly does legitimate Exploration coaching stop?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may explain what each assessment criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposed topic can sustain the required mathematics, model a technique on a different example, read the student's own draft and question reasoning that does not hold. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete any part of it. IB Gram tutors do not produce assessed work. The marks students actually lose on the Exploration are usually on personal engagement and reflection rather than on the mathematics, and those are fixed by owning the topic early enough to change it.

faqs.question: Which part of the Diploma Maths assessment should we target first?
faqs.answer: The one that is losing marks, which takes one timed paper to identify rather than a term to guess. Mark it honestly against the official mark scheme and sort the losses into four buckets: content not known, method not shown, question misread, and time mismanaged. Three of those four are technique and move faster than content does. Confirm the component weightings from your school's subject outline rather than from a tutoring page. A student who understands the mathematics and still loses a third of the marks is almost always losing them to the last three buckets.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education block affect our session planning?
faqs.answer: It affects the week more than most families account for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, with KHDA's requirements due from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Those periods sit inside the school day alongside six Diploma subjects, so the student is more tightly timetabled than the subject list suggests. Plan the Mathematics hour against the real timetable.

faqs.question: What happens to our weekly Maths slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It should move deliberately rather than quietly lapse. School hours shorten, the shape of the day changes and useful working energy moves to after Iftar, so a slot that works in November will not work unchanged. Agree before Ramadan starts that the session shifts to a post-Iftar time for that period and returns afterwards. Families who plan this keep continuity through a month that otherwise costs them four sessions and the momentum with them. Online delivery makes the shift straightforward; a fixed in-home arrival window is the hardest thing in the week to move.

faqs.question: Is an in-home Maths tutor worth the premium when the drive in Oud Metha is so short?
faqs.answer: The premium is real and the drive is not what you are paying for. Published Dubai rates put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online tutor, read October 2026. In this district the journeys are short, so the premium reflects scarcity: the number of people who can teach Higher Level calculus well and will commit to arriving in Karama at five o'clock is small, and a small pool prices itself. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; sessions run online, one-to-one.

faqs.question: Will my child actually engage in a Maths lesson over video?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the hour contains far more than on the format. A session spent watching an explanation loses any teenager, in a kitchen or on a screen. A session where the student is working problems with their written work screen-shared and marked line by line holds attention, because they are the one doing the work and the feedback is immediate. For Mathematics specifically, shared digital working can be clearer than a notebook at the edge of a table. Take the free trial in the slot you intend to keep and judge this student rather than the medium.

faqs.question: Does my child's school inspection rating tell us anything useful about tutoring?
faqs.answer: It tells you what not to buy. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai and inspects on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the reports are published and free to read. If the report names mathematics attainment as a strength at your child's school, the school's own provision may already cover the ground you were about to pay for, and your money is better spent on technique or on the Exploration process. If it names mathematics as an area for improvement, a specialist weekly hour is doing more work.

faqs.question: How do we verify that a Maths tutor is legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask directly, and know what the answer should look like. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Because the permit costs nothing, no part of a quoted rate is a permit fee. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can you tell us the IB exam and results dates so we can plan backwards?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and we will not invent them. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and publishing one anyway would put a date a family acts on behind a guess. Take yours from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org. What we can plan around are the school-set milestones, which are the ones that actually govern the work: the Exploration internal deadline, the mock window, and the end-of-year-one audit of what year two will assume.

faqs.question: My child is strong at Maths but drowning in six Diploma subjects. Is a Maths tutor the answer?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, and it is worth saying so before taking the booking. A student who handles the mathematics but cannot fit the Diploma's breadth into a week has a timetable problem, and more mathematics hours make the week worse rather than better. The conversation to have is with the school about subject levels, and sometimes about whether the Diploma or A Level suits this student. If the mathematics is genuinely the pressure point, a short diagnostic block will show it within three sessions rather than a term.

faqs.question: What do you need from us before the first Maths session?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which takes long. The Mathematics route and level from your school's option form, so the match is exact. The school name and the end-of-day time, so the slot is realistic. The school's term calendar, so the hour is not booked onto a weekday already claimed by clinics, fixtures or supervision meetings. And the most recent piece of marked mathematics work, however bad, because a marked script tells a tutor more in five minutes than a report comment does. The trial lesson then starts from evidence rather than from a description.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Pick the hour first, then the tutor
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: Most Mathematics tuition in this part of Dubai underperforms for a scheduling reason rather than a teaching one. The session sits too late in the day, lands on a weekday the school has already claimed, and quietly becomes the appointment that moves. Fix that first: find the earliest hour your child is genuinely home and alert, check it against the school's term calendar, and hold it. Then take a free trial lesson in that exact slot with a tutor matched to your child's Mathematics route and level, bring one piece of marked work, and let the diagnosis set the length of the plan. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

intro.heading: Where the money goes, and where it should go
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject Palm Jumeirah families spend the most on and the one where the spending is aimed worst. The pattern is consistent. A student starts the Diploma, the first set of marks is lower than the family expected, and an hour a week is bought at whatever rate seems reasonable. Six months later the marks are broadly where they were, the family concludes that the tutor was wrong, and a more expensive tutor is bought. Nothing in that sequence involved finding out what was actually wrong, which is the only thing that would have changed the outcome.

There are four or five distinct problems that all present as a weak mathematics grade, and they cost wildly different amounts to fix. Procedural slowness - algebra, indices, rearrangement - is cheap and quick, because it is drill. Conceptual gaps in a specific topic are moderate, because they are teaching. Method-mark illiteracy, where a student gets right answers and loses marks for not showing the route, is the cheapest of all and takes about three weeks. Wrong course choice is the most expensive, because no amount of tutoring fixes being on Higher Level Analysis and Approaches when Applications and Interpretation was the right route. Exam management is free to diagnose and takes practice rather than teaching.

This page prices each of those honestly and sets out how many hours each plausibly takes. It also publishes the Dubai market bands with the provider who published each figure attached, because three of the six competitor pages examined for this cluster quote no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a UAE family transacts in. And it explains the in-home travel premium specifically, because Palm Jumeirah is one of the addresses in Dubai where that premium is largest and least visible.

There is a particular reason the island matters to a mathematics decision rather than a geography one. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists are among the scarcest tutors in the emirate, and the subset of them willing to drive onto the fronds at six in the evening is smaller still. Selecting from that subset means paying a travel premium for a smaller pool, which is the worst of both arrangements. Selecting by course and level instead removes the premium and widens the pool, which is why our model is what it is.

Stated once and plainly: tutoring for UAE families is one-to-one and live online, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. On a page about cost that is the central argument rather than a footnote, because the published figures show exactly what the travel inside an in-home rate is worth, and it is not teaching.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through every stage of the IB sequence and the cost question looks different at each one. These are the programmes we support from Palm Jumeirah.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four courses: Analysis and Approaches at Standard and Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard and Higher Level. Standard Level sits two examination papers; Higher Level sits three. All four include an internally assessed mathematical exploration marked against published criteria. The course and level decide what a tutoring hour has to do, which is why no sensible quote exists before the course is named.
programmes.countryNote: Palm Jumeirah students reach Diploma campuses in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Sufouh and along the Jumeirah coast. Three of the seven new private schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 run International Baccalaureate programmes. None of that changes the scarcity of Higher Level Analysis and Approaches teachers, which is an absolute shortage rather than a distribution problem.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria including investigating patterns and applying mathematics in real-life contexts, which is a broader brief than procedural fluency and a thinner one on drill. Support here is cheap relative to Diploma support and prevents the most expensive problem of all, because a student who leaves MYP 5 without automatic algebra meets that wall in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: The single best-value mathematics purchase available to an island family is a short block between MYP 5 and DP1, aimed at algebraic fluency and index laws. Eight to twelve hours there removes the problem that otherwise generates a year of DP1 tutoring at a higher rate. Almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Cambridge 0580 and 0607 International Mathematics, and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, with Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure 4PM1 taken alongside by students heading for a mathematical sixth form. The grade earned here governs which Diploma mathematics course a campus will allow, which makes it a financial decision as well as an academic one.
programmes.countryNote: A student entering the Diploma from a Core-tier or single-award background faces a genuine gap into Analysis and Approaches, and campuses usually set an entry grade for the Higher Level route. Ask the sixth form what grade it requires for each of the four mathematics courses, in writing, during Year 10 rather than Year 11.

programmes.name: A Level mathematics, for comparison
programmes.description: The alternative route at several campuses the island commutes to, and worth naming because families comparing cost should compare the whole two years rather than the hourly rate. A Level mathematics has no internally assessed project, so there is no exploration to support, which removes a real block of tutoring hours from the budget.
programmes.countryNote: That difference is worth money. A Diploma mathematics student needs exploration support spread across several months; an A Level mathematics student does not. Families weighing the two routes on an island budget should factor it in alongside the subject breadth the Diploma requires.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.subjectsIntro: These are the mathematics courses and the subjects whose grades move with them. The note on each one is about where tutoring hours pay back, because that is the decision a family is actually making.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers, with Paper 3 asking extended problem-solving on unfamiliar ground. The scarcest tutoring match in the emirate and the one where the specialist band is genuinely earned. Marks go on unwritten method lines and on Paper 3 questions abandoned rather than attempted in parts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers, one without a calculator. The commonest Diploma mathematics course on the island and well served in the middle rate band. Most of the recoverable marks sit in algebraic accuracy and in showing a method rather than in new content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling heavy, with a substantial calculator component and a third paper. Students who arrive expecting an easier Higher Level course are usually surprised by the volume of interpretation required in writing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Often the right course for students heading to business, social science or design, and often chosen late by students struggling with the Analysis route. Switching is cheaper than persisting, and the last sensible date for it is set by the school.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: The internally assessed component, marked against published criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Needs hours spread over months rather than a block before the deadline, and the writing must be entirely the student's own.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject whose grade moves most when mathematics improves. Formula rearrangement, unit conversion and graph gradients are mathematics skills examined inside physics papers, which means a mathematics block frequently returns marks in two subjects.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, significant figures and logarithmic work in acids and bases. A student with slow algebra is slow in chemistry too, and families who buy chemistry hours for an arithmetic problem pay twice for one fix.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level carries quantitative work that catches students who chose Applications and Interpretation expecting to avoid calculation. Diagram accuracy and numerical interpretation both improve with mathematics fluency rather than with more economics content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Taken alongside mathematics by students heading for engineering or computing. The internal assessment is a software solution and the marks sit largely in documentation, which is a different purchase from mathematics teaching.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Includes finance and ratio work that students on the Applications and Interpretation route handle comfortably and students avoiding numbers do not. Worth naming when a family is choosing a sixth subject on cost and workload grounds.

sections.heading: What you are actually buying in an hour of IB maths support
paragraphs: An hour of mathematics tutoring can be spent on one of about six things, and they are not interchangeable. Diagnosis. Re-teaching a topic. Drilling procedural fluency. Past-paper technique and method marks. Calculator skill. Exploration coaching. Each one changes something different, each takes a different number of hours, and each is worth a different amount depending on what is actually wrong with the student in front of you. Buying hours without naming which of the six you are buying is how a Palm Jumeirah family spends a year without moving a grade.

The table below is the most useful thing on this page. Read the last column first, because it is the one nobody tells you: what each kind of hour cannot change. Drilling fluency will not fix a wrong course choice. Re-teaching topics will not fix method-mark illiteracy. Exploration coaching will not improve examination performance. Past-paper technique will not install algebra that was never automatic. A tutor who offers a single undifferentiated hour is offering an average of six things, and averages are expensive.

The hour counts in the table are from our own matching experience rather than from a published study, and they are deliberately ranges. What they are good for is sizing a decision. If the diagnosis says method marks, the honest answer is about six hours and a family should not be sold thirty. If it says a wrong course, the honest answer is a conversation with the school rather than any tutoring at all. If it says conceptual gaps across three topics in DP2, the honest answer is a larger number and a family deserves to see it before committing rather than discovering it in instalments.

One warning about the sequence. Families almost always want to start with re-teaching, because it feels like the substance. Starting with diagnosis feels like a delay and is in fact the only step that makes the others efficient. A single hour spent finding out which of the six problems exists typically saves between five and fifteen hours of the wrong work, which at the published Dubai specialist band of AED 200 to 450 an hour is a straightforwardly good trade.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that costs more than any tutor
paragraphs: No tutoring decision an island family makes matters as much as this one, and it is usually made at sixteen on incomplete information. The two courses are genuinely different subjects rather than harder and easier versions of one. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, with a non-calculator paper at both levels. Applications and Interpretation is statistical and modelling-oriented, with a calculator permitted throughout and a heavier burden of written interpretation. A student on the wrong one does not need a better tutor; they need a different course.

The financial consequence is large and nobody frames it that way. A student placed on Higher Level Analysis and Approaches who should be on Standard Level Applications and Interpretation can absorb two years of weekly specialist tutoring at the published AED 200 to 450 band and still finish in the lower bands, because the gap is structural. The same student moved to the right course in the first term of DP1 may need no tutoring at all. That is the single most expensive error available in Diploma mathematics and it is reversible for a window that the school sets.

So the question to ask the campus is practical: what are the entry requirements for each of the four courses, what is the last date a change can be made, and what evidence would be needed? That evidence is where tutoring genuinely helps. Six weeks of marked work at the target level, with the marks recorded, is a stronger case to a head of mathematics than any conversation, and it works in both directions - it can also demonstrate that a student is coping and should stay.

University requirements belong in the same conversation and are set by the receiving institution rather than by the school or by us. Some engineering and mathematics programmes specify Analysis and Approaches; some accept either; some name a minimum subject grade rather than only a total. Open the admissions pages of the target universities and write the mathematics requirement into one document before the course is chosen. Where a UAE institution is on the list, check the Ministry of Education equivalency route separately, because recognition and admission are different processes and tutoring is a requirement of neither.

sections.heading: Calculator and non-calculator are two separate purchases
paragraphs: Families treat mathematics as one skill and the examination does not. Analysis and Approaches includes a paper sat without a calculator, where fluent algebra and arithmetic are the whole game, and a paper where a graphic display calculator is permitted and the skill is knowing which function to reach for and how to present the result. Applications and Interpretation allows a calculator throughout, which shifts the burden onto interpretation and onto presenting calculator output as reasoning rather than as an answer.

The practical consequence is that a student can be strong on one paper and weak on the other, and the remedy for each is different. The non-calculator weakness is fluency and it responds to timed drill, which is cheap. The calculator weakness is technique and it responds to being taught the machine properly, which is cheaper still and almost never taught, because teachers assume students who grew up with devices will work it out. They do not. Students lose marks reaching for the wrong function under time and then write down a number with no reasoning attached.

Presentation is the third element and the one worth the most marks per hour of work. A calculator paper answer that gives a correct value with no indication of what was done earns less than one that states the function used and the values entered. A non-calculator answer that reaches the right number in one leap loses the method marks along the route. Teaching a student to write the method line before the answer is a three-week habit change that applies to every paper in every course, and it is the cheapest mark recovery in Diploma mathematics.

Look at the table and then at your child's last two paper marks separately rather than at the overall grade. If the gap between the calculator and non-calculator papers is more than a band, the diagnosis is sitting in plain sight, and the hours should go to one of them rather than being spread across both. That is a free piece of analysis any parent can do with the marked papers already in the house.

sections.heading: Four diagnoses that all look like being bad at maths
paragraphs: A parent describing the problem will usually say that their child has lost confidence in mathematics, or has always found it hard, or was fine until the Diploma started. None of those is a diagnosis, and treating them as one is how money gets spent on the wrong hours. There are four distinct conditions underneath, they are separable in a single session, and they cost different amounts.

The first is procedural slowness. The student understands what is being asked, knows the approach, and cannot execute the algebra fast enough or accurately enough under time. In DP1 this is extremely common and it almost always originates in a curriculum transition, from MYP or from a British Key Stage where the investigation and application work was richer than the drill. It is the cheapest condition to fix and the one families least expect, because the student sounds knowledgeable when they explain their thinking.

The second is a genuine topic gap, usually in two or three places rather than everywhere. Calculus, trigonometric identities and probability are the recurring ones. This is real teaching and it costs real hours, three to six per topic, and it should be bought topic by topic against a list rather than as an open commitment. The third is method-mark illiteracy, where the student is getting answers right and losing marks for showing nothing, and it is the cheapest of all to fix. The fourth is exam management: answering in order, abandoning Paper 3 parts, no time check, and no plausibility check on the final number.

What makes this worth writing down is that the four have different price tags and families default to buying the second, which is the most expensive. In a diagnostic session a competent tutor separates them by watching the student work rather than by asking questions, because a student's description of their own difficulty is almost always wrong. One hour, honestly reported, is what stands between a thirty-hour plan and a six-hour one, and an island family deciding between those is deciding something worth several thousand dirhams.

sections.heading: The exploration: hours, milestones and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is the internally assessed component of all four courses, marked against published criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Confirm the current criterion wording and weighting against your child's subject guide, because the IB revises guides on a cycle. What does not change is the cost shape: the exploration needs a modest number of hours spread across several months, and it is ruinously expensive to support in a single block before the school's deadline.

The failure mode is always the same and it is a scoping failure. A student picks a topic they find interesting and which contains almost no mathematics at the right level, writes eighteen pages about it, and discovers in the final week that the use-of-mathematics criterion has nothing to reward. Fixing that late means starting again, which is where a family suddenly buys twelve hours in a fortnight at the specialist band. Fixing it in the first two weeks costs about two hours and is the single highest-return intervention in the whole component.

The hours are better understood as milestones than as a total. Topic generation and a mathematical feasibility check. A narrowed research direction with the mathematics identified. A first attempt at the mathematics, which is where most topics are revealed as too thin or too hard. Drafting, written by the student. A feedback pass against the criteria. A reflection pass, because reflection is a criterion in its own right and is almost always written last and thinnest. Spread across months, that is six to ten hours, and it fits comfortably inside a weekly slot that exists anyway.

Now the boundary, stated so nobody has to infer it. A tutor may explain each criterion and what the next band requires. A tutor may say plainly that a topic will not produce enough mathematics, which is the most valuable thing they will say all year. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration needs, the conventions of mathematical writing, and how to reflect in a way the criteria credit. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and give feedback on it. A tutor may not write any part of it, redraft the student's sentences, supply the structure, or produce the mathematics for the student to copy. The test is whether your child could explain and defend every line. The subject teacher is the supervisor of record and the school's deadlines govern.

sections.heading: What the Dubai market charges for IB maths, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Start with the premium, because it is the figure island families pay without seeing. A qualified subject tutor working online is published in Dubai at AED 150 to 300 an hour. An in-home one-to-one visit is published at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure - Bestimate reports AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500. The gap between those two bands is the car. For a Palm Jumeirah address, and particularly for a frond or Crescent address, the tutor is absorbing fifty minutes or more of round trip, and no business absorbs that without pricing it.

Monthly packages make the same point more starkly. The market shows roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour home visits. That is the same eight hours of teaching, at double the price, with the difference going to a journey. A family is entitled to decide that a person in the room is worth that, and some genuinely are - a younger child, a student who will not engage with a screen. For a DP2 student working on Paper 3 technique, it buys nothing the lesson needs.

The rest of the ladder, read from providers' own pages in October 2026. Budget online tutoring is published from roughly AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik at AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. The specialist band for IB, IGCSE and A Level teaching is AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai table reaching AED 450 and beyond. Premium named tutors reach AED 650 at BartyED. None of these figures is an IB Gram price, and before paying the premium band a parent should ask exactly what it buys and ask for evidence of any examiner claim in writing.

The honest guidance for mathematics specifically. Standard Level problems, and almost all procedural fluency and method-mark work, sit comfortably in the AED 150 to 300 band. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, Paper 3 technique and a rescued exploration are where the specialist band at AED 200 to 450 earns its difference, because the knowledge required is course-specific rather than subject-general. The budget band rarely buys anybody who has taught the current courses. And the travel premium buys a journey, which is why we do not sell it.

sections.heading: Tutoring next to a Dubai school fee: the proportion nobody calculates
paragraphs: Families decide about tutoring in isolation and then feel the cost acutely, when the useful comparison is the whole education budget. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. Against a frozen school fee, a diagnosed block of mathematics hours is a small and unusually controllable line - and controllability is the point, because it is the one part of the budget a family can aim precisely.

Scale matters as well. Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with UK curriculum schools holding 37% of enrolment, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. For 2026-27 the emirate added seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. The IB share is small in a very large market, which is precisely why Higher Level mathematics specialists are scarce and why their published rates sit where they do.

The table puts a mathematics tutoring decision next to the other things a Diploma costs, so a parent can see the proportion rather than the absolute figure. Two cautions about reading it. The school fee row is a band rather than a quote, because fees vary by campus and year group and the only authority on your own is the campus itself and KHDA's published fee information. And the exam entry row depends entirely on whether a student sits through their school or as a private candidate, which is a question for the exams officer.

The conclusion we would draw from the arithmetic, and the one our own commercial interest argues against, is that fewer hours aimed better is almost always the right answer in mathematics. A paid diagnostic plus a six-hour fluency block, reviewed against the next set of school marks, is a small line in the table. Two years of undifferentiated weekly sessions at the specialist band is a large one, and in the cases where it is genuinely needed - Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with real content gaps - a family should at least be choosing it deliberately rather than drifting into it.

sections.heading: The cheapest honest step, and when to stop paying
paragraphs: If you take one action from this page, take this one. Buy a diagnostic session, on its own, with no package attached, and ask for the output in writing: which of the five conditions is present, which topics if any are genuinely missing, and how many hours each plausibly needs. Our first session is a free trial and it is built exactly that way, which means you can get the document at no cost, and you are free to act on it with us or with anybody else. A provider unwilling to give you that in writing is telling you something.

Then act on the smallest version first. If the diagnosis says procedural slowness, buy the fluency block and measure it against timed drills rather than against a feeling. If it says method marks, buy four to eight hours and measure it against the next marked paper. If it says topic gaps, buy them topic by topic against the list. If it says the course is wrong, do not buy any hours at all - go to the head of mathematics, and use six weeks of marked work as the evidence if a change needs arguing for.

Equally important is knowing when to stop, because nobody in this market will tell you. Stop the fluency block when the drill times stop improving. Stop a topic when the student can do an unseen past-paper question on it unaided. Stop weekly sessions if two consecutive school assessments show no movement and the tutor cannot explain why, because at that point either the diagnosis was wrong or the limiting factor is not teaching. Reviewing against the school's own marks at six weeks, rather than against how the sessions feel, is the mechanism that makes stopping possible.

And the limits on our side, since this page has argued for honesty about money. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists are the scarcest match we make, and some weeks the right person has no slot inside a usable Gulf Standard Time evening for an island school day; when that happens we say so and give a date. We will not promise a grade, a point total or an improvement, in any phrasing. We will not write or redraft an exploration. And we will not claim approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, from KHDA, from the Ministry of Education or from any school, because we hold none of them.

faqs.question: What should an hour of IB maths tutoring cost a Palm Jumeirah family?
faqs.answer: It depends on which of five problems you are buying a fix for. Published Dubai rates read in October 2026 run AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, and AED 200 to 450 and above for a specialist with TutorChase at AED 270. Most Standard Level work, fluency drill and method-mark coaching sits in the middle band. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and Paper 3 technique are where the specialist band earns its difference. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation the cheaper course to support?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level generally needs the fewest tutoring hours of the four, and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level needs the most, both because the mathematics is harder and because the specialists are scarcer. The expensive mistake is not choosing the harder course; it is being on the wrong one. A student on Higher Level Analysis and Approaches who belonged on Applications and Interpretation can absorb two years of weekly specialist sessions and still finish low, because the gap is structural rather than a knowledge deficit.

faqs.question: How many hours of maths support does a DP1 student actually need?
faqs.answer: Far fewer than most families buy, if the diagnosis is done first. Procedural slowness, which is the commonest DP1 condition and usually originates in a curriculum transition, takes six to twelve hours. Method-mark illiteracy takes four to eight. A genuine topic gap takes three to six hours per topic. Exam management takes practice rather than teaching. Where a student has two or three real topic gaps plus slow algebra, the total climbs, and you should see that number written down before committing rather than discovering it in instalments.

faqs.question: Where do families waste the most money on IB maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Buying re-teaching when the problem is fluency or method marks. Re-teaching feels like substance, so it is what families ask for, and it is the most expensive of the options. Second is buying thirty hours against a problem that takes six, because nobody produced an hour count. Third is paying the in-home travel premium - published at AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online - for a DP2 student working on Paper 3 technique, where a person in the room adds nothing the lesson needs.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor ever the right choice for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: For some of the work, yes, and this is worth knowing. Procedural fluency drill - timed algebra, indices, rearrangement - does not require a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist, and paying the specialist band for it is waste. What does require the specialist is Paper 3 technique, the harder content, and a rescued exploration, because that knowledge is course-specific. Some families sensibly split the work: a middle-band tutor for the drill, a specialist for a short block on the parts that need one.

faqs.question: How much does exploration support cost in tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Six to ten hours if it is spread across months, and far more if it is compressed into a fortnight before the school's deadline. The milestones are topic feasibility, narrowing within a fortnight of the first idea, attempting the mathematics before any prose is written, the student's own drafting, a feedback pass against the criteria, and a reflection pass. The expensive version happens when a topic with too little mathematics in it is only caught in the final weeks, at which point the work starts again at whatever the going rate is.

faqs.question: Does the graphic display calculator skill need separate paid sessions?
faqs.answer: It needs explicit teaching and it rarely gets any, which makes it unusually good value. Three to five hours is normally enough. Students who grew up with devices are assumed to work the machine out and frequently do not: they reach for the wrong function under time, or produce a correct value with no indication of what was done, which loses method marks on a calculator-permitted paper. Compare your child's calculator and non-calculator paper marks separately. A gap of more than a band tells you where the hours belong.

faqs.question: Should we pay for maths tutoring in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, and the cheapest version of all is the summer before it. Procedural fluency built in DP1 is available to be used for two years; the same work bought in the February of DP2 competes with revision for five other subjects. DP1 is also when a course change is still possible, which is the most valuable decision available. Waiting until DP2 converts a six-hour fluency problem into a thirty-hour catch-up problem, at the same hourly rate, which is how mathematics budgets quietly quintuple.

faqs.question: Is a group maths class cheaper than one-to-one for the same result?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, and the same result only when the students share the same problem. For revision of content everybody has already been taught, a small group led by somebody competent is a reasonable purchase. For a diagnosed individual problem - this student's algebra, this student's method marks, this student's exploration - the whole value of one-to-one is that the hour goes on that. None of the providers we researched publishes a per-student group rate, so ask for the figure in writing before agreeing to anything.

faqs.question: What does a diagnostic maths session involve and is it chargeable?
faqs.answer: Ours is the free trial, deliberately. The student works a timed section at their actual course and level while the tutor watches where the method breaks, and then they mark it together against published conventions. The output is a written note separating procedural slowness, topic gaps, method-mark losses, exam management and course fit, with an hour count against each. You may act on that document with us or with anybody else. A provider unwilling to give you it in writing is worth noticing.

faqs.question: Do maths tutoring rates in Dubai rise before the May session?
faqs.answer: The published bands we read in October 2026 do not advertise a seasonal increase, but availability tightens sharply from January, and scarce availability behaves like a price rise whether or not the number on the page changes. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialists with a usable Gulf-evening slot are the first to be unavailable. The practical answer is to book the slot in the autumn term if you expect to want it in the spring, and to treat a February enquiry for Higher Level support as a scheduling problem rather than a pricing one.

faqs.question: Does the quoted hourly rate include marking of past papers?
faqs.answer: Ask, in writing, because practice varies widely and this is where quoted rates become hard to compare. Marking a student's written work between sessions takes the tutor real time, and some providers include it while others treat the hour as contact time only. For mathematics it matters more than in most subjects, because method-mark discipline is built by having working annotated line by line rather than by discussing it afterwards. A rate that includes marking at AED 250 may be better value than one that excludes it at AED 200.

faqs.question: Is in-home maths tutoring on Palm Jumeirah worth the travel premium?
faqs.answer: Rarely, for a Diploma mathematics student, and the published figures show what you are paying for. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor, and monthly packages run about AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour home visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. The difference is a journey to the island. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible maths tutoring commitment?
faqs.answer: A diagnostic session, then the smallest block the diagnosis justifies, with a review point attached. In practice that is often one free trial plus a six-hour fluency block, measured against timed drills, or four to eight hours of method-mark work measured against the next marked paper. What it is not is a monthly retainer agreed before anybody knows what is wrong. Buying small first also tests the diagnosis, which matters, because a wrong diagnosis costs more than a wrong hourly rate ever will.

faqs.question: How does online delivery change what a Palm Jumeirah family pays?
faqs.answer: It removes the travel from the hour, which is the single largest controllable cost on an island address. The published gap between online and in-home delivery - AED 150 to 300 against AED 180 to 500 with travel inside - is the journey, and a frond or Crescent address sits at the expensive end of it. Online delivery also widens the pool of Higher Level specialists from those willing to drive onto the Palm to all of them, which is why the cheaper option is usually the better-matched one as well.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingHeading: Diagnose first, then buy the smallest thing that works
dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-palm-jumeirah.closingBody: Mathematics is where island families spend most and aim worst, and the fix costs nothing to start. Send the course, the level and the marks on the last two papers separately, take the free diagnostic session, and ask for the written note: which of the five problems is present, which topics are genuinely missing, how many hours each needs. Then buy the smallest version and review it against the school's own marks at six weeks. Lessons run one-to-one and live online, in Gulf Standard Time, with no travel priced into the hour.

intro.heading: Two decisions, one afternoon, and not much room for either
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics puts two things in front of a Pearl Jumeira family at once. The first is a choice between two different courses with the same name, made in the spring of Year 11 and difficult to reverse after the first term of Year 12. The second is a weekly hour that has to exist inside an afternoon with very little slack in it. The choice gets discussed at school and the hour gets left to chance, which is the wrong way round, because the hour is what makes the choice survivable.

Take the choice first. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation share five syllabus topics, number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus, and then diverge sharply in emphasis. Analysis and Approaches is the abstract route: proof, algebraic manipulation, calculus technique, and a Paper 1 at both levels where no calculator is permitted. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling route: data, statistics, technology used throughout, and both papers allowing a graphical calculator. A student who is quick and accurate with algebra and a student who is strong at interpreting data are suited to different courses, and the second is not a lesser version of the first.

The complication is that university entry does not treat them identically. Several competitive courses in mathematics, engineering, physics and economics specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who takes Applications and Interpretation can close a door without being told they have done so. That is not a reason for everyone to take Analysis and Approaches, which is the more common error. It is a reason to check the requirements of the courses a student might plausibly apply for before the choice is confirmed, on the universities' own admissions pages rather than on any tutoring website.

Now the afternoon. Schools serving this island finish between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. The causeway approach and the drive home take thirty to forty-five minutes. Activity programmes in this cluster run roughly 4pm to 6pm. What remains is an early slot around 4:45pm for students with a free day, and a reliable slot from 6:45pm. Mathematics is unusually sensitive to the time of day, because a tired student still recognises question types and still makes arithmetic slips, which is the least diagnosable combination there is. Nothing useful happens after about 8:30pm.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with working annotated on a shared screen and kept afterwards. For maths that record is the practical benefit: a method line written in October is available in April, which is exactly when a student is trying to remember what the examiner wanted.

dubai/ib-maths-tutor-in-pearl-jumeira.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of Diploma mathematics that generate the most tutoring hours among Pearl Jumeira families, with what each actually demands of a session.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation and proof
subjects.description: Partial fractions, binomial expansion, induction and the written structure of a proof. The reason Analysis and Approaches cannot be taught by somebody who has only taught applied mathematics: the marks are in the argument, not the answer.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, rational functions, asymptotes and transformation notation. Students lose marks describing a transformation in words when the paper asks for notation, and by sketching without labelling intercepts or asymptotes.

subjects.name: Differential calculus
subjects.description: Chain, product and quotient rules, implicit differentiation and related rates at Higher Level. The common failure is a correct derivative applied to the wrong variable in a context question, which is a reading problem rather than a calculus one.

subjects.name: Integral calculus
subjects.levels: Both courses, substantially deeper in AA HL
subjects.description: Substitution, integration by parts and volumes of revolution in Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Heavy, procedural and rewarding of drilled practice, which makes it the clearest case for a standing weekly hour.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and trigonometric identities
subjects.description: Identities, equations, and the compound angle work that Higher Level requires. Students who know the identities often cannot choose between them under pressure, which is a decision habit built by timed practice rather than revision.

subjects.name: Statistics, distributions and hypothesis testing
subjects.description: Binomial and normal distributions in both courses, with chi-squared and regression work central to Applications and Interpretation. Marks are lost in the wording of a conclusion rather than in the calculation.

subjects.name: Vectors and geometry
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products, lines and planes in three dimensions, and intersection problems. One of the heaviest Higher Level blocks and a frequent trigger for adding a second weekly hour in the second year.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator technique
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections, regression, and distribution functions. Applications and Interpretation permits technology in both papers, so calculator fluency is an assessed skill rather than a convenience, and it is routinely under-taught.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.levels: Both courses, 20 per cent of the grade
subjects.description: Marked against five criteria worth 20 marks in total, over roughly twelve to twenty pages. The work must be the student's own; a tutor teaches the mathematics and the criteria and gives feedback on drafts.

subjects.name: Command terms and method marks
subjects.description: Distinguishing show that, hence, verify and justify, and writing the method line that earns credit even when the final answer is wrong. The single most transferable teaching in the course and the fastest source of recovered marks.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: how to decide
paragraphs: The two courses are compared below on the things that actually differ. The decision is normally made in the spring of Year 11 and becomes difficult to change after the first term of Year 12, so it is worth a deliberate hour rather than a conversation in a corridor.

The honest starting question is about the student rather than the university. A student who is quick and accurate with algebraic manipulation, who enjoys a problem with a single clean answer, and who tolerates abstraction, belongs in Analysis and Approaches. A student who reads data well, who is interested in what a number means in context, and who finds extended algebraic manipulation a source of errors rather than pleasure, belongs in Applications and Interpretation. The second is not the easier course; it is a different course with a graphical calculator in both papers and a heavier statistical load.

The second question is about doors. Several competitive courses in mathematics, engineering, physics and economics specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who chooses Applications and Interpretation can foreclose those applications without being told. The right response is not to default everybody into Analysis and Approaches, which produces students at Higher Level who would have achieved materially more at Standard Level in the other course. The right response is to check the stated requirements of plausible courses on the universities' own admissions pages before the form is signed.

The third question is level, and it is separate from course. Higher Level in either route carries 240 teaching hours against 150, adds a third paper, and deepens the content substantially. A student capable of a strong Standard Level grade in Analysis and Approaches is often not capable of a strong Higher Level one, and the difference between those two outcomes matters more to most applications than the label. Taking the honest level is almost always the better strategy, and a marked past paper is the only reliable instrument for deciding.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth, and which hour should target which
paragraphs: Session planning becomes straightforward once the weightings are visible, and they are not the same at the two levels. At Standard Level there are two papers, each worth 40 per cent, with the exploration at 20 per cent. At Higher Level there are three papers, worth 30, 30 and 20 per cent, with the exploration again at 20 per cent. That structural difference, rather than content depth alone, is what makes Higher Level a different proposition.

The papers reward different things. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 permits no calculator, which makes exact values, algebraic fluency and clean manipulation assessed skills in their own right. Paper 2 permits a graphical calculator, which shifts the demand towards setting up a problem correctly and using technology efficiently. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended problem-solving paper in which a long investigation is built up in stages, and it rewards something neither of the other papers does: persistence through a structured sequence where a mistake early on propagates.

That gives a family a planning rule worth using. Name the paper at the start of each session. An hour aimed at Paper 1 is algebraic drill and exact-value work. An hour aimed at Paper 2 is problem setup and calculator technique. An hour aimed at Paper 3 is one long question worked end to end with the structure made explicit. A session described as maths revision will default to whichever topic feels most urgent, which is how families pay for twelve hours and improve on nothing in particular.

Paper 3 deserves one further note because it is the most commonly neglected component in the whole course. It is 20 per cent of a Higher Level grade, it is unlike anything in the first two papers, and it is frequently met for the first time a few weeks before the examinations. Two or three sessions on it during the second year, worked as whole questions rather than as topics, is among the highest-value spending available in Diploma mathematics.

sections.heading: The exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, and a tutor's limits
paragraphs: The exploration is 20 per cent of the mathematics grade at both levels, runs to roughly twelve to twenty pages, and is marked against five criteria worth 20 marks in total. The table sets them out with their allocations, which is information most students never see laid out and which changes how they approach the task.

Read the allocations rather than the names. Use of mathematics carries the largest single share, which means a well-written exploration about mathematics that is too simple cannot reach the upper bands however elegant the prose. That single fact resolves most exploration problems before they start, because the commonest failure is a topic chosen for personal interest with no mathematics in it beyond the level of the course's first term.

The other failures are predictable. Presentation marks are lost through an absent structure and an argument the reader has to assemble. Mathematical communication marks are lost through inconsistent notation and undefined variables. Personal engagement marks are lost through a topic the student has no actual connection to, which is visible immediately to a reader. Reflection marks are lost through a closing paragraph that summarises rather than evaluates: saying what was done instead of what the result means, where the approach was limited, and what a next step would be.

The boundary on help is firm and belongs in plain words. A tutor explains what each criterion rewards and how many marks it carries, teaches the mathematics the student has chosen to use, asks the questions that establish whether a topic has enough mathematics in it, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write, draft, redraft or supply any part of the exploration, and will not hand over a topic for adoption. At least one operator ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments; submitting purchased work is a malpractice risk carried by the student rather than by the seller.

sections.heading: Where Diploma maths marks are actually lost on this island
paragraphs: Across cohorts in this cluster the losses concentrate in four places, and none of them is the content a student would name if asked what they find difficult.

The first is the missing method line. Diploma mark schemes award method marks for a correct approach even where the final answer is wrong, and students who work in their heads or on a calculator and write only the answer forfeit them. This is the single largest recoverable loss in the course, it costs several marks a paper, and it is a writing habit rather than a mathematical weakness. Three weeks of being required to write the line fixes it permanently.

The second is command terms. Show that, hence, verify and justify make different demands, and a student who treats them as interchangeable will answer a show that question by verifying a value, which earns little. Hence in particular signals that the previous part must be used, and ignoring it discards an intended route. These distinctions take one session to teach and recur in every paper.

The third is calculator discipline, and it cuts both ways. In Analysis and Approaches, students practise on Paper 2 and then meet Paper 1 with no calculator and no fluency in exact values, surds or standard form. In Applications and Interpretation, where technology is permitted throughout, students under-use it: they do by hand what the calculator was intended for and run out of time. Each is a specific, teachable correction.

The fourth is Paper 3 at Higher Level, discussed earlier, where the loss is structural rather than topical. A student who abandons a long structured question after an early error loses the remaining parts, most of which were accessible. Teaching the habit of carrying on with a stated assumption recovers marks that no amount of topic revision would reach.

sections.heading: Fitting the maths hour into a Pearl Jumeira afternoon
paragraphs: Mathematics is the Diploma subject most sensitive to the time of day, which makes the slot a substantive decision rather than an administrative one. A tired student reading a history chapter learns something. A tired student carrying a four-stage calculation with an exact value at the end does not, and worse, produces errors that look like gaps in understanding and send the tutor after the wrong problem.

The afternoon on this island runs as follows. Senior school days in the Jumeirah, Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster end between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm. The causeway approach plus the drive home takes thirty to forty-five minutes, so the student is in at around 3:30pm to 4:15pm. Activity programmes occupy roughly 4pm to 6pm for most students. That produces two workable windows, an early one around 4:45pm on activity-free days and a dependable one from 6:45pm after food.

For Standard Level, one hour in either of those windows is normally the whole requirement across the two years. For Higher Level, the second year usually needs two hours on separate days, because the vectors and integration blocks arrive alongside the exploration deadline and the mock window. Two separate hours allow work to be set, attempted alone and then marked, which a single long session cannot, since nothing has been attempted in between.

The slots have to be claimed in September. Activity programmes, school revision sessions and fixtures fill progressively through the year, and by January the available windows in this cluster have usually narrowed to after 7pm. A family that decides in September keeps the better slot for two years at no extra cost, which is the cheapest advantage available in Diploma mathematics.

sections.heading: The maths inside the rest of the Diploma
paragraphs: A maths tutor in a Diploma household is frequently solving problems that appear on other subjects' reports, and recognising that saves a family from buying two tutors for one problem.

Physics is the clearest case. Diploma physics expects rearranging before substituting, confident standard form, trigonometry for resolving vectors, gradients and areas under graphs, and at Higher Level some calculus. A student on Applications and Interpretation meets less of that incidentally than one on Analysis and Approaches, and the result is a physics mark that reflects mathematical technique rather than physics understanding. One or two sessions aimed at the mathematical technique will move the physics more than physics revision would.

Chemistry is similar in a narrower way. Logarithms for pH, rearrangement in equilibrium and energetics calculations, and proportional reasoning in stoichiometry are all mathematics, and a student who is hesitant with any of them will be slow and error-prone in chemistry without the chemistry being the issue. Economics at Higher Level carries calculation and graph interpretation that reward the same underlying fluency.

There is a reverse direction too, and it is worth stating because it is the opposite of an upsell. A student struggling in physics and chemistry whose maths is sound does not need a maths tutor, and anybody recommending one is selling hours. The diagnostic question is simple: in the marked script, is the error in the physics or in the algebra that the physics required? A marked paper answers it in minutes, which is why the diagnostic session is worth buying before any standing booking.
